Later, Tarique visited the grave of his younger brother Arafat Rahman Koko, who died in 2015, for the first time at the Banani Graveyard at about 2:00pm and offered prayers at his brother’s grave. Afterwards, Tarique went to the Banani Military Cemetery, where his father-in-law and former Navy chief Rear Admiral Mahbub Ali Khan, is buried. He also offered prayers there. Later, Tarique visited the graves of the army officers who were killed at a massacre at the erstwhile Bangladesh Rifles headquarters at Pilkhana in Dhaka. He offered prayers at the graves. After returning to Bangladesh on December 25, Tarique visited Evercare Hospital after a reception on 300 feet road in Purbachal, to see his ailing mother and former prime minister Khaleda Zia. On December 26, he paid tribute to his father, the late president Ziaur Rahman, at his grave at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in the capital Dhaka and later visited the National Memorial at Savar, on the outskirts of the capital, to honour the Liberation War martyrs.

title: Inqilab Mancha shifts blockade from Shahbagh to facilitate Tarique’s visit
body: Inqilab Mancha on Saturday moved its blockade from Shahbagh to in front of Aziz Super Market ahead of the arrival of Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman. The platform withdrew blockade from Shahbagh at about 8:30am and took position near Aziz Super Market. In a post on its official Facebook page, Inqilab Mancha said it cleared the Shahbagh area to facilitate Tarique Rahman’s movement. It said that it would return to Shahbagh after Tarique Rahman visits the grave of Sharif Osman Hadi, the platform’s convener who died at a Singapore hospital after being shot in Dhaka. As part of a pre-announced programme, Inqilab Mancha staged an overnight sit-in at Shahbagh from Friday night.

title: Crew member dies as St Martins-bound vessel catches fire
body: A crew member died on Saturday morning as a fire broke out on a St Martins-bound vessel Atlantic Cruise in Cox’s Bazar. The incident occurred at around 6:45am at the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority jetty in Nuniachhara of Cox’s Bazar Sadar where the vessel was docked on the Bakkhali River, according to the police and district administration officials. The victim was identified as Nur Kamal, 25, son of Mohammad Ilias from Teknaf Damdamiya Border Guard Bangladesh Camp area, said Fire Service and Civil Defence deputy director Morshed Hossain. ‘The deceased crew member was taking rest alone in the engine room when the fire broke out,’ he said. He also said that although the fire was brought under control at about 8:00am but it took three more hours to douse it completely after which the victim’s body was recovered from inside the burnt vessel. Several police officials said that the fire originated from the engine room. Cox’s Bazar deputy commissioner Md Abdul Mannan said that the vessel had been anchored at the BIWTA jetty since early morning for passengers to board for its next scheduled trip to the island. ‘Fortunately, there was no passenger in the ship when the fire broke out,’ he added. He also said that they had already formed a seven-member probe committee headed by an additional deputy commissioner to investigate the fire. Representatives from the Fire Service, Department of Shipping, Coast Guard and BIWTA were included in the committee, he added, saying that the committee was asked to submit its report within seven working days. General secretary of the Sea Cruise Operators Owners Association of Bangladesh Hossain Islam Bahadur said that Atlantic Cruise reached the jetty in the morning to pick up tourists when suddenly smoke was noticed being spewed out from inside the vessel. ‘The fire spread quickly. Fire Service and other agencies immediately rushed to the spot and douse the fire,’ he said. Hossain Islam also said that 194 tourists waiting at the jetty to board the vessel escaped the flame.

title: Coast Guard recovers two bodies in Galachipa River
body: The Bangladesh Coast Guard recovered the bodies of two missing fishermen in the Galachipa River in Patuakhali on Friday. The Coast Guard in a press release said that a fishing boat going fishing in the estuary of the Bay of Bengal adjacent to the Galachipa River in Patuakhali sank in strong currents, leaving two fishermen missing. When the Coast Guard was informed about the matter, two Coast Guard stations, Rangabali and Charmanika, immediately launched a rescue operation using high-speed boats. After an operation, the Coast Guard rescue team was able to recover two bodies at 2:00pm on Friday. The deceased, Shamim Jamaddar, and his son Md Shihab Hossain, were residents of Rangabali in the district. The process of handing over the bodies to the family is under way.

title: JnUCSU Leftist panel’s 40,000 leaflets ‘stolen’
body: Just one day before the end of campaigning for the Jagannath University Central Students’ Union elections, allegations have surfaced that 40,000 leaflets of the leftist Maulana Bhasani Brigade panel were stolen. The panel leaders made the allegation at a press conference held at 3:30pm on Friday. Amrin Jahan Opi, the panel’s candidate for social welfare and student affairs secretary, said, ‘Yesterday [Thursday] at noon, 40,000 campaign leaflets of our 21 candidates went missing. At that time, we did not receive any satisfactory response from the university administration. Later, we came to know that the leaflets were taken away by cleaning staff in the name of cleaning.’ General secretary candidate Ivan Tahseeb said, ‘Yesterday[Thursday], our 40,000 leaflets were stolen from in front of the staircase of the Abakash Building. Although we managed to recover a portion of them, the campaign materials of several candidates are still missing. We demand compensation for this incident and call for punishment of those involved, following a proper investigation.’ Vice-president candidate Gourab Bhowmik said, ‘The cleaning staff who took our leaflets are claiming that since the campaign period was over, they sold them. However, we have seen that no leaflets of any other panel were stolen. We demand the administration to take appropriate action.’ At the press conference, the Maulana Bhasani Brigade also demanded that voting be conducted through a manual system. In this regard, the panel’s assistant general secretary candidate Shamsul Alam Maruf said, ‘In previous student union elections, we have seen allegations of election manufacturing. Moreover, the election commission has failed to provide any clear explanation on how the machine would read ballots if voters mark the cross symbol more than once. Therefore, we demand that voting be held through a manual system.’

title: Kishoreganj road named after Osman Hadi
body: A newly constructed road in Rashidabad Union of Kishoreganj Sadar has been named ‘Shaheed Osman Hadi Road’ to honour Shaheed Sharif Osman Hadi, frontline fighter of the July uprising and spokesperson of the Inquilab Mancha. A doa-mahfil and inauguration programme were held after jumma prayers on Friday at the Sagra Bishwaroad signboard intersection under the banner of ‘Kishoreganjbashi’, with participation from people of all walks of life. Speakers recalled Shaheed Osman Hadi’s sacrifice and described him as a symbol of resistance against injustice. They also demanded swift and exemplary punishment for those responsible for his killing. The programme ended with a special doa seeking eternal peace for Shaheed Sharif Osman Hadi. Hadi, also an aspiring candidate for Dhaka-8 constituency, was shot on December 12 while he was on a battery-run auto-rickshaw in the Dhaka’s Purana Paltan area.

title: Prosecute killers, not gunmen, for politicians’ safety: Akhter
body: National Citizen Party member-secretary Akhter Hossen said that if the murderers were arrested and proper punishment was ensured, then no one, including politicians, would need gunmen. ‘If the murderers commit crimes and get away with it, then the politicians will be insecure. Therefore, it is not possible to ensure security by gunmen alone without arresting and prosecuting the murderers,’ he said while talking to local reporters at the 36 July Memorial Square in front of the Public Library ground of Rangpur city Thursday afternoon. Earlier, Akhter Hossen reached Rangpur to participate in election campaigning and party activities in his Rangpur-4 (Pirgachha-Kawnia) constituency. Later, he came to the 36 July Memorial Square in the city and met with the party leaders and activists. Akhter said that a database of the country’s criminals and murderers needs to be created. This database will act as a real security ring for everyone. ‘If the murderers will roam around outside and we will roam around with gunmen, this cannot ensure security in any way. If the murderers are arrested and proper punishment is ensured, then no gunmen are needed,’ he continued. He said, ‘If Bangladesh has to be protected and an environment has to be created for a peaceful transfer of power, then the law and order situation must be improved.’ The government will have to work to ensure people’s participation in the elections with peace and order. The NCP leader said that the law enforcement agencies are not able to give a clear message about whether those involved in the murder of Shaheed Osman Hadi Bhai are hiding inside the country or have fled to India. ‘We want the gang behind Osman Hadi’s murder to be found and punished as soon as possible. The murderer is known, and everything is public, it is not possible for him to kill and escape alone or hide. A big gang is working here,’ he said. If the murderers are brought to justice and exemplary punishment is ensured for them, then all the people of the country will be safe. The law and order situation in the country will improve. He said, ‘There are attempts to obstruct the elections in various ways. We want the murder of Shaheed Osman Hadi Bhai to be tried and the murderers to be arrested. We want the government to ensure that such murders do not happen again.’ The NCP leader said that the ousted Awami League and their allies are trying to destabilise the country. It was possible to bring the Awami League’s allies under the law after the mass uprising. At this time, NCP Rangpur district committee convener Md Al Mamun, metropolitan member-secretary Abdul Malek, district joint conveners Alamgir Nayan and Abu Raihan, Rangpur-4 constituency election steering committee chief coordinator Abdullah-Al Mamun and NCP leader Toufiq Islam, among others, were present.

title: Youth linked to AL arrested over arson at election office
body: The police in Lakshmipur on Friday said that they arrested a youth in connection with the arson attack on the district election office on December 13. The arrested youth was Md Rubel, 40. The superintendent of police Md. Abu Tarek said that Rubel had confessed to setting fire after allegedly receiving money from Shimul Chakrabarti, assistant personal secretary to the late AKM Shahjahan Kamal, a former minister of the ousted Awami League government and lawmaker from Lakshmipur-3. ‘The fire was intended to create panic and fear among voters after the election schedule was announced,’ the police officer said at a press conference in his office. According to police and election officials, a fire broke out at the election commission office at about 3:30am on December 13, when masked individuals allegedly poured petrol into a storeroom on the ground floor. The blaze damaged part of the office and destroyed several documents and pieces of equipment, officials said. On December 10, chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin announced the schedule for the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections to be held on February 12. The police said that Rubel is the brother of Azizur Rahman, former general secretary of Lakshmipur Sadar upazila unit of the Bangladesh Chhatra League. Rubel, a former driver at a power office, allegedly set the fire in exchange for Tk 10,000, police said, citing his confession. Police also said that they seized the mobile phone Rubel allegedly used to take photographs of the fire after carrying out the attack. Investigations are ongoing, the police added.

title: Abdullah, Salam, Ratan get BNP nominations in Munshiganj
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party has nominated Sheikh Md Abdullah, Md Abdus Salam Azad and Md Kamruzzaman Ratan to contest the forthcoming 13th national parliamentary election in Munshiganj’s three constituencies. Member of the district BNP convening committee Sheikh Md Abdullah received the nomination paper, signed by BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, for Munshiganj-1 (Sirajdikhan-Sreenagar). The party also nominated BNP joint secretary general Md Abdus Salam Azad for Munshiganj-2 (Louhjang-Tongibari). Earlier, former state minister for health and district BNP convener Mizanur Rahman Sinha was initially nominated for the seat. For Munshiganj-3 (Sadar-Gazaria), BNP nominated its social welfare affairs secretary and former district BNP member secretary Md Kamruzzaman Ratan.

title: Bangladesh
body: Religious minorities want polls manifestos include their rights, safety Leaders of the Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council at a discussion on Saturday called on the political parties to include issues of ensuring rights and safety of religious minorities in their election manifestos for the general elections scheduled for February 12 next year...

title: Bangladesh-China literature club launched
body: Marking the golden jubilee of China-Bangladesh diplomatic relations, the Chinese Literature Readers Club was formally launched in Dhaka on Friday to strengthen literary and cultural exchanges between the two countries. The inauguration ceremony was held in the morning at the Apon Friendship Exchange Center in the capital’s Baridhara area, where speakers expressed optimism that the initiative would promote people-to-people connectivity through literature and intellectual dialogue. Jointly organised by the China Writers Association and the Apon Friendship Exchange Center, the club aims to create a sustainable platform for cooperation among writers, researchers, publishers and readers of both countries. The club’s plaque was unveiled by Li Shaofeng, cultural counsellor of the Chinese embassy in Bangladesh, and Yu Guangyue Anandi, director of the Bangla department of China Media Group, in the presence of noted Bangladeshi writers, publishers, researchers and literature enthusiasts. Speaking on the occasion, Yu Guangyue Anandi said China has a five-thousand-year old history and a rich literary heritage, adding that the club would allow Bangladeshi readers greater access to Chinese literature and help expand bilateral literary exchanges. Eminent writer Ahmed Riaz said the folk traditions of both countries span thousands of years, noting that the exchange of folk narratives could serve as a strong foundation for wider literary cooperation. Publisher Pradip Roy of Prosidhi Publishers said the club would open opportunities to translate Chinese books into Bangla and Bangladeshi books into Chinese, while also encouraging collaboration in book fairs and the exchange of modern publishing technologies. Faisal Abdullah, feature editor of CMG Bangla’s Dhaka office, said language barriers have limited Bangladeshi readers’ access to Chinese literature, expressing hope that the club would serve as an effective platform for translation, publication and promotion of literary works from both countries. In his remarks, cultural counsellor of Chinese embassy Li Shaofeng said the establishment of the club was significant, as it would enable deeper dialogue among writers, researchers and readers of both nations. People-to-people exchanges, particularly in literature and ideas, would further strengthen China-Bangladesh relations and described the club as a positive example of connectivity under the Belt and Road Initiative, he added. Li also stressed the importance of organising regular reading circles at the Chinese Book Corner of the National Library with participation from Bangladeshi writers, and assured continued cooperation with local writers and publishers working on Chinese literature.

title: Case filed over battery-run van driver’s death from torture
body: A case was filed over the death of a battery-powered van driver who died of beating as a suspected thief at Bagmara upazila in Rajshahi, the police said on Friday. Moslem Sardar, father of deceased Omar Faruk, filed the case with the Bagmara police on Thursday night, naming 12 people and accusing another 10–12 unidentified individuals, said Bagmara police officer-in-charge Saidul Alam. The police officer said that two of the accused were already arrested and sent to jail through a court, adding that efforts were under way to arrest the remaining suspects. According to the case statement, Omar Faruk parked his battery-run van at the Bhabaniganj CNG-auto-rickshaw stand on December 17 evening and went to relieve himself. When he returned, he was detained by Rezaul Karim, president of the Bagmara upazila CNG-auto-rickshaw owners’ association, and Abdul Matin, its general secretary, on suspicion of attempting to steal batteries from CNG-run three-wheelers. The associates allegedly severely beat Faruk with iron rods, the complaint said. The attackers later forced him to stand against a wall, hammered iron nails into his hands and legs, drowned him naked in a nearby river when he asked for water, and inserted dry chilli powder into his rectum. The accused then staged a scene of recovering cannabis from the critically injured man and informed the Bagmara assistant commissioner (land) Saiful Islam Bhuiyan, who conducted a mobile court. The mobile court sentenced Faruk to seven days’ imprisonment and fined him Tk 100, the complaint said. The police then took Faruk to Bagmara Upazila Health Complex for primary treatment before sending him to Rajshahi Central Jail, according to the case documents. He was admitted to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital the following day in critical condition. There he died on December 20. Sources at Bagmara Upazila Health Complex said that police brought Faruk to the hospital in the evening of December 17, where he received initial medical treatment. Hospital physician Saklain Hossain said that Faruk had swelling and injuries on different parts of his body, though none appeared life-threatening at the time of examination. Assistant commissioner (land) Saiful Islam Bhuiyan said that Faruk had been sentenced after cannabis was found in his possession and claimed that he was unaware of any prior assault. ‘At the time of sentencing, he appeared slightly unwell, but there was no visible bleeding in his body,’ he said. Investigation officer sub-inspector Abu Zahid Sheikh said that they were doing an investigation and working to arrest all those accused in the case.

title: Swift amendment to tobacco law demanded
body: Research and advocacy organisation PROGGA, Knowledge for Progress, and the Anti-Tobacco Media Alliance have welcomed the government’s approval of the ‘Smoking and Tobacco Products Usage (Control) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025’ at the advisory council meeting. The two organisations have expressed their appreciation to the government for this important step and have urged that the ordinance be published in the official Gazette without delay to ensure its timely implementation. In a press release issued on Friday, PROGGA and ATMA stated that the approval of the amendment represents a significant milestone in safeguarding public health in Bangladesh. The organisations emphasised that swift gazette notification is critical to completing the legal process and preventing undue influence by vested interests. Welcoming the decision, PROGGA executive director ABM Zubair stated that to complete the legal process, the ordinance had to be published in the gazette at the earliest possible time. ‘Any delay increases the risk of interference by tobacco companies. In the past, we have witnessed extensive and systematic interference by the tobacco industry during similar amendment processes.’ Tobacco use remains one of the most serious public health challenges in Bangladesh. More than 130,000 people die each year from tobacco-related diseases, including cancer, stroke, heart disease, and chronic respiratory illnesses. Despite existing control measures, 35.3 per cent of the adult population in the country continues to use tobacco. According to research findings, tobacco use and production cause an annual health and environmental loss amounting to Tk 87,000 crore, a staggering figure that is more than double the revenue earned from the tobacco sector during the same period. These loss places a significant burden on individuals, families, and the national economy. With the aim of effectively reducing tobacco use and protecting public health, the ministry of health and family welfare took the initiative to further strengthen the existing tobacco control law. PROGGA and ATMA noted that once the ordinance is gazetted and fully implemented, it will lead to a substantial reduction in tobacco-related deaths. The organisations further highlighted that effective implementation of the amended law will contribute directly to achieving one of the key targets of the sustainable development goals—namely, reducing premature mortality from non-communicable diseases by one-third.

title: JP announces candidates for 243 seats demand level playing field
body: The Jatiya Party led by Ghulam Muhammad Quader on Friday announced its candidates for 243 seats for the next Jatiya Sangsad election slated for February 12, 2026. Secretary general of the party Shamim Haider Patwary at a press conference in Dhaka announced the names and constituencies of the candidates for the general election. Announcing the party candidatures, Shamim Haider Patwary said that their party would withdraw the candidates and not participate in the elections if level playing field was not ensured for every political party and law and order situations were not improved. Presidium members of the party Mir Abdus Asud, SM Abdul Mannan, Mizanur Rahman, Saifuddin Ahmed Milon, Rejaul Islam Bhuiyan and Sherifa Quader, among others, were present at the press conference.

title: Mustard fields turn yellow in Gaibandha
body: Vast tracts of mustard fields across Gaibandha have turned bright yellow as the crop has reached full bloom, raising hopes among farmers for a bumper production this season. Sources said mustard cultivation has gained growing popularity among local farmers in recent years due to satisfactory yields and fair market prices of the Rabi crop. According to the department of agricultural extension, mustard has been cultivated on 9,460 hectares of land across all seven upazilas of the district during the current season. Of the total cultivated area, 855 hectares were brought under mustard cultivation in Gaibandha Sadar upazila, 1,250 hectares in Sadullapur, 850 hectares in Palashbari, 4,150 hectares in Gobindaganj, 1,330 hectares in Sundarganj, 735 hectares in Saghata and 290 hectares in Fulchhari upazila. Farmers are now busy taking care of the mustard fields following the guidance of field-level sub-assistant agriculture officers to ensure optimal production. Field-level agriculture officials said farmers have shown increasing interest in mustard cultivation in recent years after experiencing repeated bumper harvests and better prices. District training officer of DAE Md Asaduzzaman said favourable weather conditions, timely supply of quality seeds, fertilisers and other agricultural inputs, along with comparatively low pest attacks, have contributed to the positive outlook. Meanwhile, commercial banks, including Rajshahi Krishi Unnayan Bank, have disbursed soft loans to mustard growers during the season to boost production, bank sources said. DAE deputy director Md Atiqul Islam told BSS that lands owned by marginal farmers were also brought under mustard cultivation this year to help them improve their economic condition. He added that anyone visiting the mustard fields at this time would be delighted by the eye-catching yellow scenery, which has also enhanced the natural beauty of the area.

title: Union digital centre empowered Rangpur women
body: Haridebpur union is located 15 kilometres away from Rangpur district town. About 35,500 people of the union are mostly farmers. However, some people age engaged in different professions. Starting from birth registration to applying for university admission, the village people do everything online at the Union Parishad Digital Centre. As a result, the suffering of people to go far-flung areas or cities has reduced. People are happy to have digital services at their doorsteps. Lovely Rani is one of them who brought the digital services to the doorsteps of the common people. After establishment of the Haridevpur Union Digital Centre, people of different classes and professions, including students, businessmen, employees, daily wage earners and others are getting all the services at one place. This has reduced their sufferings as well as the waste of money and time. At the same time, some people found their employed in this centre. Becoming an entrepreneur at this digital centre has changed Lovely’s life, a middle-class girl who grew up amidst various crises. In a recent interview, she herself spoke about those days of struggle to survive. Lovely said that she had to endure many setbacks and hear people’s negative comments while embarking on this path of entrepreneurial life. However, she ignored all these and passed the Higher Secondary Examination and started working to establish the Digital Centre in 2010. ‘At that time, my father was sick and he was diagnosed cancer. My source of income was closed. I heard about the government’s initiative to establish digital centre in every union. So, despite having no prior experience, I took the risk and started the work,’ said Lovely, the eldest daughter of the family. She said, at the beginning, money was earned very little. No additional charge but only the service fees were taken from the clients. I still kept my morale high. I regularly ran from one village to another in the union to inform them about the digital services and benefits of the services. I could make people understand about the benefit of the digital centre. Entrepreneur Lovely’s life changed after such a struggle. Now she is a successful female entrepreneur, provided employment of more eight men and women. Lovely said, ‘My father is ill. I am the eldest child. I have just passed my higher secondary examination. And in this situation, I am worried about whether I will be able to continue my studies or not. And the responsibilities of the family naturally fall on my shoulders. I tried to get a job but failed.’ Finally, I came to know about the government support to establish union digital centre. After contacting with concerned people, I could start as an entrepreneur by establishing the Haridevpur Union Parishad Digital Centre,’ she added. Describing the early days of her business, she said, ‘Initially, no one would come to receive services. I myself went to villages and explained to people about the services of the digital centre. This is how people came to the centre to receive the services.’ ‘But there was a time when I couldn’t even take home Tk 30 after a full day work. Now I have employed seven to eight people in this digital centre. I ride a scooty to go every day to my work 15km away from home. Once upon a time people in society used to say harsh things, why am I doing all this as a woman? But on Friday everyone inspires me and praises me.’ In the meantime, Lovely got married. Her first child was born. At this time, another bad news came. Her husband lost a leg in an accident. As a result, she was left with the entire responsibility of her family, as well as her father’s house. She said her husband became paralysed. He can’t do much work. As a result, she had to take responsibility for everything herself. However, despite all this, she continued her studies till securing a master’s degree. Regarding the services of the digital centre, the female entrepreneur said, ‘All the work that falls under the scope of digital services are provided at my centre. Most of the customers come for land registration, document copies, e-registration, apply for allowances for elderly persons, disabled and widows. Job forms, application for admission in different universities at home and abroad, birth registration, payment of Union Parishad taxes are also done from the centre. Hundreds of people also come here every day for photographs, sending e-mails, electricity bills, computer compose and various online tasks. From morning to night the centre remains busy with different jobs. It is known that Aspire to Innovate is working under the Information and Communication Technology Division to provide services to people of all classes and professions at their doorsteps quickly, transparently, without harassment and at low cost by using information technology delivered from the centre. By simplifying the services of various initiatives of a2i under the office of the chief adviser, time, cost and travel have been saved in availing government services. As a result, people are becoming more interested in availing the services. Another entrepreneur from Rangpur, Aleya Khatun, said, ‘With the establishment of the digital centre, people who used to go to distant offices can now get their services seamlessly online. This process is generating more revenue from government services, which is helping to create other areas of development.’ Mallika Rani, a resident of Haridebpur Union, is a mother of two children. She has come to the digital centre for the birth registration of her second child. Mallika Rani said, ‘It was a lot of trouble to register the birth of my first child. I had to travel for a long time go to the upazila. But now there is a digital centre in my union. They came here and applied very quickly. There was no problem, I didn’t have to go far, I came to Lovely’s digital centre near my house and got the service instantly.’ Aspire to Innovate is working to make more such services easily and affordably available at the doorsteps of the common people across the country, its head of communications Mohammad Saiful Azam said. He told this reporter that more than 350 services are being provided through about 8,900 digital centres across the country. With the establishment of the digital centre, people now can easily get those services in less time and at a lower cost. This initiative to deliver services to the doorstep of the people has been recognised internationally,’ he added. Saiful Azam said that more than 80 crore services have already been provided to citizens through the digital centre. Currently, more than 16,400 entrepreneurs have become self-reliant by providing services to citizens through the digital centre. Out of them more than 5,200 are women entrepreneurs, he added.

title: Jamaat to prioritise youth jobs over unemployment aid: Shafiqur
body: Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami amir Shafiqur Rahman on Friday said that his party would priorities employment generation for young people instead of providing unemployment allowances, stressing that youths should become active builders of the nation rather than recipients of stipends. ‘We do not want our youths to accept unemployment allowances from anyone. We want to turn every young hand into a hand that builds the country,’ he told the central members’ conference of Islami Chhatrashibir as the chief guest at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre. Shafiqur said Jamaat-e-Islami would work in unity with people of all classes to build a humane and discrimination-free Bangladesh. ‘We want to place work in every hand, strength in every heart and the message of revolution on the lips of our youths. Not unemployment allowance, but youths themselves will bring revolution in every sector of this country.’ Calling upon young people to prepare themselves, the Jamaat amir said, ‘You will succeed, Insha Allah. We are with you.’ Highlighting the party’s vision for education, Shafiqur said Jamaat wants to establish an education system that would help students become complete human beings, reach the highest standard of learning, develop strong moral character and acquire technical skills so that no young man or woman remains unemployed. Referring to Chhatrashibir’s recent victories in different student unions, he said the youths now carry the responsibility of 180 million people. ‘May Allah make this burden easier for you and grant you the strength to bear it. These victories indicate that the victory of justice will come to Bangladesh, Insha Allah.’ ‘Students voted for Chhatrashibir as a symbol of justice in educational institutions, not for any other reason,’ he added. The Jamaat chief also said his party wants to establish justice in the country, noting that Bangladesh is currently facing an acute shortage of justice. ‘The foundation of justice is the Quran and the Sunnah of the Prophet (Sm). Justice has never been established anywhere in the world by abandoning the Quran and Sunnah.’ Shafiqur reiterated Jamaat-e-Islami’s commitment to restoring peace and discipline in people’s lives in line with divine guidance and to building a corruption-free, discrimination-free and justice-based humane Bangladesh. The day-long conference is being attended by members from across the country. The first session began at 8:00am with the recitation of the Holy Quran, followed by the inaugural declaration and opening remarks. The first session concluded at 1:00pm after speeches by invited guests, while the closing session began at 2:00pm after a short break.

title: End to mob violence before polls demanded
body: Leaders of Ganatantrik Jukta Front, a combine of seven political parties, at a protest rally in Dhaka on Friday called on the interim government to take immediate steps to stop mob violence before next national election scheduled for February 12. Jukta Front organised the rally in front of the National Press Club with coordinator of the combine Bazlur Rashid Firoz in chair, protesting against arson attacks on dailies Prothom Alo and The Daily Star and the brutal lynching of garment worker Dipu Chandra Das. Calling for immediate steps to stop mob violence nationwide, Bazlur Rashid Firoz also demanded that the government must ensure a level playing field for the political parties participating in the next general election Communist Party of Bangladesh president Kazi Sazzad Zahir Chandan said that the interim government had failed to fulfil people’s aspirations. Bangladesh Jasod standing committee member Mushtauq Husain said that people were eagerly waiting to cast their votes in next Jatiya Sangsad election which must be held in free, fair and credible manner. The rally was followed by a procession that marched through different city roads, including Gulshtan, Mitijheel and Purana Paltan. Left leaders Abdullah Al Kafee Ratan, Mushrefa Mishu, Masud Rana, Iqbal Kabir Jahid and others attended the programme. The partners of the combine are Communist Party of Bangladesh, Socialist Party of Bangladesh, SPB (Marxist), Revolutionary Communist League, Democratic Revolutionary Party, Bangadesher Samajtantrik Party, and Bangladesh Jasod.

title: Prof Jamal Uddin dies
body: Jamal Uddin Ahmed, a retired professor of the finance department of Dhaka University, passed away while undergoing treatment at a hospital in the capital early Friday. He was 75. He is survived by his widow, two daughters and a son, said a press release. His namaz-e-janaza was held at the Dhaka University Central Mosque, Masjidul Jamia, and was buried at the Azimpur Graveyard. DU vice-chancellor Professor Niaz Ahmed Khan expressed deep shock at the death of Professor Jamal Uddin Ahmed. In a condolence message, the VC said that he had made a unique contribution to education and research. ‘He will be remembered for this contribution.’ Niaz Ahmed prayed for the eternal peace of the deceased and expressed his deepest condolences to the bereaved family members. In his career, Professor Jamal Uddin Ahmed served as dean, departmental chairman, and provost of the hall of business studies at Dhaka University, among other administrative and academic responsibilities.

title: Farmers busy with planting Boro paddy in Sunamganj
body: Cultivation of Boro paddy, the main crop of farmers of the haor belt, is now going on in full swing in Sunamganj. After completion of preparing seedbeds and growing sapling between Kartik and Agrahayan months of the Bangla Calendar, farmers of the Sunamganj have started to plant Boro paddy, which is their main source of income. After harvesting the Aman crop, farmers in the area started Boro cultivation. They are busy with lifting seedlings of the Boro paddy from seedbeds and planting them on the prepared fields as the livelihood of around 90 per cent people of the district is directly depended on this crop. Faruk Miah, a farmer of Kandigaon village at Shalla upazila in the district, told New Age that this season he would plant Boro paddy on 20 acres of land. ‘In the meantime, I have sowed seedlings of Boro rice on three acres of land. I have a plan to sell the surplus seedlings from the seedbed after completion of cultivating my land,’ he said. Abdul Khalik of Bishnupur village at Fenerbak union under Jamalganj upazila in Sunamganj, said that he has taken preparation to plant Boro paddy, including several hybrid varieties, on 24 acres of land this year. ‘I started to plant the Boro seedlings on Tuesday,’ he said, adding that he is hopeful of completing the paddy cultivation in time due to the favourable weather in this year. Talking to New Age, Shawkat Ali, a day-labourer of Madhyanagar upazila, said that he works of lifting and planting boro saplings usually for Tk 500 a day. ‘I am thinking to demand Tk 600 as the daily wage since prices of daily essential goods have increased compared to the past years. Moreover, the demand for workers is also high now,’ he added. According to the Department of Agricultural Extension, Sunamganj, the target for this season has been set to cultivate Boro paddy on 2,23,505 hectares of land. To achieve the target, seedbeds have been set on 10,510 hectares of land. Among these, 2,720 hectares of hybrid, 7,730 hectares of Ufshi and 60 hectares of seedbeds of local variety paddy have been prepared in accordance with the statistics available in the district DAE office. The DAE’s Sunamganj deputy director Omar Faruk told New Age on Thursday that rice growers in most of the areas across Sunamganj district already started to plant saplings in full swing. ‘We hope, it would be possible to hit the target of planting Boro paddy this time if the weather remains suitable like now,’ he added.

title: Dr Zafrullah Chowdhury’s birth anniv today
body: Today is the 84th anniversary of birth of freedom fighter and Gonoshasthaya Kendra founder, Dr Zafrullah Chowdhury. Born at Raujan in Chattogram on December 27, 1941, vascular surgeon Zafrullah Chowdhury founded Gonoshasthaya Kendra in 1972 to provide healthcare services to underprivileged communities in Bangladesh. The public health activist is known more for his contribution to formulating Bangladesh’s National Drug Policy in 1982. He spent his early life in Kolkata, as his father was a police officer. After completing his matriculation at Nabakumar High School at Bakshibazar in Dhaka, he studied at Dhaka College. He later studied medicine at Dhaka Medical College, where he got involved with leftist political ideologies and was general secretary of the Dhaka Medical College Students’ Union. After a turbulent student life, he finished his MBBS degree in 1964 and left for the United Kingdom for post-graduate studies in general and vascular surgery. While studying at the Royal College of Surgeons in the UK, he joined the country’s War of Independence in 1971. In July 1971, Zafrullah, with the support of the Bangladesh Medical Association in London and local people, established a 480-bed ‘Bangladesh Field Hospital’ on the war field at Melaghar in Tripura to provide healthcare to injured freedom fighters. A huge number of freedom fighters took treatment at the hospital. After independence, he founded Gonoshasthaya Kendra in 1972 to provide healthcare services to underprivileged communities in the country. The healthcare centre is now providing healthcare services at an affordable cost across the country through several hospitals and over 50 sub-centres. Now, Gonoshasthaya runs the largest kidney dialysis unit in the country. For his outstanding contribution to ensuring healthcare for the poor, Zafrullah earned the title ‘Poor People’s Doctor’. Zafrullah had authored several books, including ‘The Politics of Drug’, and achieved many prestigious awards, including the country’s highest civilian award the Independence Award, the Ramon Magsaysay Award for his contribution to poor people’s good healthcare and well-being, the Right Livelihood Award for his outstanding record of promoting health and human development. Medical journal The Lancet hailed his works as a breakthrough in 1975, in one of their issues, after Gonoshasthaya had started family planning, vaccination and other basic health services employing young rural women. The demystification of healthcare and integrated healthcare were first introduced by Gonoshasthaya, which the global community appreciated. In fact, it became one of the basic pillars of the Alma-Ata Declaration of the World Health Organisation. Besides the healthcare sector, Zafrullah had also been involved in various social and political activities throughout his life and advocated for human rights, democracy and social justice in the country. He was chief adviser of Bhasani Anushari Parishad and was involved in the formation of the Jatiya Oikya Front in October 2018, ahead of the national polls, pressing for the demand of ensuring free and fair polls. Zafrullah Chowdhury passed away at the Gonoshasthaya Nagar Hospital in Dhaka on April 11, 2023. His body was buried on Gonoshashthya Kendra premises at Savar in Dhaka.

title: JSD to participate in national polls separately
body: The Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal-JSD led by ASM Abdur Rob, a partner of the Ganatantra Mancha, will participate separately in the next general elections scheduled for February 12 next year. An alliance of five political parties, the Ganatantra Mancha also include Nagorik Oikya, Revolutionary Workers Party of Bangladesh, Ganosamhati Andolan and Bhashani Onushari Parishad. JSD general secretary Shahid Uddin Mahmod Shapon at a press conference at the National Press Club in the capital Dhaka on Friday said that their party would take part in the forthcoming 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections separately. Shahid Uddin said that the JSD was taking part in movements jointly with the other partners in the Ganatantra Mancha for reforms and democratic transition of the country and his party believed that the continuation of national unity was required for achieving those. ‘Considering different circumstances, our party has decided to take part in the next general elections separately with the party symbol “Star”,’ Shahid Uddin added. The party’s senior vice-president, Tania Rob, said that the Bangladesh Nationalist Party had failed to show due respect to their alliance partners before the forthcoming general elections, which could be difficult for their policy of accumulation and democratic transition of the country would be difficult. Standing committee members of the party Mohammad Siraj Mia, KM Zabir, central leaders Mainur Rahman, Syed Belayet Hossain Belal and Mosharrraf Hossain Montu, among others, attended the press conference. The JSD has already given party nominations for 170 seats across the country for the forthcoming Jatiya Sangsad elections.

title: Hefazat leader threatens to erase Prothom Alo, The Daily Star
body: A Hefazat-e-Islam leader on Friday issued explicit threats against Prothom Alo and The Daily Star that the two newspapers would be ‘obliterated’ if their ‘hostility’ towards Islamist activists continued. Mir Farhad, international affairs secretary of Hefazat-e-Islam’s Rajshahi city unit, issued the threat while addressing a protest rally, demanding justice for Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi. The rally was held a week after the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star were burned down in Dhaka city on December 18, following Hadi’s death from bullet injuries at a Singapore hospital. Farhad said that Hadi’s activism had been ideological and cultural rather than militant, and that he had sought to counter Indian influence through discourse instead of violence. ‘He did not take up arms or call for an armed movement. He tried to build a cultural discourse against Indian hegemony,’ he said. He accused Prothom Alo and The Daily Star of promoting hostility towards Islamist activists. ‘When we try to confront them intellectually and build cultural resistance, we are destroyed before we can even rise,’ he stated. Farhad alleged that despite the government being formed ‘through bloodshed’it had failed to keep its promises and had again come under ‘Delhi’s shadow’. ‘The way you have gone on a killing spree on us, we will not spare you,’ he said, claiming support from ‘Tawhidi people’. Farhad also warned of further unrest if those arrested over recent attacks on media properties were not released. ‘If those detained are not freed amicably, the interim government will face severe consequences,’ he warned. Questioning the space for freedom of expression, he criticised the closure of online portal ‘Bangla Edition’ he said that the operating of the two newspapers showed that the same standard was not applied to all media. If Bangla Edition is closed for one offence, the editors of Prothom Alo and ‘Dilli Star’ should have been killed by hanging at the Gulistan crossing in Dhaka, the Hefazat-e-Islam leader said. He further claimed that despite their influence, the two newspapers had failed to protect their offices from public anger. ‘We have already removed bricks from Prothom Alo. If this continues, its name will be erased. These are not empty threats,’ he said. He also threatened other media outlets he accused of acting as foreign agents. Any media working for Indian or American hegemony and inciting violence against Muslims will not be allowed to exist, he said. Presided over by National Citizen Party district organisational secretary Nahidul Islam Sazu, the rally was addressed, among others, by NCP Rajshahi city member secretary Atikur Rahman, July Kathgora spokesperson Soaib Ahmed, and student leaders Ibnul Kaif and Maulana Md Masum.

title: Record potato output deepens growers’ misery
body: A record potato harvest has plunged thousands of farmers in the northern districts into a financial crisis, as prices have collapsed mainly due to a massive oversupply. Weak market regulation, lack of market forecast, and ineffective government intervention have also been blamed for the situation. Growers said that they were facing a rare and serious ‘double crisis’ at this time of year as potatoes stored in cold storages from the previous season lacked buyers, while they were forced to sell their early harvest at Tk 10–12 per kilogram—less than half of their production cost. Early potato varieties are produced with expectations of extra earning as usually the period of November–December is a time when potato prices go up just before new harvests hit the market. But farmers said that the market completely failed them this year. According to the Department of Agricultural Extension and growers in Rajshahi and Rangpur divisions, production costs for early varieties surged this season due to higher fertiliser prices, rising irrigation fuel costs and increased labour wages. Farmers estimated average production costs for early potato varieties at Tk 20–25 per kilogram, pitched against a bleak scenario of downhill wholesale prices. ‘I spent about Tk 22 to produce one kilogram of new potatoes (notun aloo), but had to sell them at Tk 10 per kilogram,’ said Abdul Malek, a farmer from Shibganj upazila in Bogura. ‘Traders are saying that old potatoes are flooding the market, so there is less demand for new ones,’ he added. Similar accounts have emerged from Rangpur and Nilphamari districts where farmers said that potatoes were being sold as cattle feed, with prices falling to Tk 7–10 per kilogram—barely enough to cover harvesting and transport costs. Last season a record 1.15 crore tonnes of potatoes were produced against an estimated domestic demand of around 90 lakh tonnes, leaving a surplus of more than 20 lakh tonnes, according to official data. This excess production has clogged the supply chain, with cold storages still holding large volumes even as the new harvest enters the market. Cold storage owners estimate that 10–15 per cent of last season’s stored potatoes remain unsold. ‘Farmers are not coming to release their potatoes because the market prices are lower than the cold storage rent,’ said Fazlur Rahman, general secretary of the Bangladesh Cold Storage Association’s Rajshahi chapter. Prices of potatoes at the cold storage gates have dropped to Tk 4–5 per kilogram, while storage rent stands at Tk 6.75 per kilogram. ‘If I take my potatoes out, I have to pay Tk 450 per sack in rent, but that sack is worth only Tk 200 in the market,’ said Lutfar Rahman, a trader from Tanore upazila in Rajshahi. He said that many farmers were not visiting cold storages at all and were instead urging storage owners to sell the potatoes on their behalf and deduct the rent, even if it meant total financial loss. The losses have pushed many farmers into debt, as a large number relied on bank loans and borrowing from micro-finance entities. Despite mounting distress, government intervention has remained largely ineffective. In August, the government announced a minimum price of Tk 22 per kilogram at the cold storage gate to protect growers, but farmers and traders said that the directive had not been implemented. The government also announced a plan to procure 50,000 tonnes of surplus potatoes to stabilise the market, but growers said that the plan also did not see the light of the day. ‘The decisions exist only on paper,’ said an angered Mizanur Rahman, a farmer from Tanore. Export prospects remain weak due to inconsistent quality standards, the absence of an organised cold-chain logistics system and bureaucratic delays, exporters and industry insiders said. Agricultural economists warn that prolonged losses could force farmers to scale back potato cultivation in the coming season, creating future supply instability. ‘If farmers reduce potato farming because of repeated losses, it could lead to sharp price volatility and supply shocks in the future,’ said Elias Hossain, a professor of economics at Rajshahi University.

title: EC demarcates four seats after polls schedule
body: The election commission has redefined the boundaries of four parliamentary constituencies in Pabna and Faridpur districts following the announcement of the election schedule, in compliance with an order of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court. The constituencies affected by the latest delimitation are Pabna-1, Pabna-2, Faridpur-2 and Faridpur-4, said EC director for public relations Md Ruhul Amin Mallik on Friday. The commission issued a gazette on Wednesday finalising the revised boundaries of the four seats. According to the gazette, Pabna-1, constituency no-68, now comprises Santhia upazila and parts of Bera upazila, including Bera municipality and the unions of Haturia Nakalia, Natun Varenga, Chakla and Kaitola. Pabna-2, constituency no-69, includes Sujanagar upazila and the remaining areas of Bera upazila, excluding Bera municipality and the four unions—Haturia Nakalia, Natun Varenga, Chakla and Kaitola. Faridpur-2, constituency no-212, now consists of Nagarkanda upazila and Saltha upazila. Faridpur-4, constituency no-214, has now included Bhanga upazila, Charbhadrasan upazila and Sadarpur upazila. Before the latest revision, Pabna-1 comprises only Santhia upazila, while Pabna-2 included Sujanagar and Bera upazilas. Faridpur-2 previously covered Nagarkanda, Saltha and two unions—Algi and Hamirdi—of Bhanga upazila, while Faridpur-4 consisted of Bhanga upazila, excluding Algi and Hamirdi unions, Charbhadrasan and Sadarpur upazilas. On September 4, the election commission finalised the delimitation of all 300 parliamentary constituencies, changing the boundaries of 46 seats across 16 districts. That move reduced the number of seats in Bagerhat from four to three, while increasing Gazipur’s representation from five to six seats. Just before the announcement of the election schedule, the commission had also revised constituency boundaries under court orders by reducing one seat in Gazipur and restoring one seat in Bagerhat. However, the latest changes—made after the schedule announcement—mark a rare precedent, as such post-schedule boundary revisions have not been seen in the recent elections. Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin on December 11 announced the schedule to arrange the 13th parliamentary election and the referendum on the July National Charter, Constitutional Reform, Implementation Order simultaneously on February 12 next. According to the election schedule, the deadline for the submission of nomination papers is December 29, while the last date for the withdrawal of candidature is January 20. The election campaign will start on January 22 and continue till 48 hours before the balloting period, 7:30am on February 10.

title: 46.52 lakh cases pending
body: Chief justice Syed Refaat Ahmed is scheduled to retire today, after presiding over some major reforms but leaving more than 46.52 lakh cases pending with the Supreme Court and the subordinate courts as of June 2025. Syed Refaat Ahmed became the 25th chief justice of Bangladesh on August 10, 2024. During his tenure, he prioritised judicial reform, the establishment of the Supreme Court Secretariat, the new law on the appointment of Supreme Court judges, and other related reform measures to ensure independence of the judiciary. According to Supreme Court statistics, the number of pending cases in all courts stood at 46,52,260 as of June 30, 2025. These include 37,200 cases with the Appellate Division, 6,16,453 cases with the High Court Division, and 39,98,805 cases in the lower courts. On 30 September 2024, nearly one month after he was appointed as the chief justice, the total number of pending cases was 44,43,510. At that time, there were 28,901 pending cases with the Appellate Division and 5,77,280 cases with the High Court Division. Thus the overall backlog went up by more than two lakh unsettled cases during his tenure. The disposal rate increased only in the lower court, according to the statistics. Several major political and constitutional cases were, however, disposed of by the Supreme Court during his period. On constitutional matters, the Supreme Judicial Council was restored and brought back into operation through the Appellate Division verdict in the 16th amendment case. The provision for a caretaker government during the Jatiya Sangsad elections was also restored, reviving the system to be applied from the 14th JS elections, according to another Appellate Division verdict. On political cases, the Appellate Division acquitted Jamaat-e-Islami leader ATM Azharul Islam, who had earlier been sentenced for war crimes, as well as Brahmanbaria war crimes convict Mobarak Hossain. Former prime minister and BNP chair Khaleda Zia, and the party’s acting chair Tarique Rahman were also acquitted by the Supreme Court in several cases in which they had been convicted earlier. Interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus was also cleared in a number of cases, including cases related to alleged money laundering and tax evasion. The Appellate Division could not dispose of a number of long-pending major cases. These include appeals in the 2009 BDR mutiny case and the 2014 Narayanganj seven-murder case. Appeals in the 2012 killing of tailor Biswajit Das in Old Dhaka also remain pending. The cases over the 2004 killing of Awami League leader Ahsan Ullah Master and the 2019 killing of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology student Abrar Fahad are also yet to be disposed of. The 2016 Holey Artisan attack case has likewise remained stuck for years. Syed Refaat took over as chief justice when over 42 lakh cases were pending. In a September 2024 speech, he said that the reduction in the case backlog was a big public demand. He also said that delays were caused due to too few judges, shortages of staff and courtrooms, and poor infrastructure. About 2,000 judges disposed of nearly 10 lakh cases each year, he noted. Between January 1 and March 31, 2025, the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court received 4,689 new cases, but managed to dispose of only 828 cases during the same period. This reflected a modest disposal rate of 17.7 per cent. As of March 31, the number of pending cases with the Appellate Division stood at 34,981, according to the SC quarterly statistics. The High Court Division witnessed comparatively higher activities during the period. A total of 28,111 cases were filed in the first quarter of 2025, of which 18,644 were disposed of, yielding a disposal rate of 66.3 per cent. Despite the improved rate of clearance, the High Court is still burdened with 5,99,126 pending cases at the end of March. In the lower-level judiciary, the year 2025 began with a staggering backlog of 38,96,430 pending cases. Over the first three months of the year, 3,80,060 new cases were filed and 1,80,874 cases restored. During the same period, the lower judiciary disposed of 3,04,333 cases, amounting to a disposal rate of only 6.8 per cent against the total caseload. However, compared only to the newly filed cases, the disposal rate was significantly higher at 80.1 per cent. As of March 31, 2025, the number of pending cases in the lower courts stood at 36,98,961. During the tenure of Justice Refaat Ahmed, the Supreme Court Secretariat was set up on the court premises, partially activating the secretariat. But the organogram for the secretariat is yet to be approved by the government. However, promotions, postings and transfers of lower court judges are still done by the president in consultation with the Supreme Court. Carrying out these functions receive secretariat support from the law ministry, as a final gazette about the Supreme Court Secretariat has not yet been issued. The SC secretariat Ordinance stipulates that the final gazette would be issued after making the secretariat functional. A key reform was the Supreme Court Judges Appointment Ordinance, 2025 which introduced a collegium system. Under this law, 25 additional High Court judges and two Appellate Division judges were appointed, and 23 additional judges were confirmed. The Supreme Judicial Council investigated allegations against several judges. Nine High Court judges were removed, resigned or were not retained following inquiries. Three more judges remain under review. The chief justice issued a 12-point directive to prevent corruption in the judiciary. However, details of actions taken under these directives were not made public. He also took administrative measures to improve case management. Two Appellate Division benches and two separate chamber courts were created, one for criminal matters and the other for writ matters. The chief justice heard cases three days a week and used the remaining days for administration and writing judgments. The chief justice promoted his reform roadmap both at home and abroad and visited Brazil, South Africa, Thailand, the UAE to share and promote the idea of judicial reform. He also campaigned for a separate budget and secretariat for the judiciary. However, some promised reforms remain incomplete. Full electronic court operations were not yet launched beyond a small pilot project on paperless document handling. A permanent merit-based list for promotions, postings, and transfers of lower court judges also could not be finalised. Supreme Court Bar Association president AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon said that the chief justice was honest and sincere and worked for judicial independence. He added that case disposal increased, but the backlog remained high because the number of judges is still too low. The Appellate Division’s Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury who was appointed the 26th chief justice of Bangladesh, is due to take oath of his office at a ceremony at the Bangabhaban at 10:30am on December 28. Justice Syed Refaat Ahmed, who was then a High Court judge, was appointed as the chief justice after his predecessor Obaidul Hassan resigned amid mass movement of the students. Five other Appellate Division judges also resigned immediately after the resignation of the then chief justice Obaidul Hasan.

title: NCP female leaders protest at move to ally with Jamaat
body: A group of female leaders of the National Citizen Party has sharply reacted to the party’s reported move to forge an electoral alliance with the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, a party that collaborated with the Pakistan occupation forces during the 1971 War of Independence. Several news reports on Thursday, along with the confirmation from some leaders of the NCP, formed by student and youth organisers of the July uprising in February this year, indicated that the party was considering a reform-centric alliance with Jamaat before the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections and a referendum, scheduled for February 12, 2026. The dissenting female leaders said that any alliance with Jamaat would amount to a betrayal of the spirit of the War of Independence as well as the democratic ethos of the July uprising. Speaking to New Age on Friday, they said that the move would undermine the party’s declared ideology and make political participation by women increasingly difficult. The leaders have meanwhile launched an internal campaign to collect signatures for a memorandum opposing the alliance, which they plan to submit to the party’s central leadership that is reportedly in favour of the move. By Friday evening, about 30 female leaders — some of whom have already received NCP nominations for the forthcoming parliamentary polls — had signed the memorandum, party insiders said. They said that senior joint convener Samantha Sharmin, joint conveners Nusrat Tabassum, Tajnuva Jabeen and Monira Sharmin, and senior joint member secretary Nahida Sarwar Chowdhury were among the signatories. Contacted for comment, the leaders declined to speak publicly, describing the issue as an internal party matter. ‘I will clarify my position if my party decides to join a Jamaat-led alliance,’ Samantha Sharmin told New Age. Nusrat Tabassum, Monira Sharmin and Nahida Sarwar Chowdhury echoed Samantha’s stance. The memorandum says, ‘The basis of our objection lies in our party’s declared ideology, our historical responsibility in relation to the July uprising, and questions of democratic ethics.’ The document further alleges that Jamaat and its student wing, Islami Chhatra Shibir, have engaged in divisive political activities, espionage and sabotage within other parties, attempted to shift blame for various misdeeds onto the NCP, rigged student union elections, and spread false narratives about student power since the July uprising. ‘Through their online forces, they have also attempted to defame the character of female members of the NCP and our student organisation. Above all, the growing risk of religion-centric social fascism has emerged as an ominous signal for the country’s future,’ the memorandum reads. The signatories said Jamaat’s political history — particularly its role during the 1971 War of Independence and its stance on the genocide and other wartime crimes — was fundamentally incompatible with Bangladesh’s democratic values and the NCP’s core principles. They also noted that NCP chief coordinator Nasiruddin Patwary had repeatedly declared the party’s intention to contest all 300 parliamentary seats independently. Citing recent party activities, the memorandum said that the NCP had sold nomination forms to about 1,500 aspirants nationwide and had already nominated about 125 candidates. ‘An alliance with Jamaat would create confusion and disappointment among many of our activists and supporters, especially among the younger generation and ordinary citizens who support new politics,’ it said. Talking about the matter, Syeda Nilima Dola, NCP’s Faridpur coordinator and a prospective candidate for the Faridpur-3 constituency, said that she was deeply concerned by the discussions on seat-sharing with Jamaat. ‘Such seat-sharing-based politics would betray the spirit of the July uprising and make women’s political activism extremely difficult in the future,’ she said.

title: Jamaat keeps exploiting religion to woo voters
body: The Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami is allegedly using religious sentiment as a political tool to attract voters ahead of the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections slated for February 12 next year. Grassroots leaders of the party are mainly campaigning among voters saying that it was their religious duty to vote for the Jamaat, or else their faith in the Almighty would not survive. Many of such election campaign contents have gone viral, drawing huge criticism and fear of exploiting religious belief in the election. Political analysts, rights activists, and civil society leaders said that such practices could undermine democratic norms and fuel social polarisation. They said that the Jamaat’s voter mobilisation strategy heavily relied on invoking religious identity, which they warned could destabilise the pre-election environment by creating fear, coercion and communal tension. They alleged that the Jamaat was deliberately exploiting faith and religious emotion to enhance and consolidate its voter base while using religion as a shield to deflect criticism of its political agenda and historical record. There are growing allegations that Jamaat activists and supporters are telling voters that casting ballots for Jamaat candidates will ensure their entry into jannat (heaven), while failure to vote ‘in favour of Islam’ in the upcoming election would put their iman (faith) at risk. At a rally in Kutubdia of Cox’s Bazar, Jamaat leader and Kutubdia Samadia Alim Madrasa principal Mohammad Abu Musa defended the statement that Jamaat was ‘selling tickets to heaven.’ Invoking religious scripture, he said that Allah spoke of selling jannat in exchange for sacrifice and asked rhetorically, ‘If the Jamaat does not sell the ticket to heaven, then who will?’ At another rally, Jamaat supporter Mohammad Hafijur Rahman sought votes for Jamaat-nominated candidate Mubarak Hossain in the Comilla-5 constituency, saying that if people did not vote ‘in favour of Islam’ in the upcoming election, their faith would not survive. Asked, former Jahangirnagar University teacher and rights activist professor Anu Muhammad said that the Jamaat had always used religion for political purposes and even took pride in doing so. He described this as a systematic exploitation of people’s religious sentiments. ‘The Jamaat can’t offer meaningful political or economic programmes and carries a major historical crime from 1971. To cover up that past, it continues to use religion,’ he said. Anu Muhammad also said that the way Jamaat presented religion gave it a fascist character because rejecting Jamaat politics was made to appear as rejecting Islam itself. ‘They promote the idea that Islam must be practised only in the way they define, which is a fascist mindset,’ he said, adding that the Jamaat used religion as a shield to pursue its core political and corporate interests. He said that the Jamaat sustained discriminatory politics through the use of religion and that its consequences were seen in 1971. ‘These are still visible today,’ he added. Such misuse of religion, he warned, is dangerous for society, including for people who are themselves religious. According to Communist Party of Bangladesh former president Mujahidul Islam Selim, the election code clearly prohibits the use of religious sentiment in election campaigning. He urged the Election Commission to take strong action against violations involving money, muscle power, administrative manipulation, and communal provocation. The Jamaat, Selim said, lost its moral and political legitimacy on December 16, 1971, when Pakistan surrendered along with its auxiliary civil and paramilitary forces, which, he said, included Jamaat. However, he said, both the Awami League and the Bangladesh Nationalist Party later enabled the Jamaat to return to politics despite that historical record. Transparency International Bangladesh executive director Iftekharuzzaman said that money, muscle, and religion had long been the dark tools of political capital in Bangladesh. ‘When people’s religious sentiments are exploited through deceptive interpretations of religion, it is not only unethical but also a form of religious sacrilege,’ he said. He added that such practices contradicted the July Charter, which commits Bangladesh to being a multi-religious country where all citizens enjoy full religious freedom. ‘Creating fear and intimidation by playing the religious card for political gain is blatantly deceitful,’ he said. Bangladesh Rashtra Songskar Andolon president Hasnat Kayum said that the Jamaat was simultaneously exploiting religion and attempting to co-opt leaders of the July uprising to expand its political base. By switching between religion, coercion and the July movement whenever it suits its interests, the Jamaat is breaking established political norms, which could create instability and uncertainty and push Bangladesh toward a serious future crisis, he said. Among other examples of using religion by the Jamaat, Jamaat candidates in Rajshahi and Chapainawabganj have openly framed their campaigns around establishing Islamic governance. New Age staff correspondent in Rajshahi reported that at a campaign meeting in Char Ashariadaha Union under Godagari upazila recently, the Jamaat’s Rajshahi-1 JS polls candidate professor Mujibur Rahman urged voters to support the party’s ‘scale’ symbol, saying Qur’anic law could only be implemented through state power. He said that although Bangladesh had ‘hundreds of thousands of huffaz and khatibs,’ Islamic laws had not been established because they did not fight ‘as soldiers or mujahids’ to implement them. He told the crowd that those who rejected Qur’anic guidance were ‘kafir’, ‘zalim’ and ‘fasiq’, which he said were ‘Allah’s words’, adding that the ‘light of the Qur’an’ must enter parliament so that no ‘man-made law’ could operate. He also urged supporters to mobilise neighbours and women voters, saying that on the Day of Judgement people would be asked whether they voted for ‘Allah’s law or man-made law.’ In Chapainawabganj, Jamaat central working committee member and Rajshahi city amir professor Keramat Ali, the party’s nominee for Chapainawabganj-1, told voters during door-to-door campaigning that the country’s problems could be solved if state affairs were run according to Islamic principles. He criticised corruption, mismanagement and inequality, claiming that Islamic governance had historically eliminated social deprivation, claiming that the Jamaat would soon publish its election manifesto focused on honesty and accountability. Similar campaigning is being reported from Sylhet. New Age staff correspondent in Sylhet reported that Abdur Razzak, a farmer of Mollarchak village in Dakshin Surma upazila, said Jamaat-e-Islami and Islami Chhatra Shibir leaders had repeatedly asked him and his neighbours to vote for the Jamaat, saying it was a religious duty of Muslims. Shahin Ahmed, a grocer in Satpara village of Biswanath upazila, said that the Jamaat activists told them that Islamic laws would be introduced if the party was voted to power. ‘They told us that the Jamaat would win this election and all Muslims must take part in establishing the law of Allah and the rule of righteous people,’ he said. Among many other similar statements available on social media, the Jamaat nominated candidate Iqbal Hossain for the Pabna-5 constituency said that ‘choosing the leader of a Muslim state is the foremost obligation (farz) which is even more important than saying prayers, fasting, performing Hajj and giving Zakat’. Islamic speaker Amir Hamza, also a Jamaat candidate for the Kushtia-3 seat, recently commented that casting a vote in the election will earn the reward for the prayers of 18 crore people. Contacted, Jamaat assistant secretary general Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair on Friday told New Age that the party did not allow the use of religion in election campaigning. He said that the party was centrally monitoring the issue and warned that strict action would be taken against anyone found using religion for electoral purposes.

title: Mild cold wave grips parts of country
body: A mild cold wave was sweeping across several districts while the rest of the country shivered with moderately low temperatures on Friday, hitting poor people the most. The Bangladesh Meteorological Department in its Friday evening bulletin forecasted that the cold spell would continue for several days. According to the BMD bulletin, a mild cold wave was affecting Jashore, Chuadanga, Gopalganj, Rajshahi, Pabna, Sirajganj and Nilphamari. Till 6:00pm on Friday, Jashore recorded the lowest temperature at 9C while the highest temperature 31C was recorded at Teknaf in Cox’s Bazar, according to the bulletin. New Age correspondent in Jashore reported that a very few people were seen outside their homes on Friday, but low income people such as day labourers and rickshaw-pullers had to do their jobs amid pinching cold. Amir Hossain, a rickshaw-puller, said that he was unable to earn expected income due to lack of passengers. According to the local met office, Chuadanga recorded this season’s lowest 9.6C of temperature on Friday, the United News of Bangladesh reported. People, particularly, low income group, children and senior citizens, suffered the most due to the intense cold while the district sadar hospital witnessed increased number of cold-affected patients. Meanwhile, the Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha reported that residents of char areas along the Brahmaputra, Teesta, Dudhkumar, Gangadhar and Dharla rivers experienced severe hardship, compounded by a lack of warm clothing and limited income opportunities. Shah Alam, a boatman at Jatrapur Brahmaputra Ghat at Kurigram Sadar, said that the fog on the river had made rowing boat risky. ‘There has been no income for two days,’ he said. According to the BMD bulletin, moderate to thick fog might occur at places over the country during mid night to morning and it may continue till noon at places. ‘Air navigation, inland river transport and road communication may disrupt temporarily due to thick fog,’ the bulletin said. The BBS reported that all ferry movement on the Paturia-Daulatdia and Aricha-Kazirhat river routes had been suspended due to poor visibility caused by dense fog over the Padma and Jamuna rivers. Assistant general manager Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Corporation at Paturia Ghat, Abdus Salam, said that ferry services on the Paturia-Daulatdia route were suspended from 12:00am of Friday to avoid any untoward incidents. New Age staff correspondent in Rajshahi reported that Rajshahi was shrouded in dense fog from early Friday morning as the season’s lowest temperature intensified a cold spell, disrupting normal life and reducing visibility across the city. Sanjay Kumar, a resident of the Budhpara Railway slum, said that the cold had worsened over the past few days, accompanied by chilling wind that made conditions unbearable. ‘Standing in the wind feels like our clothes are getting wet,’ he said, adding that neither the government nor private organisations had distributed blankets in the area so far this winter. New Age correspondent in Rangpur reported that due to the bone-chilling cold over the Rangpur region for the past four days, traffic on the highways was disrupted, compelling vehicles to move on the road switching the headlights on even at midday. Saifur Rhaman, a driver of SR Travels, said that driving became tough and risky on the highways. Farmers, however, in different areas of the region said that crops might be affected if the cold wave persisted for days. Habibullah Miah,60, a farmer at Nabdiganj bazar in Rangpur sadar upazila, said that agriculture, including boro seedbeds and potato fields, would be badly affected amid the prevailing cold weather. Rangpur deputy commissioner Mohammad Enamul Ahsan said that some 20,000 pieces of blankets were distributed among the cold-hit people in eight upazilas under the district. A requisition letter was sent for more blanket allocation to the ministry concerned, he added. New Age correspondent in Pabna reported that the seedbed of boro rice was turning reddish amid extreme cold in the district. Officials of the district’s Department of Agricultural Extension advised farmers to cover the seedbeds with polythene. At Pabna Sadar Hospital, the number of children and elderly patients was increasing. Quoting Rafiqul Islam, assistant director of the hospital, the correspondent reported that about 500 patients were being treated for various issues, including respiratory problems, fever and diarrhoea.

title: 24 high-powered electric detonators recovered in Sunamganj border
body: The Border Guard Bangladesh recovered 24 high-powered electric explosive detonators from a border point at Tahirpur upazila in Sunamganj district on Friday morning. BGB 28 Battalion commander Lieutenant Colonel AKM Zakaria Qaudir confirmed to New Age that the detonators were recovered. He said that based on a tip-off, a patrol team of Charagaon border outpost of the BGB 28 Battalion conducted a drive in Maizhati area at Tahirpur upazila in the morning. ‘The BGB team in the drive recovered the detonators wrapped in polythene and hidden under tree branches,’ the battalion commander said, adding that the recovered detonators could be used to make high-powered improvised explosive devices. A preliminary investigation predicted that the explosives were smuggled in the country through the border to use in subversive activities in the country.

title: No legal bar for Tarique to be voter: EC
body: Election commissioner Abdur Rahmanel Masud on Friday said that there was no legal obstacle for Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman to be enlisted as a voter. Talking to BSS on Friday, the election commissioner said the election commission has the authority to enlist any individual as a voter at any time under Section 15 of the Voter List Act. ‘According to Section 15 of the Voter List Act, the election commission can include any person in the voter list at any time. In this case, there is no legal barrier,’ Masud said. BNP standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed after a meeting with the chief election commissioner on December 22 informed the press that Tarique Rahman would complete all formalities related to voter registration and preparation of the National Identity Card on December 27 to formally take part in the electoral process.

title: HADI MURDER: 2 sent to jail, Shahbagh blocked demanding justice
