body: A Dhaka court on Friday sent two accused to jail in connection with the murder of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi. Meanwhile, leaders and activists of Inquilab Mancha, along with general students and public, blocked Shahbagh, demanding justice for Sharif Osman Bin Hadi, who died on December 18 after a shooting attack days earlier. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ripon Hossain passed the order as the police produced the two, Sivion Dio, 32, and Sanjay Chisim, 22, in court and appealed to keep them in jail custody after their two rounds of remand ended. On the day, the protester brought out a procession from the Dhaka University Central Mosque and marched to Shahbagh, where they blocked the road from about 3:00pm until about 8:30pm. Shahbagh police officer-in-charge Md Moniruzzaman said that the protesters blocked Shahbagh crossing, halting vehicular movement in the area for about five hours. At the time of filing this report at 10:00pm, vehicular movement to and from Dhaka University was closed, while some vehicles were allowed to move in the other directions around Shahbagh crossing, New Age Dhaka University correspondent reported. At around 7:30pm during the sit-in, the platform’s central member secretary Abdullah Al Zaber announced that the blockade at Shahbagh crossing would continue on Saturday. He said that people from across the country were heading to the capital to join the blockade by morning. ‘We will not leave until justice is ensured,’ he vowed. The organisation also demanded formation of a fast-track judicial tribunal for the trial of the killing of Hadi within a maximum of 30 working days, inclusion of internationally-recognised investigation agencies, such as, the FBI or Scotland Yard to ensure a neutral probe, and resignation of the home and law advisers. On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head from close quarters in the capital while conducting his electioneering as an independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency. After treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital and Evercare Hospital in the city, he was flown to Singapore for advanced treatment but there he succumbed to injuries on the night of December 18. Law enforcers have so far arrested at least 11 people for their suspected involvement in the attack on Hadi, but the main suspects are yet to be arrested and are believed to have fled to India.

title: Bangladesh shipping adviser announces compensation for launch accident victims
body: The Bangladesh interim government shipping adviser, Brigadier General, retd, M Sakhawat Hossain, on Friday said the government will provide Taka 1.5 lakh to each of the families of the persons died in a lunch accident at Chandpur on Friday. Families of each injured person will get Taka 50,000, he said while talking to reporters after inspecting the damaged launches at Sadarghat in the capital. ‘Today’s incident was sad one. Among all the types of transport, the river route is the safest, yet any accident might happen,’ he said. He shared his personal experience in water route journey saying, ‘I myself travel by waterway, and I have also noticed that many vessels don’t use light while operating in the dark at night.’ An eight-member committee has been formed by the ministry to probe into the incident and the authorities concerned were asked to arrest those responsible for the launch accident, he said. The shipping adviser said the real cause behind the incident could be known after investigation. The adviser said several instructions have already been given. ‘No launch will operate in fog at night and lights must be used if parked anywhere at night. Bulkheads will not operate before 8 am this season, and those who violate the instructions will be arrested.’ In the future, he said, if any launch drivers do not operate the launch properly or do not use lights at night or do not follow the instructions, their route permits and licenses will be canceled. Four people were killed in a collision between two passenger launches—Zakir Samrat-3 and Adventure-9 amid dense fog on the Meghna River in the Harina area of Chandpur Sadar. The deceased were identified as Abdul Gani, 38, Md Saju, 45, Md. Hanif, 60 and Mosa Rina, 35. All of them hail from Bhola district.

title: Two missing in launch-bulkhead collision in N’ganj
body: Two workers went missing after a collision between a sand-laden bulkhead and a passenger launch in the River Buriganga in Fatullah upazila of Narayanganj Friday morning. The incident occurred at around 6:15am in Dharmaganj area when the Dhaka-bound launch Sundarban-16 rammed into the stationary bulkhead MV Kashfa Sneha, inspector Akibul Islam, in-charge of Pagla river police outpost, said. The missing workers are Md Zahurul Islam Shakil, 25, of Patuakhali, and Md Hasan, 20, of Rajapur in Jhalakathi. Three other workers on board managed to swim ashore safely. Members of coast guard, fire service and Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority jointly launched rescue operations shortly after the incident, said BIWTA assistant director Kamrul Hasan. Inspector Akibul said dense fog may have caused the accident in the morning. On December 14, a similar bulkhead sank in the same area following a collision, though no casualties were reported then.

title: Fire breaks out at rooftop warehouse of shopping complex in Gulistan
body: A fire burnt a warehouse on the rooftop of an eight-storey shopping complex at Gulistan in Dhaka on Friday. The Fire Service and Civil Defence said that nine fire engines contained the fire by 7:00pm which broke out at about 5:15pm at Khaddar Bazar Shopping Complex at the Gulistan zero point. Warehouse inspector Md Anwarul Islam reported no casualties. The cause of fire and damage could not be immediately established.

title: Tarique pays tribute at Zia’s grave, National Memorial
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chair Tarique Rahman on Friday paid tribute to his father, the late president Ziaur Rahman, at his grave at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in the capital Dhaka and later visited the National Memorial at Savar, on the outskirts of the capital, to honour the Liberation War martyrs. Tarique arrived at the mausoleum amid cheering crowds at about 4:40pm and laid a wreath shortly before 5:00pm to his father’s grave on Friday after his homecoming in the previous day. He later took part in prayers at the graveside. Tarique returned to the country on Thursday after ending 17 years of forced exile in the United Kingdom, receiving a roaring welcome from more than a million people. BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, standing committee members Mirza Abbas, Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Nazrul Islam Khan, Salahuddin Ahmed, Selima Rahman and Hafizuddin Ahmed, as well as senior joint secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, among others, were present at Zia’s grave on Friday. Tarique paid tribute at his father’s grave after 19 years, having last done so on September 1, 2006, on the occasion of the BNP’s founding anniversary, when he was serving as the party’s senior joint secretary general. After paying tribute, Tarique stood silently for some time in front of his father’s grave. As he entered the area, BNP leaders and activists lined both sides of the road, greeting him with slogans to mark his arrival. Tarique set off for Ziaur Rahman’s grave from his Gulshan residence at about 3:00pm, travelling in a red-and-green coloured bus — the same vehicle he had used a day earlier to go from the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in the capital to a public reception venue along the Purbachal Expressway, known as the 300 Feet Road, after returning from London. From early morning, BNP leaders and activists, along with members of its affiliated organisations, gathered in the area of Zia’s grave. Law enforcement agencies imposed tight security across the area, with traffic halted on Lake Road beside the Jatiya Sangsad complex from Friday morning. Members of the army, police, Rapid Action Battalion, Armed Police Battalion and Border Guard Bangladesh were deployed in and around the grave area to maintain security. After paying tribute at the grave of his father, Tarique set off for the National Memorial at Savar to pay homage to the martyrs of the 1971 Liberation War. According to protocol, tribute must be paid at the main altar of the memorial before sunset. However, due to massive crowds along the route, it was not possible for Tarique to reach the memorial before sunset. Consequently, BNP standing committee members Gayeshwar Chandra Roy and Abdul Moyeen Khan paid homage on his behalf at about 5:00pm. Amid enthusiastic cheers from the crowds along the way, Tarique reached Savar at about 10:00pm. To ensure a safe and smooth visit, ample security personnel, including police and BGB, had been deployed at the Savar National Memorial and at key points along the Dhaka–Aricha highway. After concluding the reception on Thursday, Tarique visited his ailing mother and former prime minister Khaleda Zia at her bedside at Evercare Hospital, where she has been undergoing treatment for more than a month and remained in a critical condition. Tarique had previously been sentenced in several cases, including to a life-term imprisonment, and faced numerous other charges, most of which were filed during the 2007–08 military-backed caretaker government. He was arrested during an anti-corruption drive in March 2007 and released on bail on September 3, 2008, after which he travelled to London on September 11 for medical treatment and remained there. Following the end of the Awami League’s 16-year rule on August 5, 2024 amid a mass uprising, the High Court acquitted Tarique of all cases filed during both the caretaker government and Awami League administration periods, clearing the legal hurdles to his return.

title: Shahbagh blocked demanding justice for Hadi
body: Leaders and activists of Inquilab Mancha, along with general students and members of the public, blocked the Shahbagh intersection on Friday demanding justice for Sharif Osman Bin Hadi. The protesters brought out a procession from the Dhaka University Central Mosque and marched to Shahbagh, where they staged a sit-in. Officer-in-Charge of Shahbagh Police Station Md Moniruzzaman said the demonstrators blocked the intersection at around 3:00pm. Vehicular movement on the busy road remained suspended as of 4:30pm, he added. Hadi was shot in the head on December 12 while conducting electioneering in the capital as an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency. The attack occurred a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections and a national referendum, slated for February 12, 2026. He initially underwent surgery at Dhaka Medical College Hospital before being transferred to Evercare Hospital. For advanced treatment, he was later airlifted to Singapore, where he succumbed to his injuries on the night of December 18. Law enforcement agencies have so far arrested at least 10 people in connection with the attack. However, the main suspects are yet to be detained and are believed to have fled to India.

title: Security tightened at Zia Udyan, Savar National Memorial ahead of Tarique’s visit
body: Security has been tightened at key points along the Dhaka-Aricha highway, including Zia Udyan and the Savar National Memorial, ahead of BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman’s scheduled visit to the area. A sufficient number of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel have been deployed to maintain law and order, said Shariful Islam, Public Relations Officer (PRO) of BGB headquarters. According to the programme, following Jumma prayers, Tarique Rahman will visit the grave of BNP founder and former president Ziaur Rahman. He is later expected to pay homage to the martyrs of the Liberation War at the National Memorial in Savar. Tarique Rahman returned to Bangladesh on Thursday morning after nearly 17 years in exile. Upon his arrival, he called BNP Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus expressed gratitude for the arrangements and security provided during his return. The day witnessed a massive public turnout, as the reception at the 300 Feet venue in the capital drew enthusiastic party leaders, activists and supporters.

title: 6 dead in 2 waterway accidents amid dense fog
body: At least six people were killed and several others injured in two separate incidents of vessel collisions in the Meghna River in Chandpur and in the Buriganga River in Narayanganj in dense fog early Friday. Of the deceased, four were killed after two passenger launches collided in the Meghna while two others were killed after a passenger launch rammed a sand-laden cargo vessel anchored in the Buriganga in Narayanganj, New Age correspondents in Barishal and Narayanganj reported. The police seized MV Adventure-9, one of the two launches involved in the Meghna River collision, and arrested four of its crew members in Jhalakathi, New Age correspondent in Barishal reported. Barishal river police superintendent Nazmul Haque said, ‘The MV Adventue-9 launch has been seized and four crew members have been arrested.’ The police were investigating the incident to determine how the accident had occurred, he added. The accident happened at about 2:30am when MV Zakir Samrat-3, which had started from Ghosher Hat under the Dularhat police station, collided head-on with MV Adventure-9, in the Meghna river channel, said Shohag Rana, officer-in-charge of the Sadarghat river police station. Chandpur river police station officer-in-charge ASM Iqbal said that the river police received the information about the collision at about 3:00am but found no launch on the spot after they reached it as both the launches had already left the area. However, Barishal-bound MV Adventure-9 was seized later in the morning in Jhalakathi, he said, adding that the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority would file a case over the incident. The Chandpur river police OC said that the four bodies were handed over to their respective families from the capital Dhaka. All the deceased hailed from Bhola district, according to the river police. The deceased are Abdul Gani, 38, son of Sirazul Bepari, from Lalmohon upazila in Bhola, Md Saju, 45, son of Md Kalu Kha, also from Lalmohon upazila, Md Hanif, son of Amir Hossain, from Char Fasson upazila in Bhola, and Mosammat Rina, 35, daughter of late Moktar Hossain, from Lalmohon upazila. Meanwhile, shipping adviser retired Brigadier General M Sakhawat Hossain announced that the government would provide Taka 1.5 lakh to each of the families of the persons who died in the accident. On the other hand, each of the families of the injured persons will get Taka 50, 000,’ he said while talking to reporters after inspecting the damaged launches at Sadarghat in the capital. Meanwhile, an eight-member committee was formed by the ministry to probe into the incident and the authorities concerned were asked to arrest those responsible for the accident, he further said. Witnesses said that MV Zakir Samrat-3, which began its journey from Ghosher Hat in Bhola for Dhaka, was passing by Haimchar shortly after 2:00am. At the same time, MV Adventure-9, carrying passengers who had attended the Bangladesh Nationalist Party meeting to mark the homecoming of Tarique Rahman in Dhaka, was returning to Barishal from the opposite direction. Due to extremely poor visibility caused by dense fog across the river, Adventure-9 reportedly lost its bearings and rammed Zakir Samrat-3 at a high speed. Passengers further said that Zakir Samrat-3 was left severely damaged and began sinking mid-river. Another Dhaka-bound launch, MV Karnaphuli-9, arrived from Bhola and rescued many passengers before continuing towards the capital. At Fatullah of Narayanganj, sand-laden cargo vessel MB Kasfa Shahana sank immediately after being hit by Dhaka-bound launch Sundarban-16 also in dense fog at about 6:00am, said Akibul Islam, in-charge of the Pagla river police outpost. ‘The incident occurred when workers were sleeping inside the cargo vessel. Three workers managed to escape out of the vessel while sinking but two others went missing,’ he said. Later, the bodies of the two persons were recovered, he said, adding that the accident was believed to have occurred due to dense fog. The deceased are identified as Johrul Islam Shakil, 25, and Md Hasan, 20. Meanwhile, another collision took place between Barishal-bound MV M Khan-7 and Chandpur-bound passenger launch Eagle-4 in the Meghna River at around 12:00am on Friday. However, no casualties were reported in the accident. At least 57 accidents involving river vessels, including passenger carriers in inland waterways, occurred with 31 deaths reported, 17 missing and 59 injured in 2024, according to data presented by the National Committee to Protect Shipping, Roads and Railways. At least 29 people were killed in 58 accidents in 2023 while 24 killed in 47 accidents in 2022, according to the data. Besides, more than 2,000 cases related to vessel capsizes and launch accidents remained pending with the country’s lone marine court for years as of 2021, according to the court officials.

title: Mercury dips to 13
body: Mercury dips to 13.5°C in Bangladesh capital Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, recorded the season’s lowest temperature on Friday, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department. Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, recorded the season’s lowest temperature on Friday, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department. Only 27.24 per cent of citizens say they can influence government decisions at any level, according to the final report on the Citizen Perception Survey 2025... A young man was beaten and stabbed to injuries after being tied to an electric pole at Shibganj upazila in Chapainawabganj on Wednesday evening, allegedly due to an internal feud... Chinese ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen has said that media exchange plays a vital role in understanding the civilisation and culture of both countries... A crude bomb was exploded near Malibagh intersection in the capital Dhaka on Thursday, a day after a youth was killed in a crude bomb explosion at Moghbazar on Wednesday... Two women and a kid, including a grandmother and her granddaughter, were killed after being hit by a train at Kaliganj in Gazipur on Thursday... The participants in the primary school assistant teacher recruitment test can start downloading their admit cards from government website from tomorrow (Saturday)... Another body was recovered on Thursday, two days after the clashes and gunfire between two rival groups over control and dominance of a char at Hatiya in Noakhali, raising the number of deaths to six in the incident on December 23... The Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami is allegedly using religious sentiment as a political tool to attract voters ahead of the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections slated for February 12 next year.

title: NCTB makes all 2026 textbooks available online
body: The National Curriculum and Textbook Board uploads and makes all free textbooks for 2026 academic year available online on Sunday amid concern of not being able to distribute all the books among the students on January 1. From Sunday online versions of all 647 Bangla and English versions of textbooks are available on the NCTB website — www.nctb.gov.bd. For the first time since 2010, NCTB this year uploaded the online versions of textbboks before distributing these among the students on January 1. Regarding this, the board on the day held ‘Uploading of online version of textbooks for the 2026 academic year to the website’. Education adviser Professor Chowdhury Rafiqul Abrar and primary and mass education adviser professor Bidhan Ranjan Roy Podder are scheduled to attend the event at NCTB Bhaban in the capital. According to the board officials the students can read books before the starting of 2026 due to availability of their online version. Many students, especially of Class VII and VIII are unlikely to get all textbooks on the first day following the government’s cancellation of some tenders for printing books.

title: BNP acting chairman Tarique collects nomination paper for Dhaka-17
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman on Sunday collected his nomination paper to contest the upcoming national election from the Dhaka-17 constituency. On behalf of Tarique, BNP chairperson’s private secretary ABM Abdur Sattar collected the nomination form from the office of Dhaka divisional commissioner Sharf Uddin Ahmed Choudhury at about 11:10am, said BNP media cell member Sayrul Kabir Khan. Earlier on Saturday night, BNP Standing Committee member Salahuddin Ahmed told UNB that Tarique Rahman would contest the 13th parliamentary election, scheduled for February 12 next year, from two constituencies — Bogura-6 and Dhaka-17. ‘Our party’s acting chairman Tarique Rahman will contest the election from two seats. One is Bogura-6 and the other is Dhaka-17. This is a party decision,’ Salahuddin said. Responding to questions about campaign activities suggesting that Bangladesh Jatiya Party chairman Andaleeve Rahman Partho, a BNP ally, would contest from Dhaka-17, Salahuddin said Partho would not run from that seat. ‘He will contest the election from his home constituency, Bhola-1, using his party’s own election symbol,’ the BNP leader said.

title: Religious minorities want polls manifestos include their rights, safety
body: Leaders of the Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council at a discussion on Saturday called on the political parties to include issues of ensuring rights and safety of religious minorities in their election manifestos for the general elections scheduled for February 12 next year. The organisation arranged the discussion on human rights of minorities, at the CIRDAP auditorium in the capital Dhaka. The president of the organisation, Nirmal Rozario, chaired the discussion. Economist Debapriya Bhattachariya said that the use of religion in politics was not acceptable for healthy politics and it would loosen the social bonding in the society. ‘In our country, religion-based politics has increased during the interim government that assumed office after the victory of July uprising past year. Such a rise in religion-based politics has created complexities in politics in the country and put the forthcoming Jatiya Sangsad elections at risk,’ Debapriya said. Transparency International Bangladesh executive director Iftekharuzzaman said that it was unfortunate that in the country people were facing attacks for their religious identities and grabbing their land and wealth. The Human Rights Commission has failed to ensure rights and safety of the minorities, he said. He called on the interim government to take immediate steps to ensure rights and safety of the minority people in the country. Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council acting general secretary Monindra Kumar Nath read out the keynote at the programme. In the keynote, he said that in 11 months of this year, 2,673 incidents of attacks on minorities happened across the country and 90 minority people were killed. He called on all political parties participating in the forthcoming general elections to include the issues of ensuring rights and safety of the minority people of the country in their election manifestos. He also demanded that the political parties should give 10 per cent of nominations for the national polls to minority people across the country. He also demanded ensuring safety and securities of the minorities before the elections and on the day of vote casting on February 12, 2026.

title: NCTB to make available all 2026 textbooks online today
body: The National Curriculum and Textbook Board is set to upload and make all free textbooks for 2026 academic year available online today (Sunday) amid concern of not being able to distribute all the books among the students on January 1. From today online versions of all 647 Bangla and English versions of textbooks will be available on the NCTB website – www.nctb.gov.bd. Regarding this, the board today will hold ‘Uploading of online version of textbooks for the 2026 academic year to the website’. Education adviser professor Chowdhury Rafiqul Abrar and primary and mass education adviser professor Bidhan Ranjan Roy Podder are scheduled to attend the event today morning at NCTB Bhaban in the capital. According to the board officials the students can read books before the starting of 2026 due to availability of their online version. Many students, especially of Class VII and VIII are unlikely to get all textbooks on the first day following the government’s cancellation of some tenders for printing books. ‘We cannot give all textbooks to the students on January 1,’ NCTB chairman Md Mahbubul Hoque Patwary told New Age on December 24, adding, ‘we hope that we can give all books by January.’ Due to re-tender for a portion of books, they have to give the printers time till January 22 next year, he mentioned. The situation has arisen even though the interim government from time to time this year said that all students would get free textbooks on January 1. On December 16, the education ministry announced that the NCTB had successfully completed printing and distribution activities for the textbooks for the pre-primary and primary levels (Class I to V) for 2026. However, as per the board, about 93 per cent of books for the ibtedayi students were printed and distributed at district and upazila levels before the final distribution till Tuesday. Currently, the board, under the education ministry, is mandated to formulate, develop, renew, monitor and reform the curriculum, syllabus and textbooks, and print, publish, distribute and market textbooks for the pre-primary to secondary level students. The government has been distributing free textbooks for the pre-primary to secondary level students since 2010 through the board. The board faced huge criticism earlier this year for failing to provide textbooks on time. After much delay, all students got textbooks by March, three months after their classes started. Following this, the board decided to start the initiatives of printing textbooks for 2026 early this year and set a target to print about 30.02 crore books by November 30 this year. According to the NCTB, the board is scheduled to print 60.67 lakh pre-primary, 7.90 crore for Class I-V, 1.85 lakh ethnic minority for groups, 6.43 lakh additional pre-primary (4+), 4.43 crore for Class VI, 4.15 crore for Class VII, 4.02 crore for Class VIII, 5.7 crore for Class IX-X, 3.11 crore Ibtedayi, and 6,026 Braille method textbooks this year. Till December 23, as per the NCTB, 93.27 per cent of ibtedayi, 66.35 per cent of Class VI, 31.03 per cent of Class VII, 9.86 per cent of Class VIII and 68.14 per cent of Class IX books were distributed. All pre-primary and primary levels books were printed and distributed among district and upazila authorities concerned.

title: Tajnuva Jabeen, joint convener of the National Citizen Party, resigned from the party on Sunday, expressing strong objec
body: Tajnuva Jabeen, joint convener of the National Citizen Party, resigned from the party on Sunday, expressing strong objections to the manner in which its electoral alliance was formed. She made the announcement in a post on her verified Facebook account. In the post, Tajnuva said many were assuming her objection stemmed from ideological or gender-related concerns regarding the alliance with Jamaat-e-Islami, but stressed that the real issue was ‘far more alarming.’ ‘What is more frightening than ideology is the process through which this has been done. It is being labelled as political strategy or an electoral alliance. I would call it a planned move, carefully staged to reach this point,’ she writes. Emphasising that trust matters more than ideology, she said the party had recently invited nominations from across the country with much fanfare, issued 125 nominations, but later decided to strike seat-sharing arrangements for only 30 constituencies — effectively barring the rest from contesting the election. ‘They dragged the matter to the very last moment so that no one could even contest as an independent candidate. Tomorrow is the last day for submitting nominations,’ she writes, adding that although she currently has no intention to run independently, ‘everything has been thrown into chaos and disowned in the blink of an eye.’ Expressing frustration, Tajnuva also dismissed media reports suggesting she opposed the alliance out of fear of losing her nomination. ‘I had clearly written earlier that if negotiations took place in my constituency, I would not contest the election. No matter how tough the opponent was, I was ready to fight. But that opportunity was not given,’ she said. She alleged that while Jamaat-e-Islami was negotiating seat-sharing for 70 constituencies with the Charmonai Pir-led group, the party born out of the mass uprising was being allocated only 30 seats. Tajnuva had initially received the NCP’s primary nomination for the Dhaka-17 constituency and had been actively campaigning there for several days. Her resignation comes a day after senior joint member secretary of the NCP, Tasnim Jara, stepped down on Saturday over the party’s decision to forge an alliance with Jamaat ahead of the 13th national parliamentary election. Besides, 30 members of the party have sent a letter to NCP convener Nahid Islam, stating their unwillingness to join any alliance with Jamaat. A central leader of the NCP, speaking on condition of anonymity, told UNB that more resignations are likely in the coming days. ‘Not only Jara and Tajnuva—more leaders will leave the party. In particular, women leaders holding senior positions are not interested in aligning with Jamaat,’ the NCP leader said.

title: Main accused has fled to India, two ‘associates’ arrested: DMP
body: The police on Sunday said that Faisal Karim, main suspect in the killing of Inqilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi, fled to India. Meanwhile, the Meghalaya police arrested two individuals, reportedly associates of Faisal. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police additional commissioner, SN Nazrul Islam, disclosed the information at a press conference held at DMP media centre in the capital. 'Investigators had established that Faisal fled to India’s Meghalaya state. The police in Meghalaya have arrested two people suspected of helping Faisal escaping after the shooting,’ he said. The police had earlier said they suspected that Faisal had left Bangladesh, but his whereabouts could not be confirmed at the time. On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head from close quarters in the capital while conducting his electioneering as an independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency. After treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital and Evercare Hospital in the city, he was flown to Singapore for advanced treatment. There he died from his injuries on the night of December 18. Law enforcers have so far arrested at least 11 people in the country for their suspected involvement in the attack on Hadi.

National Citizen Party member-secretary Akhter Hossen said that if the murderers were arrested and proper punishment was ensured, then no one, including politicians, would need gunmen. The police in Lakshmipur on Friday said that they arrested a youth in connection with the arson attack on the district election office on December 13. Bangladesh Nationalist Party has nominated Sheikh Md Abdullah, Md Abdus Salam Azad and Md Kamruzzaman Ratan to contest the forthcoming 13th national parliamentary election in Munshiganj’s three constituencies. Marking the golden jubilee of China-Bangladesh diplomatic relations, the Chinese Literature Readers Club was formally launched in Dhaka on Friday to strengthen literary and cultural exchanges between the two countries. A case was filed over the death of a battery-powered van driver who died of beating as a suspected thief at Bagmara upazila in Rajshahi, the police said on Friday. Research and advocacy organisation PROGGA, Knowledge for Progress, and the Anti-Tobacco Media Alliance have welcomed the government’s approval of the ‘Smoking and Tobacco Products Usage (Control) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025’ at the advisory council meeting. The Jatiya Party led by Ghulam Muhammad Quader on Friday announced its candidates for 243 seats for the next Jatiya Sangsad election slated for February 12, 2026. Vast tracts of mustard fields across Gaibandha have turned bright yellow as the crop has reached full bloom, raising hopes among farmers for a bumper production this season. Haridebpur union is located 15 kilometres away from Rangpur district town. About 35,500 people of the union are mostly farmers. However, some people age engaged in different professions. Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami amir Shafiqur Rahman on Friday said that his party would priorities employment generation for young people instead of providing unemployment allowances, stressing that youths should become active builders of the nation rather than recipients of stipends. Leaders of Ganatantrik Jukta Front, a combine of seven political parties, at a protest rally in Dhaka on Friday called on the interim government to take immediate steps to stop mob violence before next national election scheduled for February 12. Jamal Uddin Ahmed, a retired professor of the finance department of Dhaka University, passed away while undergoing treatment at a hospital in the capital early Friday. Cultivation of Boro paddy, the main crop of farmers of the haor belt, is now going on in full swing in Sunamganj. Today is the 84th anniversary of birth of freedom fighter and Gonoshasthaya Kendra founder, Dr Zafrullah Chowdhury. The Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal-JSD led by ASM Abdur Rob, a partner of the Ganatantra Mancha, will participate separately in the next general elections scheduled for February 12 next year.

title: Mercury dips to 13.5°C in Bangladesh capital
body: Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, recorded the season’s lowest temperature on Friday, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department. The Dhaka Meteorological Office reported a temperature of 13.5°C on Friday morning — the lowest recorded so far this season, said Shahnaj Sultana, a meteorologist. Earlier, the temperature was 14°C on Thursday. Meanwhile, the lowest temperature in the country was recorded at 10.2°C in Rajshahi over the 24 hours until 6:00pm on Thursday, while the highest temperature was 29°C in Teknaf.

title: Only 27.24pc can influence govt decisions: final report
body: Only 27.24 per cent of citizens say they can influence government decisions at any level, according to the final report on the Citizen Perception Survey 2025. The figure, however, drops to 21.99 per cent when it comes specifically to political influence, said the report released by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics at a ceremony at the BBS auditorium in the capital Dhaka on Wednesday. The preliminary report on the survey was released in June. While the findings suggest a widespread sense of distance between citizens and political power, 24.62 per cent of the respondents said that the decision-making within the country’s political system was inclusive and responsive at the national level. The percentage is 24.47 per cent in the rural areas compared with that of 24.91 per cent in the urban areas. The Citizen Perception Survey was conducted by the BBS between February 6 and 23 in all 64 districts to assess public views on key aspects of the Sustainable Development Goal 16, including governance, accountability and citizen participation. Aleya Akter, secretary of the Statistics and Informatics Division under the planning ministry, was present as the chief guest at the report unveiling event. SM Shakil Akhter, secretary of the Planning Division of the ministry, and Mohammad Masud Rana Chowdhury, additional secretary of the Statistics and Informatics Division, attended the event as special guests. The survey report said that 31.67 per cent paid bribes to avail public services in the country. Of the public services, the highest 63.29 per cent of citizens were forced to pay bribes at the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority under the road transport and bridges ministry and the second highest 61.94 per cent of citizens were subjected to pay kickbacks to the law enforcing agencies operated under the home ministry. The BBS survey also showed that the Department of Immigration and Passports, which is also operated under the home ministry, held the third position with 57.45 per cent of citizens paying bribes to get passports and the Directorate of Registration under the law ministry was at the fourth position with 54.92 per cent facing incidents of bribes to get land-related services. A significantly greater percentage of males at 61.43 per cent reported bribery experience compared with females at 41.85 per cent. Regarding the public services, only 47.12 per cent of the respondents used government healthcare facilities. Of them, 82.72 per cent found services easily accessible and 89.34 per cent considered treatment affordable. For education, over 90 per cent reported primary schools as accessible and affordable, compared with about 80 per cent for secondary schools. Quality concerns emerged for both levels, with satisfaction over facilities and services dropping below 80 per cent.

title: Youth beaten after being tied to electric pole in Chapainawabganj
body: A young man was beaten and stabbed to injuries after being tied to an electric pole at Shibganj upazila in Chapainawabganj on Wednesday evening, allegedly due to an internal feud. The incident took place at about 7:00pm in the Umorpur Ghat area of Shyampur union. The injured was Abu Sufian Siju, 25, son of Rabiul Islam of Shyampur–Bajitpur village under the upazila. According to the police and local residents, a group of local youth tied Siju to an electric pole and stabbed him with sharp weapons, injuring both his wrists and the soles of his feet. Locals later rescued him and took him to the Shibganj Upazila Health Complex, from where he was referred to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital after receiving primary treatment. Shibganj police station officer-in-charge Humayun Kabir told New Age that the victim’s father filed an attempt to murder case with the police station against three named and some unnamed persons on Thursday.

title: People’s life, culture key to China-Bangladesh media exchange: Chinese envoy
body: Chinese ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen has said that media exchange plays a vital role in understanding the civilisation and culture of both countries. ‘Media exchange allows us to learn closely from each other. The foundation of China-Bangladesh media exchange is the life and culture of our peoples. This provides a strong base for building a relationship of justice between the two countries,’ he said. The envoy made the remarks at a function titled Golden Silk Road Bangladesh Media Award held at the National Art Gallery of the Shilpakala Academy in Dhaka on Wednesday. Yao Wen said that the Golden Silk Road platform had been formed with the participation of 10 media groups from Bangladesh and China. He added that it would help build mutual confidence among the people and strengthen the friendship between the two countries. ‘The Golden Silk Road platform is an excellent example of mutual learning and is contributing to the progress of human civilisation,’ he said, adding, ‘It shines brightly due to the efforts of media professionals. I believe it will serve as a bridge connecting our civilizations.’ Referring to the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Bangladesh, the ambassador said that this year also marked a period of enhanced people-to-people exchanges. He added that Bangladesh would complete 10 years of joining the Belt and Road Initiative next year. Yao highlighted China’s commitment to high-quality development, emphasising the importance of people-centric growth, self-reliance in technology, and environmental sustainability. ‘This is the foundation of China’s development.’ Expressing hope for media cooperation in showcasing China-Bangladesh friendship, he said, ‘I hope the media of both countries will highlight the friendship stories between China and Bangladesh. Together, we will strengthen the bond between our peoples. The Golden Silk Road will help build a developed future and open a bright chapter for our friendship.’ During the function, media awards were distributed in five categories. SM Nazmul Huq Imon of Bhorer Kagaj won first place in the sports and cultural category, while Mahmud Zaman Avi of bdnews24.com received first place in the visual category. Munir Hossen of Daily Sun won first place in the economy and technology category, Selim Hossain of Rupali Bangladesh topped the news reporting category, and Imrul Hasan of RTV received first place in media innovation. Managing director and chief editor of Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha Mahbub Morshed handed over the prize among the winners of visual category. Addressing the event, the BSS chief said that the programme had created a cultural bond between China and Bangladesh. He hoped that similar initiatives would continue in the future to deepen people-to-people relations and promote cultural exchange. The function was also attended by Faruk Wasif, director general of Press Institute Bangladesh; Mainul Hasan Sohel, general secretary of Dhaka Reporters Unity; and officials from the Chinese embassy and other dignitaries.

title: Crude bomb explodes at Malibagh
body: A crude bomb was exploded near Malibagh intersection in the capital Dhaka on Thursday, a day after a youth was killed in a crude bomb explosion at Moghbazar on Wednesday. A case has been filed in connection with the murder of the youth, the police said. At Malibagh, the crude bomb was exploded at about 12:00pm, according to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s traffic division. No casualties were reported in the incident. Meanwhile, a firecracker-like object exploded next to the garbage depot at Malibagh intersection at about 1:15pm on the day, traffic division officials said. No casualties were reported in the incident. In the Wednesday’s incident, Siam Majumdar, 21, employee of a car decorator shop at Moghbazar, was killed when the crude bomb thrown by miscreants from the Moghbazar–Mouchak flyover exploded near the Moghbazar Muktijoddha Sangsad office gate in the capital. Ali Akbar Majumdar, father of the victim, filed a case with Hatirjheel police against some unidentified people early Thursday, said Golam Mortuza, officer-in-charge of the police station. ‘Siam’s body was handed over to his family after an autopsy at Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue. The police are investigating the incident and efforts are on to arrest the perpetrators,’ he added. The incidents took place at a time when Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman returned home from the United Kingdom after 17 years on Thursday.

title: Three killed in Gazipur train accident
body: Two women and a kid, including a grandmother and her granddaughter, were killed after being hit by a train at Kaliganj in Gazipur on Thursday. The victims were identified as Sadiya Begum, 24, wife of Mobarak Hossain of Dewalertek village under Kaliganj municipality; Anadi Akter, 13, daughter of Babu Mia of the same area; and Komola Begum, 55, of Morjal area under Shibpur in Narsingdi. Anadi and Kamala were granddaughter and grandmother and Sadiya was their neighbour. The accident took place near Arikhola Railway Station in the afternoon when the Noakhali-bound Upakul Express train was passing through the area. According to the locals, the victims were walking together near the railway track when they were hit by the moving train due to carelessness. Two of them died on the spot and Anadi was taken to Kaliganj upazila health complex in critical condition but died on the way. Sub-inspector Dilip Chandra of the Narsingdi railway police outpost said, ‘The bodies were handed over to the families without autopsy following their request.’ Md Zakir Hossain, officer-in-charge of Kaliganj police, said, ‘Police visited the scene after receiving the information and completed the necessary legal procedures.’

title: Pry teaching aspirants to get admit cards tomorrow
body: The participants in the primary school assistant teacher recruitment test can start downloading their admit cards from government website from tomorrow (Saturday). The written test is scheduled to be held across the country on January 2 between 10:00am and 11:30am. A press release, issued by the Directorate of Primary and Mass Education on Wednesday, gave a set of directives for the candidates. It reads that SMS will be sent to the candidates’ mobile numbers given in the applications from the number 01511-662266 for downloading their admit cards. From 10:00am tomorrow, the candidates can start downloading the copy of their admit cards from admit.dpe.gov.bd website using their Username and Password or the roll number, board name and passing year of the Secondary School Certificate examinations. To participate in the written exam, the candidates will have to bring colour print of their admit cards and original National ID or Smart Card. The candidates will have to enter the exam centres by 9:00am on January 2. Mobile phone, books, answer papers, note or any other documents, calculator, vanity bag, purse, hand watch or electric hand watch or any other electric device, communicative device or similar objects are completely prohibited to bring inside the exam centres. If any candidate brings any of them inside the centres, he or she will be expelled immediately and legal action will be taken, according to the directives. The directorate also urged the candidates to be aware of all kinds of fraudulence. On November 5 and 12, the directorate issued circulars to recruit a total of 14,385 assistant teachers in the country. As per the 2023 Annual Primary School Census, there are 65,567 government primary schools and 48.8 per cent or around half of these schools are running without head teachers.

title: Another body recovered, case filed
body: Another body was recovered on Thursday, two days after the clashes and gunfire between two rival groups over control and dominance of a char at Hatiya in Noakhali, raising the number of deaths to six in the incident on December 23. The body of Md Shamsuddin, 59, was recovered from a garden in the area at about 6:30pm, Hatiya police station officer-in-charge Saiful Alam said, adding that taking legal action regarding the matter was under way. Saiful alam also said that victims Md Shamsuddin and Mobarak Hossain Shihab’s family members filed a murder case in the afternoon against 30 named and 10-12 unidentified accused. ‘The police are investigating the incident, efforts are on to arrest the perpetrators as soon as possible,’ he added. Earlier, on December 23, violent clashes broke out on the remote Jagla Char at Hatiya of Noakhali as the Shamsuddin and Alauddin groups allegedly fought for control over the newly emerged land. In the violence, six people, including Shamsuddin and Alauddin were killed and at least seven to eight people were injured. The police recovered the bodies of five people, including Alauddin, from the scene while the body of Shamsuddin could not be found until Thursday evening. The six deceased are Md Shamsuddin, 59, a resident of Jahazmara union at Hatiya, his son Mobarak Hossain Shihab, 21, rival Md Alauddin, 36, of Char Aman Ullah village of Sukhchar union, Haque Sab, 55, of West Lakshidia village of Hatiya Municipality, Kamal Uddin, 38, of Mannan Nagar area of Chandi Union, and Abul Kashem, 57, a resident of Subrna Char.

title: 32 on way to Tarique reception hurt in Cumilla road accident
body: At least 32 leaders and activists of Bangladesh Nationalist Party were injured in a road accident in Cumilla in the early hours of Thursday on their way to Dhaka to join the reception of the party’s acting chairman Tarique Rahman. Witnesses and locals said that their bus started from Maizdi Rashid Colony of Noakhli towards Dhaka and at the Bagmara Bazar area in Cumilla, the driver lost control of the steering and the bus got onto the road divider. Two of the injured were in critical condition. Locals rushed the injured to the Cumilla Medical College Hospital. After primary treatment, severely injured Noakhali municipality ward 4 BNP former president Jamal Uddin Jamal and Newazpur union BNP activist Yusuf were sent to Dhaka for better treatment. The BNP central vice chairman and Noakhali-4 constituency candidate, Md Shahjahan said that the accident was very tragic. They had taken initiatives for the treatment of the victims, he added.

title: EC clarifies voting process for prisoners
body: The Election Commission has issued detailed guidelines enabling voters detained in prisons or under legal custody to cast their votes in the upcoming national election. According to Rule 10A of the Election Conduct Rules 2008 (amended in 2025), inmates and detainees will be able to exercise their voting rights through the In-Country Postal Voting system. The guidelines, signed by Election Commission deputy secretary Mohammad Monir Hossain, were sent to the inspector general, prisons, on Wednesday, said a handout issued on Thursday. Under the guidelines, the enrolment of voters detained in prisons or under legal custody will be approved by the respective authorities. Registration must be completed using the designated web portal: https://prisoner.ocv.gov.bd/login. Prison or legal custody authorities will nominate two representatives to carry out the registration process. After registering interested voters, the authorities will send a printed list of registered voters, duly sealed and signed, to the Election Commission. At the same time, the nominated representatives will upload the required voter information in .xls or .csv format to the designated portal. Registered voters in prison or legal custody will receive a postal ballot envelope through the concerned authority. The envelope sent by the Election Commission will contain two separate ballot papers—one for the national election and another for the referendum—along with voting instructions, a declaration form and a return envelope addressed to the returning officer. The guidelines mentioned that prison or legal custody authorities must ensure a suitable environment for detainees to vote. The postal ballot papers will not contain the names of candidates; only the allotted symbols with blank spaces beside them will be printed. To facilitate voting, the authorities will provide voters with the final list of candidates, including names and symbols, for their respective parliamentary constituencies. Voters will cast their votes in the parliamentary election by placing a tick (✓) or cross (×) in the blank box next to the preferred symbol. For the referendum, voters will similarly mark a tick (✓) or cross (×) in the box next to ‘yes’ or ‘no’. Before voting, the declaration form must be signed using the voter’s name and national identity card number. If a voter is unable to sign, another voter may attest the declaration. After voting, the ballot papers must be placed in two small envelopes, which will then be sealed. The sealed envelopes, along with the signed declaration form, must be placed inside the yellow return envelope addressed to the returning officer and submitted to the designated collection point or box within the prison or legal custody facility. Upon completion of the voting process, the prison or legal custody authorities will securely store all postal ballot envelopes and send or hand them over to the nearest post office as soon as possible. Postal officials will then ensure the ballots are delivered promptly to the respective returning officers. No postage fee will be required for sending the ballot envelopes, as the cost will be borne by the government, the handout added.

title: 7,40,000 registered for postal voting
body: Some 7,40,000 voters, including more than 5,34,000 expatriates from different countries across the world, have been registered to vote through postal ballots in the national election scheduled for February 12, 2026. The Election Commission opened the ‘Postal Vote Bd’ app for the out-of-country voting on November 19 and for the in-country postal voting on December 17. ‘The Postal Vote Bd app will remain open for the registration of all entitled voters till December 31,’ said public relation director at the Election Commission secretariat Ruhul Amin Mollik on Thursday. Though the postal balloting system has been in the laws for a long time, it was never practiced in the previous elections. This is the first time the Election Commission has introduced an effective IT-supported hybrid postal balloting system, enabling expatriates, government staff who are posted outside their respective constituencies, polling personnel, and the persons who will be in the legal custody to exercise their franchise through a combination of digital registration and manual voting. As of 7:05pm on Thursday, a total 7,40,412 voters were registered to vote through postal ballots in the February-12 elections. Among them, 2,05,942 voters were registered from Bangladesh, while 5,34,470 expatriates from different countries across the world. Among the expatriate registrants, the highest number came from the Saudi Arabia (1,55,535) followed by Qatar (57,521), Oman (43,484), Malaysia (41,469), UAE (30,713), US (25,557), Kuwait (22,975), UK (21,299), Singapore (17,471), Italy (15,232), Canada (11,990), Bahrain (11,422), South Korea (10,159), Australia (9,405), Japan (7,475), Maldives (6,968), France (5,783), Portugal (5,320), South Africa (5,110) and Germany (4,392), Spain (2,532), China (1,905), Finland (1,713), Poland (1,617), Brunei (1,317), Sweden (1,229) and Irelands (1,137). Among the registered ones, the highest 67,555 will vote in Cumilla district, while 59,891 in Dhaka district, 58,891 in Chattogram, 38,624 in Noakhali, 28,472 in Sylhet, 26,748 in Chandpur, 26,195 in Feni, 22,497 in Brahmanbaria, 20,553 in Lakshmipur and 18,847 in Cox’s Bazar. In terms of parliamentary seats, the highest 10,960 registered ones will vote in Feni 3 constituency, while 9,479 in Chattogram 15 constituency, 9,025 in Cumilla 10 constituency, 8,925 in Noakhali 1 constituency and 8,453 in Noakhali 3 constituency. Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin on December 11 announced the schedule to arrange the 13th parliamentary election and the referendum on the July National Charter (constitutional reform) Implementation Order simultaneously on February 12. According to the election schedule, the deadline for the submission of nomination paper is December 29, while the last date for the withdrawal of candidature is January 20. The election campaign will start on January 22 and continue till 48 hours before the balloting period (7:30am on February 10).
