title: Four make confession
body: Three accused, including the wife of prime suspect Foysal Karim Masud, gave confessional statements in the case filed over the murder of Inquilab Moncho spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi. The accused are Saheda Pervin Samia, wife of Foysal Karim Masud, her brother Wahid Ahmed, and Foysal’s friend Maria Akter Lima. Besides, Md Kamal Hossain, 46, who was driving the auto-rickshaw carrying Sharif Osman Hadi during the armed attack on him has given his statement in the court here as a witness on Thursday, reported the Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha. Kamal Hossain was produced before the chief metropolitan magistrate court by investigating officer of the case, DB inspector Faisal Ahmed and he prayed for recording the statement of Kamal as a witness. Following the petition, metropolitan magistrate Jamshed Ahmed on behalf of the CMM recorded his statement under section 164 of the criminal procedure code. Dhaka metropolitan magistrate Aminul Islam Zunayed recorded the confessional statements of Samia and Wahid, while Dhaka metropolitan magistrate Kamal Uddin recorded Lima’s statement under Section 164 on Wednesday night. The trio were produced before the Dhaka chief metropolitan magistrate court after completion of their two rounds of remand in the case. Investigating officer of the Detective Branch of police, inspector Foysal Ahmed, prayed to the court for recording their confessional statements, saying the accused persons were willing to confess their involvement in the crime. Earlier, on December 15, the court of Dhaka additional chief metropolitan magistrate Joshita Islam placed each of the three accused on a five-day remand. They were again placed on a further four-day remand on December 20 by the court of Dhaka metropolitan magistrate Siddiq Azad. On December 20, the court ordered the inclusion of Section 302 (murder) of the Penal Code in the case following the death of Sharif Osman Hadi on December 18, which was initially filed as an attempted murder. The United News of Bangladesh reported that the Inqilab Mancha on Thursday announced plans to hold nationwide prayers and protest marches, demanding justice for the murder of its spokesperson, Sharif Osman Bin Hadi. In a Facebook post, the platform said that following jumma prayers on Friday, prayers and protest marches will be held across the country, seeking justice for the killing of Osman Hadi, described as a martyr, a vanguard of the anti-Indian hegemony movement, and an architect of a just Bangladesh. The programmes will also include prayers for the forgiveness of his soul. Osman Hadi, also a prospective candidate for Dhaka 8 constituency, was shot in the head on December 12 while travelling in a rickshaw on Culvert Road at Paltan. He was airlifted to Singapore for advanced treatment, where he succumbed to his injuries on the night of December 18.

title: Youth lynched in Rajbari over extortion
body: A 29-year-old man, Amrit Mondal, also known as Samrat, was beaten to death by local people at Pangsha in Rajbari on Wednesday on allegations of extortion. The incident occurred in Hossaindanga Old Market area. Confirming the incident, interim government chief adviser’s press wing in a statement on Thursday said that the murder incident happened on allegation of extortion. The statement, however, said that misleading information was being circulated on social media and in some sections of the media regarding the killing that took place on Wednesday night. According to police and preliminary investigation, the incident was not a communal attack, but a result of violence stemming from extortion and criminal activities, it said. The deceased was identified as ‘notorious criminal’ Amrit Mondal, who had gone to the area to collect extortion money and was killed following a clash with angry local residents. The statement also said that Samrat was a top-listed crime suspect and had been accused in multiple serious cases, including murder and extortion, filed in 2023. Warrants for his arrest were also pending in those cases. During the operation, police arrested Samrat’s associate Selim from the scene along with one foreign-made pistol and one pipe gun, it said, adding that three cases have already been filed in connection with the incident. The government strongly condemned the killing and said it does not support any form of extrajudicial action, mob violence or vigilantism. ‘Those directly or indirectly involved in the incident will be brought under the law, the government said, adding that law enforcement agencies are conducting a full investigation into the matter. The government also expressed deep concern over attempts by a certain group to portray the incident as a communal attack by highlighting the religious identity of the deceased, calling such claims baseless and malicious. Such propaganda, the government warned, could harm communal harmony and deteriorate the law and order situation in the country. The government urged all concerned to act responsibly and refrain from spreading misleading, provocative and communal statements.

title: Bholaganj Land Port inaugurated
body: Bangladesh interim government’s shipping, and labour and employment affairs adviser retired Brigadier General M Sakhawat Hossain inaugurated the Bholaganj Land Port at Companiganj upazila in Sylhet on Thursday noon. The adviser said that trade with India’s Meghalaya, Tripura, Nagaland and Assam states and Bhutan will expand through launching activities of the Bholaganj Land Port. Apart from playing a vital role to enhance revenue earning, the port will be able to move away the local people from quarry-centric employment and engage them to different import-export activities, he hoped. The government has been importing limestone for more than 20 years through the Bholaganj Customs Station at Companiganj upazila in the district. As a result, it was declared the country’s 24th land port in 2019. Later, construction of the port began in January 2024 on 52 acres of land near the popular tourist spot Sadapathar of the upazila involving an amount of Tk 175 crore and ended in November this year. Shipping ministry secretary Nurunnahar Chowdhury, Bangladesh Land Ports Authority chairman (additional secretary) Mohammad Manzarul Mannan, Sylhet deputy commissioner Md Sarwoer Alam, Sylhet police superintendent Kazi Akhtar-Ul Alam and Companiganj upazila nirbahi officer Mohammad Robin Mia, among others, attended the inaugural event.

title: Christmas celebrated
body: The Christian community on Thursday celebrated Christmas in Bangladesh like elsewhere in the world in a befitting manner commemorating the birth of Jesus Christ. Christmas, the biggest religious festival of the Christian community, is the celebration of rebirth, new beginning, forgiveness and peace and renewing relationship with God and human beings. The celebrations of the Christmas featured decoration of Christmas trees with colourful lights, special prayers and distribution of gifts among children and exchange of pleasantries. Christmas carols and hymns were sung before and after the prayer sessions at the churches. Bangladesh Television and Bangladesh Betar and different private TV channels and radio stations aired programmes highlighting the significance of the day, reported the United News of Bangladesh. In separate messages, president Mohammed Shahabuddin and chief adviser Muhammad Yunus extended their greetings to the Christian community on the occasion, reported the Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha. They wished peace, welfare and prosperity for all citizens of the country, including members of the Christian community. President, in his message, said, ‘Bangladesh is a country of communal harmony, where people of all faiths freely practice their religions and rituals.’ He urged all to further strengthen this communal harmony and join the journey of building a modern and developed Bangladesh. He wished for peace, prosperity and well-being of all members of the Christian community. Muhammad Yunus, in his message, said that Jesus came into the world with the message of peace, justice and the liberation of humanity. Mentioning Bangladesh as a shining example of communal harmony, Yunus said, ‘Since time immemorial, the people of this country have maintained cordial coexistence by respecting different religions, cultures and customs.’ He expressed hope that the celebration of Christmas with due dignity and enthusiasm would further strengthen this bond of harmony. He called upon all Christians to come forward, inspired by patriotism and the great ideals of humanity, to help realise the dream of a new Bangladesh. He wished peace, prosperity and well-being to all, including the Christian community.

title: Dilapidated relics cast long shadow over justice at Amtali court
body: Two crumbling buildings, relics of a bygone era, have become a looming threat to nearly 20,000 people who frequent the Amtali upazila senior judicial magistrate court in Barguna. Built more than half a century ago, the abandoned structures now stand as silent hazards, shedding bricks and cement onto a passage used daily by litigants, lawyers and court staff. A recent visit to the site paints a troubling picture. The narrow main entrance to the court runs directly between the two decaying, two-storey buildings, forcing thousands of visitors each day to pass beneath unstable walls. Chunks of masonry have already fallen, heightening fears that a sudden collapse could trigger a serious disaster. The buildings were constructed in 1975 by the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation to store machinery and equipment. Around 15 years ago, the local administration declared them abandoned. Since then, neglect has taken its toll. Weeds and creepers now blanket the walls, giving the structures a haunted appearance that unsettles court-goers even before they step inside. Concerns over safety have been raised repeatedly by those who use the court. ‘Every day, thousands of people come and go through the court entrance at their own risk,’ said Md Abubakar, a member of the court staff, adding, ‘These buildings are extremely vulnerable and could collapse at any moment, causing severe casualties.’ Abdul Majed, who regularly visits the court, said, ‘The structures are not only an eyesore but a grave danger. These abandoned buildings spoil the image of the court and pose a serious risk to life. They must be evicted immediately.’ Former local ward councillor Jannatul Ferdous echoed the concern, warning that the hazardous condition of the buildings undermined the dignity of the court and endangers everyone passing through its entrance. District Bar Association member and additional public prosecutor Jasim Uddin added that the administration had been informed several times about the risks, but no effective action had followed. ‘The removal of these abandoned buildings should be expedited to safeguard the lives of litigants and lawyers.’ Officials, too, acknowledge the urgency. Syed Mohayminul Islam, deputy assistant engineer of Amtali BADC, expressed surprise at the prolonged inaction. ‘I do not understand why they have not been removed yet,’ he said, stressing that the matter required immediate attention. Local Government Engineering Department official Md Idris Ali said that the issue would be reviewed, assuring that steps would be taken promptly if the buildings remained officially listed as abandoned. Amtali upazila nirbahi officer Muhammad Zafar Arif Chowdhury said that the structures would be removed as soon as possible, following due procedure.

title: Cold wave continues, affecting normal life in northern region
body: Although the minimum temperatures remained mostly unchanged and maximum temperatures increased slightly, the mild cold wave blowing over the northern region continued affecting the normal life for the third consecutive day on Thursday. The sky remained partly cloudy and misty till noon with cold winds blowing from the west and northwest. The sufferings of the poor people living in the riverbank and char areas of the Brahmaputra basin remained deplorable on Thursday as it has been for the past few days. The cold forced many people to stay indoors, and business and normal activities were partially affected until the sun shone for a few hours in the afternoon, breaking through a layer of thick fog in the cool air. Officer-in-charge of Rangpur Meteorological Office Md Mostafizar Rahman said that the minimum temperatures remained mostly unchanged with a little rise at places while maximum temperatures marked a rise on Thursday. The intensity of cold, however, remained almost unchanged in the region. ‘Although the gap between the minimum and maximum temperatures increased slightly compared to yesterday, it is still feeling cold for the third consecutive day,’ he said. The minimum temperature of 11.2 degrees Celsius was recorded at 6:00am on Thursday against Wednesday’s 12.2 degrees and maximum of 20 degrees against Wednesday’s 17.5 degrees Celsius in Rangpur city. The minimum temperatures recorded at 6:00am on Thursday were 10.6 degrees Celsius against Wednesday’s 11.6 degrees at Tetulia, 10.5 degrees Celsius against Wednesday’s 11.5 degrees in Dinajpur, 10.5 degrees against Wednesday’s 12 degrees at Saidpur, 11 degrees against Wednesday’s 12.4 degrees at Dimla, 11.5 degrees like Wednesday at Rajarhat, 10.7 degrees against Wednesday’s 11.5 degrees at Thakurgaon and 11.8 degrees Celsius like Wednesday in Gaibandha points. The maximum temperatures recorded at 3:00pm on Thursday were 22.9 degrees Celsius against Wednesday’s 16.5 at Tetulia, 22 degrees against Wednesday’s 19.5 degrees in Dinajpur, 18.6 degrees against Wednesday’s 16.5 degrees at Dimla, 17 degrees against Wednesday’s 18.7 degrees at Rajarhat, 21.8 degrees against Wednesday’s 18.2 degrees at Thakurgaon and 21.2 degrees against Wednesday’s 18.5 degrees Celsius in Gaibandha points in the region. Sources at different district level hospitals said that the number of patients with cough, fever, asthma and other cold and climate change related diseases had been increasing again during the past couple of days in the northern region. Rangpur divisional director, health, Dr Md Gausul Azim Chowdhury said that there were adequate stocks of medicines and steps had been taken in all government hospitals and upazila health complexes to provide proper treatments to cold-related patients. The district administrations, few NGOs, voluntary and socio-cultural organisations, business bodies, banks and other institutions have started distributing warm clothes among the cold-stricken people to mitigate their sufferings. District Relief and Rehabilitation officer of Rangpur Md Golam Kibria said that distribution of warm clothes continued among the cold- hit distressed people in the district as elsewhere in the sub-Himalayan region. ‘We have got allocations of 7,500 pieces of blankets in two phases and Tk 48 lakh to purchase warm cloths locally for distribution among the cold-hit people in all eight upazilas in Rangpur district,’ he added. ‘Like the other northern districts of Rangpur division, we have also received 7,500 pieces of blankets and Tk 54 lakh for purchasing warm clothes locally and distributing among the cold-hit people,’ Kurigram DRRO Md Abdul Matin said. More allocations of money and blankets are expected soon for every cold-hit district in the region. Reports from remote areas say that the normal lives of the poor people living in the riverine char areas of Rangpur, Kurigram, Lalmonirhat, Gaibandha, Nilphamari and other adjoining northern districts in the Brahmaputra basin are being disrupted.

title: City commuters suffer amid fewer transports, extra fare
body: Dhaka city commuters on Thursday suffered due to a very few number of public and other transports throughout the day on roads amid the celebration of homecoming of Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman. Tarique returned to the country after ending more than 17 years in forced exile in the United Kingdom. Road users on Thursday struggled to find buses, CNG-run auto-rickshaws and vehicles under ridesharing services and they had to pay much higher as fares. Till evening on the day, most of the city roads stayed clear, except the reception venue along the Purbachal Expressway, known as the 300 Feet Road. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police issued a set of directives for Thursday, where it set some diversions for roads and arranged some parking spots for the vehicles of BNP leaders and activists. However, since morning thousands of activists of the BNP had gathered in the airport, Uttara and Purbachal areas, which halted the vehicular movements. Following an announcement by the interim government, the Dhaka Elevated Expressway was toll-free for four hours between 11:00am and 3:00pm on Thursday. Huge crowds were seen under the expressway. A very few number of buses and CNG-run auto-rickshaws were seen on roads while the ridesharing services drivers asked for extra. One Mozammel Hossain, a Bashundhara resident, said that he regularly came Hatirpool by motorcycle under ridesharing services at about Tk 200. ‘Today [Thursday] no motorcyclists wanted to come using the apps and one of them asked Tk 1,000 from me for the Bashundhara-Hatirpool ride,’ he said. He added that later he had reached Hatirpool paying Tk 300 to a motorcyclist. Suvenkar Ghosh, managing director of Shyamoli NR Paribahan and general secretary of the Bangladesh Bus Truck Owners Association, said that inter-district buses from Gabtoli and Saidabad on northern, southern and western districts were normal while buses did not start from Dhaka on Gazipur and Mymensingh routes till afternoon. The Biman Bangladesh Airlines authorities requested the airport-bound passengers to start from their homes with enough time in hand for Thursday. The Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport authorities, citing special operational and security reasons, prohibited all visitors except designated passengers from entering its area for 24 hours ending 6:00pm on Thursday. The Bangladesh Railway cancelled the scheduled journeys of three trains on Thursday, as it ran 10 special trains to carry BNP leaders and activists to and from the capital from different destinations.

title: NCP likely to join Jamaat-led alliance
body: The National Citizen Party, formed by student and youth organisers of the July uprising in February this year, is likely to join the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami-led alliance ahead of the next general election and the national referendum. The NCP is, however, in confusion about its involvement with the recently formed Ganatantrik Sanskar Jote, an NCP-led alliance launched on December 7. The components of the alliance are the NCP, the Bangladesh Rashtra Sanskar Andolan and the Amar Bangladesh Party. NCP joint convener Javed Rasin told New Age on Thursday that their party was holding meetings with the leaders of the Jamaat-led alliance to hold campaigns in favour of ‘yes’ votes in the referendum for implementing the reform proposals inscribed in the July National Charter 2025. The next general election and the national referendum on the July National Charter (Constitutional Reform) Implementation Order 2025 are scheduled to be held on February 12, 2026. ‘But our joining in the Jamaat-led alliance is yet to be finalised. It can be finalised soon,’ Javed added. Ganatantrik Sanskar Jote leader and Rashtra Sanskar Andolan president Hasnat Quiyum told New Age that their party would not join any alliance with Jamaat. The Jamaat-led alliance had been holding programmes with some Islamic political parties to press its five-point demands including the implementation of the July National Charter, holding the next Jatiya Sangsad elections in a proportional representation system, and ensuring a level-playing field for all political parties before the election.

title: SoEs’ operating surplus decreases in FY25
body: The operating surplus of about 90 state-owned enterprises in sectors like industry, utility and service stood at Tk 45,330.56 crore in the 2024-25 financial year, decreasing by about Tk 6,800 crore compared with that in the previous financial year, according to the Economic Survey 2025. The operating surplus of the enterprises was Tk 52,143.88 crore in the FY24, said the survey. Released by the Finance Division in the past week, the survey highlighted financial performances of SOEs between July 2024 and June 2025. A total of 17 SOEs failed to make operating surplus and 73 made surplus in the FY25 marked by the political changeover following the ouster of the Awami League regime on August 5, 2024, in the wake of a mass uprising. The interim government that assumed power on August 8, 2024, focused on streamlining operation of the SOEs and increased distribution of subsidised food items to shield the poor from high inflation prevailing then at the double digit level. The Trading Corporation of Bangladesh which distributes food items like rice, ata, sugar and edible oil at subsidised rates among people faced the second highest operational deficit of Tk 7,876.06 crore among the SOEs. In FY 24, the TCB under the commerce ministry made operating surplus of Tk 1,046.94 crore. The Bangladesh Power Development Board hit the highest amount of operating deficit in FY25 with Tk 8,803.66 crore, extending its losing record to the fourth straight financial year. The operating deficit of BPDB in FY25 was higher than the operating deficit of Tk 8,446 crore in FY24, but lower than the deficit of Tk 11,163 crore recorded in FY23. The BPDB suffered operating deficit Tk 3,243 crore in FY22, ending its brief operating surplus record of Tk 3.9 crore in FY20 and Tk 145 crore in FY21. Among the other loss-making SOEs, the Bangladesh Sugar and Food Industries Corporation managed to reduce its operating deficit to Tk 439 crore in FY25 from Tk 508 crore in FY24 and the Dhaka Power Distribution Company to Tk 11.41 crore from Tk 302.9 crore in the same period. The survey conducted by the Finance Division said that the operating deficit of the Bangladesh Sugar and Food Industries Corporation had decreased because of projections on revenue generation and production. It also said that the Bangladesh Jute Corporation had made operating deficit of Tk 132 crore in FY25 and Tk 172 crore in FY24 because of its virtual closure. The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation also continued to make operating deficit of Tk 278.9 crore in FY25, after incurring deficit of Tk 250 crore in FY24. The survey highlighted that the Bangladesh Chemical Industries had made a turnaround to make Tk 1,087 crore operating surplus to end its record of previous deficit over the past nine financial years. The Titas Gas Distribution PLC made the highest operating surplus of Tk 35,298 crore in FY25, while the figure was Tk 34,628.04 crore in FY24. The Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation’s operating surplus almost halved to Tk 2,050 crore in FY25 from Tk 3,943.9 crore in FY24. The Chittagong Port Authority increased its operating surplus to Tk 2,297.75 crore in FY25 from Tk 2,141 crore in FY24, but the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission saw operating surplus decreasing to Tk 3,187 crore in FY25 from Tk 4,134 crore in FY24. To make operations of the SOEs more transparent, the Finance Division examined budgets of the 90 entities.

title: Poor progress disappoints reform stakeholders
body: The year 2025 began with high expectations of wide-ranging state reforms, but the year is ending on a negative note, with limited progress in reforms. The interim government, after assuming office after the fall of the Awami League regime amid the July uprising in August 2024, formed six reform commissions in early October. The commissions submitted their recommendations in January–February. In mid-November 2024, the government formed five more reform commissions. They also submitted their recommendations in April. Several members of the commissions and analysts have expressed their disappointment about the pace and the scope of reforms, as a few of the recommendations, including the one provisioning for a secretariat for the judiciary, have so far been implemented. The six commissions formed in October 2024 are for the constitution, judiciary, police, electoral system, public administration and the Anti-Corruption Commission. The five commissions formed in November 2024 are for labour, health, land, media and women’s affairs. Economist Debapriya Bhattacharya, a distinguished fellow of the Centre for Policy Dialogue, citing the Electoral Reform Commission’s 31 immediately implementable proposals, said, ‘Only two proposals are in the implementation phase right now.’ Chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus, in his Victory Day message on December 16, however, said, ‘The wide-ranging reform initiatives undertaken by the current interim government to build a well-governed and progressive Bangladesh are now moving toward successful completion.’ All the reform proposals broadly fell into two categories, some required constitutional amendments, and those that could be implemented through ordinances. To forge political consensus on the recommendations by the Constitution Reform Commission and others requiring constitutional reforms, the government formed the National Consensus Commission in mid-February, which subsequently drafted the July National Charter. Most of the recommendations from the Constitution Reform Commission are subject to the referendum scheduled for February 12 next year. In terms of implementation, the interim government has so far executed nine of the 30 recommendations made by the Judicial Reform Commission. The measures implemented include establishing a separate secretariat for the Supreme Court, forming a judges’ appointment commission, amending civil and criminal laws, including the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, and revising the International Crimes (Tribunals) Act. However, no visible progress has been made on a range of other recommendations, including setting up courts at the upazila level, establishing a permanent government attorney service, curbing presidential clemency powers, creating an independent criminal investigation service, reducing harassment of litigants, preventing corruption in the judiciary, implementing alternative dispute resolution laws, operationalising village courts, reforming legal education and the legal profession, preventing false cases, and reducing case backlogs. Supreme Court lawyer and one of the Judicial Reform Commission members, Tanim Hossain Hossain Shawon, said, ‘Compared to other reform commissions, the implementation of the JRC’s recommendations had been relatively satisfactory.’ Among the proposals of the Anti-Corruption Commission Reform Commission, one is issuing an ordinance to ensure that the ACC operates as an independent and effective institution free from political bias, with the aim of restoring public trust. The cabinet approved the ordinance in late November. Transparency International Bangladesh, however, expressed concern, saying that the ordinance ignored several key strategic recommendations made by the reform commission. The commission had proposed the formation of a selection and review committee to ensure transparency in appointing ACC commissioners and accountability in the commission’s performance. The ordinance, however, excluded the review mechanism. TIB executive director Iftekharuzzaman, who chaired the ACC Reform Commission, said that the ACC had long been used to harass political opponents and shield ruling parties. He said that the review mechanism would have enabled periodic assessment of the commission’s performance. He also questioned the selection committee formed under the ordinance, saying that it excluded crucial recommendations that had enjoyed broad political support. ‘The government itself formed the reform commission and created an opportunity for national consensus, yet it is now disregarding the recommendations,’ he said. The Electoral Reform Commission recommended changes to make the Representation of the People Order and the code of conduct for political parties and candidates more democratic and accountable. The Election Commission revised the RPO and the code of conduct in November. Former Electoral Reform Commission chief Badiul Alam Majumder said that the revised RPO ignored a key recommendation to introduce a three-member panel of each of the political parties in each constituency for nominating their party candidates. He also said that the revised RPO failed to bring registered political parties under the Right to Information Act, 2009. Other recommendations omitted from the revised RPO include reinstating a requirement of at least three years’ involvement with a political party for nomination aspirants, allowing legal action against election commissioners for breaching their constitutional oath, empowering the Election Commission to scrutinise candidates’ election expenses and cancel nominations for false reporting, and barring habitual loan defaulters from contesting elections. Of the key recommendations made by the Police Reform Commission, the interim government has so far introduced the Police Commission through an ordinance on December 9. Under the ordinance, the five-member Police Commission will recommend measures to strengthen discipline, accountability, transparency, and professionalism within the police force, investigate complaints from citizens, determine responsibility for misconduct, and recommend punitive action. Zarif Rahman, who served as a member of the Police Reform Commission, said, ‘While the ordinance introduces some checks on policing, it provides no accountability mechanism for the home ministry, leaving the bureaucracy largely untouched.’ The Public Administration Reform Commission recommended abolishing police verification for issuing passports, a measure the interim government has implemented. The commission also recommended reducing the number of ministries from 43 to 25 and divisions from 61 to 40. Although the interim government merged the Internal Resources Division with the National Board of Revenue and brought two security divisions under the Ministry of Home Affairs, no steps have been taken to reduce the number of ministries. Proposals to empower deputy commissioners to try CR-type cases as district magistrates, establish magistrate courts at the upazila level, and appoint public security and immigration officers remain unimplemented. Recommendations to restructure the Public Service Commission into three bodies and to create a Superior Executive Service have also yet to be implemented. Among the recommendations submitted by the Labour Reform Commission, the government issued the Bangladesh Labour Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025, widening the definition of workers and their trade union rights. The cabinet of the interim government also approved the Anti-harassment ordinance to protect women at their workplaces as recommended by the Women’s Affairs Reform Commission.

title: Tarique returns home to roaring reception
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chair Tarique Rahman returned to the country on Thursday after ending 17 years in forced exile in the United Kingdom, marking his homecoming with a historic reception attended by over 10 lakh people. Tarique arrived at the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at around 11:40am on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from London. He was accompanied by his wife Zubaida Rahman, their daughter Zaima Rahman, and the family’s pet cat Zeebu. Extensive security measures were in place as he travelled from the airport to the designated reception venue along the Purbachal Expressway, known as the 300 Feet Road. Tarique delivered a brief speech in response at the mass reception before meeting his mother, former prime minister Khaleda Zia, who has been undergoing treatment at Evercare Hospital for more than a month and remains in a critical condition. In his address, the BNP acting chair expressed gratitude to the people for their overwhelming support, saying that he had a plan aimed at fulfilling the aspirations of the people of Bangladesh. Although he did not provide details of the plan, he expressed confidence that the country could move forward through collective efforts. Tarique also urged all sections of society to stay united and called for the maintenance of peace, discipline and public safety, stressing the importance of national harmony during the current period. Shortly after landing at the airport, Tarique was seen passionately touching the soil of his homeland, a symbolic gesture that resonated strongly with his supporters and marked the end of his long absence from the country. ‘This country is home to people of the hills and the plains, Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists and Christians. Together, we want to build a Bangladesh – which a mother dreams of – that is a safe Bangladesh,’ he said. Tarique reflected on the country’s political history and struggles, recalling the Liberation War of 1971, the November 7 event in 1975, the mass movement against the military rule in 1990, and the 2024 mass uprising. ‘Our beloved motherland was achieved in 1971 at the cost of the blood of countless martyrs. In the same spirit, the people of this country – students, farmers, workers, women, and men from all walks of life – stood united on August 2024 to protect Bangladesh’s independence and sovereignty,’ he said. The people of Bangladesh, Tarique Rahman said, now want to regain their right to speak freely and their democratic rights. Soon after disembarking, Tarique was taken to the airport VIP lounge, where he was received at 11:56am by BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, other senior party leaders and family members. His mother-in-law, Syeda Iqbal Mand Banu, welcomed him by placing a floral garland around his neck. From the VIP lounge, Tarique made a phone call to chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus, thanking him for the arrangements made for his return and security. He then boarded a specially prepared bulletproof bus bearing the slogan ‘Bangladesh First’ at its front. Tarique’s motorcade left the airport at around 12:30pm under heavy security, with army personnel deployed on both sides of his route. At around 3:50pm, the BNP acting chair arrived at the reception venue when the surrounding areas became full of life with slogans chanted by party leaders, activists, and supporters. The area witnessed great excitement as he took to the stage and waved in response to greetings and goodwill gestures from the gathering. Tarique said that the blood of the martyrs had placed a responsibility on the nation to build the Bangladesh they had envisioned, adding that repaying this debt required collective efforts to realise the country the people expected and to work together for their welfare. He also appealed for calm and order, repeatedly urging everyone to avoid disorder and saying that the country needed peace. Tarique paid tribute to Sharif Osman Hadi, the young activist of the July uprising who was recently killed by bullets, saying that Hadi had wanted democracy to be established and the democratic rights of the people to be restored. ‘No matter what our religion, class, or political identity are, we must ensure peace and security in this country at all costs,’ Tarique asserted. From the early hours of the morning, massive crowds began gathering at the reception site. By 10:00am, the venue and surrounding neighbourhoods were completely packed with activists and supporters, leaving little space open. Security personnel were deployed throughout the venue and nearby places to maintain order. Large screens installed on and around the stage showcased documentaries on BNP founder Ziaur Rahman and the July uprising. Supporters continued arriving from multiple highways, while many processions were accompanied by band music, adding to the celebratory mood as followers welcomed Tarique Rahman back to the country. Before concluding, Tarique spoke emotionally about his mother -- BNP chair Khaleda Zia -- saying that she is a person who has loved the soil of this country and its people more than her own life. Tarique said that although his heart, as a son, was with his mother in her hospital room, he could not avoid the people for whom Khaleda Zia had dedicated her life, citing that that was why he chose to address the gathering before visiting her. BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and standing committee members were present on the reception stage. Among others, leaders of the BNP’s allied parties— including Bangladesh Jatiya Party, Nagorik Oikya, Ganosamhati Andolan, Gono Odhikar Parishad, Gono Forum, National Democratic Movement, and Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh -- also attended the reception. Although leaders of the National Citizen Party were not present, party convener Nahid Islam hailed Tarique’s homecoming in a Facebook post. After concluding the reception Tarique headed to Evercare Hospital to visit his mother Khaleda Zia. He left the reception stage at around 4:45pm and arrived at the hospital at approximately 5:50pm. The 79-year old leader, who has long been suffering from multiple chronic health complications, including liver and kidney diseases, heart ailments, hypertension, diabetes, arthritis and recurrent infections, was admitted to Evercare Hospital on November 23. After visiting his ailing mother at her bedside, Tarique left the hospital at around 7:00pm, heading to his Gulshan residence in a convoy. Tarique Rahman had previously been sentenced in several cases, including to a life-term imprisonment, and faced numerous other charges, most of which were filed during the 2007–08 military-backed caretaker government. He was arrested during an anti-corruption drive in March 2007 and released on bail on September 3, 2008, after which he travelled to London on September 11 for medical treatment and remained there. Following the end of the Awami League’s 16-year rule on August 5, 2024 amid a mass uprising, the High Court acquitted Tarique of all cases filed during both the caretaker government and Awami League administration periods, clearing the legal hurdles to his return. On the occasion of Tarique’s return, most city roads remained relatively clear on Thursday, except around the reception venue, as public transport was limited. Commuters struggled to find buses, CNG auto-rickshaws, and ridesharing vehicles, with some paying significantly higher fares than usual. Inter-district bus services operated normally on northern, southern, and western routes, but those to Gazipur and Mymensingh did not run until the afternoon. The Bangladesh Railway cancelled three scheduled trains but operated 10 special services to transport BNP leaders and supporters from remote areas. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police effected road diversions and designated parking for party vehicles, while the Dhaka airport allowed entry only to the authorised passengers. Biman Bangladesh Airlines advised its passengers to allocate extra time for their travels. Meanwhile, the Dhaka Elevated Expressway was made toll-free for four hours between 11:00am and 3:00pm under interim government arrangements.

title: ARSON AT BNP LEADER’S HOUSE : Another daughter dies at Dhaka hospital
body: Another daughter of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party leader, whose house was allegedly locked from the outside and set on fire in Lakshmipur died while being treated at a hospital in the capital Dhaka early Thursday. Salma Akter Smriti, 17, the eldest daughter of Belal Hossain, a businessman and assistant organising secretary of Bhabaniganj union BNP, breathed her last at about 12:30am at the intensive care unit of National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in the capital. In the fire, Belal’s youngest daughter, Ayesha Akter Sanju, was burnt to death on the spot. Confirming the death, Lakshmipur additional superintendent of police Hossain Mohammad Raihan Kazemi said that the police were investigating the incident and efforts were on to arrest the perpetrators. Shaon Bin Rahman, resident surgeon of the bunt institute, said that Smriti suffered 90 per cent burns on her body. Belal along with his two other daughters — Smriti and Samia Akter Bithi, 14, — sustained burn injuries in an alleged arson attack on the house in the early hours of December 20. Belal received treatment at Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital, while Smriti and Bithi were shifted to the National Burn and Plastic Surgery Institute in Dhaka with 90 per cent and two per cent burns on their bodies, respectively. Bithi was released from the hospital the day after admission, but Smriti remained in the ICU in critical condition before succumbing to her injuries. On December 23, Belal filed a case four days after the incident with Lakshmipur Sadar Model police station against unidentified suspects. However, the police said that no one had been arrested so far and no clear evidence of petrol being used to start the fire was found at the spot. Meanwhile, the police recovered three padlocks from the scene — two locked and one unlocked.

title: HADI KILLING: auto-rickshaw driver Kamal gives statement
body: Md Kamal Hossain, 46, who was driving the auto-rickshaw carrying Sharif Osman Hadi during the attack on him has given his statement in the court in Dhaka as a witness. Hadi, an independent candidate in the 13th national election and convener of Inquilab Mancha, was fired from a shot at blank range in city’s Box Culvert Road under Palton police station on December 12 while traveling by an auto rickshaw towards Suhrawardy Udyan from Motijheel area. Kamal Hossain was produced before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court on the day by investigating officer of the case, DB inspector Faisal Ahmed and he prayed for recording the statement of Kamal as a witness. Following the petition, metropolitan magistrate Jamshed Ahmed on behalf of the CMM recorded his statement under section 164 of the criminal procedure code. The IO in his petition stated that on December 12, on the paved road in front of DR Tower on Box Culvert Road under Paltan police station, in the direction of Bijoynagar Water Tank, accused Faisal Karim Masud alias Daud, who were on a motorcycle following from behind, along with their unidentified associates, shot Hadi with a firearm. Injured Hadi was first taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for treatment and later to Evercare Hospital. As his physical condition deteriorated, he was taken by air ambulance to Singapore for better treatment and admitted to Singapore General Hospital. He later died on December 18 while undergoing treatment there. The case is a sensational murder case. At the time of the incident, Hadi was traveling by the auto rickshaw driven by witness Md Kamal Hossain (46) from Motijheel, towards Suhrawardy Udyan, when he was shot at the scene. Kamal Hossain is an eyewitness. The witness is willing to voluntarily give his statement in court. For the sake of proper investigation of the case, it is essential to record the witness’s statement under Section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code. On December 12 at about 2:20pm, miscreants shot at Hadi on Box Culvert Road under Paltan police station and fled. In connection with the incident, on December 14, Abdullah Al Jaber, member secretary of Inquilab Mancha, filed a case at Paltan police station alleging attempted murder. Charges were brought against the accused under sections 120(B)/326/307/109/34 of the Penal Code. Later, on December 20, following an application by the investigating officer, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Siddiq Azad ordered to add section 302 (murder) of the Penal Code to the case.

title: JCD leader hacked to death in Bhola
body: A leader of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, the student wing of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, was hacked to death in front of his house in the Closer Bazar area under Sadar upazila in Bhola district on Wednesday night. The deceased is Rezwan Amin Sifat, 25, a leader of Rajapur Union Chhatra Dal and an aspirant for the post of the president of the union unit of the students’ organisation. According to the victim’s father, Sifat left home in the evening to attend the reception programme in Dhaka marking the homecoming of BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman. As he reached the road in front of his house, five to six people, including his cousin Hasib Hawlader attacked him with sharp weapons, leaving him critically injured in a pool of blood. Locals rescued Sifat and took him to Bhola General Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The victim’s father Alauddin Howlader alleged that the murder stemmed from a long-standing land dispute with his brother Helal Howlader, who is a former union parishad member. He claimed that Helal, who is involved in Awami League politics, had been using political influence to harass their family for the past 17 years. He further alleged that Helal’s son Hasib led the attack and killed Sifat over the land dispute. Dr Junaid Hossain, medical officer of the emergency department at Bhola General Hospital, said that Sifat was brought to the hospital in a critical condition at about 8:00pm Wednesday and was declared dead after examination. ‘He had multiple marks of injuries on different parts of his body. It is presumed that he died due to excessive bleeding,’ the doctor said. Bhola sadar police station officer-in-Charge Monirul Islam said that the police were conducting raids to arrest the killers. Neither Helal nor Hasib could be reached over the telephone for their comments.

title: BGB seizes Yaba, contraband goods worth Tk 29 lakh in Kushtia
body: The Border Guard Bangladesh seized drugs and contraband goods worth about Taka 29 lakh in a series of operations conducted in different border and urban areas in Kushtia on Thursday. In a press release, Lieutenant Colonel Rashed Kamal Rony, commander of BGB Battalion 47 in Kushtia, said that the BGB members seized 7,000 Yaba pills during a search of a Meherpur-to-Kushtia-bound bus at Mirpur bus stand area on Thursday noon. The BGB conducted another drive at Lalon Chatwar area in the district town, where 4,000 packets of illegal fake bidis were recovered. On the same day, the BGB seized 30 bottles of Indian liquor, 700 pieces of Sildenafil tablets and 1,140 pieces of chocolate fireworks from the Borderpara area under the jurisdiction of Kazipur BOP. Additionally, another 30 bottles of Indian liquor and 500 pieces of Sildenafil tablets were recovered from the Dharmadah border area. Later, BGB members recovered 177 bottles of Indian syrup from the Char Mathpara area under Charchilmari BOP.

title: Case filed over Moghbazar crude bomb explosion that kills youth
body: A case has been filed in connection with the murder of a youth in a crude bomb explosion at Moghbazar in Bangladesh's capital Dhaka. Ali Akbar Majumdar, father of the victim, filed the case with Hatirjheel police against some unidentified people early Thursday, said Golam Mortuza, officer-in-charge of the police station. Siam Majumdar, 30, a construction worker, was killed when a crude bomb thrown by miscreants from the Moghbazar–Mouchak flyover exploded near the Moghbazar Muktijoddha Sangsad gate in the capital on Wednesday evening. Md Mohiuddin, inspector, operations, of Hatirjheel police, said that the crude bomb was hurled from the flyover on the road and hit Siam on his head, killing him on the spot.

title: Nomination paper collected for Jamaat chief
body: Nomination papers were collected on Thursday on behalf of Jamaat chief Shafiqur Rahman to contest the Bangladesh national election from the Dhaka-15 constituency. ‘The nomination paper was collected for Ameer of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami today,’ said Md Yunus Ali, the returning officer for Dhaka-13 and Dhaka-15 constituencies on Thursday afternoon. As of Thursday, nomination papers for eight aspirants, including BNP nominated Md Shafiqul Islam Khan, have been picked to contest the election from the Dhaka-15 constituency, he told UNB. On behalf of the Jamaat chief, a resident of Dhaka-15 constituency Mohammad Shah Alam collected the nomination paper from the office of the returning officer at the Electoral Training Institute in the city’s Agargaon area in presence of several Jamaat central leaders, including its assistant secretaries general Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair and Abdul Halim. The deadline for submission of nomination papers will expire on December 29, according to the schedule announced by the Election Commission on December 11 last. Till Thursday, the nomination papers were collected for a total of 21 aspirants -13 in Dhaka-13 and 8 in Dhaka-15, but only one nomination paper was submitted, said the returning officer. In Dhaka-15 constituency comprised of the Ward No: 04, 13, 14 and 16 of Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC), the nomination papers were collected for Shafiqur Rahman (Jamaat), Shafiqul Islam Khan (BNP), Muhammad Alamgir Ferdous (NCP), SM Fazlul Haque (Islami Andolan Bangladesh-IAB), AKM Shafiqul Islam (Gonoforum) and Khan Shoab Aman Ullah (Independent), Ahmed Sajedul Haque (Independent) and Md Tanjil Islam (Independent). In Dhaka-13 constituency comprising Ward No: 28-34 of the DNCC, the nomination papers for 13 aspirants were collected, but only one nomination paper (independent aspirant Sohel Rana) was submitted on Thursday, he said. The 13 aspirants are Bobby Hajjaj (BNP), Md Kamruzzaman Jewel (BNP), Kayes Mahmud (BNP/Independent), Md Akram Hossain (NCP), Md Mamunul Haque (Bangladesh Khelafat Majlish), Md Murad Hossain (IAB), Nek Mohammad (JSD), Md Mahbubur Rahman (Nagorik Oikya), Md Sohel Rana (Bangladesh Jatiya Party-BJP), Shahriar Iftekhar (Ganomukti Jote), Md Ashraful Islam (Bangladesh Republican Party-BRP), Sohel Rana (Independent) and Sheikh Md Rabiul Islam (Independent). On December 11, chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin announced the schedule to hold the 13th parliamentary election and the referendum on the July National Charter (Constitutional Reform) Implementation Order simultaneously on February 12 next. According to the election schedule, the scrutiny of nomination papers is on December 30-January 4 and the last date for the withdrawal of candidature is January 20. The election campaign will start on January 22 and continue till 48 hours before the balloting period (7:30am on February 10).

title: President hosts reception on Christmas Day
body: President Mohammed Shahabuddin and his wife Dr Rebeka Sultana on Thursday hosted a reception for members of the Christian community at the Durbar Hall of Bangabhaban marking Christmas Day, the biggest religious festival of the Christian community. The president exchanged greetings with the leaders and representatives of Christian community joined the reception began at 12:00 noon. Religious affairs adviser to the interim government AFM Khalid Hossain was present. President flanked with the guests also cut a ‘Merry Christmas’ cake while a cultural troupe performed Christmas carols. Archbishop Bejoy Nicephorus D’Cruze, Bangladesh Christian Association President Nirmal Rozario, Father Albert Rozario, Reverend Martha Das, foreign diplomats and representatives of various foreign missions, distinguished members of the Christian community joined the reception. Senior officials of Bangabhaban were present.

title: Over 7.17 lakh voters registered for 13th general election
body: A total of 717,217 voters have so far registered their names to cast their votes in the upcoming 13th general election and referendum through postal ballot, Election Commission said. Apart from expatriate Bangladeshis, government officials and employees engaged in electoral duties, as well as government employees residing outside their designated voting areas, are registering through the Postal Vote BD app. The EC has already begun dispatching postal ballots to expatriate voters worldwide. Salim Ahmad Khan, team leader of the Out of Country Voting System and Implementation (OCV-SDI) project, confirmed that postal ballots have been sent to 22,888 expatriate voters in different countries in the last six days. Data available on the EC website at 12:00 noon today shows that 659,356 are male and 57,859 are female voters have registered their names. Among expatriate voters, Saudi Arabia tops the list with 154,692 registered voters. Next is Qatar with 57,316, Oman with 43,206, Malaysia with 40,333, the United Arab Emirates with 30,662 and the United States with 25,500 registered voters. Within the country, 186,305 voters have registered under the ‘In Country Postal Vote’ category. District-wise registration figures show Cumilla leading with 66,592 registered voters, followed by Dhaka (58,585), Chittagong (57,458), Noakhali (38,118), Sylhet (28,067) and Chandpur (26,356). At the constituency level, Feni-3 recorded the highest number of registrations with 10,779 voters. Other notable constituencies include Chittagong-15 with 9,410 voters, Cumilla-10 with 8,935 and Noakhali-1 with over 8,800 registered postal voters. The EC has been dispatching ballots in phases to various countries. Over the past week, ballots have been sent to countries including Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Malaysia, Oman, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, Italy, Germany, France, Japan, South Korea and several European and Middle Eastern countries. Meanwhile, the Election Commission has extended the registration deadline up to December 31, 2025.

title: Tarique reaches Evarecare to meet ailing mother
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman on Thursday evening reached Evercare Hospital to meet his ailing mother, Begum Khaleda Zia, former prime minister and Bangladesh Nationalist Party chairperson, at the hospital. Tarique's motorcade reached Evercare Hospital at about 5:50pm on Wednesday, as he directly came to the hospital after addressing a public reception held in the 300 Feet area of Purbachal in Dhaka. Meanwhile, hundreds of leaders and activists of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and its associate bodies gathered in front of the Evercare Hospital to welcome Tarique Rahman. Md Abu Bakar Siddique Kayes, BNP Dhaka North City's ward no. 21 joint secretary, said that he came to the hospital to welcome their leader, Tarique Rahman. 'It is a matter of great joy that Tarique Rahman will come here to meet his mother. We pray for our leader Begum Khaleda’s swift recovery,’ he said. Members of the police, the Bangladesh Army, the Rapid Action Battalion, Border Guard Bangladesh and the Armed Police Battalion were deployed near the hospital to ensure security. Khaleda was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis on November 27. The 79-year-old leader, who has long been suffering from multiple chronic health complications, including liver and kidney diseases, heart ailments, hypertension, diabetes, arthritis and recurrent infections, was admitted to Evercare Hospital on November 23. Earlier, Tarique returned to Bangladesh from London with his wife, Zubaida Rahman, and daughter, Zaima Rahman, ending his 17 years of exile. A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying them landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka via Sylhet at about 11:40am. After landing in Dhaka, Tarique Rahman was received at the airport by BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and senior party leaders, including members of the party’s standing committee. They welcomed him at the VIP lounge of HSIA at about 11:55am. His mother-in-law, Syeda Iqbal Mandu Banu, also welcomed him with a floral garland. Strict security measures were taken at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport and in nearby areas for his arrival. Multiple layers of security were deployed around the VVIP terminal, with members of the army, Border Guard Bangladesh, air force, police and Rapid Action Battalion on duty. RAB dog squads conducted searches, while a special army team was also stationed in the area. In addition, the personal security force of the BNP chairperson and acting chairman, known as the CSF, was overseeing the overall security arrangements.

title: BNP wants to build a safe Bangladesh: Tarique
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party wants to build a safe and secure Bangladesh, its acting chairman Tarique Rahman said on Thursday. Addressing a public reception, he said the party envisions a country that reflects the dreams of a mother. ‘Together, we will build a Bangladesh that every mother dreams of. That is, we want to build a safe Bangladesh—where every woman, man or child can leave home safely and, return home safely,’ Tarique said. He made the remarks while speaking at a mass reception held in the 300 Feet area of Purbachal. Earlier, at about 3:50pm, Tarique Rahman arrived at the reception venue, where the 300 Feet Road, also known as the July 36 Expressway, and surrounding areas became lively with slogans from party leaders, activists and supporters. The area witnessed scenes of great excitement as he took to the stage and waved in response to greetings and expressions of goodwill from the crowd. In his speech, Tarique said that just as the people of the country achieved independence in 1971, people from all walks of life came together in 2024 to protect Bangladesh’s independence and sovereignty. He said that the people of Bangladesh now want to regain their right to speak freely and restore their democratic rights. Tarique reached Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at approximately 11:40am on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from London. From the early hours of the morning, massive crowds gathered at the reception site in the capital’s Bashundhara area. By 10:00am, the 300 Feet Road and surrounding neighbourhoods were packed with supporters, leaving little space to stand in adjacent areas. Members of the security forces were deployed across the area to maintain order. Large screens installed on and around the stage showed documentaries on BNP founder and former president Ziaur Rahman, and the July uprising. Supporters continued to pour in from both the western and eastern highways, with the flow of people showing no sign of slowing. Processions of BNP leaders and activists arrived from various points including the airport, Purbachal, Banani and the Jamuna Future Park area, chanting slogans and waving party flags as they made their way towards the reception venue. The atmosphere along the 300 Feet Road was festive, with slogans echoing throughout the area. Processions, some accompanied by band music, added to the celebratory mood as party supporters welcomed Tarique Rahman back to the country.

title: Tarique calls chief adviser after landing at airport, expresses gratitude for security arrangements
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chair Tarique Rahman on Thursday expressed his gratitude to interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus for the arrangements made, particularly for his security, on the occasion of his return from London. Soon after landing at the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, Tarique Rahman made a phone call to the chief adviser from the airport lounge. A video of the conversation was later shared in Tarique’s verified Facebook page with the caption, ‘Thanks to the chief adviser’. In the video, Tarique Rahman is heard asking Professor Yunus about his health before thanking him on behalf of himself and his family. ‘I would like to thank you on my behalf and on behalf of my family. You have made various arrangements, especially for my security. Thank you so much,’ he said before ending the call with greetings. Earlier, a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying Tarique Rahman along with his family members first landed at the Sylhet Osmani International Airport at 9:57am. After a brief stopover, the aircraft reached the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at around 11:40am. Tarique returned home ending his long 17-year exile in the United Kingdom.

title: Christmas being celebrated across Bangladesh, world
body: The Christian community is celebrating Christmas Day in Bangladesh like elsewhere in the world on Thursday in a befitting manner commemorating the birth of Jesus Christ. Christmas, the biggest religious festival of the Christian community, is the celebration of rebirth, new beginning, forgiveness and peace, and renewing relationship with God and human being. The celebrations of the Christmas Day feature decoration of Christmas trees with colourful lights, special prayers, and distribution of gifts among children and exchange of pleasantries. Christmas carols and hymns are sung before and after the prayer sessions at the churches. Bangladesh Television and Bangladesh Betar and different private TV channels and radio stations are airing programmes highlighting the significance of the day. Chief adviser Muhammad Yunus exchanged greetings with representatives of the Christian community at the State Guesthouse Jamuna in Dhaka marking Christmas Day on Wednesday. The chief adviser said the interim government aims to build a healthy society, adding that the July Charter has been prepared to uphold the spirit of the mass uprising. ‘You are the mirror of society. By looking at you, we can understand whether everything is in order,’ Professor Yunus said while exchanging Christmas greetings with representatives of the Christian community. Archbishop Bejoy N D’Cruze described Jesus Christ as a universal figure and said that inspired by Christ’s ideals of forgiveness and service to humanity, millions of people around the world, including in Bangladesh, are celebrating Christmas with joy and enthusiasm. Leaders of the Christian Religious Welfare Trust also thanked the interim government for granting Tk 2.5 crore to the trust on the occasion of Christmas. They said the grant was being distributed in three phases among 800 churches across the country.

title: 6 more arrested over lynching RMG worker Dipu
body: The police on Thursday arrested six more people in connection with the lynching of a Hindu youth at Bhaluka upazila in Mymensingh district allegedly for hurting Islamic religious sentiments. The six arrested people allegedly forced victim Dipu Chandra Das, 25, to resign from his job at Pioneer Knit Composite Factory, according to the district police. The arrested are Takbir, 22, of Sunamganj district, Ruhul Amin, 42, of Thakurgaon district, Nur Alam, 33, of Sadar upazila and Shamim Mia, 28, of Tarakanda upazila in Mymensingh district, Selim Mia, 22, of Noakhali district and Masum Khalashi, 23, of Madaripur district. With the latest arrests, the total number of accused arrested in the case stood at 18. On December 18, Dipu was lynched and his body was burnt after hanging it from a tree branch near his workplace in the Dubaliapara area under Bhaluka upazila. He was beaten to death allegedly for hurting religious sentiments by making derogatory remarks about Prophet Muhammad. The investigators, however, found no evidence of hurting religious sentiments against the victim. Mymensingh police’s additional superintendent for finance and administration, Abdullah Al Mamun, said that the Detective Branch of the police arrested the six accused in a raid in the Kashar area of Habirbari union under Bhaluka upazila at midnight. ‘The arrestees incited the employees present inside the factory, and pressured Dipu to be relieved of his job,’ he said. An investigation was under way to determine why Dipu was handed over to the public instead of the police, ADC Abdullah said, adding that a drive was going on to arrest the other accused.

title: Tarique Rahman begins journey from airport towards 300 feet road
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman has begun his journey from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport towards the 300 feet road, where party leaders and activities have gathered to welcome him. Tarique Rahman boarded a bulletproof bus as his motorcade left the airport at around 12:30pm. Earlier, he returned to Bangladesh from London with his wife, Zubaida Rahman, and daughter, Zaima Rahman, ending nearly 17 years of exile. A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying them landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka via Sylhet at around 11:40am. After landing in Dhaka, Tarique Rahman was received at the airport by BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and senior party leaders, including members of the party’s standing committee. They welcomed him at the VIP lounge of HSIA at 11:56am. His mother-in-law, Syeda Iqbal Mandu Banu, also welcomed him with a floral garland. Strict security measures were in place at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport for his arrival. Multiple layers of security were deployed around the VVIP terminal, with members of the army, Border Guard Bangladesh, air force, police and Rapid Action Battalion on duty. RAB dog squads conducted searches, while a special army team was also stationed in the area. In addition, the personal security force of the BNP chairperson and acting chairman, known as the CSF, was overseeing the overall security arrangements. BNP leaders and activists started crowding the 300 Feet Road since Thursday morning to welcome him.

title: Flight carrying Tarique Rahman lands at Dhaka airport
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman returned home from London on Thursday with his wife and daughter after his 17-year exile in London. A flight of Biman Bangladesh Airlines carrying them landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport via Sylhet in Dhaka at 11:40am. Earlier, the flight made a stopover at Sylhet's Osmani International Airport at about 9:58am.

title: Bulletproof bus arrives at airport ahead of Tarique Rahman’s return
body: A bulletproof bus arrived at the CIP gate of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Thursday morning amid tight security ahead of the return of Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman. The specially prepared bus, painted in red and green, bears large portraits of BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia, BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman and party founder Ziaur Rahman. It also displays slogans highlighting democracy and political struggle. The vehicle’s windows are reinforced, and security personnel were seen surrounding it as it entered the airport’s CIP area. Senior BNP leaders, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Tarique Rahman is likely to use the bus to travel directly to Evercare Hospital after completing airport formalities to visit his ailing mother. On the way, he is scheduled to deliver a brief address at a gathering on the 36 July Expressway, also known as the 300 Feet Road. Security in and around the airport has been tightened, with members of the army, police, RAB and other law enforcement agencies deployed to ensure safety during his movement.

title: BNP activists crowding 300 Feet Road, adjacent places to welcome Tarique
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party leaders and activists started crowding the 300 Feet Road since Thursday morning to welcome its acting chairman Tarique Rahman’s homecoming after 17 years. Leaders and activists were joining the rally since Morning holding placards, photos of Tarique Rahman, fastoons and wearing T-shirts and caps. Kazi Khairuzzaman Shipon, BNP Bagherhat district vice-president, said that he reached Dhaka city two days ago and was staying at a hotel for attending the event. ‘We are here since yesterday night. We came here to see our leader,’ he added. He also hoped that the country would be on the right direction under Tarique Rahman’s leadership. BNP activists are also thronging the venue through bus, truck and pick-up vans from different places in Dhaka and elsewhere across the country. The gate of Basundhara Residiential Area near 300 feet area is now almost blocked with BNP leaders and activists. They are chanting slogans for Tarique Rahman’s homecoming like ‘Ma Mati Kapchhe Tarique Rahman Aschhe.’ Sumon Jaman, a BNP supporter from Tongi, said that he usually did not attend political programmes, but came here to see Tarique Rahman. A good number of law enforcement agencies members were also deployed in different places in the capital. Tarique was arrested during an anti-corruption drive in March 2007 and released on bail in September 2008, after which he travelled to London for medical treatment on September 11, 2008, and remained there. Following the fall of Awami League’s 16-year rule through a mass uprising on August 5, 2024, the High Court acquitted him of all cases filed during both the caretaker government period and the Awami League administration, clearing the legal obstacles to his return.

title: Tight security at airport ahead of return of Tarique Rahman
body: Strict security measures have been put in place at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport ahead of the return of Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman. Several layers of security have been deployed around the VVIP terminal, with personnel from the army, BGB, air force, police and RAB on duty. RAB dog squads are conducting searches, while a special army unit has also been stationed in the area. In addition, the personal security force of the BNP chairperson and acting chairman, known as the CSF, is overseeing the security arrangements. From early Thursday morning, heightened security was visible across the airport area. Outside the airport, check posts have been set up at several points where vehicles are being searched. BNP Media Cell convener Maudud Hossain Alamgir Pavel told reporters that Tarique Rahman is expected to land first at Sylhet airport before flying to Dhaka. He said the stopover in Sylhet may be brief, allowing the flight to reach Dhaka at about 11:45am. Pavel said the 36 July Expressway, also known as the 300 Feet Road, has already turned into a sea of people. He added that formalities at the airport would be very brief, with only BNP standing committee members welcoming Tarique Rahman with flowers. After arriving, Tarique Rahman will travel to Evercare Hospital to visit his ailing mother. On the way, he is scheduled to address a short public gathering on the 36 July Expressway, where he is expected to thank the people and call for unity. BNP health affairs secretary Rafiqul Islam said that an adequate number of law enforcement personnel have been deployed to ensure security. According to Biman Bangladesh Airlines, Tarique Rahman left London’s Heathrow Airport on Wednesday night at about 12:15am on a regular Biman flight bound for Dhaka. He is travelling with his wife, Zubaida Rahman, and daughter, Zaima Rahman. The flight is scheduled to land at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 11:45am. BNP standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed said senior party leaders will receive Tarique Rahman at the airport before he travels by road to Evercare Hospital. On the way, he will attend a reception programme organised by the party. The BNP has arranged a brief event on the 36 July Expressway, where Tarique Rahman will express his gratitude to the people and offer prayers. After visiting Evercare Hospital, he will later go to his residence at house number 196 on Gulshan Avenue.

title: Nation ready to welcome Tarique Rahman in fascist free Bangladesh: Salahuddin
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party Standing Committee member Salahuddin Ahmed has said that the nation is ready to accord a grand reception to the party’s acting chairman Tarique Rahman in fascist free Bangladesh. ‘The fascist regime was toppled by a student-people uprising last year. We are very happy and pleased that the nation will welcome BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman in a fascist free Bangladesh,’ he said while briefing journalists in front of the VIP gate of the Hazrat Shahjalal Airport in the capital on Thursday morning. The BNP leader said the country and the world would see the return of Tarique Rahman. Asked about Wednesday night’s bomb blast in Dhaka’s Moghbazar area, he said this was an attempt to foil the elections. ‘Fascist forces are active. They are trying to destabilise the country from India and hinder the democratic journey through foiling polls. But we will prevent them unitedly,’ he added. Salahuddin sought people’s cooperation to make Bangladesh truly a discrimination free and democratic country. Tarique is scheduled to travel from London’s Heathrow Airport on a regular Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight, departing around midnight Bangladesh time on Thursday, and that the aircraft was expected to arrive in Dhaka at 11:50am the same day after a brief stopover in Sylhet. Senior leaders of the BNP, including members of its standing committee, are now waiting to receive him at the airport in an on-door reception. Tarique Rahman is set to return to Dhaka today after more than 17 years in exile in the United Kingdom, marking a moment of major political significance. The homecoming has generated widespread anticipation nationwide, with supporters preparing to welcome him.
