title: Khoda Baksh resigns as special assistant for home ministry
body: Banglades interim government’s special assistant for the home affairs ministry, Khoda Baksh Chowdhury, resigned on Wednesday amid deteriorating law and order situation. The president, Mohammed Shahabuddin, accepted the resignation of Khoda Baksh, a former inspector general of police, who was given the status and executive power of a state minister, according to a gazette notification issued by the Cabinet Division. His resignation came days after organised attacks on media outlets the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star in the capital Dhaka on December 18 night without any visible efforts from the law enforcement agencies to prevent the attackers and harassment of Editors’ Council president and New Age editor Nurul Kabir, who rushed to the Daily Star premises, which were set ablaze, to rescue journalists trapped there in the early hours of December 19. On the night of December 18, hundreds of attackers vandalised and looted the offices of the Prothom Alo in the capital’s Karwan Bazar area and The Daily Star on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, and then set fire to the offices. Officials said that Khoda Baksh opted to resign in the face of sudden deterioration in the law and order situation although he was offered the expatriates’ welfare and overseas employment ministry in the same position. In November 2024, the interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus appointed Khoda Baksh as the special assistant to the home affairs ministry with the status of state minister.

title: Tarique leaves UK for Bangladesh
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman left Heathrow Airport early Thursday for Dhaka, ending nearly 17 years in exile in London and sparking widespread interest, emotion and political excitement across the country. 'Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight BG-102, carrying Tarique and his entourage, took off around 12:23 am (BST),' said BNP media cell member Sayrul Kabir Khan. The flight is scheduled to land at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 11:50 am on Thursday, via Sylhet Osmani International Airport. Senior BNP leaders, including members of the party’s Standing Committee, will receive him at the airport. Tarique is travelling with his wife, Zubaida Rahman, his daughter, Barrister Zaima Rahman, and other personal aides. Zaima Rahman’s pet cat, Jebu, is also travelling to Bangladesh with the family. It will also mark the end of Zaima Rahman’s nearly 17-year exile in London. Party leaders say her return symbolises the close of a long chapter of forced separation from the country. The party has completed extensive preparations for his welcome, with measures taken to ensure maximum security. After arrival, Tarique will briefly address party leaders, supporters, and the nation near the 300 Feet area of the capital, where thousands are expected to gather. He will offer thanks to people and perform a short prayer of gratitude for his safe return. Following the programme, Tarique will visit his mother and BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia, who is currently receiving treatment at the Coronary Care Unit (CCU) of Evercare Hospital, Bashundhara. After spending some time with her, he will proceed to House No-196 on Gulshan Avenue, where he will stay. A three-layer security system has been arranged at the reception venue, combining government security with the party’s own special arrangements. Tarique spent more than 17 years in exile in London, living with his wife, Dr Zubaida Rahman, and daughter, Barrister Zaima Rahman. From abroad, he continued to guide BNP, keeping in touch with leaders and activists and overseeing the party’s political strategy. Excitement and anticipation have spread among BNP leaders and activists in Dhaka and across the country as the long-awaited return of the party’s Acting Chairman approaches. Supporters have already begun arriving in the capital to catch a glimpse of their leader. Tarique left Bangladesh in 2008 for medical treatment after being released from jail during the military-backed caretaker government period and later settled in the UK with his family. During his exile, he faced numerous legal hurdles but was recently cleared of all cases. While Zubaida Rahman visited Bangladesh twice earlier, Tarique had been unable to return until now.

title: Environmentalists call for crackdown on New Year fireworks
body: Environmental experts and campaigners, criticising lax enforcement of law, have called for proactive measures against indiscriminate detonation of fireworks during New Year celebrations. They warned that traders and retailers had already stockpiled fireworks and expressed concern over delayed preventive action, with only a week left until December 31. Regulatory officials, however, told New Age on Monday that an inter-ministerial meeting was held on the day to plan measures in this regard during this year’s New Year celebrations. Professor Ahmad Kamruzzaman Majumder, founder and director of Stamford University Bangladesh’s Centre for Atmospheric Pollution Studies, criticised that the government was already late in acting. ‘The government must now initiate preventive steps to control fireworks damaging for both environment and public health,’ he said. Since 2017, CAPS has been monitoring air quality and noise pollution during New Year celebrations in Dhaka. According to its latest analysis, Dhaka’s air quality index was 256 on December 31, 2024, but rose to 321 on January 1, 2025, indicating 25 per cent deterioration due to excessive fireworks. CAPS data also showed that on December 30, 2024, the equivalent continuous sound level (Leq) in Dhaka was 62 decibels, which surged to 103 decibels during New Year celebrations, showing a 53 per cent increase compared to the previous day. On December 31, 2024, environment, forest and climate change adviser Syeda Rizwana Hasan said that the Department of Environment would conduct mobile courts against indiscriminate detonation of fireworks. However, DoE law enforcement data show that no punitive action was taken on January 1, 2025. On December 30, 2024, the Detective Branch of Dhaka Metropolitan Police arrested only one person—Sajjad Hossain Rahat—from Lalbagh for stockpiling a large quantity of fireworks and firecrackers. Localities in Old Dhaka, including Lalbagh, Tantibazar and Shankharibazar, are known as major hubs for retailing fireworks. Local traders said that explosives were mainly imported from China and India. Since 2018, the DMP has imposed restrictions on New Year fireworks under the Explosives Act 1884, though the rules have never been strictly enforced. On January 1, 2022, a four-month-old child, Tanzim Umair, died after being terrified by loud fireworks on New Year’s Eve. That night, hundreds of birds reportedly died due to fireworks and sky lanterns, while several fire incidents were also recorded nationwide. Between January 11, 2022, and December 30, 2024, multiple writ petitions were filed with the High Court seeking a ban on fireworks and firecrackers. On December 31, 2024, the High Court directed law enforcement agencies and other authorities to strictly prevent fireworks on rooftops of buildings to avoid accidents on Thirty-First Night. Animal welfare campaigner Amirul Rajiv, coordinator of the Bangladesh Tree Protection Movement, criticised the government for failing to implement the court order. ‘Dogs, cats and birds become terrified by the loud sounds of fireworks and often flee in panic, unable to return to their territories,’ Rajiv said, highlighting the impact on animals. To raise awareness, writer Sadika Rumon and her friends launched a social media campaign under the platform Prakritimangal in mid-December. ‘We are trying to make parents and children aware with slogans like “No celebration by killing birds”,’ Sadika said, urging people to avoid fireworks in residential areas that shelter animals. DoE director general Md Kamruzzaman told New Age that the recently issued Noise Pollution (Control) Rules 2025 prohibited fireworks and similar explosives anywhere at night. Violators face up to one month’s imprisonment, a maximum fine of Tk 50,000, or both, under the new rules. He added that the government decided to raise public awareness through text messages to mobile phone users and scrolling messages on public and private television channels. Mosque imams would also be instructed to discourage fireworks during Friday prayers ahead of the New Year, Kamruzzaman said. ‘Several mobile courts will operate on New Year’s Eve to enforce the law and raise awareness about the environmental and health impacts of fireworks,’ he said.

title: Motorcycle rider’s ‘associate’ held with firearm
body: The police on Wednesday arrested an alleged associate of the rider of the motorcycle used in the killing of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi. The police also seized a foreign firearm and ammunition. The arrested is Himon Rahman Shikdar, 32, alleged associate of Alamgir Sheikh, who rode the motorcycle used in the shooting of Hadi and an alleged activist of the Awami League’s youth wing Juba League. Himon was arrested on Wednesday morning at a local motel at Adabor in Dhaka city, said Jewel Rana, additional commissioner of police for Tejgaon Division. The police later in another raid at Adabor recovered a foreign pistol and three rounds of bullets during a raid also at Adabor, he said. ‘Himon had close relationship with Alamgir, but the police were investigating whether Himon had anything do with Hadi’s killing,’ he said, adding that necessary legal action was taken against the arrestee. Meanwhile, a Dhaka court on Wednesday ordered ballistic examination of fire cartridges and bullet-like objects recovered from the scene of the shooting that killed Hadi, Bangladesh Sangbad Sanstha reported. Dhaka Additional Metropolitan Magistrate Awlad Hossain Mohammad Junaid issued the order on Wednesday in response to an application filed by the case investigation officer. The court directed the special police superintendent of the Ballistics Branch of the Criminal Investigation Department to examine the seized evidence and submit a detailed opinion in the interest of proper investigation. Osman Hadi, also one of the organisers of the July uprising, breathed his last at a Singapore hospital at around 9:45pm Bangladesh time on December 18. The 32 year-old leader, Hadi, who was an independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency in the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad polls, was shot in the head on December 12 in city. The incident took place a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. He initially underwent surgery at Dhaka Medical College Hospital and was later admitted to Evercare Hospital. For advanced treatment, he was airlifted to Singapore, where he succumbed to his injuries on the night of December 18.

title: Pro-BNP panel sweeps RU officers’ association polls
body: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party-backed panel swept the Rajshahi University Officers’ Association election as the panel bagged all the posts, leaving the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami-backed panel without a single post. Chief election commissioner Md Shahidullah announced the results on Tuesday night, following a day-long voting held at the university’s Juberi Building. From the pro-BNP panel, Anowarul Islam was elected as president and Riaz Uddin as general secretary. Anowarul bagged 449 votes while his rival from Jamaat-e-Islami-backed panel Masud Rana got 248 votes. On the other hand, Riaz managed to secure 507 votes while his rival Kazi Mamun Rana bagged 186 votes. The other elected office bearers are vice-president Rokonuzzaman Mamun, treasurer Al-Amin Bidyut, joint secretary Monwar Hossain Utpal, office secretary AHM Rakibul Islam, publicity secretary Abdul Manik, literature and cultural secretary Alamgir Hossain, social welfare and sports secretary Mujibur Rahman and organising secretary Forman Ali. The elected members are Ali Reza, Abdul Matin, Roksana Begum, Mainul Islam, Borhan Uddin, Shahidul Islam, Habiba Haider and Md Nasir Uddin.

title: Govt issues new rules for VVIP security
body: The government has issued the gazette of the ‘resident, Prime Minister or Chief Adviser and Very Very Important Persons Security Rules 2025, which was formulated to ensure the security of the president, prime minister, chief adviser and other very very important persons. The chief adviser’s office issued the gazette, signed by secretary M Saifullah Panna, to this end on Tuesday as per the president’s order. According to the gazette, the rules will come into immediate effect. Through the new rules, the security management of the highest level persons of the state has been brought under a well-organised, modern and clear legal framework. The rules have detailed the responsibilities, structure and duties of the concerned forces and organisations to ensure the security of the president, the prime minister, the chief adviser and other very important persons in their movement, residence, workplace, event venues and during their visits, the gazette read. The rules have been formulated considering the recent security challenges and realities. It is expected that through the new rules, it will be possible to make the overall law and order system more effective and strong apart from ensuring security of important state persons. The relevant sources confirmed that a notification containing necessary explanations and detailed instructions in this regard will be published separately later.

title: Postal vote registration deadline extended
body: The election commission has extended the registration time for voting in the 13th National Parliament Election and Referendum through the ‘Postal Vote BD’ app until December 31. ‘The deadline for registration through our ‘Postal Vote BD’ app was fixed until December 25. Now it has been extended to December 31.’ EC senior secretary Akhtar Ahmed told reporters. He said that those who have not yet participated in the registration process can complete their registration by December 31. Regarding a request to remain open Bank next Saturday, the EC Secretary said, ‘We have requested Bangladesh Bank to keep scheduled banks open next Saturday so that the issues relevant to the nomination paper submission and any issues of the bank, if any, can be completed properly by the candidates or their agents.’ Responding to a question about following the code of conduct in the elections, the EC secretary said, ‘We will all follow the code of conduct. That should be our objective.’ Expatriate Bangladeshis, election officials and employees, and government employees outside their areas are registering to cast postal votes through the ‘Postal Vote BD’ app. Meanwhile, as of 5.15pm on Wednesday, according to the information provided on the EC website, 681,060 voters have registered. On the other hand, the election commission has already started sending postal ballots to expatriates. Salim Ahmad Khan, team leader of the ‘Out of Country Voting System and Implementation’ project, confirmed to BSS that ballots have been sent to 168,900 expatriate voters in different countries of the world in the last five days.

title: Local BNP protests at Rashed Khan nomination
body: Kaliganj upazila unit of Bangladesh Nationalist Party in Jhenaidah on Wednesday brought out a rally protesting against the nomination of Rashed Khan, general secretary of the Gono Odhikar Parishad, for the Jhenaidah 4, Kaliganj-sadar partial, parliamentary constituency. Around 100 leaders and activists of the party brought out the rally in front of the upazila BNP office, which ended at the same place after parading through the main streets of the upazila. Speakers at the rally criticised the BNP central leadership for selecting an outsider who was not a registered voter in the constituency. They said that long-serving local leaders, who had contributed to the Kaliganj unit for over 17 years, were overlooked. The nomination of someone with no local ties disregards the efforts of grassroots leaders and risks weakening the party locally, a protester said. The protest highlighted the internal dissatisfaction within Kaliganj BNP over candidate selection, raising concerns about party unity ahead of the upcoming elections.

title: ICT sets January 20 to deliver verdict
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Wednesday set January 20 to deliver the verdict in the crimes against humanity case over the killing of six protesters at Chankharpool during the July 2024 mass uprising. The case is against former DMP commissioner Habibur Rahman, four senior police officers, and three constables. The seven other accused include former DMP joint commissioner Sudip Kumar Chakraborty, former Ramna assistant deputy commissioner Shah Alam Md Akhterul Islam, former Ramna assistant commissioner Mohammad Imrul, Shahbagh police station inspector (operations) Ashrad Hossain, and suspended constables Sujan Hossain, Imaz Hossain Imon, and Nasirul Islam. Of them, Ashrad, and suspended constables Sujan Hossain, Imaz Hossain Imon, and Nasirul Islam are in jail. The remaining four are still in hiding and were tried in absentia. The three-judge tribunal, chaired by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder, fixed the date after completing closing arguments. The prosecution sought the death penalty for all eight accused. The defence lawyers sought their clients’ acquittal, arguing that the accused had no command responsibility and acted under orders. This will be the second verdict among the 13 July uprising cases pending before the two tribunals for trials. Although deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan and detained former inspector general of police Chowdhury Abdullah Al Mamun were named as conspirators in the Chankharpool killings, they were not included in this case because they are already accused in a separate case over superior command responsibility for the July incidents. On November 17, Hasina and Asaduzzaman were tried in absentia and sentenced to death, while Mamun, who became a state witness, was jailed for five years. According to the charge sheet, senior police officials allegedly ordered, abetted, and facilitated the shootings, while constables carried out the firing that left six protesters dead on August 5, 2024 when Sheikh Hasina fled the country amid student-led mass uprising. The victims of the August 5 shooting are Shahriar Khan Anas, a class X student who left behind a heartbreaking letter to his mother, Sheikh Mahadi Hasan Zunayed who is also known as Mostakin, Mohammad Yakub, Md Rakib Hawlader, Mohammad Ismail Haque, and Manik Mia, also known as Saharik Chowdhury. Anas, the very young student, left his Gandaria residence that morning after writing, ‘I cannot stay at home while people from all walks of life have joined the July uprising,’ according to the case. 26 prosecution witnesses, including Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, recently resigned adviser for the ministry of local government, rural development and cooperatives, who is also an organiser of the mass uprising, testified in the tribunal during the trial. Video evidence was also submitted during the trial. The prosecution alleged that the police failed to prevent attacks on protesters and, in some instances, facilitated them.

title: Protest on against RMG worker lynching
body: Fresh calls for justice were made on Wednesday in continued protests over the gruesome lynching and burning of readymade garment worker Dipu Chandra Das in Mymensingh. Chief adviser’s press secretary Shafiqul Alam, meanwhile, said that the case over the incident would be brought under the Speedy Trial Act. Leaders of Bangladesh Garment Sramik Samhati on Wednesday at a protest rally in Dhaka demanded arrest and exemplary punishment for the killers of the Hindu youth. Garment Sramik Samhati organised the rally in front of the National Museum at Shahbagh in Dhaka city with its president Taslima Akhter in chair. Speakers at the human chain stated that Dipu was brutally killed on the basis of false allegations of hurting religious sentiment, demanding the interim government must take immediate steps to arrest the killers and ensure their exemplary punishment. Organisation general secretary Mizanur Rahman Chowdhury, vice-president Anjan Das, central leaders Prabir Saha, student leader Saikat Arif and others spoke at the rally. Press secretary Shafiqul Alam at a briefing on Wednesday said that the government condemned the Dipu’s murder and arrested at least 12 individuals. ‘The law adviser today informed the Council of Advisers that the trial of Dipu murder will be held under the Speedy Trial Act,’ Shafiqul Alam said. ‘We are making the highest effort to ensure protection for the minority communities,’ he added.

title: EC puts JS polls at risk by ignoring key reform proposals: roundtable
body: Civil society members on Wednesday warned that security lapses and weak accountability could put the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections at risk, scheduled for February 12 next year as the Election Commission allegedly ignored key reform proposals. They said that the interim government-formed Electoral Reform Commission recommended reforms to make the Representation of the People Order and the code of conduct for political parties and candidates more democratic and accountable. Many key proposals were excluded from the revised legal framework, they said. The observations came at a roundtable reviewing the progress of electoral reforms, held at the CIRDAP Auditorium in the capital and organised by SHUJAN—Citizens for Good Governance. Most members of the Electoral Reform Commission were present at the event. Presenting the keynote, SHUJAN executive chief and former ERC chief Badiul Alam Majumder said that the revised RPO ignored a key recommendation to form a three-member panel in each constituency for nominating party candidates. He also said that the revised RPO did not bring registered political parties under the Right to Information Act, 2009. Other ERC recommendations left out of the revised RPO included reinstating a provision requiring a minimum three-year involvement with a political party for nomination aspirants; allowing legal action against election commissioners for breaching their constitutional oath; empowering the EC to scrutinise candidates’ election expenses; and cancellation of candidacies for misreporting; and barring habitual loan defaulters from contesting polls. Badiul further said that although the revised RPO disqualified parties with affiliated organisations locally and abroad, the Election Commission took no action against parties violating the provision. The EC revised the RPO and the code of conduct from early to mid-November in preparation for the upcoming parliamentary elections. Centre for Policy Dialogue Economist Debapriya Bhattacharya distinguished fellow expressed concern over the security situation during and after the polls. He urged the authorities to recover looted weapons from police stations during the July 2024 uprising, seize smuggled arms, and strictly control election expenditure by candidates. ‘Given these security concerns, the Election Commission’s responsibility has increased manifold,’ he cautioned, adding that the EC’s failure to adopt key reform recommendations raised serious doubts about its ability to conduct a credible election. SHUJAN vice-president Justice MA Matin chaired the roundtable. Former ERC members Mir Nadia Nivin, Sadik Al Arman, Jasmine Tully and Md Abdul Alim, along with SHUJAN representatives Zubair Nahid and Zannatul Nahar, also spoke.

title: TIB finds misappropriation of Tk 2,926.88cr
body: The country incurred extra expenditure of about Tk 2,926.88 crore because of about 1.5 times higher than the actual cost of power generation from solar plants, according to a study conducted by the Transparency International Bangladesh, an anti-corruption watchdog. The study report was launched at an event at the TIB office in the capital Dhaka on Wednesday. The study titled ‘Generating Power from Renewable Energy in Bangladesh: Governance Challenges and Way Forward’ showed that while Tk 8 crore a megawatt was required for solar power projects according to the Bangladesh Power Development Board, but the six projects under the study had an average estimated cost of Tk 13.8 crore a megawatt. This means Tk 2,926.88 crore of state resources were wasted through inflated cost estimates, said TIB executive director Iftekharuzzaman at the report unveiling event. To a query, he said that the study period was limited to the power purchase deals signed by the Awami League regime before being ousted on August 5, 2004, in the wake of a mass uprising. The Quick Enhancement of Electricity and Energy Supply (Special Provision) Act, 2010, which was misused by the AL regime to sign inflated power purchase agreements on political consideration, was scrapped by the interim government that assumed power on August 8, 2024. Some 37 renewable energy projects out of total 42 power plants approved by the AL were cancelled by the interim government. The AL failed to implement the Bangladesh’s Renewable Energy Policy 2008, as the target of getting 10 per cent total electricity from renewable sources by 2020 was missed for too much emphasis on costly fossil fuels. Bangladesh’s current electricity installed capacity, comprising contributions from both on-grid and off-grid sources, is 28,616.48 megawatts, of which only 1,314.70MW or four per cent come from renewable energy sources. In the past month, the government approved a dozen solar power plants through competitive biddings. Iftekharuzzaman said that they would examine the current projects in the future studies. Responding to a question, the TIB executive director said that the reform initiatives by the interim government since the ouster of the AL regime on the state affairs should not be compared with the reforms in the power and energy sector. It will take more than two to three years to mend the damage made during the AL regime to the crucial sector, he said. The average electricity tariff of the selected renewable energy projects in this study is $0.124 per kWh. In comparison, the average tariff in the neighbouring countries is significantly lower — $0.03 in India, $0.032 in Pakistan and $0.045 in China. Thus, the tariff in Bangladesh is nearly four times higher than in these countries. The report highlighted that the interests of the fossil fuel lobby were being protected by marginalising renewable energy in the energy sector’s master plans, resulting in the failure to realise the vast potential of renewable energy. The TIB has proposed 15 recommendations to address the existing institutional and policy challenges and build a sustainable and transparent energy system. The recommendations include immediate cancelation of the existing fossil fuel-dependent energy master plan and implementing a new master plan based on the principles of reducing fossil fuel use and increasing the share of renewable energy in the energy mix. Formulation of a realistic road map for power generation from renewable sources with uniform targets in all existing policies, including the Renewable Energy Policy 2025, has also been suggested. Besides, amendment to the Power Act 2018 to provide a legal basis for power generation from renewable energy and providing clear instructions on the transmission, supply, and distribution of generated power through national or alternative grids is among the recommendations. TIB energy governance coordinator Newazul Moula and assistant coordinator Ashna Islam presented the report.

title: Fazlur Rahman’s death anniv today
body: The second anniversary of death of City Group founder, Fazlur Rahman, will be observed today. On his death anniversary, colleagues, employees and stakeholders will remember Fazlur Rahman not only for what he built but for the values he embedded — values that continue to guide the organisation’s path forward, said a press release. Widely regarded as a pioneering business leader, Fazlur Rahman began his journey in 1972 with a small mustard oil mill, laying the foundation for what would later become one of the country’s ‘most trusted’ conglomerates. Over the decades, City Group expanded across multiple sectors, guided by his unwavering commitment to ‘integrity, quality and long-term value creation’. This disciplined yet ambitious expansion reflected Fazlur Rahman’s long-term vision and commitment to building sustainable enterprises. Beyond business growth, Fazlur Rahman leadership was marked by ‘integrity, resilience and a belief in people-driven progress’. His legacy lives on through the thousands of individuals employed across City Group’s enterprises and through the enduring values that continue to guide the organisation’s journey, added the press release.

title: Madhu’s canteen vandalised
body: Madhu’s Canteen at Dhaka University was vandalised on Wednesday afternoon by an unidentified young man. Video footage of the incident went viral on social media, showing the attacker speaking incoherently, chanting ‘Allahu Akbar’ and ‘Takbir’, and reciting Kazi Nazrul Islam’s famous poem Bidrohi (rebel). The footage also shows him kicking and damaging a Chhatra Dal banner in front of Madhur Canteen and throwing tables inside the canteen. In the clip he identified himself as Mohammad Sagar and said that he was from Titas upazila of Comilla and that he worked in Islampur. He is heard saying in the footage that he came there to visit the grave of Sharif Osman Hadi. Contacted, Dhaka University proctor Saifuddin Ahmed told New Age that they primarily believed the man to be mentally unstable and that the mobile proctorial team handed him over to the police.

title: Christmas today
body: The Christian community will celebrate Christmas in the country as elsewhere across the world on Thursday, commemorating the birth of Jesus Christ. Christmas, the biggest religious festival of the Christian community, is the celebration of rebirth, new beginning, forgiveness and peace, and renewing relationship with God and human beings. The celebrations of the Christmas Day feature decoration of Christmas trees with colourful lights, special prayers, and distribution of gifts among children and exchange of pleasantries. Christmas carols and hymns will be sung before and after the prayer sessions at the churches. Bangladesh Television and Bangladesh Betar and different private TV channels and radio stations are supposed to air special programmes. President Mohammed Shahabuddin and chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus have issued separate messages on the eve of Christmas. In his message, Sahabuddin said learning from the ideals and teachings of Jesus Christ, everyone, regardless of religion or caste, must work together for the welfare of the country and its people. He urged all to further strengthen the existing communal harmony and join in the march towards building a modern and developed Bangladesh. Professor Yunus said Jesus was always devoted to serving the distressed, neglected, and hungry, and preached the values of forgiveness, love, and devotion until his death. His life and noble character continue to serve as an enduring example for his devotees and followers, he said. Yunus expressed hope that celebrating Christmas with due dignity and enthusiasm would further strengthen this bond of harmony. ‘The current government is working to build a non-discriminatory, just, and prosperous Bangladesh for all, regardless of religion, caste, or community,’ he added. Meanwhile, police have taken special security measures ahead of the celebration of Christmas. Security will also be heightened in all tourist areas including Cox’s Bazar and Kuakata. Authorities said action would be taken against anyone who honks loudly or drives recklessly on the roads. People are urged to contact the National Emergency Service 999 or their nearest beat police officer in case of any emergency.

title: Quasi-judicial council to oversee phone tapping
body: Bangladesh interim government on Wednesday approved the Bangladesh Telecommunications (Amendment) Ordinance 2025, banning internet shutdowns and illegal phone-tapping and abolishing the National Telecommunications Monitoring Centre. The council of advisers approved the ordinance at a meeting chaired by chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus at his Tejgaon office in the capital Dhaka. There was a demand from different quarters for the abolition of the NTMC established in 2013, alleging that the agency was involved in hacking mobile phones and illegally leaking private conversations of citizens during the tenure of Awami League regime which was ousted on August 5, 2024 in the wake of a mass uprising. The amended law also allows the formation of a ‘quasi-judicial council’ to oversee phone-tapping and other interception activities. Complaints against illegal interception can be submitted to the quasi-judicial body, which will consist of the minister for law, justice and parliamentary affairs as chair, the principal staff officer and the home secretary. At a press briefing at the Foreign Service Academy in the capital, chief adviser’s press secretary Shafiqul Alam said that breaking away from the controversial ‘2010 amendment framework’, the ordinance ensured the independence and accountability of the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission. Previously, all licensing approvals were issued by the ministry. But now, the ministry will approve only a limited number of nationally significant licences on the basis of independent studies, while the authority to issue all other licences has been returned to the BTRC. An ‘accountability committee’ will also be formed under the chairmanship of the head of the parliamentary standing committee on posts and telecommunications. The ordinance reduces previously prescribed high fines and recurring penalties, making the telecommunications sector more investment-friendly. The BTRC will now be required to hold a public hearing every four months, publish follow-up actions on its web site and comply with provisions aimed at preventing conflicts of interest. The ordinance also states in the draft amendment that using SIM and device registration data to conduct surveillance or harass any citizen without justification has been made a punishable criminal offence. The restrictive ‘speech offence’ provisions have been amended in line with the Cyber Protection Ordinance 2025, limiting criminal liability only to incitement to violence. A ‘centre for information support’ will be established under the home ministry to facilitate only judicially authorised and emergency lawful interception, in compliance with the Personal Data Protection Ordinance. Only agencies explicitly named in the law, and only within their respective jurisdictions, will be authorised to carry out such an interception. Interception through the proposed centre for information support will require role-based access control and approval from a quasi-judicial council. The parliamentary standing committee will publish an annual national report on lawful interception, detailing its scope and areas of use, and will also review budgets, operations and institutional capacity every year. Shafiqul Alam said that the council of advisers also approved a revised budget of Tk 7.88 lakh crore for the current financial year of 2025–26, down from the original Tk 7.90 lakh crore. The size of the annual development programme has been reduced by Tk 30,000 crore to Tk 2 lakh crore. Regarding the killing of Inqilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi, Shafiqul said that investigators were receiving vital clues and that the government was making maximum efforts to solve the case.

title: NCP seeks revision of nomination submission, withdrawal deadlines
body: The National Citizen Party on Wednesday expressed concern about the Election Commission’s capacity for holding the national polls on February 12 next year. The party urged the commission to reconsider the dates for submission of nomination papers and withdrawal of candidature, keeping the voting date unchanged. Speaking after a meeting between an NCP delegation and chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin at the commission headquarters in Dhaka, NCP chief coordinator Nasiruddin Patwary said that the party had requested the commission to consider whether these dates could be revised. The Election Commission on December 11 announced the schedule for the 13th parliamentary election and the referendum on the July National Charter (Constitutional Reform) Implementation Order, both set for February 12 next year. According to the schedule, the last date for submission of nomination papers is December 29, scrutiny between December 30 and January 4, and the final date for withdrawal of candidature is January 20. The election campaign will run between January 22 and 7:30am on February 10, 48 hours before balloting. Nasiruddin alleged that the Awami League was attempting to destabilise Bangladesh to delay the national election. ‘The Election Commission wants to conduct the election on February 12. From the National Citizen Party, we have emphasised that this date must not be postponed. We have requested the EC to ensure the polls are held on schedule,’ he said. On concerns about the election, Nasiruddin said that the NCP was aware of risks, including the killing of one aspirant, and urged the EC to ensure security for all candidates. ‘We have asked the Election Commission not to make any small mistakes that can cause the polling date to be postponed,’ he said. The Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, on the other hand, on Wednesday urged the Election Commission to ensure a level playing field in the upcoming elections, saying that providing VVIP facilities to some candidates and denying them to others undermines fairness. ‘If some individuals receive numerous facilities, including VVIP privileges, while others do not, that cannot be considered a level playing field,’ said Jamaat assistant secretary general Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair while talking to reporters after a meeting with the chief election commissioner at Nirbachon Bhaban. A three-member Jamaat delegation met the chief election commissioner to discuss their concerns. Zubair said that senior party leaders, including the Jamaat amir and the party’s secretary general, would be conducting extensive tours across the country during the election period, and the party had highlighted their security needs. He emphasised that ensuring equal treatment for all candidates was crucial for the credibility and fairness of the electoral process.

title: 4 more arrested, protests on against attacks on media
body: The police and Rapid Action Battalion arrested four more people in connection with the December 18 vandalism, looting of and arson attacks on the offices of two newspapers, Prothom Alo and The Daily Star. With the latest arrests on Tuesday and early Wednesday, the number of arrested in connection with the attacks rose to 32. The police had earlier arrested 28 people in connection with the attacks immediately after the death of the Inquilab Mancha convener and July uprising organiser Sharif Osman Hadi at a hospital in Singapore. Meanwhile, journalist organisations continued to protest demanding the arrest of the perpetrators in the attacks on the two prominent newspapers. A Dhaka Metropolitan Police press release issued on Tuesday said that its Detective Branch Cyber North unit arrested Niaz Mahmud Farhan, 22, from Borhanuddin upazila in Bhola at about 1:15am Wednesday. The release also said that the DMP’s Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime unit arrested Md Swapan Mondal, 30, from Abdullahpur crossing under Tongi in Gazipur district at about 12:05am Wednesday. On Tuesday night, the CTTC unit also arrested Md Zakir Hossain Shanto, 29 from the capital’s Bayley Road area, the release added. The Rapid Action Battalion arrested a key suspect in connection with the recent attack on The Daily Star building in Dhaka. Azmir Hossain Akash, 27, was arrested from the Tejgaon area of Dhaka following an operation based on intelligence and CCTV footage on Tuesday, RAB-3 said in a press release issued on Wednesday. Azmir was directly involved in the vandalism and arson carried out at the Daily Star office, according to the RAB press release. Electronic equipment looted during the attack, including CPUs, hard disks and cables, was recovered during the arrest. RAB in its release also said that further drives were under way to identify and arrest other individuals involved in the incident. The Dhaka Reporters Unity on Wednesday afternoon protested against the attack on the two newspapers’ offices forming a human chain on the DRU premises. DRU president Abu Saleh Akon said that attacks on Prothom Alo and The Daily Star offices and harassing New Age editor Nurul Kabir were a direct attack on the freedom of press. ‘Justice was not ensured in attacks on journalists in the past which has emboldened the miscreants,’ he added, issuing an ultimatum to arrest all involved in these attacks within 72 hours. Journalists in Khulna formed a human chain in front of Khulna Press Club, demanding justice for the attacks on the two newspapers’ offices. On Monday, Prothom Alo and The Daily Star authorities filed separate cases with the Tejgaon police over the devastating arson attacks on their offices. Prothom Alo filed a case against 400–500 unnamed people and The Daily Star in its case accused 350–400 unnamed individuals over vandalism, looting and arson attacks on their offices. According the statements of the cases, Prothom Alo incurred Tk 32 crore loss and The Daily Star incurred Tk 40 crore loss. On the night of December 18, several hundred men attacked and looted the offices of Prothom Alo in the capital’s Karwanbazar and The Daily Star across the road on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, and then set the offices on fire. Veteran journalist and writer Nurul Kabir, editor of New Age and president of the Editors’ Council, faced physical harassment in front of The Daily Star office, while he rushed to the rescue of the journalists and staff trapped inside in the small hours of December 19. In the early hours of December 19 Chhayanaut-Sanskriti Bhaban in Dhanmondi area was also attacked and the same day in the evening, the central office of cultural organisation Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi on Topkhana Road in Dhaka was torched.

title: Textbook distribution on Jan 1 uncertain
body: The National Curriculum and Textbook Board is set to fail to distribute all free textbooks among the students on the first day of 2026. Under this circumstance, the board is now planning to make all textbooks available online. Many students especially of Class VII and VIII are unlikely to get all textbooks on the first day following the government’s cancellation of some tenders for printing books. ‘We cannot give all textbooks to the students on January 1,’ NCTB chairman Md Mahbubul Hoque Patwary told New Age on Wednesday, adding, ‘we hope that we can give all books by January.’ Due to re-tender for a portion of books, they have to give the printers time till January 22 next year, he mentioned. ‘We will make all books available online,’ he said, adding that they would organise a programme on December 28 to upload all books online and make these accessible to all. The situation has arisen even the interim government time to time this year said that all students would get free textbooks on January 1. Most recently, on December 16, the education ministry announced that the NCTB had successfully completed printing and distribution activities for the textbooks for the pre-primary and primary levels (Class I to V) for 2026. However, as per the board, about 93 per cent of books for the ibtedayi students were printed and distributed at district and upazila levels before the final distribution till Tuesday. Currently, the board, under the education ministry, is mandated to formulate, develop, renew, monitor and reform the curriculum, syllabus and textbooks, and print, publish, distribute and market textbooks for the pre-primary to secondary level students. The government has been distributing free textbooks for the pre-primary to secondary level students since 2010 through the board. The board faced huge criticism earlier this year for failing to provide textbooks on time. After much delay, all students got textbooks by March, three months after their classes started. Following this, the board decided to start the initiatives of printing textbooks for 2026 early this year and set a target to print about 30.02 crore books by November 30 this year. According to the NCTB, the board is scheduled to print 60.67 lakh pre-primary, 7.90 crore Class I-V, 1.85 lakh ethnic minority groups, 6.43 lakh additional pre-primary (4+), 4.43 crore Class VI, 4.15 crore Class VII, 4.02 crore Class VIII, 5.7 crore Class IX-X, 3.11 crore Ibtedayi, and 6,026 Braille method textbooks this year. Till Tuesday, as per the NCTB, 93.27 per cent of ibtedayi, 66.35 per cent of Class VI, 31.03 per cent of Class VII, 9.86 per cent of Class VIII and 68.14 per cent of Class IX books were distributed. All pre-primary and primary levels books were printed and distributed among district and upazila authorities concerned. A senior NCTB official said that the only reason for delay in completing all procedures for books was re-tendering. After the government cancelled some tenders, he continued, for re-tenders the board started fresh tender procedure in October, which was completed in November. Usually the process completes in July–August, he added. This year the government decided to cancel the tender for printing textbooks for Class VI, VII and VIII in November. In addition, there was a delay in getting approval for the printing work from the ministry and the purchase committee. As per the board, till Tuesday, the percentage of ready books, after binding but before pre-delivery inspection to send for distribution, is 94.69 per cent for ibtedayi, 74.86 per cent for Class VI, 49.83 per cent for Class VII, 33.5 per cent for Class VIII and 79.97 per cent for Class IX. In cases of the percentage of books gone through pre-delivery inspection but not yet to be distributed at district and upazila levels is 94.69 per cent for ibtedayi, 70.8 per cent for Class VI, 36.95 per cent for Class VII, 23.67 per cent for Class VIII and 73.87 per cent for Class IX. The board chairman, Mahbubul Hoque Patwary, also said that they were hoping to give all Class VI and IX books to the students on January 1. ‘For Class VII and VII books, our plan is to give at least 50 per cent of the books to students on January 1,’ he added.

title: Road diversions, special trains to avoid traffic congestion
body: The government has taken special measures today to facilitate the movement and celebrations of Bangladesh Nationalist Party leaders and activists in the capital on the occasion of BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman’s homecoming. A huge gathering is expected throughout the day across the capital as Tarique Rahman is scheduled to return to Dhaka after more than 17 years of stay in the United Kingdom. Dhaka Metropolitan Police issued a set of directives on Wednesday, where it set some diversions for roads and arranged some parking spots for the vehicles of BNP leaders and activists. The activists on motorcycles will not be allowed to stay on roads from Gulshan to the airport via Banani or drive through gatherings, the metropolitan police said. It said that emergency services’ vehicles, including ambulances and those of fire services, would be out of the purview of these directives. The Bangladesh Railway has cancelled the scheduled journeys of three trains today, as it will run 10 special trains to carry BNP leaders and activists to and from the capital from different destinations. Biman Bangladesh Airlines authorities requested the airport-bound passengers to start from their homes with enough time in hand today. Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport authorities, citing special operational and security reasons, prohibited all visitors except designated passengers from entering its area for 24 hours ending 6:00pm today. The interim government has announced that the Dhaka Elevated Expressway would be toll-free for four hours today. A public notice issued by Dhaka Metropolitan Police headquarters on Wednesday reads that Tarique, after arriving at the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport today, will go to Evercare Hospital from airport using Purbachal Expressway, also known as 300 feet road, and then he will go to his Gulshan home from there. The metropolitan police urged the people to avoid the Mohakhali-Abdullahpur road and Kuril-Mostul section on Purbachal Expressway between 4:00am and 10:00pm today and use six alternative road routes, metro rail and Bangladesh Railway services. The alternative road routes are the Abdullahpur -Kamarpara - Dhour Bridge - Panchaboti - Mirpur Beribadh - Gabtoli, the House Building - Zamzam Tower - Uttara 12 no sector Khalpar - Metro rail Uttara north station - centre station - Mirpur DOHS and the Uttara centre station-Uttara 18 no sector - Panchaboti - Mirpur Beribadh routes for Uttara and Mirpur residents, the Gulshan-1/Police Plaza - Amtoli - Mokhali route for Gulshan, Badda and Pragati Sarani passengers instead of the Kakoli - Gulshan–2 and Kamal Atartuk road, the Mirpur - Gabtoli roads for buses from Mohakhali terminal, Bashundhara residential area and Madani Avenue for vehicles coming from Purbachal Expressway and Mirpur DOHS and roads under metro rail for vehicles from Tejgaon-Mirpur. The metropolitan police set some parking spots for vehicles to come for the celebration at Bishwa Ijtema field in Tongi, Nila Market, Purbachal/Trade Fair field in Purbachal, Diabari Cattle field, old Trade Fair field in Agargaon and Motijheel commercial area. The railway on December 22 had cancelled the scheduled journeys of three regular trains—Rajbari Commuter on Rajbari-Poradah route, Dhalar Char Express on Pabna-Rajshahi route and Rohonpur Commuter on Rohonpur-Rajshahi route — for today as it would use 10 special trains to carry the party leaders and activists. The special trains will run on Cox’s Bazar-Dhaka-Cox’s Bazar, Jamalpur-Mymensingh-Dhaka- Jamalpur, Tangail-Dhaka-Tangail, Bhairab Bazar-Narsingdi-Dhaka-Narsingdi-Bhairab Bazar, Joydebpur-Dhaka Cantonment-Joydebpur (Gazipur), Panchagarh-Dhaka-Panchagarh, Khulna-Dhaka-Khulna, Chatmohor- Dhaka Cantonment-Chatmohor, Rajshahi-Dhaka-Rajshahi, and Jashore-Dhaka-Jashore routes. On Wednesday, special trains started to run from Chattogram, Panchagarh, Chatmohor and Rajshahi to the capital, according to the railway officials. A press release, issued on Tuesday by the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport authorities, read that entry of all visitors would be prohibited between 6:00am Wednesday and 6:00pm Thursday. The Biman press release, issued on Tuesday, citing the possibility of a large gathering in the airport area today, requested airport-bound passengers to leave their homes with enough time in hand. Chief adviser’s press wing in a press release on Wednesday said that the toll plaza of the expressway would be free for the public from 11:00am to 3:00pm today. Bangladesh Bridge Authority chief engineer Quazi Muhammad Ferdous said that all toll plazas of the expressway would be toll-free during the period.

title: Tarique returns home today
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman is set to return to Dhaka on Thursday after more than 17 years in exile in the United Kingdom, marking a moment of major political significance. The homecoming has generated widespread anticipation nationwide, with supporters preparing to welcome him. The BNP has taken wide-ranging preparations, which party leaders say mirror both the significance of the moment and the sheer scale of public anticipation it has generated. They expressed confidence that the occasion would draw the largest public gathering in Bangladesh’s history, setting a landmark precedent. The government has imposed stringent security measures ahead of Tarique’s homecoming. Law enforcement agencies have taken several steps, including banning unapproved drones and deploying additional personnel, to ensure maximum security during the highly anticipated event. The BNP, at a press conference on Wednesday at the party chairperson’s office in Gulshan, said that Tarique was scheduled to travel from London’s Heathrow Airport on a regular Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight, departing around midnight Bangladesh time on Thursday, and that the aircraft was expected to arrive in Dhaka at 11:50am the same day after a brief stopover in Sylhet. Senior leaders of the BNP, including members of its standing committee, will receive him at the airport in an on-door reception. After arriving at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Tarique would travel along the 36 July Expressway, popularly known as the 300-feet road. A short section of the route, limited to one side of the carriageway, has been set aside for a very brief public reception. Party leaders said that the event would not constitute a rally or formal political meeting; rather, Tarique would speak briefly to express his gratitude to the people and seek prayers for the welfare of the country and BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia, being the sole speaker on the occasion. Immediately afterwards, he would proceed to Evercare Hospital, where his ailing mother and BNP chairperson, Khaleda Zia, is currently undergoing treatment. Following the hospital visit, Tarique will return to his home at Gulshan Avenue in the city. On Friday, after Jummah prayers, Tarique will leave his home to visit the mausoleum of his father, BNP founder and former president Ziaur Rahman. He will then travel to the National Martyrs’ Memorial at Savar, where he will pay tribute to those who sacrificed their lives during the Liberation War. On Saturday, Tarique will complete procedures related to his national identity card and voter registration. Tarique Rahman homecoming reception committee convener Salahuddin Ahmed told the press conference that it was prioritising crowd management, security and medical preparedness. He said that the timing of the programme was chosen deliberately to reduce disruption, with December 25 falling on a government holiday followed by two additional consecutive holidays, creating a three-day break that was expected to ease traffic pressure. To ensure smooth movement for international travellers and emergency vehicles, help desks have been installed at Kakoli intersection, the front of the international airport and Abdullahpur. These desks would coordinate motorbike escorts to keep key routes clear, particularly for ambulances carrying patients. Security arrangements include the deployment of the chairperson’s security force, alongside support from state agencies, following government instructions to facilitate the programme. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police issued two separate public notices prohibiting the flying of unapproved drones across key areas of the capital. According to one notice, drones will be banned from operating around Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Jashimuddin Road, Kuril Flyover, the 36 July Purbachal Expressway, Banani, Kamal Ataturk Avenue, Gulshan-2 North Avenue, and Tarique Rahman’s home from Thursday until further notice. Another notice extended the ban to Evercare Hospital and its surrounding areas from Wednesday onwards. Both measures, the DMP said, were issued in the public interest under the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Ordinance. DMP spokesperson Muhammad Talebur Rahman said that all-out security arrangements had been made for Tarique Rahman’s return. In addition to the DMP, the Border Guard Bangladesh would deploy personnel to maintain law and order and ensure the safe movement of the public. A senior BGB official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said, ‘We will do our utmost to provide security alongside other forces,’ though the exact number of personnel deployed was not disclosed. BNP leader Salahuddin said that despite their efforts to keep the programme modest, the party did not have the capacity to control the massive influx of supporters heading to the capital after 17 years. BNP leaders said that the acting chairman would arrive at the venue, offer thanks to Allah, express gratitude to the people, and seek everyone’s support for the nation in future democratic processes. Tarique Rahman, the elder of the two sons of former prime minister Khaleda Zia, had previously been sentenced in several cases, including a life term, and faced numerous other charges, most of which were filed during the 2007–08 military-backed caretaker government. He was arrested during an anti-corruption drive in March 2007 and released on bail on September 3, 2008, after which he travelled to London on September 11 for medical treatment, and remained there. Following the end of the Awami League’s 16-year rule on August 5, 2024 amid a mass uprising, the High Court acquitted him of all cases filed during both the caretaker government and Awami League administration periods, clearing the legal obstacles to his return.

title: Woman, granddaughter burnt to death in Ctg fire
body: A woman and her granddaughter were killed after a fire broke out at their house at Kaderia Para village in Rangunia upazila of Chattogram on Wednesday. The deceased are Rumi Akhtar, 55, wife of Ruhul Amin, and her five-year-old granddaughter Jannat Akhtar, residents of the same village. Fire service and locals said the fire erupted from an electrical short circuit and engulfed six tin-shed houses within a short time at dawn. The woman and the girl were trapped inside one of the houses and burnt to death. Deputy assistant director of Chattogram fire service Abdul Mannan said firefighters from Rangunia station rushed to the spot and managed to bring the fire under control after nearly an hour of effort. The affected-families claimed that properties worth around Tk 50 lakh were destroyed in the fire.

title: Fellowship launched by ULAB, DRIK
body: Renowned photographer-activist Shahidul Alam urged the students to pay more attention to long-form storytelling (journalism) while interacting with the students of University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh. He was speaking at the inaugural session of ‘Ctrl+Alt+Story: Research and Storytelling in Journalism’ a DRIK-ULAB joint initiative to inspire and help prospective storytellers grow through active mentorship. The event was held on Thursday to welcome the participants and orient them with the four-month-long activities. Sumon Rahman, dean of ULAB’s School of Social Science and the head of Media Studies and Journalism Department, delivered the welcome address. He said that in our increasingly fast-paced world we are becoming more prone to shorter/quick things and reading/writing longer, in-depth pieces becoming rare which in the long-run may affect all aspects of our life as these habits are connected to deep and critical thinking and taking time for that. This initiative is to inspire our young minds to revive those habits and skills. He thanked DRIK to partner with ULAB in such an important and timely initiative. In his interactive session with the participants, Alam discussed the basics of (slow) investigative journalism by presenting several examples from his four decade-long career as well as from the others. He mentioned that journalism is not a clerical job of telling people who said what at where (at which event) or what happened here and there, but it is a creative arena of explaining the ‘why’ by digging deeper objectively and scientifically and telling that to people in a way they will understand the best. We must not just rush with everything, rather we need to slow down sometimes, think deeply and critically to understand the true essence of the phenomena around us – he stressed. Alam also warned the students that seeking out ‘why’ is neither easy nor safe often; same applies to sharing the answer with people. However, there will always be ways if your intent is honest and strong – he added. Sarkar Barbaq Quarmal, Associate Professor, Media Studies and Journalism, ULAB and one of the project coordinators, moderated the session while the other coordinator, Oliur Rahman Sun, Lecturer, Department of English and Humanities, ULAB presented the details of the initiative to the participants. It is noteworthy here that the Ctrl+Alt+Story initiative started with 21 participants selected through a two-step rigorous process. In next six weeks, they will participate in several workshops and master classes with renowned journalists and storytellers. Afterwards, ten students will be provided with a fellowship worth fifty thousand taka each and a mentor to pursue an investigative journalism project of their preference.

title: Desh Media newspaper ownership stake taken over by IMBD agency
body: Digital marketing and technology firm, IMBD Agency Limited, has officially acquired the management rights and ownership stake of Desh Media, a government-registered newspaper. The signing ceremony and transfer of ownership took place on Wednesday at IMBD Agency’s head office in Banani, Dhaka, says a press release. The agreement was signed by Bulbul Ahmed, founder and editor of Desh Media, and Shamim Ahmed, managing director of IMBD Agency Limited, in the presence of senior officials from both organisations. Amidst the crowd of unregistered online portals in Bangladesh, IMBD Agency has taken the initiative to revamp Desh Media with a promise of reliable journalism. Registered with the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting since 2013 and listed with the DFP, the newspaper will now operate under the technical and strategic supervision of IMBD Agency. Speaking after the signing, Shamim Ahmed, MD of IMBD Agency and the newly appointed Executive Director of Desh Media, said, ‘It is essential to restore public trust in online news media. Instead of creating a random new portal, we have taken responsibility for a legitimate institution registered since 2013. Through IMBD Agency’s modern technology, re-branding, and aggressive marketing strategies, we aim to establish Desh Media as a mainstream media outlet in Bangladesh very soon.’ Bulbul Ahmed, editor of Desh Media, expressed his excitement about the partnership. ‘There is no alternative to technology for keeping pace with the times and modernizing media. I believe that under the leadership of Shamim Ahmed and the IMBD Agency team, Desh Media will find new life and play a bold role in delivering truthful news,’ he said. The authorities announced that Desh Media will soon begin its official re-launching operations with a completely new look, comprised of experienced journalists and a professional team.

title: Youth killed in cocktail explosion in Moghbazar
body: A youth was killed in a cocktail explosion in the Moghbazar area in the capital on Wednesday evening. Hatirjheel police station officer-in-charge Mohammad Raju said that the incident took place at about 7:15pm on Monday in the Moghbazar area. ‘We are yet to trace the attackers,’ he said, adding that the deceased was named Siam, 21.

title: Ali Riaz named chief coordinator for polls, referendum awareness campaign
body: Bangladesh interim government on Wednesday announced that chief adviser’s special assistant, Professor Ali Riaz, would now work as the chief coordinator of the public awareness campaign for the 13th national election and the referendum. A gazette notification, signed by Chief Adviser’s Office director (administration) Mohammad Abdul Wadud Chowdhury, confirmed the appointment. Chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus had appointed Ali Riaz as his special assistant on November 13, granting him the status of an adviser. Ali Riaz previously served as vice-chair of the National Consensus Commission from February 12 to October 31 this year. Before that, he headed the Constitution Reform Commission from October 7, 2024, to January 15, 2025. He is a distinguished professor of political science at Illinois State University in the United States.

title: Bangladesh interim govt chief exchanges Christmas greetings with Christian leaders
body: Chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Wednesday exchanged Christmas greetings with representatives of the Christian community at the state guest house Jamuna in Dhaka on the occasion of Christmas. Religious affairs adviser AFM Khalid Hossain, head of Catholic Christians of Bangladesh Archbishop Bejoy N D’Cruze, president of the National Christian Fellowship of Bangladesh Bishop Philip P Adhikary, trustee of the Christian Religious Welfare Trust Benedict Alo D’ Rozario, president of the National Council of Churches in Bangladesh Christopher Adhikari and other prominent leaders of the Christian community were present on the occasion, said the chief adviser’s press wing in the evening. In their welcome address, Christian leaders highlighted Yunus’s global reputation and his role in improving the country’s economy and overall situation. They expressed hope that the next election would be held in a free and fair manner under his leadership. In his address, Archbishop Bejoy N D’Cruze described Jesus Christ as universal and said that inspired by the great ideals of forgiveness and service to humanity preached by Jesus Christ, millions of people around the world, including those in Bangladesh, are celebrating Christmas this year with joy and enthusiasm. Extending Christmas greetings to the chief adviser, N D’Cruze said, ‘After the July mass uprising, the people have keep their trust on you to rebuild Bangladesh anew. You have been carrying out that responsibility with great dedication. We pray that your efforts will succeed through a beautiful and peaceful election’. Wishing everyone on the occasion of the Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year, Yunus said, ‘You are the reflection of society. By looking at you, we can understand whether everything is in order.’ ‘We want to build a healthy society. For that reason the July Charter has been prepared to uphold the spirit of the mass uprising,’ the chief adviser said, adding, through a referendum on this charter, the country will move one step forward. He noted that alongside the parliamentary election, a referendum will also be held this time. The next parliament will adopt reform measures based on the verdict given by the people in the referendum, Yunus said. He called upon religious leaders to play a role in raising public awareness about the upcoming election and referendum. On the occasion, leaders of the Christian Religious Welfare Trust specially thanked the interim government for granting Tk 2.5 crore to the trust on the occasion of Christmas. They said the grant is being distributed in three phases among 800 churches across the country. Later, the chief adviser cut a cake together with representatives of the Christian community to mark Christmas.

title: BRDB discusses PPR 2025
body: A daylong workshop on ‘Public Procurement Rules, 2025 (PPR-2025)’ was held by the Bangladesh Rural Development Board at BRDB conference room at Karwan Bazar in Dhaka on Monday. Abdul Khalek, chairman, Palli Sanchay Bank, was present as chief guest. The workshop was presided over by additional secretary Sardar Md Keramat Ali, director general, BRDB. Representatives of different ministries, divisions, departments and agencies were present in the workshop. Directors and joint directors, deputy directors and assistant directors working at the BRDB headquarters participated in the workshop. Ashek Ahmed Shibli, superintending engineer (public works procurement unit) of the Public Works Department, presented the main paper on the topic discussed in the workshop. The workshop’s chief guest Abdul Khalek said that the 'Public Procurement Rules, 2025' has been updated and modernised in light of the reality. Every official must follow the PPR correctly to ensure transparency and accountability in government procurement. If the PPR is followed correctly, government officials will be able to avoid future complications related to procurement. BRDB director general Sardar Md Keramat Ali said that BRDB had to perform some procurement functions to conduct development-oriented activities and in that case, he believes that, this awareness workshop will make a special contribution to purchasing with transparency.

title: DMP bans flying unapproved drones at some places in Dhaka
body: Dhaka Metropolitan Police in two separate public notices banned flying unapproved drones in different areas in the capital marking the homecoming of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman. According to a DMP public notice, flying drones from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Jashimuddin Road, Kuril Flyover, July 36 Purbachal Expressway, Banani, Kamal Ataturk Avenue, Gulshan-2 North Avenue and Tarique’s home was banned from December 25. The notice signed by DMP commissioner Sheikh Md Sajjat Ali said that they issued the order following the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Ordinance and it would remain effective until further notice. Another DMP public notice following the same ordinance said that flying drones were banned at Evercare Hospital and its adjacent places from December 24 until using further notice. DMP said that both notices were issued for the sake of public interest. Tarique was arrested during an anti-corruption drive in March 2007 and released on bail in September 2008, after which he travelled to London for medical treatment on September 11, 2008, and remained there. Following the fall of Awami League’s 16-year rule in a mass uprising on August 5, 2024, the High Court acquitted him of all cases filed during both the caretaker government period and the Awami League administration, clearing the legal obstacles to his return.

title: Rafiq Uzzaman elected as RAC vice-president
body: Islamic Television’s special correspondent and chief reporter Rafiq Uzzaman has been elected as vice-president of Reporters Against Corruption, an organisation of anti-corruption journalists. The 15-member executive committee was elected for the next one year through direct voting by the members at the end of the organisation’s annual general meeting on Friday, said a press release on Sunday. Assignment editor of Channel S Shafi Uddin Ahmed was elected as president, senior reporter of the daily Amader Shomoy Tabarul Haque was elected as general secretary associate senior reporter of Somoy Television Taslimul Alam Touhid was elected as joint general secretary and senior reporter of the daily Manabzamin Maruf Kibria was elected as organising secretary of the organisation. Saiful Islam Montu of Daily Ajkaler Khabar has been elected as finance secretary, Masud Rana of Rajdhani TV as office secretary, Naznin Akter Lucky of Sarabangla as publicity and publication secretary, Jannatul Ferdousi of GTV as training and welfare secretary and Fazlur Rahman of Daily Janakantha as sports and cultural secretary. Senior journalists Abul Kashem, Abdullah Al Mamun of Daily Jugantor, Jamiul Ahsan Shipu of Daily Ittefaq, Matlu Mallik of Daily Khabarer Kagoj and Saif Bablu of Rupali Bangladesh have won the executive member positions.
