title: Govt makes elevated expressway toll-free for four hours tomorrow
body: The interim government has announced to make the Dhaka Elevated Expressway toll free for four hours tomorrow. A press release, issued by the Chief adviser's press wing on Wednesday, read that the toll plaza of the expressway will be free for public from 11:00am to 3:00pm on Thursday. Bangladesh Bridge Authority chief engineer Quazi Muhammad Ferdous said that all toll plazas in airport, Kuril, Banani, Farmgate and Tejgaon areas will be toll free during the period. Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairperson Tarique Rahman is scheduled to return Bangladesh tomorrow.

title: BNP names 10 more candidates, with nine for allies
body: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party on Wednesday announced candidates for 10 more constituencies, sharing nine of the seats with its movement partners, for the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad elections scheduled for February 12 next year. BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir announced the names of the 10 candidates at a press conference at the party’s chairperson’s office in the capital’s Gulshan area. Of the 10 candidates, Liberal Democratic Party secretary general Redwan Ahmed, who joined the BNP on the day, will contest for Cumilla-7 using the BNP’s electoral symbol, the sheaf of paddy. Among other candidates, Jatiya Party (Kazi Zafar) chairman Mustafa Jamal Haider will contest for Pirojpur-1, National People’s Party chairman Fariduzzaman Farhad for Narail-2, Islami Oikya Jote leader Mufti Rashid Bin Wakkas for Jessore-5, and Gono Odhikar Parishad general secretary Mohammad Rashed Khan for Jhenaidah-4. In Dhaka, Bobby Hajjaj of the Nationalist Democratic Movement, who is set to join the BNP, will contest for Dhaka-13, while Revolutionary Workers Party general secretary Saiful Haque will contest for Dhaka-12. The other candidates include Nagorik Oikya president Mahmudur Rahman Manna for Bogura-2, Gono Odhikar Parishad president Nurul Haque Nur for Patuakhali-3, and Ganosamhati Andolan chief coordinator Zonayed Saki for Brahmanbaria-6. Fakhrul clarified that those who formally joined the BNP will contest the election using the party’s symbol, the sheaf of paddy, and that the BNP will not field rival candidates in those constituencies. He also said that the NPP might be allowed to use the sheaf of paddy symbol, while discussions on further decisions and seat-sharing arrangements would continue, and any decisions reached would be announced later. Fakhrul said that the BNP would take organisational action against any party member who would contest in constituencies allocated to its allies. Meanwhile, LDP secretary general Redwan’s announcement to join the BNP was formally welcomed by BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul. He described Redwan’s return as ‘a son returning home’ and said that the move would further strengthen the party. On Tuesday, the party announced that four seats would be given to Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh. Earlier, on Monday, Bangladesh Jatiya Dal Chairman Syed Ahasanul Huda dissolved his party and joined the BNP. He is set to contest the upcoming parliamentary election for the Kishoreganj-5 constituency using the BNP’s electoral symbol. On December 9, Bangladesh Liberal Democratic Party chairman Shahadat Hossain Selim joined the BNP after dissolving his own party. Following his joining, the BNP announced him as the party’s candidate for the Laxmipur-1 constituency. Earlier, the BNP had announced its candidates for 272 constituencies out of 300 across the country in two phases.

title: Jasas leader stabbed to death by unidentified killers in Gazipur
body: A leader of Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha was stabbed to death by unidentified killers at village Latifpur of Sreepur upazila in Gazipur district on early Wednesday. The deceased was identified as Farid Sarkar, joint secretary of Gosinga union unit of the party. Nasir Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Jasas, said Farid Sarkar returned home from abroad after 17 years after the July movement last year and got involved in a brick kiln business. A group of killers intercepted Farid at his brick kiln on Tuesday midnight and stabbed him indiscriminately, leaving him injured. Being informed, Faruk Hossain, brother of Farid, took him to Shaheed Tajuddin Medical College and Hospital where the doctors declared him dead. Family members of the victim said he that had an enmity with his neighbour over a piece of land and they suspected that Farid might have killed over the issue. ‘Police are investigating to unearth the motive behind the killing,’ said the OC. Legal action would be taken after identifying those involved in the killing, he said.

title: Ataur Rahman Bikrampuri arrested in Narsingdi, sent to jail
body: A team of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch arrested religious speaker Ataur Rahman Bikrampuri at a location in Narsingdi district on Tuesday night. The metropolitan police’s DB chief Md Shafiqul Islam said that they arrested him as there was a detention order against him. Tongi East police station officer-in-charge Md Mehedi Hasan said that Ataur was arrested as there is a three-month detention order from the home ministry under the Special Powers Act, 1974 against him. ‘He has already been sent to the Kashimpur High Security Central Jail in Gazipur,’ Mehedi added. In some social media videos, Ataur was seen supporting the attacks on the offices of The Daily Star and the Prothom Alo. On the night of December 18, hundreds of attackers vandalised and looted the offices of the Prothom Alo in the capital’s Karwanbazar area and The Daily Star on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, and then set fire to the offices. New Age editor Nurul Kabir, also the Editors’ Council president, was harassed when he went to The Daily Star office early December 19 to rescue the journalists and staff members trapped in the office during the fire. On Monday, the authorities of the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star filed separate cases with the Tejgaon police station over the December 18 vandalism and arson on their offices.

title: Import, export via Benapole port to remain suspended on Thursday, Friday
body: Import and export trade through the country’s largest land port Benapole will remain suspended on Thursday and Friday on the occasion of Christmas and the weekend, officials said Wednesday. Benapole port director Shamim Hossain said that no goods will be imported or exported during the period, and customs operations at the port will remain closed. He, however, said trucks carrying Indian goods for clearance can return and regular trade activities will resume on Saturday. Officer-in-charge of Benapole Immigration Police SM Sakhawat Hossain said that movement of passengers with passports between the countries will remain as usual despite the suspension of trade.

title: Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury appointed as Bangladesh’s 26th Chief Justice
body: Appellate Division judge, Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, has been appointed the 26th chief justice of Bangladesh. President Mohammed Shahabuddin made the appointment, according to a gazette notification issued on Tuesday by law secretary Liaquat Ali Molla. The president will administer the oath of office of the chief justice at a ceremony at Bangabhaban on December 28. Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury will succeed Justice Syed Refaat Ahmed, who retires on December 27. On August 10, 2024, the president appointed High Court judge, Justice Syed Refaat Ahmed, the 25th chief justice of Bangladesh after his predecessor Obaidul Hassan resigned amid mass movement of the students. Five other Appellate Division judges also resigned immediately after the resignation of the then chief justice Obaidul Hasan. Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury superseded Appellate Division judge Justice Md Ashfaqul Islam, who was the lone remaining Appellate Division judge after the resignations of the then chief justice and five other judges. Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury will retire on May 18, 2028. He is among four judges elevated to the Appellate Division after those resignations. He is the son of Justice AFM Abdur Rahman Chowdhury and writer and social reformer Begum Sitara Chowdhury. He obtained LLB (Honours) and LLM in International Law from Dhaka University. He was enrolled as an advocate of the District Court on March 3, 1985, and of the High Court Division on May 17, 1987. He was appointed an additional judge of the High Court Division on August 27, 2003, and a permanent judge on August 27, 2005. He was elevated to the Appellate Division on August 13, 2024.

title: Murder case filed over death of sleeping child in Lakshmipur house fire
body: A murder case was filed against unnamed people with the Lakshmipur Sadar police station on Tuesday night over the incident of killing a seven-year-old girl in an alleged arson attack on the house of a local Bangladesh Nationalist Party leader at Lakshmipur Sadar upazila in the early hours of December 20. Although the case was filed four days after the incident, none has so far been arrested in this connection. Lakshmipur Sadar police officer-in-charge Wahid Parvez said that BNP leader Belal Hossain, also father of the victim, filed the case at about 10:30pm on Tuesday. ‘We are trying to identify the perpetrators and drive is under way to arrest those,’ the police official said, adding that they were trying to arrest the accused. The plaintiff Belal expressed dissatisfaction over the police’s failure to apprehend the perpetrators of his daughter’s death. The deceased, Ayesha Begum, was the youngest daughter of Belal, assistant organising secretary of the BNP Bhabaniganj union unit at the upazila. Belal and his two other daughters, Bithi Akhter, 17, and Smrity Akhter, 14, were also injured in the incident. The two other daughters of Belal are now undergoing treatment at the National Burn Institute and Plastic Surgery. On Monday night, BNP senior joint secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvy and its joint secretary general Shahid Uddin Chowdhury Anee visited the affected house. BNP Lakshmipur district unit joint convener Hasibur Rahman said that none was arrested in the past five days after such a heinous incident. He also demanded that law enforcement agencies take swift action over this incident.

title: Dhaka becomes 2nd most polluted city with AQI score of 236
body: Dhaka, the overcrowded capital city of Bangladesh, has ranked second on the list of cities with the worst air quality with an AQI score of 236 at about 9:50am on Wednesday morning. On Wednesday, Dhaka’s air was classified as ‘very unhealthy’ referring to an alarming healthy threat, according to the AQI index. When the AQI value for particle pollution is between 50 and 100, air quality is considered ‘moderate’, usually sensitive individuals should consider limiting prolonged outdoor exertion, between 101 and 150, air quality is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, between 150 and 200 is ‘unhealthy’, between 201 and 300 is said to be ‘very unhealthy’, while a reading of 301 and above is considered ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks to residents. India’s Kolkata, Egypt’s Cairo and India’s Delhi cities respectively occupied the first, third, and fourth spots on the list, with AQI scores of 247, 197, and 190 respectively. The AQI, an index for reporting daily air quality, informs people how clean or polluted the air of a certain city is and what associated health effects might be a concern for them. The AQI in Bangladesh is based on five pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), NO2, CO, SO2, and ozone. Dhaka has long been grappling with air pollution issues. Its air quality usually turns unhealthy in winter and improves during the monsoon. As per World Health Organisation, air pollution kills an estimated seven million people worldwide every year, mainly due to increased mortality from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.

title: July uprising mural replaces Mujib artwork at RU hall
body: Rajshahi University authorities have installed a mural commemorating the July uprising at Bijoy-24 Hall, replacing a mural of the country’s founding president Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, triggering debate among teachers, students and cultural activists over historical memory and due process. RU vice-chancellor Professor Saleh Hasan Naqib unveiled the new mural, titled ‘Bijoy-24 Mural’, at the main entrance of the hall on Monday, nearly seven months after the hall, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall, was renamed ‘Bijoy-24 Hall’ on May 22. At the centre of the new mural is Abu Sayeed, a student at Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur, who was shot dead during the July mass uprising. Behind him is a rickshaw, and on the right side, the words ‘Quota or discrimination’ are written in bold, while above are images of two of his fellow protesters who were killed during the mass uprising. On August 15, 2024, a group of youths damaged Sheikh Mujib’s mural at the then Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall. On February 5, a group of students removed name plaques, graffiti and wall writings bearing the names of members of Sheikh Mujib’s family and replaced them with new ones. They subsequently changed the name of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall to ‘Bijoy-24 Hall’ by hanging a banner. Several senior teachers, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that removing the mural of Sheikh Mujib amounted to an attempt to ‘replace the country’s independence history’. ‘This is not merely about installing a new mural. It is about erasing an existing historical symbol without following any due process,’ said a professor of history department. A senior professor of the mass communication and journalism department said that such actions were contributing to a culture of fear on campus, which he said posed a serious obstacle to academic work and free intellectual practice. Student organisations also expressed concern over the manner in which the changes were made. They said that while commemorating contemporary movements was legitimate, doing so by displacing nationally significant symbols reflected poor judgment and a lack of inclusivity. Fuad Ratul, convener of the Rajshahi University unit of Samajtantrik Chhatra Front, said ‘During the previous Awami League fascist regime, we saw a politics of naming different establishments based on one’s own ideology.’ ‘After the uprising, we hoped that if names or murals were to be changed, it would be done through discussions with stakeholders or students. Instead, these changes have been carried out without any discussion, which has raised serious questions,’ he added. Cultural activists warned that the move risked politicising public art on university campuses and setting a precedent in which murals and monuments change with shifting political narratives rather than reflecting enduring historical values.

title: IGP urges end to road blockades for smooth polls
body: Inspector general of police Baharul Alam on Tuesday warned that the growing practice of blocking roads and highways over trivial issues had to stop immediately, or else it would hamper the police’s ability to provide full security support for the national election scheduled for February 12. ‘We see attempts to create instability in society through road and highway blockades with minor demands or trivial matters. We think the time has come to stop these. If we cannot establish order everywhere, it will not be possible for us to provide all-out support to the election commission for conducting the elections,’ he said while addressing a briefing arranged for the returning officers and the senior field officers. The election commission arranged the briefing on electoral management affairs for deputy commissioners, superintendents of police and other field-level high officials at 10:00am at the Nirbachan Bhaban in the city’s Agargaon area. Besides DCs and SPs, the briefing is being attended by divisional commissioners, metropolitan police commissioners, deputy inspectors general of police, regional election officers and district election officers. Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin and four election commissioners—Abdur Rahmanel Masud, Tahmida Ahmad, Anwarul Islam Saker, and Brigadier General (retired) Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah—provided guidelines and instructions to ensure free, fair, and festive elections. EC senior secretary Akhtar Ahmed presided over the briefing. Reflecting on past challenges, IGP Alam said police faced significant difficulties in maintaining law and order due to the reality during the post-July movement period in Bangladesh. ‘We must overcome such situations. I believe that we have enhanced our capabilities enough at this stage ahead of this election. We seek the election commission’s continued support for taking strict measures [to maintain the order],’ he said. The police chief pledged that the police would exert their utmost efforts to ensure the elections are conducted successfully and peacefully. ‘On behalf of Bangladesh Police, I assure the chief election commissioner and all election commissioners that we will be able to hold this election successfully, fairly and peacefully with all our strength and with all our efforts, and we have the full capability to do so. You can have faith in it,’ he said. He praised the EC’s initiatives, including empowering the Electoral Inquiry Committee to conduct summary trials for immediate action on election-related offenses. ‘This provision is highly timely.’ During the briefing, IGP Alam sought clarification on field-level police transfers, particularly the lower police personnel like sub-inspector and constables. He said the commission issues directives on superintendents of police or senior officer postings, but clear guidelines are needed regarding transfers of lower-ranking personnel such as constables or sub-inspectors. High-level government officials also attended the opening session of the briefing.

title: COMMUNITY CLINICS: Uninterrupted supply of hypertension drugs urged
body: Public health campaigners on Tuesday demanded uninterrupted supply of anti-hypertensive medicines to the community clinics for poor patients in remote areas. Currently, poor patients in remote areas in particular were facing difficulty in getting the drugs for hypertension in time since the programme under which the government used to supply the drug to the community clinics had ended, they said at a discussion organised by non-governmental organisation Knowledge for Progress with support from the Global Health Advocacy Incubator. According to the Health and Morbidity Status Survey 2025 by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics, hypertension ranks first among the country’s top 10 diseases. The availability of anti-hypertensive drugs must be ensured in all community clinics and Upazila Health Complexes across the country by ensuring uninterrupted production and supply of medicines, speakers said. Many speakers complained that the supply of anti-hypertension drugs was not adequate for the high number of patients suffering from the condition. The government-owned sole drug producing company Essential Drugs Company Limited’s deputy general manager Md Riad Arefin said that they produced the drugs that were in high demand at the government hospitals under work orders. ‘We are ready to produce the medicine but the Non-Communicable Disease Control Unit did not place any order last year due to a fund crisis,’ he said. The Community Clinic Health Support Trust’s former programme manager Dr Geeta Rani Devi said that the government was working to deliver anti-hypertensive medicines to the grassroots. ‘Gradually, we will be able to ensure the availability of these medicines at all community clinics and Upazila Health Complexes,’ she said. Non-communicable diseases account for 71 per cent of total deaths in the country, but budget allocation for this area is only 4 per cent of total health budget which is again less than 5 per cent of total budget. The World Health Organisation suggests 15 per cent of a nation’s total annual budget for healthcare. Channel 24 head of news and current affairs Zahirul Alam, GHAI Bangladesh country lead Muhammad Ruhul Quddus and executive director of PROGGA ABM Zubair were also present as discussants.

title: Newborn found dead
body: Police recovered the body of a male newborn, aged around one day, from a lane in Chandni Ghat area of Chawk Bazar in Dhaka Tuesday afternoon. The newborn, found in an unconscious state wrapped in black plastic, was rushed to Dhaka Medical College Hospital where physicians declared him dead. Sub-inspector Ashraful of Chawk Bazar police station said they collected CCTV footages from the area and trying to identify those responsible. The body has been sent to the morgue for autopsy and legal action will be taken accordingly, he said.

title: Long-standing Eastern Refinery 2nd unit project approved
body: A meeting of the executive committee of the National Economic Council on Tuesday approved 22 projects, including the construction of the second unit of Eastern Refinery Limited at Tk 35,465.14 crore in the next five years. The overall cost of the 22 projects has been estimated at Tk 46,419.66 crore at the meeting presided over by chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus at the Planning Commission in the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar area in the capital Dhaka. Of the approved projects, a long-standing project titled ‘Modernisation and Expansion of Eastern Refinery Limited’ has finally been cleared. Conceived in early 2010, the proposed second unit of the ERL at Patenga in Chattogram had been delayed over the years for a shortage of funds. Initiatives for implementing the proposed project with foreign financing brought no positive outcome. In 2023, the Awami League government, which was ousted on August 5, 2024 in the wake of a mass uprising, took an initiative to implement the project under the public-private-partnership with the S Alam Group, a controversial business group linked to the AL regime. However, the interim government which assumed power on August 8 past year cancelled the PPP initiative. Tuesday’s ECNEC meeting approved the construction of the new unit with domestic resources, with the government providing Tk 21,277.59 crore. The rest Tk 14,187.55 crore will come from the ERL. The deadline for the implementation of the project has been set at 2030. ‘This is a very important project,’ said finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed while talking to reporters after a meeting of the advisory council committee on government purchase at the secretariat in the capital Dhaka. Once commissioned, the second unit will process 30 lakh tonnes of crude oils annually, double than the first unit of the ERL established in 1968. Both units can meet about 45-50 per cent of the country’s petroleum fuel oil demand. Unlike the first unit that can only refine crude oils from the Middle Eastern countries, the second unit will have the technology to refine crude oils shipped from any port of the world. The finance adviser said that the quality of refined oil would improve once the second unit was commissioned. Among the approved projects, 14 are new, five are revised and three involve extensions of project tenure. The ECNEC approved three projects under the road transport and bridges ministry. They are the development of a connecting road from the Karnaphuli Tunnel at Anwara to the Chattogram–Cox’s Bazar National Highway, upgrading the land port on Hilli–Dugdugi–Ghoraghat National Highway in Dinajpur and land acquisition and utility relocation under the four-lane Dhaka Sylhet–Tamabil highway. The housing and public works ministry received approval for the revised project to construct 672 residential flats in eight 15-storey buildings for government officers and employees at Aliganj in Narayanganj. Five projects were approved under the local government, rural development and cooperatives ministry. They include the establishment of the Dhaka WASA Training and Research Academy, a revised project for waterlogging mitigation, safe water supply and infrastructure development in the Sylhet City Corporation, the Climate Resilient and Livelihood Enhancement Project (CRALEP), the development of important rural infrastructure in Patuakhali district, and the widening and strengthening of key upazila and union roads in the Sylhet division. The defence ministry secured approval for two projects — the revised infrastructure development of Mongla Commander Flotilla West and the infrastructure development of the Army Institute of Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation at Savar, on the outskirts of the capital. The committee approved the revised reconstruction project of the Destitute Children Training and Rehabilitation Centre at Konabari in Gazipur under the social welfare ministry, and the education and research capacity building project of the National Institute of Advanced Nursing Education and Research under the health and family welfare ministry. The education ministry received approval for two projects — the development of Hajee Mohammad Danesh Science and Technology University and the third revision of the Bangladesh University of Professionals development project.

title: Lawyer Alif murder case sent to trial court
body: Lawyer Saiful Islam Alif murder case has been sent to the trial court after completing all legal procedures by a Chattogram Court. Chattogram metropolitan magistrate Abu Bakkar Siddique issued the order on Tuesday. The court’s assistant public prosecutor Md Raihanul Wazed Chowdhury stated that the Chattogram metropolitan magistrate court had directed the lawyer Saiful Islam Alif murder case to be transferred to the metropolitan sessions judge court for additional legal proceedings. Jamal Uddin, the father of the martyred lawyer Alif, a member of the District Bar Association, and the plaintiff in the case, was present in court at that time. Subsequently, the judicial proceedings of the case will commence in the Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court or any other court designated by the court. Among the 39 accused listed in the charge-sheet of the Alif murder case, 17 are currently absconding. Arrest warrants, Hulia, and Croki warrants have been issued against the fugitive accused. Notices have also been published in newspapers. On November 26 in 2024, lawyer Alif was brutally beaten and hacked to death during a clash over the bail of Sanatani Jagran Jote spokesperson Chinmoy Krishna Das at the Chattogram Court Building area. Following the incident, his father Jamal Uddin filed a murder case with the city’s Kotwali police station, naming 31 individuals as suspects. On June 1, 2025, the investigation officer of the case, assistant police commissioner Mahfuzur Rahman, who was serving in the Kotwali Zone of the Chattogram metropolitan police at the time, submitted a charge-sheet to the relevant branch of the Chattogram court in the Alif murder case. A charge-sheet was filed in court accusing 38 people, including Chinmoy Krishna Das Brahmachari, the spokesperson of the Sanatani Jagran Jote. On August 25, the court accepted the charge-sheet against 39 people, including Sukanta Dutta, after the investigation officer submitted it for admissibility in the court of the then Chattogram metropolitan magistrate SM Alauddin Mahmud.

title: Govt primary school head teachers put in grade 10
body: The primary and mass education ministry on Tuesday issued an order to raise the salaries of the head teachers of all government primary schools to the 10th grade. Following this, basic salary of the head teachers will start at Tk 16,000 with the highest range of Tk 38,640. Before Tuesday, the head teachers got salaries as per the 11th grade where the basic salary started at Tk 12,500 and ended at Tk 30,200 as the highest phase. The ministry issued a press release on Tuesday saying that the ministry issued the order for the 65,502 head teachers of the government primary schools. Within 18 months of the issuance of the order, the untrained head teachers will have to complete Basic Training for Primary Education, the order read. The release also read that following this breakthrough decision, the long expectations of the head teachers have been fulfilled. The initiative will also ensure financial security of the teachers and their social dignity, it continued, as a result they will fulfil more creative and enthusiastic role in the development of primary education. Earlier, the government made the decision on July 28following a Supreme Court order in a civil review Petition Number 124/2022. After a long legal procedure, the order was issued on Tuesday. Earlier, a consultation committee on quality improvement of primary and non-formal education formed by the ministry in September last year recommended an immediate pay rise for the government primary school teachers. They made the recommendation in February this year.

title: Attempted murder case filed, one arrested
body: An attempted murder case was filed with the Sonadanga police station on Tuesday over the shooting of a senior leader of Jatiya Sramik Shakti, the labour wing of the National Citizen Party, at a flat in the Sonadanga area of Khulna city the previous day. Victim Motaleb Shikder’s wife Fatima Akter filed the case as plaintiff against Tania Tonni and seven to eight unnamed people on charges of attempted murder and extortion, said Khulna Metropolitan Police South Division deputy commissioner Mohammad Tazul Islam. ‘We have arrested the woman named Tania Tonni as she is the named accused in the case. The incident took place at Tonni’s rented flat,’ Tazul told New Age. Motaleb, 45, who was the organising secretary of the labour organisation’s Khulna Divisional unit, suffered bullet injury in his ear at about 11:45am on Monday allegedly following a clash over the sharing of money from peddling drugs. ‘He was rushed to Khulna Medical College Hospital,’ the police official added. The Border Guard Bangladesh’s Battalion- 6 has tightened security along the bordering areas in Chuadanga and Meherpur to bar the perpetrators from fleeing to India, said the battalion’s commanding officer, Lieutenant Colonel Md Nazmul Hasan. He also said that they received a photo of a man named Sourav Gazi, the suspect of opening fire at the NCP leader, from their headquarters. Several police officials, seeking anonymity, said that Motaleb was shot inside the flat and the incident took place following a clash over sharing money from peddling drugs. They said that they had seized several bottles of liquor, instruments for consuming drugs like Yaba, and other substances that are used in doing immoral activities. They said that a woman rented the flat and the victim used to live there identifying himself as her husband.

title: Helen Keller Int’l hosts learning sharing workshop
body: A learning-sharing workshop of the ‘Building resilient futures: Advancing livelihoods and financial inclusion for marginalised communities’ project organised by Helen Keller Intl Bangladesh was held at a Dhaka hotel on Tuesday. The project was successfully implemented by Helen Keller Intl Bangladesh in two remote unions of Bishwambharpur Upazila under Sunamganj, said a press release. Director general of department of livestock services SM Abu Sufiun was present as chief guest. The event commenced with a welcome address by Pooja Pandey Rana, country director of Helen Keller Intl Bangladesh and Nepal. Md Akram Hossain Chowdhury, project director, department of agricultural extension, Md Amimul Ehshan, deputy director, department of fisheries, were present as special guests. High officials of DLS, DoF, department of agricultural extension, department of youth development, department of women affairs, union chairmen, representatives of development partners, media and officials of Helen Keller Intl Bangladesh were also present. Additionally, representatives of project participants attended the event to share their positive changes through the project. At the event, Project Manager Md. Mahabub Hassan shared impactful learnings and scalable model to further expand income-generating opportunities and financial inclusion of women from disadvantaged communities. The event concluded with the vote of thanks by Md Mahmudul Hasan, deputy country director of Helen Keller Intl Bangladesh. Over the past year, the project carried out under the supervision of Helen Keller Intl Bangladesh has been implemented in the two unions of Dakshin Badaghat and Palash, Bishwambharpur Upazila, Sunamganj.

title: Bhashani’s path guides human emancipation: int’l confce
body: Dhaka University professor emeritus Serajul Islam Choudhury on Tuesday said that Maulana Abdul Hamid Khan Bhashani’s path remains a guide to human emancipation and genuine freedom amid the current global crisis. He said these at a two-day international conference titled ‘Decolonisation and Maulana Bhashani’, which began at Dhaka University on Tuesday, organised by the Centre for Advanced Research in Arts and Social Sciences of Dhaka University. In his presidential address, professor Serajul Islam Choudhury described Maulana Bhashani as a lifelong social revolutionary and visionary thinker committed to the liberation of the people of this land. His politics, he said, was aimed not at power or elections but at equality, social ownership and democratic socialist transformation. The inaugural session was held at the auditorium of the Nabab Nawab Ali Chowdhury Senate Building, beginning with a welcome address by the centre director professor Ashfaque Hossain. Education adviser to the interim government Chowdhury Rafiqul Abrar attended the programme as the chief guest, while CARASS chairman and emeritus professor Serajul Islam Choudhury presided over the session. The keynote paper was presented by University of Brunei Darussalam associate professor Iftekhar Iqbal. In his speech, education adviser professor Abrar said that Maulana Abdul Hamid Khan Bhashani was not merely a political leader, but the conscience of the masses, a symbol of morality and a visionary anti-imperialist thinker. He said Bhashani’s politics was never detached from the people, as he always stood by poor farmers, workers and the oppressed, prioritising people’s politics over power-centric politics. In his welcome speech, professor Ashfaque Hossain said that Maulana Bhashani was a rare social revolutionary who stood against colonialism, capitalism and imperialism. Following the inaugural session, a photographic exhibition on the life and struggle of Maulana Bhashani was held. On Wednesday, the second day, the conference will feature a panel discussion on Bhashani’s worldview, political thought and role in the process of decolonisation, with speakers including professor Ahmed Kamal and professor Mahbub Ullah, among other scholars. A special review session titled ‘Fire dekha Farakka Long March’ will also be held by their research team, analysing the political and social significance of the historic Farakka long march.

title: NDF sets candidates for 122 seats
body: The newly-formed National Democratic Front, led by Jatiya Party factions, announced the names of the candidates for 122 seats for the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad elections scheduled for February 12. The executive chairman of a JP faction, Mujibul Haque Chunnu, announced the names of aspirant candidates at a press conference at a city hotel on Tuesday. JP faction chairman Anisul Islam Mahmud, secretary general ABM Ruhul Amin Hawlader, Jatiya Party-JP chairman Anwar Hossain Manju and others spoke at the programme. The aspirant candidates are Anisul Islam Mahmud for Chattogram-5, Anwar Hossain Manju for Pirojpur-2, ABM Ruhul Amin Hawlader for Patualhali-1, Kazi Firoz Rashid for Dhaka-10, Mujibul Haque Chunnu for Kishoreganj-3, JP secretary general Sheikh Shahidul Islam for Madaripur-3, coordinator of NDF Golam Sarwar Milon for Manikganj-2, Shah Mohammad Abu Zafar for Faridpur-2, Jahirul Islam Jahir for Tangail-7 and others.

title: Hadi murder trial in 30 working days demanded
body: Inquilab Mancha on Tuesday took an ‘oath of martyr’, urging the government to arrest the killers of its slain convener Sharif Osman Hadi and complete the offenders’ trial within 30 working days. They took the oath in front of the Bangladesh National Museum in Dhaka, while its member secretary Abdullah Al Jaber administered the oath in the presence of Osman Hadi’s brother Omar Bin Hadi. Hadi, also an organiser of the July uprising, died at a hospital in Singapore on December 18, six days after he was shot in the head in Dhaka on December 12. After taking the oath, Abdullah Al Jaber announced a two-day programme, including drawing graffiti on walls and presenting Hadi’s struggle in Bangladesh and across the globe for today and tomorrow. ‘We will announce our next programme after December 26,’ he added. Addressing the ‘oath of martyr’, Osman Hadi’s brother Omar Bin Hadi said, ‘Osman Hadi said that the national election would have to be held in the country in February. He came to the field after taking preparations for contesting the election. But, efforts were made to hinder the election by killing him.’ On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head in the capital while conducting his electioneering as an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency, a day after the Election Commission had announced the schedule for the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections and the national referendum on February 12 next year. Law enforcers have so far arrested at least 10 people for their suspected involvement in the attack on Hadi, but the main suspects are yet to be arrested and are believed to have fled to India.

title: Cultural activists protest at mob violence, demand govt action
body: Cultural activists on Tuesday protested at the recent incidents of mob violence in the country and demanded that the government check mob violence and ensure security of citizens. They made the demands in the wake of mob violence on newspaper offices, cultural organisations and shrines. The Nipiran Birodhi Shilpi Samaj, a platform for cultural activists, made an eight-point demand at a protest rally in front of the Abahani Math at Dhanmondi in the capital Dhaka on Tuesday. It organised the protest against the arson attacks on the offices of two media houses, The Daily Star and the Prothom Alo, and on the offices of cultural organisations, Chhayanaut and Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigoshthi, on December 18 and 19. The protest rally consisted of musical performances, poetry recitation, performance arts and live scroll painting which also addressed the ongoing target killings, crimes based on identity and majority and the government’s failure in preventing violence across the country. Artist, art critic and curator Mustafa Zaman, curator Shehzad Chowdhury, artist and curator Kazi Tahsin Agaz Apurbo, artist Suborna Morsheada, singers and activists Arup Rahee, Krishnakali and Sohini Alam, filmmakers Akram Khan and Leesa Gazi, theatre activists Azad Abul Kalam and Bakar Bakul, photographer and activist Jannatul Mawa, writer Tahmid Zami, actress Azmeri Haque Badhon and Bengal Foundation director general Luva Nahid Choudhury, among others, participated in the protest rally. Arup Rahee said that the nation was waiting for general elections, but target killings and mob violence were increasing, which made the law and order situation in the country unstable. ‘After the 2024 mass uprising, the interim government failed to restore law and order in the country and a vested group promoted identity- and majority-based politics instead of unity,’ Arup Rahee said, adding that ‘people desire power but hate mob violence.’ Tahmid Zami said that ‘annihilation’ politics had been practiced since the mass uprising in Bangladesh, as ‘nearly the same number of people was killed in violence before and after the uprising.’ At the rally, the activists announced their eight-point demand, including immediate investigation and trial of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi murder, punishment of perpetrators of the attacks on the offices of newspapers and cultural organisations and the attacks on shrines, and upholding autonomy of state-run cultural and educational intuitions. Cultural institution Chhayanaut on Tuesday organised a musical event, protesting at vandalism and arson attacks on the offices of two media houses and the offices of cultural organisations in front of its building at Dhanmondi in the capital. Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigoshthi also organised a torch rally on Topkhana Road in the capital as part of its nationwide protest rally on the mob attacks.

title: Traders fined for selling fertilisers at higher price in Rajshahi
body: The National Consumer Rights Protection Directorate on Tuesday fined a fertiliser trader Tk 30,000 at Godagari upazila in Rajshahi for selling fertiliser at prices higher than the government-fixed rates. The assistant director of Rajshah office, Bipul Biswas, fined Hasan Ali, owner of Messrs Hasan Traders at Ujanpara Bypass of Matikata union in the upazila, under the Consumer Rights Protection Act, 2009. Bipul Biswas told New Age that they conducted a drive at the fertiliser’s shop following complaints from farmers that the trader was charging prices higher than the government-set rates. ‘The trader was found selling diammonium phosphate, also known as DAP, at Tk 1520 per 50 kilogramme sack and triple superphosphate, also known as TSP, at Tk 1600 per sack, although the government-set rates were Tk 1050 and Tk 1350 respectively. The official added that regular market monitoring and mobile court operations were being conducted across different upazilas of Rajshahi district to protect farmers’ interests and ensure fair prices.

title: Petrobangla, BMTF sign deal
body: Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation and Bangladesh Machine Tools Factory Limited signed a contract, aiming to implement ‘Designing, development, implementation, commissioning and maintenance of GPS location based gas metres and metring stations monitoring management system’ in Petrobangla’s gas production and marketing companies on Monday. The event was attended by Md Rezanur Rahman, chairman of Petrobangla, and Major General Md Naheed Asgar, managing director of BMTF, said a press release. The contract was signed by Md Amzad Hossain, secretary and senior general manager of Petrobangla, and Lieutenant Colonel ASM Fakhrul Islam Chowdhury from BMTF. The event was also attended by the directors of Petrobangla, senior officials of BMTF, and the managing director of the Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution PLC.

title: EU stresses press freedom during democratic transition
body: The European Union has underscored the centrality of media freedom to Bangladesh’s democratic transition, stressing the need to promote and protect freedom of expression as the country moves forward amid ongoing political reforms. Marking International Migrants Day, the union joined BRAC and Bangladeshi authorities to recognise excellence in investigative journalism and reporting on migration issues through the 10th media awards ceremony, said the EU delegation in Dhaka on Tuesday. The union reiterated its support for safe, dignified and legal migration, while firmly opposing exploitation, abuse and risks associated with irregular migration. On the occasion, the union encouraged the interim government to finalise provisions to include migrant smuggling in the proposed Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking and Smuggling of Migrants Ordinance, 2025. It also reaffirmed its determination to expand legal pathways for skilled and semi-skilled regular migration from Bangladesh to EU member states. As Bangladesh continues its transition and approaches elections, the EU, in the presence of award-winning journalists, highlighted the vital role of a free and independent media in ensuring transparency, accountability and democratic progress.

title: Parties pledge democratic country thru reforms
body: Leaders of major political parties on Tuesday expressed grave concern, saying that the recent incidents of violence were casting uncertainty over the forthcoming 13th Jatiya Sangsad election. They also outlined their respective visions for democratic reform, economic recovery and governance in post-uprising Bangladesh. The leaders at a dialogue also pledged to build a new Bangladesh through necessary reforms and obliterating fascism, and by means of leading the country to achieve economic freedom, good governance, democracy, and by protecting the rights of the citizens, including women and national and religious minorities. Their commitments came at the Star Elections Dialogue titled ‘Your Party, Voters’ Questions’, organised by The Daily Star at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka. Representatives of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, Communist Party of Bangladesh and the National Citizen Party were present at the dialogue. BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said at the dialogue that attacks on different institutions centring Sharif Osman Hadi’s death caused concern among the public over holding of the general elections. ‘The incidents that occurred over the past few months, and particularly in the past several days, have made people seriously anxious,’ he said, adding, ‘People are now once again questioning whether the election will be held at all.’ Fakhrul said that although an opportunity for a fair election emerged after the fall of the previous regime in a mass uprising, that opportunity now appeared to be ‘almost slipping away’. ‘Whenever we have an opportunity, certain groups and incidents destroy it. We want to remove that pall of anxiety and move towards the election with hope,’ he stated. Highlighting BNP’s long-standing emphasis on elections, he said that the party was often criticised for prioritising polls. ‘But it is now proved that delays have given opportunities to sabotage the election. That is why we have always demanded election,’ he said. Referring to BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia’s Vision 2030 announced in 2016, Fakhrul said that many of the current reform proposals were already included in that document among which was restructuring of the political system, balancing of power among state institutions, and ensuring full independence of the judiciary and media. He also stated that his party placed strong emphasis on women empowerment. He mentioned the party’s 31-point reform proposal made public in 2023 contained, among other propositions, formation of a constitutional reform commission, a national reconciliation commission, and the restoration of a non-party caretaker government system. On economy, Fakhrul said that democratic and economic institutions were destroyed, creating an oligarchic system allowing a coterie to plunder national wealth. The BNP prepared a comprehensive economic plan with a view to overcoming the economic crisis within five years. CPB presidium member Mujahidul Islam Selim said that when the economy was dictated by ‘market fundamentalism’, lawmaker and ministerial positions became commodities. ‘Politics is the concentrated expression of economics. If the economy is one of looting, the politics will also be of looting,’ he said, adding that the War of Independence was not fought to establish a capitalist state. He advocated allocating 30–40 per cent of the national budget to local governments, criticising the growing influence of money in elections, particularly the increase in candidate security deposits to Tk 50,000. Jamaat-e-Islami assistant secretary general Hamidur Rahman Azad said that his party wanted to build a just, ‘insaf’ based Bangladesh ensuring economic freedom, good governance and democracy. ‘Just as a child is safe in a mother’s lap, we want citizens to feel safe in this country,’ he said, identifying corruption as the root cause of instability and pledging zero tolerance. National Citizen Party convener Nahid Islam said that the upcoming election should be viewed as a referendum to realise the promises of the mass uprising, not merely a transfer of power. He said that the uprising aimed to establish a democratic system, create an anti-discrimination and economically just society, and protect national sovereignty and dignity. Nahid alleged that the BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami were competing to secure the vote bank of ousted Awami League and criticised the absence of a Truth Commission to address past crimes of the authoritarian regime. ‘Supporting a fascist party is a moral crime, but those involved in genocide must face justice,’ he said. BNP and Jamaat leaders rejected the allegations of infiltration of AL people in their parties. Mujahidul Islam Selim remarked that political infiltration was a long-standing reality rooted in the country’s political culture. The Daily Star editor and publisher Mahfuz Anam who could not attend the event due to illness, in a statement, expressed concern over the recent attacks on his office and that of Prothom Alo. ‘These were not just attacks on media houses. These attacks are against democracy and are meant to jeopardise the upcoming election,’ he said. The Daily Star believed in democracy and in ‘an honest, accountable, and transparent government’ that protected people’s fundamental rights, the editor’s statement read.

title: Ex-PDB member Masud Jamali dies
body: Former member of Bangladesh Power Development Board and renowned Masud Hasan Jamali passed away at Uttara Crescent Hospital on Monday. He was 89. He is survived by his wife and a daughter. PDB chairman Md Rezaul Karim expressed deep shock at the death of Masud Jamali and extended deep sympathy to the bereaved family. Masud Hasan Jamali joined the then EP WAPDA as an assistant engineer on May 10 in 1962. Later, he held several important positions of the Bangladesh Power Development Board. He was well-known as a skilled engineer in his professional life. He retired as member (generation) of PDB in December 1995. Masud Hasan was also known as a prominent sports organiser. He served as general secretary of the Bangladesh Tennis Federation for two terms, from 1986 to 1990 and then from 1996 to 1998. He is the proud father of the late Shovon Jamali, former national tennis champion and a player of the Bangladesh Davis Cup team. Masud was buried at the Azimpur Old Garveyard on Tuesday following his namaz-e-janaza after Zuhr prayers at Uttara Jame Mosque.

title: ICT rebukes chief prosecutor for interrupting hearing
body: A judge of the International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Tuesday rebuked and cautioned chief prosecutor Muhammad Tajul Islam for repeatedly interrupting the proceedings during a hearing in the enforced disappearance case involving deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina, 11 army officers and five other accused. The exchanges took place while the three-member tribunal, chaired by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder, was hearing defence submissions on the timeline for starting the trial and recording witness depositions. Justice Shofiul Alam Mahmood rebuked chief prosecutor Tajul Islam for repeatedly standing up and speaking without permission, saying that the chief prosecutor could not address the tribunal unless he was allowed. The judge asked whether Tajul was trying to stop the tribunal from speaking. At one stage of the hearing, as Tajul had been standing up repeatedly for speaking without permission, tribunal member Justice Md Shofiul Alam Mahmood asked him to sit down and maintain courtroom decorum, saying the tribunal expected restrained and professional conduct from the prosecution. The chairman intervened to calm the situation and clarified that the defence must be heard before the prosecution. He also said that the tribunal had not yet formed any opinion on granting time. As one of the defence counsels, Tabarak Hossain, sought three months for beginning the trial, the tribunal noted that the defence had already received case documents on November 25 and that the additional four weeks granted would make the preparation period nearly two months, although the law allows only 21 days. Defence counsel Tabarak Hossain argued that more time was needed to ensure a fair trial. Tajul opposed the request, alleging that the defence was attempting to delay the proceedings and stressed that the case must be tried speedily under a special law. The chairman said that the tribunal would not repeat past practices and added that no adjournments would be allowed after beginning the trial. The hearing ended with the tribunal asking both the defence and the prosecution to maintain discipline and avoid such confrontations in the future.
