title: Dhaka becomes 2nd most polluted city with AQI score of 230
body: Dhaka, the overcrowded capital city of Bangladesh, has ranked second on the list of cities with the worst air quality with an AQI score of 230 at about 10:15am on Sunday morning. On Sunday Dhaka’s air was classified as ‘very unhealthy’ referring to an alarming healthy threat, according to the air quality index. When the AQI value for particle pollution is between 50 and 100, air quality is considered ‘moderate’, usually sensitive individuals should consider limiting prolonged outdoor exertion, between 101 and 150, air quality is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, between 150 and 200 is ‘unhealthy’, between 201 and 300 is said to be ‘very unhealthy’, while a reading of 301 and above is considered ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks to residents. India’s Delhi, Egypt’s Cairo and Pakistan’s Karachi cities respectively occupied the first, second and third spots on the list, with AQI scores of 250, 218, and 215 respectively. The AQI, an index for reporting daily air quality, informs people how clean or polluted the air of a certain city is and what associated health effects might be a concern for them. The AQI in Bangladesh is based on five pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), NO2, CO, SO2, and ozone. Dhaka has long been grappling with air pollution issues. Its air quality usually turns unhealthy in winter and improves during the monsoon. As per World Health Organisation, air pollution kills an estimated seven million people worldwide every year, mainly due to increased mortality from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.

title: Name of DU Sheikh Mujib hall replaced with Shaheed Osman Hadi Hall
body: After burying beside the grave of National Poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, agitated students replaced the name of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall with Shaheed Osman Hadi Hall at Dhaka University on Saturday night. On Saturday night around 9:00pm, leaders of the hall union brought a crane to the site and removed the existing name and wrote Shaheed Sharif Osman Hadi Hall in its place. At the same time, the portrait of Sheikh Mujib on the upper wall of the old building at the hall’s entrance was disfigured. Earlier on Thursday night, students of the dormitory pasted posters reading Shaheed Sharif Osman Hadi Hall over the hall’s nameplate. Earlier on Saturday, Dhaka University Central Students’ Union announced a programme to besiege the vice-chancellor’s office at 2:30pm on Sunday, demanding the renaming of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall and Sheikh Fazilatunnesa Mujib Hall. According to a media release signed by the DUCSU literary and cultural affairs secretary, the central student union announced to enforce the programme to press their three demands, renaming Mujib Hall as Shaheed Osman Hadi Hall, Fazilatunnesa Hall as Felani Hall, and taking administrative action against teachers, officers, and staff who took position against the July uprising. Speaking about the removal of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall’s name, the hall’s vice-president Muslimur Rahman said those responsible for Hadi’s killing are linked to the fallen fascist forces, and Sheikh Mujib is the ideological father of those fascists. ‘By removing Sheikh Mujib’s name and renaming the hall after Osman Hadi, we are showing respect for Hadi,’ he said. Despite identifying the killers, the government has failed to arrest the killers, he alleged, saying that ‘From our position, this is what we can do renaming the hall after Hadi.’ Muslimur claimed that they conducted an opinion poll where the majority of students supported the renaming of the hall. Earlier on September 3, the university administration partially changed name of the hall by removing Jatir Janak and Bangabandhu and set Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall.

title: Shipping adviser inaugurates Ananda Bazar launch terminal in Bhola
body: Shipping adviser M Sakhawat Hussain inaugurated the Ananda Bazar launch terminal at Charfasson in Bhola on Saturday, built by the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority. The people of Dhalchar and Ananda Bazar have been neglected and deprived for generations. With the inauguration of this launch terminal today, their long-standing sufferings have come to an end, he said at the inaugural ceremony. He added, ‘This is not just an infrastructure project; rather, it is a bridge to safe communication and development for the marginalised population.’ Dhalchar is a remote and isolated island area located at the extreme southern end of upazila, near the confluence of the Meghna River and the Bay of Bengal. It is actually one of the last frontiers of Bangladesh. Because of its geographical location, the people of this area had long been deprived of safe and regular water transport facilities. Due to adverse weather, tidal fluctuations, and unsafe jetties, travel was risky and difficult. The shipping adviser said, ‘People of this region used to face severe hardships in accessing healthcare, education, administrative services, and transporting daily necessities. With the operation of this new launch terminal, access to these services will become easier, and local economic activities will gain momentum.’ The adviser said that the government was giving special importance to improving water transport infrastructure to connect people of marginal and remote island areas with the mainstream of development. Harnessing the potential of riverine Bangladesh, the government aims to ensure balanced development in every corner of the country, he said. BIWTA chairman, officials of the shipping ministry and BIWTA, district and upazila administration were present at the programme.

title: Some parties trying to fish in troubled waters for political gains: Abbas
body: Senior leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party Mirza Abbas on Saturday alleged that a few political parties were trying to fish in troubled waters by holding people hostage to serve their narrow political interests. The people of this country earned independence in 1971 and secured their right to speak freely in ’24 through immense blood and sacrifice, he said. Speaking at a workers’ meeting in the capital, the BNP leader also said that attempts were now being made to snatch away those rights achieved in 1971 and 2024. ‘A few political parties are trying to hold the people of Bangladesh hostage to gain political advantage. They want to muddy the waters and fish in them,’ he said. Abbas, a BNP standing committee member, called upon party leaders, activists and the general public to remain alert to tackle the plots against the country. He warned that any attempt to create unrest in Dhaka city will not be allowed, saying the BNP will resist all such efforts. ‘Our leader Tarique Rahman announced that he would be coming to Bangladesh… After that announcement, a murder took place, followed by a series of incidents one after another. This means it is a planned design,’ Abbas observed. He said that such activities were aimed at ‘snatching away the democratic rights of the people’ that were achieved in 1971. ‘We will not allow those rights to be taken away. We will restore our right to vote at any cost.’ The BNP leader also warned against any attempts to disrupt the next election. ‘Those who try to foil the polls will receive their answer through the election process itself. The election will be held in this country, and it must take place.’ The meeting was organised at the Sadeque Hossain Khoka Community Centre in Gopibagh by the Dhaka South City unit of the BNP as part of preparations to welcome Tarique Rahman on his return home on Thursday, ending his nearly 18 years in exile in London. Abbas told the meeting that the return of the BNP Acting Chairman symbolises the return of democracy to Bangladesh. ‘He is coming to restore democracy. Do not be misled by what others say.’ In an oblique reference to Jamaat-e-Islami, he said, ‘The party does not want Bangladesh to remain peaceful as it had opposed the country’s birth.’ ‘Those who do not wish well for the country and do not love it may look like human beings, but they are devils in human form. They opposed Pakistan in 1947 and opposed Bangladesh in 1971. They do not want peace in the country. Even if they remain silent for some time, their claws and poisonous fangs grow again. Their activities are systematic and continuous,’ the BNP leader said. He said that undemocratic forces would not be able to survive in the face of democracy and warned those engaged in conspiracy to be cautious as the people of the country knew them well. ‘Several newspaper offices and a number of institutions were torched and burned down. Who are these people? Do they love the country? They are enemies of the nation and enemies of the country. They must be stopped,’ Abbas said. He also criticised the government and law enforcement agencies for failing to prevent arson attacks and mob violence. ‘When we went to meet the head of this government, we repeatedly said that we had extended a hand of cooperation to you. But you did not accept that hand of cooperation,’ the BNP leader said. He also alleged that the interim government was siding with anti-Bangladesh forces working to destroy the country. ‘So many incidents are happening—where are the arrests? Where are the law enforcement agencies? They are nowhere to be seen on the ground.’ The meeting was chaired by Dhaka South BNP member secretary Tanvir Ahmed Robin. Candidates and leaders from several Dhaka constituencies, including Nabi Ullah Nabi, Ishraque Hossain, Hamidur Rahman Hamid, Habibur Rashid Habib and Sheikh Robiul Alam, also addressed the programme.

title: 3 day int’l conference EICT 2025 ends at KUET
body: A three-day international conference titled the 7th International Conference on Electrical, Information and Communication Technology concluded at Khulna University of Engineering and Technology on Friday evening at the Teachers’ Auditorium of the university guest house. The conference was organised by the university’s electrical and electronic engineering department and brought together researchers, engineers and academics from home and abroad. Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, intergovernmental organisations and consular affairs, M Farhadul Islam, addressed the programme as chief guest. Vice-chancellor of KUET, Professor Md Maksud Helali, was present as the chief patron of the conference. The programme was presided over by conference chair and dean of the faculty of electrical and electronic engineering, Prof Md Rafiqul Islam. The international conference, which began on December 18, focused on recent developments and challenges in the fields of electrical, information and communication technology. Researchers and engineers from different countries presented their latest research findings during the sessions. The event was technically co-sponsored by the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE). Speakers at the closing session said that such international conferences played a vital role in knowledge exchange and in addressing the challenges of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. At the end of the programme, the Fatema Rashid Best Paper Award and IEEE Best Paper Award were presented to authors of selected outstanding research papers. Among others, Organising Chair Prof Kazi Md Rakibul Alam, Publication Chair Prof Monir Hossain, TPC Chair Prof Md Rafiqul Islam and TPC Secretary Prof A B M Awlad Hossain, were present. The three-day conference featured discussions on modern research trends, challenges and prospects in the electrical and ICT sectors. A total of 142 technical papers, selected from 1,042 submissions from 15 countries, were presented in 25 technical sessions. Researchers, teachers, renowned engineers and technologists from the United States, France, Japan, Canada, Taiwan, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, India and Bangladesh, among others, participated in the conference.

title: Female leader of anti-discrimination movement files rape case
body: A youth leader of the anti-discrimination movement in Barishal filed a rape case on Saturday against a man, alleging that he committed the crime after pledging to marry her. The victim filed the case against Suwan Al Talukder, 24, with the Kotwali Model Police under the Barisal Metropolitan Police. Barishal Kotwali police officer-in-charge Al Mamun Ul Islam confirmed filing of the case. The police took cognisance of the case filed by the plaintiff against Suwan, he said, adding that no arrest had been made in the case. Accused Swan Al Talukder, son of Jahangir Talukder, is a resident of Manosha Bari Talukder Villa under Kaunia police in Barishal city. According to the case statement, the plaintiff had met Suwan during the anti-discrimination movement and their friendship turned to an affair. Later, the accused raped the plaintiff against her will several times with temptation of marriage. In addition, on October 11, he forcibly took her to a hotel on Sadar Road in Barishal city and recorded a video of their relationship. When she pressured the accused to marry her, Suwan started harassing her. Suwan also hit her with his motorcycle helmet with intention of killing.

title: Experts for protecting migratory birds for ecological balance
body: Experts at a workshop in Rajshahi on Saturday called for taking immediate measures to protect the migratory birds and their habitats from pollution. They also stressed the importance of strengthening existing laws against bird hunting and poaching and increasing the involvement of local administration to catch poachers. Nature and Biodiversity Conservation Forum organised the workshop titled Way Forward for Biodiversity Conservation at Christian Mission Hospital conference hall in the city. The event focused on how urban and rural areas could become better habitats for migratory birds by taking actions like improving city planning, reducing pollution, and minimising threats such as collisions and light pollution. The goal is to foster coexistence where both people and birds can thrive together in shared environments. Retired professor Bidhan Chandra Das from the department of zoology at Rajshahi University and Professor Jalal Uddin Sarder from the department of veterinary and animal sciences at RU addressed the meeting as resource persons disseminating their expertise on the issue. Director of Bangladesh Betar Hassan Akhter, NBCF general secretary Junayed Ahmed and chief executive officer of Mission Hospital Prodip Chand Mondal also spoke at the seminar, which was chaired by NBCF president Professor BK Dam. Discussions highlighted the crucial role of migratory birds played in natural balance such as insect and seed dispersal, nutrient cycling and pollination. There is a strong call for creating safe havens and gardens with adequate security to ensure the survival and breeding of migratory birds. Professor Bidhan Chandra Das called for highlighting the impact of light and plastic pollution on migratory birds and their habitats; and protecting nature and natural resources through adopting time-befitting and effective measures for conservation of biodiversity. He underlined the need for creating gardens with adequate protection and security for migratory birds to ensure their safe living and breeding. Professor Jalal Uddin Sarder said that out of about 710 species of birds, including resident and migratory birds in Bangladesh, 650 species of birds had been included in the schedule of Wildlife (Conservation and Security) Act. The birds which migrate from one place to another during a certain time of the year are known as migratory birds. These creatures play a significant role in maintaining ecological equilibrium. Earlier, the experts distributed leaflets at T-groin and Srirampur area for resisting bird hunting through creating awareness among the public in general.

title: NTMC abolition, telecommunication ordinance demanded
body: Civil society representatives on Saturday urged the government to approve the draft of the Bangladesh Telecommunication (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025 outside the authority of the ministries of law, justice and parliamentary affairs and home affairs to hold the officers and employees accountable. In a statement, issued on the day and signed by writer and organiser Nahed Hasan, they also called the government to abolish the National Telecommunication Monitoring Centre. They alleged that though stakeholders participated in the formulation of new ordinance and amendments to existing law (Bangladesh Telecommunication Act, 2001), their opinions continued to be ignored. They said that although the draft ordinance was placed in the Cabinet on December 12 but it did not get approval. For long, the NTMC is criticised for alleged violation of human rights, illegal and uncontrolled surveillance and enforced disappearances, while the full details of the activities of the centre also came from the government formed Commission of Enquiry on Enforced Disappearances. Instead of abolishing the centre, they alleged that the government on October 15 this year had drafted a law by proposing three new names for the centre without taking opinions and participation of the citizens. The statement read that—‘It is learned that NTMC has drafted this law to further strengthen the institution’s surveillance.’ Mentioning that complexities are being created over who will have the power to wiretap and monitor, which agencies will be authorised and oversee the wiretaps, and how the distribution of power will be determined, the representatives of civil society said that these days were similar to the days of Sheikh Hasina. They further alleged that led by the home adviser the entire home ministry was conspiring to fail the draft ordinance just like the Hasina government. They urged the chief adviser and other concerned officials not to shut down, disrupt or limit internet connection in any situation. They also urged the government to abolish the centre and approve the draft ordinance. The statement was signed by 94 representatives of civil society, including Transparency International Bangladesh executive director Iftekharuzzaman, former Jahangirnagar University professor and economist Anu Muhammad, writer, intellectual, and critic Salimullah Khan, human rights activists Nur Khan Liton and Rezaur Rahman Lenin, novelist and publisher Moinul Ahsan Saber, Dhaka University professor Md Kamrul Hassan Mamun, writer and researcher Rakhal Raha, writer and teacher Fahmidul Huq, and singer and researcher Arup Rahee.

title: DUCSU to besiege VC office for renaming Mujib hall
body: Dhaka University Central Students’ Union on Saturday announced a programme to besiege the vice-chancellor’s office, demanding the renaming of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall as Shahid Osman Hadi Hall and Bangamata Sheikh Fazilatunnesa Hall as Felani Hall. According to the announcement, DUCSU will besiege the VC’s office on Sunday at about 2:30pm. However, Fazilatunnesa Hall general secretary Miftahul Jannat Rifat said in a Facebook post on Saturday evening that no consultation had been held with any hall union representatives before the post was made from DUCSU’s official Facebook page. She said that they were in agreement with renaming and had been collecting opinions from female residents through internal hall groups. She added that the option receiving the highest votes from a large number of residents was Captain Sitara Begum, a Bir Protik, the students expressed the wish that their hall be named after women who played leading roles in Bangladesh’s liberation struggle. She noted that the name ‘Felani Hall’ was the second highest-voted option and that they intended to work with both names at the final stage, while condemning any imposed decision. DUCSU announced the programme through a Facebook post on Saturday. The organisation also demanded administrative action against teachers, officers and employees who supported July mass killings.

title: 6 AL men arrested in Khulna, Bagerhat, Satkhira
body: The members of Coast Guard have arrested six leaders and activists of the Awami League, activities banned, in Khulna, Bagerhat and Satkhira during an overnight operation. Coast Guard media officer Lieutenant Commander Siam-ul-Haq on Saturday said that based on secret information, the force of the west zone conducted five separate operations at Mongla and Morelganj in Bagerhat, Rupsha and Dacope in Khulna and Joykhali under Shyamnagar in Satkhira from 5:00pm on Friday 19 to 6:00am on Saturday. Asaduzzaman Sabuj, 34, Md Shahin Alam, 48, Rabiul Islam Litu, 58, Sheikh Azharul Islam, 67, Bidyut Biswas, 66 and Md Shahinur Gazi, 38, were arrested from the areas. All the people arrested in the operation are local leaders and activists of the Awami League.

title: JU entrance tests for undergraduate courses begin today
body: Jahangirnagar University begins its undergraduate admission tests for the 2025-26 academic year from today, with 219,399 candidates competing for 1,842 seats, university officials said. On average, 119 students will contest each seat this year, according to data confirmed by Syed Mohammad Ali Reza, deputy registrar, education and secretary of the central admission management committee. The admission tests start today, with the C Unit under the faculty of arts and humanities, faculty of law, institute of comparative literature and culture. Tests for the B unit under the faculty of social sciences and the E unit under the faculty of business studies will be held on December 22. The C1 unit under the department of drama and dramatics, department of fine arts exam and part of the D unit under the faculty of biological sciences test will take place on December 23, followed by the remaining D unit exams on December 24. Part of the A unit under the faculty of mathematical and physical sciences test and the IBA-JU or the institute of business administration exam will be held on December 28, while the rest of the A unit exam is scheduled for December 29. Multiple shifts will run each day. The highest competition will be in the D unit, where 70,220 applicants will vie for 310 seats–an average of 226 candidates per seat, the highest among all units. In A unit, 60,351 applicants will contend for 426 seats, averaging around 141 candidates per seat. The C Unit received 47,497 applications for 466 seats – about 101 candidates per seat. Competition will be lower in the B Unit with 20,583 applicants against 326 seats – an average of 63 per seat. The E Unit drew 11,612 applications for 200 seats, or 58 candidates per seat. In the C1 unit, 3,725 applicants will compete for 64 seats, also averaging 58 candidates per seat. At the IBA-JU, 5,411 candidates applied for 50 seats – around 98 candidates per seat. Candidates must arrive before the reporting time stated on their admit cards and are prohibited from bringing mobile phones, calculators or other electronic devices, the university administration said. Security has been tightened across the campus. A 44-member monitoring committee, led by chief proctor Professor AKM Rashidul Alam, has been formed to oversee safety arrangements, supported by 250 police personnel, 60 Ansar members, traffic police and intelligence officials. Ambulances and medical teams will be on standby for emergencies, officials said.

title: 30 injured as villagers clash in Sunamganj
body: At least 30 people were injured in a clash between the residents of two villages of Jagannathpur upazila in Sunamganj on Saturday over increasing the fare of battery-run auto-rickshaws. Local people said that the committee of vehicle stand at Raniganj Pashchimbazar under Chilaura-Haldipur union of the upazila increased the fare for travelling between Raniganj Bazar and Baudharan area to Tk 40 from Tk 30 around two weeks ago. The decision of increasing the fare, however, angered the inhabitants of Swajanshri village that created a dispute with the residents of Baudharan village, they said. On Friday afternoon, residents of Baudharan village forced the battery-run auto-rickshaws of Swajanshri village out from the vehicle stand of the Pashchimbazar following the dispute, the locals said. As a consequence, residents of both villages engaged in a one and a-half-hour clash from 10:00am with local weapons, including spears and bamboo sticks, injuring more than 30 people of the rival sides, the locals said. Jagannathpur Upazila Health Complex physician Md Badruddoza told reporters that 30 patients with injuries were provided treatment at the health complex. ‘Of them, 12 seriously injured have been sent to Sylhet Osmani Medical College Hospital for better treatment,’ he said. Jagannathpur police station officer-in-charge Shafiqul Islam told New Age that the police reached the spot at around 11:30am and brought the situation under control. ‘A team of police have been deployed in the area to avert further clash,’ he said, adding that no complaint in this regard was filed with the police station till the evening.

title: Unity urged to resist return of fascist rule
body: Jatiya Mukti Council on Saturday condemned the attacks and arson at the offices of the Prothom Alo and the Daily Star, as well as the harassment of New Age editor and Editors’ Council president Nurul Kabir. Secretary of the council Faizul Hakim in a statement also condemned the attack and torching of cultural institutes Chhayanaut and Udichi and the brutal killing of worker Dipu Chandra Das, who was beaten and set on fire. Noting that each of these attacks was pre-planned, the statement also said that the political objective behind these planned attacks was to create chaos and instability in the country in order to thwart the upcoming election. The statement also said that these attacks were act of simultaneous assaults on the people’s freedom of thought and expression. The ultimate goal of such activities was to establish a new fascist rule under the guise of extreme religious ideology, said the JMC statement. Faizul Hakim criticised the interim government’s failure to arrest the killers of Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi. He said that imperialist India and the ousted Awami fascist clique were conspiring to establish an extremist religious fascist regime in the country through creating chaos and instability. He also urged the country’s democratic and revolutionary forces to unite with the people to resist and defeat the conspiracy.

title: World Meditation Day today
body: Bangladesh is going to observe World Meditation Day today, Sunday, like elsewhere in the world, to raise awareness about meditation and its benefits. The UN declared the day last year to create awareness about the practice of meditation in daily life. Through this declaration, the UN primarily reminds people of the universal right to be mentally and physically sound, said a press release issued by Quantum Foundation on Saturday. For more than three decades in Bangladesh, Quantum Foundation has been popularizing the practice of meditation in Bangladesh, the release stated. Thousands of members and well-wishers are practicing meditation regularly and are getting involved in various social and humanitarian activities. Today a special meditation session will be held at the National Press Club premises in the capital from 7:00am to 8:00am, where thousands of practitioners will join, the release also said. On the occasion, the members and well-wishers will meditate simultaneously at various significant locations across the country, including Chattogram, Rajshahi, Barishal, Khulna, and Sylhet. These participants share the belief – ‘If the mind is well, all is well.’ The World Health Organization now refers to meditation as a ‘self-care method’ based on various scientific studies and it encourages regular meditation practice for stress management, the release added. ‘This second-year celebration of the World Meditation Day reaffirms our shared responsibility to focus on what unites us rather than what divides us – to build a world where every individual can live in peace, balance, and harmony,’ states the UN website. ‘Through the power of inner transformation, we can nurture the conditions for sustainable peace – within ourselves, within our communities, and within our shared global home,’ it added.

title: Cultural activists demand home adviser’s removal
body: Cultural activists on Saturday demanded removal of the home advisor Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury from his post due to failure to control mobs and their vandalism across the country. They also said that the government did not try to prevent the attacks on newspapers and cultural institutions although attackers announced their intentions on social media. They made those remarks at a rally at Satyen Sen Chattar, organised by Ganatantrik Sanskritik Oikya, while protesting government failure on people’s security concerns including failure to arrest killers of Sharif Osman Hadi. Ganatantrik Sanskritik Oikya convener and general secretary of Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi Jamshed Anwer Tapan and Bibartan Sangskritik Kendra general secretary Mafijur Rahman Laltu addressed the rally, which was attended by cultural and political activists. Mafijur Rahman Laltu said that the newspapers, religious and national minority communities and cultural organizations across the country suffered from mob violence and organised crime but the government failed to protect the wealth and life of citizens. ‘The government also failed to arrest killers of Hadi and those responsible for the vandalism on the Daily Star and the Prothom Alo, which is shameful for the country but the home advisor is busy on pretence,’ Laltu said, adding that the attackers announced to attack Chhayanaut and Udichi on social media but government failed to prevent them. Jamshed Anwer Tapan said that the government had forgotten its responsibility for the safety of the citizens and was letting mob violence occur across the country. The protest rally consisted of a torch march which began from Topkhana road and travelled from the Baitul Mukarram area to National Press club. Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi also organised a protest rally at the same place on the issue. Earlier, on Thursday night, some unidentified people set fire to the offices of the Prothom Alo, the Daily Star and cultural institute Chhayanaut, while on Friday evening Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi central office in the capital was vandalised and set on fire.

Amjanatar Dal on Sunday received the registration certificate with election symbol of ‘butterfly’ from the Election Commission. Bangladesh interim government foreign secretary Asad Alam Siam on Sunday said diplomatic journalism is playing an important role in strengthening Bangladesh’s foreign policy as three journalists received the DCAB Media Award for outstanding reporting on diplomacy. Online Indian visa application services resumed in Khulna on Sunday morning after remaining suspended since Wednesday afternoon. The police are still in the dark about the current location of Faisal Karim Masud, the alleged shooter in the attack on Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi. A group of Rajshahi University students on Sunday padlocked the offices of the vice-chancellor, pro-vice-chancellors, proctor, registrar and several deans, demanding the resignation of pro-Awami League deans. A man was beaten to death over theft allegations at Konaura village of Kaitola union at Nabinagar upazila in the district in the early hours of Sunday. Two siblings died of suspected food poisoning at Wireless Mor in the capital’s Hatirjheel area on Sunday... The deputy chief of staff of the Bangladesh Armed Forces during the War of Independence, Air Vice Marshal AK Khandker Bir Uttam, was buried at the Shaheen graveyard at the Bangladesh Air Force Base Bashar in the capital Dhaka on Sunday. Three people were killed and one remained missing after a truck and four other vehicles fell into the River Dhaleshwari from a ferry in Baktaboli area in Narayanganj on early Sunday... Bangladesh foreign minister Md Touhid Hossain on Sunday said that ‘normal security’ was not maintained at the Bangladesh mission in India and the high commissioner, who was staying there with his family, felt threatened. Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin has convened a high-level meeting with senior officials from law enforcement and intelligence agencies to assess the country’s overall security situation ahead of the national election and referendum scheduled for February 12, 2026... A case has been filed over recent vandalism and arson attack on the building of cultural organisation Chhayanaut in Dhanmondi area of the capital. Indian Assistant High Commission in Chattogram has suspended its visa services for an indefinite period, citing security concerns... The Election Commission has issued stringent directives to law enforcement and security agencies to ensure a safe and orderly electoral environment, warning that any attempt to disrupt the process would be dealt with firmly. Namaz-e-Janaza of six peacekeepers who were martyred in a barbaric terrorist drone attack on a United Nations peacekeeping mission base in the Abyei area of Sudan on December 13 last was held on Sunday at the Central Mosque of Dhaka Cantonment.

title: Minor boy killed after being hit by truck at Uttara
body: A 10-year-old boy was killed after being hit by a truck in the capital’s Uttara area on Saturday morning. The deceased was Mohammad Suhan. The accident occurred around 6:00am in front of the Uttara House Building area when a speeding truck hit him as he was crossing the road. Critically injured Suhan was taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College and Hospital, where the attending doctors declared him dead around 11:00am. Runa Akhter, the boy’s aunt who took him to the hospital, said that Suhan had come to Dhaka from his village home to visit relatives. ‘A reckless truck hit my nephew while he was crossing the road. He was seriously injured and later died at the hospital,’ she said. Suhan, son of Ranak Hasan, hailed from Polghat village under Bagerhat Sadar. The family of Suhan had been staying in Turag Nayanagar area during the visit, she added. Inspector Mohammad Faruk, in-charge of the DMCH police camp, said that the body had been kept at the Dhaka Medical College morgue for an autopsy. The incident has been reported to the concerned police station for further investigation.

title: Dry weather, fog, stable temperatures forecast
body: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has forecast that most parts of the country will remain generally dry with intervals of partly cloudy skies, while foggy conditions and nearly unchanged temperatures are expected during the next 24 hours beginning at 9:00am on Saturday. According to the BMD bulletin, moderate to thick fog may occur at places over Rangpur, Rajshahi and Khulna divisions, while light to moderate fog is likely elsewhere across the country from midnight to morning. Night temperature may remain nearly unchanged countrywide. Day temperature may fall slightly in Rangpur, Rajshahi and Khulna divisions, but is expected to remain almost steady in other regions. On Friday, Teknaf recorded the highest temperature at 31.5 degrees Celsius, while Sreemangal registered the lowest at 13.0 degrees Celsius.

title: Patuakhali’s Dashmina emerges as livestock hub, boosting local economy
body: Cattle rearing in the vast char areas of Dashmina upazila in Patuakhali have evolved from a supplementary livelihood into a major driver of the local economy, contributing to poverty alleviation and employment generation. Alongside agriculture, thousands of small and marginal farmers in the upazila are becoming self-reliant through cow and buffalo rearing, mostly using their own labour and limited capital, without depending on bank loans. According to the Upazila Livestock Office, more than 5,620 cows and buffaloes are currently being reared at Dashmina. Of these, around 2,500 are in Rangopaldi and Char Borhan unions, 1,300 in Alipura, 1,100 in Betagi-Sankipur, 1,150 in Baharampur, 1,900 in Banshbaria and about 1,950 in Dashmina Sadar. Officials said that nearly 65 per cent of the total cattle population are buffaloes, an unusually high proportion compared to other upazilas. The char environment, with its wetlands and natural grasslands, is particularly suitable for buffalo rearing. A buffalo can produce nearly twice as much milk and one-and-a-half times more meat than a local cow. Estimates suggest that existing buffaloes in Dashmina have the potential to produce around 1.05 million litres of milk and about 7.4 million kilograms of meat annually. Abdus Salam, a farmer from Char Hadi, said that cattle rearing had transformed his family’s livelihood. ‘Earlier, I depended only on paddy cultivation, which was barely enough to survive. Now I have three cows and a buffalo and earn Tk 800 to Tk 1,000 a day from milk sales,’ he said. Women farmers are also benefiting from livestock rearing. Chhakina Begum of Char Banshbaria said that buffalo rearing was profitable as feed costs were low in the char areas. ‘If we receive government support, we can expand our farms and increase our income.’ Duck farming has also gained popularity in the wetland-rich chars. Salma Begum of Char Shahjalal and Md Yunus Hawlader of Char Borhan said that ducks could graze freely after paddy harvests, reducing costs while increasing profits. They added that government assistance could further boost production. The Upazila Agriculture Office has reported that around 25 per cent of Dashmina’s land consists of chars. Of this, nearly 10 per cent remains uncultivated, while about 75 per cent is mono-cropped, leaving large areas unused for at least six months each year. During these periods, livestock rearing has emerged as a vital alternative source of income. Despite the potential, farmers face several challenges. Karim Molla of Char Samad said that sick animals often had to be taken to the mainland for treatment, causing delays and sometimes resulting in losses. ‘Many animals die because veterinary services are not readily available in the chars,’ he said. Experts believe that declaring char areas as planned pastures, introducing improved grass cultivation, ensuring regular vaccination, providing low-interest loans, training farmers and improving marketing facilities can transform Dashmina into a major milk and meat production zone. Dashmina upazila livestock officer Shuvendu Sarkar said, ‘The area has huge potential for cow and buffalo rearing due to its natural pastures and wetlands.’ He stressed the need for regular deworming, vaccination, farmer training and strengthened veterinary services. ‘If a coordinated government initiative is taken, Dashmina’s char pastures could become a major hub for milk and meat production, contributing significantly to poverty reduction, employment generation and national economic growth,’ he said. People of the area expressed hope that combined efforts by the government and private sector would soon turn Dashmina’s neglected char lands into an important livestock-based economic zone.

title: Semi-decomposed body of missing police recovered in Panchagarh
body: The half-decomposed body of a missing police constable, Akhtaruzzaman, 46, a resident of Chaugacha in Jashore, has been recovered from Panchagarh. The police said that the body was found in a sugarcane field at the Nine Mile area of Satmora unionunder Panchagarh Sadar on Thursday. Family members were informed of the recovery on Friday. Akhtaruzzaman had been missing for about 22 days. He was initially identified from police-logo underwear found on the body. Later, the victim’s widow identified him after being shown photographs of the clothes — trousers, shirt and shoes — he was wearing. According to police, local residents informed the authorities after a foul smell spread in the area. The police recovered the body and completed legal formalities. With no immediate identification available, investigators relied on the police-logo underwear as the first clue. Panchagarh Sadar police sub-inspector Belal Hossain, the investigating officer, said that the body had been kept at the police station and would be sent for an autopsy once family members arrived. ‘After which it would be handed over to them.’ Akhtaruzzaman’s brother-in-law Mamunur Rashid Mamun said that the family left for Panchagarh on Friday night after receiving the news. Akhtaruzzaman was serving at Rampal police station in Bagerhat under the Khulna Range (BP 8403024644). Family sources said that he lived with his widow and children in a rented house at Ichhapur under Chaugacha. His widow, Shahina Akhtar Shima, filed a general diary with Chaugacha police on November 30, stating that he had left home on November 27, saying he was going to Maheshpur. He left behind his two mobile phones at home and never returned. Chaugacha police officer-in-charge Rezaul Karim confirmed the recovery of the body.

title: Manikganj sees bumper aman paddy harvest
body: Aman paddy harvesting has been completed with bumper production in all seven upazilas in Manikganj during the current season, officials of the Department of Agricultural Extension said. The DAE set a target to produce 67,858 tonnes of clean rice from 31,761 hectares of land across the district. Of the total output, around 50,283 tonnes were harvested from 13,200 hectares under transplanted aman cultivation, while another 17,575 tonnes were produced from 18,561 hectares under broadcast aman cultivation. Officials said that production from both transplanted and broadcast aman exceeded the fixed targets, bringing satisfaction among local farmers. Farmers expressed happiness over the outcome, saying that aman paddy had become a profitable additional crop. Abdul Matin, 50, a farmer from Jagir village under Manikganj Sadar, said that farmers cultivated aman after harvesting the main boro crop. ‘This extra crop increases our income, and the straw is used as fodder for cattle,’ he added. Deputy director of the Department of Agricultural Extension Shahjahan Siraj said that Aman cultivation was expanding every year as more farmers were showing interest in growing Aman paddy as an additional crop after boro harvest.

title: Worker killed as scaffolding collapses in Agargaon
body: A construction worker was killed after scaffolding collapsed at an under construction building in the Agargaon 300 Feet area of Sher-e-Banglanagar in Dhaka on Saturday. The deceased was Mohammad Abu Musa, 27. The accident occurred around 11:30am while he was working on plastering on the second floor of a multi-storey under construction building. According to his colleague Mohammad Badsha Mia, Musa was critically injured when the scaffolding suddenly gave way. He was rescued and first taken to the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital. As his condition deteriorated, he was later shifted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where the attending doctors declared him dead in the afternoon. Musa hailed from Manikchar village under Godagari in Rajshahi. His father’s name is Mohammad Sadiqul Islam. He had been living in a rented house in Agargaon for work. Inspector-in-charge of the DMCH police camp, Mohammad Faruk, said that the body had been kept at the DMCH morgue and the incident had been reported to the concerned police station for further legal proceedings.

title: 5,29,091 expatriates, govt employees register for postal voting
body: Through the Postal Vote BD app, 5,29,091 voters have so far registered to exercise their franchise in the upcoming 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections and referendum, according to Election Commission on Saturday. Expatriate Bangladeshis from different countries as well as government employees engaged in election duties and those staying outside their respective voter areas have been registering through the app. Of the total registered voters, 4,97,033 are male and 32,056 are female. Of them, 4,62,593 are expatriates, while 66,498 are government employees deployed in election duties and staying outside their voter constituencies. Among expatriates, the highest number of registrations came from Saudi Arabia with 1,32,111 voters, followed by Qatar with 49,663, Oman 36,893, Malaysia 33,981, the United Arab Emirates 26,273, the United States 23,544, Kuwait 18,309, the United Kingdom 18,133, Singapore 17,005, Italy 13,437 and Canada 10,992. Meanwhile, 66,498 voters currently staying in the country have registered under the in-country postal voting category through the app. District-wise, the highest number of registrations was recorded in Cumilla with 54,948 voters, followed by Dhaka with 46,502, Chattogram 45,687, Noakhali 31,773, Sylhet 22,923 and Chandpur 21,428. Besides, constituency-wise, the highest number of registrations was in Feni 3 with 8,550 voters, followed by Chattogram 15 with 7,874, Noakhali 1 with 7,586, Cumilla 10 with 7,380 and Noakhali 3 with 7,091 voters. Salim Ahmad Khan, team leader of the Out of Country Voting System and Implementation project, said that the initiatives would be taken to deliver ballots to expatriates as quickly as possible at this stage. He expressed optimism that the number of registrations through the app would reach between 5,00,000 and 6,00,000 for expatriates, while in-country postal voting should reach at least one million. He said that all challenges, including cyber challenges, were being addressed, adding that the cost of in-country postal voting would be only Tk 22, while the average cost for expatriates would be around Tk 700. The EC has asked persons engaged in election duties to register for postal voting through the app between December 18 and 25. Voters under legal custody have been instructed to register between December 21 and 24. In separate messages, the EC has said that voters must provide correct and complete addresses as per the prevailing rules of the country of residence while registering to receive postal ballots, as ballots cannot be sent without proper addresses. The EC has also directed all officers and employees of the Election Commission secretariat and its field offices who are staying outside their voter areas due to official duties to complete mandatory registration by December 21 for IT-supported in-country postal voting. Government employees staying outside their voter areas can register through the app until December 25. Registration will remain open daily from 8:00am to 8:00pm. On November 18, the chief election commissioner inaugurated the Postal Vote BD app and announced the registration schedule for voters in 148 designated countries for the 13th national elections. Expatriate voters must use the mobile number of the country from where they will cast their vote and download and install the app from Google Play Store or App Store to register.

title: BRAC University, BRAC observe death anniversary of Abed
body: BRAC University and BRAC observed the sixth death anniversary of Fazle Hasan Abed through a programme titled ‘Young Abed: Crossroads of Courage and Conviction’ on the university’s campus in Dhaka on Thursday. At a panel discussion, Asif Saleh, executive director of BRAC, said, ‘Sir Fazle Hasan Abed always carried a hunger within him, a hunger for knowledge. That curiosity stayed with him throughout his life. It made him unique. He was eager to pass it on, to make others more curious. Tamara Hasan Abed, managing director of BRAC Enterprises, said, ‘Sir Fazle Hasan Abed always followed what his heart told him. By following my father’s philosophy, I have also found success in my own life.’ Vice-chancellor Professor Syed Ferhat Anwar said, ‘Abed bhai used to say that we must ask ourselves why we exist. No one else can answer that question for us. Once we find the answer, we discover the meaning of life.’ Tareq Refat Ullah Khan, managing director and CEO of BRAC Bank, said, ‘Abed bhai spoke very little, but when he did, his words were deeply meaningful. He never worked for personal recognition; serving humanity was always the core purpose of his work.’ Researcher Afsan Chowdhury, also an adjunct faculty member at the English department, Paroma Husain, director of BRAC’s Accelerating Impact for Young Women program; senior lecturer Tawhid Anwar, and Rana Tabassum, valedictorian of BRAC University’s 17th Convocation, took part in the discussion. Afsan Chowdhury noted that although Abed bhai was born to an upper-class family and may have needed certain triggers to work for society, the spirit of service was always within him. He added that all human beings carry that spirit too and simply need triggers. Excerpts from ‘Hope Over Fate’, the biography of Fazle Hasan Abed written by Scott MacMillan, were read out by Imran Matin, executive director of the BRAC Institute of Governance and Development (BIGD), and Rubana Ahmed, proctor of BRAC University. Asif Saleh, Tamara Hasan Abed, and Syed Ferhat Anwar presented certificates to six students who reflected on Fazle Hasan Abed’s youth and posted the most compelling prose, poetry, and visual art on social media as a part of a contest marking the anniversary. The programme also featured a short play titled ‘If Abed Bhai Were Here’ performed by members of the BRAC University Drama and Theatre Forum and depicting an imaginary dialogue between a young Abed and the present generation. Recitations and musical performances were presented by students of Monon, BRAC University’s cultural organisation. Lady Syeda Sarwat Abed, founder and adviser of the BRAC Institute of Languages and spouse of Sir Fazle Hasan Abed, also shared her memories. Moutushi Kabir, senior director of People, Culture and Communications at BRAC, and BRAC University student Azwad Mostafiz Ador moderated the event. Founder of both BRAC and BRAC University, Fazle Hasan Abed passed away on December 20, 2019, at the age of 83.

title: Monzur gets Moyurpongkhi Star Award
body: Monzur A Khoda, senior consultant of Popular Diagnostics in Dhaka, received Moyurpongkhi Star Award 2025 recently. Monzur is pioneer interventional and regenerative rheumatologist of Bangladesh, who introduced permanent pain and arthritis cure without surgery and traditional medicine. He received the award at an event at Bangladesh Parjatan Corporation auditorium on Friday, said a press release.

title: BARD holds confce on governance
body: The international conference on integrated research, titled ‘Governance in the Digital Era for Peace and Prosperity’, began at the Bangladesh Academy for Rural Development. The two-day international conference was inaugurated by chief guest Professor ABM Obaidul Islam, vice-chancellor of Bangladesh Open University. The inaugural ceremony was presided over by convener of the conference Professor AKA Firowz Ahmed. He discussed the nature of AI in the current era of globalisation. A total of 240 participants, including professors and researchers from different universities of 12 countries, presented their research papers at the conference. At the inaugural ceremony, BARD director general Saif Uddin Ahmed gave a brief introduction to the organisation and highlighted BARD’s role in rural development. He said that four comprehensive development projects in Bangladesh have been undertaken through BARD. Irrigation management, microfinance, and rural infrastructure development are some of the successful projects implemented by BARD. In his special guest speech, Comilla University vice-chancellor Professor Md Haider Ali emphasised the importance of ensuring good governance in the education sector. Other co-organisers of the conference are Netisearch International, Stamford University, Department of Public Administration, Dhaka University, Rural Poverty Alleviation Foundation, Army Welfare Organisation and international research organisation (GAIN) International. The conference is conducted by Fauzia Nasrin Sultana, director, BARD and the assistant conference director is Md Aminul Islam, assistant director, BARD.

title: Journalist Anis Alamgir sent to jail after 5-day interrogation
body: A Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court on Saturday sent journalist Anis Alamgir to jail after a five-day interrogation in connection with a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Hasan Shahadat issued the order when the police produced Anis Alamgir before the court and sought his detention in jail, said prosecution department sub-inspector Shamim Hossain. In the petition, the police said that ‘crucial information relevant to the case was obtained’ during the interrogation. It added that the information was being verified and it might be necessary to place him on remand again if the information was found true. In view of that, the investigation officer appealed the court to keep him in prison. Earlier, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court on December 15 remanded the senior journalist in police custody for five days for interrogation in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police Detective Branch on December 14 evening took Anis to its office in the capital’s Minto Road for questioning and later he was shown arrested in a case filed with the Uttara (West) police. July Revolutionary Alliance central organiser Aryan Ahmed on December 15 filed the case against the senior journalist, actress Meher Afroz Shaon and two others under the Anti-Terrorism Act over hatching conspiracy to destabilise the country committing anti-state crimes. Two other accused in the case are model Maria Kispotta and Imtu Ratish Imtiaz. According to the case statement, the accused are involved in conspiring to destabilise the country and destroy its infrastructure. The case statement further alleged that followers of fascist Sheikh Hasina were hiding in the country and hatching such conspiracies although she fled the country amid the July uprising in August 2024. The accused are spreading propaganda through various television talk shows and social media posts for the rehabilitation of Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, according to the case statement. Anis Alamgir in recent times expressed critical views on the activities of the Professor Muhammad Yunus-led interim government formed following the ouster of the authoritarian Awami League regime amid the July uprising.

title: Bodies of 3 unnatural death victims recovered in Ctg
body: The Chattogram district police have recovered three bodies, including the body of an old man and a young girl, from different places of the district on Friday and Saturday. District police sources said that Raujan police recovered body of night guard Md Shafi , 65 , from a secluded place near Chara Battal area under the municipality at about 7:00am on Saturday. Shafi was working as a night guard of Chara Battal Bazar and remained missing since Thursday night. Getting information from locals, the police recovered the injury-marked body of Shafi at about 7:00am. On the other hand, Hathazari police recovered the body of Md Ali Akbar, 38, which was hanging from an iron rod at the roof of his rented house at Kamal Para under Fatika union of the upazila on Friday night. Police suspected that Akbar committed suicide by hanging himself with an iron rod at the roof of his home following family feud. Ashrat Jahan, 22, a young girl also committed suicide by hanging herself from a ceiling fan inside her room on Friday morning. She was daughter of Md Jahangir, a NRB and inhabitant of Syed Bari area under Ward 8 of Rangunia municipality. Family members took Ashrat to a local health complex, where doctors confirmed her death. District police said that all three recovered bodies had been sent to CMCH morgue for autopsy and legal process would start after receiving the reports from hospital.

title: Installation of Motijheel  Rotary Club held
body: The 37th installation ceremony of the Rotary Club of Motijheel was held on Friday at the International School Dhaka at Bashundhara in Dhaka. The ceremony was graced by Professor Md Mozmmel Hoque as chief guest, while PDG Istiaque A Zaman, country coordinator, attended the programme as special guest. The event was chaired by Sujit Kumar Bhowmik, event chair. Distinguished Rotarians including Moinul Islam were also present on the occasion. During the ceremony, Enamul Hoque, president of the Rotary Club of Motijheel, delivered a speech highlighting Rotary’s commitment to humanitarian service, ethical leadership, and community development. He emphasised the club’s vision and service priorities for the upcoming Rotary year. The programme was anchored by Iffat Ara. The ceremony was attended by a large gathering of Rotarians from various Rotary Clubs along with their family members, creating a warm and vibrant atmosphere. A cultural programme, performed by the children of Rotarians, added colour to the evening and was appreciated by the audience. The 37th Installation Ceremony concluded successfully, reaffirming the Rotary Club of Motijheel’s dedication to the Rotary ideal of “Service Above Self.”

title: Mymensingh AL leader dies after jumping from house to evade arrest
body: Former organising secretary of Mymensingh Metropolitan Awami League, Kazi Manzur Morshed Raju, died Friday afternoon after sustaining critical injuries while trying to evade arrest by jumping from the second floor of his house. The incident occurred Thursday around 8:00pm when a team from Kotwali police visited Raju’s home looking for him. Sensing the police’s presence, he attempted to escape by jumping from the balcony but struck an adjoining boundary wall, suffering severe head and body injuries. People of the area later found him unconscious and bleeding and informed his family. He was admitted to a hospital at Charpara, where he underwent brain surgery but was pronounced dead at 3:30pm on Friday. Following the killing of Osman Hadi, Mymensingh police launched an operation targeting Awami League leaders and activists, including Raju. Police said that he was not involved in any recent criminal cases and had not been active in politics for the past 8–10 years. Kotwali model police officer-in-charge Nazmus Sakib said that police regularly conduct arrest operations. He added that the police team left the scene after Raju did not open the gate, and they were unaware of what occurred afterward. Raju’s wife, Sathi, said that he had been living a normal life since August 5 and had no pending legal cases.

title: Jamaat amir condemns attacks on media
body: Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami amir Shafiqur Rahman on Friday condemned the attacks on Bangla daily Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, and New Age editor Nurul Kabir, a day after leaders of Islami Chhatra Shibir called for the closure of the two dailies and urged ransacking of cultural organisations, including Chhayanaut and Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigoshthi. In a post on his verified Facebook page Jamaat amir said that while the nation was united in demanding justice for the killing of Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi, several distressing incidents had taken place across the country, which he described as concerning. A free and independent media is a prerequisite for state stability, said Shafiqur stressing that ensuring the freedom and safety of the media was a collective responsibility. ‘We do not want to return to a culture where the media were subjected to blatant attacks, as seen during the fascist era,’ he said, urging the media outlets to act responsibly during the current crisis and to refrain from any form of hate-driven reporting. Shafiqur also said that vandalism and arson at several cultural centres, including high commission offices, were unacceptable under any circumstances. All mainstream Islamist parties and organisations in the country, he commented, believe in lawful processes and do not support vigilantism under any circumstances. The Jamaat amir said that his party believed that such incidents might have been carried out deliberately by certain quarters as part of a planned sabotage attempt. Meanwhile, Rajshahi University Central Students’ Union vice-president and Chhatra Shibir president, Mostakur Rahman, on Thursday night announced that Prothom Alo and The Daily Star must be shut down. He made this announcement during a protest march and a subsequent rally immediately after the news of the death of Osman Hadi spread. Shortly before Mostakur’s threat, the Prothom Alo office in Dhaka was attacked, looted, and set afire, after which a group of assailants also vadalised the Daily Star office and set fire to the building. On the other hand, Chhatra Shibir Jahangirnagar University unit secretary general Mosatfizur Rahman on Thursday night called for ransacking cultural groups Chhayanaut, Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigoshthi, and the leftist groups. He made the remarks while addressing a rally at the university’s central shaheed minar in protest of the killing of Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi. Hours after Mostafizur’s announcement, a group of assailants stormed the Chhayanaut premises, vandalising the building and setting parts of it on fire. On Friday evening, an arson attack was also carried out at the office of Udichi Shilpigoshthi in Dhaka.
