title: Journalist shot dead, another injured in Khulna
body: A journalist was shot dead and another man injured when armed assailants opened fire at a tea stall in the Sholua Bazar area under Aranghata in Khulna on Thursday night. The deceased was identified as Emdadul Haque Milon, 45, who worked for an online news portal and also served as general secretary of the Sholua Bazar Development Committee. The injured, Debashish Biswas, 30, is a local veterinary doctor. The incident occurred around 10:00pm at a tea shop in the market. Milon was shot in the head and died on the spot, while Debashish sustained a gunshot wound to the head and was taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital, where his condition was reported to be critical. Witnesses said that four assailants arrived at the tea stall on two motorcycles and fired several blank shots, causing panic among people in the area. As people of the area fled, two of the attackers entered the tea shop and shot Milon at point-blank range. They then shot Debashish before fleeing the scene. Khulna Metropolitan Police’s assistant commissioner, media, TMR Roknuzzaman said that two people were shot in the incident, one of whom died, while the other remained under treatment. Additional deputy commissioner, north, of Khulna Metropolitan Police, Amit Kumar Barman, said that police were investigating the motive behind the killing. ‘We have learned that Milon was a journalist and a local organisation leader. The cause of the attack is yet to be determined,’ he said. The police said that efforts were underway to identify and arrest those responsible.

title: Electoral code ignored as posters cover walls
body: Posters of contestants for the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections are being pasted on walls and pillars across the country in violation of the Election Commission code of conduct for political parties and candidates. Ahead of the JS elections scheduled for February 12, 2026, the Election Commission on November 10 issued the code of conduct in accordance with the Representation of the People Order, 1972. The code of conduct prohibits the pasting of posters and the use of other campaign materials made of non-biodegradable substances. It was expected that the pasting of election campaign posters by political parties, contestants, and their supporters would stop after the announcement of the election schedule on December 13. However, violations of the code have continued since then. National Citizen Party contestant for the Dhaka-9 constituency Tasnim Jara said on Thursday that the Election Commission had failed to stop her competitors from pasting colourful posters across the Khilgaon, Goran, Sabujbagh, and Mugda areas. On her verified Facebook page, she wrote that contestants complying with the code were being sidelined while violators were becoming more prominent by displaying their presence everywhere. Communist Party of Bangladesh’s candidate for the Dhaka-12 constituency Kallol Banik said, ‘Voters are seeing only the faces of candidates from the two major parties because their posters are still pasted on walls, while those of us following the code of conduct are not being seen at all. This is discrimination.’ The Election Commission issued the code of conduct for political parties and election contestants following recommendations from the Electoral Reform Commission, which was formed on October 3 past year after the fall of the Awami League regime. The rationale for the recommendation is that the indiscriminate display of election campaign materials such as non-biodegradable posters, festoons, and banners pollute the environment. According to the polls code, any election contestant or supporter who pastes posters is liable to be punished with a maximum of six-month imprisonment or a fine of Tk150,000, or both. Any registered political party contravening the code would also face a fine of Tk1,50,000. Until Friday, neither any election contestant nor any supporter violating the code were punished by the Election Commission. Badiul Alam Majumder, former chief of the Electoral Reform Commission, told New Age on the day that he did not see the Election Commission being strict in enforcing the code of conduct among contestants and political parties. ‘Action should be taken against those who are violating the code. Otherwise, no one will respect the Election Commission,’ Badiul warned. Indiscriminate poster pasting also violates the Graffiti Writing and Poster Sticking (Control) Act, 2012. According to the law, individuals who paste posters on undesignated walls are offenders and are liable to be punished with a fine of Tk5,000 to Tk10,000 or up to 15-day imprisonment while they may also be ordered to remove the posters at their own expense. Speaking on the issue, Election Commission senior secretary Akhtar Ahmed regretted that poster pasting had continued despite being discouraged during the commission’s dialogue with political parties. ‘Returning officers have already been instructed to remove the election posters,’ Akhtar said, adding that he would personally meet officials of the Dhaka city corporations today to expedite the removal of posters, festoons, and banners.

title: 4,50,000 expats registered to vote in JS elections
body: More than 4,50,000 expatriate Bangladeshi voters from different countries across the world registered through a mobile app, Postal Vote Bd, in the past one month to vote in the upcoming national election and the referendum, scheduled to be held simultaneously on February 12, 2026. The Election Commission on November 19 opened the ‘Postal Vote Bd’ app for the expatriates to complete the registration process by December 25 next. Though the postal balloting system has been in the laws for a long time, it was never practiced in the previous elections. This is the first time the Election Commission has introduced an effective IT-supported hybrid postal balloting system, enabling expatriates, government staff who are posted outside their respective constituencies, polling personnel and the persons who will be in the legal custody to exercise their franchise through a combination of digital registration and manual voting. Alongside the expatriates, more than 61,000 voters from inside Bangladesh have also registered to vote through the postal ballots in the 13th parliamentary election. As of 6:30pm on Friday, 4,50,226 expatriates, including 28,765 females, registered through the app from 122 foreign countries throughout the world. Among the registrants, the highest number came from the Saudi Arabia, 1,27,844, followed by Qatar 47,263,Oman 34,439, Malaysia 33,379, UAE 26,123, US 23,389, UK 17,835, Kuwait 17,813, Singapore 16,980, Italy 13,269, Canada 10,939, South Korea 9,912, Australia 8,778, Bahrain 7,611, Japan 7,308, Maldives 6,294, South Africa 5,081 and Portugal 5,033. The registration process for In-Country Postal Voting started after the recent announcement of the election schedule. As of Friday evening, 61,511 voters from inside Bangladesh registered to vote through the postal ballots. With them, a total of 511,737 persons registered through the Postal Vote Bd app. Among the registered ones, the highest 53,308 will vote in Cumilla district, while 45,532 in Dhaka district, 44,271 in Chattogram, 30,859 in Noakhali, 22,389 in Sylhet, 20,652 in Chandpur, 19,673 in Feni, 17,185 in Brahmanbaria, 16,300 in Lakshmipur and 12,258 in Cox’s Bazar. In terms of parliamentary seats, the highest 8,269 registered ones will vote in Feni-3 constituency, while 7,670 in Chattogram-15 constituency, 7,411 in Noakhali-1 constituency, 7,157 in Cumilla-10 constituency, 6,869 in Noakhali-3 constituency. There are some 12.76 crore voters under 42,761 polling stations in the country’s 300 constituencies. Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin on December 11 announced the schedule to arrange the 13th parliamentary election and the referendum on the July National Charter (Constitutional Reform) Implementation Order simultaneously on February 12 next. According to the election schedule, the deadline for the submission of nomination paper is December 29, while the last date for the withdrawal of candidature is January 20. The election campaign will start on January 22 and continue till 48 hours before the balloting period (7:30am on February 10).

title: Grandi welcomes Barham Salih as newly elected UNHCR chief
body: UN High Commissioner for Refugees Filippo Grandi on Friday welcomed former Iraqi president Barham Salih for being elected as the head of the UN refugee agency. Salih was elected by the UN general assembly in New York through a competitive selection process involving candidates from several countries. He will assume office on January 1, 2026, with Geneva as his duty station. Grandi said Salih has been engaged in high-level public service for more than three decades and possesses resolute leadership qualities and thoughtful diplomatic judgment. ‘He comes from a country that has experienced conflict, persecution and displacement in recent years, which gives him a direct understanding of the challenges facing refugees today,’ Grandi said. He added that Salih’s experience and background make him well suited to lead UNHCR at a time when global displacement has reached unprecedented levels. Grandi’s 10-year tenure as UN High Commissioner for Refugees will end on December 31. He took office in January 2016 and has since led the agency through major global displacement crises, including those in Syria, Ukraine and Sudan. Despite significant cuts to humanitarian funding this year, UNHCR continues to operate in 128 countries worldwide. Earlier this month, UNHCR marked 75 years of service dedicated to the protection of forcibly displaced people across the globe.

title: Cyber Security Agency cell working to prevent fake information
body: A special cell formed under the National Cyber Security Agency to prevent fake information, misleading contents and rumours until the next national elections has been working round-the-clock to monitor online and social media, verify information and ensure authenticity. To this end, the NCSA is working in coordination with the chief adviser’s press wing, Press Institute Bangladesh, Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha, Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission and law enforcement agencies, an official release said. Before sharing any information or content on social media, the people are requested to verify its sources and immediately inform the NCSA if they find suspicious, provocative or anti-national contents. It is the responsibility of all to keep the country’s cyberspace safe. The NCSA has requested all to refrain from spreading false or misleading information, photo cards and videos and to make others aware of the trap of anti-state quarters. The NCSA has a 24/7 helpline service for the public to quickly help prevent cybercrime. The following e-mail addresses are available for receiving various complaints from citizens: [email protected], for all complaints or official communication related to rumours, misinformation/disinformation, rumours at the national, personal or institutional level. [email protected] is for all complaints or official communication related to harassment or fraud of individuals or organisations through fake profiles, photos, audio-video, obscene or harmful content, etc. [email protected] is for all complaints or official communication related to cyber attacks on critical information infrastructure-CII entities. [email protected] is for all official communications or complaints and [email protected] is for all complaints or official communications related to online gambling. The NCSA sought cooperation from all so that they can together play a role in using the country’s digital space safely and responsibly, the release said.

title: Man electrocuted to death in Gaibandha
body: A man died from electrocution while painting iron rods on the rooftop of a house at College Para in Gaibandha on Thursday afternoon. The deceased was Rakib Miah, son of Mahabub Hossain, a resident of Purba Komornoi area under sadar upazila of the district. The police said that Rakib, along with several other paint labourers, was painting iron rods at the house of Sohel Rana at College Para. At one stage, Rakib climbed onto the rooftop to continue painting and came into contact with a live electric wire and got electrocuted immediately. He died on the spot. On information, members of the Fire Service and Civil Defence rushed to the spot and recovered the body. Officer-in-charge of Gaibandha Sadar police station Shahinur Islam Talukdar said that as there was no complaint from the victim’s family, the body was handed over to his relatives.

title: Drone banned near airports until Feb 15
body: The Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh on Thursday imposed a temporary ban on all drone operations in and around airport areas, flight routes and take-off and landing zones to ensure aviation safety. The restriction will remain in force from December 18 to February 15, 2026, covering airport-adjacent areas, aircraft movement routes, training zones, and designated take-off and landing sites, according to an official notice issued by the CAAB. The CAAB said that unauthorised drone operations posed a serious threat to the safety and security of aircraft and violate the Drone Registration and Operation Policy, 2020. In cases of special necessity, drone operators must first obtain clearance from the concerned district administration and then apply to the CAAB for approval. The authority will take a final decision after reviewing the application. The CAAB has urged the public to strictly refrain from flying drones without prior permission, warning that legal action will be taken against any unauthorized drone operations.

title: Dry spell to continue across Bangladesh
body: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department forecast that most parts of the country will experience generally dry weather with intervals of partly cloudy skies during the next 24 hours, starting from 9:00am on Friday. ‘Weather may remain dry with temporary partly cloudy sky over the country,’ it said. The BMD bulletin noted that light to moderate fog may occur at places over northwestern part and light fog may occur at places elsewhere over the country during early morning. Besides, night temperatures may rise slightly over Southern part and may remain nearly unchanged elsewhere over the country, it said. It also added that day temperatures may fall slightly over northwestern part and may remain nearly unchanged elsewhere over the country. On Thursday, Feni recorded the highest temperature at 31.5 degrees Celsius, while Tetulia registered the lowest at 9.8 degrees Celsius.ax

title: 2 cops among 4 hurt in clash outside Indian assistant HC in Ctg
body: At least four people, including two police members, were injured in a clash between the protesters and the police outside the Indian assistant high commission in Chattogram following the death of Sharif Osman bin Hadi, spokesperson of Inqilab Mancha. The protesters gathered outside the mission’s office in the city’s Khulshi area and pelted bricks and vandalised the office premises around 1:00am, said the police. When police intervened, a chase and counter-chase ensued between law enforcers and the protesters, said the Chattogram Metropolitan Police commissioner Hasib Aziz. The injured were admitted to Chittagong Medical College Hospital, he said. The police detained 12 people from the spot and they would be shown arrested under the Anti-Terrorism Act, the CMP commissioner added. Meanwhile, a section of the protesters remained in front of Khulshi police station until late at night demanding the release of the detainees. Earlier, students and activists under the banner of Inqilab Mancha staged a protest rally at Soloshahar No. 2 Gate, demanding punishment for those involved in Hadi’s killing. Officer-in-charge of Panchlaish police Md Solaiman said that around 200 protesters gathered in Soloshahar and No 2 Gate areas to protest the killing of Osman Hadi. They later marched toward Mayor Goli and set a motorcycle on fire at the house of former education minister and Awami League leader Mohibul Hasan Chowdhury Naufel, he said.

title: BNP leaders inspect venue for Tarique Rahman’s reception
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party is making extensive preparations to welcome party’s acting chairman Tarique Rahman upon his return to the country after nearly 18 year. The reception is scheduled to take place in the 300-feet area of the city. To oversee the arrangements, top BNP leaders on Friday visited and inspected the proposed venue. Several members of the party’s standing committee, including, Mirza Abbas, Gayeshwar Chandra Roy, and Salahuddin Ahmed, visited the site. They were accompanied by various levels of party leaders and activists during the inspection. According to BNP, Tarique Rahman is set to return to Bangladesh on December 25. He is expected to arrive in Dhaka at 11:55am that day via a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight.

title: Envoy thanks Malaysian employers for trust in Bangladeshi manpower
body: Bangladesh high commissioner to Malaysia Manjurul Karim Khan Chowdhury on Friday thanked Malaysian employers for placing continued confidence in Bangladeshi manpower, highlighting expatriate workers’ vital contribution to Malaysia’s economy and Bangladesh’s development. He made the remark when the Bangladesh high commission in Kuala Lumpur observed International Migrants Day and National Expatriates Day 2025 under the theme ‘going abroad with skills, building the homeland with remittances’, according to a message. The programme included reading out messages from the chief adviser, the foreign adviser and the adviser for Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, followed by the screening of a documentary produced to mark the day. To recognise expatriates’ contributions and encourage their greater engagement in national development, the high commission organised a discussion meeting, documentary screening, awards ceremony for expatriate Bangladeshis, a cultural programme and a raffle draw at the G Tower hall in Kuala Lumpur. Presiding over the event, the high commissioner Chowdhury expressed gratitude to expatriate Bangladeshis for strengthening the national economy through remittances and skills. The high commissioner also said that effective arrangements have been made under initiatives of the interim government to enable expatriates to exercise their voting rights in the upcoming national parliamentary election. He urged Bangladeshis living in Malaysia to participate through postal ballots and called upon expatriate professional, social and political organisations to assist in voter registration. Speakers at the programme included Heba Abdel Latif, chief of mission of the International Organizstion for Migration Malaysia; Hariri bin Harun, head of the Foreign Workers Unit of Malaysia’s Social Security Organisation; Dato’ Nathan K Suppi, vice-president of the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers; Dato’ Rafiq, CEO of the Construction Labour Exchange Malaysia; Saidur Rahman Farazi, chief executive officer of CBL Money Transfer Malaysia; and Rakibul Hasan, representing expatriate workers. The speakers praised Bangladeshi workers for their professionalism and dedication, noting their significant contribution to Malaysia’s economic growth. They also said that the Malaysian government, employers and relevant institutions were working closely with the Bangladesh high commission to ensure workers’ protection and welfare. Marking the occasion, the High Commission honoured 23 individuals and institutions from different categories among expatriates living in Malaysia with commemorative crests and certificates. Representatives of Malaysian migration-related departments, senior officials of recruiting organisations, diplomats from various embassies, expatriate Bangladeshis, professionals, academics, workers, community leaders, Malaysian nationals, Bangladeshi students studying in Malaysian universities, expatriate journalists and officials of the Bangladesh high commission attended the event.

title: Manufacturing works of 20 KSY projects in full swing
body: Khulna Shipyard Limited operated under the guidance of the Bangladesh Navy, is currently implementing 20 shipbuilding projects simultaneously, including the construction of Landing Craft Tanks and various other vessels for different government organisations. Once considered a loss-making entity, Khulna Shipyard has been transformed into a profitable and internationally recognised shipbuilding facility since it was handed over to the Bangladesh Navy in 1999. According to shipyard officials, Khulna Shipyard has constructed more than 800 ships, vessels, tankers, dredgers and warships over the past decades. Officials said manufacturing works of all 20 ongoing projects are progressing at full pace. Among them, three Landing Craft Tanks are under construction, each measuring 74.5 metres in length, 13 metres in width and weighing 1,505 tonnes. These LCTs are scheduled to be handed over to the Bangladesh Navy on March 30, April 30 and May 30 in 2026 respectively. In addition, one search and rescue vessel will be delivered to the Mongla Port Authority on March 31, 2026. Two bollard pull tugboats are being built for the Payra Port Authority, which will be handed over in June and December of 2026 respectively. One survey vessel and one pilot vessel are also scheduled for delivery to the Payra Port Authority by February next year. For the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority, four 24-inch cutter suction dredgers and four crane boats are expected to be handed over by June 30, while four glass reinforced plastic (GRP) catamaran boats will be delivered to the Bangladesh Water Development Board by June 30, 2026. Talking to BSS, Captain A F M Enamul Hasan, General Manager, Design and Production of KSY, said that Bangladesh is now capable of constructing international-quality, cost-effective medium warships domestically. Alongside warships, vessels of various sizes and categories are also being manufactured locally, he added. He said that several large ships built to international standards have already been completed at the shipyard, significantly reducing dependence on imports. Terming shipbuilding a major source of foreign currency earnings, Hasan said KSY earned around Tk 800 crore during the 2024-25 fiscal year. Recently, Khulna Shipyard completed the construction of four warships under the guidance of the Bangladesh Navy, named Shaheed Daulat, Shaheed Farid, Shaheed Mohibullah and Shaheed Akhtar Uddin. Equipped with essential war equipment, including boat guns, large depth chargers, rocket depth chargers, solar panels and other advanced systems, the vessels are primarily designed for transporting war materials. A senior Navy official said such vessels were previously imported at high costs, but they are now being built locally at significantly lower expenses. He noted that around 30 years ago a warship of similar category cost approximately Tk 34 crore to import, whereas it can now be constructed domestically for about Tk 17 crore, marking a substantial reduction in expenditure. Contacted, Commodore Md Shahidulla Al Faruk, Managing Director of Khulna Shipyard Limited, said that the shipyard had earlier built four warships during 2012-2013 and is now capable of meeting both domestic and potential foreign demand for medium-category warships. He said KSY can currently build a wide range of vessels including ships, LCTs, patrol craft, dredgers and other specialised vessels, making imports largely unnecessary. With the support of recently formulated government policies, the shipyard is also planning to build more sophisticated warships with assistance from classified societies.

title: Mirza Fakhrul collects nomination form for Thakurgaon 1
body: Secretary general of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has collected the nomination form for the Thakurgaon 1 constituency for the upcoming 13th national parliamentary elections. On Thursday afternoon, Nur-e-Shahadat Swajan, former vice-president of Thakurgaon district BNP, collected the form from the office of the district election commission. District election officer Md Waliullah confirmed that the nomination form was collected on behalf of Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Thursday. Noor-e-Shahadat Swajan said, ‘We have collected nomination form following the instruction of the Secretary General. He has been working tirelessly for the party for a long time. I believe that the voters of Thakurgaon-1 constituency have confidence in him.’ Earlier, Mirza Fakhrul announced the party’s candidates for 237 seats in the 13th national parliament elections on November 3. In the list of party candidates, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir’s name was announced for Thakurgaon 1 constituency as the BNP candidate.

title: Youth held over controversial FB post on Hadi’s death
body: The police have detained a young man in Brahmanbaria on Friday afternoon for allegedly making controversial and provocative posts and comments on Facebook following the death of gunshot injured Sharif Osman Hadi, the convener of Inquilab Mancha. The detainee was Yasin Bhuiyan, 34, of Maijkhar village at Kasba upazila. According to the police and local people, Yasin posted ‘Alhamdulillah’ on Facebook in reference to Hadi’s death and made comments labelling him a ‘terrorist’. The posts and comments sparked widespread anger among local students and residents at Kasba. Tensions rose briefly in the area as news of the social media post spread, prompting swift action by law enforcement to prevent any untoward situation. Kasba police station officer-in-charge Najnin Sultana told journalists that locals informed the police after detaining a person for making provocative and offensive posts and comments about Hadi on social media. On information, police went to the spot and detained him, said the official, adding that legal action against the detainee was under way.

title: 2 teens riding motorbike die after being chased by police
body: Two teens met a tragic end as their motorcycle crashed into a truck from behind after being chased by the police in Chapainawabganj Sadar on Friday afternoon. The deceased were identified as Rifat Ali, 18, son of Shah Alam, and Sohag Ahmed, 19, son of Ashraful Islam, of Azaipur-Pochapukur and Chandlai-Jorbagan areas respectively of the district town. According to witnesses, patrolling police signalled the motorcycle to stop at the Mor on the Chapainawabganj-Shibganj road on Friday afternoon. Ignoring the signal, they tried to speed away but the bike lost control and hit the truck from the behind, leaving Rifat dead on the spot and Sohag critically injured. Locals initially took Sohag to Chapainawabganj General Hospital but he succumbed to his injuries on way to Rajshahi. Sohag’s father Ashraful Islam alleged that the duo was hit by the truck and thrown onto the road when police chased them, leading to the fatality. Enraged by this, locals blockaded the road at the Mor with one of the bodies, disrupting the traffic movement. The agitators carried out vandalism at a police box at Bishwaroad Mor and damaged furniture by setting fire on those after dragging out. Besides, the angry people vandalised a police outpost in the nearby Shantibagh area and set fire to a motorcycle there. Though police tried to bring the situation under control, the mob chased them, triggering tension in the area. The road blockade continued until 7:30pm while normalcy returned after Army personnel had arrived at the scene. Additional superintendent of police NM Wasim Firoz said, ‘Situation is under control now. The bodies of the deceased have been handed over to the families.’ He said that action would be taken if police members were found guilty of performing duty.

title: Decomposed body of missing timber trader recovered in Gazipur
body: Partially decomposed body of a timber trader who had gone missing nearly three months ago was recovered at Sreepur in Gazipur on Friday. The deceased was identified as Asaduzzaman Sarker Asad, 50. According to the police, locals first saw the body in an abandoned tin house under the old bridge over the Paruli River on the Kapasia-Rajendrapur road while they were allegedly chasing a fleeing thief. On information, the police recovered the body from the house. Sreepur police station inspector, operations, Sanjoy Saha said that the victim’s son Jony Sarker and daughter Sanjida Akter identified the body by the deceased’s clothing. Jony said that his father went missing on September 23 and a general diary was filed with Sreepur police on September 25 after a failed extensive search. The family suspected that unidentified criminals killed him and dumped the body there. Police sent the body to Gazipur Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital morgue for autopsy and the law enforcers were investigating the incident, said the police personnel.

title: Exams at public univs, recruitment tests postposed
body: Different public universities, government and other organisations have postponed Friday and today’s examinations and recruitment tests amid the countrywide protests over the death of political leader Sharif Osman Hadi. Osman Hadi, the convener of the Inquilab Mancha and one of the organisers of the July mass uprising, died on December 18 night while undergoing treatment in Singapore after being shot in the head on December 12 in the capital Dhaka. Demanding justice, protests erupted across the country following Hadi’s death, blocking roads and highways. The interim government also announced national mourning for Saturday. Against these circumstances, different examinations and recruitment tests were postponed on Friday. The National University authorities postponed examinations scheduled for Friday and today due to unavoidable reasons. Two separate circulars issued by the university on Friday morning also said that the new dates for the exams would be announced later. The first semester exam (2024) of the Master’s of Applied Criminology and Police Management was scheduled to be held at 3:00pm on Friday. Today the first phase of the LLB exam (2024) was scheduled to be held. The University Grants Commission of Bangladesh postponed Friday’s recruitment examination for the post of assistant director/assistant secretary of the commission due to unavoidable reasons. A press release issued by the commission same day morning also said that the new date for the exam would be announced later. The Bangladesh Bank has postponed written and viva examinations scheduled to be held on Friday and today for recruitment to the posts of senior officer and officer under the Bankers Selection Committee due to unavoidable reasons. The decision was confirmed in two separate notices published on the central bank’s verified official Facebook page on Friday. The notices also said that the new dates for the exams would be announced later. On Friday, the written examination for recruitment to the position of senior officer was scheduled to be held. Today the viva for recruitment to the position of officer-rural credit was scheduled to be held. The Dhaka University authorities have postponed today’s admission test for the first-year undergraduate programme of the Science Unit for the 2025-2026 academic year examinations as a mark of respect for the July martyrs. A press release, issued by the university on Friday, also said that the new date for the exams would be announced later. The Bangladesh Open University authorities have postponed today’s all scheduled examinations as part of the state mourning for the death of Sharif Osman Hadi. A press release, issued by the university on Friday, also said that the new date for the exams would be announced later. The posts, telecommunications and information technology ministry has postponed today’s recruitment test due to unavoidable reasons. An urgent press release, issued by the ministry on Friday, also said that the new date of the test would be announced soon on the official web site of the Posts and Telecommunications Division and through SMS to candidates’ mobile phones. Today’s written recruitment tests against vacant posts at the National Academy for Computer Training and Research in Bogura under the Technical and Madrassah Education Division of the education ministry have also been postponed. The new date of the tests will be announced later, said a circular issued by the division on Friday. The authorities of State University of Bangladesh on Friday have postponed its 7th convocation ceremony following the declaration of one-day national mourning today. The convocation will be held tomorrow, a release issued by the university said.

title: 2 Bangladeshis shot dead by Indians in Sylhet border
body: Indian nationals shot two Bangladeshi youths to death at Companiganj border in Sylhet on Friday noon. The deceased Moshahid Miah, 22, is son of Abdur Rab Miah of Purba Turang village at Uttar Ranikhai union under the Companiganj upazila, and Ashikur Rahman, 19, is son of Burhan Uddin of the Baram Siddhipur village at the same union, the police said. Local union parishad member Delwar Hossain told New Age that a group of five youths entered the Indian territory through the Damdama border point to bring firewood from Parihati, a forest area along the border. He said that after the youths started collecting firewood from the Parihati area, Indian Khasia tribesmen opened fire on them without any provocation, leaving Moshahid and Ashikur dead on the spot. ‘Being informed, relatives of the victims rushed to the spot and brought the bodies back to the country in the afternoon,’ he said. Border Guard Bangladesh’s 48 Battalion commander Lieutenant Colonel Md Nazmul Haque confirmed the killing incident of Moshahid and Ashikur. He said that he had contacted to his Indian counterpart in the afternoon after receiving the news in this regard. ‘The Border Security Force officer concerned told me that they were not aware about the killing of the two Bangladeshi youths. The BSF officer said that they would try to identify the killers and reason behind the killings,’ the BGB officer said. He also said in the evening that the process to send a formal protest letter in this regard to the BSF authorities was under way. Companiganj police station officer-in-charge Shafiqur Rahman told New Age in the evening that spot examination reports of the bodies had already been completed. ‘Preparations are going on to hand over the bodies to Sylhet Osmani Medical College Hospital for post-mortem examinations,’ he said. At least 28 Bangladeshis were killed in border violence by the India’s Border Security Force and Indian citizens between January and November this year, according to data by Ain o Salish Kendra, a rights organisation.

title: Two-thirds of highways, district roads not standard: govt report
body: About two-thirds of the national and regional highways and zila (district) roads in the country are non-standard, according to a government report. The report said that more than one-third of the country’s national and regional highways were non-standard. All national and regional highways and zila roads fall under the jurisdiction of the roads and highways department. The department, under the road transport and bridges ministry, recently prepared the report — the baseline assessment and strategic road map for the formulation of the National Integrated Multi-modal Transport Master Plan. As per the assessment, of the national and regional highways, 2.87 per cent is of single lane (non-standard), 32.43 per cent two lanes (non-standard), 53.87 per cent two lanes (standard), 10.42 per cent four lanes (standard), 0.19 per cent six lanes (standard) and 0.18 per cent 10 lanes or above (standard). In the case of zila roads, 32.79 per cent is of single lane (non-standard), 60.82 per cent two lanes (non-standard), 6.33 per cent two lanes (standard) and 0.048 per cent four lanes (standard). Road safety experts said that the authorities should determine the standard of the roads by level of services with high speed instead of increasing the lanes. According to Syed Moinul Hasan, chief engineer of the department, a single-lane highway has the width of 3.65 metres or 12 feet and a single vehicle can run using it comfortably. ‘Two vehicles can use a single-lane highway with difficulty,’ he said, adding, ‘we do not tell these roads one-way as there is no restriction on using these on two ways.’ The standard two-lane highways have the width of 7.3 metres while the non-standard two-lane highways have lower width like 5.5 metres or 6.8 metres, Moinul said. At some portions of the highways in Banani and Uttara areas in the capital Dhaka and Narayanganj and Kanchpur areas are of eight- or 10-lane, he added. Following the initiative of formulating the master plan, the department on December 14 organised a stakeholder seminar on the proposed master plan at its headquarters, Sarak Bhaban, in the capital. As per the report on the baseline assessment and strategic road map for the proposed plan, the department currently has a 22,719.3 kilometres of road network, including 4,292.92km national highways, 5,039km regional highways and 13,386.99km zila roads. Out of the national highways, 30.57 kilometres are of single-lane, 551.32km two-lane (non-standard), 2,833.53km two-lane (standard), 849.11km four-lane, 10.49km six-lane, 17.35km eight-lane and 0.55km 10-lane or above. In the case of regional highways, 237.68 kilometres are of single-lane, 2,475.35km two-lane (non-standard), 2,194.64km two-lane (standard), 124.23km four-lane and 7.5km six-lane. Out of the zila roads, 4,389.85 kilometres are of single-lane, 8,143.2km two-lane (non-standard), 847.41km two-lane (standard) and 6.53km four-lane. Professor Md Shamsul Hoque, who teaches civil engineering at the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, said that a highway’s standard should be measured by the level of services instead of the number of lanes. Shamsul, also director of the Accident Research Institute under the BUET, mentioned that usually the level of services was measured in five categories — ‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’, ‘D’ and ‘E’. ‘In Bangladesh, only the Dhaka-Mawa Expressway provides the ‘A’ category services while the Dhaka-Chattogram national highway provides the ‘D’ category services,’ he said. Though the Dhaka-Chattogram highway has four lanes, it has failed to reduce traffic congestion, he added. Syed Moinul Hasan said that expansion of the non-standard highways would require a huge amount of cost. ‘That is why we are emphasising increasing the shares of passenger and cargo on railways and waterways by developing multi-modal transport hubs across the country,’ he added. The road transport and bridges ministry plans to develop 42 multi-modal transport hubs across the country. As per the RHD report, currently roads have passenger share of 88 per cent, followed by railways 8 per cent and waterways 4 per cent in the country. Regarding cargoes, the share of roads is 76 per cent, that of waterways 14 per cent and that of railways 10 per cent.

title: CPJ, MFC condemn attacks on media outlets
body: The Committee to Protect Journalists and the Media Freedom Coalition in separate statements on Friday strongly condemned the attacks on the offices of The Daily Star and the Prothom Alo on December 18 night. Three United States’ Jefferson fellows in a joint statement on Friday strongly protested and condemned the attacks on the Bangladesh’s two prominent newspaper offices and New Age editor Nurul Kabir, by a group of hoodlums. In a statement, the CPJ said that it was alarmed by reports that crowds vandalised and set fire to the offices of the two leading newspapers, trapping journalists inside the buildings before they could be rescued. The CPJ Asia programme said that it was closely monitoring the situation and urged the Bangladeshi authorities to ensure the safety of media houses and journalists and to hold those responsible for the violence accountable. On December 18 night, a violent mob attacked the media outlets at Karwan Bazar in the capital Dhaka following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener and one of the July uprising organisers, Sharif Osman Hadi, who was shot in the head in the capital on December 12 and died at a hospital in Singapore while he was undergoing treatment there. The CPJ advised journalists to prepare communication plans, equipment and transportation in advance of assignments to minimise risks, and to research the groups involved in protests. It also cautioned reporters to consider the possibility of tear gas, violence or detention. The Media Freedom Coalition, a global partnership of 51 countries dedicated to promoting media freedom and protecting journalists worldwide, said that it strongly condemned the attacks carried out on December 18 night against journalists, editors and media houses. ‘Such acts of violence and intimidation are unacceptable and strike at the heart of press freedom and the public’s right to be informed,’ the MFC said in a statement, calling for swift, impartial investigations to ensure those responsible are brought to justice. ‘Journalists must be able to carry out their work without fear,’ it added, noting that protecting media professionals was essential to upholding the rule of law, democratic values and an open, informed society. The US Jefferson fellows in the statement also protested at vandalism across the country and demanded immediate nabbing of the killers of Osman Hadi and restoring the country’s law and order situation immediately. Signatories to the statement included senior journalists and Jefferson fellows Shahed Siddique, Azizur Rahman and Faisal Mahmud.

title: Govt urges citizens to resist mob violence
body: Bangladesh interim government on Friday urged all citizens of Bangladesh to resist ‘all forms of mob violence committed by a few fringe elements’. ‘We strongly and unequivocally condemn all acts of violence, intimidation, arson and destruction of properties,’ said a statement issued by the interim government chief adviser’s press wing. The statement came amid widespread condemnations on arson attacks on media outlets the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star and a mob attack on Editors’ Council president and New Age editor Nurul Kabir who attempted to enter the Daily Star premises to rescue its journalists trapped there during the violence on December 18 night and early Friday. ‘To the journalists of The Daily Star, Prothom Alo and New Age: we stand with you. We are deeply sorry for the terror and violence you have endured. The nation has witnessed your courage and tolerance in the face of terror. Attacks on journalists are attacks on truth itself. We promise you full justice,’ it said. The interim government called upon every citizen to honour Sharif Osman Hadi, one of the organisers of the July mass uprising who died from bullet injures while undergoing treatment at a Singapore hospital on December 18 night, by rejecting and resisting violence, incitement and hatred at this critical hour. Gunshot-injured Osman Hadi, the convener of the Inquilab Mancha, breathed his last in Singapore at about 9:30pm on December 18 (Bangladesh time). Osman Hadi, who was very vocal against Indian hegemony and an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency in the forthcoming Jatiya Sangsad polls, was shot in the head on December 12 in the capital Dhaka. ‘This is a critical moment in our nation’s history when we are making a historic democratic transition. We cannot and must not allow it to be derailed by those few who thrive on chaos and reject peace,’ the interim government’s statement said. The statement said that the parliamentary elections and referendum on February 12, 2026, were not merely political exercises. ‘They are a solemn national commitment. This promise is inseparable from the dream for which Shaheed Sharif Osman Hadi gave his life. Honouring his sacrifice and memory demands restraint, responsibility and abiding commitment to reject hatred,’ it said. ‘We wholeheartedly condemn lynching of a Hindu man in Mymensingh. There is no space for such violence in new Bangladesh. The perpetrators of this heinous crime will not be spared,’ it added.

title: Govt has to take responsibility for failure: Editors’ Council, NOAB
body: The Editors’ Council and the Newspapers Owners’ Association in a joint statement on Friday expressed deep concerns and condemnation over the December 18 night arson attacks and vandalism at the offices of the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star in the capital Dhaka. They called upon the government to arrest immediately those involved in the attacks on the two media outlets and the harassment of the Editors’ Council president and New Age editor Nurul Kabir early hours of Friday. ‘The attacks exposed the state’s irresponsibility as well as serious deterioration of the law and order situation,’ said the statement signed by Editors’ Council president Nurul Kabir and NOAB president AK Azad. The Editors’ Council and NOAB are of the opinion that these attacks were not stray incidents as the latest one was a dangerous example of the interim government’s continuous failure in containing mob violence since its inception. They said that these attacks were not only on the mass media, but also on society and the democratic values as well. ‘It is an attack on Bangladesh itself,’ the statement mentioned. The overnight attacks on the two media outlets damaged their infrastructures and properties and also heightened life risks of their news workers. Both the bodies also condemned the attack on the cultural organisation Chhayanaut. ‘Chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus has assured Prothom Alo editor Matiur Rahman and The Daily Star editor Mahfuz Anam over phone of security matters and informed them that he stands by them. But the interim government has to take the responsibility for its failure in preventing these attacks and maintaining law and order,’ said the joint statement. The attacks on the media houses proved the failure of the law enforcement agencies, it said. The statement demanded immediate arrests of all perpetrators and exemplary punishment of them, not any more statements. Both the Editors’ Council and NOAB called upon all professional bodies, civil society organisations and political parties to express solidarity with the demands.

title: Perpetrators seek to erode democratic freedoms, create new fascism: BNP
body: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party on Friday strongly condemned a series of ‘heinous and despicable incidents’, including attacks on media houses, warning that the events pointed to a deliberate effort by a known group to destabilise the country and push it towards chaos. Such actions were aimed at destroying the people’s voting rights and democratic freedoms, won through immense sacrifice, and at creating a new form of fascism in the country, the BNP said in a statement. The BNP alleged that these activities were being carried out openly, and claimed that public confidence in the government’s role had eroded as a result, damaging the country’s image both at home and abroad. BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir made the remarks at a briefing at the party chairperson’s office in the capital’s Gulshan area following an emergency meeting of the party’s standing committee. Reading out resolutions adopted at the meeting presided over by the party acting chairman Tarique Rahman, Mirza Fakhrul said that Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi had died on Thursday evening while undergoing treatment in Singapore. ‘We express our deepest condolences and strongly condemn this brutal and premeditated killing,’ he said, reiterating demands for the immediate arrest and trial of those responsible. The BNP believes that these attacks form part of a conspiracy to make the forthcoming parliamentary elections and the democratic transition process uncertain, he said. Issuing a warning on behalf of peace-loving and democracy-minded citizens, Fakhrul said that the country, won at the cost of so much blood, must not be allowed to be destroyed. He called for unity among all political, social and democratic forces to resist what he described as ‘evil forces’ and to thwart the alleged conspiracy. ‘There is no alternative to unity today,’ he said, adding that the same collective strength which had led to the fall of fascism, the formation of an interim government and the securing of a national election must now be renewed. He urged all patriotic forces to once again unite to defend democracy and the country. The BNP also condemned a spate of attacks and arson following Hadi’s death, saying miscreants set fire to the offices of the Prothom Alo, The Daily Star and several other establishments late at night, endangering the lives of journalists on duty. Fakhrul said that the Editors’ Council president and New Age editor Nurul Kabir was attacked, while cultural institutions, including Chhayanaut and Udichi, were also targeted with arson. He further said that attacks had taken place on the Indian High Commission’s premises in Khulna and Chattogram, including renewed arson at Dhanmondi 32. The Indira Gandhi Cultural Centre was vandalised and set on fire, Fakhrul said. The BNP secretary general also alleged that 32 shops were vandalised in Uttara and an Awami League leader’s house was set ablaze. Fakhrul said that a Hindu youth in Mymensingh was lynched after being accused of hurting religious sentiment. Additional incidents of vandalism and arson were reported in Chattogram, Rajshahi and at the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, he added. Reiterating the party’s position, Fakhrul said that the BNP strongly condemned and expressed utter hatred for these acts, which proved that a known group was systematically attempting to destabilise the country.

title: Political parties condemn attacks on newspapers
body: Political parties on Friday strongly condemned the attacks on Bangla daily Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, describing the incidents as a grave threat to press freedom and democratic transition. Condemnations also poured in over the harassment of editors’ Council president and New Age editor Nurul Kabir by a mob in front of The Daily Star office in Dhaka early Friday. Party leaders said that the violence over the death of Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi should have been anticipated, urging the government to take strict legal action and investigate any wider plot to create nationwide disorder. They also called for peaceful, non-violent politics, warning against provocation and attempts to undermine the spirit of the July uprising and Bangladesh’s democratic aspirations. Several hundred protesters attacked the two news paper offices in Dhaka on Thursday night following the death of Osman Hadi in Singapore. The offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star were also set on fire. Bangladesh Nationalist Party secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir condemned the attacks on the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star and New Age editor Nurul Kabir. The BNP secretary general shared a post on his verified Facebook page on Friday, expressing his protest and reminding the caretaker government of its responsibility to protect lives and property. Fakhrul described those who exploited the country’s crisis to commit such acts as enemies of the nation. BNP standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed commented that action should have been taken earlier, anticipating the chaos that had been created, including the attacks on the newspaper offices and various establishments, over the death of Hadi. Condemning the incidents, he urged the government to take necessary strict legal measures against those responsible. ‘The situation should have been anticipated. There should have been intelligence reports, and precautionary measures should have been taken in advance,’ Salahuddin said. He said that certain infrastructures appeared to have been targeted deliberately, adding that it was necessary to investigate whether there was any ulterior plan or strategy to create nationwide disorder with the aim of obstructing the country’s democratic transition. The National Citizen Party, too, on Friday slated the attacks on the newspaper offices and journalists and called for peaceful, democratic political demonstrations, warning against violence and provocation during protests. Speaking at a briefing, NCP chief coordinator Nasir Uddin Patwari said that journalists had been subjected to abuse in several places, which the party strongly denounced. He regretted the attacks on The Daily Star and Prothom Alo, apologising to the nation and acknowledging that adequate security could not be ensured. Nasir said that some infiltrators had taken advantage of the student-public movement to instigate arson, vandalism, and destruction. ‘We stand for democratic and non-violent politics and reject violence in all forms,’ he said. The NCP leader also condemned the attack on New Age editor Nurul Kabir, describing him as a veteran journalist who had fought fascist forces throughout his life. ‘The religion of the people of Bangladesh is Islam. Those who exploit Islam for political purposes have now surfaced, using the guise of Islam to carry out attacks at various places,’ he said. Drawing on historical references, Nasir said that Bangladesh must not forget the spirit of the 1971 Liberation War, which he described as a struggle for equality, human dignity, and justice. He warned that ignoring those ideals could allow attempts to divert the country’s history in a different direction. ‘We participated in the 2024 mass uprising against Delhi; in the same way, we must remain vigilant against Pindi (Islamabad) as well,’ Nasir said. Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal-JSD president and freedom fighter ASM Abdur Rob in a press statement said that the death of Hadi would be an irreparable loss for the politics of the country. He called on all to refrain from creating anarchy over Hadi’s death, adding that some quarter could divert it in different directions by attacking the two media houses. He also strongly condemned the attack on editors’ council president Nurul Kabir in front of The Daily Star office during attacks on the media house on Thursday night. ASM Abdur Rob said that everybody should work for democratic transition of the country implementing the spirit of the July uprising. Ganosamhati Andolan chief coordinator Zonayed Saki in a press statement condemned anarchy and called on all to remain united for the implementation of the spirit of the July uprising and the democratic transition of the country. A team of central leaders of the Ganosamhati, led by executive coordinator Abul Hassan Rubel, on Friday morning visited the affected media houses of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star and cultural organisation Chhayanaut Bhaban in the city. They demanded arrest and exemplary punishment for the attackers and resignation of home adviser Jahangir Alam Chowdhury. Central leaders of the party Firoz Ahmed, Taslima Akhter, and others in the team also slated the attack on New Age editor Nurul Kabir. Revolutionary Workers Party general secretary Saiful Huq condemned attacks on the media houses and the harassment of New Age editor Nurul Kabir. Democratic Revolutionary Party general secretary Mosharefa Mishu also condemned the attacks on media houses and journalist Nurul Kabir. Jatiya Party faction chairman Anisul Islam Mahmud and secretary general ABM Ruhul Amin Hawlader also condemned the attacks on media houses and New Age editor Nurul Kabir. ‘I came here as the president of the Editors’ Council as I thought that it was my moral responsibility to stand by my fellow journalists at The Daily Star, after hearing reports of the attack on the newspaper’s office,’ Nurul Kabir said. He added that New Age had condemned the heinous attack on Sharif Osman Hadi and demanded a proper investigation and justice. However, he expressed concern that a group of people attacked the two newspaper offices before any investigation had been conducted. He also noted that such incidents could have an adverse impact on the country’s global image. Besides, the Communist Party of Bangladesh, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, Amar Bangladesh Party, Democratic Rights Committee, Nagorik Oikya, Socialist Party of Bangladesh, Rashtra Sangskar Andolan, Jatiya Samajtrik Dal-Jasod, a BSD faction, Revolutionary Communist League, Jatiya Press Club also condemned the attacks.

title: Protests against attack on media pour in
body: Protests poured in against Thursday night’s vandalism and arson attacks on two media outlets, The Daily Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, and harassment of Editors’ Council president and New Age editor Nurul Kabir, as more establishments in Dhaka and elsewhere in the country were attacked and set on fire on Friday. The attacks were carried out after the news of the death of Inquilab Mancha convener and one of the July uprising organisers, Sharif Osman Hadi, spread on Thursday. Different organisations of journalists, international organisations, political parties and socio-cultural organisations and rights activists staged demonstrations and issued statements condemning the attacks. They termed the day ‘a black day for journalism in the country’s history and said that it was planned to suppress freedom of the press and free thinking to stop dissenting voices. The interim government, in a statement on Friday, condemned all acts of violence that happened following the December 18 death of Hadi in a hospital in Singapore, six days after he was shot in the head on Box Culvert Road in Dhaka on December 12. After the arson attacks, The Daily Prothom Alo and The Daily Star suspended their publication for Friday. They, however, announced to resume their publication from today. The police said that no case had been filed so far, and nobody had been arrested in connection with the incidents. At a protest rally in front of the burnt Prothom Alo office, its managing editor Sajjad Sharif said that the organized attack on the newspaper was actually an attack on the freedom of expression. ‘It is a dark day for newspapers and, in its 27-year history, Prothom Alo’s publication remained suspended for the first time without any holiday for newspapers,’ he said. He believed that the attack might be to obstruct the next election and to tarnish the image of the country. ‘There are huge reasons to believe that it is a planned attack by an organized vested quarter,’ he said, and demanded a fair investigation into the incident and punishment for the attackers. The Daily Star management termed the day a dark day for independent journalism, as the attack was not merely an attack on two newspapers. ‘It is an attack on independent journalism, freedom of speech, and the sanctity of private property.’ In a statement available online, the newspaper’s management said that they called all the authorities concerned when they were attacked and they had duly promised all help. ‘However, we also note with concern that a better coordinated response would have meant less trauma for our trapped colleagues who spent several hours in grave uncertainty in a mortal fear,’ it said. Nurul Kabir, telling about harassing him on The Daily Star premises near Farmgate in the capital in the early hours of Friday, said, ‘I came here as the president of the Editors’ Council. I, after hearing reports of attacks on the newspaper office, thought that it was my moral responsibility to stand by my fellow journalists at The Daily Star.’ He added that New Age had condemned the heinous attack on Sharif Osman Hadi and demanded a proper investigation into the incident and justice for his family. He, however, expressed concern that a group of people had attacked the two newspaper offices before any investigation. The journalist also noted that such incidents could have an adverse impact on the country’s global image. UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk urged the authorities to uphold the rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly, and security of journalists at this critical time, and prevent further escalation of unrest. Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust honorary executive director Sara Hossain, after visiting the burnt The Daily Star office building, said that the attack on the media was the attack of freedom of expression. Dhaka University Professor Samina Luthfa said that both the attackers on Hadi and media houses must be brought to the book and justice should be ensured. ‘The government cannot deny its failure to ensure safety,’ he said. The government, however, in its statement, said, ‘We strongly and unequivocally condemn all acts of violence, intimidation, arson, and destruction of properties.’ The Media Freedom Coalition in Bangladesh strongly condemned the attacks carried out on Thursday night against journalists, editors, and media houses. The MFC called for the safety of all media professionals to be ensured and for swift, impartial investigations so that those responsible are held to account. ‘Such acts of violence and intimidation are unacceptable and strike at the heart of press freedom and the public’s right to be informed,’ said the MFC in a statement. Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s joint commissioner for crime, Md Faruk Hasan, said that they asked the authorities of the two dailies to file cases and that the authorities agreed to file cases. Asked whether the police could identify the attacker on The Prothom Alo and The Daily Star offices, he said, ‘I just want to say that we will take action after filing cases.’ Ganosamhati Andolon central leader and Dhak-12 candidate Taslima Akhter said that a sense of fear had created across the country. The Editors’ Council, the Newspaper Owners’ Association Bangladesh, The Dhaka Reporters’ Unity, the Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists, the Dhaka Union of Journalists, the Diplomatic Correspondents Association, Bangladesh, the Dhaka University Journalists’ Association, the Overseas Correspondents Association Bangladesh, the Reporters for Rail and Road and the Economic Reporters’ Forum, among others, condemned the attacks. Transparency International Bangladesh condemned the attacks and blamed the failure of the government for the incidents. The police and fire service officials confirmed that hundreds of people vandalised and set fire to Chhayanaut’s seven-storey building in the capital’s Dhanmondi area and Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi under Shahbagh police station in Dhaka on Friday. The unruly people vandalised the doors and windows, destroyed musical instruments and books, and set fire to parts of the premises. In Bandarban, a house belonging to former Chattogram Hill Tracts affairs minister Bir Bahadur Ushwe Sing was set on fire at Rajar Math area. In Chattogram, former education minister Mohibul Hassan Chowdhury Nowfel’s home was also attacked. The local offices of The Prothom Alo were also attacked in Sylhet, Rajshahi, Khulna and Kushtia.

title: Hadi’s body arrives, protests continue
body: The body of Inquilab Mancha spokesperson and fearless activist Sharif Osman Hadi, who died while undergoing treatment in Singapore, arrived in Dhaka on Friday evening amid nationwide protests demanding justice for Hadi. The protesters blocked different highways across the country and blocked major crossings in the capital between Thursday and Friday. The namaj-e-janaza of Hadi will be held at 2:00pm on Saturday at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in Dhaka. The national mourning day will be observed today across the country as interim government chief adviser Muhammad Yunus on Thursday in a televised address to the nation announced the one-day state mourning. To mark the mourning day, the national flag will be flown at half-mast at all government, semi-government, autonomous institutions, educational institutions, government and private buildings, and Bangladesh missions abroad. Sharif Osman Hadi, also one of the organisers of the July uprising, breathed his last in a Singapore hospital at around 9:45pm Bangladesh time on Saturday. Hadi’s death, mourned by people from all walks of life, sparked street protests across the country, with the demand for the arrest of the killers and ensure justice for Hadi. Following an instruction from the government, special prayers were arranged after the Jumma prayers on Friday in mosques across the country, seeking salvation for the soul of martyr Hadi. Special prayers were also arranged at places of worship of other religions. The government, meanwhile, requested the people interested to attend the namaj-e-janaza of Osman Hadi not to carry any bags or heavy objects with them. At the same time, the press wing also said that the government imposed a ban on flying drones in and around the Sangsad Bhaban during the janaza. Earlier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines Flight BG 585, carrying the body of Osman Hadi landed at the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 5:48pm. Some advisers of the interim government and senior leaders of different political parties, including LGRD adviser Adilur Rahman Khan, Bangladesh Nationalist Party standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed, Jamaat-e-Islami secretary general Mia Golam Parwar, National Citizen Party member secretary Akhtar Hossen were present at that time. On behalf of the BNP, tribute was paid to Hadi by placing a wreath on his coffin at the airport, said BNP Media Cell member Sayrul Kabir Khan. Later, Hadi’s body was taken to the cold storage of the National Institute of CardioVascular Diseases to preserve it, from where the body will be taken to South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban on Saturday for the janaza on Saturday. Later, the body will be transported to the central mosque of Dhaka University and will be laid to rest beside National Poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, as demanded by his family, according to a post on Inquilab Mancha’s official Facebook page. Members of law enforcement agencies were deployed at different parts of the city while army personal and members of the Border Guard Bangladesh were also deployed at different important points in the city to avoid any untoward incident. UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk in a statement on Friday expressed condolences at the death of Osman Hadi, urging for calm and everyone to refrain from violence. ‘Retaliation and revenge will only deepen divisions and undermine the rights of all,’ he said. ‘I urge the authorities to conduct a prompt, impartial, thorough and transparent investigation into the attack that led to Hadi’s death and to ensure due process and accountability for those responsible,’ said Türk. The death of Hadi has sparked widespread protests and demonstrations in the capital and across the country since his death on Thursday night in Singapore. People, including students and July uprising fighters, burst into protests in Dhaka and elsewhere across the country on Thursday. Students, general people, and various political and social organiations began gathering at Shahbagh crossing since the Friday morning, holding protest rallies and marches demanding justice for Hadi. Shahbagh crossing in the capital was blocked again on Friday over the death of Hadi. Although the presence of protesters was relatively low in the early hours, the gathering grew steadily as the day progressed, with people from different walks of life joining the blockade. The protesters left the Shahbagh area in the capital at about 8:00pm, allowing traffic movement to return to normal. During a visit in the afternoon it was seen that Shahbagh Crossing was barricaded, halting public transport movement, while students and people staged a sit-in at the crossing. The protesters were seen divided into groups, chanting slogans. School and college students, alongside people of various professions, joined the protests. In the afternoon, an ‘anti-hegemonism rally’ was started at Shahbagh led by Dhaka University Central Students’ Union vice-president Shadik Kayem, in which students and citizens took part. Speakers at the rally said that there will be no place for the Awami League in this land and the blood of Hadi will not go in vain. They also demanded immediate arrest and exemplary punishment of those responsible for Hadi’s killing. Meanwhile, several thousand people under the banners of Bangladesh Khilafat Chhatra Majlis and Sammilito July Jote staged demonstration and rallies in front of north gate of Baitul Mokarram National Mosque after the Jumma prayers demanding the immediate arrest of those responsible for the murder of Hadi. Amid tight security, Khelafat Majlis’s Dhaka city unit organised a procession on nearby roads, demanding punishment for the killers of Hadi. The wave of protests was not confined to Dhaka alone, it also spread to different parts of the country demanding arrest and trial of the people involved with the Hadi killing. Protesters blocked Dhaka-Mymensingh, Dhaka-Barishal, Dhaka-Aricha, Dhaka-Chattogram, Dhaka–Jhalokathi and Kushtia-Khulna highways. Protesters in Dhaka city brought out protest processions, blocking the Shabagh Crossing, Banglamotor, Rampura, Jatrabari and Badda Natun Bazar, halting traffic movement in those areas that continued since midnight on Thursday. New Age correspondent in Jahangirnagar University reported that the protesters blocked the Dhaka-Aricha Highway between 11:50pm on Thursday and 1:50am on Friday. New Age correspondent in Mymensingh reported that the protesters blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway on Thursday night. Since Friday morning, about 10:00am, protesters started blocking the Shahbagh crossing, Dhaka Metropolitan Police senior system analyst (traffic) Md Nurus Samad said. According to the DMP, protesters blocked the Jatrabari crossing on Thursday night and then again at about 5:00pm on Friday. It also reported that locals on Friday blocked the Dhaka–Chittagong Highway at Shanirakhra and Jatrabari areas. The obstruction has completely halted traffic in Shanir Akhra and surrounding areas due to the blocked. Meanwhile in the capital after Jumma prayers the protesters blocked the Science Lab and Mirpur 10 crossing at about 2:00pm. In Gazipur, a section of the protesters blocked Gazipur crossing at about 10:00am but later withdrew it. New Age correspondent in Barishal reported that agitated students of BM college and Barishal University held demonstrations simultaneously at various places in the city around 10:30-11:30 pm on Thursday. They set up fires on the roads at the crossings of the city and stopped the movement of vehicles. It also reported that the protesters staged a blockade on the Dhaka–Jhalokathi highway at the College Crossing at 11:30pm on Thursday, brought traffic to a standstill in both directions. New Age correspondent in Jashore reports that students and people brought out a protest procession in Jashore town on Friday noon while doa mahfils were held at different mosques and places including Jashore University of Science and Technology for the salvation of the departed soul of Osman Hadi. In Benapole, students and people staged a protest march titled ‘Long March to Border’ at the Benapole international checkpost zero point on Friday, demanding the arrest of the killers of Hadi. Osman Hadi, who was very vocal against Indian hegemony and an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency in the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad polls, was shot in the head on December 12 in the city. The incident took place a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. He initially underwent surgery at Dhaka Medical College Hospital and was later admitted to Evercare Hospital. For advanced treatment, he was airlifted to Singapore, where he succumbed to his injuries on the night of December 18.

title: Crime suspects arrested with firearms in Cox’s Bazar
body: The Bangladesh Coast Guard and the Bangladesh Navy in a joint operation arrested a crime suspect along with six country-made firearms and a large quantity of live ammunition and country-made weapons at Maheskhali in Cox’s Bazar on Friday. As part of the Operation Devil Hunt phase 2, the operation was conducted at the hideout of Mintu in the deep hills adjacent to Keruntali in Hoanok union under Maheskhali, said a press release. During the operation, crime suspects Ahsan Ullah, 45, one of the main members of the Mintu Bahini, were arrested along with four country-made pistols, two country-made single-barrel guns, 10 rounds of live ammunition, eight live cartridges, three blank cartridges and seven country-made weapons. Ahsan Ullah is associated with the Awami League, activities banned. He had created panic in the public mind through various subversive activities, added the press release. The process of taking further legal action against the seized firearms and the arrested is under process. The Bangladesh Coast Guard will continue such operations in the future to maintain the law and order situation in the country.

title: Shafi, Tabarul new president, GS of RAC
body: Shafi Uddin Ahmed of Channel S and Tabarul Haque of Dainik Amader somoy on Friday were elected president and general secretary respectively of the new executive committee-2026 of Reporters Against Corruption on Friday for a one-year tenure. The other committee members are vice-president Rafikuzzman of Islamic Television, joint secretary Taslimul Alam Towhid of Somoy tv, organising secretary Maruf Kibria of Manabzamin, treasurer Saiful Islam Montu of Ajkalerkhabor, office secretary Masud Rana of BTV, Publicity and Publication Secretary Naznin Aktar Lucky of Sarabangla.net, Training and Welfare Secretary Jannatul Ferdousi of Gazi TV, and Sports and Cultural Secretary Fazlur Rahman of Janakantha. The elected executive members are Abul Kashem, Abdullah Al Mamun of Jugantor, Jamiul Ahsan Shipu of Daily Ittefaq, Matlul Mallik of Daily Khaborer Kagoj, and Saif Babul of Rupali Bangladesh. Election commission chief Shahidul Islam along with two election commissioners – Abu Saleh Akon and Touhidur Rahman – announced the polls results. Earlier on the day, the annual general meeting of the RAC was held at a restaurant in the capital’s Segunbagicha with outgoing president Alauddin Arif in the chair.

title: UN calls for calm refraining from violence
body: UN Human Rights Chief Volker Turk on Friday urged the authorities to conduct a 'prompt, impartial, thorough, and transparent' investigation into the attack that led to Sharif Osman Bin Hadi's death, and to ensure due process and accountability for those responsible. Turk said he was deeply troubled by the killing of Hadi, a prominent leader of last year's protests in Bangladesh, who died of his injuries after being shot last week. Turk called for calm and for everyone to refrain from violence. ‘Retaliation and revenge will only deepen divisions and undermine the rights of all,’ he said. Several protests erupted at various locations around the country after Hadi's death was announced on Thursday, six days after he was shot. Some buildings were torched and vandalised, and a number of journalists have reportedly been assaulted. With the parliamentary elections scheduled for February, Turk said it was vital to ensure an environment in which all individuals can participate safely and peacefully in public life, and freely express different views. ‘I urge the authorities to uphold the rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly, and security of journalists at this critical time, and prevent further escalation of unrest,’ Turk said. The High Commissioner said his Office stands ready to work with the authorities and all stakeholders to support efforts that uphold human rights and prevent further violence.

title: Journalists must be able to carry out their work without fear: MFC
body: The Media Freedom Coalition in Bangladesh on Friday strongly condemned the attacks carried out Thursday night against journalists, editors, and media houses. ‘Such acts of violence and intimidation are unacceptable and strike at the heart of press freedom and the public's right to be informed,’ said the MFC in a statement. The MFC called for the safety of all media professionals to be ensured and for swift, impartial investigations so that those responsible are held to account. ‘Journalists must be able to carry out their work without fear,’ it said. The MFC said protecting them is essential to upholding the rule of law, democratic values, and an open, informed society. Meanwhile, the US Embassy in Dhaka joined the people of Bangladesh in mourning the loss of youth leader Sharif Osman Hadi and offered their deepest condolences to his family, friends and supporters. Besides, the High Commission of Canada in Dhaka said it stands with its Media Freedom Coalition partners in condemning attacks on media professionals in Bangladesh. ‘The safety of media professionals is essential to democracy,’ said the high commission.
