title: Udichi’s Dhaka office set on fire
body: An arson attack was carried out at the office of Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi in Dhaka on Friday amid protests over the death of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi at a hospital in Singapore. The fire was reported at about 7:42, said Rozina Islam, duty officer of the Fire Service and Civil Defence’s control room. A total of four units of firefighters were dispatched, and the fire was brought under control at about 8:13pm, according to Fire Service officials.

title: Posts ministry postpones tomorrow’s recruitment exam
body: The posts, telecommunications and information technology ministry has postponed recruitment test scheduled to be held on Saturday due to unavoidable reasons. The ministry issued an urgent press release in this regard on Friday. The release also read that the new date of the test will be announced soon on the official website of the Posts and Telecommunications Division and through SMS to candidates’ mobile phones.

title: Khaleda’s condition stable after minor procedure
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party chair and former prime minister Khaleda Zia has undergone a minor medical procedure on Friday, which was completed successfully, according to her personal physician. Speaking to reporters outside Evercare Hospital in Dhaka on Friday, BNP chair’s personal physician AZM Zahid Hossain said that the procedure was carried out smoothly, which Khaleda Zia tolerated well. He confirmed that the BNP chair was currently receiving treatment in a critical care unit equipped with full intensive care unit facilities. Khaleda Zia has been undergoing treatment at Evercare Hospital for nearly a month, having been admitted on November 23. ‘I mentioned on Thursday that her physical condition has been stable. Following the latest procedure, her condition has not deteriorated and is stable now,’ he said. Zahid also said that Khaleda Zia was being treated under the supervision of a medical board comprising both local and foreign physicians. He said that her condition had shown greater stability than earlier, due to the treatment being provided by the medical board. Through the media, Zahid appealed to the nation to pray for Khaleda Zia’s recovery, hoping that the continued treatment under the medical board would lead to further improvement in her health. Khaleda Zia was admitted to Evercare Hospital on November 23 and after examinations doctors confirmed that she had developed a lung infection. The 79-year-old politician has long been suffering from multiple health conditions, including arthritis, diabetes, kidney complications, and eye problems.

title: Hadi’s body kept at NICVD, Janaza Saturday
body: The body of Sharif Osman Hadi, the convener of the Inquilab Mancha and one of the organisers of the July uprising, has been kept at the mortuary of the National Institute of Cardio Vascular Diseases in Dhaka, reported United News of Bangladesh. His namaz-e-janaza will be held on Saturday at 2:00pm at Manik Mia Avenue. A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying Hadi landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at around 5:45pm on Friday. Biman Bangladesh Airlines Flight BG 585 took off from Singapore Changi International Airport at around 2:03pm Dhaka time. Osman Hadi, who was very vocal against Indian hegemony and an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency in the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad polls, was shot in the head on December 12 in the Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026.

title: NU postpones exams scheduled for Friday, Saturday
body: The National University authorities have postponed examinations scheduled for Friday and Saturday due to unavoidable reasons. Two separate circulars issued by the university on Friday morning also read that the new date for the exams will be announced later. On Friday, the first semester exam (2024) of the Master’s of Applied Criminology and Police Management was scheduled to be held at 3:00pm. On Saturday, the first phase of the LLB exam (2024) was scheduled to be held.

title: DCAB condemns attacks on Prothom Alo, Daily Star, harassment of Nurul Kabir
body: Diplomatic Correspondents Association, Bangladesh on Friday expressed deep concern and strongly condemned the violent attacks, vandalism and arson at the offices of daily Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, as well as the harassment of the president of the Editors’ Council and editor of New Age, veteran journalist Nurul Kabir. In a statement, the DCAB said it believes that independent and responsible journalism is one of the main foundations of a democratic state. ‘Violence, intimidation, attacks, or harassment aimed at silencing the media are in no way acceptable. Such actions are completely contrary to media freedom, the constitutional right to freedom of expression, and the rule of law,’ said the statement. The harassment of veteran journalist and editor Nurul Kabir, in particular, is a matter of grave concern, DCAB said, noting that this incident is not only an attack on professional dignity but also raises serious questions about the personal safety of journalists. The DCAB strongly demanded that the perpetrators be identified and brought to justice through a fair, impartial and speedy investigation into these incidents. At the same time, the DCAB expects effective and visible measures from the government and the relevant authorities to ensure the safety and security of media professionals. Besides, the DCAB expressed deep concern and strongly condemned the arrest of its former president Anis Alamgir and expressed solidarity with the statements issued by the Editors' Council and other organisations regarding his arrest. The DCAB also expressed solidarity with the national mourning, to be observed on Saturday, following the tragic death of Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi, who passed away on Thursday while undergoing treatment in Singapore after being shot and injured. The DCAB president, AKM Moinuddin, and general secretary Md Arifuzzaman Mamun jointly issued the statement.

title: Prothom Alo Kushtia office vandalised
body: Unidentified group of people attacked and vandalised the Prothom Alo office in Kushtia town early Friday. The incident took place around 1:30am at the newspaper’s office located at Majampur Gate, where an agitated mob damaged the office signboard, doors and windows of a room, along with various pieces of furniture. Following the incident, the police intensified patrolling across the district to maintain law and order. According to witnesses, agitated students and local residents brought out protest processions in Kushtia following the death of Inquilab Moncho spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi in Singapore on Thursday night. Later, the protesters blocked the Dhaka-Kushtia Highway by setting tyres on fire. Normal traffic resumed around midnight after the hour-long blockade was withdrawn. Around 1:30am, a group of people suddenly carried out attacks and vandalism at the newspaper office and at the residences of several Awami League leaders in different parts of the town. Officer-in-charge of Kushtia police station Kabir Hossain Matubbar said police have heard about the incidents but have not yet received any written complaint. The police are on alert to prevent any further disorder, he added.

title: Protesters block crossings across Bangladesh capital demanding justice for Hadi
body: Protesters have blocked different crossings across the Bangladesh capital since Friday morning, demanding justice for bullet-hit Sharif Osman Hadi, the convener of the Inquilab Mancha and one of the organisers of the July mass uprising, who died on Thursday night. while undergoing treatment in Singapore. Several hundred protesters brought out a procession from Baitul Mukarram mosque after Jumma prayers. Protesters also briefly blocked Gazipur crossing and Dhaka-Chattogram National Highway in the morning and vowed to block the areas after Juma prayer. As the news of the death of bullet-hit Hadi spread on Thursday night, people, including students and July uprising fighters, burst into protests in Dhaka and elsewhere across the country. Protesters in Dhaka city brought out protest processions, blocking the Shabagh Crossing, Banglamotor, Rampura, and Badda Natun Bazar, halting traffic movement in those areas that continued past midnight on Thursday. The New Age correspondent in Jahangirnagar University reported that the protesters blocked the Dhaka-Aricha Highway between 11:50pm on Thursday and 1:50am on Friday. The New Age correspondent in Mymensingh reported that the protesters blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway on Thursday night. Since Friday morning, at about 10:00am, the protesters blocked Shahbagh crossing, DMP senior system analyst (traffic) Md Nurus Samad said. ‘Traffic police are diverting the vehicles,’ he said and added that huge numbers of people were also gathering at the Jatrabari area by bus since morning. DMP police sources also said that after Jumma prayers the protesters blocked the crossing. Protesters blocked the Science Lab crossing at about 2:00pm. Protesters also blocked the Mirpur 10 crossing at about 2:00pm. In Gazipur, a section of the protesters blocked Gazipur crossing at about 10:00am but later withdrew it. They have announced the resumption of the protest after Jumma prayers. The protesters also blocked the Dhaka-Chattogram Highway in the afternoon briefly at Feni point.

title: Attack on two leading media outlets tantamount to attack on freedom of media : Yunus
body: Bangladesh interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Friday said that the attack on the country’s two leading media houses was tantamount to an attack on freedom of media. ‘The attack on the country’s two leading media outlets is tantamount to an attack on free media. This incident has created a major obstacle to the country’s democratic progress and the path of independent journalism,’ he said. The chief adviser made the remarks while speaking over the phone with the editors of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star following the attack on the two media outlets on Thursday night, according to a statement from the Chief Adviser’s Press Wing this afternoon. Expressing deep sympathy to Prothom Alo editor Matiur Rahman and The Daily Star editor Mahfuz Anam, Prof Yunus said, ‘This unwanted and barbaric attack on your institutions and journalists has deeply shocked me. In this difficult time, the government stands beside you.’ During the phone conversation, he assured the editors of full security for them and their media organisations, along with all necessary support. The chief adviser also said that he would meet the editors in person very soon.

title: Bangladesh interim government condemns mob violence, calls for restraint
body: The Bangladesh interim government has urged all citizens to resist mob violence and condemned recent acts of intimidation, arson, and property destruction, says a press release. In an official statement, the government emphasised that the country is undergoing a historic democratic transition, which must not be derailed by fringe elements who reject peace. ‘The upcoming elections and referendum are not merely political exercises. They are a solemn national commitment,’ the statement said, linking the commitment to the memory of Saheed Sharif Osman Hadi. The government also expressed solidarity with journalists of The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, and New Age, condemning attacks on media personnel as attacks on truth, and promised full justice for those affected. In addition, the statement strongly condemned the lynching of a Hindu man in Mymensingh, stating that perpetrators of such crimes ‘will not be spared’ and reaffirming that there is no space for violence in Bangladesh. Citizens were called upon to honor Saheed Hadi by rejecting and resisting all forms of violence, incitement, and hatred.

title: Youth lynched, body burnt in Mymensingh
body: A Hindu youth was lynched on Thursday night and his body was burnt after being hung from a tree branch near his workplace in the Dubaliapara area under Bhaluka upazila in Mymensingh, allegedly for hurting religious sentiments by making derogatory remarks about the Prophet. The deceased, Dipu Chandra Das, 25, a worker at Pioneer Knit Composite Factory under Bhaluka upazila, is a resident of Tarakanda upazila in Mymensingh. Chief adviser Muhammad Yunus, in a statement on Friday, condemned the murder. According to the police and eyewitnesses, a group of people alleged that Dipu, who had been working at his workplace on Thursday night, had made derogatory comments about the Prophet and a mob was created at the same time on the factory premises. He came out of the factory at about 9:00pm when the mob caught him and beat him mercilessly and he died on the spot, the police said. The mob then took the body to the Dhaka – Mymensingh Highway, hung it from a branch of a roadside tree and set fire to it, the police said. The group blocked the highway, disrupting traffic for some time. Bhaluka police station officer-in-charge Zahidul Islam said that the victim’s younger brother Aku Chandra Das filed a murder case with the police station on Friday. In his statement on Friday, chief adviser Muhammad Yunus said ‘We wholeheartedly condemn lynching of a Hindu man in Mymensingh. There is no space for such violence in the new Bangladesh. The perpetrators of this heinous crime will not be spared.’ The Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council and the Sree Sree Janmastami Udjapan Parishad Bangladesh, in separate statements on the day, also condemned the lynching incident.

title: Protesters block Shahbagh, Gazipur crossings demanding justice for Hadi

DMP police sources also said that after Juma prayer the protesters announced they would hold different demonstrations in different areas in Dhaka. In Gazipur a section of the protesters blocked Gazipur crossing at about 10:00am but later withdrew it. They have announced the resumption of the protest after Juma prayer.

title: Chhayanaut building set on fire in Bangladesh capital
body: A group of unidentified people set fire to the building of cultural organisation Chhayanaut in Bangladesh capital’s Dhanmondi area in the early hours of Friday as violence spread in the country over the death of Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi. ‘The incident took place around 2:15am,’ said Khaleda Yasmin, duty officer at the Fire Service and Civil Defence Headquarters control room. She said two firefighting units rushed to the spot and doused the blaze around 3:50am. No injuries were reported. Witnesses said a group of assailants wearing helmets and face coverings entered the building, damaged valuables and set fire to those both inside and outside the premises. Sharif Osman Bin Hadi, a prominent figure of the July Uprising, convenor of Inquilab Mancha and a prospective candidate for the upcoming 13th national parliamentary election, passed away on Thursday at 9:45pm while receiving treatment at Singapore General Hospital. Hadi was critically injured on December 12 when assailants opened fire on him while he was traveling in a rickshaw near the water tank in Bijoynagar, Dhaka. Two individuals on a motorcycle approached his rickshaw, and one of them shot him at close range before fleeing the scene.

title: Hadi’s body to be brought back to Bangladesh Friday evening
body: The body of Sharif Osman bin Hadi, spokesperson of Inqilab Moncho, who died while undergoing treatment in Singapore, will be brought back to Bangladesh on Friday. In a Facebook post on early Friday, Inqilab Moncho said a Biman Bangladesh Airlines commercial flight is scheduled to depart at 3:50pm (local time) and is expected to arrive in Dhaka at around 6:05pm. The first Namaz-e-Janaza of Hadi will be held at Angullia Mosque in Singapore at 10:00am on Friday. In Bangladesh, his Janaza will take place on Saturday after Zohr prayers at Manik Mia Avenue in the capital, Inquilab Mancha said. Hadi, the fiery face of the July Uprising and a prospective candidate for the upcoming 13th national parliamentary election, passed away on Thursday at 9:45 pm while receiving medical treatment at Singapore General Hospital. Expressing deep sorrow and grief at Hadi’s untimely death, Chief Adviser Prof Muhammad Yunus said the loss is irreparable for the country’s political and democratic landscape. ‘I pray for the eternal peace of his soul and express my deepest condolences to his bereaved wife, family members, relatives and colleagues,’ he added. He also called for calm, unity and steadfast progress towards establishing democracy, justice and the rights of the people, without falling into the trap of those seeking to destabilise the country. ‘This will be our true tribute to martyr Hadi,’ he said in a televised address to the nation. Meanwhile, Political parties and leaders, including the BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami have expressed deep condolences over the death of Sharif Osman bin Hadi. Following his death, widespread outrage erupted across the country. Protesters began gathering in Dhaka’s Shahbagh area on Thursday night after his death was announced. Hadi was critically injured on December 12 when assailants opened fire on him while he was traveling in a rickshaw near the water tank in Bijoynagar, Dhaka. Two individuals on a motorcycle approached his rickshaw, and one of them shot him at close range before fleeing the scene.

title: UGC postpones today’s recruitment test
body: The University Grants Commission of Bangladesh has postponed today’s (Friday) recruitment examination for the post of assistant director/assistant secretary of the commission due to unavoidable reasons. A press release issued by the commission on Friday morning also read that the new date for the exam will be announced later. As the news of the death of bullet-hit Sharif Osman Hadi, the convener of the Inquilab Mancha and one of the organisers of the July uprising, spread on Thursday night, people, including students and July uprising fighters, burst into protests in Dhaka and elsewhere across the country. Protesters in Dhaka city brought out protest processions, blocking the Shabagh Crossing, Banglamotor, Rampura, Badda and Natun Bazar, halting traffic movement in those areas that continued past midnight on Thursday. Several hundred protesters at one stage set fire to the office of the Bangla language daily Prothom Alo at Karwan Bazar and The Daily Star, English language newspaper, on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, and vandalised the offices in the absence of the law enforcement agencies.

title: Editors’ Council president Nurul Kabir harassed near The Daily Star office
body: Nurul Kabir, editor of New Age and president of the Editors' Council, was harassed in front of The Daily Star office near Farmgate in Dhaka early Friday. Kabir was rescued by law enforcement officials and army personnel stationed in the area to maintain law and order. They intervened and escorted the senior journalist to safety at The Daily Star office. The incident occurred after Kabir arrived at the site in response to reports of attacks on the offices of two prominent newspapers. ‘I came here as president of the Editors' Council, and I thought it was my moral responsibility to stand by my fellow journalists at The Daily Star, after hearing reports of attacks on the newspaper office,’ Kabir said. He added that New Age had condemned the heinous attack on Sharif Osman Hadi and demanded a proper investigation and assurance of justice. However, he expressed concern that a group of people attacked the two newspaper offices before any investigation had been conducted. He also noted that such incidents could have an adverse impact on the country’s global image. The demonstrators took to the streets late Thursday night following the announcement of the death of July uprising leader Sharif Osman Hadi, who had been wounded by gunfire and was undergoing treatment at a hospital in Singapore. The protesters also targeted the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star. During the protests, they vandalised and set fire to the buildings of both newspapers.

title: Protests flare up across country
body: As the news of the death of bullet-hit Sharif Osman Hadi, the convener of the Inquilab Mancha and one of the organisers of the July uprising, spread on Thursday night, people, including students and July uprising fighters, burst into protests in Dhaka and elsewhere across the country. Protesters in the Dhaka city brought out protest processions blocking the Shabagh Crossing, Banglamotor, Rampura, and Badda Natun Bazar halting traffic movement in those areas that continued midnight past Thursday. Several hundred protesters at one stage set fire to the office of the Bangla language daily Prothom Alo at Karwan Bazar and The Daily Star, English language newspaper, on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue and vandalised the offices in the absence of the law enforcement agencies. Addressing a protest rally, National Citizen Party convener Nahid Islam, also a student leader of the July mass uprising, vowed to continue their democratic peaceful movement. He called upon all the July uprising activists to remain united and act responsibly so that no one could carry out sabotages during the heated situation. Another July uprising leader and former information adviser Mahfuj Alam said that they did not think that Bangladesh should maintain social relations with India as the prime suspect in the Hadi murder case was believed to have fled to India for shelter. Military troops were deployed at places around 1:00am in the capital to maintain the law and order amid violence. At the time of filing this report at around 1:00am, the protest was continuing at Shahbagh. Participants included activists of the Dhaka University Central Students’ Union, Inqilab Mancha, Jatiya Chhatra Shakti, Islami Chhatra Shibir, Chhatra Odhikar and other student organisations. They chanted slogans such as ‘Catch the League and put them in jail’, ‘Who are you, who am I ,Hadi, Hadi’, ‘Set fire together to Jahangir’s throne’, ‘We will all become Hadi and speak in the face of bullets’ , etc. At around the same time, students from Dhaka University halls were seen protesting at the base of the Anti-Terrorism Raju Memorial Sculpture, where several students broke down in tears. Students marched from the hall areas and gathered at the Raju Sculpture at about 10:30pm, holding a brief protest rally there. DUCSU leaders expressed solidarity with the programme. Meanwhile, another mourning procession led by Jatiya Chhatra Shakti started from the TSC, marched past the VC Chattar and converged at the Shahbagh Crossing, where people from different walks of life had already gathered. Besides, at about 11:50pm, Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal’s Dhaka University unit brought out a procession, where Chhatra Dal general secretary Nasir Uddin Nasir was present. On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head in the Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. In Chattogram, a group of youths identifying themselves as ‘students and public’ staged a protest outside the assistant high commission office of India in the port city on Thursday night, condemning the killing of Inquilab Mancha convener Osman Hadi, New Age staff correspondent reported. Witnesses said that 20 to 25 protesters gathered in front of the assistant high commission office on Zakir Hossain Road in Khulshi area around 11:00pm after reports on Hadi’s death was aired by the electronic media. The protesters chanted slogans against the ousted Awami League regime and India, the witnesses added. On information, members of the Chattogram Metropolitan Police arrived at the spot and dispersed the protesters, according to eyewitness. In Rajshahi, several hundreds of Rajshahi University students gathered in front of Shaheed Professor Dr Shamsuzzoha graveyard at 10:50pm, demanding justice into the killing of Inquilab Mancha convener and July uprising organiser Sharif Osman Hadi. Later, they brought out a procession and marched towards the Awami League Rajshahi city unit half-demolished party office. During their procession, protesters chanted a series of aggressive and inflammatory slogans, including calls to resist what they described as Indian domination, revolutionary chants, and pledges not to let the death of Hadi go in vain.

title: Yunus urges calm, assures justice
body: Interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Thursday night in a televised address to the nation assured that all those involved in Sharif Osman Hadi’s brutal killing would be swiftly brought to book, and the maximum punishment would be ensured for them. ‘Fearless frontline fighter of the July Mass uprising and spokesperson of the Inquilab Manch, Sharif Osman Hadi, who was undergoing treatment in Singapore, is no longer among us,’ he mentioned. In his address at around 11:30 pm, the chief adviser urged people to have patience, ignore propaganda and rumours, and refrain from any impulsive decisions am in this situation. While announcing the state mourning, Yunus said that the national flag will be flown at half-mast at all government, semi-government, autonomous institutions, educational institutions, government and private buildings, and Bangladesh missions abroad to mark the day. He said special prayers will be arranged after Jumma prayers on Friday in every mosque across the country, seeking forgiveness for the soul of martyr Osman Hadi. Special prayers will also be arranged at places of worship of other religions. Expressing deepest sorrow and grief at the untimely death of Osman Hadi, Yunus prayed to the Almighty Allah to accept the immortal soldier of the anti-fascist and anti-imperialist movement as a martyr. He said that Hadi’s death was an irreparable loss to the country’s political and democratic landscape. ‘I pray for the salvation of his soul and extend my deepest condolences to his bereaved wife, family members, relatives, and colleagues,’ he added. Yunus also announced that the government will take the responsibility for the welfare of the wife and only child of martyr Osman Hadi. He said, ‘Energized by revolutionary blood, this young leader, Osman Hadi, was a unique symbol of resistance. Through his actions, he left behind not only protest, but also exemplary lessons of patriotism, patience, and unwavering resolve.’ Noting that the state is fully committed to upholding the rule of law, he urged all citizens of the country to maintain patience and restraint. ‘Allow the law enforcement agencies and relevant authorities to carry out the investigation professionally,’ he said. ‘I want to state clearly once again: Osman Hadi was an enemy of the defeated fascist terrorists. The attempt to silence his voice to intimidate revolutionaries will be completely thwarted. No one will be able to stop this country’s democratic progress through fear, terror, or bloodshed.’ ‘We have now reached the final stage of democratic transition. Martyr Hadi was an inseparable part of this process. His heartfelt wish was to contest in the upcoming election and play an active role in the next phase of building a new Bangladesh.’ ‘Tragically, this noble aspiration remained unfulfilled. The responsibility of realizing his dream now rests on the shoulders of the entire nation.’

title: EC asks home ministry to ensure security of RO, AROs offices
body: The Election Commission has requested the senior secretary of the Ministry of Home Affairs to ensure overall security and safety of the offices of returning officers and assistant returning officers across the country during the upcoming election and referendum scheduled for February 12. The EC issued a letter in this regard on Thursday. ‘The schedule of the 13th National Parliamentary Election was announced on December 11. A gazette notification has also been issued for the appointment of returning officers and assistant returning officers to conduct the polls smoothly,’ the letter said. It said that ensuring the security of poll officials and employees, along with the safety of important documents and electoral equipment kept at the offices of returning officers and assistant returning officers across the country, is essential. Considering the law and order situation during the polls, the EC requested the concerned authority of the Ministry of Home Affairs to issue necessary instructions for deploying an adequate number of police personnel to ensure security at the offices of returning officers and assistant returning officers.

title: Bangladesh, US troops hold joint fitness event in Dhaka
body: Bangladesh military and the United States marines’ military personnel held a joint physical fitness exercise, strengthening camaraderie, teamwork and defence cooperation between the two countries, in Dhaka on Thursday. The camaraderie-building event took place at the Bangladesh Army Stadium, centring on the marine corps combat fitness test, and aimed at promoting mutual trust, readiness and coordination among participating service members, said a US embassy press release in Dhaka. A representative of the US defence attaché office said that the exercise reflected the enduring partnership between the United States and Bangladesh, adding that training side by side reinforced trust and teamwork essential for regional security. The joint activity builds on longstanding US-Bangladesh military cooperation encompassing joint training, humanitarian assistance, disaster response and professional military education. The US embassy in Dhaka reiterated its commitment to advancing defence collaboration and further deepening ties between the armed forces of the two nations.

title: Chinese national among 2 held with 76 mobile phones at Bashundhara
body: The Detective Branch of Police have arrested a Chinese national and a Bangladeshi with 76 stolen mobile phones, mobile parts and two cartons of syringes in the Bashundhara residential area. The arrested are Wang Yujian, 33, and Alfat Hossain Shuvo, 26, according to a Dhaka Metropolitan Police statement issued on Thursday. The statement said that two teams of the DB Cyber Unit conducted a joint raid in Bashundhara area at 11:00pm on Wednesday night and arrested them with the stolen mobile phone sets and syringes. During the raid, the DB teams recovered 45 iPhones of different models, 31 Android phones of various brands, 10 mobile phone displays, a laptop, a mobile checkerboard, a phone battery booster, a phone toolbox, phone casings, two cartons of syringes, and a money-counting machine from their possessions, the statement added. It said that the police produced them before the court after completing legal procedures

title: ICT orders arrest of Obaidul Quader, 6 others
body: The International Crimes Tribunal 2 on Thursday issued arrest warrant against seven individuals, including Awami League general secretary and former minister Obaidul Quader, in a case filed against them on the charges of committing crime against humanity during the July Mass Uprising. Other accused of the case are – Awami League joint general secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, former state minister for information and broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat, Juba League president Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and general secretary Mainul Hossain Khan Nikhil, president of the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League Saddam Hossain and its general secretary Wali Asif Inan. The ICT 2 issued the order, taking the formal charge filed against the seven into cognisance. The tribunal also set December 29 for holding further hearing on the matter. The prosecution earlier in the morning filed the formal charge with the office of the tribunal registrar.

title: Shaheed Felani Hall’s provost building inaugurated at BRUR
body: The provost building of Shaheed Felani Hall at Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur has been inaugurated. BRUR Vice-chancellor Professor Md Showkat Ali inaugurated the building in a ceremony as the chief guest on Thursday. At this time, provost of the hall Professor Sifat Rumana, director of the university’s Institutional Quality Assurance Cell Professor Md Tajul Islam, registrar Md Harun-or Rashid, assistant hall provosts, engineering and administrative officers and other concerned people were present. It may be mentioned that the BRUR authority renamed a residential hall of the university as Felani Hall after the July uprising as a mark of deep respect to Felani Khatun. Felani Khatun, a 15-year-old Bangladeshi girl, was shot dead by India’s Border Security Force while attempting to cross the India-Bangladesh border near Anantapur village under Phulbari in Kurigram district on January 7, 2011. Her body became famously and tragically known worldwide for being left to hang on the barbed-wire border fence for several hours after the shooting. A photograph of Felani’s lifeless body hanging from the fence was widely circulated internationally sparking massive outrage and protests in Bangladesh and abroad over the BSF’s use of excessive force and human rights violations along the border. Felani has become a symbol demanding an end to border killings and a reminder of the vulnerability of undocumented migrants. A road in Dhaka’s Gulshan diplomatic zone has even been renamed Felani Avenue in Shaheed Felani Khatun’s memory.

title: RAB arrests accused in Khulna court double murder
body: The Rapid Action Battalion has arrested Md Ejajul Hossain in connection with the double murder that had taken place in front of the Khulna metropolitan court. The information was disclosed at a press conference on Thursday by Lieutenant Colonel Md Nistar Ahmed, commanding officer of RAB 6. He said that Fazle Rabbi Rajan, 30, and Hasib Hawladar, 40, were shot and hacked to death in in front of the court’s main gate on November 30. Following the incident, RAB 6 collected evidence, including the CCTV footage and mobile video recordings. Ejajul Hossain, who was clearly identified in video footage, was arrested on December 17 around 5:30pm from the Aichgati area of Rupsha. He later confessed to his involvement and disclosed the names of seven others involved in the killing. Fazlur Rahman, media officer of RAB 6, said that the murders stemmed from long-standing rivalry between two drug trafficking groups over illegal business supremacy, adding that drives were continuing to arrest the remaining accused.

title: HR shortage hits family planning: dialogue
body: Family planning services across Bangladesh are being severely disrupted due to a long-standing shortage of human resources and a recent crisis in contraceptive supplies, health rights activists and frontline caregivers said at a policy dialogue in Dhaka on Thursday. The dialogue, titled Preparatory National Policy Dialogue on Community Care as a Common Priority Agenda in Bangladesh, was organised at the Directorate General of Family Planning by Safeguarding All Lives in collaboration with UNI Global Asia Pacific Regional Organisation, the Family Welfare Assistants Association and the Family Planning Inspectors Association, said a press release. Family welfare assistants said that their field-level activities had been hampered since mid-2024 because of an acute shortage of contraceptives, limiting their ability to provide essential services to couples at the community level. They also highlighted the growing workload caused by insufficient staffing. At present, about 17,000 family planning workers are employed nationwide, with some assistants responsible for more than 2,000 eligible couples, despite the planned coverage being around 600 couples per worker. Sohel Hossain, a family planning inspector, said that the existing human resources schedule was approved in 1984 and has not been updated since, making it impossible to address current population and service demands. Several family welfare assistants said that the absence of a clear recruitment policy has left them vulnerable, affecting job security, career progression and morale. Dr Ashrafi Ahmad said that unresolved recruitment rules for family welfare assistants and family planning inspectors have created persistent administrative challenges, undermining the effectiveness of community-based health services. Mir Sajedur Rahman, director, administration, at the Directorate General of Family Planning, outlined the prolonged delays in recruitment, issues related to grade advancement and the institutional constraints affecting staffing decisions. Tilak Jang Khadka, director of UNI APRO and UNI Global Union, stressed the need for institutionalised recruitment rules, fair wages and labour rights protections for community health workers, advocating research-based dialogue with authorities. Sapran research director Md Zarif Rahman and researcher Zeba Sajida Saraf presented findings from a regional study on community health workers, offering recommendations to improve working conditions in Bangladesh. Senior officials of the Directorate General of Family Planning were also present at the event.

title: July Oikya protests at Indian statement, seeks explanation
body: July protesters under the banner of ‘July Oikya’ on Thursday protested at and condemned a statement by the Indian government that termed those who staged Wednesday’s march towards the Indian High Commission in Dhaka ‘extremist elements’. Dhaka University Central Students’ Union Social Service Secretary and July Oikya organiser Zubair Bin Nesary, addressing a press conference at Madhu’s Canteen on the university campus, also urged the interim government to seek an explanation within 72 hours from India about their Ministry of External Affairs’ statement. He claimed that India had termed the former army personnel and the July fighters of Bangladesh ‘extremists’. Zubair also demanded that the Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh, Pranay Kumar Verma, be declared persona non grata. He announced a march towards the Bangladesh foreign ministry on December 23 if an explanation from India was not sought by the time and said that protest rallies would be held in Chattogram, Barishal and Sylhet divisions today. On Wednesday, ‘July Oikya’ marched towards the Indian High Commission in Dhaka, demanding the extradition of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and others involved in crimes against humanity during the July uprising. The Indian Ministry of External Affairs, on the same day, summoned the Bangladesh high commissioner to India and issued a statement that said that the MEA had ‘apprised of India’s strong concerns at the deteriorating security environment in Bangladesh. His attention was drawn, in particular, to the activities of some extremist elements who have announced plans to create a security situation around the Indian Mission in Dhaka.’

title: ACC presses charges against Asaduzzaman, family
body: The Anti-Corruption Commission on Thursday submitted a charge sheet against former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, his wife and their two children in a case involving corruption and money laundering. ACC director general Md Akhtar Hossain revealed the information at a regular media briefing at the commission’s headquarters. The case was filed on October 9, 2024, by the ACC’s Dhaka 1 Integrated District Office. According to the charge sheet, during his tenure as home minister, Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal allegedly acquired and possessed assets worth about Tk 22.58 crore through corrupt practices and abuse of power, which were inconsistent with his known sources of income. The investigation further found that he conducted transactions amounting to over Tk 87.46 crore through nine bank accounts operated in his own name. The funds were allegedly laundered to conceal and convert their illegal sources. The charge sheet also named his wife Lutful Tahmina Khan, son Shafi Moddassir Khan Jyoti and daughter Shafia Tasnim Khan as accused. According to the investigation, each of them allegedly assisted in concealing the illegal sources of approximately Tk 15.45 crore of crime-derived funds through house construction and business establishments registered in their respective names. The ACC investigation determined the former home minister’s total net assets at over Tk 28.17 crore against which lawful sources of income of nearly Tk 5.59 croe were identified. The commission submitted the charge sheet under Section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004; Section 5(2) of Corruption Prevention Act, 1947; and Sections 4(2) and 4(3) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012.

title: Govt to draw FY27 budget outline on Dec 22
body: The interim government is going to draw an outline of the national budget for the 2026-27 financial year on December 22 for prudent management of fiscal measures by the new government to be elected through the national polls scheduled for February 12, 2026. Chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus will preside over the meeting to be held in this connection at the chief adviser’s official residence Jamuna in the capital Dhaka. The FY27 budget size may be set at about Tk 8.50 lakh crore with 6 per cent growth in the gross domestic product, said finance ministry officials. Finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed, planning adviser Wahiduddin Mahmud and Bangladesh Bank governor Ahsan H Mansur will attend the meeting. Finance secretary Khairuzzman Majumder is expected to present the budget outline while an update of the country’s macro-economy will be presented by the macro wing under the Finance Division. Finance ministry officials said that it was necessary to draw the budget outline before the February 12 national election for elementary exercises by the Finance Division. Waiting for the new government poses challenges for the Finance Division to complete preparatory works timely, said the officials. The officials also said that the new government would get about three and a half months before the announcement of the FY27 budget in the first week of June. The December 22 meeting is likely to endorse a revised budget for the current financial year of 2025-26. On November 10, a joint meeting of the coordination council and the budget management and resource committee presided over by the finance adviser estimated to cut the size of the FY26 budget by Tk 20,000 crore from Tk 7.9 lakh crore. It also decided to revise down the country’s GDP growth to 5 per cent from 5.5 per cent for the FY26 and an upward revision of inflation to 7 per cent from 6.5 per cent. The current annual development programme may be slashed by about Tk 30,000 crore amid its slow implementation rate. The revised ADP for FY26 will stand at Tk 2,00,000 crore from Tk 2,30,000 crore set by the National Economic Council at a meeting on May 18, 2025.

title: Bangladesh to open embassy in Switzerland
body: The interim government on Thursday approved a proposal to establish a Bangladesh embassy in Bern of Switzerland. The approval was given at a meeting of the council of advisers, held with chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus in the chair at his office at Tejgaon in the capital Dhaka, according to information shared by the chief adviser’s press wing. Since independence, Bangladesh has maintained in Geneva of Switzerland a permanent mission which handles both United Nations-related work and bilateral embassy functions due to the absence of a resident embassy in Bern, the capital of Switzerland. Considering Switzerland’s role as an important development partner and strategic ally of Bangladesh, the council decided to open an embassy in Bern, said the press wing. Initially, the embassy will begin operations with the appointment of an ambassador, a first secretary and a limited number of officials and staff, it added. Bangladesh currently operates 82 mission offices, including embassies, across the world.

title: Cumilla bus services suspended as owners enforce strike
body: Bus services from three terminals in Cumilla city remained suspended on Thursday as the Cumilla Bus Owners’ Association enforced a strike to press home their demands, causing severe inconvenience to passengers. No buses left the Jangalia, Shasangacha and Chakbazar bus terminals since morning, halting bus movement on nearly 40 routes in the district. Both inter-district and long-distance services, including those on Cumilla-Dhaka, Cumilla-Chattogram, Cumilla-Sylhet and Cumilla-Chandpur routes remained suspended. The strike was called demanding a halt to the operation of Aidi Paribahan on the Cumilla-Chandpur route from the Jangalia bus terminal. Transport leaders alleged that thousands of buses and minibuses use the city’s three terminals every day but Aidi Paribahan had been attempting to operate from the terminals without proper route permits. Aidi Paribahan chairman Mir Parvez Alam alleged that the company began operating buses on the Cumilla-Chandpur route in 2023 after obtaining permission from the Chandpur deputy commissioner’s office. However, he claimed that a syndicate of the Cumilla bus owners’ group obstructed their operations from the outset, resulting in the Cumilla district administration not issuing a route permit. He said that since February this year, Aidi Paribahan had been forced to operate its services from Paduar Bazar Bishwaroad, about two kilometres away, instead of using the Jangalia terminal. Despite no legal barriers, the company has yet to receive a no-objection certificate from the Cumilla district administration, he alleged. Executive vice-president of the Cumilla Bus Owners’ Association Md Tajul Islam said that although Aidi Paribahan had obtained permission from Chandpur district administration it failed to secure a route permit from Cumilla and despite this, the company has been trying to use Cumilla’s bus terminals. When the attempt was made again on Thursday, all three terminals were kept closed from the morning, he said, adding that they would not resume services until the issue was settled. The suspension of bus services caused severe hardship for office-goers, students and long-distance travellers. Many passengers were seen heading to their destinations using alternative modes of transport at higher fares.

title: Bangladesh
body: ISD celebrates Victory Day International School Dhaka has observed the 55th Victory Day of Bangladesh with an assembly that brought the whole school community together to honour the country’s rich history and the sacrifices of the martyrs. International School Dhaka has observed the 55th Victory Day of Bangladesh with an assembly that brought the whole school community together to honour the country’s rich history and the sacrifices of the martyrs. A juice vendor was stabbed to death during an Islamic gathering organised by the Darul Aman Trust at Pabna Sadar in the district on Wednesday. The notification for filling the form for the secondary school certificate examination of 2026 has been published under the Dhaka education board. Nearly two-thirds of child labourers in Bangladesh are employed in industrial and factory settings, exposing them to serious health and safety risks, a report said on Wednesday. Speakers at a meeting in Rajshahi on Thursday called for integrated efforts of all government and non-government organisations concerned for the welfare of the elderly and people with disabilities.
