title: ISD celebrates Victory Day
body: International School Dhaka has observed the 55th Victory Day of Bangladesh with an assembly that brought the whole school community together to honour the country’s rich history and the sacrifices of the martyrs. The assembly featured a series of student-led performances that celebrated the spirit of patriotism and unity. The assembly began with a warm welcome from Michael Palmer, primary school principal. Following the welcome speech, the event, hosted by students from both the Primary Years Programme and the Middle Years Programme, continued with the national anthem. This was followed by a series of captivating performances showcasing the talent and enthusiasm of the students across various grade levels. The assembly included a narration of the history of Bangladesh, captivating dance performances on the songs ‘Agami Ponchashe,’ Ekti Bangladesh Tumi Jagroto Jonotar’, ‘Cholo Shobai’, and ‘O Prithibi Ebar Eshe’. The audience also enjoyed a drama presentation of ‘Potakar Mullo’, a live musical performance on the song ‘Brave’, followed by a poetry recitation of ‘Abar Ashibo Phire’, leaving them inspired and united in the spirit of Victory Day. Speaking at the event, Palmer said, ‘Victory Day is a reminder of the sacrifices that shaped Bangladesh, and it is important that our students grow up understanding what this day truly represents. To see them confidently and respectfully lead today’s assembly is a true indicator of how much they cherish our country’s heritage. The performances today very nicely reflected our students’ creativity, resilience, and pride in their nation, and we couldn’t have been prouder.’ The event emphasised the immense sacrifices made during the Liberation War, and reaffirmed ISD’s commitment to fostering a sense of community and cultural appreciation among learners and staff members.

title: Juice vendor stabbed to death in Pabna, accused held
body: A juice vendor was stabbed to death during an Islamic gathering organised by the Darul Aman Trust at Pabna Sadar in the district on Wednesday. The victim was Sujan Mollah, 17, son of Saiful Mollah of Titpulia villag under Santhia. The police, however, detained the suspect, 20-year-old Md Sohan, elder son of Sheikh Sharif from Mahendrapur area under Pabna Sadar. According to witnesses, Sohan visited a juice stall near the gathering around 9:30am. After drinking the juice, he delayed paying the shopkeeper leading to an argument between them. At one stage, the accused allegedly said, ‘You know me, so what will you do if I do not pay?’ The altercation escalated when Sohan suddenly stabbed the seller in multiple places and injured him critically. He was taken to Pabna General Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries at 4:15pm on Wednesday. Officer-in-charge Md Dulal Uddin of Pabna Sadar police said that a murder case had been filed in this connection.

title: SSC exam form filling notice published
body: The notification for filling the form for the secondary school certificate examination of 2026 has been published under the Dhaka education board. The process of filling the form will start from December 31 and will continue till January 10, 2026, said a notification signed by Professor SM Kamal Uddin Haider, controller of examinations of the board of intermediate and secondary education, Dhaka on Thursday. The notification stated that, subject to the registration period, unsuccessful candidates in 2025 in one to four subjects in the compulsory and elective subjects, including GPA development candidates, will have to apply on a white paper to the head of their respective educational institution by December 24 to participate in the failed subject or subjects in the 2026 SSC examination. Educational institutions will conduct the selection examination and publish the results by December 30, it added. The notification stated that the online form could be filled out with a late fee from January 12 to January 17, 2026. The fee can be submitted online with a late fee of Tk 100 per candidate until January 18. The form filling fee for regular students in the science department including the 4th subject is Tk 2,435, the form filling fee for the business education department including the 4th subject is Tk 2,315, and the form filling fee for the Humanities department including the 4th subject is Tk 2,315. Students registered for the year 2024-2025 will participate in the 2026 SSC examination as regular examinees.

title: Two-thirds of child labour work in factories: report
body: Nearly two-thirds of child labourers in Bangladesh are employed in industrial and factory settings, exposing them to serious health and safety risks, a report said on Wednesday. The findings were presented at an event in Dhaka jointly organised by the International Organisation Educo Bangladesh and the Child Labour Elimination Platform. Economist Khondaker Golam Moazzem presented the policy recommendations, while Educo Bangladesh country manager Afzal Kabir Khan chaired the session. Speakers at the event stressed the need to strengthen social protection measures to prevent child labour and provide adequate support to affected families. The report revealed that 66.6 per cent of child labourers were engaged in the industrial sector, while 44.4 per cent work in services and 38.8 per cent in agriculture. Many of these children are exposed to hazardous conditions that pose serious threats to their physical and mental wellbeing. According to the data, hazardous child labour is most prevalent in the industrial sector, accounting for 54.7 per cent of cases. The service sector follows with 29.9 per cent, while agriculture accounts for the lowest share at 3.3 per cent of children engaged in dangerous work. Moazzem said that despite international commitments, existing laws and social protection mechanisms, millions of children remained engaged in labour, particularly in the informal sector. He mentioned that around 3.5 million children were involved in various forms of work, but official data was available for only 1.7 million of them. ‘Of this number, about 1,00,000 children are engaged in hazardous occupations.’ He said that child labour was more visible in urban areas due to the availability of diverse job opportunities, but rural child labour remains significant, particularly in agriculture and seasonal work. To address the problem effectively, he recommended increasing budgetary allocations to social protection programmes and expanding their coverage to reach vulnerable families. Md Kamal Uddin Biswas, additional secretary of the Ministry of Social Welfare, said that the United Nations sustainable development goals explicitly called for ending child labour, exploitation, trafficking and all forms of violence against children. He reaffirmed the government’s commitment to achieving the SDG targets. He added that several initiatives, projects and programmes had already been undertaken by different ministries and departments to eliminate child labour. The government, he said, would take steps to implement recommendations aimed at bringing out-of-school children under social protection schemes and increasing allocations in this sector. Associate professor Md Aurangzeb Akand of Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University stressed the need for universal child benefits and adequate social protection systems. He called for increased investment in quality education and urged authorities to bring all out-of-school children back into classrooms. He also emphasised greater spending on child protection, agricultural development, rural public services, infrastructure and livelihoods. Afzal Kabir Khan said that eliminating child labour required a robust and inclusive social protection system. He underscored the importance of reducing gaps in coverage, expanding social safety net programmes and strengthening support for the families of child labourers to address the root causes of the problem.

title: Integrated efforts for elderly people sought
body: Speakers at a meeting in Rajshahi on Thursday called for integrated efforts of all government and non-government organisations concerned for the welfare of the elderly and people with disabilities. They also viewed that many of the elderly and the people with disabilities were subjected to repression and oppression due to their vulnerable conditions in the family and society. The remarks were made in the district-level conference on the ‘possibilities of promoting one stop solution centres in every upazila’ at the conference hall of the office of Department of Social Services in the city. Organised by the Rajshahi regional office of Caritas Bangladesh, senior citizens, people with disabilities, members of the civil society, religious leaders and representatives from government and non-government entities attended the meeting. The Social Development for Dignity and Betterment project supported the meeting. DSS deputy director Monira Khatun and deputy civil surgeon Dr Mahbuba Khatun addressed the meeting as chief and special guests with Caritas regional director Arook Toppo in the chair. The speakers observed that the society could benefit from the knowledge and experience the old aged people gained in their lifetime. Schoolgirls can play a pivotal role in caring for their near and dear old people, helping them lead their life peacefully and that is very important for their welfare, they noted. By nature, girls take more care of their parents and traditionally have been contributing a lot towards ensuring congenial atmosphere everywhere in the society and the family as well for the welfare of the elderly people. Monira Khatun stressed the need for ensuring congenial atmosphere in the society, including family for the welfare of the elderly people. She viewed, ‘Many people become vulnerable when they reach their old age and face multifarious problems due to various reasons.’ To mitigate the odd situation, the respective family members should take the responsibility of protecting them as there is no way to discard their contribution to the field of culture, economy and politics in the country, she added. Mahbuba Khatun mentioned that if every son and daughter paid due respect to their parents, no aged people would face an unexpected condition. junior programme officer Augustine Ratia Nunia said that the SDDB aimed to uplift vulnerable communities by eradicating poverty, promoting economic empowerment, ensuring inclusive education, improving health and nutrition. Fostering ecological sustainability, and strengthening disaster resilience, focusing on marginalised groups like people with disabilities, the poor and national minority peoples are the objectives to achieve integral human development and dignity.

title: BNP prepares to make Tarique return historic
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chair Tarique Rahman is scheduled to arrive in Dhaka on December 25 on a regular commercial flight of Biman Bangladesh Airlines. The aircraft is expected to land at the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport around 12:00pm. BNP standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed made the announcement on Thursday while speaking to reporters at the BNP chair’s office at Gulshan in the capital. He said that the party wanted to make Tarique Rahman’s return a historic occasion that would surpass political precedents of the past 55 years and remain unmatched in the decades ahead. Salahuddin said that the BNP was assessing possible venues for receptions, saying that people across Bangladesh were eager to see Tarique and hear him speak. He disclosed that party leaders were visiting locations to determine where large crowds could be accommodated with minimal public inconvenience. Instructions, he said, have been issued to leaders and activists of the BNP and its affiliated bodies at district, upazila, and union levels to arrive in Dhaka by the night of December 24 or the morning of December 25 to welcome their leader. Salahuddin said that BNP leaders had carried out on-the-ground inspections of arrangements at the airport, including where Tarique would disembark, and how he would proceed on a vehicle. Routes for Tarique’s travel to the hospital treating his mother, his residence and other planned programmes are also being reviewed in coordination with the relevant authorities, he said. Security arrangements were being coordinated separately with government agencies concerned, said Salahuddin. Tarique Rahman, the elder of the two sons of BNP chair and former prime minister Khaleda Zia, had previously been sentenced in several cases, including a life term, and faced numerous other charges, most of which were filed during the 2007–08 military-backed caretaker government. He was arrested during an anti-corruption drive in March 2007 and released on bail on September 3, 2008, after which he travelled to London on September 11 for medical treatment, and remained there. Following the end of the Awami League’s 16-year rule in a mass uprising on August 5, 2024, the High Court acquitted him of all cases filed during both the caretaker government and Awami League administration periods, clearing the legal obstacles to his return. BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir announced at a press conference on Friday that Tarique Rahman was scheduled to return to Bangladesh on December 25. BNP has already formed a committee to organise the reception, with Salahuddin Ahmed as its chair and senior joint secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi as member secretary. Rizvi told reporters that organisational preparations were progressing as planned and expressed confidence that the gathering would be historic. Meanwhile, Tarique Rahman on Tuesday at a discussion in London confirmed that he would return to Bangladesh on December 25, ending more than 17 years of stay in the United Kingdom. While the BNP was preparing for a huge gathering in Dhaka to receive Tarique, the BNP acting chair urged party leaders and supporters not to go to the Heathrow Airport in London to see him off, warning that large gatherings could create disorder and harm both the country’s and the party’s image. The BNP on Thursday requested the railways ministry to arrange special trains or additional carriages on seven key routes on the night of December 24, ahead of the return of Tarique Rahman from the United Kingdom. In a letter to the ministry’s secretary, the BNP highlighted the expected arrival of large numbers of students and supporters from across the country who plan to welcome Tarique in Dhaka. The party requested train services on major routes including Cox’s Bazar–Dhaka, Sylhet–Dhaka, Jamalpur–Mymensingh–Dhaka, Tangail–Dhaka, Chapainawabganj–Rajshahi–Dhaka, Panchagarh–Nilphamari–Parbatipur–Dhaka, and Kurigram–Rangpur–Dhaka. The party said that all fares would be paid in accordance with government regulations and appealed for the approval of at least one special train or additional carriages on each route to ensure smooth travel for the travelling supporters. Earlier this year, the government provided eight special trains to carry people from different districts to Dhaka city on August 5 to join the July Declaration announcement ceremony, had passengers fewer than the usual trains. Before that, Chattogram Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal rented a special train to take part in a student rally at the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka on August 3, and the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami rented four special trains to transport leaders and supporters to Dhaka for its July 18 rally at the Suhrawardy Udyan in Dhaka.

title: BNP assures  Ganatantra Mancha of 3 JS seats
body: Several leaders of the Ganatantra Mancha on Thursday expressed dissatisfaction following a seat-sharing meeting with the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, as the party indicated it would concede three seats to three parties of the platform. The BNP assured the Nagorik Oikya, the Ganosamhati Andolan and the Revolutionary Workers Party of Bangladesh that each would receive one seat, but no final decisions were made regarding other parties, including the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD), the Bhashani Janashakti Party and the Gano Forum, leaders attending the meetings told New Age. BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, along with standing committee members Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury and Iqbal Hasan Mahmud Tuku, held separate meetings with the five Ganatantra Mancha parties and the Gano Forum. BNP standing committee member Tuku told New Age that the party was holding discussions with movement partners and that the allocation of seats for allies would be finalised within a couple of days following consultations with party acting chair Tarique Rahman. The BNP began meetings on Wednesday at its Gulshan office with like-minded parties, coalitions and other movement partners to resolve disputes over seat-sharing ahead of the forthcoming parliamentary elections. Despite the BNP’s assurances, several allied parties expressed disappointment over the ‘low’ allocation of seats and the lack of clarity regarding final arrangements. RWPB general secretary Saiful Haque said that the BNP leaders had held one-on-one discussions with various Ganatantra Mancha parties and would announce in the coming days in which constituencies they plan to support other parties or leaders. He said that the RWPB had primarily proposed contesting for the Dhaka-8 constituency, but the BNP had already announced Mirza Abbas as their candidate for the seat. Discussions were also held over the Dhaka-12 constituency, with mostly positive outcomes. Saiful said that the concerns of the RWPB were not personal grievances but related to party dignity, partnership and parliamentary representation for the people engaged in the political movement. He criticised the BNP for not finalising top leadership decisions, saying that the party had not shown sufficient respect during discussions, leaving allies dissatisfied with the progress. Ganosamhati Andolan chief coordinator Zonayed Saki said that his party had held a meeting with the BNP, covering joint movements on constitutional reform, its implementation, and the forthcoming election, along with preliminary talks on seat-sharing arrangements. The BNP expressed support for Saki’s candidature from the Brahmanbaria-6 constituency, though further discussions were planned. Several constituencies remain open, where both BNP and Ganosamhati Andolan would field candidates, Saki said. Nagorik Oikya president Mahmudur Rahman Manna said that the BNP informed him that his seat in Bogra-2 was already confirmed and that no additional seats could be offered. Manna argued that contesting the election with only one seat would make it difficult for his party to remain politically active. Manna recalled that in the 2018 election the party had contested for five seats. He questioned the practicality of contesting after seven or eight years with only a single seat adding that securing just one seat against the five constituencies would not satisfy supporters. Gano Forum acting president Subrata Chowdhury said that his party had submitted a list for seven constituencies, but the BNP gave no assurance. BNP leaders mentioned that if the party could form the government, there might be scope to accommodate movement partners in the upper house, he said. Other sources said that the JSD had discussions with BNP leaders, but no specific seat-sharing agreements were reached. Meanwhile, a leader of the Liberal Democratic Party told New Age that their scheduled meeting with the BNP was postponed on Thursday due to the absence of BNP standing committee member Nazrul Islam Khan. The LDP leader said that although the meeting did not take place, they visited the BNP Gulshan office and were assured by the secretary general that two seats–Comilla-7 and Chattogram-14–remained confirmed for the party. The BNP on Wednesday met with the 12-party alliance and the Jatiyatabadi Samomona Jote, indicating that it might concede one seat to each group. Earlier, the BNP announced its candidates for 272 constituencies out of 300 across the country in two phases.

title: Tribunal to announce ‘disappeared’ after 5 years
body: The interim government on Thursday approved the draft ‘Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress (Amendment) Ordinance 2025’, introducing a key provision that allows a tribunal to officially declare a person as ‘disappeared’ if he or she remains missing for at least five years. The Council of Advisers gave its approval at its weekly meeting at the chief adviser’s office in the capital’s Tejgaon area. Chief adviser Muhammad Yunus presided over the meeting. According to the draft amendment to the ordinance, if a person remains missing for not less than five years and does not return alive, the tribunal shall, upon the application of any interested person, presume the person to be ‘disappeared’ and declare him or her as such. The form and procedure of applications, attestations and certificates of disappearance under this section may be prescribed by rules. But until such rules are framed, the matters shall be determined by the tribunal, according to the draft ordinance. Under the amended draft ordinance, the government will be empowered to appoint the required number of public prosecutors for the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Tribunal following recommendations from the National Human Rights Commission. The amendment also strengthens legal access for victims, as victims or complainants will be allowed to appoint lawyers of their own choice to represent them before the tribunal. Aiming at easing hardships for families of the victims, the ordinance allows the spouse or dependent family members of a disappeared person to use the individual’s property without prior approval from the commission. Where proceedings under this section are initiated by the spouse of a disappeared person or any dependent member of his or her family, prior permission of the commission shall not be required, said the ordinance. However, the tribunal may, if it deems necessary, call for a report from the commission for verification. ‘In my understanding, you are aware that due to enforced disappearance, families are unable to operate their bank accounts for a long time. They also cannot claim or manage their rightful shares in land and property,’ rights activist ASM Nasir Uddin Elan told New Age. ‘This is because the disappeared person cannot be declared dead, nor can he or she be declared alive. It is my understanding that this technical issue is the main reason behind the decision to introduce this amendment,’ he said. Law ministry officials, on the other hand, confirmed that the government was going to set up specialised ‘Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress’ tribunal in eight divisions in the country to conduct trials of the enforced disappearance cases. The tribunal will be set up under the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Ordinance. These special courts will not only try cases relating to enforced disappearances across the country, but also will take strict action against cases on false allegations or aimed at harassing people. At the same time, they will ensure financial compensation for victims. The officials also said that, following the promulgation of the Ordinance, the law ministry recently prepared a Statutory Regulatory Order and sent the SRO to the BG Press for publication in the gazette regarding the establishment of the tribunal. The tribunals will be established at the divisional headquarters of all eight divisions of the country, including Dhaka. These tribunals will have jurisdiction not only over their respective divisional territories but also over cases from the concerned metropolitan areas. As a result, victims and their families will be able to access legal remedies more easily. The proposed locations of the tribunals are Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet, Mymensingh, Rajshahi, Rangpur, Khulna and Barishal. Earlier, on December 2, the government issued a gazette notification promulgating the ‘Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Ordinance, 2025’, formally criminalising the act of enforced disappearance. Under the law, the ‘maximum punishment for enforced disappearance is the death penalty’. Acts such as denying a person’s detention, abduction, or unlawful confinement, or concealing their whereabouts in a manner that deprives them of legal protection, are defined as enforced disappearance and are punishable by imprisonment and fines. Where a victim of enforced disappearance is determined to be permanently untraceable or is found dead, the ordinance prescribes ‘capital punishment along with a fine of up to Tk 1 crore’ for the offender. The minimum penalty for any enforced disappearance offence is 10 years’ imprisonment and a fine of Tk 50 lakh. Destroying or tampering with evidence related to enforced disappearance is punishable by ‘seven years’ imprisonment, while constructing, establishing, or using a ‘secret detention centre’ carries a penalty of up to seven years in prison and a fine of Tk 20 lakh. The ordinance states that willful ignorance amounts to complicity. Senior officers of disciplined forces will be held equally liable if they order, plan, support, ignore, or fail to prevent acts of enforced disappearance committed by their subordinates. All offences under this law are non-bailable and not eligible for out-of-court settlement. The National Human Rights Commission has been assigned responsibility for investigating enforced disappearance cases, while special tribunals will conduct judicial proceedings. Investigators must complete investigations within 90 days, extendable by a maximum of 30 days; failure to comply may result in departmental disciplinary action. The draft of the Bangladesh Haor and Wetland Conservation Ordinance 2025 was also approved on Thursday by the Council of Advisers, specifying the responsibilities, authority, and jurisdiction of the Bangladesh Haor and Wetland Development Department. The ordinance included provisions for issuing protection orders to conserve biodiversity, environment, ecology, and ecosystems of haor and wetland areas. The ordinance includes provisions for declaring protected haor and wetland areas to ensure their conservation.

title: Prothom Alo, Daily Star offices attacked, set on fire
body: Several hundred protesters on Thursday night set fire to the offices of the Prothom Alo and the Daily Star in the capital following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi at a hospital in Singapore. Witnesses said that a group of people came from the capital’s Shahbagh area and forcibly entered the Prothom Alo office at Karwanbazar, chanting slogans against the Bangla daily and India. Hundreds of demonstrators reached the Prothom Alo office at about 11:00pm and cordoned off the building. They then vandalised inside the building in the absence of law enforcement agencies. Enraged protesters vandalized the office premises, throwing papers and computers onto the floor and setting them on fire. Though the workers at Karwanbazar had been requesting to work to put out the fire at about 1:15am on Friady, the protesters were not allowing them to do so, witnesses said. After attacking the Prothom Alo building, angry protesters moved to the office of The Daily Star near Farmgate at about 12:15am on Friday. The protesters vandalised glass panels, dragged out chairs, tables, and papers, and set them on fire while chanting slogans including ‘Naray-e-Takbir’, ‘Allahu Akbar’, ‘Bharoter Dalalera-Hushiar, Sabdhan’. Several employees reported at about 12:45am that they became trapped on the roof of the Daily Star building. The army arrived at the Daily Star office at about 12:35am to control the situation. Two units of firefighters reached the spot, Anwarul Islam, warehouse inspector at the Fire Service and Civil Defence headquarters media cell, told New Age at about 1:00am on Friday. ‘We will need support from the law enforcers to go inside to work to put out the fire as huge number of agitated crowd took position there,’ he said. A reporter of The Daily Star said at 1:00am that the residents of the nearby buildings were trying to rescue them from the building.

title: State mourning Saturday over Osman Hadi’s death: chief adviser
body: Bangladesh’s interim government chief adviser Muhammad Yunus on Thursday night announced a one-day state mourning on Saturday following the death of Sharif Osman Hadi, convener of Inqilab Mancha. He made the announcement in a televised address to the nation. Osman Hadi passed away Thursday night while undergoing treatment at a Singapore hospital after fighting for his life for six days. ‘Today, I came before you with very heartbreaking news. Sharif Osman Hadi, the fearless frontline fighter of the July Uprising and spokesperson of the Inqilab Mancha, is no more among us. Singapore’s Foreign Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan informed the matter over phone a few minutes ago,’ the chief adviser said while addressing the nation. ‘May the Almighty Allah accept this immortal soldier of the struggle against fascism and hegemony as a martyr. We all pray this together,’ said the chief adviser. State-owned Bangladesh Television and BTV News simultaneously broadcast the speech at 11:30 pm. Hadi, also an aspiring independent candidate for Dhaka-8, was shot on December 12 while he was on a battery-run auto-rickshaw in the city’s Paltan area.

title: Shahbagh blocked over Hadi’s death
body: Traffic came to a standstill at Shahbagh Thursday night as leaders and activists of Inqilab Mancha, along with Dhaka University students, began gathering around 10:30pm to mourn the death of Sharif Osman Hadi. Osman Hadi, the fiery face of the July Uprising, convener of Inqilab Mancha and a prospective candidate for the upcoming 13th national parliamentary election, died on Thursday while receiving medical treatment in Singapore. Hadi was critically injured on December 12 when assailants opened fire on him while he was traveling in a rickshaw near the water tank in Bijoynagar, Dhaka. Two individuals on a motorcycle approached his rickshaw, and one of them shot him at close range before fleeing the scene. He was initially taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital and later transferred to Evercare Hospital for advanced ICU care, where he succumbed to his injuries

title: Bangladesh July uprising leader Hadi dies from bullet wounds in Singapore
body: Gunshot-injured Sharif Osman Hadi, the convener of the Inquilab Mancha and one of the organisers of the July uprising, breathed his last under treatment in Singapore at around 9:30pm Bangladesh time. Inquilab Mancha member-secretary Abdullah Al Jaber confirmed his death to New Age at around 10:15pm. ‘We have come to know over telephone from his elder brother Omar, who is accompanying Hadi in Singapore, that Osman Hadi passed away at around 9:30pm,’ Jaber said, adding that the doctors could not conduct his surgery due his unstable condition. Later, at 11:20pm, interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus in an address to the nation expressed deep condolences over the death of Hadi. He announced national mourning for Saturday and called upon the country’s people to have patience and stay calm. As the news of Hadi’s death spread, people, including students and July uprising fighters, held protests in Dhaka and other places across the country. Osman Hadi, who was very vocal against Indian hegemony and an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency in the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad polls, was shot in the head on December 12 in the city. Earlier in the day, the family of critically injured Hadi, has approved his surgery in Singapore as his health condition remained ‘very critical’. Different orginsations and political parties, including the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, National Citizen Party, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, and Islami Andolan Bangladesh, expressed deep condolences over the death of the young politician. Meanwhile, police in their petition for remand of Sivion Dio and Sanjay Chisim, who help people to cross the border illegally, said that the duo helped prime accused Faisal Karim Masud and his associates to flee the country to India. The police found evidence on the basis of interrogation and technological suppor that Faisal and his associates had fled to India with the support of Sivion and Sanjay, the petition said. Besides, protests at the assassination attempt on Hadi continued on Thursday demanding the immediate arrest of the perpetrators and the resignation of home adviser retired Lieutenant General Jahangir Alam Chowdhury for the failure to arrest them yet. Referring to Hadi’s family, the Inquilab Mancha in a Facebook post on Thursday afternoon said that the family had granted permission for a surgery on Hadi to be carried out in Singapore. It described Hadi’s present health condition as being in between life and death. The interim government’s advisory council on Thursday discussed Hadi’s health condition at its meeting, said a press release shared by the chief adviser’s press wing, saying that Hadi’s condition remained extremely critical. Regarding Hadi’s situation, Singapore foreign minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan has been in regular contact with chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus, providing updates, it said. ‘A senior official of Bangladesh foreign ministry arrived in Singapore yesterday (Wednesday). The official is directly overseeing Hadi’s medical treatment,’ said the press release. Jatiya Chhatrashakti, the student wing of the National Citizen Party, held a protest rally at Shahbagh in the capital demanding immediate arrest of the perpetrators and resignation of the home adviser for alleged failure to arrest them yet. The student body’s president Zahid Ahsan said, ‘The assailants in the shooting on Hadi must be arrested immediately.’ He alleged that home adviser Jahangir was still in the position despite his long failure to maintain the law and order as a vested group wanted to take advantage of the situation during the forthcoming national elections. The protesters also burnt an effigy of the home adviser after the protest rally. Meanwhile, the Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch on Thursday afternoon produced Sivion Dio and Sanjay Chisim before a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court that allowed the police to take them in custody for three days each for interrogation in Hadi’s attempted murder case, reported New Age Court Correspondent. The remand petition also alleged that Sivion was a relative of a local activist of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, and involved in helping people to cross the border illegally. It appealed the court to grant seven-day remand each to interrogate them to ascertain whose plan and advice led the assailants to cross the border. In addition, remand is necessary to identify the people who planned the attack on Hadi and other people involved, to recover the weapons used in the assassination attempt, to identify the planners, financiers and accomplices of the attack, the petition said. Critically injured Hadi was airlifted to Singapore from Dhaka for advanced medical treatment on Monday. He is undergoing treatment at the Singapore General Hospital while the Inquilab Mancha sought prayers from the public for his recovery. The platform also called on his supporters across Bangladesh to gather at Shahbagh demanding justice if Hadi dies. It also warned that protesters would continue their sit-in at Shahbagh until those responsible for the attack were arrested. The Inquilab Mancha also threatened to bring the country to a standstill if the assailants were not arrested. Additionally, the platform’s statement asserted that if the accused had fled to India, the Bangladesh government should discuss with Indian authorities to ensure the assailants’ arrest and repatriation. Law enforcers have so far arrested at least 10 people for their suspected involvement in the December 12 attack on aspiring independent candidate Hadi in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad election for the Dhaka-8 constituency. It is believed that the main identified assailants, Alamgir Sheikh, the motorcycle rider, and the pillion of the motorcycle, Faisal Karim Masud, the suspected shooter, who took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for a few days, fled to India illegally through the Haluaghat border in Mymensingh. On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head in the Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026.

title: Asif Nazrul meets CJ, raises concern over ‘abnormal’ bail orders
body: Interim government law adviser Asif Nazrul on Thursday said that he raised concerns with chief justice Syed Refaat Ahmed over what he described as ‘abnormal’ bail orders granted by some High Court benches. He made the remarks after meeting the outgoing chief justice at his office in the afternoon. Justice Refaat Ahmed will retire on December 27 and December 18 was his last court appearance before his retirement. Asif Nazrul also said that the name of the next chief justice might be known within three or four days, adding that the appointment was a policy decision of the government and not within his jurisdiction. The adviser said that the chief justice had responded to his concerns and had called judges of benches that were granting a large number of bail orders in a short time. ‘I raised this issue publicly and also directly with the chief justice whenever I met him. He took action,’ he said. He said that although the tendency to grant such bail orders had declined slightly, the practice had not stopped. The law adviser said that granting bail to ‘dangerous persons’ created fear, particularly when such accused later threatened people involved in the July mass uprising. ‘We feel frightened and concerned when this kind of bail is granted,’ he said. The law ministry has no control on the High Court and it should not have any such control, as judicial independence must be preserved, Asif Nazrul said. He said that the chief justice, as guardian of the High Court Division, was the appropriate authority to be informed of such concerns. ‘I reiterated my concerns today to the outgoing chief justice and will raise the issue again at my first meeting with his successor,’ he said. He said that granting bail to followers of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who he claimed was continuing to issue threats while staying in India, was inconsistent with bail rules and the existing laws. If a judge grants bail to an individual who poses a serious risk and that person later commits murder, the issue of judicial responsibility should be examined, Asif Nazrul said. ‘I regret having to say this, but the situation has reached such a point. We must speak out to protect the lives of our children,’ he said. Judges must grant bail where it is legally justified, but bail should not be granted if there is a clear risk that the accused may commit violence after release, he added.

title: Govt appoints 673 ‘deprived’ candidates from 27th BCS
body: Bangladesh interim government has appointed 673 candidates who were ‘deprived’ in the 27th Bangladesh Civil Service examination to various cadres of the Bangladesh Civil Service as per a court verdict. The Public Administration Ministry issued a gazette notificationon Thursday following recommendations from the Bangladesh Public Service Commission. The newly appointed officers have been asked to join their respective offices designated by the cadre-controlling ministries or divisions by January 1, said the notification. If no further instructions are received from the cadre-controlling ministry or division, the appointees are required to join on that date. The gazette also said that failure to join on the stipulated date will be considered as unwillingness to accept the appointment and the appointment letter will be deemed cancelled.

title: Police stop marches towards Indian missions in Rajshahi, Khulna
body: The police on Thursday stopped anti-India marches of groups of youths, mostly July protesters, towards the Indian Assistant High Commission offices in Rajshahi and Khulan cities. The youths, under the banner of July-36 Mancha, began the march in the Rajshahi city, demanding the extradition of the ousted prime minister and Awami League president Sheikh Hasina and others allegedly involved in crimes against humanity during the July uprising, New Age staff correspondent in the district reported. Another group of people under the banner of ‘Adhipatyabad Birodhi Jote’ (Anti-Hegemony Alliance) marched towards the Indian Assistant High Commission office in the Sonadanga area in Khulna city at about 3:30pm on Thursday, the police said. The police, however, said that they had barred the protesters on their way to the mission office. In Rajshahi, the protesters began their march at about 12:30pm from Bhadra Mor, but the police stopped them by erecting barricades about 100 metres ahead of the Indian Assistant High Commission. The protesters, after being obstructed, waited there for about 15 minutes for permission to go ahead. As they were not permitted, they attempted to move forward. This triggered a brief scuffle between the police and the demonstrators there. The protesters then staged a sit-in in front of the barricade for more than an hour. During that time, law enforcement agencies restricted access to the road adjacent to the assistant high commission. Addressing the sit-in, participant Miftahul Jannat Biva alleged that India was sheltering fugitives accused of criminal cases. She said that they organised the programme in protest against ‘India’s role in harbouring them’. She placed three demands: the repatriation of fugitive ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and all others now sheltered in India, withdrawal or suspension of activities of the Indian High Commission in Bangladesh if Hasina and others were not repatriated, and accountability for police assault on demonstrators during their march. National Citizen Party’s Rajshahi district unit former organising secretary Iffat Uddin Abir, Jatiya Juba Shakti organiser Hazrat Anas, former Rajshahi city unit joint member-secretary Soaib Ahmed, and July uprising participant Abu Raihan, among others, took part in the sit-in. Later, the demonstrators handed a written statement outlining their demands to Rajshahi Metropolitan Police’s Boalia zone deputy commissioner Golam Rabbani Sheikh. Khulna Metropolitan Police’s deputy commissioner for South, Tajul Islam, told New Age that the law enforcers, including the police and the army, had set up multiple layers of barricades for security purposes surrounding the office. ‘After breaking the first barricade, the protesters gathered near the courthouse and chanted slogans. They were unable to cross the second barricade and there was no serious confrontation,’ he said. The protester left the place after staying for a while, he added. On Wednesday, several thousand people marched towards the Indian High Commission in the capital’s Baridhara area, demanding the extradition of Sheikh Hasina and others allegedly involved in crimes against humanity during the July uprising.

title: Tarique to land in Dhaka at around 12:00pm on Dec 25
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman would arrive in Dhaka on December 25 on a regular commercial flight of Biman Bangladesh Airlines, with the aircraft expected to land at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport around 12:00pm. The BNP standing committee member, Salahuddin Ahmed, made the announcement on Thursday while speaking to reporters at the BNP chairperson’s office in Gulshan. He said that the party wanted to make Tarique Rahman’s return a historic occasion that would surpass political precedents of the past 55 years and remain unmatched in the decades ahead. Salahuddin said that BNP was assessing possible venues for receptions, saying that people across Bangladesh were eager to see Tarique and hear him speak, and that party leaders were visiting locations to determine where large crowds could be accommodated with minimal public inconvenience. He said that instructions had been issued to BNP leaders and activists at district, upazila and union levels, as well as leaders of its affiliated bodies, to arrive in Dhaka by the night of December 24 or the morning of December 25 to welcome their leader. Salahuddin said that BNP leaders have carried out on-the-ground inspections of arrangements at the airport, including where Tarique would disembark and how he would proceed by vehicle. Routes for Tarique’s travel to the hospital, residence and other planned programmes are also being reviewed in coordination with the relevant authorities, he said. Salahuddin also said that security arrangements were being coordinated separately with concerned government agencies. Tarique Rahman, the eldest son of BNP chairperson and former prime minister Khaleda Zia, had previously been sentenced in several cases, including a life term, and faced numerous other charges, most of which were filed during the 2007–08 military-backed caretaker government. He was arrested during an anti-corruption drive in March 2007 and released on bail in September 2008, after which he travelled to London for medical treatment on September 11, 2008, and remained there. Following the fall of the Awami League’s 16-year rule in a mass uprising on August 5, 2024, the High Court acquitted him of all cases filed during both the caretaker government period and the Awami League administration, clearing the legal obstacles to his return. BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir announced at a press conference on Friday at the party chairperson’s Gulshan office in the capital, Dhaka, that Tarique Rahman is scheduled to return to Bangladesh on December 25. BNP has already formed a committee to organise the reception, with Salahuddin Ahmed as its chair and senior joint secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi as member secretary. Rizvi told reporters that organisational preparations were progressing as planned and expressed confidence that the gathering would be historic.

title: Hadi’s condition remains ‘very critical’, family approves surgery in Singapore
body: The family of gunshot injured Sharif Osman Hadi, the convener of Inquilab Mancha, has approved his surgery in Singapore as his health condition remained ‘very critical’. The Inquilab Mancha in a Facebook post on Thursday afternoon described Hadi’s present health condition as being on the brink between life and death. Referring to Hadi’s family, it said that the family had granted permission for an operation to be carried out in Singapore. Critically injured Hadi was shifted to Singapore from Dhaka by an air ambulance for advanced medical treatment on Monday. He is undergoing treatment at the Singapore General Hospital and Hadi’s platform has sought prayers from the public for his recovery. The platform also called for supporters across Bangladesh to gather at Shahbagh demanding justice if Hadi dies. It also warned that protesters would continue their sit-in at Shahbagh until those responsible for the attack were arrested. Inquilab Mancha also threatened the authorities concerned to bring the country to a standstill if the assailants were not arrested. Additionally, the statement asserted that if the accused flee to India, Bangladesh government should discuss with Indian authorities to ensure the assailants’ arrest and repatriation by any means. The law enforcers have arrested at least 10 people for their suspected involvement in the attack on Hadi, aspiring independent candidate in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad election for the Dhaka-8 constituency, on December 12. It is believed that the main identified assailants, Alamgir Sheikh, the motorcycle rider, and the pillion of the motorcycle, Faisal Karim Masud, the suspected shooter, who took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for a few days, fled to India illegally through the Haluaghat border in Mymensingh. On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head in Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. CCTV footage showed that Hadi was heading towards Bijoynagar by an auto-rickshaw when the two men, wearing helmets on a motorcycle, opened fire on him on the Box Culvert Road before fleeing the scene. The assailants also took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for the past few days wearing face masks and also on the day of the incident. Physicians said that Hadi was seriously injured as a bullet pierced his head above the right ear, causing significant brain damage.

title: Farmer crushed under excavator for opposing cropland digging in Rajshahi
body: A young man was run over by an excavator while protesting against illegal pond excavation on arable land at Mohonpur upazila in Rajshahi on Wednesday night. The deceased was identified as Ahmed Jubayer, 22, son of Rafiqul Islam of Baro Palsha village under Dhurail union. Police detained the excavator driver, Abdul Hamid, a resident of Tangail district, from the scene immediately. Local people said that the land at Poob (East) Beel in Baro Palsha village is entirely a cropland and that no commercial ponds had previously been excavated there. They alleged that an attempt was made to secretly dig a pond on the land with an excavator on Wednesday night. Joynal Abedin, a farmer of Baro Palsha village, told New Age that villagers opposed pond excavation on cropland as it would create waterlogging in the beel and damage crops. ‘We are mostly marginal and small-scale farmers. Some of us own just five decimals which we cultivate for paddy. If ponds are excavated in the middle of the beel, it will cause waterlogging in surrounding fields and disrupt cultivation,’ he said. Upon learning about the excavation, local mosque’s muezzin Abdul Mannan announced the matter over the loudspeaker, prompting villagers to rush to the fields. Witnesses said that initially seven to eight people, including Jubayer, protested against the excavation. At one point, the excavator driver allegedly began rotating the machine’s bucket rapidly, hitting Jubayer and knocking him to the ground. As the driver attempted to flee, he allegedly drove the excavator over Jubayer’s body, killing him on the spot. Following the incident, more than a hundred villagers gathered at the site, detained the driver, and set fire to the excavator, locals said. The villagers also set fire to a motorcycle belonging to the alleged organiser of the pond excavation, Anisuzzaman Bokul, assistant general secretary of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party’s Dhurail union, who had arrived at the scene. However, Anisuzzaman could not be reached for his comment over phone despite repeated attempts. Jubayer’s wife Nusrat Jahan Mohona Akter Jui said that they were married recently and did not have any child. ‘My husband was killed after an excavator ran over him. I want justice,’ she said while crying. Former Dhurail union parishad chairman and former Mohanpur upazila BNP organising secretary Kazim Uddin Sarkar, who visited the spot, said that Anisuzzaman was involved in the excavation. He alleged that although Anisuzzaman held a position in the BNP union committee, he previously supported the Awami League and was now allegedly abusing political influence to lead pond excavation on cropland. ‘Whoever is involved in this incident must be brought to justice through a proper investigation,’ Kazim added. SM Moinuddin, officer-in-charge of Mohonpur police station, told New Age that none had informed them earlier about the pond digging in the beel. He said that the father of the deceased filed a murder case with the police station against six named and 10 to 15 unnamed people in connection with the incident. According to the Rajshahi district fisheries office, the number of ponds in the district increased from 40,788 in 2015 to 51,275 in 2025, marking a 25 per cent rise in a decade. However, local residents claimed that the actual number of ponds excavated during this period would be more than three times the official figure.

title: Foreign diplomats briefed on polls preparations
body: The Bangladesh foreign ministry on Thursday briefed foreign diplomats stationed in Dhaka about the interim government’s preparations for the upcoming Jatiya Sangsan polls and the referendum slated for February 12 next year and the overall security situation. The envoys were informed that the country’s law enforcement agencies, including the armed forces, had remained vigilant and were actively working to maintain the law and order, according to officials concerned. Foreign secretary Asad Alam Siam held the briefing for the heads of diplomatic missions and the United Nations Resident Coordinator Office in Dhaka at the state guest house Padma in the city, where he assured them of their security before and during the polls, the officials confirmed. ‘The Ministry of Foreign Affairs held a briefing for diplomats at the State Guest House Padma this afternoon to inform foreign missions in Dhaka about the updated preparations and security measures taken in connection with the upcoming 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections and the referendum,’ said a foreign ministry statement issued later on the day. In the briefing, the diplomats were informed that the Election Commission would welcome foreign election observers and also told them that they were invited to send election observers for the February elections. The foreign ministry initiated the move amid security concerns expressed by various political parties after the recent shooting of Sharif Osman Hadi, an aspiring independent candidate for Dhaka-8 constituency and one of the July uprising organisers, who is now under treatment in a critical condition in a Singapore hospital. About 40 diplomats from the embassies of different countries, including the United Kingdom, Australia, Germany, Russia, China, India, Pakistan, the United Arab Emirates, and Malaysia and the UNRCO in Dhaka attended the briefing that lasted for around 20 minutes. The foreign ministry invited all heads of diplomatic missions and the UN Resident Coordinator Office to attend the briefing session. The security concerns came up further when a group under the banner of ‘July Oikya’ (July Unity) marched to the Indian High Commission in the city on Wednesday, demanding the extradition of fugitive ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and others convicted or allegedly involved in crimes against humanity during the July uprising and return of the prime suspect, Faisal Karim Masud, in the shooting of Hadia, who is also believed to have fled to India. The interim government led by Professor Muhammad Yunus took over on August 8, 2024 after the fall of the authoritarian regime of Sheikh Hasina amid the student-led mass uprising on August 5.

title: SC corrected AL-era rulings for judicial independence, says CJ
body: The Supreme Court has corrected constitutional deviations by overturning its past rulings delivered during the ousted Awami League regime, chief justice Syed Refaat Ahmed said on Thursday. He also said that those rulings had weakened judicial independence, including the abolition of the provision for the Supreme Judicial Council and the introduction of other distortions under the 15th and 13th amendments. The chief justice was speaking at a felicitation programme in his courtroom on his last working day ahead of his retirement on December 28. He said that the judiciary remained the only fully functional constitutional organ during the past turbulent period and acted within constitutional limits to protect fundamental rights and institutional autonomy. The July revolution, he further said, was not intended to overturn the constitution but to restore integrity, transparency and accountability in constitutional governance. The Supreme Court has, for the first time, operationalised a judicial appointment collegium to ensure transparency, consultations and accountability in judicial appointments, he observed. The judiciary, he went on to say, adopted a reform roadmap focused on transparency, accountability and responsiveness, ensuring that no right was undermined and no institution became captive. According to the chief justice, recent judicial roadshows across the country demonstrated renewed commitment among judges and lawyers to safeguard the judiciary’s constitutional role and independence. He acknowledged the role of the Supreme Court Bar Association in advancing judicial independence, particularly through the Masdar Hossain case, thanking lawyers for supporting the demand for a separate judicial secretariat. Steps are under way to introduce structural reforms, regularise judicial service careers and establish a Supreme Court Secretariat through an ordinance to ensure full administrative autonomy of the judiciary, he said The chief justice said that lawyers, journalists, and politicians played a crucial role in shaping the nation, warning that a lack of professional ethics weakened the rule of law. He stressed the role of the Bangladesh Bar Council in strengthening legal ethics and suggested including justice and professional responsibility in bar examinations. He also urged law faculties to introduce courses and clinical programmes on access to justice, legal aid, and community-based legal services. The chief justice said that the strength of the judiciary lay in collective integrity and commitment to justice, not in any single office.

title: ICT starts trial of Hasina, Tarique Siddique, 11 DGFI officers over enforced disappearances
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Thursday framed charges against deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former defence adviser retired major general Tarique Ahmed Siddique, and 11 other serving and retired army officials for their alleged involvement in committing crimes against humanity, including abduction, detention and torture of people with dissenting views against the Awami League. The three-member tribunal, headed by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder, framed charges against them after rejecting discharge petitions filed by the accused and set January 19 for the commencement of their trial through recording depositions of prosecution witnesses. Besides Hasina and Tarique Siddique, the other accused are serving Major Generals Sheikh Md Sarwar Hossain and Kabir Ahmed, and Brigadier Generals Mahbub Rahman Siddique and Ahmed Tanvir Mazhar Siddique, and retired army officers lieutenant general Md Akbar Hossain (former DGFI director general), major general Md Saiful Abedin (former DGFI DG), lieutenant general Md Saiful Alam (former DGFI DG), lieutenant general Ahmed Tabrez Shams Chowdhury (former DGFI DG), major general Hamidul Huq (former DGFI DG), major general Mohammad Towhidul-Ul Islam (former DGFI director) and lieutenant colonel Mokhsurul Haq. Three of the serving officers, Sheikh Md Sarwar Hossain, Mahbub Rahman Siddique and Ahmed Tanvir Mazhar Siddique, are now detained and were produced before the tribunal. They were brought to the tribunal from the sub jail inside the Dhaka Cantonment amid tight security in an air-conditioned prison bus. Sheikh Hasina, Tarique Siddique, serving army officer Kabir Ahmed and seven other retired army officers are still in hiding and will be tried in absentia. The prosecution alleged that the crimes were committed at the Joint Interrogation Cell of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence inside Dhaka Cantonment. According to the charges, 26 people, including former Jamaat chief Ghulam Azam’s son and former brigadier general Abdullahil Amaan Azmi, Chittagong Hill Tracts-based UPDF leader Michael Chakma and executed BNP leader Salahuddin Quader Chowdhury’s son Hummam Quader Chowdhury, were forcibly disappeared, abducted, tortured and illegally detained at the JIC between July 2, 2017 and March 4, 2020. Earlier, chief prosecutor Muhammad Tajul Islam read out excerpts from the 81-page charge sheet against the 13 accused and urged the tribunal to frame charges against them for their superior command responsibility. The prosecution said that the five former DGFI directors general were placed on forced retirement after the fall of the Hasina-led Awami League regime on August 5, 2024 amid a student-led mass uprising. The JIC case is the second enforced disappearance case linked to the Joint Interrogation Cell at the DGFI’s secret detention facility during the Awami League regime. The ICT-1 is scheduled for December 21 to pass its order on charges of crimes against humanity against 17 accused allegedly involved in the second phase of abduction, detention and torture of people with dissenting views against the Awami League at the Task Force for Interrogation Cell run by the Rapid Action Battalion. Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman, Tarique Ahmed Siddique, and 14 former Rapid Action Battalion officers, including 11 army officers deputed to the RAB-1 and the three police officers deputed to RAB as directors general, are accused in the case.

title: Unidentified arsonists set fire to Grameen Bank office in Feni
body: Unidentified arsonists set fire to Grameen Bank office at Sharshadi Bazar in Feni Sadar upazila on early Thursday. The fire damaged three motorbikes and furniture on the office premises. Police said that the attackers poured petrol from outside the main gate and ignited the fire at about 3:30am. Seeing the fire at the stairway, the security guards started screaming seeking help. Hearing this, some officials who live at the second floor of the same building informed fire service personnel who later brought the fire under control. Branch manager Ashok Kumar Debnath said that the miscreants had jumped off the boundary wall to enter the premises before setting fire to the gate area. Local people initially helped to control the fire before firefighters arrived, he said. Feni Model Police Station inspector (investigation) Sajal Kanti Dash said police visited the spot after receiving information. The bank authorities lodged a complaint in this regard and action would be taken accordingly, he added.

title: Khaleda’s condition unchanged
body: The health condition of Bangladesh Nationalist Party chair and former prime minister Khaleda Zia remained stable as she continued to receive treatment in a critical care unit, her personal physician AZM Zahid Hossain said on Thursday. Speaking to reporters outside Evercare Hospital on Thursday, Zahid said that the BNP chair was currently able to receive medical treatment as advised by a medical board comprising doctors from the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Bangladesh. ‘She is responding well to the treatment being administered in line with the recommendations of the doctors. Her physical condition has remained the same as it was a few days ago,’ he said. Zahid said that the medical team and all those involved in her care remained hopeful of her recovery. ‘We are optimistic that BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia will make a gradual recovery,’ he said. Earlier, on December 11, the medical board stated that she continued to receive intensive treatment in the ICU, with all necessary medical interventions being administered at the highest standard appropriate for her critical condition. According to the board, her kidney function has deteriorated, requiring regular dialysis. Complications from digestive tract bleeding have necessitated multiple blood transfusions while she continues to suffer from persistent fever. In a statement issued on behalf of the medical board on Thursday, Professor Dr Shahabuddin Talukdar said that Khaleda Zia’s oxygen levels had fallen and carbon dioxide levels had risen, requiring support through high-flow nasal cannula and BiPAP machines. As her condition did not improve she was placed on elective ventilator support to rest her lungs and other organs, the statement said. Khaleda was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis on November 27, which remains under intensive management, the December 11 update said. The board also reported that she was battling severe bacterial and fungal infections, requiring advanced antibiotic and antifungal therapy. Her kidney failure has also made regular dialysis essential. The 79-year old leader, who has long been suffering from multiple chronic health complications, including liver and kidney diseases, heart ailments, hypertension, diabetes, arthritis and recurrent infections, was admitted to Evercare Hospital on November 23. On December 10, Zahid said that her ongoing treatment was consistent with standard medical protocols, adding that she had been responding to the interventions. He said that the medical board had decided on December 5 to transfer her abroad for further treatment, but technical difficulties with the air ambulance and concerns over her fitness to fly prevented her transfer. The medical board continues to monitor her condition closely.

title: NCP leader found hanging in her room at Hazaribagh hostel
body: The police recovered the hanging body of a leader of the National Citizen Party from a female students’ hostel at Hazaribagh in the capital city Dhaka on Thursday. The deceased, Jannat Ara Rumi, 30, was the joint coordinator of the NCP’s Dhanmondi thana unit and daughter of Md Zakir Hossain from Nazirpur area under Patnitala upazila in Naogaon, according to the police officials. Being informed in the morning, the police recovered the hanging body from a room on the fifth floor of Jannati Girls Hostel on Jhigatala’s Old Kachabazar Road, said Hazaribagh police station’s officer-in-charge Hafizur Rahman. The room, where Rumi used to live alone, was found locked from inside, he said. ‘The body was sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for post-mortem examinations. It is yet unclear whether the death was a suicide or homicide,’ he added. Abdul Ahad, member secretary of National Health Alliance, backed by the National Citizen Party, told reporters in front of DMCH in the afternoon that Rumi’s body was handed over to the family after the necessary examination. Rumi died five days after she had filed a general diary with Dhanmondi police station on December 13, alleging that they were receiving death threats, Ahad said, adding that real cause of the death would be known after the autopsy report. ‘We have noticed an increase in cases of unnatural deaths of the July Uprising heroes. They had been getting continuous threats from unknown sources,’ he said. During the media briefing, Samantha Sharmin, senior joint convener of the NCP, alleged that no adequate action was taken to ensure safety and security of the ‘July Warriors’

title: 483 people killed in 534 road accidents across Bangladesh in Nov: RSF
body: As many as 483 people, including 64 women and 71 children, were killed and 1,317 others were injured in 534 road accidents across the country in November, according to a report of Road Safety Foundation. Like October, Dhaka division recorded the highest number of accidents at 141, resulting in 119 deaths, the RSF report released on Thursday said. The report noted that the number of fatalities and accidents rose compared to October, increasing by 42 deaths and 48 accidents respectively. The RSF prepared the report based on the reports of nine national dailies, seven online news portals and electronic media. Among the deceased, 194 people died in 227 motorbike accidents, accounting for 40.16 per cent of total fatalities and it is 57 fewer than in the previous month. The deceased also included 106 pedestrians, 57 drivers and their assistants. Besides, six waterways accidents claimed at least seven lives with five missing. Besides, 38 people were killed and nine others injured in 47 accidents involving trains across Bangladesh last month. Of the total accidents, 131 accidents occurred on the national highways, 245 on regional roads, 82 on rural roads and 71 on city roads, said the report. According to the report, 26.40 per cent accidents occurred in Dhaka division, 16.10 per cent in Rajshahi, 20.97 per cent in Chattogram, 12.17 per cent in Khulna, 6.36 per cent in Barishal, 5.61 per cent in Sylhet, 7.11 per cent in Rangpur and 5.24 per cent in Mymensingh division. Sylhet division saw 30 accidents with lowest 24 deaths during the same period, said the report. The RSF identified several key factors behind the rise in road accidents including faulty vehicles, reckless driving, drivers’ incompetence or illness, unsettled wages and working hours, low-speed traffic on highways, risky motorcycling by youth, frequent violation of traffic rules, poor traffic management, inefficiency of the BRTA, and extortion in the transport sector. The RSF urged the concerned authorities to take necessary measures to improve road safety across the country.

title: Another Bangladeshi peacekeeper wounded in drone attack in Sudan
body: Another Bangladeshi peacekeeper has been injured in a drone attack by separatist forces in Sudan, raising the total number of wounded Bangladesh Army personnel serving in the UN mission to nine. According to a media release from the Inter-Services Public Relations, eight Bangladeshi peacekeepers were initially injured when a United Nations mission camp in the Abei area of Sudan came under a drone strike. Later, reports confirmed that another soldier was wounded in the attack, bringing the total number of injured to nine. The injured personnel are receiving treatment at Aga Khan University Hospital in Nairobi, Kenya. One of them has already been discharged, while the remaining peacekeepers are reported to be out of danger, the ISPR said. Meanwhile, the bodies of six Bangladeshi peacekeepers killed in the December 13 drone attack on the Kadugli logistics base under the UN mission will be sent to Dhaka on December 20. State honour will be accorded during their funeral rites, added the release issued on Wednesday. The Bangladesh Army continues to closely monitor the situation to ensure the safety and welfare of its peacekeepers deployed in Sudan.

title: Indian visa centre in Dhaka now operational, functioning as normal
body: After assessing the security situation on Thursday morning, Indian Visa Application Centre in Dhaka is now operational and functioning as normal. ‘We do understand the difficulties faced by applicants,’ said an official. Based on evolving security situation, there will be a reassessment on IVAC operations, the official said. Visa services at other IVACs in Bangladesh are also being reviewed in light of the prevailing security situations. Due to security situation, IVAC JFP Dhaka was closed at 2:00pm on Wednesday, said a notification issued by the IVAC in Dhaka. All applicants who have appointment slots booked for submission on Wednesday will be given a slot accordingly. The Indian Visa Application Centre at Jamuna Future Park in Dhaka is the main, integrated centre for all Indian visa services in the capital.

title: Dhaka’s air still in ‘unhealthy zone’ with AQI score of 166
body: Dhaka, the overcrowded capital city of Bangladesh, has ranked 10th on the list of cities with the worst air quality with an AQI score of 166 at about 9:50am on Thursday morning. On Thursday, Dhaka’s air was classified as ‘unhealthy’ referring to a healthy threat, according to the AQI index. Such unhealthy air quality continued for the past few days. When the AQI value for particle pollution is between 50 and 100, air quality is considered ‘moderate’, usually sensitive individuals should consider limiting prolonged outdoor exertion, between 101 and 150, air quality is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, between 150 and 200 is ‘unhealthy’, between 201 and 300 is said to be ‘very unhealthy’, while a reading of 301 and above is considered ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks to residents. Egypt’s Cairo, Pakistan’s Lahore and India’s Delhi cities respectively occupied the first, second and third spots on the list, with AQI scores of 293, 284, and 280 respectively. The AQI, an index for reporting daily air quality, informs people how clean or polluted the air of a certain city is and what associated health effects might be a concern for them. The AQI in Bangladesh is based on five pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), NO2, CO, SO2, and ozone. Dhaka has long been grappling with air pollution issues. Its air quality usually turns unhealthy in winter and improves during the monsoon. As per World Health Organisation, air pollution kills an estimated seven million people worldwide every year, mainly due to increased mortality from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.

title: Six killed in road accidents
body: At least six people were killed in road accidents at different places in the country on Wednesday night and Thursday. An elderly man was killed in a road accident in Cinema Hall area under Chilmari upazila of Kurigram district on Thursday. On Wednesday night, at least five people were killed and four others were injured in road accidents in Dinajpur and Sylhet districts. In Thursday’s incident, the deceased is identified as Nasim Uddin Dewani, 70, a resident of Samajpara village under Thanahat union of the upazila, reports the Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha. The accident occurred at about 9:00am on the Bajragami road when a tractor ran over Nasim while he was crossing the road. He died on the spot, Chilmari police station officer-in-charge Alamgir Hossain said. The BSS also reported that three people were killed and two were injured in separate road accidents in Dinajpur on Wednesday night. The deceased are identified as Anisur Rahman, 55, Tarini Barman, 35, and his wife Iti Barman, 28. Anisur, a local Jamaat leader, died on the spot when a truck hit his motorcycle from behind at about 10:30pm near Lakshmitola Bazar of Sadar upazila on the Dinajpur-Phulbari regional highway. Two pedestrians were injured and admitted to Dinajpur Medical College Hospital. The police seized the truck, while its driver and his assistant fled. Dinajpur kotwali police station officer-in-charge inspector Md Nurun Nabi confirmed the incidents. In another accident, motorcycle rider Tarini and his wife Iti were killed in a head-on collision with a tractor at about 9:00pm at Komorpur Bottola crossing on the Dinajpur-Panchagarh highway at Birganj upazila. Tarini died on the spot, while his wife succumbed to her injuries at Dinajpur Medical College Hospital later at night. Confirming the news, Birganj police station officer-in-charge inspector Md Saiful Islam said that legal action was under way in connection with both accidents. Two people were killed and two others injured in a collision between two motorcycles on the Sylhet-Zakiganj road at Golapganj upazila of Sylhet district at about 11:30pm on Wednesday, BSS reports. The deceased are identified as Abdul Ahad, 42, and Sabbir Ahmad, 21, of Goashpur and Ranaping Chatrish villages respectively under the Golapganj upazila. Golapganj model police station officer-in-charge Md Ariful Islam said that the motorbikes collided in Termail area, leaving one dead on the spot. The injured three was rushed to Sylhet Osmani Medical College Hospital where physicians declared another as dead, he said, adding that the remaining two was receiving treatment.

title: Bangladesh
body: ISD celebrates Victory Day International School Dhaka has observed the 55th Victory Day of Bangladesh with an assembly that brought the whole school community together to honour the country’s rich history and the sacrifices of the martyrs. International School Dhaka has observed the 55th Victory Day of Bangladesh with an assembly that brought the whole school community together to honour the country’s rich history and the sacrifices of the martyrs. A juice vendor was stabbed to death during an Islamic gathering organised by the Darul Aman Trust at Pabna Sadar in the district on Wednesday. The notification for filling the form for the secondary school certificate examination of 2026 has been published under the Dhaka education board. Nearly two-thirds of child labourers in Bangladesh are employed in industrial and factory settings, exposing them to serious health and safety risks, a report said on Wednesday. Speakers at a meeting in Rajshahi on Thursday called for integrated efforts of all government and non-government organisations concerned for the welfare of the elderly and people with disabilities. Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chair Tarique Rahman is scheduled to arrive in Dhaka on December 25 on a regular commercial flight of Biman Bangladesh Airlines. Several leaders of the Ganatantra Mancha on Thursday expressed dissatisfaction following a seat-sharing meeting with the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, as the party indicated it would concede three seats to three parties of the platform. The interim government on Thursday approved the draft ‘Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress (Amendment) Ordinance 2025’, introducing a key provision that allows a tribunal to officially declare a person as ‘disappeared’ if he or she... Several hundred protesters on Thursday night set fire to the offices of the Prothom Alo and the Daily Star in the capital following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi at a hospital in Singapore. Bangladesh’s interim government chief adviser Muhammad Yunus on Thursday night announced a one-day state mourning on Saturday following the death of Sharif Osman Hadi, convener of Inqilab Mancha... Traffic came to a standstill at Shahbagh Thursday night as leaders and activists of Inqilab Mancha, along with Dhaka University students, began gathering around 10:30pm to mourn the death of Sharif Osman Hadi... Gunshot-injured Sharif Osman Hadi, the convener of the Inquilab Mancha and one of the organisers of the July uprising, breathed his last under treatment in Singapore at around 9:30pm Bangladesh time. Interim government law adviser Asif Nazrul on Thursday said that he raised concerns with chief justice Syed Refaat Ahmed over what he described as ‘abnormal’ bail orders granted by some High Court benches. Bangladesh interim government has appointed 673 candidates who were ‘deprived’ in the 27th Bangladesh Civil Service examination to various cadres of the Bangladesh Civil Service as per a court verdict. The police on Thursday stopped anti-India marches of groups of youths, mostly July protesters, towards the Indian Assistant High Commission offices in Rajshahi and Khulan cities.

title: Biman introduces body cameras for baggage security at HSIA
body: Biman Bangladesh Airlines in a press release on Wednesday said that the airlines had introduced body cameras for baggage-handling staff at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, strengthening security, transparency and accountability in handling baggage for domestic and international flights. As the ground handling agent, the airlines has taken the technology-driven initiative to ensure safer and more transparent baggage operations for passengers. Under the initiative, body cameras have been provided to traffic staff involved in baggage transportation. The system will allow continuous monitoring of the entire baggage-handling process— from unloading baggage, aircraft holds, and movement through conveyor belts to final delivery to passengers.
