The initiative will cover both the Biman’s domestic flights and international flights of foreign airlines for which Biman provides ground handling services, ensuring a uniform standard of security and transparency across all operations. The airlines officials said that the measure would significantly enhance baggage security, improving operational transparency and staff accountability. In case of baggage-related complaints, recorded footage can be reviewed to verify incidents promptly and ensure timely and appropriate resolution.

title: Civil society, experts express deep concern over deterioration in public safety
body: Civil society, political leaders and researchers expressed deep concern on Wednesday over the deterioration of public safety and the weakness of the judicial system in Bangladesh. At a dialogue titled ‘Security and Rights: What We Want, What We Get?’ organised by Democracy International, speakers stressed that ensuring citizens’ safety and rights could not rely on a single party. They called for national unity, political accountability and effective institutional reforms. Catherine Cecil, chief of party at Democracy International, cited a survey conducted from November 5–30, before the shooting of Osman Hadi, showing 92.3 per cent of respondents would not vote for any party or candidate involved in violent acts. About half believed that political parties were failing to curb violence and establish peace. Other speakers highlighted the human impact of political violence, weak law enforcement, and the need for impartial governance. Faruk Hasan of the Gonadhikar Parishad said that 24 years of politically motivated violence had eroded public safety and the rule of law. Monira Sharmin of NCP emphasised building consensus beyond election-focused politics, while BNP’s ABM Mosharraf Hossain stressed accountability and professionalism in law enforcement to protect innocent citizens. Experts also noted the gendered aspect of insecurity. University of Dhaka professor Salma Akter said that fear of violence affected women in both public and private spaces. Human rights activist Noor Khan Liton called for consistent attention to human rights beyond election periods. Speakers concluded that safeguarding public safety required national unity, sustained political will and state support to ensure citizens could live without fear and the rule of law was upheld. The dialogue was held under the B-Space project with support from FCDO and organised by Democracy International in collaboration with Jamuna Television.

title: Court discharges Mirza Abbas, Aman, 43 others in 2 cases
body: A Dhaka court on Wednesday discharged 45 leaders and activists of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, including standing committee member Mirza Abbas and chairperson’s adviser Aman Ullah Aman, in two separate cases filed with the city’s Paltan and Shahjahanpur police stations. Dhaka metropolitan magistrate Mehedi Hasan passed the order, allowing the discharge petitions filed by the defence, said Mirza Abbas’s lawyer Mohiuddin Chowdhury. Other persons discharged included Gayeshwar Chandra Roy, Abdullah Al Noman, Syed Moazzem Hossain Alal, Saiful Alam Nirob, Habib-un-Nabi Khan Sohel, Ishak Sarkar and Khandaker Enamul Haque Enam. The two cases, filed in early 2013, involved allegations of obstructing law enforcers and hurling cocktails.

title: JICA hosts workshop on UGDP
body: The Japan International Cooperation Agency Bangladesh on Wednesday hosted a dissemination workshop to showcase the achievements of the upazila governance and development project and outline strategies for strengthening local governance in Bangladesh. Mobasser Monem, chairman, Bangladesh Public Service Commission, attended as chief guest at the workshop at a hotel in Dhaka, said a press release. Md Nazrul Islam, secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works, attended as guest of honour; while Morikawa Yuko, senior representative, JICA Bangladesh Office, joined as special guest at the workshop. Chaired by Md Rezaul Maksud Jahedi, secretary, Local Government Division, the workshop was coordinated by Abu Nasar Mohammad Abdullah, joint secretary and project director, UGDP. UGDP, implemented countrywide, introduced performance-based financing, digital governance tools and capacity development initiatives to empower upazila parishads as key institutions for grassroots service delivery. The workshop brought together policymakers, development partners, and local government representatives to reflect progress and persistent challenges in achieving SMART governance—Strategic, Measurable, Accountable, Responsive, and Technology-enabled. UGDP is driving innovation to build a sustainable model for local development. Key accomplishments presented at the event include the rollout of performance-based allocation, an approach that ties financial initiatives to governance outcomes, encouraging accountability and positive behavioural change. The project has also advanced digital innovation, introducing web-based governance performance assessment that has boosted transparency and operational efficiency in local government operations. In addition, inclusive capacity development initiatives have delivered training programmes targeted towards upazilla officials. Local women and youth were also central to capacity development efforts for better livelihoods and income generation. The workshop highlighted insights from UGDP’s implementation experience, reaffirming that financial incentive was a powerful tool to drive reform and improve accountability. The sustainability of these reforms depends on institutionalisation, while strong leadership and effective coordination amplify the impact. Additionally, continuous capacity development remains the foundation for robust governance systems. Additionally, while digital governance enhances transparency, a hybrid oversight approach ensures optimal results.

title: Assets worth Tk 66,146 crore attached at home, abroad
body: Bangladesh interim government has attached and frozen movable and immoveable assets worth Tk 66,146 crore at home and abroad in more than 16 months in its efforts to check money laundering. Of these, assets worth Tk 55,638 crore have been attached at home and assets worth Tk 10,508 crore abroad, according to a review meeting by the National Coordination Committee, the apex committee for formulating and implementing policies for combating money laundering and terror financing, held at the secretariat in the capital Dhaka on Wednesday. Presided over by finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed, the meeting was told that 14 charge sheets had been submitted out of 104 priority cases in this connection. The meeting directed agencies concerned to file charge sheets as soon as possible on all priority cases. Investigations into money laundering allegations against business groups such as Summit Group, Beximco Group, Bashundhara Group, S Alam Group, Orion Group, Gemcon Group, Nabil Group, NASSA Group and Sikder Group have been prioritised by the interim government after it assumed power on August 8, 2024, after the ouster of the Awami League regime in the wake of a mass uprising. Bangladesh Bank governor Ahsan H Mansur said that they were looking forward to a quick settlement of the cases, now pending in London, against Saifuzzaman Chowdhury, an Awami League politician and former land minister. Mansur made the remarks after the committee meeting. Some 350 properties owned by the controversial former minister in London and various cities in southeast England have been frozen and put on auction by the United Kingdom’s National Crime Agency following requests from the Bangladesh interim government to seize illegal assets owned by Saifuzzaman. UK media has reported that steps have been taken to sell part of Saifuzzaman’s properties, valued at approximately £170 million (equivalent to about Tk 2,788 crore) in the UK, to settle his debts with creditors which include the Singapore-based DBS Bank and the British Arab Commercial Bank. Since Saifuzzaman did not contest the cases, Mansur expected that the outcome of the cases would favour them. Islami Bank Bangladesh and United Commercial Bank are also parties to that cases, though the exact time frame for repatriation of the funds remains uncertain, said the Bangladesh central bank governor. It may take until February, March, April, May or even June next year, he added. In May 2025, the BB governor said that about $18 to $20 billion was siphoned out of the country during the Awami League’s 16-year regime ousted on August 5, 2024. Responding to a question on the petition filed by S Alam Group owner Mohammad Saiful Alam at the World Bank’s arbitration forum, Mansur said that the Bangladesh Bank would take part in legal fight in Washington. In his petition, Saiful Alam, also known as S Alam, and his family members have claimed that they are citizens of Singapore. ‘But the BB will prove that S Alam is a Bangladeshi citizen,’ said the BB governor. The meeting also asked ministries and divisions to make necessary preparations for the forthcoming mutual evaluation by the Asia Pacific Group which assesses member countries’ anti-money laundering efforts. The meeting was participated, among others, by Anti-Corruption Commission chairman Mohammad Abdul Momen, principal secretary to the Chief Adviser’s Office M Siraz Uddin Miah, Finance Division secretary Khairuzzman Majumder and National Board of Revenue chairman Abdur Rahman Khan.

title: Jatiya Party to join election if level playing field ensured
body: Jatiya Party will take part in the next general election if level playing field ensured for all political parties. ‘We will participate in the next general election and will nominate party candidates for 300 seats of Jatiya Sangsad if level playing field is ensured,’ said JP secretary general Shamim Haider Patwary at a press conference in party’s central office at Kakrail on Wednesday. He called on the interim government to take immediate steps to ensure level playing field for every political party which, he said, has not been created so far. He also called on the government to withdraw the cases field against Jatiya Party leaders across the country. ‘From today we have started selling party nomination papers for the aspirant candidates,’ Shamim Haider said. ‘We want next general election be held in free, fair and credible manner and voters can cast their votes in favour of their desired candidates,’ he added. Replying a question of a reporter, Shamim Hader Patwary said that so far they would not form any electoral alliance and take part in the election unilaterally. Shamim Haider Patwary said that JP supported July Uprising of 2024 and as an Election Commission registered political party it was preparing to participate in the election. JP central leaders Razaul Islam Bhuiyan, Abul Khaer, Saifuddin Ahmed Milon, Golam Mohammad Raju, Shafiqul Islam Modhu, Alamgir Sikder Lotan and others attended the press conference. Jatiya Party faction led by Anisul Islam Mahmud also taking preparations to take part in the election under an alliance, National Democratic Front. However which faction would get party symbol ‘plough’ is not yet settled in the High Court.

title: March to Indian HC stopped
body: Visa office closes on security grounds, Bangladesh envoy in Delhi summoned India’s advice on polls unacceptable Several thousand people marched to Indian High Commission in the capital’s Baridhara on Wednesday, demanding extradition of fugitive ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and others allegedly involved in crimes against humanity during the July uprising. The demonstrators, comprising mostly of July uprising participants, under the banner of ‘July Oikya’ (July unity) started the march from Rampura Bridge at around 3:15pm and were stopped by the police at Uttar Badda in front of Hossain Market at about 4:00pm. Meanwhile, the Indian Visa Application Centre at Dhaka’s Jamuna Future Park was closed at 2:00pm on security grounds. Hours after the group announced that they would march to Indian High Commission on Wednesday afternoon, the Ministry of External Affairs in New Delhi summoned the high commissioner of Bangladesh to India Riaz Hamidullah, according to officials in Dhaka. The Bangladesh envoy was reminded of Dhaka’s responsibility for ensuring safety and security of the Indian mission and visa facilities in Bangladesh, said the officials. About the summoning of the Bangladesh high commissioner in Delhi, foreign affairs adviser Md Touhid Hossain told reporters at his ministry on late Wednesday afternoon that it was not very unexpected. ‘It usually happens when one person is summoned, the other is summoned, too,’ Touhid said. Touhid said that India’s advice about Bangladesh’s upcoming general elections slated for February 12, 2026 was unacceptable as the neighbouring country had remained silent about the ‘farcical elections’ held in the past 15 years. He said that the interim government had taken all preparations for a free, fair and credible election. ‘The Government of India in the latest statement has advised us about the upcoming elections. From the day beginning, we have been saying that we are going hold a free and fair election where people could cast their votes in a festive manner. India did not say any words in the past 15 years although all the elections held under the previous regime were farcical,’ said the adviser. Commenting on India-Bangladesh relations, Touhid said that it was better to accept the reality that the interim government’s relations with India had been strained since the beginning. ‘It is better to accept that there has been tension since the beginning of this government in our relation with India. Taking this into account we have been saying that we want a good working environment with them,’ he said. On Sunday, Bangladesh foreign affairs ministry summoned Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh Pranay Verma to convey the Bangladesh government’s serious concern to the Indian government about allowing fugitive deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina to continue making ‘incendiary statements’. Adviser Md Touhid Hossain also remarked that it was normal that any mission could suspend its visa processing activities amid such an event over security concerns. ‘But we have successfully ensured security for the mission against the march to the Indian High Commission programme,’ he said. Deputy commissioner for Dhaka Metropolitan Police Gulshan Division Rownak Alam said that law enforcers erected a barricade at Uttar Badda and barred the demonstrators from moving forward. Later, the protesters rallied there on the road. ‘No violence is reported. Protesters went back peacefully after holding a rally,’ he said. Protesters were seen holding placards written with slogans, such as, ‘Ban state force backed by India’, ‘Ban India-backed political party’, ‘Ban Indian proxy media’. Speakers at the on-street protest rally said that they had heard that India helped Bangladesh’s War of Independence in 1971 and if India failed to hand over suspected shooters of Inqilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi, Sheikh Hasina and others, the protesters would help India’s seven eastern provinces, known as seven sisters to become independent. The Dhaka University Central Students’ Union literature and cultural secretary Musaddiq Ali Ibne Mohammad at the demonstration said that they would not allow any Indian proxy in the new Bangladesh. Hadi sustained critical injuries after he was shot at Bijoynagar in Dhaka city on December 12, while he was conducting his electioneering. He is undergoing treatment at a Singapore hospital. The prime accused in the case of the murder attempt on Hadi has reportedly fled to India. The Indian Visa Application Centre on its website on Wednesday announced that all applicants with appointment slots scheduled for submission on the day would be rescheduled for a later date. Organisers said that the march was participated in by former army officers, DUCSU and Jahangirnagar University Central Student Union leaders, and representatives from universities, colleges, madrassahs, schools and various civil society groups.

title: Victory Day celebrated with vow to establish war ideals
body: The nation celebrated the 55th Victory Day on Tuesday, remembering the heroic and supreme sacrifices of freedom fighters to free the country from the marauding Pakistani military in the War of Independence, with a call to establish the ideals of the war. Marking the day, the nation renewed its pledge to translate into reality the hopes and aspirations of the War of Independence and the 2024 mass uprising. The government, political parties, and Bangladesh missions abroad, socio-cultural organisations, educational institutions, professional bodies, and other organisations celebrated the day with various events across the country. The Victory Day celebration started with a 31-gun salute and the hoisting of the national flag atop all government and semi-government and private offices as well as offices of autonomous bodies across the country. Receptions were hosted for the freedom fighters and family members of martyrs at the city, district, and upazila levels, marking the day. People from all walks of life started visiting the National Memorial at Savar and other memorials across the country from dawn to pay tributes to the martyrs. President Mohammed Shahabuddin and chief adviser Muhammad Yunus paid tributes to the martyrs by placing wreaths at the National Memorial with the rise of the sun on the day. The Bir Shrestha families, war-wounded and brave freedom fighters, under the leadership of the liberation war affairs adviser, later laid wreaths there. Members of the Advisory Council, other important state dignitaries and foreign diplomats paid homage to the martyred heroes at the main altar of the memorial. Later, leaders and activists of different political, social, and cultural organisations, along with students of various public and private universities, paid floral tributes in an orderly manner by standing in queues. New Age Jahangirnagar University correspondent reported that since early morning, thousands of people from all walks of life gathered there to remember the nation’s brave sons. Some attendees expressed frustration over what they described as persistent inequality, weak public institutions and a political culture detached from the everyday concerns of ordinary citizens. Leaders and activists from major political parties, including the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and the National Citizen Party, paid tribute at the memorial. NCP convener Nahid Islam said that successive governments had failed to honour the core promises of the 1971 war, allowing inequality and authoritarianism to take root. He said that Bangladesh’s post-independence history was marked by broken commitments to equality, human dignity and social justice. ‘We achieved independence, but in 54 years we have repeatedly seen the people of Bangladesh being betrayed,’ Nahid said. ‘The ideals on which this country was founded were never fully realised.’ He said those failures had culminated in mass uprisings in 2024, which he described as part of a longer historical struggle stretching from the anti-colonial movement to the war of independence. President Mohammed Shahabuddin and his wife Rebeka Sultana, on Tuesday hosted a reception at Bangabhaban on the occasion of Victory Day. The BNP hoisted the national and party flags at all party offices in the morning, paid homage at the National Memorial at Savar, and laid wreaths at the grave of BNP founder and former president Ziaur Rahman at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in Dhaka. After paying homage at the grave of Ziaur Rahman, BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir told journalists that those who opposed Bangladesh’s independence in 1971 are once again raising their heads. He said, ‘The freedom-loving people of Bangladesh, who believe in independence and democracy, will foil all their conspiracies and keep the country’s independence and sovereignty intact. Democracy will be established.’ Communist Party of Bangladesh, Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal factions, Revolutionary Workers Party of Bangladesh, Gono Forum, Ganosamhati Andolan, Liberation War Museum, National Press Club, Dhaka Reporters Unity, Dhaka Club, among other organisations, paid homage at the National Memorial in Savar. Newspapers published special supplements while television channels and radio stations aired special programmes highlighting the glorious history of the War of Independence to mark the day. As part of the nationwide celebrations of Victory Day, chief adviser Muhammad Yunus enjoyed the Victory Day Fly Past, parajump and band display at the National Parade Ground in the morning. To mark the country’s 54 years of independence, 54 paratroopers from the Bangladesh Army, Navy and Air Force performed a national flag-bearing skydive. Victory Day songs were performed at Suhrawardy Udyan in the afternoon while new-generation artistes performed songs of Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra simultaneously in 64 districts across the country. On the occasion, various social and cultural organisations, including Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy, Bangla Academy, National Museum, Liberation War Museum and Bangladesh Shishu Academy organised Liberation War-based discussions, cultural programmes, and screenings of Liberation War-based documentaries. Special prayers were offered at mosques, temples, churches, pagodas, and other places of worship seeking eternal peace for the departed souls of martyred freedom fighters and the well-being of wounded veterans and peace and progress of the country. Improved diets were served in all hospitals, prisons, old-age homes, orphanages, street-children rehabilitation centres, disability welfare centres, daycare centres, child development centres and Shishu Paribar and under-privileged children across the country. Back on the night of March 25, 1971, the Pakistani occupation forces launched an onslaught on the Bangalee community and committed genocide on the unsuspecting and unarmed people to tame the struggle for self-determination. The War of Independence was preceded by 23 long years of intense political struggle for democracy and national identity. The commander of 92,000 marauding troops of the Pakistan military, Lieutenant General AAK Niazi, surrendered at Ramna Race Course, now Suhrawardy Udyan, in Dhaka on December 16, 1971 following nine months of the War of Independence, which was a people’s war.

title: Clashes, arson at FF’s grave mar celebration at places
body: Scuffles broke out between the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami at places during the celebration of Victory Day on Tuesday. Besides, a grave of war hero was set on fire in Shariatpur. At Niamatpur village of Shariatpur Sadar, the grave of valiant freedom fighter Abdul Mannan Khan was set on fire by unknown people late Monday night. Local people said that freedom fighter was a pride of the locality and setting fire to his grave was a heinous crime. Mannan died on January 8, 2010 and was buried beside his house. Mannan’s wife Mahfuza Begum demanded that that the perpetrators must be brought to book. Shariatpur Sadar upazila nirbahi officer Elora Yasmin said that she directed officials concerned to look into the matter. At Daulatkhan in Bhola, 15 people were injured as BNP and Jamaat leaders and activists scuffle over seating arrangement at a Victory Day celebration at the Amir Jang Ghaznabi Stadium. The scuffle began when BNP leaders and activists called the Jamaat leaders ‘razakars’, seeing them occupying seats in the front row. BNP-affiliated Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and Jamaat-affiliated Islami Chhatra Shibir activists scuffled at Chittagong University, when a procession of Chhatra Dal reached the venue and began protesting against the presence of pro-vice chancellor Mohammed Shamim Uddin Khan at the discussion. Earlier on December 14, Shamim at a programme marking Martyr Intellectuals Day stated that the narrative that the Pakistani occupation army killed intellectuals at the fag end of the War for Independence was ‘absurd’. The Chhatra Dal procession also demanded the resignation of Shamim. Later, the proctorial body brought the situation under control. The Chatra Dal and nine Chittagong University Central Students’ Union leaders, including assistant general secretary Ayobur Rahman, boycotted the discussion. A tense situation prevailed at Jagannath University overnight as clashes sparked following the painting of Pakistani flag on a road on the campus. The incident occurred when several students painted a Pakistani flag on the road near the main gate. The university administration and a group of students protested at the action triggering tensions. The situation worsened when a bus carrying students of As-Sunnah Hall, headingto national memorial, was barred from leaving the campus. Black colour was poured on the over image of the Pakistani flag. During live coverage of the incident, Bangla daily Kaler Kantho journalist Minhajul Islam and Mehedi were harassed by individuals at the scene. In protest, the Chatra Dal brought out a procession and confined the vice-chancellor and the proctor to the administrative building. The Chatra Dal called off the protests after the Pakistani flag had again been painted on the road in front of the administrative building and the vice-chancellor, the proctor and others left the campus for the National Martyrs’ Memorial at about 5:00am. The unrest, however, continued till Tuesday afternoon, when students at the Shanto Chattar staged a symbolic protest by throwing shoes at images representing razakars. Another controversy emerged after some students painted the Indian flag alongside the Pakistani flag.

title: Victory Day health camp held in city
body: A free health camp of cardiac treatment was held in the capital on Tuesday to mark Victory Day and to contribute to public healthcare. The health camp was organised by cardiac surgeon Muhammad Ali Bhuiyan and interventional cardiologist Fauzia Khan, said a press release. The charitable event took place at Priyo Ma Pharmacy on RK Mission Road. More than 50 cardiac patients received free medical consultations, necessary tests, and treatments during the camp. The initiative received an enthusiastic response from the local community, reflecting a strong commitment to public health improvement and the true spirit of Victory Day. The organisers expressed sincere gratitude to all those who extended assistance and emphasised the importance of raising public awareness about heart disease and the value of preventive cardiac care.

title: Body of septuagenarian recovered in Ctg
body: The police recovered the body of a septuagenarian from the Ichamati River in Chattogram on Wednesday, nine days after his disappearance. Being informed by a cowboy, a team of Anwara police went to the spot and rescued the floating body of Abu Sayed, 70, a resident of Pirkhayin village under Haildhar union of the upazila. The almost decomposed body of the deceased had been floating on the river at a place near the upazila warehouse under sadar union. Abu Syed’s family sources said that he remained untraced after leaving home about nine days ago, and they could not ascertain his whereabouts after a search for the past nine days. Anwara police said that they had not yet confirmed whether the death was a killing or an accidental one. ‘The body was sent to the CMCH morgue for an autopsy.’

title: ACC sues S Alam, 67 others
body: The Anti-Corruption Commission on Wednesday filed two separate cases against S Alam Group chairman Saiful Alam Masud, also known as S Alam, and 67 others over embezzlement of Tk 3,184.81 crore from Janata Bank. ACC Chattogram-1 office deputy director Subel Ahmed said that the commission’s deputy director, Mohammad Sirajul Haque, filed the cases with the ACC Chattogram district integrated office-1 on Wednesday morning. In one case, the ACC accused S Alam Refined Sugar Industries Limited, a concern of S Alam Group, of embezzling Tk 2,032.30 crore from Janata Bank. Saiful Alam Masud has been made an accused in the case as the company’s managing director. Among the 32 accused, the case has also named the company’s director Abdullah Hasan, Global Trading Corporation managing director Rashedul Alam, several directors of different S Alam Group firms, and officials of Janata Bank. According to the case statement, loans were taken from Janata Bank in the name of S Alam Refined Sugar Industries Limited between August 25, 2009 and March 6, 2025 through different means, including Covid stimulus packages and LTR loans, and the money was misappropriated along with interest. In the other case, the ACC brought allegations of embezzlement of Tk 1,152.51 crore against S Alam Super Edible Oil Limited, another concern of S Alam Group, saying loans were taken in different ways between September 13, 2005 and March 6, 2025 and the money was misappropriated along with interest. The case has named S Alam Super Edible Oil Limited director Shahana Ferdous and managing director Miskat Ahmed and 34 others, including Janata Bank officials. In both cases, the accused have been charged under sections 409, 420 and 109 of the Penal Code, section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947, and section 4(2) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012. Earlier, the ACC started inquiries against the S Alam Group chairman over the allegations of amassing illegal wealth and laundering $1 billion to Singapore and several other countries.

title: Home adviser urges law enforcers to uphold loyalty, professionalism
body: Bangledesh interim government's home adviser Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury on Wednesday urged the members of the law enforcement agencies to maintain loyalty, honesty and professionalism in discharging of their duties. ‘Maintain professionalism, honesty and loyalty while performing duties,’ he said while speaking at an event at Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association office in Narayanganj. Six police vans were distributed to Narayanganj district police and industrial police 4 on behalf of the BKMEA at the programme. The adviser said that a significant number of police vehicles and equipment were damaged during the July uprising and the interim government had taken up various initiatives to overcome the losses. Jahangir noted that continued cooperation from government and private organisations would further strengthen the operational capacity of law enforcement agencies, contributing to the establishment of a safe and prosperous Bangladesh. Highlighting the importance of the ready-made garment sector, particularly knitwear, Jahangir said, ‘It is one of the main driving forces of the national economy.’ He stressed that sustainable development of the sector depended on secured industrial zones, stable law and order, and mutual cooperation between factory owners and the administration. He described the BKMEA’s donation as a positive example of public-private partnership. Responding to the withdrawal of a BNP-nominated candidate from the Narayanganj 5 constituency election, the adviser said that the decision was a personal matter and declined to comment further. Regarding security concerns, he said, ‘Individuals are free to assess the situation personally. Journalists may uncover the reasons behind such decisions through investigation.’ He also informed that Sharif Osman Hadi was currently undergoing treatment in Singapore and urged everyone to pray for his recovery, describing him as a July movement fighter with notable contributions. Special assistant to chief adviser Md Khuda Baksh Chowdhury attended the event as a special guest while BKMEA president Mohammad Hatem presided over the programme. Among others, industrial police chief Gazi Jashim Uddin, Narayanganj deputy commissioner Md Raihan Kabir, police superintendent Mohammad Mizanur Rahman Munshi, industrial police 4 chief Md Asaduzzaman, BKMEA vice-president Md Morshed Sarwar and senior officials, were present.

title: ICT-1 takes cognisance of charges against Ziaul
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Wednesday took cognisance of formal charges against former National Telecommunication Monitoring Centre director general and retired major general Ziaul Ahsan for his alleged involvement in enforced disappearances and killing more than 100 people. The prosecution alleged that the crimes were committed mainly between 2009 and 2016 while Ziaul Ahsan was serving in the Rapid Action Battalion and holding commanding positions. Chief prosecutor Muhammad Tajul Islam placed the formal charge before the three-member tribunal and urged it to take cognisance of three charges against the accused. After hearing the prosecution, the tribunal, headed by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mazumder, took the charges into cognisance on three counts and ordered the authorities to produce Ziaul Ahsan before the tribunal on December 21. Ziaul Ahsan is currently in jail in connection with several other cases. According to the first charge, Ziaul Ahsan allegedly planned and directly participated in the killing of Sazal and three unidentified people in a shooting at the Pubail Bypass Road in Gazipur on July 11, 2011. The second charge relates to the killing and enforced disappearance of at least 50 people, including Nazrul Islam Mollick and Alkash. The prosecution said that the victims were killed and their bodies were dumped at the confluence of the Baleshwar River at Charduani under Patharghata upazila in Barguna district between 2010 and 2013. The third charge accuses Ziaul Ahsan of killing at least 50 people, including Masud, during alleged operations against so-called pirates in different areas of Sundarban in Sarankhola of Bagerhat between 2010 and 2013. The prosecution told the tribunal that separate investigations were ongoing against Ziaul Ahsan for the alleged killing of at least 200 people whose bodies were dumped into the Shitalakhya and Buriganga rivers using the so-called ‘Gestapo’ or ‘golf’ method. He is also accused of involvement in the enforced disappearance of BNP leader Chowdhury Alam, Islami Chhatra Shibir leader Golam Mortuza Mihir and two others in 2010, BNP leader Elias Ali and his driver Ansar Ali in 2012, and Adabor thana Islami Chhatra Shibir president Hafez Zakir Hossain, who was later killed in 2013. The prosecution further alleged that Ziaul Ahsan was involved in the killing of at least 61 unarmed and apolitical Hefazat-e-Islam supporters during the May 5, 2013 crackdown at Shapla Chattar in the capital. He is also a suspect of enforced disappearance of seven others, including BNP leader Sazedul Islam Suman, and of the enforced disappearance of BNP leader Salahuddin Ahmed and his subsequent deportation to India in 2015. According to the prosecution, Ziaul Ahsan was additionally involved in abduction, torture, enforced disappearances and killings during the July-August mass uprising. These crimes were allegedly facilitated through digital surveillance while he was serving as head of the NTMC. Asked to comment Ziaul Ahsan’s sister and his lawyer Naznin Nahar termed the allegations a ‘cinema script’ and alleged that the media aired them as part of a planned campaign.

title: BNP assures 2 seats, partners want more
body: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party on Wednesday started meetings with like-minded parties and coalitions and simultaneous movement partners to resolve disputes over seat sharing ahead of the forthcoming parliamentary elections. On the first day of the meeting, the BNP met with the 12-party alliance and the Jatiyatabadi Samomona Jote, indicating that it might concede one seat to each group, leaders attending the meetings told New Age. They said that discussions also included offering another seat to the 12-party alliance, while assuring that other member parties within these coalitions would be evaluated separately. Meeting sources said that the BNP had signalled that the 12-party alliance chief and chairman of a faction of the Jatiya Party (Kazi Zafar), Mostafa Jamal Haider, may contest the election for the Pirojpur-1 constituency, while the Jatiyatabadi Samomona Jote coordinator and NPP chairman, Fariduzzaman Farhad, may contest the polls for the Narail-2 constituency, with an official announcement expected on December 20. BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, along with standing committee members Nazrul Islam Khan and Iqbal Hasan Mahmud Tuku, attended the meetings held at the party chairperson’s Gulshan office in Dhaka. Meetings with other allies, including the Liberal Democratic Party, Ganatantra Mancha, and Gonoforum, are scheduled for Thursday and talks with the Nationalist Democratic Movement, the Left Democratic Alliance, and the Bangladesh Jatiya Party are set for Friday. The BNP would conclude the series of meetings with a discussion with the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam. Leaders from the 12-party alliance and the Samomona Jote said that their allies had requested reconsideration of certain constituencies, including Kishoreganj-5 and Kushtia-2. They said that the BNP’s high command responded positively, assuring maximum consideration for both coalitions. The leaders said that the BNP had planned to evaluate those who were not nominated for parliamentary seats for potential roles in the upper house and urged all parties to remain united for democracy and the national interest. Speaking after the meeting, 12-party alliance coordinator Syed Ehsanul Huda described the discussions as positive, saying that the party had raised its demands and received assurances of maximum consideration as long-term allies. Meanwhile, Jatiyatabadi Samomona Jote coordinator Fariduzzaman Farhad said that the talks had been fruitful, with BNP promising at least one or two seats to their coalition and pledging to evaluate remaining leaders for positions in the upper house based on merit once in power.

title: Bangladesh
body: Defeated fascist force plots clandestine killings before polls: Yunus Bangladesh interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Tuesday said that the fascist force defeated by the July mass uprising had a tough plot and preparations for assassinating unarmed young people during the run-up to the general elections slated for February 12, 2026, to come back...

title: Defeated fascist force plots clandestine killings before polls: Yunus
body: Bangladesh interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Tuesday said that the fascist force defeated by the July mass uprising had a tough plot and preparations for assassinating unarmed young people during the run-up to the general elections slated for February 12, 2026, to come back. He said that no one would be able to halt the country’s democratic progress by intimidation, terrorism or bloodshed in the country. ‘I want to state clearly — the attempts by the defeated fascist force will be completely foiled. No one will be able to stop this country’s democratic progress by intimidation, terrorism, or bloodshed,’ he said in his televised address to the nation on the occasion of Victory Day. Yunus emphasised protection of the youth and ensuring a peaceful and festive election with collective efforts to build a new Bangladesh, resisting all the ill-efforts of defeated fascist and terrorist forces. He said, ‘I call upon you to maintain restraint. Do not pay heed to propaganda or rumours. We will certainly confront the fascist terrorists, who seek to create instability, together. We will not fall into their traps.’ In an oblique reference to the fall of the authoritarian regime of Sheikh Hasina who fled to India, amid the July mass uprising on August 5, 2024, the chief adviser asserted that the defeated fascist force would never again return to the sacred soil of this country. Mentioning the recent assassination attempt on independent candidate aspirant for the forthcoming national polls Sharif Osman Hadi, Yunus said, ‘Today I stand before you with a deeply sorrowful heart. On this day of joy, it is with profound grief I inform you that the recent attack on Sharif Osman Hadi, a frontline fighter of the July uprising and spokesperson of Inquilab Mancha, is not merely an attack on an individual — it is an attack on the very existence of Bangladesh and on our democratic journey.’ He said that the government had taken all necessary measures to ensure treatment of critically-injured Hadi, who had already been sent to Singapore for advanced medical care. The chief adviser said that the government was treating the incident with utmost seriousness and that those involved had been initially identified. ‘I want to assure the nation that those involved in this conspiracy, wherever they are, will not be spared.’ At the outset of his address, he extended his heartfelt greeting to the people of all ages and walks of life at home and abroad on the occasion of Victory Day. ‘On this day in 1971, after nine months of bloody Liberation War, we achieved our long-cherished victory. Through immense sacrifices and blood of millions of martyrs, we attained an independent country and the red-green flag.’ ‘With deep respect, we remember the brave fighters and martyrs who sacrificed their lives in the Liberation War and in struggles for independence throughout the ages.’ ‘The new sun of independence that rose through victory in the Liberation War has dimmed in recent years by autocracy and fascism.’ However, through the July uprising with the participation of students and mass people, the nation has once again received an opportunity to establish ‘a discrimination-free, corruption-free, independent, sovereign and democratic state system’, the chief adviser said. But the forces which fled the country in face of the uprising consider the fearless and unarmed young people as the biggest obstacle to their return and therefore, their target is to eliminate them before the elections to re-establish their reign, he said. ‘Once the elections are over, their cohorts will face a trouble to garner support. That’s why there is such a rush. They want to ensure their return before the polls. They will do it in various ways. This clandestine killing attempt is one form of that. They are prepared with more difficult plans,’ Prof Yunus said. ‘Everyone in the country must say loudly: we will protect the youth together, we will establish our full control over the country by holding festive and peaceful elections,’ he added. About illness of Bangladesh Nationalist Party chairperson and three-time former prime minister Khaleda Zia, the chief adviser said, ‘She is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital, which is a matter of concern for all of us.’ Noting that the interim government has given the highest importance to the treatment of Khaleda Zia, he said that the government was ensuring all necessary cooperation for her treatment. Reflecting on the interim government activities since its beginning, Yunus reiterated that the interim government had prioritised three key issues — justice for the July–August killings, fundamental state reforms for a democratic transition, and a free and fair election. Noting that the trial of the July massacres was proceeding in due legal process, he said that the International Crimes Tribunal had already delivered verdict in one case. The tribunal through an independent, transparent and evidence-based trial process sentenced ousted fascist prime minister Sheikh Hasina to death as the main architect of indiscriminate killings of students, workers and ordinary citizens of the country, he said. As part of the legal process, he said, the government has formally requested India to repatriate Sheikh Hasina and another convict former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan, both of whom are fugitives. Noting that several institutional and structural reforms had already been completed, Yunus said that his government had amended dozens of old laws and formulated new ones. The most significant reform, he said, is the July National Charter, which has been issued as an order to ensure fundamental constitutional reforms. Now it is time to seek the citizens’ approval to implement the July National Charter, he added. Urging citizens to cast ‘their votes carefully’, he said, ‘If anyone creates obstacles, resist them in an orderly manner and seek the assistance of law enforcement agencies.’ Yunus said that during the fascist regime, the country’s people were forced to live in a terrible state without human rights despite having the National Human Rights Commission. ‘In order to end the dishonest system, the interim government has formulated the National Human Rights Commission Ordinance, 2025,’ Yunus said. He urged all to move forward together with the goal of empowering the people, being imbued with spirit of the great Liberation War and the July uprising.

title: Shakawath Hossain appointed editor of Amader Shomoy
body: Journalist and columnist Md Shakawath Hossain has assumed charge as editor of the daily Amader Shomoy. He succeeds Abu Sayeed Khan in the role, said a press release on Monday. He took over his responsibilities at the newspaper’s office at the Tejgaon Industrial Area in Dhaka on Sunday. Publisher of Amader Shomoy, Khondkar Showkat Hossain, along with journalists, officials and employees of the organisation, welcomed the new editor with flowers. The event was attended by Md Abdul Motaleb, director of human resources of Unique Group; Syed Enamul Haque, DGM of PHP Family; and journalists, officers, and staff from various departments of Amader Shomoy. Upon assuming office, Shakawath Hossain addressed the journalists and staff, stating that all necessary initiatives would be undertaken to take Amader Shomoy forward. He emphasised making every effort to uphold the newspaper’s legacy and reputation. Alongside urging professional excellence among journalists, he assured improvements in employees’ welfare and benefits. He called upon everyone to perform their respective duties with dedication to further establish Amader Shomoy as a reader-friendly and reliable source of news. Shakawath Hossain began his career in journalism during his student life. He later transitioned into the corporate sector while continuing to write columns for various national dailies. Subsequently, he joined the English-language national daily The Business Post as managing editor, a position from which he stepped down earlier this year. Recently, he has been elected vice-president of the Bangladesh Cricket Board. Prior to this, he played a significant role for many years in the development of sports tourism in the country. As a senior leader in tourism and hospitality, Hossain has amassed extensive experience with global hotel brands, with his visionary leadership and operational excellence widely acknowledged. He has also made notable contributions to the expansion of tourism and hospitality education in Bangladesh. In this capacity, he serves as an adjunct faculty at the University of Dhaka, Southeast University and American International University–Bangladesh. He is currently pursuing a PhD in tourism and hospitality management at the University of Dhaka, having previously earned an MBA and MPhil in the same discipline from the university.

title: Child marriage higher in urban slums than rural areas: ICDDR,B
body: Child marriage rates are alarmingly high in the country’s urban informal settlements, surpassing rural areas, according to a new study by the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh. The study found that 65 per cent of women living in urban informal settlements were married before the age of 18, compared with 43 per cent in rural areas, said a press release. The study titled ‘Understanding the context and needs related to sexual and reproductive health and rights among newlywed couples in selected rural and urban areas of Bangladesh’ also revealed high rates of early pregnancy, intimate partner violence and limited autonomy among married adolescent girls. The ICDDR,B disseminated the findings at an event organised at its Sasakawa Auditorium in the capital, with support from Global Affairs Canada. The mixed-methods study was conducted between December 2022 and December 2024 across four Health and Demographic Surveillance System sites of the ICDDR,B—Chakaria and Matlab in rural areas, and Mirpur and Korail slums in Dhaka city. A total of 666 newlywed couples were enrolled, all in their first marriage, married for less than six months and with no prior pregnancy. The couples were followed every four months, generating six rounds of data over two years. According to the study, nearly three-quarters—73 per cent—of participating women became pregnant within the first year of marriage, despite many expressing a clear preference to delay childbearing. Almost half of these pregnancies were reported as mistimed or unintended, with urban women more than three times as likely as their rural counterparts to experience mistimed pregnancies. The research also highlighted widespread intimate partner violence soon after marriage. Within the first six months, four in five women reported controlling behaviour by their husbands, while over the two-year period, more than half experienced economic violence, while many also faced emotional, physical and sexual abuse. The findings show that early marriage remains common among both women and men. Among men, 15 per cent in rural areas and 37 per cent in urban areas were married before the age of 21. Almost all marriages were legally registered. Early-married women were predominantly married through arranged unions—85 per cent in rural areas, and 53 per cent in urban settlements. Self-choice marriages were more common in urban areas, accounting for over half of such unions. Educational disruption emerged as a major concern: nearly half of the women had not completed secondary education, while 60 per cent of rural and 66 per cent of urban women discontinued schooling immediately after marriage. The study was led by ICDDR,B scientist Dr Fauzia Akhter Huda.

title: Amnesty wants release of journalist Anis Alamgir
body: International rights organisation Amnesty International on Wednesday demanded the immediate release of journalist Anis Alamgir, warning that the use of anti-terror legislation against media professionals poses a serious threat to freedom of expression ahead of the national election. Anis Alamgir was arrested on December 15 under the Anti-Terrorism Act following a complaint accusing him and four others of spreading propaganda in favour of the Awami League, activities of which are now banned, through social media and other media platforms, said a statement issued by the organisation. A Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court later allowed the police to take him in custody for interrogation for five days in the case. Responding to the arrest, Amnesty International’s Rehab Mahamoor said that the detention reflected an ‘alarming trend’ of targeting individuals perceived to support the Awami League. ‘Rather than misusing anti-terror legislation to silence people expressing their views and opinions, the interim government and authorities should instead be facilitating freedom of expression and association, including in the lead up to elections,’ Mahamoor said in the statement. She added that the interim government must respect Bangladesh’s obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and immediately release Anis Alamgir. According to media reports, Alamgir told the court that he had worked as a journalist for two decades and that his role was to question those in power, not to show allegiance to any authority. The Anti-Terrorism Act was amended in May this year by the interim government to ban the activities of the Awami League. Since the amendment, the law has been used against individuals accused of supporting the party, including journalists such as Monjurul Alam Panna, rights groups say. Amnesty International warned that the use of counter-terror legislation to suppress freedom of expression and association violates international human rights law and risks creating a climate of fear in the media.

title: Sharif Osman Hadi’s condition extremely critical
body: Singapore foreign minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan on Wednesday evening informed the chief advisor, Professor Muhammad Yunus, that the Inquilab Mancha convener and one of the July uprising organisers, Sharif Osman Hadi, who is now under treatment there, was in a very critical condition. ‘Singapore foreign minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan today visited Sharif Osman Hadi. At 9:40 pm, Vivian Balakrishnan talked to Professor Yunus on phone and informed him that Hadi’s condition is very critical,’ said a statement shared by the chief adviser’s press wing. The chief adviser urged the people of Bangladesh to remain calm and pray for Hadi who was shot in the head on Box Culvert Road in Dhaka on December 12 and was flown to Singapore on December 15. Meanwhile, members of law enforcement agencies have arrested four more people, including the prime suspect’s parents and a close associate, in connection with the attempted murder of Sharif Osman Hadi. With the latest arrests, 10 people were arrested and another was detained until Wednesday for their suspected involvement in the incident. ‘Hadi’s health condition is not stable yet,’ Inquilab Mancha said in a statement on Wednesday. The statement said that his health condition needed to be stabilised before carrying out any operation in the Singapore hospital and the operation was needed for his brain to be cured. It also said that all parts of his body, except the brain, remained active. The law enforcers, meanwhile, have also recovered the pistol and the motorcycle allegedly used in the attack on Hadi. The newly arrested individuals on Monday and Tuesday are the prime suspect Faisal Karim Masud’s father Humayun Kabir, 70, mother Hasi Begum, 60, close associate Kabir, 30, and a rent-a-car businessman, Nuruzzaman Nomani. In addition to the arrests, a 25-year-old youth, Faisal, was detained during the recovery of the pistol from a water body in Narsingdi. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police on Wednesday said that the DMP Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime unit on Sunday recovered the motorcycle with the Dhaka Metro-La-54-6574 number plate, the helmet and the fake number plate of Dhaka Metro-La-54-6376 allegedly used in the attack on the aspiring independent candidate in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad election for the Dhaka-8 constituency, Hadi. Earlier, the Rapid Action Battalion identified the motorcycle number used in the attack as Dhaka Metro-La-54-6375 and arrested the owner, Abdul Hannan, who is now on a three-day remand. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s deputy commissioner for media and public relations, Muhammad Talebur Rahman, on Wednesday said that different specialised units of the police were conducting operations to arrest the assailants, while three more individuals were shown arrested on Monday and Tuesday. The metropolitan police’s Detective Branch on Wednesday afternoon produced Nuruzzaman before a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court that allowed the police to take him in custody for three days for interrogation in the case. The remand petition alleged that Nuruzzaman helped Faisal to go into hiding by providing a private car. RAB-10 assistant director (media) Tapas Karmakar on Tuesday night said that the battalion detained Faisal’s parents, Humayun and Hasi, early Tuesday. They were later handed over to the police. According to RAB, Faisal met his parents at his sister’s house in the capital’s Agargaon area after the incident and allegedly helped him to go into hiding. Acting on a tip-off, a team of RAB-11 conducted a drive in Narayanganj’s Pagla area under Fatullah thana and arrested Kabir alias ‘Dathbhanga Kabir’ early Monday. He was later handed over to the police, said a press release issued by RAB-11 on Tuesday. Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch on Tuesday afternoon produced Kabir before a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court, which allowed the police to take him in custody for seven days for interrogation in the case. It is believed that the main identified assailants, Alamgir Sheikh, the motorcycle rider, and the pillion of the motorcycle, Faisal Karim Masud, the suspected shooter, who took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for a few days, fled to India illegally through the Haluaghat border in Mymensingh. In another drive on Tuesday night, a team of RAB-11 recovered two foreign-made pistols, one of which was suspected to be used in the attack, 41 rounds of bullets, two magazines, and a toy pistol from a water body in Narsingdi’s Torua area, according to RAB officials. RAB-2 also conducted a drive on early Tuesday at Faisal’s sister Jasmine’s house and nearby areas in the capital’s Bijoynagar area and seized two fully loaded magazines, 11 bullets, one knife, several electronic devises, national ID cards, check books of different banks, passports and others, said RAB-2 senior assistant director (media) Md Shamsul Islam, adding that the seized items would be handed over to police for investigation. Inquilab Mancha member secretary Abdullah Al Jabir on Sunday filed an attempted murder case against Faisal Karim Masud and several unidentified people over the shooting of Hadi. The law enforcers earlier arrested Sivion Dio and Sanjay Chisim, who help people to cross the border illegally, Faisal’s wife Samia, his brother-in-law Shipu and Faisal’s girlfriend Maria in connection with the attempted murder case. On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head in the Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. CCTV footage showed that Hadi was heading towards Bijoynagar on an auto-rickshaw when the two men wearing helmets on a motorcycle opened fire on him on the Box Culvert road before fleeing the scene. The assailants, wearing face masks, also took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for a few days. Physicians said that Hadi was seriously injured as a bullet pierced his head above the right ear, causing significant brain damage.

title: Ontik Technology hosts global tech experts
body: Ontik Technology recently hosted a delegation of global leaders from academia and industry, marking a significant step in strengthening Bangladesh’s growing engagement with the international technology ecosystem, said a press release. Javed Mostafa, dean and professor of the University of Toronto, Sam Oh, professor of South Korea’s Sungkyunkwan University, and Jin Hyeong Lee, chief executive officer of Data Marketing Korea, among others, comprised the delegation. Their visit to Dhaka emphasised growing opportunities for collaboration in research, data-driven innovation and industry-academia partnerships. Industry insiders said that the visit represented more than a ceremonial exchange, offering tangible opportunities for Bangladesh’s young engineers, researchers, and technology professionals to gain exposure to global standards, advanced research practices, and large-scale digital transformation projects. Such engagements can pave the way for collaborative research, skills development, mentorship and future partnerships, they said. During their stay, the guests were welcomed with the warmth of Bengali tradition and participated in discussions on technology innovation, data-driven solutions and strengthening links between academia and industry. Ontik Technology facilitated these dialogues, reinforcing its role as a connector between global expertise and local innovation. The visit concluded with an Autumn Soirée, an informal gathering of professionals from technology and other sectors, where participants exchanged ideas in a relaxed setting over traditional food and discussion. Organisers noted that the event highlighted the importance of human connection alongside technical collaboration. Observers believed such cross-border exchanges signal Bangladesh’s readiness to actively engage in the global technology conversation and contribute to shaping a more connected, innovation-driven digital future.

title: Assets worth Tk 66,146 crore attached at home, abroad
body: The interim government has attached and frozen movable and immoveable assets worth Tk 66,146 crore at home and abroad in more than 16 months in its efforts to check money laundering. Of these, assets worth Tk 55,638 crore have been attached at home and assets worth Tk 10,508 crore abroad, according to a review meeting by the National Coordination Committee, the apex committee for formulating and implementing policies for combating money laundering and terror financing, held at the secretariat in the capital Dhaka on Wednesday. Presided over by finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed, the meeting was told that 14 charge sheets had been submitted out of 104 priority cases in this connection. The meeting directed agencies concerned to file charge sheets as soon as possible on all priority cases. Investigations into money laundering allegations against business groups such as Summit Group, Beximco Group, Bashundhara Group, S Alam Group, Orion Group, Gemcon Group, Nabil Group, NASSA Group and Sikder Group have been prioritised by the interim government after it assumed power on August 8, 2024, after the ouster of the Awami League regime in the wake of a mass uprising. Bangladesh Bank governor Ahsan H Mansur said that they were looking forward to a quick settlement of the cases, now pending in London, against Saifuzzaman Chowdhury, an Awami League politician and former land minister. Mansur made the remarks after the committee meeting. Some 350 properties owned by the controversial former minister in London and various cities in southeast England have been frozen and put on auction by the United Kingdom’s National Crime Agency following requests from the Bangladesh interim government to seize illegal assets owned by Saifuzzaman. UK media has reported that steps have been taken to sell part of Saifuzzaman’s properties, valued at approximately £170 million (equivalent to about Tk 2,788 crore) in the UK, to settle his debts with creditors which include the Singapore-based DBS Bank and the British Arab Commercial Bank. Since Saifuzzaman did not contest the cases, Mansur expected that the outcome of the cases would favour them. Islami Bank Bangladesh and United Commercial Bank are also parties to that cases, though the exact time frame for repatriation of the funds remains uncertain, said the Bangladesh central bank governor. It may take until February, March, April, May or even June next year, he added. In May 2025, the BB governor said that about $18 to $20 billion was siphoned out of the country during the Awami League’s 16-year regime ousted on August 5, 2024. Responding to a question on the petition filed by S Alam Group owner Mohammad Saiful Alam at the World Bank’s arbitration forum, Mansur said that the Bangladesh Bank would take part in legal fight in Washington. In his petition, Saiful Alam, also known as S Alam, and his family members have claimed that they are citizens of Singapore. ‘But the BB will prove that S Alam is a Bangladeshi citizen,’ said the BB governor. The meeting also asked ministries and divisions to make necessary preparations for the forthcoming mutual evaluation by the Asia Pacific Group which assesses member countries’ anti-money laundering efforts. The meeting was participated, among others, by Anti-Corruption Commission chairman Mohammad Abdul Momen, principal secretary to the Chief Adviser’s Office M Siraz Uddin Miah, Finance Division secretary Khairuzzman Majumder and National Board of Revenue chairman Abdur Rahman Khan.

title: Biman equips baggage-handling staff with body cameras
body: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has introduced body cameras for baggage-handling staff at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport to strengthen security, transparency and accountability in handling baggage for domestic and international flights. As the Ground Handling Agent at the country’s main international airport, Biman has taken the technology-driven initiative to ensure safer and more transparent baggage operations for passengers, said a Biman press release on Wednesday. Under the initiative, it said, body cameras have been provided to traffic staff involved in baggage transportation. The system will allow continuous monitoring of the entire baggage-handling process - from unloading baggage from aircraft holds, movement through conveyor belts, to final delivery to passengers. The initiative will cover both Biman’s domestic flights and international flights of foreign airlines for which Biman provides ground handling services, ensuring a uniform standard of security and transparency across all operations. Biman officials said the measure would significantly enhance baggage security while improving operational transparency and staff accountability. In case of baggage-related complaints, recorded footage can be reviewed to verify incidents promptly and ensure timely and appropriate resolution. The national flag carrier believed the move reflects its commitment to adopting modern technology, maintaining professionalism and prioritising passenger-centric services, said the release. Biman Bangladesh Airlines reaffirmed that passenger safety, service quality and trust remain at the core of its operational priorities as it continues to modernise its ground handling services.

title: Govt suspends 14 secretariat employees over allowance protests
body: Bangladesh interim government has suspended 14 employees from various ministries and divisions following protests at the Bangladesh Secretariat demanding a special allowance. The action comes after a court accepted the chargesheet in a case filed against the employees. Different ministries and divisions issued notifications in this regard on Monday. On December 10, officials and employees staged protests in several offices of the Bangladesh Secretariat, demanding a Secretariat Allowance. During the protest, led by a section of the Bangladesh Secretariat Officers and Employees Joint Council, Financial Adviser Dr. Salehuddin Ahmed was confined to a Secretariat office for around six hours. Some employees leading the demonstrations were detained. Subsequently, a case was filed against them under the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2009 and they were formally shown as arrested. The employees are currently on remand in connection with the case. Among those suspended are Badiul Kabir, president of Bangladesh Secretariat Officers and Employees Sangjukta Parishad, vice-president Shahin Golam Rabbani and Nazrul Islam. Other suspended employees include Md Tayeful Islam, Bikash Chandra Roy, Islamul Haque, Md Mohsin Ali, Roman Gazi and Abu Belal of the Ministry of Health; Mizanur Rahman Sumon of the Ministry of Information; Kamal Hossain and Mohammad Alimuzzaman of the Ministry of Public Administration; Bipul Rana Biplob of the Ministry of Finance; and Nasirul Haque of the Cabinet Division.

title: Journalist Nahid Riyasad dies
body: Nahid Riyasad, the in-charge of the national desk at the Times of Bangladesh, died early Wednesday. He was 38. He died of a heart attack about 2:15am at his house at Rayerbazar in Dhaka, the family said. Nahid had a chest pain and was taken to Ibne Sina Hospital at Dhanmondi where he was pronounced dead. His burial will take place after his namaz-e-janaza in his home town of Narayanganj after his sister’s return from abroad. He is survived by his wife. Nahid, who began working with Newsnextbd.com in February 2012, joined New Age in September 2017 and moved to Drik Picture Library in July 2023 before joining the Times of Bangladesh in July 2025. He did his master’s in English literature and cultural studies at the University of Liberal Arts, Bangladesh in 2017.

title: Bangladesh does not need India’s advice regarding polls, says foreign adviser
body: Foreign affairs adviser Md Touhid Hossain on Wednesday said that Bangladesh does not want advice from neighbouring India on how its elections should be conducted, stressing that the government is committed to holding a free and fair election in which people can exercise their democratic rights freely. ‘Bangladesh’s neighbour is trying to admonish it over the elections. This is completely unacceptable,’ he said, mentioning that India did not issue similar calls for fair elections over the past 15 years. ‘We know we will hold a fair election, and we will do so,’ Hossain told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs while responding to questions. Earlier, India’s Ministry of External Affairs summoned Bangladesh high commissioner to India Riaz Hamidullah and said it was in favour of peace and stability in Bangladesh, adding that it had consistently called for free, fair, inclusive and credible elections conducted in a peaceful atmosphere. The adviser said summoning the Bangladesh high commissioner in New Delhi was a normal diplomatic practice, noting that the Indian high commissioner in Dhaka had also been summoned a few days earlier. Responding to another question, Hossain said it was difficult to say whether the already tense Dhaka–Delhi relations had taken on a new dimension. He also said no decision had yet been taken on downsizing the Bangladesh mission in India, adding that such a decision would depend on whether staff members had adequate engagement. Amid renewed tensions between the two neighbours, India’s MEA on Wednesday summoned high commissioner Hamidullah and briefed him on what it described as the activities of certain extremist elements that have reportedly announced plans to create a security situation affecting Indian territory. High commissioner Hamidullah was apprised of India’s strong concerns over the deteriorating security environment in Bangladesh. His attention was drawn in particular to the activities of some extremist elements who, India claimed, have announced plans to create a security situation around the Indian Mission in Dhaka. ‘India completely rejects the false narrative sought to be created by extremist elements regarding certain recent events in Bangladesh,’ the MEA said in a media release issued after the meeting. ‘It is unfortunate that the interim government has neither conducted a thorough investigation nor shared meaningful evidence with India regarding the incidents,’ the statement added. India said it maintains close and friendly relations with the people of Bangladesh, rooted in the Liberation War and strengthened through various development initiatives and people-to-people exchanges. India also said it expects the interim government of Bangladesh to ensure the safety and security of diplomatic missions and posts in the country in line with its international obligations. Meanwhile, in view of the ongoing security situation, the Indian Visa Application Centre at Jamuna Future Park in Dhaka closed at 2:00pm on Wednesday. ‘In view of the ongoing security situation, we wish to bring to your kind notice that IVAC JFP Dhaka will be closed at 2:00pm today,’ said a notification issued by the IVAC. The notification added that all applicants with appointment slots scheduled for submission on Wednesday would be rescheduled for a later date. The IVAC at Jamuna Future Park is the main integrated centre for all Indian visa services in the capital

title: SAD serves legal notice to CEC
body: Students Against Discrimination on Wednesday served a legal notice to the chief election commissioner, urging the Election Commission to announce that all candidates who contested the 12th parliamentary elections in 2024 are disqualified from contesting the upcoming 13th parliamentary elections, scheduled to be held on February 12 next year. The notice, sent on behalf of Students Against Discrimination president Rifat Rashid and drafted by Bangladesh Supreme Court lawyer Md Ishtiak Hossain, alleged that the 2024 election was a ‘dummy’ and non-participatory poll and was held in fundamental violation of constitutional democratic principles. The notice gave a seven-day deadline for the EC to launch an investigation into the roles of all candidates who contested the 2024 national election, implement legal measures to bar them from contesting the 2026 election, and issue a clear public decision on the matter. It warned that if the commission failed to act within the specified timeframe, a writ petition would be filed in the High Court Division under Article 102 of the constitution. According to the legal notice, the 2024 election lacked genuine political competition and failed to ensure effective voter participation. Candidates, whether representing the then ruling Awami League or contesting as independent ‘dummy’ candidates, are accused of providing a veneer of legitimacy to an undemocratic exercise. The notice said that the election had undermined the nation’s democratic framework and violated the constitutional mandate for free and fair elections. It also alleged that by facilitating the 2024 poll, the commission had failed to uphold its responsibility of conducting transparent and representative elections. The notice said that, on both constitutional and moral grounds, candidates who participated in undermining the democratic process should be declared ineligible for future elections. Leaders of the Students Against Discrimination on Wednesday afternoon served the legal notice at the commission headquarters in Agargaon, where they also held a meeting with the chief election commissioner. The delegation was led by the organisation’s president, Rifat Rashid, and included chief coordinator Hasib Al Islam and lawyer Md Ishtiak Hossain. Following the meeting, Rifat Rashid told reporters that they were deeply concerned that ousted and fugitive forces were conspiring against Bangladesh from abroad. He alleged that plans were being made to assassinate local leaders who uphold the spirit of July and speak in favour of Bangladesh. He said that the Students Against Discrimination would no longer compromise on these issues and warned that the organisation would move towards increasingly stringent programmes in the coming days.

title: 200 observers to monitor Bangladesh national election
body: The European Union would deploy between 175 and 200 observers to monitor Bangladesh’s 13th parliamentary elections, Election Commission senior secretary Akhtar Ahmed said on Wednesday. Briefing reporters at the Election Commission headquarters, he said that a tripartite agreement had been signed with the EU under which the commission would provide logistical support to the observers, including facilitation of movement and travel. Akhtar said that the commission had requested EU observers to comply with local protocols in certain areas, particularly in the Chittagong Hill Tracts. He said that the observers would bring some equipment and accessories into the country and would take those back on departure, for which they might submit a declaration upon arrival. The EC secretary further said that an administrative arrangement had been finalised between the European Union, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Election Commission, based on which the EU would send its delegation. Responding to questions about firearm licences for candidates’ security, the EC secretary stated that the issue had gained importance following recent instructions from the home ministry regarding security arrangements, including the provision of arms where necessary. Akhtar said that the commission did not see any immediate conflict between such measures and the election code of conduct. He also said that adjustments could be made in the election code of conduct, if required during the election period.

title: BNP leader shot dead at Ishwardi
body: A leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party was shot dead allegedly by his cousin at the latter’s home in Kamalpur village under Ishwardi upazila in Pabna on Wednesday. The deceased Biru Molla, 48, of the village, is the convener of Laxmikunda union unit of the BNP. According to locals and the police, Biru Molla’s cousin Jahurul Molla had dug soil from their family’s disputed land on Tuesday. At about 9:15pm on Wednesday, Biru went to Jahurul’s house with some people to discuss the matter, and, at one stage, an argument broke out, after which Jahurul and his son fired blank shots and asked them to leave, the police, quoting locals, said. As Biru and his companions did not leave, Jahurul and his son again opened fire and one of the bullets hit Biru’s head and he died on the spot. Iswardi police station officer-in-charge Mominuzzaman said, ‘Biru Molla went to Jahurul’s house to discuss a family dispute. At that time, he was shot from inside the house and died there.’ None was arrested and no case was filed in this connection until Wednesday afternoon, he said.

title: India shuts visa centre in Bangladesh capital
body: The Indian Visa Application Centre in Bangladesh capital Dhaka has been closed, reports ndtv.com. According to the report, the move came hours after India summoned Bangladesh’s high commissioner in New Delhi, Muhammad Riaz Hamidullah, to issue a formal diplomatic protest over recent threats to the Indian High Commission in Dhaka and inflammatory anti-India statements from Bangladeshi political leaders. ‘In view of the ongoing security situation, we wish to bring to your kind notice that the Indian Visa Application Centre in Jamuna Future Park in Dhaka will be closed at 2:00pm today. All applicants who have appointment slots booked for submission today will be given a slot at a later date,’ a statement from the Visa Application Centre said, reads the report available online. India has 16 visa application centres spread across Bangladesh.

title: DMP intensifies security through setting up additional check-posts across Dhaka
body: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police has intensified security through setting up more check posts in the capital on Wednesday to ensure public safety and maintain law and order. The check-posts were operational from 4:00pm at several strategic locations under different crime divisions of the DMP, said DMP deputy commissioner (media) Talebur Rahman on Wednesday afternoon. The areas include Bosila under Ramna Division; Babubazar under Lalbagh Division; Postogola Bridge, Matuail U-loop and Staff Quarter under Wari Division; Basabo Road (Kamalapur) under Motijheel Division; Gabtoli under Mirpur Division; 300 Feet Road under Gulshan Division; and Abdullahpur Bridge, Kamarpara and Dhaur Bridge under Uttara Division. Law enforcement officials said the checkposts will focus on monitoring suspicious movements, verifying vehicles and individuals, and preventing any untoward incidents. The DMP has urged city residents to cooperate with police personnel during the check-post operations in the greater interest of public safety and security.

title: 458,315 Bangladesh govt employees, expatriates register for postal voting
body: A total of 458,315 voters have so far registered through the ‘Postal Vote BD’ app to cast their votes in the 13th national election and referendum. Alongside expatriate Bangladeshis from different countries, government employees engaged in election duties and those staying outside their own voter areas are also registering through the app. Until 11:30am on Wednesday, 45,440 Bangladeshi voters residing inside the country registered under this category. The information was obtained from the postal voting update published on the Election Commission (EC) website.
