title: Khaleda now not fit for travelling: Medical Board
body: NN ONLINE: BNP Chairperson Begum Khaleda Zia is currently not fit to travel by air, according to the latest assessment of the medical board treating her at the capital’s Evercare Hospital. Dr AZM Zahid Hossain, one of her physicians, said on Saturday that Khaleda’s travel to London for advanced treatment will be delayed until she is medically declared fit to fly by an air ambulance. Some senior BNP leaders, however, said an air ambulance might arrive in Dhaka on Tuesday if she becomes fit to fly, and she could be taken to London on Wednesday. A doctor from the medical board, wishing anonymity, said on Saturday evening that Khaleda’s condition has slightly improved but she is still not able to travel. “Her condition is better than before, but not good enough for travel. We cannot say yet when she will be able to fly. The board is hopeful she will eventually be able to go abroad for advanced treatment,” he said. The doctor said Khaleda is given sleeping medication daily and she sometimes tries to speak. “She underwent an endoscopy on Friday, and some of her vital parameters have shown slight improvement.” He also said Dr Zubaida Rahman, Khaleda’s daughter-in-law, has been closely coordinating with the medical board. BNP Chairperson’s Adviser Dr Enamul Haque Chowdhury has been maintaining regular contact with Qatari authorities regarding the air ambulance. “We will request the air ambulance once the medical board gives final approval to take her to London. The Qatar government is fully prepared to provide it at any moment,” he said on Saturday evening. Earlier in the afternoon, Dr Zahid briefed reporters outside Evercare Hospital about Khaleda’s condition. He said the air ambulance could not arrive on Friday due to technical issues. Dr Zahid went on to say, “It is true that the air ambulance could not come because of a technical fault. At the same time, the medical board made an urgent decision that she should not fly in her condition at that moment. This has delayed the plan to take her abroad. In the coming days too, her physical condition will determine when she can be taken abroad.” Dr Zahid said an air ambulance is always ready, but Khaleda’s proper treatment and safety are the top priority. “Local and foreign doctors — from the UK, USA and China — are working together on her treatment,” he noted. He also said the medical board members have been treating Khaleda for the past six years under very challenging circumstances. “Whenever she becomes fit, she will fly. We are fully prepared to take her abroad. But the decision depends entirely on when the board feels she is physically stable enough for safe transfer. A 12 to 14-hour flight at high altitude can cause major physical stress, which a sick patient may not tolerate. So please do not be confused by any misinformation,” he said. Dr Zahid urged people not to pay attention to rumours circulating on social media. “Out of respect and affection for the leader, I request everyone to avoid spreading or believing anything beyond the facts,” he said. Zahid expressed hope that Khaleda will recover again with prayers and proper care. “She has recovered from even worse situations before with Allah’s mercy and everyone’s prayers. We are hopeful she will recover this time too,” he said. The BNP chief has been receiving treatment at Evercare Hospital since November 23 and was moved to the Critical Care Unit on November 27 with multiple health complications. Khaleda’s treatment is being supervised by a medical board led by Professor Shahabuddin Talukder, with both local and foreign specialists involved. Dr Zubaida Rahman — also a member of the medical board — arrived in Dhaka from London to accompany her mother-in-law abroad once she is cleared to fly. On Wednesday, the board reviewed her latest test reports and recommended taking her abroad for treatment. She was initially expected to leave for London on Friday, but BNP later said the plan was delayed due to the air ambulance’s technical problems and her unfit physical condition.

title: Tarique Rahman may return home anytime: Amir Khosru
body: NN ONLINE: BNP senior leader Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury on Saturday (December 06, 2025) said their party’s Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman may return to Bangladesh anytime as all preparations for his homecoming have been completed. “Who is raising questions about Tarique Rahman not returning? I really don’t understand. Those who want to talk can keep talking. But we know he will come. He will return home very soon,” he said. While talking to reporters at a hotel in Banani, the BNP leader said that arrangements—from Tarique’s residence to his office—have nearly reached completion. “The work on preparing his office is also almost done. The party has already completed all necessary preparations based on his plans for Bangladesh. So, he can come back to Bangladesh at any time,” he added. Khosru, a BNP Standing Committee member, said those who are spreading rumours can continue doing so as there is no harm in it, since Bangladesh always has some people who like to gossip and they can stay busy with that. “I don’t know whether there are any other motives behind such rumours… There is no point in responding to these rumours anymore,” he said. Khosru also expressed the hope that BNP will form the next government with people’s support, and Tarique Rahman will lead the new cabinet as Prime Minister. “We believe that under his leadership, we will take the country forward, fulfilling the expectations and aspirations of the people,” he said. Replying to a question, the BNP leader said he is not aware of whether Dr Zubaida Rahman, wife of BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman, will enter politics or not. Asked about Khaleda Zia’s possible travel to London, he said her trip depends on doctors’ approval and the air ambulance is not an issue here. “The main question is whether she is fit for travel. We are waiting for the doctors’ decision.” “It is better for me not to comment on the medical side because these are very technical matters. The doctors who are treating her know everything, so it is better for them to speak about it,” Khosru said. He also said Khaleda’s travel abroad now completely depends on the doctors’ opinion. “They are working on that now and discussing the matter among themselves. So, whenever they make the decision, she will be able to travel, and then she will be taken for treatment.” The BNP chief has been receiving treatment at Evercare Hospital since November 23 and was moved to the Critical Care Unit on November 27 with multiple health complications. Khaleda’s treatment is being supervised by a medical board led by Professor Shahabuddin Talukder, with both local and foreign specialists involved. Khaleda’s daughter-in-law, Dr Zubaida Rahman — also a member of the medical board — arrived in Dhaka from London on Friday to accompany her mother-in-law abroad once she is cleared to fly.

title: Upcoming election a big test for law enforcers: Touhid
body: NN ONLINE: Foreign Affairs Adviser Md Touhid Hossain today said the upcoming 13th Jatiya Sangsad election is a major test for the country’s law enforcement agencies. “Chief Adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus said the upcoming election will be an ideal election, and the law enforcement agencies will have to remain vigilant,” he said. He made the remarks while speaking as chief guest at a view-exchanging meeting with Rangpur district officials at the Deputy Commissioner’s conference room this morning. Newly appointed Deputy Commissioner of Rangpur Mohammad Enamul Ahsan presided over the event. The Foreign Affairs Adviser said the present interim government wants to hand over the responsibility to the elected government through a fair election. “Law and order is at the root of everything. Although there were problems in the beginning, the situation is good now. The police have managed to organize themselves and integrate effectively,” he said. He emphasized that more importance should be given to the education and health sectors. He added that the present interim government has initiated some projects and hopes the next government will continue them. “Regarding potato exports, Md Touhid Hossain said the government is seriously considering them, but it is not easy since only two or three countries in the world import potatoes regularly.” On the export of human resources abroad, he said, “If you go abroad, you must go as a skilled person. Otherwise, the salary is low. Our country’s people do not go abroad as skilled people. Due to which they get low salaries.” He noted that there are many vacant nursing positions abroad and said skilled nurses can earn good salaries. He urged the concerned department to take initiatives in this regard. Newly appointed Superintendent of Police Mohammad Marufat Hussain, Civil Surgeon Dr Shaheen Sultana, Deputy Police Commissioner of Rangpur Metropolitan Police Md Tofail Ahmed, District Livestock Officer Dr Md Abu Sayeed, and other officials also spoke at the event. Earlier, a video titled “Rangpur, the center of progress in the northern region” was screened. Meanwhile, Foreign Affairs Adviser Md Touhid Hossain visited key places and establishments in the city and is scheduled to visit Rangpur Cadet College this afternoon.

title: Extra climate funding needed for women entrepreneurs: Adviser Farida
body: NN ONLINE: Fisheries and Livestock Adviser Farida Akhter has stressed the need for additional financing from global public-sector climate-risk funds to support women entrepreneurs and all others facing climate-induced vulnerabilities. “Those who run environment-friendly and sustainable businesses with climate risks in mind must be prioritised under these funds,” she said on Saturday at a seminar titled ‘Voices for Change: Putting Climate Action, Women Entrepreneurs, and SMEs in Bangladeshi Public Policy’ held at a city hotel. Farida said promoting women entrepreneurs should not only be about increasing numbers, but ensuring their visibility in economic activities. “Although institutions like Bangladesh Bank and SME Foundation provide special support for women entrepreneurs, the overall scope is still insufficient despite women making up 51% of the population. Women themselves must claim their rightful share of opportunities,” she added. Highlighting the significance of small and medium enterprises, Farida said SMEs are the largest source of employment generation in the country, offering 50–60% employment potential for women. Each woman entrepreneur, she noted, creates opportunities for several other women. Praising women’s financial discipline, she said it is a proven fact that women repay loans responsibly. “So, loan support for women should be expanded.” Turning to the impact of climate change, the adviser said earthquakes may strike once, but climate change is a daily crisis. Although Bangladesh contributes little to global carbon emissions, it remains among the seven most climate-vulnerable countries, she added. Recalling her experience as the head of Bangladesh’s delegation to COP30 in Belém, Brazil, Farida said women’s voices were not given due recognition in climate negotiations. She noted that non-environment-friendly agricultural and livestock practices in Bangladesh are contributing to increased carbon emissions. However, the ministry is working to reduce methane emissions by improving cattle feed. “Meanwhile, industrialised nations’ large-scale livestock production is responsible for far higher emissions,” the adviser added. Farida identified the fisheries sector as the biggest victim of climate change, with declining hilsa availability in rivers and the sea, and expanding low-oxygen zones in ocean areas posing grave threats to marine resources. Speakers at the seminar called for stronger participation of women entrepreneurs and SMEs in combating climate impacts, along with sustainable policy support for these sectors. They also emphasised women’s role in building a climate-resilient economy and the need to expand the SME sector, urging public-private collaboration to drive growth, create jobs, and achieve sustainable development goals.

title: Khaleda Zia’s leadership a nat’l asset: Asif Mahmud
body: NN ONLINE: The nation regards the leadership and wisdom of former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia as a valuable asset, Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Adviser Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain has said in a social media post. In a post on his verified Facebook page shared Thursday, Asif, also the Youth and Sports Adviser, said Begum Zia has long been an uncompromising and widely respected leader in upholding democracy, civil rights and political freedom in the country. “From the anti-Ershad movement to her courageous role against the authoritarian rule of Sheikh Hasina, her contributions remain a shining example in the nation’s political history,” he wrote. Asif Mahmud further said the country values her leadership and prudence as a national treasure. “We do not want to lose her. We seek the prayers of the people for the good health and speedy recovery of this guardian of the democratic process,” he added.

title: Zubaida Rahman visits Khaleda Zia at hospital today
body: NN ONLINE: Ailing BNP Chairperson and former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia’s daughter-in-law Dr Zubaida Rahman today visited her at the Evercare Hospital in the city. She reached the hospital at 3:20pm. Earlier, Zubaida Rahman arrived in Dhaka yesterday (Friday) from London. Upon arrival, she went directly to Evercare Hospital from the airport around 12:00 PM to see her mother-in-law. Then she stayed at the hospital for more than two and a half hours. Later, around 2:30 PM, she went to her ancestral home in Dhanmondi. She returned to the hospital again at night. Khaleda Zia was admitted to the hospital on November 23 after developing breathing difficulties due to a lung infection. Subsequently, she developed pneumonia. She also has pre-existing chronic conditions, including kidney, liver, arthritis, and diabetes issues. As a result, the situation is complex- treating one illness often has an adverse effect on another.

title: Khaleda Zia to be taken abroad when medical board would allow: Dr Zahid
body: NN ONLINE: BNP Chairperson’s personal physician and BNP Standing Committee Member Dr AZM Zahid Hossain today said that the transfer of BNP Chairperson and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia to London by an air ambulance for advanced treatment might be further delayed. He said, “The air ambulance that was supposed to take Begum Zia abroad could not arrive due to a technical glitch. Furthermore, the members of the medical board held an urgent meeting and decided that it would not be appropriate for her to fly at that moment. That is why the matter of taking Khaleda Zia abroad is being delayed, and perhaps it will be delayed further as well.” Dr Zahid made these remarks at a press briefing in front of the main gate of Evercare Hospital in the city. He said, “We have the full preparation for going abroad. She will be taken abroad whenever the medical board deems it appropriate.” “It must be remembered that when you air-fly for 12 to 14 hours, it is not always possible for an ill person to cope with the physical changes that occur in humans at high altitudes. Therefore, keeping this in mind, please do not be confused, and please do not try to spread any confusion. Her physical condition will dictate when she can or will be taken abroad for treatment.” Earlier, on December 4, Dr Zahid announced that Khaleda Zia will be taken to London sometime after midnight or early tomorrow morning (Friday) at a press conference. Mentioning that Khaleda Zia’s best treatment is being ensured, he said, “The highest standard of treatment and her safety and security, meaning the medical aspects are being prioritized for ‘Deshnetri’ Begum Khaleda Zia. The medical board, which includes doctors from the UK, America, China, and local physicians, is giving the most importance to her physical condition.” Appealing not to spread rumors about Khaleda Zia’s treatment and not to listen to them, he urged, “Various kinds of rumors are being spread on social media regarding Madam’s treatment. I would request you to stay away from these.” Khaleda Zia was admitted to the hospital on November 23 after developing breathing difficulties due to a lung infection. Subsequently, she developed pneumonia. She also has pre-existing chronic conditions, including kidney, liver, arthritis, and diabetes issues. As a result, the situation is complex- treating one illness often has an adverse effect on another.

title: Onion price surge again, yet veg stays elevated
body: Sr.Staff Reporter, Kishoreganj : The price of onion has slightly increased again. It has increased by about tk.10 per kg compared to last week. Even though the supply of winter vegetables has increased, the price is not decreasing. However, the price of green chilli has decreased by half compared to last week. The prices of other products including eggs, chicken and others are stable. Onion traders said that the prices have increased due to the news that they will not import. This has affected the wholesale and retail markets due to the increase in prices at the stockist and farmer levels. On the other hand, vegetable traders said that the prices of winter vegetables are still high in the production areas. Due to this, the prices are not decreasing in the wholesale and retail markets. This information was obtained by visiting in Kishoreganj ‘s Bara Bazar, kachari Bazar, Puranthana the on Thursday and talking to the traders. A month ago, the onion market suddenly became unstable. In a span of four to five days, the price increased by about 40 taka. The price per kg rose to 115 to 120 taka. Then, when the government decided to allow imports, the price started to decrease slightly. It gradually decreased to 105 to 110 taka. Last week, the commerce ministry said that there is sufficient stock of onions. New onions will also be available in the market soon. Therefore, to protect the interests of farmers, import is not being allowed. Hoarding traders are taking advantage of such government measures. As a result, prices are increasing again. Yesterday, onions were sold at a price of 115 to 120 taka per kg in the retail market of the capital. Accordingly, the price has increased by 10 taka per kg in a week. However, according to TCB, the price of onions is still 10 percent lower than last year. Meanwhile, although new round onions have not arrived in the market, leaf onions have arrived. They are being bought at 70 to 80 taka per kg. Rajon Miah, a wholesaler told the New Nation that, Government will not import onions. Therefore, the stockists have increased the prices again. Even though the supply of vegetables has increased in the market, the prices have not decreased. Except for two or three, most vegetables are priced above Tk 50 to 60 per kg. In the retail market, beans are being sold for Tk 80 to 100 per kg. A couple of weeks ago, the price was Tk 60 to 70. Like last week, a kg of beetroot, brinjal and scallion is being sold for Tk 70 to 80. Two weeks ago, a kg of dal and patol was Tk 40 to 50. Yesterday, it was sold for Tk 50 to 70. However, the price of flowers and cabbage has decreased by Tk 10 compared to last week. Medium-sized flowers and cabbage are being sold for Tk 40 to 50 per piece. Even though new potatoes have arrived in kitchen market , their prices are high. They are being sold for 80 to 100 taka per kg. Last week, the price of a kg was 140 to 150 taka. At the same time, the price of old potatoes has increased by 2 to 4 taka per kg. They are being sold for 24 to 28 taka per kg. Although the vegetable market is high, there is some relief in the egg and chicken market like last week. A dozen eggs from the farm are being sold for 120 taka. Although they have been seen being sold for 125 taka in the neighborhoods. The chicken market is also stable like last week. Broiler is being sold at 160 to 170 taka per kg and golden chicken is being sold at 260 to 280 taka per kg. The market for other daily necessities including fish and meat is as normal as before.

title: Int’l Volunteer Day 2025 observed
body: Staff Correspondent : Home Affairs Adviser Lieutenant General Md. Jahangir Alam Chowdhury (Retd.) said that volunteers play a key role in tackling national disasters, preventing accidents, and responding to humanitarian crises. To encourage young people to engage in volunteer work, coordinated initiatives from both government and private organizations are essential. The country needs more skilled personnel and volunteer teams for effective earthquake response. Without proper training, it is impossible to deal with major disasters, which is why the government is emphasizing advanced and modern training. He made these remarks on Friday morning at the Fire Service Multipurpose Training Ground in Purbachal, Rupganj, Narayanganj, while speaking as the chief guest at the International Volunteer Day 2025 celebration. The adviser also mentioned that 55,000 volunteers are being trained for disaster management. A total of 22 individuals were honored for their special contributions. He further said that the operation to recover heavy weapons ahead of the 13th National Parliament Election is ongoing. “There has been no failure on the part of the government in recovering the looted weapons,” he said. The police force works for the people, and if there are any issues within the force, there is room for providing suggestions. The government will accept such suggestions as recommendations. He also praised the ongoing activities of the interim government, formed following the mass student-public uprising in July-August, aimed at building a just and inequality-free Bangladesh. During the event, various volunteer organizations showcased their field activities and conducted training-based demonstrations. Officials from government and private institutions, local representatives, and volunteers attended the programme.

title: Nat’l grid receives add’l gas from Habiganj well
body: Brahmanbaria Correspondent : Following the completion of workover operations, gas supply from Well No. 5 of the Habiganj Gas Field has commenced to the national grid. The supply was officially inaugurated on Wednesday afternoon by Petrobangla Chairman Rezanur Rahman. Well No. 5, located in the Raghunandan area of Habiganj, was originally drilled in 1988. At present, the well is contributing 14 million cubic feet of gas per day to the national grid. After the workover process, daily production is expected to increase to 26 million cubic feet, meaning an additional 12 million cubic feet of gas will be supplied daily. Due to various technical complications, including water rise along with gas production, the authorities of Bangladesh Gas Fields Company Limited (BGFCL) undertook the workover initiative for Well No. 5. The project began on 24 October and was completed on 27 November at a cost of approximately Tk 75 crore. The inaugural ceremony was attended by BGFCL Managing Director Md Faruk Hossain, Workover Project Director Ismail Molla, and other officials associated with the project.

title: Mongla sea port regains momentum
body: Bagerhat Correspondent : Mongla Sea Port have returned to normal. At the same time, cargo handling, revenue income and net profit have increased. In addition, the modernization of the port has created a far-reaching prospect of importing and exporting transit goods to neighboring countries through Mongla Port. The information was given by Rear Admiral Shaheen Rahman, Chairman of the Authority, on Monday at the 75th founding anniversary and jubilee festival of Mongla Sea Port. He further said that in the last fiscal year (2024-25), the target of cargo handling at this port was 88 lakh 80 thousand metric tons, but at the end of the fiscal year, the port handled 1 crore 4 lakh 12 thousand metric tons of cargo. In addition to achieving the target, 1.5 lakh 32 thousand metric tons more cargo was handled. In addition, although the target of container handling was 20 thousand TEUs, 1 thousand 456 TEUs more containers were handled. On the other hand, the port earned a revenue of 343 crore 30 lakh taka at the end of the year. Although the port’s net profit target was Tk.20 crore 46 lakh 20 thousand, a net profit of Tk.62 crore 10 lakh was achieved. He further said, in the first five months of the current fiscal year, 356 ships arrived, 13,854 TEUs of containers were handled, 4,139 reconditioned vehicles were imported, and 4.4 million tons of goods were imported and exported. In addition, due to the procurement of modern equipment, it is possible to handle more than 24 containers per hour for the first time. Due to regular dredging in front of the port jetty, goods are being handled on the same ship at 5 jetties. This has created a far-reaching prospect of importing and exporting transit goods to neighboring countries through Mongla Port. On the other hand, the port, the lifeblood of the south-western region, is currently playing a special role in the country’s ongoing economy by importing food grains, cement clinker, fertilizer, motor vehicles, machineries, rice, wheat, coal, oil, stone, corn, oilseeds, LPG gas and exporting white fish, shrimp, jute and jute products, frozen food, crab, clay tiles, silk fabrics and general cargo, in addition to creating employment. Using Mongla Port, the transportation of goods of Rajshahi, Rangpur and Barisal divisions through land, water and railways is becoming easier and faster. Several projects are underway to make Mongla Port more modern and world-class, and some projects have been undertaken for future development, said Chairman Rear Admiral Shaheen Rahman. The journey of the Mongla Port Authority began on December 01, 1950. On the occasion of the 75th founding anniversary of the port, according to the enthusiastic lagan, at 12-01 am, all the domestic and foreign ships stationed in the Pashur Channel were whistled for one minute without interruption. Later, at 11-00 am, a rally was taken out from the port headquarters to the jetty gate of the port in presence of officials and employees and the chairman of the authority, Rear Admiral Shaheen Rahman, inaugurated the programme by flying balloons and pigeons. Later, the 75th port platinum jubilee festival was celebrated inside the port jetty by the authority’s member (Harbor and Marine) Commodore Md. Shafiqul Islam Sarkar, member (Finance) and director (Administration) (A:Da:) Kazi Abed Hossain (Joint Secretary), member (Engineering and Development) Dr. A. K. M. Anisur Rahman (Joint Secretary), Director (Board) Kalachand Singh (Joint Secretary), Captain Mohammad Shafiqul Islam, Harbor Master, Colonel Md. Firoz Wahid, department heads, officers and employees and port users were present.

body: Selim Reza, Sirajganj : Former president of Kazipur Upazila BNP Salim Reza has been nominated by party high command for Sirajganj 1 seat (four unions of Kazipur and Sadar). title: 3rd int’l conference held at CUET
body: Chattogram Correspondent : The Honorable Vice-Chancellor of Chattagram University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), Professor Dr. Mahmud Abdul Matin Bhuiyan, said that youth are the future builders of sustainable Bangladesh. The creativity, research and innovative vision of the youth will ensure a livable Bangladesh of the future. In today’s world, universities are not only knowledge-providing institutions but also the driving force behind innovation, policy influence and industrial transformation. He further said that in building and community construction, they should not only be environmentally friendly but also supportive of human health, inclusive and sustainable. Interdisciplinary and inter-institutional collaboration of architects, engineers. planners and researchers is essential to achieve such goals. He made these remarks while addressing the inaugural ceremony of the two-day international conference titled “3rd International Conference on Green Architecture (ICGA 2025)” organized jointly by the Green Architecture Cell of the Department of Architecture, CUET at the Central Auditorium on Thursday. The special guests were Mr. Md. Khalequzzaman Chowdhury, Chief Engineer of the Public Works Department of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh, Professor Dr. Muhammad Rashidul Hasan, Dean of the Faculty of Architecture and Planning, Professor Dr. S. M. Nazmul Imam, Head of the Department of Architecture, BUET, Conference President and Professor of the Department of Architecture, BUET, Dr. Ashikur Rahman Joarder, and Professor of the Department of Architecture, BUET, Dr. Zebun Nasrin Ahmed. The keynote speaker was Dr. Masa Noguchi and Urbana Bangladesh Principal Architect Mr. R. Kashef Mahbub Chowdhury. The closing speech was delivered by the Conference Secretary and Head of the Department of Architecture, CUET, and Professor Dr. Sajal Chowdhury. The program was moderated by 20th batch students of the Department of Architecture, CUET, Dr. Marma Opi and Nahrin Ahmed Nakshatra. It is to be noted that leading academicians, scholars and researchers from various countries including Australia, USA, UK, Canada, and Netherlands participated in the conference of the Department of Architecture. Two keynote speakers were present. A total of 16 technical sessions will be held in the conference. In addition, there will be a poster exhibition, a joint international PhD research seminar and 5 parallel workshops on environmental architecture. 6 PhD research from different countries will be presented. A total of 150 papers were submitted to the conference, out of which more than 80 papers will be presented in 16 sessions over 2 days and more than 40 posters will be presented. A two-day architectural project exhibition will be organized in the Department of Architecture on the occasion of the conference. Sponsors will be Nippon Paint, BSRM, Seven Rings Cement, DBL, Bangladesh Infrastructure Finance Fund Limited (BIFFL), Stella-Luxury Sanitary Ware, Techno Art Software and Nestle.

title: Tension erupts over BNP candidate selections in Rajshahi
body: Staff Reporter : Ahead of the 13th National Parliament Election, intense tensions have arisen within the local BNP over candidate nominations in four constituencies of Rajshahi. Protests and demonstrations demanding changes in nominations are taking place, and incidents of internal conflict and violence within the party have already occurred. Several clashes have left three people dead and many others injured. These internal disputes are posing significant challenges to the election process, and there are even fears of “rebel candidates” contesting in multiple constituencies. Local leaders and activists have alleged that candidates were imposed centrally without assessing grassroots realities or popularity. Meanwhile, due to the ill health of Begum Khaleda Zia, election campaigning has largely been suspended. Although no major incidents occurred in recent days, there are fears that serious internal clashes could erupt at any time. On 3 November, the central leadership announced the party-nominated candidates for 34 out of 39 constituencies in the Rajshahi division. According to the announcement, out of Rajshahi’s six constituencies, two received new faces while four were allocated to existing candidates. The nominated candidates for the six constituencies are: Rajshahi-1 (Godagari-Tanore): Md. Shafik Uddin,Rajshahi-2 (Sadar): Mizanur Rahman Minu, Rajshahi-3: Shafiqul Haque Milan, Rajshahi-4: D.M.D. Ziaur Rahman, Rajshahi-5: Professor Nazrul Islam, Rajshahi-6 (Bagha-Charghat): Abu Saeed Chand. Among these, local BNP members have demanded changes in four constituencies, excluding Rajshahi-2 (Sadar) and Rajshahi-6 (Bagha-Charghat). Local leaders claim that during the nomination process, consideration was not given to BNP leaders who remained loyal during difficult times. They also allege that candidates were imposed from the centre without evaluating their popularity or ground-level support. Supporters of the deprived aspirants have been protesting against the nominations. Since the announcement, followers of the four deprived constituencies have held protests, violent clashes, press conferences, road blockades with shrouds on their heads, and other forms of demonstration demanding candidate changes. There have even been attacks on the homes of supporters of nominated candidates by aspirants’ supporters. With reciprocal protests, the situation has escalated rapidly. However, the central leadership of BNP has not intervened, allowing tensions to grow further day by day.

title: Jatiya Party holds milad mahfil
body: Cumilla Correspondent : A doa and milad mahfil was organised by Jatiya Party in Chauddagram, Cumilla, for the well-being of former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia. Jatiya Party Presidium Member Kazi Nahid was present as the chief guest at the doa mahfil held at Meshtala in Munshirhat Union of the upazila on Wednesday afternoon. Doa and munajat were conducted by Maulana Salimullah, the Pesh Imam of Munshirhat High School Mosque. Munshirhat Union Jatiya Party leader Abdul Malek presided over the event, and Upazila Jatiya Party Organizing Secretary Obaidul Haque Patwary, Upazila Jubo Sanghati Convener Kazi Shahid, Munshirhat Tahera Khatun High School Headmaster Nasir Uddin Miyaji, Union Jatiya Party leader Nur Hossain Nuru, Jalal Ahmed BSC, Abul Kashem Bhuiyan, Subedar Titu Mia, Abul Hashem, Soleman Mia, Shafiqur Rahman, Mohammad Hossain, Nazir Ahmed, Istaq Ahmed, Abdul Barek, Azgar Ali and others were present. Chief guest Kazi Nahid said, “We believe that the situation that has arisen in the country in the last few days, if Allah Ta’ala keeps Begum Khaleda Zia alive, then the ongoing political crisis in the country will be resolved.” Former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia is the leader of all the people of this country. On the news of his illness, people from all over the country raised their hands and prayed to Allah Almighty for his health. Prayers are being held all over the country on the instructions of our party chairman Mustafa Jamal Haider. Begum Khaleda Zia has worked to overcome any crisis in the country at different times and in different situations in Bangladesh. The people of Bangladesh will not be able to forget Khaleda Zia’s contribution. She has fought to the death for democracy. The Awami League government has tried many times to send her abroad. She has said that if I die, it will be on the soil of Bangladesh, no one can force me to go abroad.

title: Tangail achieves T-Aman target, farmers seek fair price
body: Tangail Correspondent : Favorable weather conditions and timely guidance from the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) have resulted in a bumper yield of transplanted Aman (T-Aman) paddy in Tangail this year. With production exceeding expectations, farmers across the district are delighted, though many remain hopeful for better market prices. From early Agrahayan, farmers began harvesting Aman paddy, and the process is now in full swing across the district. According to the DAE, nearly 63 percent of the cultivated fields have already been harvested. Farmers and farm workers are currently busy drying, threshing, and storing the new crop. A visit to Digar village under Sahadevpur Union in Kalihati upazila revealed a festive mood as farmers harvest their fields. Many are using modern machinery, including combine harvesters, to speed up harvesting, while about 80-85 percent still prefer manual cutting to ensure better straw quality. Yards in the village are already filling up with fresh paddy, and women farmers are working tirelessly alongside men. This season, the cultivation target for T-Aman in 12 upazilas was set at 102,000 hectares. Due to government incentives and the supply of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, the actual cultivation reached 104,583 hectares-exceeding the target in most upazilas, including Kalihati, Ghatail, Mirzapur, Nagarpur, Sakhipur, and others. Farmers report that previous yields were around 14-16 maunds per bigha, but this year production has risen to 18-20 maunds. They say the increased yield has brought smiles to their faces. However, they stress that fair market prices are essential for ensuring profitability. Labourers engaged in harvesting are also benefiting from increased daily wages during the peak season. Abu Bakkar, a farmer from Digar village, said that despite some crop damage from natural causes and grain sterility, he expects a good yield of around 18-20 maunds from his two bighas of land. Another farmer, Abdur Jabbar, noted that although storms and rain caused lodging and some grain loss, he is optimistic about covering production costs if market prices remain favorable. Ashok Parvez, Deputy Director of DAE Tangail, said that the success came from regular field-level guidance, training in modern cultivation methods, improved seed management, and effective disease control. He expects harvesting across the district to be completed by the second week of December.

title: Political pressure to rise if NCT given to foreigners
body: Chattogram Bureau : Chattogram has become agitated over the initiative to hand over the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) to a foreign company. Demonstrations, human chains and protest programmes are going on every day inside and outside the Chattogram port. The issue is not limited to port-centric movements; it has also spread to national politics. Experienced sources say that if the interim government remains adamant on its decision, the unrest over NCT will increase further. NCT is one of the most modern container handling facilities in the country. Thousands of workers and employees of the country work here every day. It has been managed by a domestic company for the last 17 years, maintaining international standards. About 44 percent of the total containers at the Chattogram port are loaded and unloaded through this terminal. In 2007, where the average stay of a ship was 10-12 days, it has now come down to only two and a half days. In the 2022-23 fiscal year, NCT’s net income excluding expenses was Tk 574 crore. NCT has the world’s most advanced technology gantry cranes. 12 were required, 14 are operational. There are 33 rubber-tire gantry cranes, which have a service life of at least 20 years. Although the terminal has an annual capacity of 1 million containers, it handled about 1.281 million TEUs last year. With skilled manpower and modern management, it can now handle up to 1.3 million TEUs. In March 2023, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs during the Awami League government approved the operation of NCT under a public-private partnership (PPP). The International Finance Corporation (IFC) was assigned as the transaction advisor. In continuation of that project, the current interim government has taken the initiative to operate NCT under a G2G agreement with DP World of the United Arab Emirates. From 2007 to 2025, a total of 12.397 million TEUs containers and 8,791 ships have been handled at NCT. With improved infrastructure and efficient management, the country’s import and export costs have decreased, and the speed of port services has increased. There are currently four container terminals operating at Chattogram Port. The NCT, which is about a thousand meters long, is the largest of them. It can handle four ocean-going ships and one inland vessel at a time. Of the remaining three, 19 percent of goods are loaded and unloaded at the CCT and 37 percent at the General Cargo Berth (GCB). The Patenga Terminal, which was launched in June 2023, is not yet fully usable. Workers, employees, port-related organizations and the general public are regularly protesting against the possibility of NCT going to a foreign company. They claim that the terminal’s equipment, capacity and management skills are world-class.

title: Reception for meritorious students held
body: Moulvibazar Correspondent : A reception ceremony was held on Wednesday for the meritorious students of the newly established Paikpara MA Ahad Modern College in Kulaura Upazila of Moulvibazar, which achieved the highest average pass rate in this year’s HSC examinations. The programme took place at the college auditorium. Kulaura Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Md Mohiuddin attended the event as the chief guest. In his speech, he said, “Life is one. To build it, we must use every opportunity, because each opportunity comes only once. The HSC stage is a very important phase of your educational journey.” He advised students to attend classes regularly, stay attentive, build positive relationships with teachers and classmates, and continually learn new skills. He also urged them to reduce excessive mobile phone use. stressing that discipline and focus are essential for success. Congratulating the successful candidates, the UNO added that education alone is not enough-students must also develop practical skills aligned with workplace demands. Referring to the achievements of many prominent personalities from Kulaura serving in fields including administration, he expressed hope that today’s students would also reach similar heights through dedication and hard work. The programme was chaired by Shamsul Haque, Founder President of the college, and moderated by lecturer Alauddin Kabir. Special guests included Hajipur Union Parishad Acting Chairman Nur Ahmed Chowdhury Bulbul, College Principal Md Hanif, Founding Principal Chinmoy Dey, Kanihati High School Headmaster Fazal Uddin Ahmed, Executive Committee Member Chaiful Alam Saiful, Engineer Mizanur Rahman, Guardian Member Helal Ahmed, and Hajipur Girls’ High School assistant teacher Md Nasir Uddin, among others.

title: Controversial OC Ahad reposted in Gowainghat
body: Sylhet Correspondent : The OC posts of all police stations in Sylhet district have been reshuffled through a lottery. Gowainghat’s name is also on that list. And here the controversial OC Abdul Ahad is returning to duty again – who is known for praise and criticism. The reaction of the people of Gowainghat to his return to duty has become more intense this time. It has triggered a new discussion among the common people. Protests are going on on social media, with questions being raised in posts: ‘Will the previous story return to Gowainghat again?’ Gowainghat seems to have once again become the center of discussion. OC Abdul Ahad is generally known as the former OC of Gowainghat Police Station. In 2019, he was awarded the Best OC for his special contribution to maintaining law and order while in charge of Gowainghat Police Station. Under his leadership, significant success was achieved in crime prevention activities in the police station area. But there is also the opposite side of the coin in his career. Because his career has not been entirely sweet. In 2021, a case was filed against him under the Anti-Corruption Act, which has made him known as a controversial character. OC Ahad’s name came into discussion for the second time in 2019 for the arrest and torture of Chhatra Dal leader Annu Malik Liton and later for framing him in a drug case. In 2018, Gowainghat Police Station OC Ahad is accused of smuggling 450 crore taka from the country to India through hundi and accepting a bribe of 4.5 crore taka, Abdul Ahad. Liton’s family and party BNP claim that he was first disappeared, later ‘preparations for crossfire’ were made in the Jaflong tea garden area, when the matter became public, he was shown detained with 1 kg of heroin, and he was subjected to inhuman torture in police station custody. Liton’s family alleges that the heroin seized was actually flour and no forensic report was presented to the court. However, the police filed a chargesheet in the case. On October 5, 2023, the court ordered the death penalty for Liton. The case is currently pending in the High Court. Liton’s family and the BNP are expecting justice, claiming that the case is “formulaic and motivated”. In the wake of various past allegations, OC Ahad has received mixed reactions from locals. Many have expressed their anger, especially on social media. At the same time, Liton’s family says – “They will not stop until justice is done.” As soon as the news of today’s posting spread, a strong reaction began on social media. Local resident Rubel Ahmed wrote, “The previous line will be resumed… the devils will remain in peace.” Sadiqur Rahman, president of the Goainghat Reporters Club, commented, “Controversial OC Abdul Ahad is back in Goainghat. There has been a mixed reaction in the public mind.” Many are protesting on social media. Posts and statuses are saying, ‘Goainghat residents do not want him’ and are calling for his arrest to restore peace and stability to the police station. Public opinion is heated and controversial. On the one hand, his skills, experience and crime-fighting capabilities are being welcomed, while on the other hand, past allegations and controversies are being recalled. Goainghat is like a special ‘sweet police station’ for him-where his repeated returns have created new fears and expectations among the locals. Well-wishers say that OC Ahad’s reassignment is not only administrative, it could also affect the relationship between the local community and the police. Local businessmen, teachers and ordinary people are worried whether the police station will remain as stable and safe as before.

title: Disabled Persons’ Days observed
body: Sr. Staff Reporter : The 34th International Day of Disabled Persons and 27th National Day of Disabled Persons observed across the country on Wednesday. In Kishoreganj, Department of Social Services including District Administration have arranged with various programmes aimed at promoting an inclusive society under the theme “Build a disability-inclusive society, accelerate social progress.” Deputy Commissioner (DC) of Kishoreganj, Md. Aslam Mollah attended as chief guest and Civil Surgeon (CS) dr.Ovijeet Sharma, ADC(General) Mizabe Rahmat as special guests while Deputy Director (DD) of Social Services, Md. Kamruzzaman in the chair. Marking the day, a colorful rally was brought out in the town led by Deputy Commissioner (DC) Md.Aslam Mollah on Wednesday morning. A discussion meeting held at local Callectorate Conference room on Wednesday. Deputy Commissioner( DC) Md.Aslam Mollah said that persons with speech, hearing and physical disabilities are integral members of society. “They are our children; they are not a burden. We want to build a harmonious and beautiful Bangladesh with them,” DC added. Later, wheelchairs were distributed among helpless and elderly persons with disabilities as part of the day’s programme.

title: 40 bhori gold, Tk 20L robbed
body: Pabna Correspondent : At least Five gold shops and a house were robbed by some miscreants at night in Ashtomanisha Bazar of Bhangura Upazila of Pabna. The incident took place at around 2 am on Wednesday after midnight. According to local sources, miscreants broke the lock of the gold shop of Ratan Karmakar, Tapan Karmakar, Uttam Karmakar, Yusuf Ali and Attab Ali in Ashtomanisha Bazar and looted about 30 bhoris of gold jewelry and 5 lakh taka. Then they attacked Ratan Karmakar’s house, beat up his wife Jamuna Rani Karmakar and son Ranjan Karmakar and snatched about 10 bhoris of gold and 15 lakh taka in cash. The victims claimed that the robbers looted a total of 40 bhori gold and 20 lakh taka in cash. Ranjan Karmakar said that an armed gang of 8/9 people first broke the lock of the shop and looted the jewelry. Later, they entered the house and took the gold and cash hostage at gunpoint. When his mother took time to remove her jewelry, the robbers beat her up. When Ranjan tried to stop him, he was also beaten up and injured. He also said that they had two firearms and sharp weapons in their hands. Locals also said that the robbers came to Ashtomanisha Bazar in a speedboat and after the robbery, fled towards the below reaches of the Gumani River in the same boat. Md. Shafiqul Islam, Officer-in-Charge of Bhangura Police Station said that the police reached the spot as soon as they received the information. However, it is not yet known who was involved in the incident. On Thursday afternoon, Pabna Additional Superintendent of Police Crime and Ops Md. Rezinur Rahman, Assistant Superintendent of Police (Chatmohar) Manjurul Alam, Pabna DB Police OC Md. Rashidul Islam and members of the CID Crime Scene Team visited the spot and collected necessary evidence.
