title: Premier Div Chess to begin Wednesday
body: The Premier Division Chess League will begin on Wednesday (Dec 3) at the Bangladesh Chess Federation (BCF) hall in the city. Ahead of the league, the number draw of the participating team will be held tomorrow at the same venue. A total of twelve teams are participating in the League, organized by BCF. The participating teams are reigning champion Titas Club, reigning runner-up Manha’s Castle, Leonine Chess Club, Bangladesh Navy, Sports Bangla, Uttara Central Chess Club, Dipali Memorial Chess Club, Janata Bank Officers Welfare Society, Khelaghar Chess Association, Bangladesh Police Chess Club, E-Soft Arena Chess Club and Sadharan Bima Corporation Sporting Club.

title: Messi’s Inter Miami advances to MLS Cup final with 5-1 win over NYCFC in East final
body: NN ONLINE: Inter Miami booked a place in the MLS Cup final for the first time in the club’s history as Lionel Messi inspired a 5-1 victory over New York City FC in the Eastern Conference final on Saturday. Tadeo Allande stole the show with a stunning hat trick, scoring in the 17th, 23rd and 89th minutes, with the first two goals assisted by Jordi Alba and Sergio Busquets, who are set to retire at the end of the season. Mateo Silvetti and Telasco Segovia added the other goals for Miami. Messi set up Silvetti’s 67th-minute strike, recording the 405th assist of his career for club and country — believed to be the highest assist tally in football history. Inter Miami, the No. 3 seed in the East, will host the MLS Cup final on December 6 against either San Diego or Vancouver. This marks a dramatic turnaround for the club, which had never advanced beyond the first postseason round in its first five seasons. NYCFC’s lone goal came from Justin Haak in the 37th minute. Messi, who joined Inter Miami in 2023 when the club was mired at the bottom of the MLS table, has since helped transform its global profile. With a new stadium set to open next season and the Argentine star signed through 2028, Miami now stands just one win away from its first league title. Tennis star Carlos Alcaraz and members of the U.S. women’s national team were among those in attendance, as Messi once again proved to be the main attraction on and off the field.

title: Rajshahi recruits Pakistan duo to bolster squad for BPL
body: Agency : The Rajshahi Warriors have bolstered their squad for the 12th Bangladesh Premier League (BPL) by roping in Pakistan duo-Shahibzada Farhan and Mohammad Nawaz. The two Pakistan cricketers are considered as valuable assets in T20 format. Farhan, a top order batter is known for his aggressive stroke play. He has amassed 834 runs in 34 T20I matches at a strike rate of 129, hitting seven half-centuries along the way. This will be the right-hand batter’s maiden appearance in the BPL. Nawaz, an all-rounder is a seasoned campaigner, who proved his worth repeatedly in domestic T20 tournaments around the world. The left-handed batter who is also a dynamic slow left-arm orthodox spinner has already featured in more than 85 T20Is, scoring 839 runs at a strike rate of 135.98 while also bagging 83 wickets at an impressive economy rate of 7.21. He previously represented the Khulna Titans in the BPL.

title: BD make losing start in Hockey Jr. World Cup
body: BSS, Dhaka : Bangladesh made losing start in the FIH Hockey Men’s Junior World Cup when they suffered a 5-3 goals defeat to Australia in their opening group match held at Mayor Radhakrishnan Hockey Stadium in Chennai, India on Saturday. In the first quarter, Australia took lead in the very first minute through a field goal but Aminul Islam restored the parity for Bangladesh converting penalty corner in the 14th minute. The second quarter saw, strong Australia added three goals in their tally in the 18th, 22nd and 24th minutes by maintain their domination. In the third quarter, Amirul Islam reduced the margin scoring his second goal again converting a penalty corner in the 42nd minute of the match. In the last quarter, Australia further widened their margin scoring the fifth through a field goal in the 48th minute while Aminul reduced the margin for Bangladesh completing his hat-trick goal in the 59th minute of the match. Bangladesh will play their remaining group matches against South Korea and France on November 30 and December 2 respectively.

title: Bangladesh face China today
body: BSS, Dhaka : Motivated Bangladesh U-17 national football team take on host China in their fifth and ultimate group match of the 2026 AFC U-17 Asian Cup qualifiers scheduled to be held at Tongliang Long Stadium in Chongqing, China today. The match kicks off at 5.35 pm Bangladesh time. Both Bangladesh and China secured equal 12 points each from four. If Bangladesh able to win the Sunday’s encounter, then they would qualify for the AFC U-17 Asian Cup. Earlier, Bangladesh made a flying start in the tournament crushing Timor-Leste by 5-0 goals in opening group A match and thrashed Brunei by 8-0 goals in their second match. The boys in red and green again registered a massive 5-0 goals victory over Sri Lanka in their third match and defeated Bahrain by 2-1 goals in the second match. Seven group champions will secure places in the 16-team finals, joining hosts Saudi Arabia andeight other nations who have already qualified for the 2025 FIFA U-17 World Cup.

title: BPL drops players linked to fixing allegations
body: UNB, Dhaka : The Bangladesh Cricket Board has removed a group of players from the final Bangladesh Premier League (BPL) auction list amid ongoing concerns over alleged fixing links. While the board has not formally named the cricketers, seven players who appeared in the preliminary draft are missing from the final list, effectively confirming their exclusion. Those omitted are Enamul Haque, Mosaddek Hossain, Alauddin Babu, Sanjamul Islam, Mizanur Rahman, Nihaduzzaman and Shafiul Islam – all of whom have played domestic cricket, and in some cases for the national team. The BCB has not stated publicly that the omissions are linked to corruption allegations, but officials have reiterated their position that anyone suspected of involvement in fixing will not be considered for BPL participation. The board has also instructed franchises to submit, by last night, the names of officials they intend to include in their BPL backroom staff. In its advisory, the BCB urged teams to avoid hiring individuals under suspicion. Anyone identified in that category will be denied tournament accreditation, effectively barring them from taking part in team operations. Last year, following the BPL season, the BCB formed an independent three-member committee to investigate corruption concerns. The committee’s 900-page report recommended sidelining several players and officials from the upcoming edition. The findings were later forwarded to Alex Marshall, the BCB’s anti-corruption consultant, for further scrutiny. This year’s BPL auction will take place today at a five-star hotel in Dhaka. The opening ceremony is scheduled for December 24 in Mirpur, with the first match slated for December 26 at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium.

title: Brothers Union play goalless with PWD SC
body: Brothers Union Club split point with PWD Sports Club when their match ended in a tame goalless draw in the Bangladesh Football League held at Shaheed Barkat Stadium in Gazipur on Saturdayday. In the day’s match, both the teams got several scoring chances but failed to break the deadlock lacks of proper finishing. With the day’s outcome, the all-orange Gopibagh outfit Brothers Union Club secured seven points from four matches while PWD collected five points playing the same number of matches. Brothers Union Club will take on Bashundhara Kings while PWD meet Mohammedan Sporting Club in their next respective matches on December 5 and 6 respectively.

title: RB Leipzig held to draw by Moenchengladbach
body: Agency : RB Leipzig’s David Raum was left to rue a late shot that hit the woodwork as his side played out a goalless draw at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Friday that prevented them from making much of a dent in Bayern Munich’s lead at the top of the Bundesliga. The draw leaves second-placed Leipzig on 26 points, five behind Munich, who take on third-from-bottom St. Pauli on Saturday. Moenchengladbach are 11th with 13 points. After a tight, nervous first half, Moenchengladbach thought they had broken the deadlock through Franck Honorat three minutes after the break, but his goal was ruled out for offside after a VAR review, and the home side also had a penalty award overturned later in the second half. In a game short on goal-scoring chances, fullback Raum came closest to finding the net, but his shot in the 80th minute smacked off the inside of the far post and bounced away to safety, and despite a late onslaught from both sides, the game ended scoreless.

title: Germany, Spain draw 0-0 in Women’s Nations League final first leg
body: Agency : Germany dominated the first leg of their Nations League final against Spain on Friday but could not find the back of the net as they were held to a scoreless draw ahead of Tuesday’s second leg in Madrid. As the Germans attacked in wave after wave, Spanish keeper Cata Coll was outstanding in the first half, throwing herself around her penalty area to cut off angles and block shots, much to the frustration of the home fans. Germany forward Klara Buehl reached deep into her bag of tricks to try to break the deadlock, but her threatening dribbles and fizzing shots could not get the better of the Spanish defence, and the Germans were almost sucker-punched when Esther Gonzalez hit the woodwork for Spain just after the break. Despite rain falling steadily through the second half, Buehl never relented and she finally got a shot past Coll, only to see it bounce back off the foot of the left-hand post and away to safety. Winger Jule Brand followed up that effort with a shot that skimmed off the top of the crossbar in the 76th minute but despite 19 attempts on goal for Germany and nine for the visitors, neither managed to score, leaving the tie delicately balanced ahead of the second leg.

title: Bangladesh beat Bahrain
body: Sports Reporter : Bangladesh Under-17 Football team defeated Bahrain Under-17 Football team by two goals to one in their fourth Group-A match of the AFC Under-17 Asian Cup Qualifiers at Yongchuan Sports Centre in China on Friday. It was Bangladesh’s fourth consecutive win. Bangladesh Under-17 Football team will face China Under-17 Football team in their last Group-A match of the AFC Under-17 Qualifiers on Sunday. If Bangladesh can beat China, the Bangladeshi youngsters will qualify the final round of AFC Asian Cup, which will be held in Saudi Arabia. After a barren first half, Bayezid of Bangladesh put his team ahead in the 59th minute of the play. Manik of Bangladesh doubled the margin in the 72nd minute of the game. Juhair Ibrahim of Bahrain reduced the margin in the 85th minute of the clash. Bahrain got two opportunities in the injury time of the second half but Bangladesh defenders thwarted those attacks. Bangladesh began their Group-A campaign of AFC Asian Cup Qualifiers thrashing East Timor by five goals to nil on November 22. Bangladesh retained their winning streak crushing Brunei by eight goals to nil in their second Group-A match on November 24. The Youngsters of Bangladesh kept their supremacy after defeating Sri Lanka by five goals to nil in their third Group-A match on November 26. A total of 16 teams will take part in the AFC Under-17 Asian Cup. Nine teams have already confirmed their final round berth of AFC Under-17 Asian Cup. Rest of the seven teams will move into the final round after qualifying from the AFC Asian Cup Qualifiers.

title: Tigers-Ireland 2nd T20I today
body: Sports Reporter : Bangladesh Cricket team will face off Ireland Cricket team in their second Twenty20 International (T20I) cricket match today at the Bir Shreshtha Shaheed Flight Lieutenant Matiur Rahman Stadium in Chattogram, the port city of the country. The match will start at 6:00pm (Bangladesh Standard Time). Captain of Tigers Litton Das will lead his squad, while Captain of Ireland Paul Stirling will lead his side. Earlier, the Tigers tasted a 39-run loss to the visitors’ in the first T20I at the same venue on Thursday last. Towhid Hridoy alone fought back against Ireland bowling attack. He remained 83 runs. He hit seven fours and three sixers in his 50-ball innings. Before today’s match, the Tigers and Ireland faced each other in nine T20I matches. Of them, Bangladesh registered five victories, while Ireland posted three wins and rest of the one match ended without any result. Towhid Hridoy said to the journalists, ” You can criticise us. From your criticism we can get positive outcome. I request you to criticise us according to the logic. If you do that we shall get smoothing good.” He said, ” Earlier, we scored above 200 runs. But we conceded defeat. We also chased above 180 runs successfully. So, big score is not a factor. I hope we shall come out from the previous result.” ” We must try to achieve a good result. We shall play according to our plan and our duty is to execute our plan. We have to improve not only middle-order position but also top-to-bottom positions. If we can develop all the sides, we shall regain a good result.” Bangladesh T20I squad: Litton Das (Captain), Saif Hassan (Vice-Captain), Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon, Towhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali Anik, Nurul Hasan Sohan, Mahidul Islam Ankon, Mahedi Hasan, Rishad Hossain, Nasum Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Shoriful Islam and Mohammad Saifuddin. Ireland T20I squad: Paul Stirling (Captain), Mark Adair, Ross Adair, Ben Calitz, Curtis Campher, Gareth Delany, George Dockrell, Matthew Humphreys, Josh Little, Barry McCarthy, Harry Tector, Tim Tector, Lorcan Tucker, Ben White and Craig Young.

title: Abahani post first win in BFL
body: BSS, Dhaka : Ten-man Abahani Limited Dhaka registered their first win in the United Healthcare Bangladesh Football League (BFL) defeating Bangladesh Police Football Club 2-0 held at Shaheed Dhirendranath Datta Stadium in Cumilla on Friday. The breakthrough came for Abahani Limited in the 25th minute when Malian forward Souleymane Diabate scored the first goal converting a spot kick. Midfielder Enamul Islam Gazi doubled the lead scoring the second goal for Abahani in the 43rd minute of the match. Alamgir Mollah of Abahani Limited got the marching order by the referee following his double yellow cards. After the breather, Abahani Limited however got several scoring chances but failed to convert any due to lack of proper finishing. With this win, the traditional sky blue Dhanmondi outfit Abahani Limited raised their tally with four points from four matches while Bangladesh Police Football Club remained at their previous collection of five points playing the same number of matches. Meanwhile, in the remaining fourth round matches on the following day (Saturday), Fakirerpool Young Men’s Club face holders Mohammedan Sporting Club at Shaheed Miraj-Tapan Stadium in Manikganj, PWD Sports Club meet Brothers Union Club at Shaheed Barkat Stadium in Gazipur and Bashudhara Kings face old Dhaka outfit Rahmatganj Muslim and Friends Society at Bashundra Kings Arena in the capital.

title: Portugal clinch maiden FIFA U-17 World Cup
body: Agency : Portugal became FIFA U-17 World Cup champions for the first time after beating Austria 1-0 in a compelling Doha final on Thursday night. Anisio Cabral’s first-half strike proved the difference at Khalifa International Stadium, as the reigning U-17 European champions completed a dream 2025 double. Portuguese legend Cristiano Ronaldo congratulated the World Champions on Instagram, sharing an image with the message: “Giants! Congratulations, World Champions!” to his 668 million followers. Austria, competing in their first World Cup final at any level, battled tirelessly as they hunted a leveller and came agonisingly close when Daniel Frauscher struck the inside of the post late in the game. Portugal made a fast start and almost bagged an early opener when Duarte Cunha dragged a shot wide. Austria’s rapid counter-attacking has been a feature of their U-17 World Cup campaign, though, and from one such break Hasan Deshishku burst clear and forced a fine save from Romario Cunha. The Portuguese would strike the first blow, with Cabral applying the finishing touch from close range after a slick team move. It was his seventh goal of the tournament – only adidas Golden Boot winner Johannes Moser scored more, with the Austria star netting eight times. The Austrians have displayed impressive powers of resilience all tournament long and refused to buckle after falling behind. Early in the second half, Deshishku was denied again by Cunha, with the goalkeeper making a sprawling save from the striker’s curling free-kick. Cunha was in fabulous form, and he athletically tipped an Ifeanyi Ndukwe header over the bar to preserve Portugal’s lead. The goalkeeper was grasping at thin air when substitute Frauscher took aim on 85 minutes, but the Austrian’s effort came crashing off the post. The collective relief among the Portugal players was palpable, and despite some more late pressure from their spirited opponents, they held out to secure the nation’s maiden global title at U-17 level. Over the past 34 years, Portugal have produced some of world football’s greatest talents. None, however, managed to achieve what this generation of Mateus Mide, Anisio Cabral, Mauro Furtado and Co just have in Qatar, becoming FIFA U-17 World Cup™ champions. Since their back-to-back FIFA U-20 World Cup™ triumphs in 1989 and 1991, Portugal have been waiting for the moment they would once again climb to the top step of a global football podium. That wait ended on Thursday. The Portuguese, who became U-17 European champions earlier this year, captured the U-17 World Cup crown with a hard-fought 1-0 final victory over Austria at Khalifa International Stadium. “It’s a dream year,” said goalkeeper Romario Cunha, winner of the adidas Golden Glove. “Before the final, I received a message saying it would be one of the happiest days of my life, and I don’t think, not even in our wildest dreams, that we imagined we would win the World Cup. It’s a wonderful feeling.” The dream started to become reality back in May of this year in Albania. The team, expertly coached by Bino, won the UEFA European Under-17 Championship with most of the squad that would later go on to become world champions. That title secured Portugal’s return to the U-17 World Cup for the first time in 22 years, and it also prepared the group for their unprecedented achievement in Qatar. “My heart, it’s just full of joy,” proclaimed Mateus Mide, winner of the adidas Golden Ball. “I don’t know how to express what I feel, or what my parents feel. For now, it is just going to be the best year of my life.” As delighted as they were with the victory, Portugal’s youngsters never lost sight of the magnitude of what they had done. Not only had they never won this tournament before, but they also became the first Portuguese national team to win two major trophies in the same year. “It’s the best year of my life,” commented central defender Chelmik. “I won the Euros, and now the World Cup. Two dreams have come true in one year, and I couldn’t be prouder of myself, my team, my family, and everyone who helped us along the way.” Coach Bino, meanwhile, was part of the Portugal side that reached the semi-finals of the tournament back in 1989 (when it was called the FIFA U-16 World Championship). He had therefore been waiting more than three decades to experience a moment like this. “It will be years before something like this happens again, because it’s not easy,” said Bino. “With so many matches, so many teams, it’s a historic achievement for this generation, and that’s why I’m so proud to be their coach. I’m so thrilled with the boys’ performance, proud of the journey they’ve had. Reaching the final, with all the tiredness in their legs, we played so well against such a tough side. Huge credit to Austria too, who made it very difficult for us.” These world champions have a bright future ahead of them, but they know that what they’ve just done in Qatar will forever be part of Portugal’s history. It may feel like a dream, but it’s a reality built on the talent and determination of 21 young players. “It’s an unforgettable year,” said midfielder Bernardo Lima. “The feeling of lifting another trophy was unbelievable, but I think this one is just a little bit more special because we conquered the world, and we have taken Portugal to the very top. That’s what we wanted to do – and we have done it.”

title: Roma tame Midtjylland, Malen double earns Villa win over Young Boys
body: Agency : AS Roma ended Midtjylland’s perfect record in the Europa League with a 2-1 home win on Thursday, while a Donyell Malen double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 win over Young Boys where the Swiss away fans disrupted proceedings at Villa Park. Elsewhere, Celtic came from behind to win at Feyenoord. Midtjylland were the only side on maximum points after four matches but it was Roma who went in front at the Stadio Olimpico in the seventh minute. Zeki Celik’s floated pass into the box was met by Neil El Aynaoui’s crisp volley to put the Serie A leaders in control and Roma looked to have wrapped up the win seven minutes from time with Stephan El Shaarawy’s side-footed finish. The visitors pulled one back with three minutes remaining, substitute Paulinho’s goal making for a nervy ending for the home side. El Shaarawy rocked the crossbar with another effort as Roma held on and are now on nine points. Midtjylland still lead the table but Villa’s win moves the Premier League side level on 12 points with the Danes. Villa made their early pressure pay off in the 27th minute when Youri Tielemans sent a cross into the box and Malen rose between two defenders to power a header which the keeper could only push onto the upright on its way into the net. Young Boys continued to sit back and Villa took control three minutes from the break. Malen, sent through on goal by Morgan Rogers, skipped past a defender on his way into the box before calmly steering his finish into the far corner. Play was stopped for a few minutes after the goal as police dealt with trouble in the away end. Young Boys captain Loris Benito went over to plead for calm, as fans launched objects onto the pitch – not for the first time during the game. Malen had the ball in the net again after the break although he was denied a hat-trick by a Rogers offside in the build-up and the visitors looked to have pulled one back with their first chance of the game but Chris Bedia’s goal was also chalked off. Young Boys did net a 90th-minute goal through Joel Monteiro, who chested down a floated ball into the box before firing home but the Swiss side were unable to pull off what would have been a remarkable comeback having offered little at Villa Park. Celtic were 1-0 down by the 11th minute with Ayase Ueda scoring for Feyenoord and what could be Interim Manager Martin O’Neill’s last game in charge looked like ending in their third loss of the competition but they were in front by the break. Reo Hatate put in a looping ball towards the back post where Yang Hyun-Jun arrived to smash home and Feyenoord keeper Timon Wellenreuther, under pressure from Celtic’s Daizen Maeda, played a poor ball out that Hatate struck first time into an empty net. Feyenoord came close to levelling but Benjamin Nygren’s effort eight minutes from time sealed the win for the visitors.

title: Bangladesh take on Bahrain today
body: BSS, Dhaka : A confident Bangladesh U-17 football team will meet Bahrain today in their fourth Group A match of the 2026 AFC U-17 Asian Cup qualifiers at the Tongliang Long Stadium in Chongqing, China. The match kicks off at 1 pm Bangladesh time Bangladesh have enjoyed a dominant run so far, opening their campaign with a 5-0 win over Timor-Leste before routing Brunei 8-0 in their second outing. They continued their momentum with another emphatic 5-0 victory against Sri Lanka in their third match. The boys in red and green will conclude their group stage fixtures against hosts China on November 30. Under the tournament format, seven group champions will advance to the 16-team finals, joining hosts Saudi Arabia and eight other nations already qualified for the 2025 FIFA U-17 World Cup.

title: Arsenal stun Bayern to seize CL top spot
body: Agency : Arsenal beat Bayern Munich for the first time in a decade to maintain their 100 percent record in this season’s Champions League (CL) with a 3-1 home win sending Mikel Arteta’s side clear at the top of the group on Wednesday. Jurrien Timber headed Arsenal in front from a corner after 22 minutes only for teenager Lennart Karl to equalize for the six-time European champions before halftime. Arsenal dominated the second half though and displayed their enviable squad depth as substitutes Noni Madueke and Gabriel Martinelli scored the goals to make it five wins from five. It proved a quiet return to north London for prolific Bayern striker Harry Kane as his side suffered their first defeat of the season in all competitions. With Inter Milan losing, Arsenal are now the only team in the competition with a maximum 15 points and look all but assured of a place in the last 16. “We went man to man with them in the second half and I thought tonight we were outstanding,” Declan Rice, who covered every blade of grass in midfield, said. “The manager is so happy. It was a special European night.” Six points clear at the top of the Premier League and Bundesliga respectively and boasting flawless records after four games in the Champions League, Arsenal and Bayern Munich have been Europe’s stand-out teams this season. The sides met in the quarter-finals two years ago with Bayern edging it, but Arsenal have reached another level since that clash and went into Wednesday’s game on a 15-match unbeaten run in all competitions. While the 15th meeting between the clubs lacked jeopardy, given their strong positions in the group, bragging rights and psychological blows were up for grabs. It was Arsenal who emerged with both, thanks to a statement win that will reverberate around Europe. “Individually, we were immense,” Arteta said. “Today is another massive victory, now we go home, have a nice dinner and go to Stamford Bridge (to face Chelsea in the Premier League). The energy again we created in the stadium, it’s incredible.” Bayern, backed by a vociferous travelling army, oozed confidence early on but were stunned in the 22nd minute by the sort of devastatingly simple goal Arsenal have trademarked. Bukayo Saka swung in a corner, Myles Lewis-Skelly made himself a nuisance in front of Bayern keeper Manuel Neuer and Timber was free to glance a header into the net. The lead lasted only 10 minutes though as Bayern responded with another move right off the training ground. After a long passing sequence, Joshua Kimmich’s raking diagonal pass found Michael Olise whose volleyed pass across the goal was met by 17-year-old Karl who became the first player to score against Arsenal in the Champions League this season. While Kane, scorer of 26 goals for club and country this season, was largely shackled and taunted by the home fans, Karl was a livewire and should have scored again early in the second half when he burst through but shot straight at David Raya. After that Arsenal swept Bayern aside. Mikel Merino nodded a header down and just wide from a Rice corner, Cristhian Mosquera forced Neuer into a desperate block and the keeper then saved from Rice after the midfielder’s marauding run into the area. Bayern’s defense was creaking though and Arsenal’s pressure paid off in the 69th minute when Riccardo Calafiori fired in a cross from the left that fellow substitute Madueke turned in for his first goal since joining from Chelsea. Eight minutes later Neuer had a moment to forget when he charged out of his goal trying to cut out Eberechi Eze’s pass but got nowhere near the ball and Martinelli was left with the simple task of shooting into an empty net. Bayern slipped to third as one of four clubs on 12 points although with home games against Sporting and Union Saint-Gilloise next they are in good shape to seal a top-eight spot. “I have to congratulate Arsenal, in the end it was a deserved win for them,” Bayern coach Vincent Kompany said. “The first half I felt we could edge it but we allowed them to control the second half.”

title: Mbappe’s 4-goal bonanza earns Real Madrid comeback win at Olympiacos
body: Agency : Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe scored four goals, including the second fastest hat-trick in Champions League history, to earn them a 4-3 comeback victory over hosts Olympiacos on Wednesday. Mbappe’s first three goals came in a spell of six minutes and 42 seconds in the first half but it was a tough encounter for the Spaniards before they earned their first victory at Olympiacos on their fifth attempt, and ended a three-game run across all competitions without a win. Real moved up to fifth place in the standings on 12 points, with the top eight earning automatic qualification for the knockout stage and with three matchdays remaining. Olympiacos dropped to 33rd on two points. “The important thing was to win, to break the cycle, to feel that feeling,” said Real Coach Xabi Alonso. “The three points were also important, to be in the top eight. It was competitive and hard-fought, but we needed it. “In the Champions League, there are moments for everything, just like in the league. I really liked that at 1-0 we didn’t lose our heads, we played calmly and maturely and turned it around. We are back to winning ways, and we won in Greece for the first time.” He also had special praise for his top scorer. “Mbappe is very important, that goes without saying,” Alonso said. “His goals are fundamental, but that’s not all. His personality… teamwork, unity.” The visitors opened their account when Mbappe beat two defenders to slot in from Vinicius Jr’s assist in the 22nd minute, cancelling out Chiquinho’s goal that gave the hosts an eighth-minute lead. He then headed in an Arda Guler cross two minutes later, and before the Greeks had time to recover from the double strike, the France forward completed his hat-trick with another fine finish. The Spaniards were in complete control for the rest of the first half and also hit the woodwork through Aurelien Tchouameni but the hosts cut the deficit seven minutes after the restart through Mehdi Taremi’s close-range header. Mbappe looked to have restored order with a tap-in from yet another Vinicius Jr assist for his fourth goal on the hour mark but Olympiacos refused to give up. They scored again through Ayoub El Kaabi’s 81st-minute header and had Real firmly pinned in their own half as they piled on late pressure. El Kaabi went close again as did Gabriel Strefezza but they could not find another goal.

title: Noakhali Express sign Lankan star Kusal Mendis
body: Agency : Sri Lankan wicketkeeper-batter Kusal Mendis has officially joined Noakhali Express as their first major overseas signing ahead of the franchise’s maiden Bangladesh Premier League (BPL) campaign. The newly introduced team confirmed the signing through a statement on Facebook as they begin assembling a competitive squad for their inaugural season. Meanwhile, Khaled Mahmud Sujon will serve as the team’s head coach. According to BPL governing council regulations, franchises are allowed to directly sign two local players before the auction. Using that opportunity, Noakhali Express has roped in Soumya Sarkar and Hasan Mahmud. Ahead of the auction, several other franchises have also secured local players. Rangpur signed Mustafizur Rahman and Nurul Hasan Sohan; Dhaka picked Taskin Ahmed and Saif Hassan; Sylhet brought in Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Nasum Ahmed; Rajshahi signed Najmul Hossain Shanto and Tanzid Hasan Tamim; while Chattogram secured spinners Sheikh Mehedi Hasan and Tanvir Islam. Discussions with foreign players remain ongoing across multiple teams.

title: Mohammad Amir joins Sylhet Titans
body: Sylhet Titans, the newest franchise in the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL), continue to make bold and strategic moves ahead of the players’ auction. The team has now secured the signature of Pakistani pace star Mohammad Amir, adding experience, and proven match-winning ability to their bowling attack. Alongside Amir, the Titans have also signed talented Pakistani all-rounder Saim Ayub yesterday. On the local side, the franchise had already brought in two key Bangladeshi names, Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Nasum Ahmed, through direct contracts. With Amir, Ayub, Miraz, and Nasum on board, Sylhet Titans are shaping up as one of the most exciting and well-rounded teams entering their first-ever BPL campaign.

title: Two matches of BFL to be held today
body: BSS, Dhaka : Two fourth round matches of Bangladesh Football League (BFL) will be held at two separate venues across the country today. On the day, Abahani Limited Dhaka will take on Bangladesh Police Football Club at Shaheed Dhirendranath Datta Stadium in Cumilla while Arambagh Krira Sangha face Fortis Football Club at Shaheed Miraj-Tapan Stadium in Manikganj. Both the matches kick off at 2.30 pm. After the third round matches, the traditional sky blue Dhanmondi outfit Abahani Limited have one point while Bangladesh Police Football Club collected five points. On the other hand, Fortis Football Club bagged four points while Arambagh Krira Sangha collected one points. Meanwhile, in the remaining fourth round matches on the following day (Saturday), Fakirerpool Young Men’s Club face holders Mohammedan Sporting Club at Shaheed -Miraj Tapan Stadium in Manikganj, PWD Sports Club meet Brothers Union Club at Shaheed Barkat Stadium in Gazipur and Bashudhara Kings face old Dhaka outfit Rahmatganj Muslim and Friends Society at Bashundra aKings arena in the capital.

title: BPL set to start on Dec 19
body: Ending all speculations, the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL) governing council announced that the BPL T20 will kick off on December 19. The tournament will be held in a short window with the final scheduled to take place on January 16. A total of six teams will take part in the tournament although the governing council earlier informed that it will be a five-team event. However, Noakhali Express is the new edition of the tournament. Old two franchises– Rangpur Riders, Dhaka Capital and new other three teams– Sylhet Titans, Chattogram Royals and Rajshahi Warriors– are the other five to grace the 12th edition of the tournament. Speaking to the media today, BPL governing council member secretary Iftekhar Rahman Mithu revealed that a total of 500 foreign players put their name to play the BPL but they selected 250 amongst them. He also clarified to increase the number of teams, saying that: “We have taken the decision to increase the number of franchises from five to six to accommodate more local players.”

title: Estevao cracker for Chelsea leaves Yamal in shade
body: Agency : The eagerly-awaited teenage battle of Stamford Bridge was won in emphatic style by Chelsea’s Estevao on Tuesday as he capped a lively display with a fabulous goal in a 3-0 win, as Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal was as anonymous as most of his teammates. Estevao surged past two defenders before slamming an unstoppable shot into the roof of the net from a tight angle to put Chelsea 2-0 up in the 55th minute of their Champions League tie after an early Barcelona own goal, with Liam Delap adding a deserved third. Estevao had pushed and probed throughout a one-sided first half that ended with Barcelona reduced to 10 men, shooting wildly with his one good opportunity. But he oozed teenage self-confidence and after his memorable strike, he declared it the best moment of his fledgling career. “I don’t really have any words to sum up how I’m feeling – the perfect night,” the 18-year-old Brazilian said. “It just happened before I even knew it, I wriggled through. I hope to score many more, it was definitely the most special moment of my career. I am so happy my family were here watching.” Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca did his best to play down the result, and the hype around his teenage star, but could not help but appreciate the goal. “It’s a big win, especially as it’s Barcelona, but nothing has changed in terms of what team we are and what we can achieve,” he said. “Estevao had a very good game, not only for the goal, he helped the team with how we were pressing. “The goal reminded me of the one he scored against us in the Club World Cup – very similar, the same action,” he said of Estevao’s effort for Palmeiras in Chelsea’s 2-1 quarter-final victory in July. As the crowd acclaimed their new hero, Yamal was substituted late on after making absolutely no impact – though he was far from alone in his team on that front. And when Maresca was asked if Estevao reminded him of Lionel Messi, he was quick to shoot the idea down. “With him, Lamine, they are so young at 18 that if you start to talk about Messi, (Cristiano) Ronaldo, I think it’s too much pressure for young boys like them,” he said. “At 18, they need to enjoy, they need to arrive at the training ground happy, but when you start to compare them with the Messi or with the Ronaldo, I think it’s too much for them.”

title: Bangladesh look to dominate Ireland in T20I series
body: BSS, Dhaka : Bangladesh will look to start their T20I series on a winning note as they face off Ireland in the opening game of the three-match series today at the Bir Shrestha Shaheed Flight Lieutenant Motiur Rahman Stadium in Chattogram. The match is scheduled to begin at 6 PM and will be broadcast live on T-sports. This series will be Bangladesh’s final international assignment ahead of next year’s T20 World Cup, unless the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) arranges additional fixtures. Bangladesh comes into the series on the back of a dominant 2-0 Test series win over Ireland and will start as favorites in the T20I format as well. Despite their recent 3-0 whitewash at the hands of the West Indies in their last T20 series at home, Bangladesh’s track record against Ireland in this format is strong. The two teams have met eight times in T20Is, with Bangladesh winning five, losing two, and one match ending in a no result. The last time Ireland toured Bangladesh for a T20I series was just two years ago, where they managed to avoid a series sweep by winning the final match, which ended 2-1 in Bangladesh’s favor. That victory in their most recent meeting could provide Ireland with some motivation heading into this series. However, for both teams, the primary focus will be preparation for the upcoming T20 World Cup. While Bangladesh will be aiming for a series win to fine-tune their squad, the series offers valuable exposure for Ireland in subcontinent conditions ahead of global events. Bangladesh comes into this series after playing 27 T20I matches this year – making it their busiest year in the format. They will be without their key fast bowler, Taskin Ahmed, who has been granted an NOC (No Objection Certificate) by the BCB to play in the Abu Dhabi T10 league until November 30. The BCB has left out Shamim Patwari from the squad, with Mahidul Islam Ankon being called up for his first T20I appearance. Bangladesh: Litton Das (Captain), Saif Hassan (Vice Captain), Tanzid Hasan Tamim, Parvez Hossain Emon, Towhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali Anik, Nurul Hasan Sohan, Mahidul Islam Ankon, Mahedi Hasan, Rishad Hossain, Nasum Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Shoriful Islam and Saifuddin. Ireland: Paul Stirling (c), Mark Adair, Ross Adair, Ben Calitz, Curtis Campher, Gareth Delany, George Dockrell, Matthew Humphreys, Josh Little, Barry McCarthy, Harry Tector, Tim Tector, Lorcan Tucker, Ben White and Craig Young.

title: Sylhet Titans rope in Saim Ayub for upcoming BPL
body: Agency : Sylhet Titans, the new franchise in the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL), set to sign Pakistani opener Saim Ayub ahead of the players’ draft. While local stars Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Nasum Ahmed have already secured on direct contracts, Ayub’s inclusion adds an international edge to the Titans’ squad. The Titans’ coaching panel also promises surprises, with Imrul Kayes set to serve as batting coach for the first time in the BPL, while discussions are ongoing with Syed Rasel as bowling coach. Final confirmations are yet to be officially announced. Sylhet Strikers had participated in the last three editions of the BPL. However, they did not express interest in taking franchise ownership for the next five years. Cricket With Sami, Bangladesh’s first full-fledged sports management company, has long been working with players.

title: Leverkusen shock City
body: Agency : Manchester City dominated possession, launched more attacks, and fired more shots, yet it was Bayer Leverkusen who left Etihad Stadium with a memorable 2-0 Champions League victory on Tuesday night. Alejandro Grimaldo broke the deadlock in the first half, and Patrik Schick doubled the lead after the break, securing a clinical win for the visitors. Pep Guardiola, mindful of a packed schedule, rested key players including goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, Erling Haaland, Phil Foden, and Jérémy Doku. All three attackers were brought on in the second half, but City could not overturn the deficit. City struggled early, lacking the speed and sharpness to penetrate Leverkusen’s organized defence. Although the hosts grew more threatening after halftime, the Bundesliga side adapted and capitalized on their chances. Leverkusen struck first in the 23rd minute when Malik Tillman’s counter cross led to Grimaldo firing a left-footed finish past the City goalkeeper. Just before the break, Tijjani Reijnders missed a golden opportunity to equalize. Despite Guardiola’s halftime substitutions, Leverkusen scored again in the 54th minute, with Ibrahim Maza’s cross met by Schick’s powerful header to make it 2-0. City pressed after Haaland and Rayan Cherki entered in the 65th minute, but Leverkusen’s defence held firm. Cherki’s free kick in the 85th minute was superbly saved, leaving City to suffer their first Champions League loss of the season.

title: South Africa condemn India to biggest home Test loss for series sweep
body: AFP, Guwahati : Spinner Simon Harmer took six wickets as South Africa (SA) romped to victory by 408 runs in the second Test for their first series win in India in 25 years on Wednesday. World Test champions South Africa bowled out a dismal India for 140 in a mammoth chase of 549 on day five in Guwahati for a 2-0 Test sweep. It is India’s biggest defeat at home by runs and a fifth loss in seven home Tests, having been whitewashed 3-0 by New Zealand last year. Off-spinner Harmer, 36, returned figures of 6-37 as South Africa clinched a Test series in India for only the second time, the first in 2000 under Hansie Cronje. Ravindra Jadeja resisted with 54 before Keshav Maharaj had him stumped and the spinner soon got the final wicket of Mohammed Siraj, with Marco Jansen pulling off a stunning catch in the deep. India lost the opening Test in Kolkata inside three on a pitch with uneven bounce before South Africa once again beat the hosts in their own game of spin on a batting-friendly track. The visitors declared their second innings on 260-5 on day four to hand India a record chase but the hosts batting once again failed and they never threatened to get close. India rode their luck early in the day when Jansen had Sai Sudharsan caught behind but the delivery was declared a no-ball after the bowler overstepped. The batter was on four. In the next over another overnight batter Kuldeep Yadav survived a reprieve on four when Aiden Markram dropped him at first slip off Harmer. But the relief was short-lived for India as a relentless Harmer soon bowled Kuldeep for five for the first wicket of the day. The off-spinner then dismissed Dhruv Jurel, for two, three balls later and soon sent back skipper Rishabh Pant for 13 as India slumped to 58-5. The batters fell like nine pins on a pitch where South Africa posted 489 after they elected to bat. India were bundled out for 201 to concede a first-innings lead of 288 but South Africa did not enforce the follow-on and decided to bat again. Left-arm quick Jansen returned figures of 6-48 in India’s first innings after the bowler hit a quickfire 93 with the bat. South African all-rounder Senuran Muthusamy led the batting charge with his 109, his maiden Test century.

title: Mushfiq takes place 30th position, according to ICC rankings
body: Sports Reporter : Mushfiqur Rahim showed a splendid performance in the recently concluded two-match Test series against Ireland. Mushfiqur Rahim has taken 30th position as a batter, according to the latest International Cricket Council (ICC) rankings. ICC is the highest governing body of world cricket. He crossed seven steps to achieve the feat. Mushfiqur Rahim played 100 Test matches at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in the capital’s Mirpur recently. He is the first Bangladeshi batter who played 100 Test matches. He hit century in his 100th Test match. He was adjudged the Man of the Match for his outstanding performance. Ace wicketkeeper-batter Litton Das also scored century at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium recently. He climbed eight spots to reach the 37th position as a batter. Experienced batter Mominul Haque also crossed eight steps to reach the 46th position as a batter. Promising batter Mahmudul Hasan Joy advanced two spots to reach 72nd position. Meanwhile, experienced left-arm bowler Taijul Islam also climbed four spots to reach the 15th position. He is now the highest wicket-taker of Bangladesh. Taijul Islam crossed 250-wicket land-mark after playing 57 Test matches. He achieved a number of records in the outgoing two-match Test series against Ireland. He was adjudged the Player of the Series for his outstanding performance.

title: AFC U-17 Asian Cup Qualifiers Bangladesh beat Sri Lanka
body: Sports Reporter : Bangladesh Under-17 Football team beat Sri Lanka Under-17 by five goals to nil in their third Group-A match of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Asian Cup Under-17 Qualifiers at Tongliang Long Stadium in China on Wednesday. Najmul Huda scored two goals, while Manik, Bayzid and Ikramul Islam netted one goal each. Earlier, Bangladesh blanked East Timor 5-0 in their first Group-A match on November 22 at the same venue. The Youngsters of Bangladesh thrashed Brunei Youth team by eight goals to nil in their second Group-A match at the same venue on November 24. Bangladesh Under-17 Football team will take on Bahrain in their fourth Group-A match at the same venue tomorrow. The red-and-green out-fit will face hosts China Under-17 Football team in their last Group-A match at the same venue on November 30. The champions of the Group-A of the AFC Asian Cup Qualifiers will get the tickets of the final round of AFC Under-17 Asian Cup scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia in May of 2026. A total of 16 teams will take part in the final round of the AFC Under-17 Asian Cup. A number of nine teams have already confirmed their final round berth. Rest of the seven teams will move to the final round after playing the AFC Under-17 Asian Cup.

title: FIFA announces procedures for 2026 World Cup draw
body: Agency : FIFA revealed Tuesday the procedures of the final draw for the 2026 World Cup, which will take place at John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington DC, the United States, on December 5. With less than 200 days to go before the kick-off of the 48-team tournament in Canada, Mexico and the United States, the three hosts and 39 qualified teams are allocated to four pots of 12 teams each, according to the FIFA Men’s World Ranking issued on November 19. The two playoff tournament winners and four European playoff winners, which are yet to be decided, are allocated to pot 4. The draw will begin with all the teams from pot 1 being drawn to groups A to L. It will then continue with pots 2, 3 and 4 in that order, FIFA said. The position A1 has already been assigned to Mexico, B1 to Canada and D1 to the United States, while the remaining nine top-ranked teams will be automatically allocated to position 1 in their respective groups. In order to have a balanced distribution of the teams, the highest-ranked team (Spain) and the second highest-ranked team (Argentina) will be randomly drawn into opposite pathways, and the same principle will apply to the third (France) and fourth (England) highest-ranked teams. In principle, no group will have more than one team from the same confederation drawn into it. This applies to all confederations except UEFA, which is represented by 16 teams. Each group must have at least one, but no more than two UEFA teams drawn into it. Following are the pots: Pot 1: Canada, Mexico, United States, Spain, Argentina, France, England, Brazil, Portugal, Netherlands, Belgium, Germany Pot 2: Croatia, Morocco, Colombia, Uruguay, Switzerland, Japan, Senegal, Iran, South Korea, Ecuador, Austria, Australia Pot 3: Norway, Panama, Egypt, Algeria, Scotland, Paraguay, Tunisia, Cote d’Ivoire, Uzbekistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Africa Pot 4: Jordan, Cape Verde, Ghana, Curacao, Haiti, New Zealand, European playoff winner A, B, C and D, FIFA playoff tournament winner 1 and 2.

title: Seminar titled on ‘Social Protection of Female Athletes in Country’s Sports Arena’ held
body: Agency : Although women’s participation in sports of Bangladesh is increasing day by day, their social protection is still facing challenge. Various obstacles and risks in the family, society, institutions and sports structures are hindering women’s sports career. To overcome this problem, a seminar titled on “Social Protection of Female Athletes in the Country’s Sports Arena” was held at the Audio Visual Center of Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protisthan (BKSP) recently. The seminar presided by BKSP Director General Brigadier General Md. Munirul Islam. The ideas, opinions, and experiences that the speakers shared about female athletes at the seminar enriched everyone present. According to them, the social protection of female athletes is not just an institutional issue, it is also a social responsibility, a national need. Speaking at the seminar, BKSP Director General Brigadier General Md. Munirul Islam congratulated the female athletes for the glory they are bringing to the country and the nation despite many limitations and adversities. He also spoke about creating a safe, dignified, and supportive environment for female athletes. He spoke of a collective effort to build a sports arena where male and female players are assured of equal opportunities, dignity, safety, and financial benefits (including salary and allowances). All current female players of BKSP, former players, teachers of BKSP College, female coaches, were among others, were present at the seminar.

title: Azerbaijan Women’s Football team in the city
body: Azerbaijan Women’s Football team arrived in the city on Tuesday morning to take part in the Tri-Nation Football series at the National Stadium in Dhaka. The other two teams of the Tri-Nation series are: Hosts Bangladesh Women’s Football team and Malaysia Women’s Football team. Bangladesh women, Azerbaijan women and Malaysia women will face each other in the single league basis Tri-Nation series. Bangladesh Women’s Football team will play for the first time Azerbaijan Women’s Football team. Azerbaijan Women’s Football team are from Europe. Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) has arranged the Tri-Nation series ahead of AFC Women’s Asian Cup final round. Bangladesh Women’s Football team created history after reaching the final round of AFC Women’s Asian Cup. The final round of AFC Women’s Asian Cup will be held in March of 2026 in Australia. After 12 years, Bangladesh Women’s Football team are going to play International matches at the National Stadium in Dhaka. Earlier, Bangladesh Women’s Football team played against Philippines Women’s Football team in a match of the AFC Women’s Asian Cup Qualifiers here in 2013. The three teams (Bangladesh Women’s Football team, Azerbaijan Women’s Football team and Malaysia Women’s Football team) were scheduled to take part in their respective practice sessions at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Tuesday.

title: ‘We will give the people good games’
body: Sports Reporter : Bangladesh will play in the Women’s Asian Cup Football in March 2026. Before that, Afeeda-Rupnara want to prepare them accordingly. Azerbaijan, Malaysia and Bangladesh Tri-Nation football series starts from Wednesday. Bangladesh will open their campaign against Malaysia on November 26 at the National Stadium before facing Azerbaijan on December 2. Azerbaijan, meanwhile, will play their opener against Malaysia on November 29. Bangladesh is ranked 104th and Malaysia is ranked 92nd in the FIFA rankings. Azerbaijan is ranked 74th. Bangladesh and Malaysia will face off at 7 pm. Bangladesh captain Afeida Khandaker has promised to give a good performance in the series. “We will definitely try to play well against Azerbaijan and Malaysia as the coaches have asked me to play. We practiced in the morning.The coach has told us how to play. Insha’Allah, we will do something good. We will give the people of Bangladesh a good game.” She said at a press conference on Tuesday, “We have clearly qualified for the U-20s. After that, we have also qualified for the Asian Cup in the senior team. Of course, there will be mistakes. We will learn from our mistakes and play in a way that will not happen in the next match.” Regarding the opponent, the captain said, “No matter what team they bring, they are definitely ahead in the rankings. We will try to win by playing our best.” In late October, Bangladesh played two friendlies against Thailand, suffering 3-0 and 5-1 defeats. Butler, unhappy with his players’ fitness levels at the time, has since spent three weeks in Chittagong addressing the team’s weaknesses.

title: Portugal edge Brazil to meet Austria in final
body: Agency : The Under-17 FIFA World Cup will have a new champion as Portugal and Austria reached their first-ever final on Monday. Portugal beat Brazil 6-5 in sudden death, while Austria pipped Italy 2-0. Austria’s recent momentum in international football continues, with the senior men’s team ending a 28-year wait to qualify for the FIFA World Cup. Now, the U-17 side has added to that rise, booking a place in the final after a brace from Johannes Moser. Moser, the highest goalscorer in the tournament (eight goals in seven games), opened the scoring in the 57th minute, converting a perfectly executed through ball, and doubled the lead with a superb free kick in second-half stoppage time. The other semifinal between Portugal and Brazil, however, turned out to be a rather cagey affair. Only four shots – two of each side – were on target in the entire game, while there were 35 fouls in the match. Brazil, the second most successful team in the competition with four titles, looked for an early breakthrough through Dell, nicknamed the Haaland of Sertão and currently the second highest scorer in the tournament with five goals in seven matches. However, Portugal goalkeeper Romário Cunha guarded the goal with authority, saving two of his attempts as the match trudged into penalty shootouts. Both teams converted the first four spot kicks, but Cunha missed the fifth penalty for Portugal, shooting it over the bar. Brazil could have won the game, but Ruan Pablo hit the woodwork. José Neto scored Portugal’s seventh penalty, and with his teammates waiting at halfway, Angelo Candido missed for Brazil, sealing Portugal’s place in its first-ever U-17 World Cup final. Austria and Portugal will lock horns in the final at the Khalifa International Stadium in Doha on November 27. The third-place match, between Brazil and Italy, will be played at the Aspire Academy in Doha earlier on the same day.

title: India, Pakistan to meet on February 15 in Colombo at T20 WC
body: Agency : India and Pakistan are set to clash on February 15 in Colombo during the 2026 T20 World Cup (WC), ahead of the ICC’s official schedule released in Mumbai on Tuesday. The high-voltage meeting set for the R Premadasa Stadium, will be the teams’ first encounter since their three fiery clashes at the 2025 Asia Cup. India and Pakistan have been placed in the same group alongside USA, Netherlands and Namibia. India open their campaign against USA in Mumbai on February 7, followed by matches against Namibia in Delhi on February 12 and Pakistan on February 15, before rounding off the group stage against the Netherlands in Ahmedabad on February 18. The group phase will feature three games per day. The tournament runs from February 7 to March 8 and will be co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka. Pakistan are scheduled to play all their group fixtures in Colombo or Kandy. The format mirrors the 2024 edition: 20 teams divided into four groups of five, with the top two from each progressing to the Super Eight stage, followed by semi-finals and the final. If India qualify for the Super Eights, their games will be held in Ahmedabad, Chennai and Kolkata. If they reach the semi-finals, Mumbai will host their match. Colombo or Kolkata will stage the other semi-final, depending on Sri Lanka’s and Pakistan’s progress. The final is slated for Ahmedabad, unless Pakistan qualify, in which case Colombo will host the title match. Alongside hosts India and Sri Lanka, the participating teams include Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, England, South Africa, USA, West Indies, New Zealand, Pakistan, Ireland, Canada, Italy, Netherlands, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Nepal, Oman and UAE.

title: Tanvir steers Barishal to 2nd victory in NCL
body: BSS, Dhaka : Left-arm spinner Tanvir Islam claimed a seven-wicket haul as Barishal registered second victory in the 27th National Cricket League (NCL), securing a six-wicket victory over Dhaka Division in their fifth round match at Cox’s Bazar Cricket Stadium on Tuesday. Tanvir ripped through Dhaka’s batting line up with 7-64, wrapping them up for just 169 in the second innings on Day 4, after they resumed at 124-5. His brilliant bowling gave Dhaka only a 102-run target for a victory and they overhauled the target, reaching 107-4 in 34.3 overs. Opener Iftekhar Hossain Ifti, who made 78 in the first innings, led the charge with the willow with 57 not out. His opening partner Adil Bin Siddik made 30. The openers added 41 runs after which Barishal tasted a hiccup, losing four wickets for 39 runs with Fazle Mahmud and Abdulah bagging duck. Ifti, however, stayed calm under pressure to lead the side to the victory. Earlier, Dhaka posted 273 in the first innings, thanks to Marshall Ayub’s 120, a knock which took him to 10,000 first class runs as the fourth Bangladeshi batter. Barishal replied with 341 all out, taking a 68-run lead that became instrumental in their victory finally.

title: BD meet Lanka today
body: BSS, Dhaka : Bangladesh U-17 national football team will take on Sri Lanka in their third Group A match of the 2026 AFC U-17 Asian Cup qualifiers at Tongliang Long Stadium in Chongqing, China, on Tuesday. The match kicks off at 12 pm Bangladesh time. Prior to the match Bayzit Bostami through a video message today said they have two big challenges ahead which they prepared to face. Bayzit, who scored two goals for Bangladesh in the last two matches, sought blessing to all so that the team can qualify for the final round of the Asian Cup. Earlier, Bangladesh made flying start in the tournament crushing Timor-Leste by 5-0 goals in opening group A match and thrashed Brunei by 8-0 goals in their second. Bangladesh will play their remaining group matches against Bahrain on November 28, host China on November 30. Seven group champions will secure places in the 16-team finals, joining hosts Saudi Arabia and eight other nations who have already qualified for the 2025 FIFA U-17 World Cup.

title: BD notch another massive win in AFC U-17 Asian Cup
body: BSS, Dhaka : Bangladesh U-17 national football team registered their second successive win in the 2026 AFC U-17 Asian Cup Qualifiers, crushing Brunei by 8-0 goals in their second Group A match held at Tongliang Long Stadium, Chongqing, China on Monday. The first goal came early in the 13th minute when Upu sent the ball into the net after receiving a pass from Faysal on the left. Rifat doubled the lead for Bangladesh in the 23rd minute as he dribbled past two defenders and finished with a clean shot. Faysal further widened the margin, scoring the third goal for Bangladesh in the 36th minute with a placing shot from close range off a pass from Riduan, while Manik made the scoreline 4-0 with a powerful shot in the 37th minute. After the breather, Upu scored his second and the fifth goal for Bangladesh in the 49th minute, taking a pass from Riduan. Rifat scored his second and the sixth goal for Bangladesh in the 73rd minute. Faysal took a long shot which the goalkeeper initially saved, but Rifat collected the rebound and scored his second goal of the match. Arif made the scoreline 7-0 in the 75th minute. The ball bounced around in a crowded penalty box and Arif got possession of the ball and executed it perfectly. Bayzit completed the winners’ tally, scoring the eighth goal for Bangladesh in the 79th minute of the match. Bangladesh created numerous chances throughout the match, with several attempts narrowly missing, including some that struck the goalpost. Earlier, on Saturday, Bangladesh made a flying start in the tournament, crushing Timor-Leste by 5-0 goals in the opening Group A match. Bangladesh, which has been placed in tough Group A along with hosts China, Bahrain, Brunei, Sri Lanka and Timor-Leste, will play their third group match against Sri Lanka on November 26, Bahrain on November 28, and meet hosts China in their ultimate group match on November 30. Seven group champions will secure places in the 16-team finals, joining hosts Saudi Arabia and eight other nations who have already qualified for the 2025 FIFA U-17 World Cup.

title: Mohammedan beat Abahani 3-2
body: Agency : Dhaka Mohammedan sporting Club defeated Dhaka Abahani Limited 3-2 in the first Dhaka derby of the season in the Bangladesh Football League (BFL) at the Shaheed Dhirendranath Stadium in Cumilla on Monday. Mohammedan took the lead in the 20th minute through Rahim Uddin. Emmanuel Keita doubled the margin in the 32nd minute, celebrating after turning in a looping ball from a Mozafar Mozafarov corner. The first goal stunned Abahani fans. From their own half, Mozafar Mozafarov sent a long pass forward. Samuel Boateng failed to break through the defence and lost possession. Rahim Uddin darted in from behind to snatch the ball. Abahani’s goal was left completely exposed, with Mitul Marma standing to one side of the post. Rahim gave him no chance, calmly slotting the ball into the net. After the break, in the 58th minute, Boateng headed in a fine cross from Jahid Hasan to pull one back for Abahani. In the 72nd minute, Abahani hinted at a comeback when Papon Singh carried the ball from midfield and struck from outside the box to find the target. In the 78th minute, an Al-Amin cross deflected off Mohammedan’s defence, falling kindly for Sheikh Morsalin, who made no mistake. With the scoreline at 3-2, the contest became even more intense. Abahani created several late chances but failed to score again. Last season, in the two league meetings between the sides, Mohammedan won once while the other ended in a goalless draw. In the day’s other matches, Bashundhara Kings beat Arambagh Krira Sangha 2-0 at Manikganj’s Shaheed Miraz-Tapan Stadium. Police FC played out a goalless draw with Fortis FC, while Fakirerpool Young Men’s Club lost 2-0 to Brothers Union.

title: India emerge champs in Women’s Kabaddi WC
body: Sports Reporter : India Women’s Kabaddi team emerged the champions in the Women’s Kabaddi World Cup (WC) defeating Chinese Taipei Women’s Kabaddi team by 35-28 points in a keenly-contested final at the Shaheed Suhrawardi Indoor Stadium in the capital’s Mirpur on Monday. It was second Women’s Kabaddi World Cup and India retained their title. Earlier, India clinched the title of the first Women’s Kabaddi World Cup. India led the first half by 20-16 points. They finished their 2nd Women’s World Cup campaign with an unbeaten note. By virtue of yesterday’s victory, India bagged gold medal, while plucky Chinese Taipei gained silver medal. On the other hand, hosts Bangladesh were satisfied with bronze medal. Sanju Devi earned the first point of the match with her opening raid. Chuang Ya-Han responded well with a bonus point. Pooja Nawal and Sonali Shingate then picked up points from their raids. In the fourth raid, Sanju secured three points, giving India the lead. Yen Chiao-Wen earned two points in a single raid to level the contest at 7-7. Chinese Taipei then took a 9-7 lead by executing a super tackle on Pooja, who had gone in to raid. In the 12th minute, Sanju dismissed four Chinese Taipei players in a single raid to push India ahead 13-12. Huang Su-chin scored in the next raid to keep Chinese Taipei in the contest. Later in the same minute, Sanju earned two more points and inflicted an all-out on the opponents, extending India’s lead to 17-14. India ended the first half with a 20-16 lead. After the break, Chinese Taipei reduced the margin with a bonus point. Pushpa Rana widened India’s lead with a three-point raid. Gradually, Chinese Taipei began to fall behind. At one stage, they reduced the deficit to 25-22 through pointsin both raids and tackles. But with India playing calculated kabaddi through Sanju and Pushpa, the match tilted firmly in India’s favour. With four minutes remaining, Chinese Taipei executed a super tackle in a final attempt to come back, bringing the score to 30-26. Near the end, India took control by inflicting another all-out on Chinese Taipei, pushing the score to 35-28 – which stood as the final scoreline. After the win, the Indian players took a victory lap around the venue, carrying the national flag. They celebrated their second consecutive Women’s Kabaddi World Cup title with dance and jubilation.

title: Flying at 40 Ronaldo scores stunning bicycle kick
body: Agency : Cristiano Ronaldo once again reminded the football world why he is regarded as one of the greatest of all time, scoring a breathtaking bicycle kick at the age of 40 as Al-Nassr defeated Al-Khaleej 4-1 in the Saudi Pro League on Sunday. The match was already decided, with Al-Nassr leading comfortably, but Ronaldo’s late strike, in the sixth minute of added time in the second half, added a spectacular flourish to the home victory. Nawaf delivered a precise cross from the right, and Ronaldo timed his leap perfectly, executing a powerful bicycle kick in mid-air. Despite the goalkeeper’s desperate attempt to reach the ball, it soared into the net. The Portuguese star then sprinted to the corner flag to celebrate with his trademark ‘Siuuu’ celebration, much to the delight of the fans. Ronaldo’s goal was the latest addition to a career filled with memorable strikes. It drew comparisons to a similar bicycle kick he scored seven years ago while playing for Juventus, demonstrating that even at 40, his fitness, technique, and vision remain exceptional. Earlier in the match, Al Nassr had taken the lead through João Félix, Wesley Ribeiro, and Sadio Mané, before Ronaldo added the cherry on top. On the path toward 1,000 career goals, Ronaldo now has 954, including 10 goals in nine Saudi Pro League matches this season. He sits just behind club teammate João Félix, who leads the league’s scoring charts by a single goal. Al Nassr remain top of the league table this season with a perfect record of nine wins from nine matches, accumulating 27 points. Title holder Al Hilal follow in second place with 23 points from the same number of games.

title: Bangladesh reach semifinal in Women’s Kabaddi World Cup
body: Sports Reporter : Bangladesh women’s kabaddi team reach semifinal of the 2nd Women’s World Cup after beating Thailand by 40-31 points in their final pool match at the Shaheed Suhrawardi Indoor Stadium in Mirpur on Saturday. The first half saw intense competition, with Bangladesh leading 14-12 at halftime. Thailand pushed hard in the second half, but the spirited Bangladeshi raiders, led by Rupa and Shraboni, maintained control, achieving a comfortable nine-point victory. The win gave Bangladesh six points in Group ‘A’, confirming their top-four position. Earlier, the team had beaten Uganda and Germany but lost to India in the group stage. Bangladesh will now play the semifinal match against Chinese Taipei, the runners-up of Group A. Iran will face defending champions India in the other semifinal on the same day. The semifinals will be held today at the same venue. With this victory against Thailand, Bangladesh also confirmed a medal in the ongoing World Cup. Bangladeshi players and officials have been expressing their expectations of a medal since the start of the ongoing tournament. There was jubilation in the red-green camp after securing a semi-final and a medal with a win over Thailand after a fierce competition. The team’s players and coaching staff responded to the cheers of the spectators in the gallery of Shaheed Suhrawardy Indoor Stadium by waving red-green flags. Raider Brishti Biwas of Bangladesh was named the player of the match for his impressive performance.

title: ‘Unity brings success for team’
body: Bangladesh raider Brishti Biswas said team’s unity enabled them to achieve resounding victory over Thailand in the ongoing Women’s World Cup. “I am feeling very good …many, many thanks to everyone. Our target was to defeat Thailand by giving our absolute best. We have achieved this, thanks to our coach, our secretary and everyone in our team. As we were united, so we have achieved the victory,” said Brishti after the match against Thailand. She said their goal now to play in the final and to go the final they are prepared to give their absolute best. Replying the question she said, “Yes, there was a bit of pressure, but we left everything up to Allah.” Our only target was that we had to win at any cost against Thailand. We never, not even one percent, not even for a second, thought that we would lose. Our morale was always high.”

title: BD make flying start in AFC U-17 Asian Cup
body: BSS, Dhaka : Bangladesh U-17 national football made flying start in the 2026 AFC U-17 Asian Cup Qualifiers crushing Timor-Leste by 5-0 goals in opening group A match was held at Tongliang Long Stadium, Chongqing, China on Saturday. The early breakthrough came for Bangladesh in the 11th minute. Rifat Kazi opened the net for Bangladesh with a header of a cross from Manik on the left flank. Manik doubled the lead scoring the second goal for Bangladesh in the 28th minute with a left-footed shot from the vantage position utilizing a free kick from Faysal. The third goal came for Bangladesh in the 43rd minute as Manik scored his second and third for team from the goal-mouth melee. After the resumption, Bangladesh continued their onslaught and added two more goals in the second half. Bayzit Bostami controlled the ball and finished confidently to make the score line 4-0 off a well-times pass from Azad and Akash Ahmed completed the tally with a stunning long-range shot in the 88th minute. Bangladesh created numerous chances throughout the match, with several attempts narrowly missing, including some that struck the goalpost. Bangladesh, which has been placed tough group A along with host China, Bahrain, Brunei, Sri Lanka and Timor-Leste, will play their second group match against Brunei on tomorrow(Nov 24), Sri Lanka on November 26, Bahrain on November 28 and meet host China in their ultimate group match on November 30. Seven group champions will secure places in the 16-team finals, joining hosts Saudi Arabia and eight other nations who have already qualified for the 2025 FIFA U-17 World Cup. Over the last nineteen years, Bangladesh’s best performances have been group runners-up finishes in 2017 and 2022. On both occasions, they came close to reach as one of the six best runners-up but ultimately fell short.

title: Marseille wallop Nice to climb top in France
body: AFP, France : Marseille climbed provisionally top of the French Ligue 1 on Friday after walloping woeful Nice 5-1 in a one-sided local derby with fireworks on and off the pitch. Marseille’s player of the season so far Mason Greenwood scored twice while former Arsenal frontman Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Timothy Weah and Igor Paixao were all on the scoresheet. Marseillle climbed to 28 points from 13 games while Paris Saint-Germain have 27 ahead of their home game with Le Havre on Saturday. PSG have been depleted by a string of injuries but have won their last two games with goals after the 90th minute. Aubameyang was unmarked when he tapped home in the 11th minute. Greenwood ripped Nice open down the right and scored either side of half-time. The Nice players were furious with a perceived elbowing and the bench joined the melee. Near the end an astonishing firework display in the Marseille section almost saw the match abandoned.

title: Bangladesh close in on victory
body: UNB, Dhaka : Bangladesh ended the fourth day of the Dhaka Test needing only four wickets to complete a commanding win over Ireland, after declaring their second innings at 297 for three and setting a target of 508. Ireland closed on 176 for six, stretched by grit but increasingly constrained by a surface breaking down beneath them. The day belonged once again to Bangladesh’s spinners, with Taijul Islam reaching a historic milestone. His three wickets in Ireland’s second innings lifted him to 249 Test scalps – surpassing Shakib Al Hasan to become the highest wicket-taker in Bangladesh’s Test history. Taijul has already taken seven in this match, bowling with the sort of accuracy and control that has defined his decade-long career. Harry Tector offered Ireland brief resistance with a spirited half-century, but he fell moments after raising the milestone, chipping a drive to mid-off. That dismissal reopened the innings, and Bangladesh pressed hard through the final hour. Curtis Campher remained unbeaten on 34 at stumps, joined by Andy McBrine, but survival appeared a matter of time rather than possibility. Earlier in the day, Bangladesh tightened their grip with a disciplined, confident morning session. Mominul Haque produced his 25th Test fifty, and Mushfiqur Rahim – fresh from his century in the first innings – moved into the 40s with characteristic calm. Their 106-run partnership framed a statement of control as Bangladesh stretched the lead past 500. Shadman Islam’s 78 anchored the early scoring before Andy McBrine pinned him in front, and Jordan Neill removed captain Najmul Hossain Shanto with a sharp bouncer. Ireland might have had more to show had Cade Carmichael held a straightforward chance offered by Mushfiqur at deep backward square – a pivotal moment that ensured Bangladesh’s dominance continued unbroken. The home side declared shortly after reaching 297 for three, adding to their first-innings 476. Ireland, who posted 265 in reply earlier, were left to withstand a relentless attack on a pitch offering sharp turn, uneven bounce and the occasional shooter. Hasan Murad delivered another canny spell of off-spin, while Khaled Ahmed added a wicket with the old ball. Ireland have battled with spirit throughout the match, showing clear signs of improvement and a willingness to absorb long spells. But against Bangladesh’s well-drilled spin unit – on a surface deteriorating rapidly – the challenge remains steep.

title: Head leads Australia to crushing defeat of England
body: BBC Online : England went down to a crushing defeat in the first Ashes Test as Travis Head’s blistering century completed an astonishing Australia fightback in Perth. In the first two-day Ashes Test since 1921, Head dismantled the England attack with the second-fastest Ashes hundred of all time, made off only 69 balls. Head’s 123 led Australia to their target of 205 in 28.2 overs – just a session of batting. An eight-wicket victory puts the home side 1-0 up in the five-match series. It was a devastating and rapid turnaround by the home side, who gave up a first-innings lead of 40 and were 105 behind when England reached 65-1 just after lunch. Led by Mitchell Starc’s 10-wicket haul, helped by some awful visiting batting, then pulling off a masterstroke to promote Head up the order, Australia extended English pain in this country. The record stands at 14 defeats and two draws in 16 Tests since 2011. England lost six wickets for 39 runs in 11 overs. A horror spell of 3-0 in six balls accounted for Ollie Pope, Harry Brook and Joe Root, ripping the guts out the middle-order. Though Gus Atkinson and Brydon Carse swiped a half-century stand, England were rolled over for 164 in 34.4 overs. They lost their last nine wickets for 99 runs. Australia faced making the highest score of the match in order to win, only for Head to play one of the all-time great Ashes innings. England were shellshocked. The pace bowlers that ran rampant over the Australia batters only 24 hours below were reduced to a rabble. The partisan Perth crowd revelled in the chaos. The only question was whether the game would bleed into a third day. Head ensured England have extra time for a post-mortem before the second Test, a day-nighter in Brisbane, begins on 4 December. Where do England go from here? They have suffered some crippling defeats in Australia. This will be among the most painful of all-time. Everything was in England’s favour: their bowlers spooked Australia on day one, their batters had control on the second morning, and Australia were hit by injuries to Usman Khawaja and Nathan Lyon. The way England unravelled was alarming in its speed and concerning for the rest of the series. Australia have not only become the first team to win a Test at this ground batting second, they have done it from behind in the game and without injured captain Pat Cummins. Much talk will centre on the pitch and the clatter of wickets. At 847 balls bowled, this was the shortest completed Ashes Test since 1888. The fact is, England were ‘Bazballed’ to defeat. When their batters tried to attack too early on the second afternoon, they let Australia back in. When Head gave England a taste of their own medicine, Stokes’ team wilted. Perth was supposed to be England’s chance to start the tour with victory. Somehow, they must regroup for Brisbane, and the day-night conditions in which Australia hardly ever lose.
