From fleets of private trailers to personal chefs and sprawling entourages, Bollywood stars’ ‘obnoxious’ demands are driving up production costs and putting a strain on the Indian film industry’s finances, insiders say...

title: BRAC Bank ATMs at 5 MRT stations now operational
body: BRAC Bank’s ATMs at the capital’s Pallabi, Mirpur-10, Farmgate, Shahbagh, and Bangladesh Secretariat stations of MRT Line-6 are now operational, said a press release. Beyond cash withdrawal, commuters can enjoy fund transfers, balance inquiries, card-less cash withdrawals, bKash cash-out services and other smart banking features through these ATMs. This initiative follows a strategic agreement between BRAC Bank and Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited, the operator of MRTs, to establish ATM and CRM facilities across MRT Line-6. BRAC Bank deputy managing director and alternate banking channels head Nazmur Rahim and DMTCL managing director Faruque Ahmed signed the agreement recently. Commenting on the ATM facilities at the MRT, Nazmur Rahim said, ‘By integrating banking access into daily commute points, we are making financial services faster, smarter, and more convenient for urban customers. We will enhance our ATM presence in key urban hubs and transport points to provide banking convenience to the people.’ At the signing ceremony, DMTCL project director Brigadier General (retired) Md Abdul Ohab, company secretary Khondoker Ehteshamul Kabir (joint secretary), BRAC Bank alternate delivery channels head Imtiaz Ahmed, regional head — distribution network Nakib Zaman, government relations head Khondker Emdadul Haq and cluster manager Sabina Sarmin were present. Currently, BRAC Bank boasts a nationwide network of 329 ATMs, 103 CRMs and 68 RCDMs.

title: BAFEDA holds 32nd AGM
body: Bangladesh Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association on Wednesday held its 32nd annual general meeting, said a press release. BAFEDA chairman Md Shawkat Ali Khan, also managing director and chief executive officer of Sonali Bank PLC, presided over the meeting. The meeting was held at a hotel in the capital. BAFEDA executive secretary Md Abul Hashem moderated the meeting. Members of BAFEDA executives committee, managing directors of AD banks, members of technical committee and head of treasury of member banks of BAFEDA attended the meeting.

title: MFS growth fails to dethrone cash
body: Cash transactions still dominated Bangladesh’s financial system in October 2025, accounting for 65.41 per cent of total transaction value, despite years of policy emphasis on building a cashless and digitally driven economy. National payment data published by Bangladesh Bank showed that cash and manual transactions remain deeply entrenched, raising questions about the pace and effectiveness of digitalisation efforts in the financial sector. According to the central bank data, total transactions in the financial system stood at Tk 26.67 lakh crore in October. Of this, Tk 17.44 lakh crore came from non-digital channels, including cash-based mobile financial services (MFS), over-the-counter banking transactions, cheque-based transfers, and ATM withdrawals. Digital transactions accounted for Tk 9.23 lakh crore, or 34.59 per cent of total value, indicating that nearly two-thirds of money movement still relied on non-digital methods The dominance of non-digital transactions contrasts sharply with government and Bangladesh Bank narratives promoting digital payments to reduce cash dependency, improve transparency, and cut transaction costs. Policymakers have repeatedly highlighted digital finance as a tool to curb illicit flows and widen financial inclusion, yet the data suggest structural resistance and trust issues persist. Banking sector transactions explain much of the imbalance. In October, non-digital banking transactions alone accounted for 62.23 per cent of total transaction value, driven mainly by cheque and voucher-based manual transfers worth Tk 8.91 lakh crore and cash deposits and withdrawals worth Tk 5.78 lakh crore. By contrast, all banking-sector digital transactions combined accounted for just 30.49 per cent of value, despite growth in real-time gross settlement (RTGS) and interbank digital transfers Mobile financial services, often seen as the backbone of Bangladesh’s digital finance drive, also show mixed signals. While MFS transactions made up over 83 per cent of total transaction volume, a large portion involved cash-in and cash-out activities. In October, MFS cash transactions amounted to Tk 84,754 crore, compared with Tk 1.09 lakh crore in digital MFS payments. Together, MFS contributed only 7.28 per cent of total transaction value, reflecting their continued use mainly for small-value transfers rather than broader commercial payments In June, non-digital transactions accounted for 68.25 per cent of total value, while digital transactions made up 31.75 per cent. By October, the digital share rose modestly to 34.59 per cent, but the non-digital share remained stubbornly high above 65 per cent. This marginal improvement suggests progress, but far slower than policymakers had hoped. Experts said that several factors are holding back digital adoption. Businesses and large traders still prefer cheques for high-value transactions due to habit, perceived security, and documentation advantages. Limited acceptance of POS and QR payments, concerns over cyber risk, service disruptions, and transaction charges also discourage wider use of digital platforms. In rural areas, weak internet connectivity and low digital literacy further constrain adoption. The data also showed that high-value payments continue to bypass retail digital channels. RTGS transactions, used mainly by banks and large corporates, accounted for nearly 22 per cent of total value in October, underscoring that digitalisation remains concentrated at the institutional level rather than across everyday economic activity. The continued dominance of non-digital transactions has broader implications. Heavy reliance on cash increases operational costs for banks, complicates monetary transmission, and limits traceability in the financial system. It also weakens efforts to formalise the economy and expand the tax base.

title: Depositors can withdraw up to Tk 2 lakh from Monday
body: Depositors of five crisis-hit Shariah-based banks that are being merged would be allowed to withdraw up to Tk 2 lakh each from Monday. BB officials said that customers of the five banks will be able to withdraw up to Tk 2 lakh per person from the banks’ respective branches. The payments will be made from the deposit insurance fund, marking the first concrete step toward compensating depositors following the declaration of the banks as non-viable. The banks under the merger process are First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, EXIM Bank and Union Bank. Bangladesh Bank has already given final approval to form Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, a new state-owned lender that will acquire and merge the five distressed banks. BB officials said that if a depositor holds multiple accounts within a single bank, they will be allowed to withdraw Tk 2 lakh from only one account. However, if a depositor has accounts in more than one of the five banks, they will be eligible to withdraw up to Tk 2 lakh from each bank separately. Earlier, on November 5, Bangladesh Bank declared the five Shariah-based banks non-viable due to severe capital shortfalls, widespread loan irregularities and persistent liquidity stress, and appointed administrators to oversee their operations. On November 30, the central bank approved the licence for Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, formally clearing the way for the merger. The merged bank will start operations with Tk 35,000 crore in paid-up capital and Tk 40,000 crore in authorised capital, making it the largest bank in Bangladesh in terms of capital base. It will initially remain under government ownership but will be run on professional lines, similar to a private commercial bank. Bangladesh Bank expects the government to gradually transfer ownership to the private sector within about two years once the bank stabilises and a strategic investor is identified. Shareholders of the failed banks, however, will not receive any compensation, as all five banks have negative net asset values. Trading in their shares was suspended on November 6, triggering concern among retail investors.

title: Credit card use jumps locally and overseas: BB
body: Credit card use in Bangladesh recorded a sharp rise in October, with both domestic transactions and spending by Bangladeshis overseas increasing significantly compared to the previous month, according to the Bangladesh Bank. According to its latest report, transactions within the country, expenditures by Bangladeshis traveling overseas and spending by foreigners within Bangladesh all showed an uptrend. The central bank’s data reveals that Bangladeshis spent Tk 534.02 crore using credit cards abroad in October, up from Tk 494.02 crore in September. This marks a significant increase of approximately Tk 40 crore within a single month. The United States remained on top in credit card expenditures by Bangladeshis. A breakdown of the top countries includes — the US Tk 72.06 crore, Thailand Tk 56.03 crore, UK Tk 52.02 crore, Singapore Tk 45.02 crore, India Tk 32.06 crore and Saudi Arabia Tk 31 crore. Other notable spending was recorded in Malaysia, the Netherlands, Canada, the UAE, China and Australia. There was also a boost in credit card usage by foreign nationals visiting or residing in Bangladesh. In September, they spent Tk 175.09 crore via credit cards, which rose to Tk 199.07 crore in October — an increase of roughly Tk 24 crore. The US citizens topped the list of foreign spenders in Bangladesh, accounting for Tk 44.02 crore in October. They were followed by citizens of the United Kingdom Tk 21 crore and India Tk 18 crore. The domestic credit card market also showed robust growth. Transactions within the country rose from Tk 3,395 crore in September to Tk 3,471 crore in October. This reflects an increase of Tk 76 crore in domestic consumer spending via credit cards in just 30 days. Economic analysts and the Bangladesh Bank report suggest that this upward trend is a strong indicator of increasing consumer confidence and heightened dynamism in both local and international financial transactions. The rise in overseas spending specifically points towards a recovery in international travel and global commerce participation by Bangladeshi cardholders, said the report.

title: Month-long textile, cottage industries fair begins in Rajshahi
body: A month-long textile and cottage industries fair began in Rajshahi on Thursday, aiming to boost regional economy through revival and promotion of handloom and cottage products. Women Entrepreneurs’ Association of Bangladesh, Rajshahi chapter has organised the fair on a field on the northern side of the Rajshahi Central Botanical Garden and Zoo to mark the organisation’s 22nd founding anniversary. Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Bangladesh Silk Industries Owners Association president Liaquat Ali said that reviving the handloom and cottage industries required a holistic approach, with particular emphasis on ensuring a business-friendly environment to encourage local entrepreneurs. He said that timely and effective measures were needed to revitalise the region’s industrial sector, including cottage industries, which played a vital role in economic development. Industrialist Hassen Ali said that handloom and cottage products reflected the true craftsmanship of Bangladeshi artisans, noting that many artisan communities across the country depended entirely on traditional crafts for their livelihoods. He stressed the importance of organising more such fairs to prevent further decline of handicraft products and called for increased investment in the sector to improve economic conditions in both urban and rural areas and to help break the cycle of poverty. WEAB Rajshahi chapter president Anzuman Ara Parvin Lipi said that women entrepreneurs engaged in handloom and cottage industries were contributing not only to their own livelihoods but also to the economic advancement of their families and society. She expressed hope that the month-long handloom, textile and cottage industries fair would positively impact the social and economic life of the Rajshahi region. Among others, local daily Sonar Desh editor Akbarul Hasan Millat, former Rajshahi Chamber of Commerce and Industry director Zia Uddin Ahmed, Rajshahi Raksha Sangram Parishad general secretary Zamat Khan, Bangladesh Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Rajshahi president Mariyam Begum and WEAB Rajshahi chapter general secretary Fatema Akter addressed the inaugural ceremony. According to the organisers, 45 stalls have been set up at the fair with participation from women entrepreneurs. Items on display include cane and bamboo products, Sirajganj handloom textiles, garments, crockery, food items, gift articles and a range of cottage industry products. The fair will remain open daily from 10:00am to 10:00pm until January 19, 2026.

title: Chevron, only foreign oil co left in Venezuela
body: The US oil company Chevron is walking a tightrope amid tensions between Washington and Caracas to retain its fragile position as the only foreign company allowed to exploit Venezuela’s oil reserves —- the largest in the world. Washington’s total blockade of oil tankers, added last week to punishing US sanctions, has put Chevron and its presence in Venezuela back in the spotlight. The Venezuelan Gulf Oil Company, Chevron’s predecessor in Venezuela, was founded in April 1923 and began operating its first well in August 1924. Initially operating near Lake Maracaibo, it then moved on to new deposits such as Urumaco and Boscan. Most reserves are now in the Orinoco Belt. Gulf Oil merged with Standard Oil of California in 1984, forming the giant now known as Chevron. The group currently extracts oil from four fields and offshore gas from another field, covering a total area of nearly 30,000 hectares (115 square miles). This is part of a partnership with the state-owned company PDVSA and its affiliates that employs around 3,000 people. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), in 2023, Venezuelan territory contained around 303 billion barrels, or about 17 percent of the world’s reserves. The US embargo on Venezuelan crude oil, in place since 2019, was relaxed in 2023 with licenses to operate in the country. But president Donald Trump revoked them all in the first half of 2025 before granting an exception to Chevron. Yet, according to an industry expert, recent presidential decisions do not affect the group’s activities. ‘We believe our presence continues to be a stabilizing force for the local economy, the region and US energy security,” the company told AFP, assuring that it operates in compliance with the law and “sanctions frameworks provided by the US government.’ Other foreign oil companies do not operate inside Venezuela because of the US embargo and a Venezuelan law that requires foreign firms to partner with PDVSA in majority state-owned ventures, a structure Chevron accepted when it was imposed. According to Stephen Schork, an analyst at the Schork Group consulting firm, Venezuela’s total production is around 800,000 to 900,000 barrels per day compared to more than 3 million at its peak. With its license, Chevron generates around 10 percent of Venezuela’s production, although sources differ on the exact figure. This currently represents around 150,000 to 200,000 barrels per day, 100 percent of which is exported to the United States. But the oil is high-sulfur ‘sludge,’ said Schork. ‘It is heavy, nasty stuff. You can’t move this oil in a pipeline,’ and it’s the hardest to refine, he explained. Because of the embargo, Caracas is forced to sell its oil on the black market at heavy discounts, mainly to Asia. But the new US blockade is expected to significantly reduce these illicit exports -- by up to 50 percent according to experts. The United States has refineries around the Gulf of Mexico that were specifically designed decades ago to process this highly viscous Venezuelan oil. Due to its lower quality, it is converted into diesel or by-products such as asphalt, rather than gasoline for cars. ‘The United States does not need this oil,’ noted Schork. If they want it, he believes, it is for political reasons. They want to ‘prevent the vacuum created by their departure from being filled by countries that do not share their values, such as China and Russia,’ according to a source close to the matter.

title: Why metal prices are soaring to record highs
body: Precious and industrial metals are surging to record highs as the year ends, driven by economic and geopolitical uncertainty, robust industrial demand and, in some cases, tight supply. Below AFP examines the reasons for the surge in demand. Gold and silver are traditionally seen as safe-haven assets, and demand has soared amid mounting geopolitical tensions, from US president Donald Trump’s tariffs onslaught to wars in Ukraine and Gaza, as well as recent pressure by Washington on Caracas. Investors are also uneasy about rising public debt in major economies and the risk of a bubble in the artificial intelligence sector. These uncertainties are driving up gold and silver, with other metals now starting to see the impact as investors seek to diversify their portfolios, explained John Plassard, an analyst at Cite Gestion Private Bank. ‘Metal is once again becoming insurance rather than just a speculative asset,’ he told AFP. Traditional safe havens like the dollar and US Treasuries have become less attractive this year. Uncertainty around Trump’s presidency and the prospect of further Federal Reserve interest rate cuts, have weakened the dollar, reducing its appeal to investors. As a result, many investors are turning to gold and silver. Gold has climbed more than 70 per cent this year and passed $4,500 an ounce for the first time on Wednesday, while silver reached a record high of $72 an ounce, with prices up about 2.5 times since January. A weak dollar is also boosting industrial metals, since commodities priced in dollars become cheaper for buyers when the currency falls. Industrial demand has surged in recent months, driven by the rise of artificial intelligence and the energy transition. Copper, used for solar panels, wind turbines, electric vehicle batteries and data centres, has seen strong gains as a result. Prices hit a record on Wednesday, topping $12,000 a ton, helped further by China, the world’s largest copper consumer, announcing new measures to boost demand. Aluminium, a cheaper alternative to copper, and silver are also benefiting from the AI boom and the shift to renewable energy. Platinum and palladium, used in car catalytic converters, have also risen, reaching a record high and a three-year high respectively, after the European Union decided to allow sales of new internal combustion vehicles beyond 2035. Copper prices have been lifted this year by fears of US tariffs, prompting companies to stockpile ahead of their introduction, with duties imposed on semi-finished products and potentially extending to refined copper. Supply risks from disruptions at mines in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Chile and Indonesia have added to the price surge. Physical markets for silver, platinum, and aluminium are also tight. According to Ole Hansen, an analyst at Saxo Bank, thin holiday trading, which increases volatility, and investor fear of missing out have further amplified the rise at the end of the year.

title: Tesla having a very bad year in the European Union
body: Sales of cars made by Tesla, the company run by Elon Musk, have slumped nearly 40 per cent in the European Union this year, data from the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association showed on Tuesday. The dive happened even though sales of electric cars across the bloc rose 28 per cent in the first 11 months of the year from the same period in 2024, according to the ACEA figures. Chinese manufacturer BYD registered the biggest jump in sales, up 240 per cent. Electric cars now account for 17 per cent of the EU car market, ACEA said, though it noted stronger consumer preference for hybrid-electric vehicles, which have 35 per cent of the market. Tesla sold a total 1,29,024 of its cars in the EU in the January to end-November period — well down from the 2,10,869 it sold last year. BYD was gaining on Tesla, having sold 110,715 cars so far this year, compared with 32,562 for the same period last year. Tesla has suffered reputational damage in Europe from its association with billionaire Musk, who backed US president Donald Trump before a falling-out, and who has endorsed Germany’s far-right AfD party. The company also faces increased competition from cheaper Chinese brands. The ACEA figures showed that Tesla’s slump in the EU continued in November alone, with sales sliding 34 per cent. The four biggest markets for electric cars in the EU are Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands and France.

title: European laws curbing big tech, irking Trump
body: The European Union is back in the crosshairs of the Trump administration over its tech rules, which Washington denounced as an attempt to ‘coerce’ American social media platforms into censoring viewpoints they oppose. The US State Department said Tuesday it would deny visas to a former EU commissioner and four others, saying they ‘have advanced censorship crackdowns by foreign states — in each case targeting American speakers and American companies’. Trump has vowed to punish countries that seek to curb US big tech firms. Brussels has adopted a powerful legal arsenal aimed at reining in tech giants — namely through its Digital Markets Act (DMA) which covers competition and the Digital Services Act (DSA) on content moderation. The EU has already slapped heavy fines on US behemoths including Apple, Meta and X under the new rules. Here is a look at the EU rules drawing Trump’s ire: Rolled out in stages since 2023, the mammoth Digital Services Act forces online firms to aggressively police content in the 27 countries of the European Union — or face major fines. Aimed at protecting consumers from disinformation and hate speech as well as counterfeit or dangerous goods, it obliges platforms to swiftly remove illegal content or make it inaccessible. The law instructs platforms to suspend users who frequently share illegal content such as hate speech — a provision framed as ‘censorship’ by detractors across the Atlantic. Tougher rules apply to a designated list of ‘very large’ platforms that include US giants Apple, Amazon, Facebook, Google, Instagram, Microsoft, Snapchat and X. These giants must assess dangers linked to their services regarding illegal content and privacy, set up internal risk mitigation systems, and give regulators access to their data to verify compliance. Violators can face fines of up to six per cent of global turnover, and the EU has the power to ban offending platforms from Europe for repeated non-compliance. Elon Musk’s X was hit with the first fine under the DSA on December 5, a 120-million-euro ($140 million) penalty for a lack of transparency over what the EU calls the deceptive design of its ‘blue checkmark’ for supposedly verified accounts, and its failure to provide access to public data for researchers. Since March 2024, the world’s biggest digital companies have faced strict EU rules intended to limit abuses linked to market dominance, favour the emergence of start-ups in Europe and improve options for consumers. Brussels has so far named seven so-called gatekeepers covered by the Digital Markets Act: Google’s Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, TikTok parent ByteDance, Facebook and Instagram parent Meta, Microsoft and travel giant Booking. Gatekeepers can be fined for locking in customers to use pre-installed services, such as a web browser, mapping or weather information. The DMA has forced Google to overhaul its search display to avoid favouring its own services — such as Google flights or shopping. It requires that users be able to choose what app stores they use — without going via the dominant two players, Apple’s App Store and Google Play. And it has forced Apple to allow developers to offer alternative payment options directly to consumers — outside of the App Store, hitting it with a fine of 500 million euros in April. The DMA has also imposed interoperability between messaging apps WhatsApp and Messenger and competitors who request it. The EU fined Meta 200 million euros in April over its ‘pay or consent’ system after it violated rules on the use of personal data on Facebook and Instagram. Failure to comply with the DMA can carry fines in the billions of dollars, reaching 20 per cent of global turnover for repeat offenders. The EU’s data protection rules (RGPD) have also tripped up US tech giants, with Brussels issuing numerous fines since they came into force in 2018. The rules require firms to seek the consent of users to collect personal data and to explain what it will be used for, and gives users the right to ask firms to delete personal data. Fines for violations can go as high as 20 million euros, or four per cent of a company’s global turnover. The EU has also adopted its AI act which will gradually bring in guardrails on using artificial intelligence in high-risk areas such as security, health and civic rights. In the face of pressure from the industry, the EU is considering weakening the measures and delaying their implementation.

title: Dow, S&P 500 end at records amid talk of Santa rally
body: Major US stock indices finished at fresh records Wednesday following a shortened pre-holiday session while gold and silver prices also struck fresh highs. Both the Dow and S&P 500 closed at all-time highs, drifting higher consistent with typical holiday season patterns. ‘It’s a continuation of a market that’s trading at a record high, and I think there’s a little bit of a seasonality bias that’s kicking in here without any upsetting news to alter the trend at the moment,’ said Briefing.com analyst Patrick O’Hare. ‘You have a bullish bias in this market, which is being helped along by the idea that 2026 has the potential to be another good year.’ Earlier, in a holiday-shortened trading session, London finished lower, Paris ended the day flat and Frankfurt was closed. Asian markets swung between gains and losses. Gold climbed above $4,500 for the first time and silver topped $72, as investors looked for safe havens amid US military and economic pressure on Venezuela. Geopolitical worries have grown as Washington continues to put pressure on Caracas with a blockade of sanctioned oil vessels sailing to and from Venezuela. Market watchers are hoping for a ‘Santa Claus’ rally in the sleepy period that comprises the last five trading sessions of one year and the first two in the next. The stretch between Christmas and New Year’s Day usually sees markets drift higher amid a dearth of major economic news. ‘What’s happening right now is we have a very strong setup and then we just need a bullish catalyst and it’ll take off and go,’ said Adam Sarhan of 50 Park Investments. The S&P 500’s fresh all-time high on Tuesday came after figures showed the world’s top economy expanded 4.3 per cent in the third quarter, the fastest pace in two years and much quicker than expected. The report provided some reassurance to investors about the economic outlook after a string of increasingly weakening jobs data. However, other figures were less upbeat, with a gauge of consumer spending falling for a fifth successive month to its lowest level since February 2021 owing to worries about jobs.

title: Hair oil business brings hope, job opportunities
body: The journey of Rakhi Saha, a housewife from Jessore, began with a simple and personal problem after severe hair loss following the birth of her second child. Who knew that this problem would spark a business venture that would not only change her life but also create employment to hundreds of people? In 2020, amid the Covid-19 pandemic, Rakhi was struggling with hair fall. Desperate for a solution, she turned to an age-old remedy passed down by her mother Durga Saha. This homemade treatment, made from a combination of natural ingredients like fenugreek, black cumin, neem leaves, aloe vera and coconut oil, not only solved her hair problem but also ignite a dream. ‘After using the oil, my hair fall decreased and new hair started to grow. This success gave me the confidence to do something for myself,’ she recalled. Encouraged by her newfound confidence, Rakhi shared her idea with her younger brother, Victor Saha, a graduate in computer science from the American International University in Dhaka. Victor, skilled in digital marketing, saw the potential to turn Rakhi’s home remedy into a business. Together, they founded ‘Naturals by Rakhi’ in 2021, with Victor taking the reins of digital marketing and branding. Rakhi began producing the oil at home, while Victor set up a Facebook page, creating a logo and promoting the product online. Starting with just a modest capital of Tk 1,700, the venture quickly gained traction. The first few orders were small, but gradually the number of customers grew rapidly. ‘In the beginning, we received only 2-4 orders a day. But soon, positive reviews started pouring in and our customer reached 40 per cent,’ says Rakhi. Unlike many competitors who made false promises such as hair growth in just seven days, Rakhi and Victor were determined to build their brand with honesty and transparency. ‘We focused on the quality of our product and were honest about the ingredients and production process,’ says Victor. This approach, combined with the effectiveness of their products, earned the trust of their customers. As demand grew, the Saha siblings set up a small factory with home-based equipment, employing over 100 workers. Today, their production facility, located in the Chaulia Rupdia area of Jessore, spans 8,000 square feet and uses modern machinery to preserve the purity of their natural ingredients. The business also features its own lab and chemist, with quality control overseen by a renowned professor from Jessore University of Science and Technology. By 2025, ‘Naturals by Rakhi’ had expanded its product line beyond hair oil to include shampoo, scalp serum, hair serum and even skin care products. With more than 3,00,000 customers and a rapidly growing team, primarily consisting of women, the company is also making waves in the retail sector with a showroom in Dhaka’s Bashundhara City Shopping Complex. Saha siblings have already achieved ISO, BSTI and GMP certification for their products, for their commitment to quality. Looking ahead, Rakhi envisions ‘Naturals by Rakhi’ as an internationally recognized brand that will continue to create employment opportunities for thousands of people, especially women. ‘Our dream is to establish ‘Naturals by Rakhi’ as a trusted brand, reaching every corner of the customers,’ says Rakhi. From a simple home remedy to a thriving business, the story of ‘Naturals by Rakhi’ is a testament to the power of innovation, hard work and perseverance.

title: UK says ‘committed’ to upholding free speech after US visa bans
body: The UK government said Wednesday it is ‘fully committed’ to upholding free speech, after the US slapped visa bans on five prominent Europeans working in the tech sphere, including two Britons. ‘While every country has the right to set its own visa rules, we support the laws and institutions which are working to keep the Internet free from the most harmful content,’ a British government spokesperson said. ‘The UK is fully committed to upholding the right to free speech,’ the spokesperson added. The US State Department announced sanctions Tuesday against Britons Imran Ahmed — of the anti-misinformation nonprofit the Centre for Countering Digital Hate — and Clare Melford, who leads the UK-based Global Disinformation Index (GDI). It also targeted former EU commissioner Thierry Breton and two others. It accused them all of promoting ‘censorship crackdowns by foreign states — in each case targeting American speakers and American companies’. It follows Washington ramping up its attacks on EU regulations after Brussels earlier this month fined Elon Musk’s X for violating rules on transparency in advertising and its methods for ensuring users were verified and actual people. The US administration of president Donald Trump has also been highly critical of the UK over tech and free speech, attacking its Online Safety Act that seeks to impose content moderation requirements on major social media platforms. In August, the State Department said Britain had ‘significant human rights issues’, including restrictions on free speech, and last week the White House suspended implementation of a multi-billion-dollar tech cooperation deal. It emerged that this was due to opposition to the UK’s tech rules. Prime minister Keir Starmer’s government, which has steered clear of public criticism of the Trump administration, struck a conciliatory tone on the tech deal hold-up. It said in response last week that it was focused on promptly resuming talks over the agreement, signed during the US president’s pomp-filled UK state visit in September. London’s public response to Tuesday’s US sanctions also appeared more tepid than other European capitals, with French President Emmanuel Macron accusing the US of ‘intimidation’ and ‘coercion’ and Berlin branding it ‘not acceptable’.

title: Sale centre for char farmers’ products launched
body: Palki, a sale centre of agricultural products grown by the char farmers here, was separately opened at Hajirhaat (Kani-charitabari) under Horipur union of Sundarganj upazila and Guyabari char under Holdia union of Saghata upazila in the district on Wednesday amid much enthusiasm to the char inhabitants. District relief and rehabilitation officer Md Shafiqul Islam formally inaugurated the centres as chief guest. Earlier, CARE Bangladesh built the centres under its Prodipto project being implemented by the SKS Foundation here. Sundarganj upazila project implementation officer Md Mashiar Rahman and Saghata upazila project implementation officer Md Mehedi Hasan and the officials of the project and SKS Foundation were present on the occasion. Speaking on the occasion, programme manager SM Jaglul Razib said that the char farmers did not get fair prices against their agro-products produced by them, due to various reasons including lack of a good marketing system. Taking the matter into cognizance, CARE Bangladesh develops the idea to make such centres where the char farmers could sell their agro-produces at fair prices. A large number of char farmers, public representatives and invited people including the media men attended the inaugural ceremonies of the centres.

title: India’s Bollywood counts costs as star fees squeeze profits
body: From fleets of private trailers to personal chefs and sprawling entourages, Bollywood stars’ ‘obnoxious’ demands are driving up production costs and putting a strain on the Indian film industry’s finances, insiders say. Bollywood has long been unpredictable at the box office and the pandemic compounded problems, but producers argue that today’s losses stem less from creative failure and more from top artists’ runaway expenses. ‘It is not so much about production cost -- it is more about star fees,’ says producer Ramesh Taurani, best known for the successful Race action franchise. Actors, filmmakers say, increasingly arrive on set with a dozen-strong entourage -- including makeup artists, hairdressers, stylists, gym trainers and assistants -- all billed to production. Stars are paid hefty fees of up to $22.18 million per film but additional requests for first-class travel, five-star hotels, multiple private trailers and work-shy hours have become routine. ‘Expansive support teams, premium travel and luxury accommodations often inflate budgets without proportionate creative impact,’ said veteran producer Mukesh Bhatt. ‘The kind of demands stars make is obnoxious.’ Distributor and trade analyst Raj Bansal added: ‘One actor usually comes with 10 to 15 staff members. ‘Earlier, actors wouldn’t mind sharing one vanity van. Then they decided to give one vanity van each to a big star -- and demand went on increasing.’ A single trailer hired for the duration of a film shoot can cost as much $18,000. For some actors, insiders say, demanding more has become a status symbol. Bollywood has always been considered high-risk, producing more flops than hits, but producers say the balance has tipped sharply as star-driven costs spiral beyond what box office returns can sustain. The fragile model was shaken after the pandemic, when streaming platforms bought films at inflated prices. When those deals dried up, producers faced a painful course correction as income plunged but actors’ demands stayed elevated. And that problem continues today. Competition has also intensified. ‘Audience behaviour has matured, streaming platforms have broadened horizons and regional cinema has elevated creative standards,’ says Bhatt. ‘Yet, alongside this progress, rising production costs -- particularly talent-driven budgets -- have introduced a significant strain. It is not the films that falter, but the economics that lose balance.’ Actor-filmmaker Aamir Khan slammed stars for burdening producers with these costs. ‘You earn in crores (tens of millions of rupees),’ Khan said, in a September interview with the YouTube show Game Changers. ‘Where’s your self-respect?’ Industry insiders say actors’ demands also have a cascading effect, as stars seek to exceed each other’s perks. ‘A measured approach will allow us to redirect resources toward what truly defines cinema -- the power of storytelling,’ said Bhatt. Producers have pushed for partnership-style compensation models. ‘When a film thrives, every contributor should benefit,’ Bhatt said. ‘When it struggles, the weight should not rest solely on the producer, who shoulders risk from the very beginning.’ The 2024 science fiction action film Bade Miyan Chote Miyan (‘Big Mister, Little Mister’), starring Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff, reportedly cost about $42 million. After poor ticket sales, producers were reported to have mortgaged property to cover debts. There have been exceptions. Actor Kartik Aaryan waived his fee for the 2023 action-comedy Shehzada, which tanked at the box office. ‘If your star value and the entire project’s value gives profit to the entire team, I think then the math adds up,’ Aaryan said. ‘If it doesn’t, then you should take a cut.’ Some producers argue that the industry must confront its own excesses. ‘If the star fee and entourage is affecting your budget, then don’t take stars,’ says actor-writer-producer Viveck Vaswani. ‘I have made 40 films with 40 newcomers and have prospered. I took SRK (Shah Rukh Khan) when nobody wanted him. I cast Raveena Tandon when nobody knew her.’ Vaswani, a longtime friend of Khan, notes that ‘SRK has no entourage cost, he pays his own’, as does Akshay Kumar ‘Lots of them do that, they don’t burden the producers,’ he said. ‘If you think your star is stronger than your script, you are wrong.’

title: Pakistan’s historic brewery cheers export licence
body: A heady aroma of malt and brewing yeast drifts through Pakistan’s oldest and by far largest brewery, which is gearing up for expansion after getting approval to sell abroad after a nearly 50-year ban. Bottles and cans clatter along the production lines at Murree Brewery, a singular scene in the Muslim-majority country where alcohol is largely banned. But Murree, founded in 1860 to quench the thirst of British soldiers and the colonial community during the Raj, has survived Islamist opposition and strict regulations to become one of Pakistan’s most well-known companies. ‘It’s a journey of a roller-coaster and resilience,’ Isphanyar Bhandara, the third generation of his family to run the business, told AFP in an interview. ‘Getting permission to export is another happy milestone,’ he added. ‘My grandfather, and late father, tried to get the export licence, but couldn’t get it. Just because, you know, we are an Islamic country.’ However, Bhandara said he got ‘a rude surprise’ in 2017 when the Chinese-run Hui Coastal Brewery and Distillery got permission to brew beer in Pakistan, mainly for the thousands of Chinese working on major infrastructure projects in the country. ‘What happened to all the Islamic lectures?’ said Bhandara, who hails from Pakistan’s small but influential Parsi (Zoroastrian) community and is also a lawmaker in the National Assembly. Soon he embarked on the years-long lobbying effort to lift the export ban. Originally housed in the mountains outside Islamabad, Murree’s red-brick facility now sits opposite the army chief’s residence in the capital’s twin city Rawalpindi, one of the most heavily guarded places in the country. Revenue surpassed $100 million in the fiscal year to June, with alcohol sales generating just over half of the total, and non-alcoholic drinks and bottle making accounting for the rest. The performance is all the more remarkable given that alcohol sales to Muslims are forbidden, meaning only religious minorities — numbering around nine million — and foreigners can buy beer or liquor in a few authorised shops or upscale hotels. But that has not stopped millions of Pakistanis from getting their occasional tipple, in a country with a long history of appreciating a fine drink. Its revered founder Mohammad Ali Jinnah was known to enjoy spirits, and the military dictator Pervez Musharraf made no secret of his love of whisky. Even prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who announced the alcohol ban in 1977 in a bid to garner support from right-wing Islamist parties, once told a rally: ‘Yes, I drink alcohol, but at least I don’t drink the blood of the poor.’ These days it’s common for bottles to appear at dinners or parties — there is usually a Christian or Hindu to be found who will buy them for you. ‘Pakistan’s affair with alcohol is like that of a secret paramour — acknowledged but not talked about extensively,’ said Fasi Zaka, a prominent columnist and political commentator. ‘It’s the tolerable vice — condemned but familiar.’ However, many Muslim drinkers obtain alcohol from bootleggers or locally produced moonshine, and every year several people die after consuming methanol-contaminated liquor. ‘I have to bribe the police and take extra risks, so the price is doubled’, a Christian bootlegger in Islamabad told AFP on condition of anonymity. ‘The extra charge is to keep everyone happy, whether it’s a Muslim customer or a police officer keeping an eye on me,’ he said with a laugh. Before the export ban, Murree had sold its products in neighbouring India and Afghanistan, but also in Gulf countries and as far as the United States. ‘It sounds very strange or very bizarre today, but we were exporting to Kabul,’ where the Taliban now govern with their strict interpretation of Islam, Bhandara said. Murree has already made limited shipments to Japan, Britain and Portugal as it explores distribution channels and strategies. ‘Right now, the target is not revenue or to make money... the target is to explore new markets’, Bhandara said. The company, which has around 2,200 employees, is looking in particular at Europe, but is also weighing a move into Asian and African markets. Selling abroad could also give Murree a chance to promote its history and brand in ways unimaginable at home. ‘We are not allowed to advertise, so we keep our heads down — we try to make a good beer with our heads down,’ Bhandara said.

title: US probing difficulty unlocking Tesla doors after accidents
body: US auto safety officials have opened a preliminary investigation into Tesla’s door design following a complaint from a driver who said poor labelling worsened an emergency, authorities said this week. The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration received a petition from a customer who said the mechanical release on his 2022 Tesla Model 3 was ‘hidden, unlabelled, and not intuitive to locate during an emergency’ in which the electric system failed, the agency said. ‘A defect petition has been opened to evaluate the issue and determine whether to grant or deny the petition,’ NHTSA said in a public notice on December 23. The action comes on the heels of recent news reports spotlighting cases where people became trapped in burning vehicles after an accident in which Tesla’s electric-run door system went down and they were unable to find a manual release. Bloomberg identified ‘at least’ 15 fatalities ‘in which occupants or rescuers were unable to open the doors of a Tesla that had crashed and caught fire,’ according to a report this week. Tesla didn’t respond immediately to a query from AFP, or to Bloomberg’s request for comment. But Bloomberg cited September remarks from a Tesla executive who said the company was working on a redesign of its door handle system. Tesla’s website includes a diagram of the manual door release, which is located near the window switches. The NHTSA disclosed the complainant as Kevin Clouse, who survived after an emergency and fire, escaping by breaking a rear window with a witness helping to pull him out, Clouse told an Atlanta local television news show.

title: Rangpur Foundry Limited approves 23pc dividend
body: Rangpur Foundry Limited, RFL in short, on Wednesday approved 23 per cent dividend for shareholders for the year 2024-25, said a press release. The company made the decision at its 45th annual general meeting held through digital platform. RFL chairman Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, managing director Rathendra Nath Paul, directors Sabiha Amjad, Chowdhury Kamruzzaman, independent directors Abu Taher Chowdhury, Zakia Sultana, director (finance) Uzma Chowdhury, director (accounts) Choudhury Atiur Rasul, acting chief financial officer Shafiul Alam and company secretary Muhammad Aminur Rahman attended the AGM alonside shareholders of the company. Rathendra Nath Paul briefed the investors on the company’s overall business progress and future plans. At the end of the meeting, Ahsan Khan Chowdhury thanked everyone and concluded the proceedings, seeking the continued support of the company’s investors.

title: SJIB Shariah supervisory body holds 90th meeting
body: Shahjalal Islami Bank PLC’s Shariah supervisory committee held its 90th meeting on Wednesday, said a press release. Shariah supervisory committee chairman Shamsuddin Zia presided over the meeting held at the bank’s corporate head office. The meeting discussed various issues related to Shariah compliance in overall Islamic Banking operations. Among others, committee members Mohammad Mizanur Rahman and Abdullah Masum were present in the meeting. Shahjalal Islami Bank managing director Mosleh Uddin Ahmed, company secretary Md Abul Bashar and Shariah Secretariat head Md Farid Uddin were also present in the meeting. The formal proceedings of the meeting began with the recitation from the Holy Quran and the meeting was concluded with Doa and Munajat and wishing continued prosperity of the bank.

title: Prime Bank signs payroll deal with Fame Group
body: Prime Bank PLC has recently signed a payroll agreement with Fame Group, said a press release. Under the agreement, employees of Fame Group will enjoy a range of exclusive banking privileges from Prime Bank, including preferential services, credit card and loan facilities. They will also have access to PrimePay, the bank’s state-of-the-art digital payroll platform that enables seamless and automated salary disbursement along with convenient, round-the-clock corporate payment solutions. Prime Bank deputy managing director M Nazeem A Choudhury and Fame Group managing director Masud Alam signed the agreement at the bank’s corporate office in the capital. Prime Bank SEVP and distribution network head Mamur Ahmed, SVP and team head — commercial banking division Mehedi Zaman Khan and VP and payroll banking head Hasina Fardous were present among others. Fame Group chief operating officer Md Golam Kabir, finance adviser Paritosh Sarker, executive director — admin Brigadier General Murad Zaman (retired) and general manager — commercial Nizam Uddin also attended the event.

title: Redington aids digital economy with Google Workspace
body: Redington Limited, a Google Cloud Premier level partner, is helping to drive workplace transformation across Bangladesh by providing organisations with access to Google Workspace, said a press release. Google Workspace reduces organisational siloes and enables teams to collaborate and communicate easily across devices and locations by combining email, meetings, file storage, document production, and scheduling into a single cloud-based platform. For Bangladeshi organisations navigating fast-changing market dynamics, this transformation is enabling a new way of working — one that prioritises speed, flexibility and insight-driven growth. Google Workspace authorised distributor companies that work with Redington receive not only technology but also the direction required to successfully adopt and scale it. From consulting and solution design to onboarding, training, and lifecycle support, Redington helps ensure that global technology is delivered with local relevance.

title: Expo Group partners with Accord Technologies
body: Expo Group has recently signed an agreement with Accord Technologies Limited to implement a comprehensive payroll management services solution for its employees, said a press release. Under the agreement, Accord Technologies will provide Expo Group with access to its proprietary cloud-based Accord HRM platform along with managed services. The scope of services includes payroll management, fund management services (provident fund and gratuity fund) and expatriate income tax return filing for eligible cases. The partnership reflects Expo Group’s continued commitment to strengthening internal systems through secure and technology-driven solutions that enhance operational efficiency and employee experience. By adopting a centralised and automated payroll system, Expo Group aims to ensure greater accuracy, and and regulatory compliance across its group of companies. Accord Technologies Limited is a Bangladesh based HR and payroll technology provider specializing in cloud-enabled HRM solutions, training, advisory and managed services for organisations operating across diverse sectors. This collaboration marks another step in Expo Group’s broader digital transformation journey, reinforcing its focus on people-centric operational excellence.

title: Walton-Intel Tech Gala Night held
body: US-based global technology giant Intel and Bangladesh’s leading technology brand Walton Computer hosted ‘Walton-Intel Tech Gala Night’ in the capital to further strengthen the country’s technology business ecosystem, said a press release. The event brought together key business partners from across the sector. At the event, Walton and Intel showcased their latest cutting-edge technology products currently available in the market, along with a range of upcoming tech solutions. It focused on performance, enterprise usability, smart solutions and customer experience. Walton Digi-Tech Industries Limited managing director SM Monjurul Alam Ovee presided over the event that took place on Tuesday at Le Méridien Dhaka. Senior officials from various government and private organisations attended the function. Zia Manzur, Intel country manager for Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Pakistan, and Boon Hau Poh, field application engineer, briefed business partners on Intel’s upcoming technologies, processor innovations, enterprise solutions and new opportunities for customers. An informative and engaging presentation outlining Walton’s growing strength in the country’s technology sector, its innovation-driven local manufacturing capabilities, and advanced tech solutions tailored to market demand along with Walton’s computer products roadmap for 2026 were presented to partners. One of the major attractions of the gala night was the display centre and experience zone featuring various Walton Computer products, where participants could directly experience the performance and features of modern technology devices. Among others, MIST commandant Major General Md Nasim Parvez and ICB Islamic Bank managing director Mojibur Rahman were present.

title: HONOR set to launch Guinness World Record holder X9d
body: Global technology brand HONOR Bangladesh is set to launch its globally hyped HONOR X9d on the Bangladesh market, said a press release. It will be available for pre-booking from January 4 to January 11, 2026, after its launch. It will be available in 3 colours — Sunrise Gold, Midnight Black and Reddish Brown. The HONOR X9d holds a Guinness World Record for the ‘Highest Smartphone Drop’, surviving a 6.133-metre fall without damage, showcasing its extreme durability and advanced anti-drop tech similar to its predecessor. It also received industry-first SGS Triple Resistant Premium Performance Certification and can easily handle complex water environments, the release said. The device is equipped with an ultra-large 8300 mAh silicon-carbon battery. Additionally, the device features a stunning 108MP ultra-sensing camera and more, powered by the Snapdragon 6 Gen 4.

title: NBR opens ‘Helpdesk’ for JS polls candidates to submit returns online
body: The National Board of Revenue has taken special measures to facilitate candidates intending to contest in the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad elections by enabling online submission of income tax returns during holidays. To simplify the process of online return filing for prospective election candidates, NBR, with the assistance of the e-Tax Management Unit, has launched a dedicated ‘Helpdesk’ at the e-Tax Management Unit office. The ‘Helpdesk’ will provide necessary services related to online income tax return submission. According to the press release, the ‘Helpdesk’ will operate on December 26, Friday, from 2:00pm to 5:00pm, and on December 27, Saturday, from 9:00am to 5:00pm, said an NBR press release on Thursday. The service will be available at the Office of the Tax Commissioner, e-Tax Management Unit, National Board of Revenue, located at Level-7, Institution of Engineers, Bangladesh (IEB) in Ramna, Dhaka. In addition, the NBR said that the ‘Helpdesk’ services would also remain operational during regular office hours on December 28 and December 29, to further assist election candidates in filing their income tax returns online without any difficulty. The initiative aims to ensure smooth compliance with mandatory income tax requirements for candidates ahead of the Jatiya Sangsad elections.

title: Net NSC sales drop by 53pc in July-Oct
body: Net sales of National Savings Certificates fell sharply at the start of the current fiscal year as the government deliberately scaled back its reliance on high-cost savings instruments and shifted toward cheaper borrowing sources, while inflation continued to erode household saving capacity. Bangladesh Bank data showed that net NSC sales dropped by 53.61 per cent to Tk 2,369 crore during July–October of FY26, from Tk 5,107 crore in the same period a year earlier. Although sales remained positive, the steep fall marked a continuation of a longer-term retreat from savings certificates as both policy priorities and investor behaviour changed. For the past three fiscal years, net NSC sales have remained negative on an annual basis. Net sales stood at negative Tk 6,063 crore in FY25 after plunging to a record negative Tk 21,124 crore in FY24, following negative Tk 3,295 crore in FY23. The outstanding stock of NSCs declined to Tk 3.41 lakh crore in October 2025 from Tk 3.51 lakh crore a year earlier, reflecting steady repayments exceeding new issuance. Economists said that inflation has played a central role in weakening demand for savings certificates. Inflation has stayed above 8 per cent for nearly three years, squeezing real incomes and forcing many households to cash in matured certificates to meet daily expenses rather than reinvest. Although inflation eased slightly to 8.17 per cent in October, it remained high enough to blunt the appeal of fixed-return instruments. At the same time, the government has moved away from NSCs as a borrowing tool because of their high interest costs. Returns on savings certificates exceed those on treasury bills and bonds, making them an expensive source of financing. To contain debt-servicing pressure, the government has prioritised repayment over fresh issuance and relied more on banks and market-based instruments. This strategy is evident in the government’s broader borrowing pattern. During July–November, net borrowing from the banking system stood at about Tk 35,000 crore. For FY26, the government has set a net bank borrowing target of Tk 1.04 lakh crore, lower than Tk 1.36 lakh crore in FY25, signalling tighter control over domestic financing and a preference for lower-cost options. Rising bank deposit rates have further reduced the relative attractiveness of NSCs. Several private banks are now offering fixed-deposit returns between 8 and 11 per cent, narrowing the gap with savings certificates while providing greater liquidity and digital access. Moreover, many individuals also purchased treasury bills which offer hefty returns. Policy tightening has also weighed on NSC demand. Since 2021, interest rates on savings certificates have been cut by up to two percentage points, while stricter documentation requirements, including mandatory national ID and tax return proof for purchases above Tk 5 lakh, have limited access. Although aimed at curbing misuse by affluent investors, the measures have discouraged some small savers as well. Net NSC sales peaked at Tk 52,417 crore in FY17 and Tk 49,939 crore in FY19, but current trends indicate a structural shift in government borrowing strategy, with lasting implications for household savings, fiscal costs and debt management.

title: Farmers sell cauliflower at Tk 5 a kg, consumers pay Tk 40 a piece
body: In the capital’s retail markets, consumers have been paying between Tk 30 and Tk 40 for a single piece of cauliflower; however, growers are struggling to sell the same produce even at Tk 5-7, leaving many unable to recover their production costs. According to the correspondents from Kurigram, Lalmonirhat, and information from Bagura, cauliflower and cabbage prices plunged sharply at these areas due to intense cold and dense fog. Moreover, excess supply amid limited demand, a lack of storage facilities, insufficient supply, and a shortage of buyers have forced farmers to sell fresh vegetables at throwaway prices, raising concerns about production costs and financial losses. At Lalmonirhat, cauliflower and cabbage were sold at Tk 5-7 per kilogram, with big-sized items usually sold at a kg. Meanwhile, in Kurigram, the prices were little higher, about Tk 10 per kg. Meanwhile, the prices of the items were Tk 30-40 apiece at Karwan Bazar, Kallyanpur Natun Bazar and other retail markets of the capital. The markets at the higher levels were crowded with vegetables across all sections, as farmers from distant areas brought their produce to the market. However, the correspondents said that while the usual presence of buyers and sellers was visible, prices, especially for cauliflower, remained far below expectations. With winter vegetables now in peak season, farmers are facing losses as prices continue to fall daily. Taherul Islam, a trader from Mahathan of Bagura, said that said around 40 large and small commission houses operate at the market, with nearly 40 truckloads of vegetables delivered daily. Farmers told the correspondent that their production costs ranged between Tk 5 and Tk 7 per kilogram, due to high prices of fertiliser, seeds and pesticides. However, prices of all winter vegetables have been falling steadily over the past two weeks, forcing farmers to sell their produce at prices that fail to cover even basic production expenses. As a result, farmers are unable to recover cultivation, labour and transportation costs, leaving many of them financially distressed and at risk of losing their capital. A month ago, cauliflower was selling at Tk 2,000 to Tk 2,500 per maund. “For the past three days, prices have dropped drastically to Tk 80–100 per maund.

title: NHA chair urges accountability as REHAB fair begins
body: National Housing Authority chairman Ferdousi Begum on Wednesday called for greater accountability and firm devotion to commitments in the housing sector. Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the four-day REHAB Fair-2025 at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center in the capital’s Agargaon area, she urged developers to work collectively to restore public trust and ensure the timely delivery of housing projects, particularly for expatriates and middle-class people. The fair, organised by the Real Estate and Housing Association of Bangladesh, was inaugurated by Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha chairman Md Riazul Islam as the chief guest. ‘We want to work together so that no allegations arise against housing companies and people’s dream homes can be built in time,’ Ferdousi Begum said. She said that complaints against some developers, especially delays in handing over flats beyond specified timelines, had raised concerns. Ferdousi Begum said that the activities carried out by REHAB closely align with the National Housing Authority. She also called on REHAB to play a stronger role in ensuring compliance and professionalism across the sector. Highlighting the need to follow the Detailed Area Plan, Ferdousi Begum stressed project implementation in line with the approved Floor Area Ratio, noting that rule-based development would help create wider roads and better urban infrastructure. She also underscored the importance of green, planned housing with special attention to middle-class needs and safe housing for women. Rajuk chairman Riazul Islam called upon housing sector businessmen to build environment-friendly cities. He noted that revising the DAP involved many challenges but said that the process was necessary to establish a rule-based framework for housing development. ‘I hope everyone will accept the rules and pledge to work accordingly in the future,’ he added, stressing that not only housing projects but also high-end hotels must comply with planning regulations. The fair at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center will continue until December 27 and will remain open daily from 10:00am to 9:00pm. Chaired by REHAB president Mohammad Wahiduzzaman, the inauguration ceremony was also addressed by its senior vice president Liaqat Ali Bhuiyan, vice-president Aktar Biswas, and other senior leaders from REHAB. REHAB leaders said that prolonged complexities over the DAP had left the housing sector nearly stagnant, but expressed optimism that the newly published DAP on December 14 and the Dhaka Metropolitan Building Rules-2025 would inject fresh momentum into the industry. According to REHAB, this year’s fair features 220 stalls, including four diamond sponsors, seven gold sponsors, 10 co-sponsors, 14 construction material companies, and 12 financial and investment institutions. The organisers said that the housing and construction sector contributes around 15 per cent to the national economy and supports nearly 20 million people directly and indirectly, with more than 200 linkage industries such as rod and cement. They added that the fair offers buyers a one-stop platform to explore flats, plots, home loans, investment options, and modern construction materials. Entry tickets are priced at Tk 50 for single entry and Tk 100 for multiple entries, with all proceeds allocated to REHAB’s corporate social responsibility activities. A raffle draw will be held every night at 9:00pm, offering attractive prizes for visitors.

title: Bangladesh witnesses strong external sector performance: GED
body: Bangladesh’s external sector demonstrated strong performance and resilience in November 2025, riding on stable foreign exchange reserves, remittance inflow, and modest export, said the General Economic Division. In its December edition of the Economic Update and Outlook, GED of the Planning Commission stated that the foreign reserves reached their highest levels of the year, reflecting improved external inflows and effective liquidity management. In November 2025, Bangladesh’s foreign exchange reserves reached their peak for the year, with gross reserves at approximately $32.33 billion and BPM6 reserves at $27.578 billion, according to the report. The month-on-month increase from October to November indicates strengthened reserve adequacy, supporting macroeconomic stability and the central bank›s capacity to manage external vulnerabilities. During the period, remittance inflows also peaked at $2.9 billion, mainly due to increased use of formal transfer channels, the report added. Export earnings, driven primarily by the readymade garment sector, remained above $3.8 billion, contributing to overall external stability, while non-RMG exports stayed relatively modest. While export earnings experienced significant fluctuations, the November figure indicated a stable phase, suggesting that seasonal disruptions and short-term shocks had eased. Although overall export levels remained below mid-year peaks, the November 2025 outcome pointed to a gradual stabilisation in external earnings, contributing positively to balance of payments management and macroeconomic stability. Bangladesh’s overall inflation rose slightly in November 2025 despite a moderation in rice prices, while strong remittance inflows, increasing foreign exchange reserves, and stable exports supported external sector resilience. The report also said that the combined strength of rising reserves, high remittance inflows, and steady exports in November underscored a positive external sector outlook. However, continued reliance on RMG exports highlights the importance of diversification for sustained resilience. Meanwhile, RMG exports remained the dominant driver of overall export performance, representing over 80 per cent of total earnings. In contrast, non-RMG exports continued to play a more minor but relatively stable role. The GED also launched a publication titled ‘Bangladesh State of the Economy 2025,’ which analysed long-term patterns in economic indicators, enabled comparisons across periods, and provided a comprehensive review of the economy›s performance over the past year, with a focus on economic reforms and recovery. When the interim government assumed power, it inherited a fragile economy affected by multiple shocks, including rising inflation, currency devaluation, declining foreign exchange reserves, deficits in both financial and current accounts, high non-performing loans, and lingering effects of macroeconomic mismanagement, the report added. The government has actively worked to restore macroeconomic stability through banking-sector discipline, exchange-rate stabilization, and inflation control, successfully stabilising the economy, rebuilding confidence in the banking sector, and proposing long-term reform plans. The report provided an overview of the policies implemented and the economic responses observed, to help policymakers adopt short-term economic measures and corrective actions to achieve a more stable and resilient economy. On the monetary front, bank deposits reached Taka 19,24,635.7 crore in October, registering a year-on-year growth of 9.62 per cent, reflecting sustained depositor confidence. Credit growth moderated, with public sector credit growth slowing to 21.43 per cent and private sector credit growth easing slightly to 6.23 per cent. Total domestic credit growth decelerated to 9.62 per cent in October. Weighted average interest rate spread varied across banking groups. Foreign commercial banks recorded the highest spread at 8.88 per cent, while specialised and development banks posted the lowest at 3.37 per cent. State-owned and private commercial banks showed similar spreads of around 5.6 per cent, a level the GED said is desirable for improving banking sector efficiency. Revenue collection by the National Board of Revenue fell short of the monthly target in November 2025, despite posting double-digit year-on-year growth. The report said the Annual Development Programme utilisation improved year-on-year during July-November of FY2025-26.

title: Banks open Saturday for polls deposits
body: In a move to facilitate the nomination process for the 13th National Parliamentary Election, all branches of scheduled banks have been directed to remain open on Saturday. Bangladesh Bank on Wednesday issued the directive to ensure that prospective candidates can smoothly deposit their security money and funds required to purchase voter list CDs. These transactions are essential for the formal submission of nomination papers. Candidates will be able to complete these financial requirements through bank drafts, pay orders, or treasury challans. This special measure follows a memorandum issued by the Bangladesh Election Commission Secretariat today. To ensure legal compliance and serve the general public interest, the order has been implemented under the authority granted by Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
