title: Customs duty on date imports cut
body: The government has reduced customs duties on the import of dates ahead of the upcoming holy month of Ramadan to ensure adequate supply and stabilise the market. In a press release issued on Wednesday, the National Board of Revenue said it had slashed the customs duty on date imports from 25 per cent to 15 per cent, a reduction of 10 percentage points on Monday, to ensure adequate supply and stable prices of dates during Ramadan. However, the importers said it would have been better if the government had issued the notification earlier, as less than two months would not be sufficient to complete import procedures. The duty concession on date imports would remain effective until March 31, 2026. Earlier, the import-stage advance income tax on dates and all other fruits was reduced from 10 per cent to 5 per cent through amendments to the relevant provisions in the previous budget. Moreover, the 50 per cent rebate on advance income tax for date and fruit imports granted last year has also been retained for this year, the NBR said. The NBR said it expects the combined reduction in customs duty and advance income tax to help keep the supply of dates steady and market prices affordable for general consumers during Ramadan. However, Nuruddin Ahmed, general secretary of the Bangladesh Fresh Fruits Importers Association, told New Age that they had urged the government to slash customs duties much earlier. ‘Ramadan is going to start from February 19 (based on sight of the moon), meaning we get less than two months to finish import procedures, including opening letter of credit, shipment, and others,’ he added. They are suspicious about the advantages of the decision for the ordinary people, he added, saying that they repeatedly urged the government to abolish AIT on date imports. Dates have always been a special item for Iftar during Ramadan in Bangladesh. However, in recent years, the fruit has advanced beyond a Ramadan delicacy to become a staple of daily consumption. With soaring demand and shifting consumer preferences, the country’s imports of dates have also surged significantly in the past few years. According to data from the NBR, Bangladesh imported 39,790 tonnes of dates in the financial year 2019-20, surged to 62,200 tonnes in FY21, followed by 88,961 tonnes in FY22, 84,151 tonnes in FY23, and 85,245 tonnes in FY24. Though official data on imports for FY25 is yet to be published, importers and customs officials predicted that imports might stand at around 85,000 tonnes. According to the BFFIA, the country’s annual demand for dates is around 90,000-95,000 tonnes, and during Ramadan it is around 60,000-70,000 tonnes. Currently, dabas, jahidi, mabrum, marium, ajwah, medjul, sukkari, and salabi are the most widely sold date varieties in the country. Several shops have been set up in the capital to sell costly date variants. According to NBR data, Bangladesh imports dates mostly from Iraq, Iran, Algeria, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia, Kuwait, Jordan, and other countries. Earlier on November 11, the Bangladesh Trade and Tariff Commission had proposed reducing import duties and advance taxes on dates ahead of Ramadan, as in the previous year. To keep prices affordable during the fasting month, the commission recommended cutting import duty from 25 per cent to 15 per cent and source tax from 10 per cent to 3 per cent, along with the complete withdrawal of the existing 3 per cent regulatory duty on date imports.

title: Workshops on PPR held at Cox’s Bazar, Ukhiya
body: In a determined effort to familiarize tenderers and procuring entities with the newly enacted Public Procurement Rules, 2025 (PPR, 2025), the Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority (BPPA) conducted two awareness workshops, first at Ukhiya and the second at Cox’s Bazar on Wednesday. The workshops were held in a bid to comprehensively outlining the key provisions, innovations and compliance requirements of PPR, 2025. Chief executive officer of the Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority (BPPA), secretary SM Moin Uddin Ahmed, and the BPPA director Shah Eyamin-Ul Islam, also a national procurement trainer, attended the workshops today. Shah Eyamin-Ul Islam made detailed presentations on the issues. The workshops drew participation from local procuring entities and tenderers, aiming to strengthen transparency, efficiency and competition in public procurement at the grassroots level, said a press release. In Cox’s Bazar, the CEO of BPPA, who was present as the chief guest, told the participants that the compliance with the provisions of the amended Public Procurement Act, 2006 and the Public Procurement Rules, 2025 is a must. Elaborating on the importance of the PPR, 2025, he said the PPR, 2025 is very important to ensure transparency, efficiency and competition in the process of public procurement. MA Mannan, deputy commissioner and district magistrate presided over the session in the conference room of his office in Cox’s Bazar. At Ukhiya, the CEO was the chief guest and the upazila nirbahi officer, Mohammad Kamrul Hossain Chowdhury chaired the session at the Upazila Parishad Auditorium. In both the workshops, Eyamin in his presentations highlighted various aspects of the newly enacted PPR, 2025. The initiative reflects BPPA’s continued commitment to ensuring that procurement reforms are not confined to policy documents alone, but are effectively communicated and implemented across even the most remote regions of the country. Bangladesh Center for Communication Programs facilitated the workshops as part of the ongoing efforts of the BPPA to create greater awareness about the PPR, 2025 in different districts and upazilas of the country.

title: BP to sell majority stake in Castrol lubricants business
body: British oil giant BP said Wednesday it has agreed to sell a majority stake in its Castrol lubricants business to US investment firm Stonepeak, as it seeks to cut debt. The sale of BP’s 65 per cent stake will net it around $6 billion, the company said in a statement. The deal, which values Castrol at $10.1 billion, is expected to be completed by the end of 2026. Castrol will be owned by a joint venture, with BP retaining a minority stake. ‘The sale marks an important milestone in the ongoing delivery of our reset strategy,’ said interim chief executive Carol Howle. To help turn around years of lagging performance, BP plans to divest $20 billion of assets by the end of 2027 as it pivots back to its more profitable oil and gas business, and slashes clean energy investment. ‘We have now completed or announced over half of our targeted $20 billion divestment programme, with proceeds to significantly strengthen BP’s balance sheet,’ Howle said. BP extended its shakeup last week as it appointed energy industry veteran Meg O’Neill to become chief executive from April, replacing Murray Auchincloss. American national O’Neill joins BP from her position as chief executive of Australian group Woodside Energy.

title: BSEC extends deadline for provisioning of 6 market intermediaries
body: The Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission, the country’s capital market regulator, has decided to conditionally extend the deadline for provision conservation and adjustment for six additional intermediary institutions. This decision aims to provide relief to firms struggling with deficits related to negative equity and unrealised losses. The decision was finalized during the 989th Commission meeting of the BSEC, held today at the BSEC conference room in the city, said a press release. The meeting was chaired by BSEC Chairman Khondoker Rashed Maqsood. According to a BSEC notification, the extension was granted after the commission reviewed and considered the action plan submitted by these institutions regarding the provisioning and adjustment of their negative equity and unrealized losses. The six institutions are: NBL Securities Limited, Unicap Securities Limited, LankaBangla Securities Limited, New Era Securities Limited, Kabir Securities Ltd and NBL Capital and Equity Management Ltd. This latest regulatory action highlighted a continuing trend of financial stress among capital market intermediaries. This extension follows a similar decision made by the BSEC earlier in November.

title: Bangladesh Insurance Association holds 38th AGM
body: Bangladesh Insurance Association organised its 38th annual general meeting on Monday at Samson H Chowdhury Centre of Dhaka Club. Vice-president of the association, Adeeba Rahman, presided over the meeting, said a press release. Vice-president and member of the executive committee, Quazi Sakhawat Hossain Linto, attended the meeting. Chairman of Eastland Insurance and president of ICC-Bangladesh, Mahbubur Rahman, former president of FBCCI Mir Nasir Hossain, and former president of the association Nasir Uddin Ahmed Pavel, among others, attended the meeting. In the Annual Report, it was stated that the total premium of private sector life insurance companies were from Tk 115,107 million in 2023 to Tk 113,897 million in 2024, first year premium Tk 32,081 million in 2023 to Tk 28,858 million in 2024, renewal premium Tk 72,880 million in 2023 to Tk 73,726 million in 2024, life fund Tk 319,182 million in 2023 to Tk 332,322 million in 2024, total investment Tk 334,613 million in 2023 to Tk 342,929 million in 2024 and total asset Tk 116,474 million in 2023 to Tk 119,167 million in 2024. The gross premium of non-life private sector insurance companies was Tk 42,351 million in 2023 to Tk 43,495 million in 2024, total investment was Tk 57,720 million in 2023 to Tk 56,140 million in 2024, and total assets were Tk 116,474 million in 2023 to Tk 119,167 million in 2024. Representatives of the insurance companies discussed the Annual Report 2024 as well as highlighted some of the activities of the Association in the meeting. The following issues have been approved in the meeting with consensus, including the Annual Report-2024, Audit Report-2024, and appointing the auditors for the year 2025 and fixing their remuneration.

title: AIB inaugurates centralised account opening programme
body: Al-Arafah Islami Bank inaugurated account opening services under the centralisation programme at its 50th branch. Managing director and CEO of the Bank, Rafat Ullah Khan, attended the event as chief guest at bank’s head office on Tuesday, said a press release. Rafat Ullah stated that Al-Arafah Islami Bank is working diligently to provide modern, efficient, and customer-friendly banking services. ‘By centralising account opening services, speed, transparency and security will further increase in customer service. This initiative will enhance the operational efficiency of the bank and further strengthen risk management,’ he added. Deputy managing director Mohammad Hossain and SM Abu Jafar, senior executive vice president and head of operations, Towhiduzzaman Fuad, executive vice president and head of ICT, Shoaib Ahmed, among others, attended the ceremony.

title: IFIC Bank organises workshop on AML-CFT
body: IFIC Bank PLC organised an Awareness Workshop on Anti Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism AML and CFT compliance for members of the board of directors on Sunday, said a press release. Chairman of the Bank, Md Mehmood Husain, along with all members of the board of directors, Md Ebtadul Islam, Kazi Md Mahboob Kasem, Md Golam Mostofa and Md Monzorul Haque, as well as the managing director of the bank, Syed Mansur Mustafa, among others, attended the workshop. The workshop was conducted by the additional director of Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit BFIU Rezwanur Rahman, and the Joint Director of BFIU, Juairia Haque, served as resource persons. The session aimed to enhance the Board members’ understanding of their roles in ensuring effective AML and CFT compliance, relevant regulatory requirements, and the responsibilities of reporting organisations, including banks. Key focus areas included observations of the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit arising from AML and CFT system check inspections, the recent money laundering landscape in the country and the Board’s role in strengthening governance and compliance oversight.

title: Sonali Life Insurance holds 12th AGM
body: Sonali Life Insurance Company Limited organised its 12th Annual General Meeting on Wednesday at the Company’s Conference Room at Malibagh in Dhaka. Chairman of board of directors Moinul Islam presided over the meeting, said a press release. Joint secretary of Financial Institutions Division at Ministry of Finance Maksura Akter Banu, directors Zafar Iqbal, Fazlutunnesa, Mostafa Quamrus Sobhan, Fauzia Quamrun Tania, Sheikh Mohammad Danial, observer Shah Alam, additional managing director and CEO Md Rafiqul Islam, CFO Mohammad Abdul Hannan, COO Md Monzur Morshed, HIAC Md Ali Reza, CIO Hasib Reza, among others, attended the meeting. Company secretary Md Abdur Rob conducted the proceedings of the meeting. During the AGM, shareholders unanimously approved the audited financial statements for 2024 along with the directors’ and auditors’ reports, declared a 15 per cent cash dividend, and appointed statutory and compliance auditors for 2025. Moinul Islam expressed his sincere gratitude to the shareholders for their continued confidence, trust, and support. He reaffirmed the Company’s strong commitment to sustainable growth, sound financial management, regulatory compliance, and maintaining the highest standards of corporate governance. The shareholders also conveyed their appreciation to the board of directors and the management for their dedicated efforts in improving operational performance, safeguarding policyholders’ interests, and contributing to the overall development of the insurance sector in Bangladesh.

title: AMCL PRAN approves 32pc cash dividend
body: Agricultural Marketing Company Ltd (AMCL PRAN) organised 40th annual general meeting on digital platform on Wednesday. The AGM approved a 32 per cent cash dividend for its shareholders for the year 2024-25, said a press release. Chairman of the company Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, managing director Eleash Mridha, director Sabiha Amjad, director Uzma Chowdhury, director Rezaul Hasan and independent director Zakia Sultana, director (Accounts) Choudhury Atiur Rasul, director (Marketing) Chowdhury Kamruzzaman, chief financial officer Mohammad Yeamin, company secretary Muhammad Shariful Islam, among others, attended the meeting. The shareholders thanked the management for the achievements of the company over the years and offered valuable suggestions for further improvement of business operations in the coming days. Eleash Mridha briefed the investors on the company’s overall business progress and plans. On his closing remarks, Ahsan Khan thanked everyone and concluded the proceedings, seeking the continued support of the company’s investors.

title: Citizens Bank opens Chatkhil Branch
body: Citizens Bank PLC inaugurated the Chatkhil branch at Noakhali on Monday, said a press release. Managing director of the bank, Alamgir Hossain, inaugurated the branch in the presence of deputy managing directors Md Mostafizur Rahman and Md Abdul Latif and other high officials of the bank. Among others, local renowned businessmen across the different segments and elites/professionals attended the occasion.

title: MGI’s FMCG hosts sales conference
body: FMCG Division of Meghna Group of Industries recently organised Annual Sales Conference 2025 with sales officials from all levels in attendance at Sea Pearl Beach Resort and Spa in Cox’s Bazar. The conference took place in two phases, where approximately 1,100 sales officials and representatives from 10 sales lines of the FMCG Division attended, said a press release. With the theme ‘Together We Rise’, participants reaffirmed their commitment to working collectively to achieve future targets in the coming years. MGI chairman and managing director Mostafa Kamal attended the conference virtually as chief guest. MGI director Tahmina Mostafa attended the conference as special guest. Mostafa Kamal said, ‘we aim to continue producing high-quality and innovative consumer goods and ensure they are easily accessible to people. This requires teamwork and collective effort. If we move forward together with the same goal, no challenge will stop us.’ Tahmina Mostafa said, ‘Factory, supply chain, finance, brand, operations, and above all, sales leaders- everyone is a part of the FMCG family. Sales is not just a department; it’s a shared commitment for everyone’. She directed everyone to work with a sense of responsibility and expressed a commitment to maintaining the strong market position for Fresh, No 1, and Actifed in 2026 through discipline, hard work, and dedication. MGI chief accounts officer Md Rahmotullah Khondoker, chief human resources officer Atiq uz Zaman Khan, GM and head of Accounts SM Muzibur Rahman, senior general manager (Brand) Kazi Md Mohiuddin, SBU head Quazi Touhiduzzaman, among others, attended the event. The sales conference featured discussions on strategic planning and execution methods to achieve future targets. Alongside these sessions, various team-building activities were held, and sales champion, sales hero, and long service awards were presented. Each phase of the conference also included cultural performances by renowned artists.

title: Pubali Bank holds 1500th board meeting
body: Pubali Bank PLC organised its 1500th meeting of the board of directors on Wednesday, marking a significant milestone in the bank’s long-standing tradition of strong corporate governance, regulatory compliance, and strategic leadership. The occasion was celebrated with a ceremony attended by former chairman Hafiz Ahmed Mazumdar alongside current board members and senior management, said a press release. Chairman of the board Monzurur Rahman presided over the meeting. Notably, Rahman also chaired the very first board meeting of Pubali Bank following its transition to the private sector in January 1985, underscoring a remarkable continuity of leadership and institutional stewardship. Board members Habibur Rahman, Rumana Sharif, Azizur Rahman, Rana Laila Hafiz, Arif Ahmed Choudhury, Shahinuzzaman Yaqub, independent directors Shahdeen Malik and Mohammad Naushad Ali Chowdhury and alternate director Nadir Ahmed attended the meeting. Managing director and chief executive officer of the bank, Mohammad Ali, also attended the meeting. Deputy managing director Mohammad Esha, general manager and chief financial officer Mohammad Liton Mia, general manager and company secretary Md Anisur Rahman and general manager and chief protocol officer (Pubali Bank Securities Limited)Md. Shah Alam attended the meeting.

title: Stocks resumes recovery momentum
body: Stocks on Wednesday resumed recovery momentum following the previous session’s correction, as market-wide speculations over anticipated clarity on the country’s political front provided some respite to subdued investor sentiment. DSEX, the broad index of the Dhaka Stock Exchange, gained 22.9 points to settle at 4,884 points as against 4,861 points in the previous trading session. Market indices managed to remain afloat throughout the session as opportunistic investors seized positions in sector-specific stocks, although prevailing cautious sentiment kept investor participation broadly subdued. Apparently, market turnover fell by 17.0 per cent to Tk 3.4 billion from Tk 4.1 billion in the previous session. On the sectoral front, Textile (15.9pc) issues exerted the highest turnover, followed by Bank (11.9pc) and Food (11.8pc) sectors. Most of the sectors displayed positive returns, out of which IT (2.0pc), Services (1.0pc) and Bank (0.9pc) exhibited the most positive returns on the bourse today, while Mutual Fund (-0.8pc), Ceramic (-0.7pc) and Food (-0.3pc) exerted some corrections. Out of the 397 issues traded, 178 advanced, 125 declined and 94 remained unchanged. The port city bourse, CSE, also settled on a green zone. The Selective Categories’ Index (CSCX) and All Share Price Index advanced by 7.5 points and 21.1 points, respectively.

title: US stocks steady
body: Wall Street stocks moved sideways early Wednesday in a tentative follow-up to a record-setting session after good US economic data. The S&P 500 finished at an all-time high Tuesday following US gross domestic product data that topped estimates by a wide margin. About 15 minutes into trading, the broad-based index was up 0.1 per cent at 6,913.04. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.2 per cent to 48,516.22, while the tech-rich Nasdaq Composite Index slipped 0.1 per cent to 23,544.20. Market watchers are hoping for a ‘Santa Claus’ rally in upcoming sessions heading into 2026. The period between Christmas and New Years usually sees markets drift higher amid a dearth of major economic news.

title: US sanctions will not ‘silence’ EU: commissioner
body: The European Union’s commissioner in charge of the bloc’s single market said Wednesday that US sanctions won’t stop him from doing his work after the Trump administration placed a visa ban on his predecessor for trying to regulate big tech companies. ‘My predecessor @ThierryBreton acted in the interest of the European general good, faithful to the mandate given by the voters in 2019,’ Stephane Sejourne, European Commissioner for Internal Market and Services, said on X. ‘No sanction will silence the sovereignty of the European peoples. Total solidarity with him and all affected Europeans,’ he said. The US State Department said Tuesday it would deny visas to Breton and four activists, accusing them of seeking to ‘coerce’ American social media platforms into censoring viewpoints they oppose. The President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, has not yet reacted, though the French government reacted strongly late Tuesday. Breton, a Frenchman, was described by the US State Department as the ‘mastermind’ of the European Union’s Digital Services Act (DSA), which imposes content moderation and other standards on major social media platforms operating in Europe. Breton, who left the European Commission in 2024, on X slammed the ban as a ‘witch hunt,’ comparing the situation to the US McCarthy era when officials were chased out of government for alleged ties to communism. The DSA has become a rallying point for US conservatives who see it as a weapon of censorship against right-wing thought in Europe and beyond, an accusation the EU furiously denies. ‘The Digital Services Act was democratically adopted in Europe. It has absolutely no extraterritorial reach and in no way affects the United States,’ French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on X. The visa ban also targeted Imran Ahmed of the Center for Countering Digital Hate, a nonprofit that fights online misinformation, as well as Anna-Lena von Hodenberg and Josephine Ballon of HateAid, a German organization that the State Department said functions as a trusted flagger for enforcing the DSA. Clare Melford, who leads the UK-based Global Disinformation Index (GDI), was also on the list.

title: Foodpanda celebrates team spirit with cricket tournament for riders
body: Online food and grocery delivery platform, foodpanda Bangladesh, organised a cricket tournament exclusively for its rider partners, celebrating teamwork, sportsmanship, and community spirit, says a press release. Held at the CricBD Lakepori Cricket Arena in Purbachal, Gazipur, the ‘Panda Rider Premier League 2025’ brought together riders from across Dhaka for a day filled with energy, competition, and camaraderie. This marks the second edition of foodpanda’s rider-only cricket tournament, following the inaugural event in 2023, and continues the platform’s ongoing efforts to engage its rider community through sports, alongside previously organised football tournaments. The daylong tournament featured eight teams representing different zones of Dhaka—Gulshan Fighters, Uttara Super Giants, Mirpur Gladiators, Lalbagh Wari Kings, Basundhara Warriors, Baily Road Knight Riders, Narayanganj Bulls, and Dhanmondi Blasters. A total of seven matches were played, including knockout rounds, two semi-finals, and a thrilling grand finale that kept players and spectators on their feet. After an intense final, Gulshan Fighter emerged as the champion of the Panda Rider Premier League 2025, while Mirpur Gladiators finished as the runner-up. The winning team received a cash prize of Tk 40,000, with the runner-up team took Tk 25,000. The Man of the Tournament, was awarded an e-bike, generously sponsored by Dongjin. Awards were also presented for Best Batsman, Best Bowler, and Man of the Match in the final. Additionally, Bimafy provided a one-year insurance package for all members of both the champion and runner-up teams, reinforcing a strong focus on rider well-being. Commenting on the initiative, Mukitur Khan, head of logistics at foodpanda Bangladesh, said, ‘The Panda Rider Premier League 2025 reflects our commitment to recognising our riders beyond their daily deliveries. By creating opportunities for sports and healthy competition, we aim to strengthen team spirit and foster a supportive rider community.’ Since 2023, foodpanda Bangladesh has organised multiple sports initiatives, including cricket and football tournaments, to promote well-being and engagement among its rider partners. The tournament was supported by Dongjin and Bimafy, with Kacchi Bhai, Khazana Mithai, and Ascott Palace Dhaka as food partners, and PRAN, Bruvana, Hanay Foods, and Chicken Buzz as beverage and snacks partners.

title: Sohel from Mymensingh wins a scooter through Nagad transactions
body: Shafiqul Islam Sohel of Mymensingh has won a Hero Pleasure Refresh 102cc scooter by making transactions through Nagad, says a press release. He received the prize by participating in Nagad’s campaign titled ‘Asha Aar Fera, Surprise Sera’ [Come back or start fresh, surprises at their best]. Popular television actress Parsa Evana handed over the motorcycle to the winner, Shafiqul Islam, on behalf of Nagad. Expressing his excitement after receiving the attractive gift from the actress, Shafiqul Islam said, ‘At first, I couldn’t believe it at all. When I saw them arrive at my home with the scooter, I was delighted. I never imagined that I could win such a prize just by transacting through Nagad.’ Recently, Nagad launched a campaign titled ‘Asha Aar Fera, Surprise Sera’. So far, more than 23,000 customers have received cashback ranging from Tk 50 to Tk 500. In addition, over 2,000 customers have received a bonus recharge by participating in the Surprise Recharge offer. title: Govt risks legal battle, penalties, says TIB
body: Bangladesh is facing risks of legal battle and penalties as the country is mulling over scrapping controversial and unfavourable international power deals especially that with the Adani Power Limited of India. Experts said the country had been trapped in overprices in the power sector because of the controversial and unfavourable international power deals. They made the observation while referring to the 1,600-megawatt Godda power plant built in the Indian state of Jharkhand by Adani Power Limited, a subsidiary of the Indian controversial Adani Group led by billionaire Gautam Adani to sell power to Bangladesh. Scrapping those unfavourable deals will risk international arbitration and penalty as the overprices have been set as per the agreements, said Transparency International Bangladesh executive director Iftekharuzzaman on Wednesday. Signed on November 5, 2017, for 25 years, the company constructed the plant at an estimated cost of about $2 billion and began supplying power from March 2023 to Bangladesh. Since then controversies have surfaced regarding the power plant as it was reported that the cost of Adani electricity rose to Tk 15 a unit — close to the average cost of electricity generated in 2022 from the most expensive furnace oil (Tk 16.86 a unit), if the charges like capacity and transmission are considered. Noting that most of the deals were signed by the Awami League regime between 2010 and 2024 to promote crony capitalism, the TIB executive director said that these controversial deals had been made through government-to-government and state-to-state arrangements. Following the ouster of the Awami League regime on August 5, 2024, in the wake of a mass uprising, the interim government that assumed power on August 8 past year, cancelled the controversial Speedy Increase of Power and Energy Supply (Special Provisions) Act, 2010, which had allowed the AL regime to bypass tendering and other standard procedures for power and energy projects to ensure quick supply. While it led to increased power generation capacity, it was criticised for lacking transparency and judicial oversight, creating opportunities for corruption and leading to high costs like the payment of capacity charges for idle power plants. The electricity generation capacity increased fourfold between 2020 and 2014, against a steep rise in payment for power by 11.1 fold. The overall payment of $638 million for power in 2010 jumped to $7.8 billion in 2024, former World Bank Dhaka office chief economist Zahid Hussain said. The TIB executive director said that that the government could not scrap many power purchase agreements, including the most controversial one with Adani Group, despite heavy financial burden to carry those. ‘The government cannot simply dump those if it wants,’ said the TIB executive director at the launching of a report titled ‘Generating Power from Renewable Energy in Bangladesh: Governance Challenges and Way Forward’ at its office in the capital Dhaka on Wednesday. In the past month, Bangladesh signalled that it could scrap the controversial power purchase agreement with the Adani Power Limited following a National Committee’s initial findings of massive irregularities and frauds in the power purchase deal recently. The National Committee appointed to review the power deals signed between 2010 and 2024 will submit its final report in January 2026 with a special focus on the Adani Power plant. Iftekharuzzaman said that the international arbitration should be sought for scrapping the controversial deal. Calling that the international arbitration was a lengthy process, the TIB executive director said that the chance of winning in such an arbitration was also slim. Zahid Hussain, who is also a member of the National Committee, said that the country could scarp the deal without being paid penalty only when it could be proved that massive corruption and underhand dealings took place over the one-sided deal. Calculating monthly capacity charge of $85 million, Zahid said that the Adani Group would recoup its investment in less than five years and would enjoy hefty profits in the remaining 20 years. The Adani Group is also reported to have concealed facts that the Indian government changed its regulations on February 25, 2019 to exempt the group from all import taxes for equipment and coal for the power plant so that Adani could extract a higher capacity charge from Bangladesh in breach of the agreement. Adani has yet to inform the Bangladesh agency of its tax or duty exemption by the Indian government. The Adani Group has recently faced controversies both in India and internationally, primarily stemming from a recent United States’ bribery and fraud indictment. The business group’s rapid rise in India has often been linked to the political patronage of Indian prime minister Narendra Modi, with opposition parties, such as the Indian National Congress, accusing the government of misusing state-owned institutions and diplomatic influence to benefit the Adani Group.

title: Govt cuts customs duty on date imports, extends VAT exemption on metro rail services
body: The government has reduced customs duty on the import of dates ahead of the upcoming holy month of Ramadan and also extended the value-added tax exemption on metro rail services until June 30, 2026. In a press release issued on Wednesday, the National Board of Revenue said it had slashed the customs duty on date imports from 25 per cent to 15 per cent, a reduction of 10 percentage points on Monday, to ensure adequate supply and stable prices of dates during Ramadan. The duty concession will remain effective until March 31, 2026. Earlier, the import-stage advance income tax on dates and all other fruits was reduced from 10 per cent to 5 per cent through amendments to the relevant provisions in the previous budget. Moreover, the 50 per cent rebate on advance income tax for date and fruit imports granted last year has also been retained for this year, the NBR said. The NBR said it expects the combined reduction in customs duty and advance income tax to help keep the supply of dates steady and market prices affordable for general consumers during Ramadan. Separately, the government has extended the value-added tax exemption on metro rail services until June 30, 2026. Earlier, VAT exemption on metro rail services had been granted until December 31, 2025, in the public interest and to promote an environmentally friendly, modern mass transit system. On Tuesday, the NBR extended the exemption following a recommendation from the Ministry of Road Transport and Bridges to continue the VAT relief on metro rail services. Earlier on November 11, the Bangladesh Trade and Tariff Commission had proposed reducing import duties and advance taxes on dates ahead of Ramadan, as in the previous year. To keep prices affordable during the fasting month, the commission recommended cutting import duty from 25 per cent to 15 per cent and source tax from 10 per cent to 3 per cent, along with the complete withdrawal of the existing 3 per cent regulatory duty on date imports.

title: Foreign debt reaches $112b in Sept
body: Bangladesh’s external debt rose sharply over the past year, reflecting heavy government borrowing from international lenders and raising concerns about repayment pressure, fiscal discipline and long-term debt sustainability. Bangladesh Bank data showed that the country’s external debt reached $112.12 billion in the July–September quarter of 2025, up from $105.27 billion in the same period a year earlier. This represents an increase of $6.8 billion in just twelve months. Although the figure was slightly lower than the $113.56 billion recorded in the April–June quarter of 2025, the overall trend points to a sustained rise in foreign liabilities. Central bank officials said the increase mainly stemmed from government borrowing. By June 2025, the government had received more than $5 billion from global development partners and lenders, pushing up foreign debt levels earlier in the year. As of September, government external debt stood at $92.54 billion, while private sector external borrowing remained largely unchanged at around $19.58 billion. The data also showed a decline in buyers’ credit, which companies use to finance imports through foreign loans. Buyers’ credit fell to $4.15 billion in September 2025 from $5.71 billion in September 2024, indicating reduced reliance on short-term external financing by the private sector. Despite this easing, the overall debt burden remains high because public sector borrowing dominates the external debt profile. Economists trace the roots of the current debt situation to the previous Awami League government’s borrowing strategy. Bangladesh’s external debt stood at just $23.5 billion in 2009 but crossed $100 billion by December 2023, driven largely by large-scale infrastructure projects financed through foreign loans. Weak project planning, cost overruns and delays limited the economic returns from many of these projects, while debt obligations continued to accumulate. They also point to flawed fiscal policies and weak oversight as key factors behind the debt surge. As a result, per capita external debt climbed sharply to $654.9 by September 2025, up from $283 in fiscal year 2016–17 and $606 in fiscal year 2023–24. Zahid Hussain, former lead economist of the World Bank’s Dhaka office, told New Age that the government needs to take a comprehensive review of its foreign debt position and restructure repayment schedules to avoid excessive payment pressure in any single period. He also cautioned against approving new projects without careful assessment of their economic viability. According to him, taking on non-viable projects financed by foreign borrowing would only deepen debt risks and worsen future repayment challenges. Economists said that ordinary citizens now face the consequences through higher fiscal pressure, reduced public spending flexibility and growing risks to economic stability. A white paper submitted to the governemnt warned that Bangladesh’s external debt sustainability has weakened due to heavy dependence on non-concessional loans denominated in foreign currencies. Such loans carry higher interest rates and expose the country to exchange rate risks, especially at a time of persistent dollar shortages. The paper identified several mega projects undertaken by the previous regime as major contributors to the debt build-up. Debt servicing costs are already rising. Data from the Economic Relations Division showed that the government repaid $4 billion in FY25 in foreign loan principal and interest, up from $2.6 billion in the previous year. Experts said that without careful debt management, rising external repayments could crowd out spending on essential imports, development and social priorities.

title: RMG productivity rises 4.19pc due to automation
body: Bangladesh’s readymade garments industry has achieved annual productivity growth of 4.19 per cent between 2014 and 2023, driven by automation and technological upgrades, according to a recent study by the Bangladesh Institute of Development Studies. The study, titled ‘Technological changes at the process and sub-process level in the RMG industry in Bangladesh’, said that RMG firms’ production of jackets witnessed the highest annual productivity growth by 6.59 per cent. Knit lingerie experienced productivity growth of 6.43 per cent over 10 years, followed by sweater (6.05 per cent), home textile (5.58 per cent), and t-shirt (4.39 per cent). However, products like woven shirts, woven trousers, and denim experienced comparatively low productivity growth, at 3 per cent, 1.15 per cent, and 1.81 per cent, respectively, due to lower automation. The report stated that automation-intensive areas of the RMG sector witnessed the strongest performance over the last decade, with cutting, knitting, and wet processing recording annual productivity increases of 11.13 per cent, 9.85 per cent, and 6.11 per cent, respectively. In contrast, sewing, which remained the least automated and most labour-dependent component of the production chain, posted the lowest growth of 3.57 per cent. Weaving and end finishing grew by 4.43 per cent and 4.78 per cent, respectively, over the 10 years. The research said that the RMG sector remains central to Bangladesh’s economy, contributing an estimated 8.5–10.5 per cent of GDP and generating 80–85 per cent of export earnings. The BIDS surveyed 51 RMG firms across eight products, 39 processes, and 140 subprocesses. In the cutting section, about 10-12 workers were able to cut 4,000-5,000 pieces daily through manual band knife, paper marker, or spreader during the 1980s and 1990s. However, currently, 2-3 operators could cut 8,000-10,000 pieces daily through fully automated CAD, CNC, ERP, RFID, or auto spreader technology, making it around 3-5x faster and more accurate. In knitting, the small-scale, highly labour-intensive, slow-changeover, and low-productivity, low-gauge circular machines have been replaced by microprocessor-controlled circular machines with CAD/CAM integration, digital design, and fine-gauge knitting. Currently, an operator could operate 8-10 machines at a time, which could produce 30-90 kg of fabric per machine daily, the study added. Kazi Zubair Hossain, a research associate at BIDS, stated that they documented changes in machines and technologies over time for each process in a product. ‘Our qualitative results suggest that while the early 2000s mark the start of the modernization of RMG, the following two decades are marked by automation and commitment to sustainability, particularly energy and water saving technology. The study also said that there are indications that technology convergence is currently occurring between large and medium-scale firms, a phenomenon previously exclusive to large firms. Technologies like automated cutting, semi-automatic sewing heads, laser or ozone finishing, auto-dosing in dyeing, digital QC tools, and many more are also becoming widespread in medium-scale industries, the report stated. Inamul Haq Khan, senior vice president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, said that manufacturers had invested millions in installing automatic cutting and fabric-spreading machines that could be operated via apps to improve efficiency. Big factories could go for full or semi-automation with support from banks and buyers, he added, noting that small and medium-sized units are still unable to secure the required support. Meanwhile, the BIDS recommended that the government subsidise or incentivise tasks with high potential but low productivity growth. BIDS also urged to anticipate where labour displacement might occur due to automation and plan accordingly. They also urged the government to support the simultaneous growth of domestic machinery assembly and component manufacturing to build a local textile capital-goods industry gradually.

title: Online VAT-payment will use the eVAT system: NBR
body: The National Board of Revenue announced on Tuesday that all online value-added tax or VAT-related activities would now be conducted through the eVAT System, following the renaming of the existing iVAS platform. The decision was taken to eliminate confusion arising from the similar pronunciation of iVAS (VAT automation system) and iBAS++, the government›s integrated budgeting and accounting system, said a press release. To ensure greater clarity for taxpayers, businesses, and stakeholders, the iVAS System has been formally rebranded as the eVAT System, with all its functions and services remaining unchanged. The NBR also said that the eVAT System would serve as the single digital platform for conducting a wide range of VAT-related activities, including online VAT registration, electronic submission of VAT returns, and all A-Challan and e-payment-based transactions. Moreover, the system would allow manufacturers to submit input-output coefficients for VAT revenue collection through Mushak 4.3, a key compliance requirement. The eVAT System would also facilitate real-time VAT collection through PKI software-based applications, strengthening transparency and efficiency in revenue mobilisation. The revenue authority emphasised that the transition is part of its broader efforts to modernise VAT administration and make compliance easier for taxpayers through digital solutions. The NBR noted that work is ongoing to enhance further the user-friendliness, capacity, and effectiveness of the eVAT System, encouraging wider adoption across the VAT ecosystem.

title: JBCCI welcomes the Bangladesh-Japan EPA
body: The Japan-Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry welcomed the announcement of the Agreement in Principle on the Bangladesh–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement. In a statement signed by JBCCI president Tareq Rafi Bhuiyan (Jun), the chamber said the EPA would mark a significant step toward finalising a comprehensive economic partnership between the two countries. ‘The EPA aims to deepen trade, investment, and service linkages and is expected to play a pivotal role as Bangladesh transitions from Least Developed Country status in 2026,’ said the statement. JBCCI also stated that the current agreement in principle reflected alignment on the structure and key provisions of the EPA, with formal signing to follow upon completion of necessary legal and cabinet-level processes in both countries. The statement also said that JBCCI actively supported this process by launching policy studies, such as ‘Accelerating Japan-Bangladesh EPA: Key Priorities and Strategies Ahead’, developed in collaboration with Policy Exchange Bangladesh. The chamber also conducted a perception survey among its members and Shoo Koo Kai (JCIAD) members, reflecting the views of businesses engaged in bilateral trade and investment. They also engaged with public and private stakeholders to present research-based recommendations and practical insights for the negotiations. Issues raised by private sector stakeholders, such as simplified rules of origin, increased market access for RMG, liberalisation of service sectors, and regulatory cooperation, have been recognised in the structure of the EPA as it stands, JBCCI stated. On Monday, the interim government announced the EPA following Commerce Adviser Sheikh Bashir Uddin’s telephone conversation with Japanese Foreign Minister Motegi Toshimitsu regarding the conclusion of the EPA negotiations. Under the EPA, Bangladesh would gain immediate duty-free access for 7,379 products. In contrast, Japan would gain preferential access to 1,039 product categories in Bangladesh, including liberalisation of over 100 service sub-sectors, promoting investment, skills, and innovation. As the process now enters its legal and ratification phase, JBCCI remained committed to supporting implementation, capacity building, and outreach so that the benefits of this landmark agreement are maximised for both nations, the statement added.

title: BB initiates integrated policy as AI reshapes financial sector
body: Experts and senior officials gathered at the Bangladesh Bank Training Academy (BBTA) to discuss the transformative power of Artificial Intelligence in the financial sector, emphasizing the urgent need for a robust regulatory framework. The seminar, titled ‘Artificial Intelligence: Reshaping Financial Services and Its Regulation,’ was held on Monday at the AKN Ahmed Auditorium in Mirpur. The event highlighted how AI is driving far-reaching changes globally, opening new frontiers in risk management, fraud detection, customer service, and product innovation. However, speakers noted that the increasing adoption of these technologies necessitates effective policies to ensure ethical and safe usage. During the panel discussion, Mohammad Zakir Hasan, executive director (ICT) of Bangladesh Bank, revealed that the central bank has already initiated the formulation of an integrated AI policy. To facilitate this, a seven-member professional AI team has been formed. Hasan emphasized that the upcoming policy will prioritize data protection, consumer rights preservation, and comprehensive risk management. Mohammad Ali, managing director of Pubali Bank PLC, delivered the keynote paper, outlining a clear roadmap for an effective AI strategy tailored for the financial sector. Md Rezaul Karim, joint director (ICT) of BBTA, presented on the practical adoption of AI within financial institutions. Professor BM Mainul Hossain, director of the Institute of Information Technology at Dhaka University, stressed that a ‘meaningful and structured bond’ between regulators, technology users, and researchers is essential for effective policy implementation. Md Mahbub Karim, director of the Bangladesh Computer Council, pointed out that while national AI policies exist, focused discussion within the banking sector has remained limited, making the central bank’s new initiative vital. M Rezaul Hassan, Group CEO of Reve Group, urged for more active engagement from user groups to scale AI pilot projects into larger implementations. Presiding over the seminar, Md Hanif Mia, executive director of BBTA, described AI as a powerful tool that can make the financial sector more inclusive, efficient, and stable if governed by proper oversight. He urged banks to view AI not merely as a series of pilot projects, but as a long-term strategic capability. He concluded by noting that successful AI integration requires a foundation of accurate data, skilled human resources, robust cybersecurity, and explainable systems. The seminar was moderated by Md Masud Rana, additional director of the academy, and attended by senior officials from various commercial banks and IT heads.

title: US stocks flat after strong GDP report
body: Wall Street stocks were little changed early Tuesday as markets digested surprisingly strong US economic data that could change the calculus on upcoming monetary policy decisions. US gross domestic product in the third quarter came in at 4.3 per cent on an annualized basis, easily topping expectations and the loftiest growth in two years. But the report, which also revealed accelerating inflation, shows ‘the US economy was certainly running on the warm side in Q3,’ said Briefing.com analyst Patrick O’Hare, adding that the data will “stir some concerns” about recent Fed interest rate cuts. About 10 minutes into trading, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.1 per cent at 48,323.52. The broad-based S&P 500 added 0.1 per cent at 6,882.02, while the tech-rich Nasdaq Composite Index also gained 0.1 percent to 23,444.24.

title: Pakistan gets three bids for privatisation of state-run airline
body: Pakistan received three bids on Tuesday for the privatisation of its embattled national carrier PIA, in what is seen as a litmus test of Islamabad’s efforts to sell loss-making state firms. Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), long accused by critics of being bloated and poorly run, has found funds drying up as the government struggles with a balance of payments crisis. ‘It was essential to make this process transparent because the biggest transaction of Pakistan’s history is about to take place,’ Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told his cabinet in a televised statement after the bidding process was broadcast live. ‘If the bidding is successful, then the privatisation process will take off,’ Sharif said. Representatives of the three bidding consortiums each placed their bids for the 75 percent stake on offer in a transparent box. One is led by the private Pakistani carrier Air Blue, another by Lucky Cement, and another by Arif Habib, an investment firm. The government will unveil a reference price for PIA later on Wednesday and then announce a winner if the minimum is met. The sale offer comes after last year’s privatisation attempt failed with just one bid for $36 million—far below the $300 million–$305 million wanted by the government. Before being de-listed from the Pakistan stock exchange, the airline reported a net loss of $437 million for the 2022 full year on revenue of $854 million. Islamabad has pledged to divest dozens of its cash-burning enterprises in the finance, energy, industrial and retailing sectors by 2029 under a $7 billion loan programme agreed with the International Monetary Fund in 2024. Many of the companies have incurred billions of dollars in losses because of mismanagement and corruption, forcing the government to inject funds to keep them afloat. Founded in 1955, PIA was a symbol of national pride and rapid growth for years, but its reputation has suffered due to financial losses and safety lapses. It was banned from flying to the European Union, Britain and the United States in June 2020, a month after one of its Airbus A-320 jets crashed onto a Karachi street, killing nearly 100 people. Europe and Britain allowed PIA flights to resume this year, but operations have not yet resumed for the United States. Just 18 of its fleet of 34 planes are in active service, according to officials.

title: Wheat cultivation target set at 7,275 hectares in Dinajpur
body: The Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) has set a target to cultivate wheat on 7,275 hectares of land in the district during the current season, aiming to boost production and meet the country’s growing demand. Deputy director of DAE Md. Afzal Hossain said the cultivation target covers all 13 upazilas of the district, with a production goal of 3.75 metric tons per hectare. If the target is achieved, total wheat production in the district is expected to reach around 25,650 metric tons. Md. Afzal Hossain said that the weather conditions this season are favorable for wheat cultivation. He expressed optimism that, barring any natural disasters, production may exceed the set target. Farmers began cultivating early wheat varieties such as BARI-25, BARI-26 and BARI-27 from November 15, and the crops have already sprouted. Wheat varieties including BARI-27, 28, 30, 31 and 32 will continue to be sown until December 31. Following the harvest of Aman paddy, farmers have been busy preparing land using organic manure and cow dung to increase yields. High-yielding wheat seeds, particularly BARI-30, 31 and 32, have been supplied by the Department of Agriculture, with the expected yield set at 3.75 tons per hectare. To support cultivation, irrigation facilities using electric-powered machines have been ensured. Drainage systems have also been installed in advance to protect crops from potential damage caused by storms or heavy rainfall. The deputy director added that the initiative is part of a broader effort to reduce dependence on wheat imports. The Wheat Research Institute is supplying improved high-yielding seed varieties, while agricultural field workers are providing continuous guidance to farmers across the district. In recent years, wheat cultivation has expanded beyond highlands to include medium lands and river-side char areas. According to agriculture department sources, wheat was cultivated on 6,210 hectares in Dinajpur last year, producing 23,287 metric tons at an average yield of 3.75 tons per hectare.

title: MTB holds trade-based financial compliance conference
body: Mutual Trust Bank PLC recently organised annual trade-based compliance conference 2025 to create awareness on key deliverables for prevention of trade-based money Laundering. The conference was held for MTB officials relevant to trade servicing from branches and corporate head offices, said a press release. More than 100 participants attended in person, and around 300 participants attended virtually. MD and CEO of MTB, Syed Mahbubur Rahman, attended the conference as chief guest. Professor of Bangladesh Institute of Bank Management Shah Md Ahsan Habib attended the conference as guest lecturer. Additional managing director and group chief risk officer Chowdhury Akhtar Asif and deputy managing director and head of credit risk management division Usman Rashed Muyeen attended the event. Deputy Managing Director and chief anti-money laundering compliance officer Rais Uddin Ahmad moderated the day-long conference.

title: Mercantile Bank holds cash management training
body: Mercantile Bank PLC organised a daylong ‘Cash Management’ training workshop in Chattogram on Saturday to strengthen operational efficiency and enhance professional competence among its cash officers. The Head of Training and Development at the bank, SM Salim Uddin, attended the inaugural session as the chief guest, according to a press release. SEVP of the Chattogram Region, Md Shaiful Alam Chowdhury, attended the ceremony as a special guest. Head of the Branches Operations Control Division Muhammad Khorshed Alam and Faculty of Bank’s training institute Shahin Akther attended the event. Addressing the participants, the speakers emphasised the importance of accuracy, compliance, and vigilance in cash operations. They provided valuable guidance and expressed optimism that the training would contribute to improved service quality and risk management across branches. The primary objective of the training was to enhance participants’ skills in detecting counterfeit currency and to familiarise them with the ‘Bangladesh Bank Note Refund Regulations, 2025’. A total of 61 officers from various branches under the Chattogram zone attended the workshop.

title: SBC pays Tk 50 crore dividend for FY 2025–26
body: The state-owned Sadharan Bima Corporation has paid Tk 50 crore as dividend to the government for the fiscal year 2025–26. The dividend cheque was handed over on Tuesday to finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed by SBC board chairman Mohammad Zainul Bari, said a press release. Secretary of the Financial Institutions Division, Nazma Mobarek, attended the event, along with SBC managing director (Additional Secretary) Md Harun-or-Rashid. Additional Secretaries of the Financial Institutions Division, Md Azimuddin Biswas and Md Saeed Qutub, joint secretary Sheikh Farid, SBC general manager (Finance) Bibekananda Saha, and deputy general manager (Central Accounts Division) A K Maksudul Ahsan Bhuiyan, among others, attended the event. In addition to the dividend, the SBC deposited Tk 230.61 crore into the national exchequer during the 2025 income year in the form of income tax and value-added tax. Over the past 10 years, the corporation has paid approximately Tk 2,880 crore to the state treasury under these heads. Notably, among all state-owned corporations and commercial entities under the Financial Institutions Division, the General Insurance Corporation paid the highest amount of dividend in the FY 2025–26.
