title: Midland Bank signs MoU with Marco Polo
body: Midland Bank PLC recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Marco Polo Dhaka Hotel. The MoU signing ceremony was held at Midland Bank’s head office in Gulshan-2 in Dhaka, said a press release. Chief technology officer of Midland Bank, Md Nazmul Huda Sarkar, and operations manager of Marco Polo, Md Asraf Uddin, signed the agreement on behalf of their respective organisations. Through this partnership, Midland Bank cardholders (Debit, Credit and Prepaid) will enjoy a 50 per cent discount on the published room rate, a 15 per cent discount at the restaurant (Polo Amber) and café (Marco Street), a 30 per cent discount on the banquet hall (Sapphire), and a 15 per cent discount on Polo Spa services. Head of PRD of Midland Bank, Md Rashadul Anwar, and assistant manager of sales and marketing at Marco Polo, Marufa Nur Maria, among others, attended the event.

title: NOVOAIR wins Excellence in Business Award
body: NOVOAIR has been awarded the prestigious ‘Excellence in Business–2025’ at the digital excellence award ceremony organised by Eastern Bank PLC. The award recognises NOVOAIR’s digital excellence and commitment to service quality, said a press release. The award ceremony was held on Sunday at a renowned convention centre in the capital. Director of marketing and sales at NOVOAIR, Sohail Majid, received the awards from EBL managing director and chief executive officer Ali Reza Iftekhar. Sohail Majid said, ‘This recognition will further inspire us in our journey ahead. NOVOAIR continues to prioritise modern technology and digital innovation to enhance passenger services. Our commitment to delivering improved service and ensuring customer satisfaction remains steadfast across all levels of our operations.’ Currently, NOVOAIR operates daily flights from Dhaka to Cox’s Bazar, Chattogram, Sylhet, and Saidpur.

title: Ansar-VDP Unnayan Bank holds 210th EC meeting
body: Ansar-VDP Unnayan Bank’s board of directors organised its 210th meeting of the executive committee on Monday, said a press release. Ansar-VDP Unnayan Bank chairman and director general of Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party Major General Abdul Motaleb Sazzad Mahmud presided over the meeting. Managing director Mir Mofazzul Hossain, director Md Ruhul Amin Bhuiyan, Md Atowar Hossen, Md Rafiqul Islam, and Md Rasheduzzaman attended the meeting. In the meeting, the bank took some important decisions along with implementation of divisional offices to accelerate the operational activities of the bank.

title: Modhumoti Bank holds 141st EC meeting
body: Modhumoti Bank PLC organised its 141st meeting of the executive committee on Monday at Bank’s head office. Chairman of the bank, Salahuddin Alamgir, presided over the meeting, said a press release. Managing director and CEO of the Bank, Md Shafiul Azam Mostafa Kamal, and Mohammad Ismail Hossain, Nemai Kumar Saha, among others, attended the meeting.

title: Runner AGM approves 10 per cent cash dividend
body: Runner Automobiles PLC organised its 25th annual general meeting on Monday at Kurmitola Golf Club, with participation from shareholders, said a press release. At the meeting, shareholders approved the board of directors’ proposal of a 10 per cent cash dividend for all shareholders, including sponsor directors, for the financial year ending on June 30, 2025. All other agenda items were also unanimously approved. Managing director and CEO of the company, Nazrul Islam, delivered a welcome speech, a presentation of the previous year’s financial report, and the shareholders’ Q and A session. Company secretary Mizanur Rahman moderated the event. CFO Sonat Dutta, other distinguished members of the board of directors, among others, attended the meeting. Chairman Hafizur Rahman Khan closed the AGM with his guiding remarks.

title: Unimass Holdings celebrates 16th anniversary
body: Unimass Holdings Limited recently celebrated its 16th anniversary of success. The day was observed through an intriguing event, said a press release. On this special day, Unimass Holdings expressed deep gratitude to all its dedicated employees, esteemed customers, suppliers, and well-wishers. This long journey would not have been possible without their continued support and cooperation. Through quality, professionalism, and innovation, the company has strengthened its position in the country’s real estate sector. On this occasion, a Spokesperson from Unimass said, ‘We are extremely excited that we have kept our promises for 16 years. Our goal is not just to achieve business success, but also to contribute to the sustainable progress of the country. We are committed to moving forward with innovative solutions and ensuring the highest quality service to our customers in the days ahead.’

title: NRBC Bank holds workshop on online monitoring system
body: NRBC Bank organised a workshop on reporting to online import monitoring system and online export monitoring system introduced by Bangladesh Bank. The workshop was held on Sunday at the Human Resource and Training Development Centre of the bank’s Head Office, said a press release. Managing director and chief executive officer of the Bank, Md Touhidul Alam Khan, attended the workshop as chief guest. Deputy director of the Foreign Exchange Operations Department of BB, Laila Akter and assistant director, Tasfia Tanjim Snigdha, conducted training on proper reporting to reduce risks in foreign exchange transactions, compliance with regulatory guidelines, ensuring compliance, and effective use of modern technology to enhance customer service. Head of the International Division of the bank, Hasnat Reza Mahibbul Alam, among other representatives from importers and exporters, attended the workshop. Touhidul Alam said that proper reporting through the import–export monitoring system helps ensure accurate import costs of goods and timely repatriation of export proceeds.

title: Kuwait signs $4.1 billion deal with China to build port
body: Kuwait has signed a deal worth $4.1 billion with China to complete the construction of a major port, as the oil-rich country seeks to diversify its economy with a bigger role in global trade. The State Audit Bureau, a government oversight body responsible for monitoring public funds, on Monday said ‘the engineering, procurement, and construction contract to complete the Mubarak Al-Kabeer Port project will cost 1.28 billion Kuwaiti dinars ($4.164 billion)’. Prime Minister Sheikh Ahmad Al-Abdullah Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah attended the ‘ceremony for inking the engineering-supply-construction contract for building Mubarak Al-Kabeer Port on Boubyan island,’ state media reported. He said the key project would ‘enhance Kuwait’s share in the regional and international trade and global supply chain’. Chinese acting charge d’affaires Liu Xiang said the deal ‘constitutes participation in the ‘belt and road’ initiative’. In 2023, Kuwait signed seven memoranda of understanding with China on projects including the Mubarak al-Kabeer Port, as well as housing, water treatment and renewable energy. China has been focusing on the Middle East as part of its Belt and Road Initiative, a vast global infrastructure project developed over the last decade under President Xi Jinping.

title: Govt approves drilling of five gas wells in Bhola
body: Bangladesh interim government on Tuesday approved a proposal to dig five gas wells in Bhola at an estimated cost of Tk 907.29 crore to boost domestic gas production, reduce reliance on imported fuel and strengthen national energy security. It also endorsed several large-scale power distribution projects aimed at modernising and expanding electricity infrastructure in the Dhaka and Mymensingh divisions. The approvals came at a meeting of the Advisers Council Committee on Government Purchaseat the Cabinet Division Conference Room of the Bangladesh Secretariat with Finance Adviser Dr Salehuddin Ahmed in the chair. The committee approved the proposal from the Energy and Mineral Resources Division to drill five new gas wells in Bhola. These include Shahbazpur-5, Shahbazpur-7, Bhola North-3 and Bhola North-4 and Shahbazpur North East-1. The wells will be drilled through an international tender process using a one-stage, two-envelope procurement method on a turn-key basis. Following technical and financial evaluation, Sinopec International Petroleum Service Corporation of China was recommended as the responsive bidder. It is also expected to support industrial growth and ensure a more stable gas supply for power generation and other economic activities. In the same meeting, the committee reviewed and approved four major power distribution procurement proposals under a special revised project titled ‘Modernisation and Capacity Enhancement of BPDB Power Distribution System (Dhaka-Mymensingh Division).’ The project include construction and augmentation of 12 air-insulated 33/11 kV substations on a turn-key basis, six substations at a cost of Tk 130.00 crore, another six substations costing Tk 113.82 crore. Two other approved proposals are construction and augmentation of 14 gas-insulated 33/11 kV substations, seven substations at an estimated cost of Tk 220.90 crore, seven more substations costing Tk 207.91 crore. The committee noted that the power distribution projects would help meet rising electricity demand, reduce system losses, improve grid reliability and ensure a better quality of power supply across the Dhaka-Mymensingh division.

title: Bangladesh interim govt to procure rice, edible oil, lentil to stabilise prices
body: Bangladesh interim government has taken fresh initiatives to strengthen food security by approving proposals to procure 100,000 metric tons of rice, 4.75 crore liters of edible oil and 10,000 metric tons of lentil to meet the local growing demand aiming to stabilise prices and ensure smooth supply apparently ahead of the holy month of Ramadan. The approvals came from the 51st meeting of the Advisers Council Committee on Government Purchase in this year held today at the Cabinet Division Conference Room at Bangladesh Secretariat with Finance Adviser Dr Salehuddin Ahmed in the chair. The meeting recommended approval of two proposals from the Ministry of Food. Under the decisions, 50,000 metric tons of non-basmati parboiled rice will be procured through international open tender method from India with around Taka 217.53 crore, while another 50,000 metric tons of white rice will be imported from Pakistan under a government-to-government (G2G) arrangement with around Taka 241.52 crore. Officials said the measures would help maintain adequate public food stocks and curb market volatility during Ramadan, when demand for essential commodities rises significantly. The Directorate General of Food will implement the procurement, ensuring timely arrival of consignments to strengthen buffer stocks. Besides, in a move aimed at keeping edible oil prices stable during the holy month of Ramadan, the government has approved separate proposals to procure 4.75 crore litres of edible oil, including soybean oil and rice bran oil. Under the decisions, the government will procure 1 crore litres of refined rice bran oil locally while 3.75 crore litres of soybean oil from international sources under direct purchase methods. Officials said the procurement would help maintain adequate supply in the domestic market and prevent price hikes during Ramadan, when consumption of edible oil increases sharply. The Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB) is expected to play a key role in distributing the oil through subsidised sales across the country. Meanwhile, the day’s meeting also approved the procurement of 10,000 metric tons of lentils through national open tender method with around Taka 72.20 crore to meet rising consumer demand during the holy month of Ramadan. Officials said the procurement would help ensure adequate supply while keeping prices within affordable levels. The lentils will be procured in 50-kg bags and distributed through government channels to stabilise the market and support low and middle-income consumers.

title: Dhaka-Delhi trade relations should follow different dynamics
body: Interim government finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed on Tuesday said that politics and trade between Bangladesh and India should follow different dynamics. There is sensitivity and naivety regarding diplomatic issues, said the finance adviser while commenting on the diplomatic row between the two neighbours since the taking of power by Professor Muhammad Yunus-led interim government after the ouster of the Awami League regime on August 5, 2024 in the wake of a mass uprising. Deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina fled to India on the day and has been staying there since. ‘Trade should remain unaffected,’ added the finance adviser after a meeting of the advisory council committee on government purchase at the secretariat in the capital Dhaka. At the meeting, the committee approved the purchase of 50,000 tonnes of non-basmati rice to be procured from India through the international open tender method at about Tk 217.53 crore and 50,000 tonnes of atap rice from Pakistan under a government-to-government negotiation at Tk 241.52 crore. Mentioning that rhetoric is used in foreign affairs and politics, the finance adviser said that the current tension between Dhaka and New Delhi would ease soon. A series of incidents in both countries has recently dampened the bilateral relations between Bangladesh and India. Salehuddin said that they were trying to improve the situation. ‘The chief adviser has reached out…,’ he said without elaborating the matter. The finance adviser said that he talked to the Bangladesh high commissioner in New Delhi who was trying to improve the situation. At Tuesday’s purchase meeting, approvals were given separately to procure 4.75 crore litres of edible oil, including soya bean oil and rice bran oil. Under the decisions, one crore litres of refined rice bran oil will be procured locally while 3.75 crore litres of soya bean oil from international sources under the direct purchase method. The procurement of 10,000 tonnes of lentils through the national open tender method at Tk 72.20 crore was approved to meet higher consumer demand for the commodity during Ramadan, the month of fasting which will begin in the second half of February, 2026. Besides, three consignments of triple super phosphate fertiliser, each of 30,000 tonnes with Tk 181.74 crore, and one consignment of 40,000 tonnes of di ammonium phosphate fertiliser at Tk 324.08 crore under state-level agreements between the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation and OCP Nutricrops of Morocco were also approved.

title: BGMEA urges factories to close near airport for Tarique’s return
body: The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association has urged export-oriented readymade garment factories located in several areas surrounding Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport to remain closed on Thursday, the day BNP’s Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman is scheduled to return to Bangladesh from London. A notice issued on Monday, signed by BGMEA acting secretary Md Saiful Islam, urged the owners of the factories located in Uttara (East and West), Uttarkhan, Dakshinkhan, Khilkhet, Abdullahpur, Turag, Tongi, Pubail, Rupganj, Kanchan Bridge, and the eastern part of Ashulia to consider keeping their factories closed on that day. ‘Tarique Rahman would arrive in Dhaka by air on Thursday at about 11:00 am. As his return comes after a 17-year absence, a large public gathering is expected in and around the airport area, the notice stated. The notice also stated that such congestion might disrupt workers’ commuting and the transportation of import-export consignments in the surrounding industrial zones. Considering the overall situation, BGMEA urged factory authorities in these areas to take necessary decisions to ensure the safety and convenience of workers and to manage import-export logistics smoothly. The association suggested that factory management might consider declaring a holiday on Thursday, following discussions with workers’ representatives, provided that duties can be adjusted on another day before or after. Moreover, BGMEA has also requested that covered vans used for urgent import-export operations use alternative routes until the overall situation of the areas returns to normal. BNP acting chairperson Tarique Rahman is scheduled to arrive in Dhaka on Thursday after spending over 17 years in the United Kingdom.

title: 5 banks to be delisted as 582cr shares wiped out
body: Bangladesh Bank has asked five crisis-hit banks to wipe out their entire paid-up share capital, a move that will permanently delist them from the stock market and wipe out shareholder investments ahead of their planned merger into a new entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC. In separate letters issued on Monday, the central bank instructed First Security Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, Union Bank and EXIM Bank to reduce the value of their shares to zero under the Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025. The decision effectively eliminates shareholder claims, as Bangladesh Bank has ruled out any compensation, citing deeply negative net asset values at the banks. As a result, investors stand to lose about Tk 5,815 crore at face value and roughly Tk 1,330 crore based on the last traded market prices. Bangladesh Bank said that both sponsor shareholders and general investors will receive nothing because accumulated losses have exceeded capital, in some cases by as much as Tk 450 against each Tk 10 share. The central bank added that compensation for small investors would only be possible if the government chooses to intervene. The five banks were among 36 listed banks on the Dhaka Stock Exchange. Trading in their shares was suspended on November 6, a day after Bangladesh Bank formally declared them non-viable and initiated the merger process. The suspension triggered widespread concern among retail investors, many of whom had already seen the value of their holdings erode sharply over the years. On November 5, Bangladesh Bank dissolved the boards of the five banks and appointed administrators to manage operations during the transition. The administrators were tasked with keeping daily banking activities running, ensuring uninterrupted remittance flows and letter of credit settlements, integrating IT systems to enable centralised operations, and rationalising branches and staffing to reduce duplication. Bangladesh Bank said prolonged mismanagement, massive loan irregularities and chronic liquidity shortages had rendered the banks unsustainable as standalone institutions. The merger, it argued, is aimed at protecting depositors and preserving financial stability rather than safeguarding shareholder value. Under the plan, Sammilito Islami Bank will begin operations with Tk 35,000 crore in paid-up capital, making it the most capitalised bank in the country. The new lender will initially remain under government ownership but will be run on professional lines, similar to a private commercial bank. Bangladesh Bank expects the government to seek a strategic partner and eventually transfer ownership to the private sector, likely within two years. Market data shows how severely investor confidence had already weakened. On the last trading day before suspension, EXIM Bank shares closed at Tk 3, First Security Islami Bank at Tk 1.9, Social Islami Bank at Tk 3, Union Bank at Tk 1.5 and Global Islami Bank at Tk 1.7 per share.

title: Dhaka, Tokyo finalise deal
body: Bangladesh will enjoy duty-free access to the Japanese market for 7,379 products, including readymade garments, under the Economic Partnership Agreement between the two countries. The proposed agreement was finalised on Monday. Japan will receive duty-free access from Bangladesh for its 1,039 products under the EPA, negotiation for which began in May 2024 between the two sides in Dhaka following recommendations made by a joint study group on December 27, 2023. Economists and trade experts welcomed the announcement on the EPA, saying that the successful implementation of it would help Bangladesh address the challenges of its graduation from the least developed country to a developing one on November 24, 2026. They, however, said that the pros and cons of the EPA would be known once it was signed. At a briefing at the secretariat in the capital Dhaka on Monday, commerce adviser Sheikh Bashir Uddin said that the signing of the EPA with the world’s fourth largest economy would take place in the next month. The seven-round EPA negotiations successfully concluded during a telephone conversation with Japanese foreign minister Motegi Toshimitsu, added Bashir. The briefing was attended, among others, by chief adviser’s special envoy on international affairs Lutfey Siddiqi, Bangladesh Investment Development Authority executive chairman Chowdhury Ashik Mahmud Bin Harun, commerce ministry secretary Mahbubur Rahman and EPA chief negotiator Ayesha Akter. Under the EPA, Bangladesh will benefit from single stage transformation provisions for RMG products, which means that the rule of origin will be easy. Besides, trade in services sector will also see a substantial commitment from both sides. Bangladesh has agreed to open 97 sub-sectors to Japan, while Japan will open 120 sub-sectors to Bangladesh across four modes of supply. This is expected to foster increased Japanese investment in Bangladesh along with greater technology transfer, said the BIDA executive chairman. Former Bangladesh Trade and Tariff Commission member Mostafa Abid Khan said that the advantages and disadvantages of the EPA would be known once the deal was made public. ‘Until then the proposed EPA is all about the country’s efforts to retain duty-free access in the Japanese market for the country’s top export item RMG,’ he said. Bangladesh will not enjoy duty-free access of markets in the developed and developing countries, including Japan, for its export items once it leaves the LDC bloc in the next year. Japan has committed to extend duty-free benefit to RMG of Bangladesh until 2029. The proposed EPA will help the country retain the benefit beyond 2029, said Centre for Policy Dialogue distinguished fellow Mustafizur Rahman. The EPA will be reciprocal for which Bangladesh will have to give benefits to Japan, he added. Bangladesh has one effective bilateral preferential trade agreement with Bhutan. But the proposed one with Japan is highly significant as far as the country’s trade and investment concerned, said Policy Exchange Bangladesh chairman M Masrur Reaz, adding that the experience of the negotiations would be handy during bilateral deals with the other developed and developing countries. Japan is one of the country’s major trading partners, with bilateral trade of about $3 billion. In the 2024-25 financial year, Bangladesh exported goods worth $1.41 billion, of which goods worth $1.19 billion were RMG items, along with home textiles, leather and leather goods, according to the Export Promotion Bureau. Bangladesh’s imports from Japan stood at $1.81 billion in FY 2023-24, according to Bangladesh Bank data, although various provisional data indicated that imports fell to $1.51 billion in FY25, including major items like automobiles, steels, iron and ships. Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association president Mohammad Hatem said that the proposed EPA would be a win-win agreement for both countries. The BKMEA always urges the government to sign bilateral trade deals with the country’s trading partners, he said.

title: NBR Revenue collection falls short of target by Tk 24,000c
body: Bangladesh’s revenue collection witnessed a year-on-year growth of 15.15 per cent in the July-November period of the financial year 2025-26 to Tk 148,975 crore, higher from Tk 129,380 crore collected in the same period of FY25, according to National Board of Revenue data. However, revenue collection fell short by Tk 24,047 crore of the target set at Tk 173,242 crore. In a single month, November 2025, revenue collection also grew by 14.2 per cent to Tk 29,659 crore, up from Tk 25,970 crore collected in November 2024. The collection in November also fell short of its target by Tk 6,667 crore, set at Tk 36,926.49 crore, according to NBR data. During the July-November period of FY26, customs collections stood at Tk 42,864 crore, 5.28 per cent higher than the Tk 40,713 crore collected in the first five months of FY25. However, the revenue collection from customs missed the target of Tk 50,980 crore by over Tk 8,100 crore. Revenue collection from the VAT section was Tk 58,231 crore in the first five months of FY26, which was 21.97 per cent higher than the Tk 47,744 crore collected in the same period of the previous financial year, though the section also missed its target of Tk 62,049 crore. Fetching a growth of 17 per cent, revenue collection from the income tax sector stood at Tk 47,881 crore in the July-November period of FY26, up from Tk 40,922 crore in the corresponding period of FY25, the NBR data stated. Collections from the income tax sector also fell short of the target by over Tk 12,000 crore, to Tk 59,995 crore. Still, revenue collected from indirect sources was higher than that from direct sources in July-October of FY26, according to NBR data. An NBR official said that the government set a highly ambitious target for FY26, so the collection from the first five months of FY26 was nothing special. For FY26, the government set a revenue collection target of Tk 4,99,000 crore through the NBR, which was about 8 per cent of the total GDP. To reach the target, Bangladesh needs to collect approximately Tk 40,000 crore in revenue per month. However, the NBR official expressed hope that the gap between targets and collections will be narrower this year, as the NBR has expanded its workforce by increasing tax zones nationwide, along with some policies on automation and online tax filing. Stakeholders always stated that Bangladesh has been struggling to finance project developments amid a persistently low tax-to-GDP ratio, one of the lowest globally. In FY25, the NBR faced a record revenue collection shortfall of Tk 92,625, after collecting Tk 3,70,874 crore, which was about 3.08 per cent lower than the Tk 3,82,678 crore collected in FY24. In FY25, the revised revenue collection target was Tk 4,63,500 crore. Recently, NBR chairman Abdur Rahman Khan said that Bangladesh’s tax-GDP ratio remained low, and more research is needed to identify why specific segments of the economy remain untaxed. As the country prepares for LDC graduation, import duties would inevitably decline due to global trade obligations, making a stronger domestic tax base essential, he said. He said that the long-delayed, World Bank-funded automation project for NBR would soon begin, and the authority intends to automate all of its internal processes under the initiative.
