title: Elected govt must prioritise capital market for finance: stakeholders
body: Bangladesh’s stock market has remained largely non-functional as a source of business finance amid prolonged government apathy, weak governance and massive manipulation, and market experts now expect the next elected government to prioritise the capital market and rebuild it as a primary source of economic financing. They said restoring the market’s role is critical as the economy can no longer rely almost entirely on banks to fund investment and industrial expansion. The failure of the stock market to mobilise long-term capital has forced banks to shoulder financing responsibilities they are not designed to handle. As a result, banks have funded long-gestation industrial projects using short-term deposits, deepening structural weaknesses, worsening asset-liability mismatches and contributing to rising non-performing loans. They said that this imbalance has reduced the economy’s capacity to diversify, invest in new industries and generate higher-value growth at a critical stage of development. The DSEX, the benchmark index of the Dhaka Stock Exchange, has lost about 762 points since September 3 amid political uncertainty, economic pressures and a series of reform initiatives by the securities regulator. With the national election scheduled for February 12, investors now expect a change in sentiment after the transfer of power from the interim government, which assumed office on August 8, 2024 following a mass uprising. Dhaka Stock Exchange director and BLI Securities managing director Minhaz Mannan Emon told New Age that the next elected government must place the capital market at the centre of economic financing because Bangladesh can no longer depend almost entirely on bank credit. He said that banks are under severe strain from high non-performing loans, weak governance and limited capacity to fund long-term investment, leaving the government with shrinking financing options at a time when the economy needs large funds to revive growth, support industry and stabilise employment. Under these conditions, he said, strengthening the capital market is no longer optional. Minhaz said the current weakness of the stock market reflects damage accumulated over the past 15 years due to political interference, poor regulatory oversight and entrenched corruption. These factors steadily destroyed investor confidence and turned the market into a largely speculative space. As a result, genuine investors left, quality companies avoided listing and the market became detached from its core function of financing productive investment. He said the interim government’s crackdown on manipulation and irregularities after the July political change was necessary and long overdue. However, the absence of a clear political horizon and prolonged market dullness kept investors cautious, with many waiting for signals of long-term policy direction. According to Minhaz, continuity of reform under the next political government is critical. The upcoming government, he said, should appoint a competent regulator, ensure policy consistency and build on the groundwork already laid by the current commission. DSE director and Shyamol Equity Management managing director Md Sajedul Islam said that expectations surrounding the next government are high because the market has suffered a severe crisis for years. He said the capital market has beenh largely ignored despite its importance as a source of long-term finance. The next government, he said, should focus on bringing quality initial public offerings and adopting stable, long-term policies rather than frequent regulatory changes that unsettle investors. However, he said that reforms take time to bear fruit and the market cannot be revived overnight. Saiful Islam, president of the DSE Brokers Association of Bangladesh, said that the next elected government must give top priority to the stock market, as economic recovery will remain difficult without a functional capital market. He stressed the need to continue reforms, ensure policy consistency, and align regulations with global practices. He also said that the government should facilitate quality IPOs and introduce diversified products, while curbing manipulation and malpractice to ensure a level playing field for all participants. Prime Bank Securities managing director and chief executive officer Md Moniruzzaman said the capital market continues to face multiple challenges and urged the next government to continue reforms while adopting investor-friendly policies. He stressed the need to curb manipulation and political interference and ensure transparency, governance and credible financial disclosures. He also said placing reasonable limits on excessive bank borrowing by large businesses could encourage companies to raise funds from the capital market, helping restore balance in the financial system and reduce pressure on banks.

title: Local mills in crisis as yarn imports from India surge
body: Textile millers in Bangladesh said that local spinning mills are in a deep crisis due to a sharp rise in low-priced yarn imports from India, threatening the existence of the country’s textile sector. They also said that yarn imports from India over the last 22 months have witnessed an alarming 137 per cent surge, as Indian traders have been dumping yarn in Bangladesh at prices around 30 cents per kilogram lower. Indian traders exported yarn at less than $2 per kilogram, at least 30 cents below prices in Bangladesh. They also said that during the period, Bangladesh imported $2 billion worth of yarn from India, averaging 1,600 tonnes per day. They were speaking at a press conference organised by the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association at Gulshan Club in the capital on Sunday. In his speech, Showkat Aziz Russell, president of the BTMA, said that due to the import of yarn at bottom prices, nearly 50 spinning mills have shut down - investments worth Tk 500–700 crore. ‘In fact, one of my five textile mills has already shut down, and I am searching for ways to close the remaining ones,’ he added. In a response to the journalists’ question, he said that based on the current prices at which Indian traders are exporting yarn, the country’s spinning mills have a yarn stockpile worth about Tk12,000 crore. ‘We are becoming overly dependent on India for yarn,’ he added, saying that in the past, India has repeatedly suspended cotton, yarn, and even onion exports without any valid reason. As they have a history of engaging in such activities, this overdependence could pose serious risks in the future, he warned. He also urged the government to take an urgent decision within the next 72 hours to protect the country’s crisis-hit textile sector. Currently, there are more than 500 yarn-producing mills in the country, and these mills are being forced to sell yarn at prices below their production costs, worsening their financial losses, he added. Responding to another question, the BTMA president also urged the government to provide 10 per cent cash incentives for the local spinning millers, along with flexible access to the central bank’s Export Development Fund. A Matin Chowdhury, former president of the BTMA, said that government policy must support remaining competitive with rivals. ‘The governments of the competitor countries have been providing sufficient support to them,’ he added. The Indian government has been providing its textile millers with policy supports such as free cost of land registration, incentives for building establishment, factory set-up, wages, and Rodtep incentives, which have enabled them to sell yarn at dumping prices. Former BTMA president Mohammad Ali Khokon said that the textile sector supported the RMG industry even during the pandemic. ‘Due to a hike in labour cost by 67 per cent in the past years and a 650 per cent hike in gas and energy prices in the last 10 years, the sector is like in an ICU,’ he added. He urged the government to provide a two-year grace period on loan repayments for textile millers. Rajeev Haidar, vice president of the BTMA, said that the sector is under the attack of Indian economic aggression. ‘If we depend on Indian yarn, we might lose the opportunity of reducing the reciprocal tariff of the United States on the clause of US origin made raw materials,’ he added. Responding a question, BTMA president said that they have been on constant contact with the government, however, it yet to put any impact. Responding to another query, he said that, due to the ban on yarn imports through land ports, they have been able to determine the actual situation of yarn imports. Responding to journalists’ queries, Russell criticised the current government, saying that while it failed to create new factories, it presided over the closure of many.

title: BB buys $3.05b to stabilise forex market
body: Bangladesh Bank has stepped up purchases of US dollars from commercial banks to stabilise the foreign exchange market following a sharp rise in inward remittances this year. Executive director and spokesperson Arif Hossain Khan said on Sunday that the central bank acquired $110 million from three commercial banks through a Multiple Price Auction (MPA) at an exchange rate of Tk 122.30 per dollar. The central bank has acted to prevent significant fluctuations in the exchange rate as commercial banks face a surplus of dollars from the remittance boom. In December alone, Bangladesh Bank has purchased $920 million, bringing total purchases in the current fiscal year, FY2025-26, to $3.05 billion. Remittance flows by expatriate Bangladeshis have shown robust growth. Between December 1 and December 27, the country received $2.75 billion, up 14.03 percent from $1.98 billion during the same period last year. Looking at the broader fiscal year, from July 1 to December 20, Bangladesh received $15.79 billion in remittances, compared with $13.54 billion in the same period of FY2024-25, representing roughly 16.16 percent growth. In November alone, expatriates sent $2.89 billion. Central bank officials attribute the surge to several key factors, including strict anti-Hundi measures to curb illegal money transfers, effective implementation of remittance incentives and improved efficiency and accessibility of formal banking channels for migrants. The sustained inflow of foreign exchange has bolstered the country’s reserves to over $32 billion, providing relief to its overall economy.

title: Livelihood severely affected by cold wave in Barishal
body: Public life in Barishal district has been severely disrupted as a cold spell accompanied by wind chills continues to grip the region, causing immense hardship for low-income and working-class people. According to the district meteorological office, the lowest temperature recorded on Sunday was 13.4 degrees Celsius, while Saturday saw the season’s lowest temperature at 12.4 degrees Celsius. Despite a slight reduction in morning fog, residents said the intensity of the cold has increased due to persistent freezing winds and the absence of sunshine for most of the day. Locals reported wind chills have made the cold feel more severe than the actual temperature. Daily activities have slowed significantly, and fewer people are venturing out onto the streets. The situation has particularly affected day laborers, rickshaw pullers, and auto-rickshaw drivers, whose earnings have dropped sharply. Sohel, an auto-rickshaw driver from the city’s Notun Bazar area, said passenger numbers have declined over the past few days due to the cold, making it difficult to earn a living. Similarly, Liton, a rickshaw puller from Sadar road, said strong winds and extreme cold have made driving exhausting, while passengers are scarce. The sudden rise in cold intensity has also increased patient inflow at local hospitals. Children and elderly people are reportedly suffering from cold-related illnesses, putting additional pressure on healthcare services. Pranab Kumar Roy, an observer at the district meteorological office, said that the lowest temperature of the season was recorded at 12.4 degrees Celsius, with the day’s highest temperature reaching 25.5 degrees Celsius. He added that the sun remained hidden until around 12:30 pm on Saturday, while light fog covered the entire district during the morning hours. Meteorological officials forecasted that cold conditions may persist over the next few days, urging residents, especially vulnerable groups, to take necessary precautions.

title: Injured England quick Archer out of Ashes
body: England pace spearhead Jofra Archer was ruled out of the rest of the Ashes series Wednesday with a side strain while batsman Ollie Pope was axed for the fourth Test against Australia. Archer has arguably been England's best bowler over the first three Tests, sending down 80 overs and claiming nine wickets. He is replaced by Gus Atkinson, who leads the attack alongside Josh Tongue, Brydon Carse and skipper Ben Stokes, with Will Jacks retained as the spin option. It is a major setback for England who are 3-0 down in the series and desperate to restore pride at the Melbourne Cricket Ground starting Friday. They are already without quick Mark Wood who bowled just 11 overs for the tour before succumbing to a knee injury. The under-performing Pope paid for his poor form at number three, with Jacob Bethell taking over in the only other change. Opener Ben Duckett, who was purportedly shown drunk on an unverified video in between the second and third Tests, held his spot. England: Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, Jacob Bethell, Joe Root, Harry Brook, Ben Stokes, (capt), Jamie Smith, Will Jacks, Gus Atkinson, Brydon Carse, Josh Tongue

title: Aminul targets a clean and fair BPL
body: Bangladesh Cricket Board president Aminul Islam reiterated on Tuesday the organisation’s commitment of ensuring a clean and fair Bangladesh Premier League, which starts at the Sylhet International Stadium on December 26. ‘This is a completely new event for me. This is the 12th edition of the BPL. And before to this one, I didn’t have any role, because I wasn’t a coach or an official in any edition,’ said Aminul during a workshop for journalists co-hosted by the BCB and the Bangladesh Sports Press Association at the Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium. ‘I am learning every day to protect the game and to present good cricket. We are also learning from the various challenges we are facing,’ he added. He also mentioned two goals for the tournament. ‘One is to conduct a clean and systematic BPL. And another is that, as you know, we have the ICC T20 World Cup soon after the BPL. [We hope that] we can get the preparation for the format if not a direct preparation,’ Aminul said. The former national team captain also stated that they’re monitoring the security situations very closely. ‘Our job is to conduct the game, to organise it nicely. We have many stakeholders. We are obediently following the instructions of our law and security enforcement departments,’ he said. ‘We will work based on those instructions. But we are keeping a close eye on everything,’ he added. Aminul also reminded everyone that all have a role to play when he was asked about some mismanagement issues. ‘The BPL hasn’t started yet. Here, we’ve got some roles; the franchises have got some roles. We, the BPL governing council, are following ours. Now the franchises should follow theirs, and they’re instructed accordingly,’ Aminul added.

title: Kings, MSC fire blank
body: Defending champions Bashundhara Kings survived an injury-time scare to play out a goalless draw against 11-time champions Mohammedan Sporting Club in their Group B match of the Federation Cup at the Shaheed Dhirendranath Datta Stadium in Cumilla on Tuesday. Kings, who have already defeated Mohammedan this season by 4-1 and 2-0 goals in the Challenge Cup and in the Bangladesh Football League, have struggled to break Mohammedan’s defence in the day’s game. Kings could have got the lead in the final minute of the first half when their forward Rakib Hossain’s shot found the net if referee Nasir Uddin didn’t rule that out for off-side. Kings mounted pressure in the final 10 minutes and created three close chances, but Mohammedan goalkeeper Sujon Hossain kept his post intact on all of the occasions. The traditional Black and White outfits squandered their chance of winning the game when their Ghanaian forward Samuel Boateng failed to beat Kings goalkeeper Anisur Rahman Zico in a one-on-one situation in the fourth minute of the six-minute injury time in the match. Mohammedan, who started their group stage with a 3-2 win over Police Football Club, maintained second place in the five-team table with five points from three outings, while four-time champions Kings have two points from as many matches to remain fourth in the table.

title: Central Zone beat South to boost title hopes
body: An all-round bowling performance helped Central Zone to secure a six-run victory against South Zone in their fifth-round fixture of the ongoing Women’s Bangladesh Cricket League at the Rajshahi Divisional Stadium on Tuesday. Opting to bat first, Central posted 114-6 in the allotted overs. Despite setting a small total, the bowlers led by Sabekun Nahar (3-17) restricted South to 108-9, to keep them alive in the title race. Central, who are currently in second position with eight points, will play table-toppers North Zone, who also have same points with superior run rate, in their final fixture of the tournament, which will determine the winner. Apart from left-arm spinner Sabekun’s three-for, Fariha Trishna (2-13) and Jannatul Ferdous (2-30) each picked up two wickets for Central. Chasing the target, South found them in a precarious 5-4 at one stage. Farzana Haque and Lata Mondol tried to steady their innings with a 47-run partnership for the fifth-wicket but Central bowlers regained the momentum. Farzana scored 38 off 37 with three fours and Lata made 28 off 29, including three fours while skipper Rabeya Khan contributed 18 runs. Earlier, opener Ishma Tanjim (27) and Mst Eva (28) gave Central a good start with a 55-run partnership for the second wicket but South took control after a disciplined bowling effort. Rabeya claimed 3-12, but went into a losing cause.

title: Mahidul eyes nat’l team return with BPL
body: Noakhali Express wicketkeeper-batter Mahidul Islam was hopeful of performing well in the forthcoming Bangladesh Premier League that would help him to retain his place in the national team for the Twenty20 World Cup. Mahidul was controversially called up for the T20I series against Ireland, as captain Litton Das and the chairman of the selection panel, Gazi Ashraf Hossain, expressed conflicting views regarding the decision to drop Shamim Hossain, whom Mahidul replaced. However, Mahidul didn’t get the chance to make his T20I debut, whereas Shamim returned to the squad for the last match of the three-game series and featured. Mahidul said that he had good involvement with the team management during the series. ‘The involvement with the team management was good; we had very good preparation. But it might be due to the team combination that I couldn’t play a match,’ Mahidul told the reporters during a practice session of Noakhali at the Cricketers Academy in Purbachal, Dhaka, on Tuesday. But Mahidul isn't losing his hope and has stated that he’ll try to contribute in any position. ‘Every player wants to play good cricket and [get the opportunity] to play in the national team. Of course, I have got that goal of contributing in any position if I get the chance. I think if I can play good cricket, opportunities will come,’ said the 26-year-old. For now, he just wants to maintain his process, which has worked well for him in the past. He said, ‘If I can think of anything other than following the process, then pressure or something like that will come. So I try to be normal and keep performing well while maintaining the process.’ Mahidul also stated that he’d always had the hunger to play in the national team. ‘I always try to improve more. Sometimes, the performance may come; sometimes, it may not. But I will always have that hunger. I am trying to improve more,’ he said. After the Ireland series, Mahidul got picked up in Bangladesh ‘A’ team for the Rising Stars Asia Cup, where Bangladesh came second after losing to Pakistan in the final in the Super Over. But he had an underwhelming outing, as he managed only 36 runs from four innings. However, he wants to put that behind and look forward to the BPL. ‘Yes, I might not have performed well according to the expectations. But I am hopeful as well as confident that I can play good cricket [in the future], inshallah,’ he said. He’s also enjoying his time with the new franchise, Noakhali. ‘They’re doing fantastic given that they’ve come for the first time. So far, everything is organised. Hopefully they will be able to continue for many years. Noakhali has a good fan base, and hopefully they will do well in this BPL,’ he added.

title: Ex-Tennis Fed general secretary Jamali dies
body: Former Bangladesh Tennis Federation general secretary Masud Hasan Jamali passed away at a hospital in the capital’s Uttara area on Monday night. He was 91. He left behind his widow, only daughter, and a host of well-wishers to mourn his death. Jamali served as the general secretary of BTF for two terms – from January 15, 1986, to February 20, 1990, and from September 16, 1996, to March 11, 1998 – and contributed to the development of Bangladesh tennis. Jamali, a retired member of the Power Generation Board, was the father of the late Davis Cup and national champion Shovon Jamali. He was laid to rest at the Azimpur old graveyard after the namaz-e-janaza after Zohr prayers at the Uttara Jame Mosque on Tuesday. The BTF expressed its deep shock and sympathy regarding his passing in a message on Tuesday, extending condolences to his bereaved family.

title: Napoli beat Bologna to lift Italian Super Cup
body: Napoli won the Italian Super Cup on Monday as David Neres scored twice to secure the reigning Serie A champions a 2-0 win over Bologna in the final in Jeddah. Brazilian winger Neres curled in a brilliant shot from distance to give Napoli the lead before half-time against last season's Italian Cup winners. He struck again in the second half after intercepting a weak pass from Bologna goalkeeper Federico Ravaglia as he tried to play out from the back. Neres finished with three goals in the Super Cup after also scoring in the 2-0 semi-final win over AC Milan last week. It is the third time Napoli have won the competition, after 1990 and 2014. ‘The lads deserve congratulations,’ Napoli coach Antonio Conte told Sport Mediaset. ‘They showed how much they wanted this trophy for the fans, and we'll also have a great Christmas celebration now with a new trophy in the cabinet.’ Traditionally featuring the Serie A and Italian Cup champions, since 2023 the Italian Super Cup has also included the runners-up from league and cup. The four-team tournament is contracted to be held in Saudi Arabia until 2029. Napoli, who trail Serie A leaders Inter Milan by two points, return to league action on Sunday away to Cremonese. Bologna are at home to Sassuolo.

title: Cummins out of rest of Ashes, Lyon to have surgery
body: Australia skipper Pat Cummins and Nathan Lyon were on Tuesday ruled out of the final two Ashes Tests against England with the veteran spinner facing surgery and an extended period on the sidelines. Quick bowler Jhye Richardson and spinner Todd Murphy were named as cover in a 15-man squad for the fourth Test starting on Friday at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Australia have already retained the famous urn with eight-wicket wins in Perth and Brisbane and an 82-run victory in Adelaide. Cummins ‘won't play any part in the rest of the series’, coach Andrew McDonald told cricket.com.au. He returned from a lower back injury to lead Australia to victory in Adelaide in his first Test since July, taking six wickets in the match. ‘That was a discussion that we had a long time out around his return. Yeah, we were taking on some risk. We've now won the series, and that was the goal,’ said McDonald. Cummins will now target full fitness for the month-long Twenty20 World Cup in India and Sri Lanka, starting in early February. ‘To position him for further risk and jeopardise him long term is not something that we want to do,’ said McDonald. ‘Pat's really comfortable with that. If he had any setback in the build-in as well, we would have shut him down straight away.’ Steve Smith, who captained the team in Cummins' absence during the first two Tests, will lead the side again in Melbourne after missing Adelaide with vertigo symptoms. His return means there will be at least three changes. Usman Khawaja replaced Smith at four in Adelaide scoring 82 and 40 and should he be retained then Josh Inglis is shaping as the fall guy. Lyon, 38, damaged his right hamstring saving a boundary on day five in Adelaide fielding and hobbled off. He claimed his 564th wicket in the match to move clear of fellow Australian great Glenn McGrath and into sixth on the all-time Test bowling list. ‘Nathan Lyon will have surgery on a torn right hamstring which will sideline him for an extended period,’ Cricket Australia said. Lyon's replacement, Murphy, is in line to play his first home Test. His seven previous appearances for Australia all came overseas. His last was in Sri Lanka earlier this year. Richardson was included after a four-year Test absence, during which he underwent three shoulder surgeries. Scott Boland and Mitchell Starc are likely to lead the seam attack after recovering well from Adelaide, with Michael Neser, Brendan Doggett and Richardson battling to join them. McDonald paid tribute to 35-year-old Starc, who has sent down close to 100 overs in the series so far and remains in good shape. ‘Starc's amazing. He's pulled up fine,’ McDonald said of the leading bowler in the series. Starc has taken 22 wickets in the three Ashes Tests so far at an average of 17.04, including a career best innings return of 7-58 in Perth. He has also contributed 150 valuable runs with the bat down the order. ‘He keeps running in and presenting the pace that he does,’ said McDonald. ‘There's a lot to be learned around preparing yourself and targeting the right matches at the right time.’ Squad: Steve Smith (capt), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Brendan Doggett, Cameron Green, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Usman Khawaja, Marnus Labuschagne, Todd Murphy, Michael Neser, Jhye Richardson, Mitchell Starc, Jake Weatherald, Beau Webster

title: Salah, Foster take Egypt and South Africa to AFCON Group B summit
body: Premier League pair Mohamed Salah and Lyle Foster were match-winners as Egypt and South Africa began their Africa Cup of Nations Group B campaigns with victories in Morocco on Monday. Unsettled Liverpool star Salah struck in the first minute of added time to snatch a 2-1 win for record seven-time champions Egypt over gallant Zimbabwe in Agadir. Earlier, second-half dominance by one-time title-holders South Africa paid off when Burnley striker Foster netted on 79 minutes to deliver a 2-1 victory over Angola in Marrakesh. The stage is now set for a top-of-the-table showdown between the Pharaohs and Bafana Bafana in Agadir on Friday. They have met three times in AFCON tournaments, with Egypt winning twice. Salah, whose unhappiness at being a substitute recently at Liverpool led to an outburst against manager Arne Slot, worked tirelessly for an Egyptian team rattled at falling behind. Prince Dube scored on 20 minutes and one of the title favourites had to wait until the 63rd minute for Omar Marmoush from Manchester City to equalise. Relentless pressure from the Pharaohs paid off in the first of five additional minutes when the perseverance of Salah grabbed them all three points. Earlier, South Africa dominated the second half against Angola in Marrakesh and Foster scored in 79 minutes to deliver a 2-1 victory in the same mini-league. The winner came after Tshepang Moremi had a goal ruled offside and Mbekezeli Mbokazi rattled the crossbar with a shot that rebounded into play. Oswin Appollis put 2024 AFCON bronze medallists South Africa ahead on 21 minutes and, as Angola took control, they levelled through Show after 35 minutes. Victory ended a six-match winless run in their opening AFCON match since 2006 by South Africa. The win also confirmed their dominance over Angola with three victories and two draw in five AFCON meetings. Belgian coach Hugo Broos, who guided Cameroon to the AFCON tilte in 2017, admitted he was unhappy with the first-half Bafana performance. ‘We had to avoid losing tonight because next up for us are Egypt. We led in the opening half and then we fell asleep,’ said Broos. ‘We let Angola back into the game so we put something right during half-time. In the second half we applied more pressure, there is more movement and we had chances. ‘Tshepang (Moremi) was wonderful when he came on, suddenly there was speed in our team, we were dangerous. He was a threat and he did it very well in the second 45 minutes.’ Mali coach Tom Saintfiet admitted that conceding a late equaliser in a 1-1 Group A draw with Zambia in Casablanca was ‘very painful’. After El Bilal Toure had a first-half penalty saved by Willard Mwanza, Mali took the lead on 61 minutes through Lassina Sinayoko. But as two Mali defenders stood still when the ball was crossed two minutes into added time, Patson Daka pushed forward to head the equaliser. ‘We were aiming to score three goals in this match. Our difficulties began after the missed penalty. We let our emotions take over,’ said Belgian Saintfiet. ‘Obviously, I would have preferred to take all three points against Zambia, especially after controlling the game. ‘The equaliser felt like a victory for Zambia and a defeat for Mali. Now we have to prepare properly for the next matches, starting against Morocco on Friday. ‘Zambia have good players in midfield, and they prevented us from achieving our objectives. Now we will need at least a point against the Moroccans.’ ‘We have to finish at least second in the group. We said we want to reach the final, and that is still possible,’ added the coach who took debutants Gambia to the 2022 quarter-finals. Hosts Morocco, who opened the tournament on Sunday with a 2-0 win over Comoros, have three points and Mali and Zambia one each. There are four matches on Tuesday, including 2024 runners-up Nigeria against Tanzania in Fes and 2022 champions Senegal against Botswana in Tangier.

title: England to probe 'stag-do' drinking on Ashes beach break
body: England managing director Rob Key pledged Tuesday to investigate whether players' drinking on a mid-Ashes beach break went too far, after reports said it had been like a ‘stag-do.’ The England team headed to Queensland tourist playground Noosa after heavily losing the first two Tests in Perth and Brisbane. They spent several days on the sand and around restaurants and bars, followed by TV crews, photographers and reporters before travelling to Adelaide where they lost the third Test and the Ashes. Britain's Daily Telegraph reported that ‘after drowning their sorrows after the Brisbane Test, it is no exaggeration to say some, certainly not all, players drank for five or six days’. It added that players ‘did nothing outrageous in Noosa’ but there was concern over the level of drinking, with England's professionalism already under question after their limited preparations. ‘If there's things where people are saying that our players went out and drank excessively, then of course we'll be looking into that,’ Key told English media in Melbourne ahead of the Boxing Day Test. ‘Drinking excessive amounts of alcohol for an international cricket team is not something that I'd expect to see at any stage. ‘It would be a fault not to look into what happened there,’ added Key, who did not travel with the team to Noosa. ‘From everything that I've heard so far, they actually were pretty well behaved. Very well behaved.’ He admitted that he did not mind players having the occasional drink, but ‘if it goes past that, then that's an issue as far as I'm concerned. ‘I have no issue with the Noosa trip if it was to get away and just throw your phone away, down tools, go on the beach, all of that stuff. ‘If it goes into where they're drinking lots and it's a stag-do, all of that type of stuff, that's completely unacceptable.’ Key also revealed he had previously looked into reports that players had been spotted drinking the night before a limited-overs match in New Zealand, just before the Ashes tour. ‘I didn't feel like that was worthy of formal warnings, but it was probably worthy of informal ones,’ he said. Key backed head coach Brendon McCullum, despite the Ashes being lost inside 11 playing days, the joint fastest defeat for more than 100 years. The fate of both McCullum and Key rests with the England and Wales Cricket Board. ‘Clearly, we've mucked up on the big occasions, whether that was the home Ashes series, whether that was last summer against India,’ he said of a home series that was drawn 2-2 when England threw away a position to win. ‘The big ones have eluded us ... we have to evolve. We have to make sure that we're doing things better.’

title: Neymar undergoes surgery for meniscus injury
body: Neymar has undergone a successful operation on his left knee to repair a damaged meniscus, his club Santos said on Monday. The 33-year-old endured a difficult season with Santos as he played through the injury to help the club avoid relegation from Brazil's top flight. Brazil's national team doctor performed the arthroscopic surgery, having previously operated on Neymar for a foot fracture as well as the ruptured anterior cruciate ligament he suffered against Uruguay in October 2023. Neymar is expected to require a recovery period of around a month. His Santos contract expires at the end of the year but he is in talks with the club over a new deal. The former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain forward has not played for Brazil in over two years but is hoping to be fit and figure in coach Carlo Ancelotti's plans for the 2026 World Cup. Neymar is Brazil's record goalscorer with 79 goals from 128 matches.

title: Isak faces two months out after 'reckless' tackle: Slot
body: Alexander Isak is expected to be out of action for two months after fracturing his leg against Tottenham, with Liverpool manager Arne Slot accusing Tottenham's Micky van de Ven of making a ‘reckless challenge’. The Sweden striker was injured in a tackle from the defender in the act of scoring the opening goal in Saturday's 2-1 victory and limped off the pitch. Liverpool said in a statement on Monday that the forward had had an operation on an ankle injury that included a fibula fracture. ‘It's going to be a long injury, for a couple of months,’ Slot told reporters on Tuesday, ‘So, yeah, that's a big, big, big disappointment for him. And as a result also of course for us.’ Slot described Van de Ven's tackle as ‘reckless’. ‘I think I said a lot about the tackle of Xavi Simons (sent off earlier in the game for Spurs), which for me was completely unintentional, and I don't think you will ever get an injury out of a tackle like that. ‘The tackle of Van de Ven, if you make that tackle 10 times, I think 10 times there's a serious chance that a player gets a serious injury.’ Isak's injury is the latest setback for the forward after he signed from Newcastle for a British record £125 million ($168 million) in September. A dispute with Newcastle meant he did not have a proper pre-season programme and arrived at Liverpool well behind his team-mates in terms of fitness. His season was then interrupted by a groin injury. The 26-year-old has scored just three goals in 16 appearances since completing his protracted move to Anfield. Isak's absence will be a major blow for Reds boss Slot, with Mohamed Salah at the Africa Cup of Nations and Cody Gakpo not ready to return from a muscle injury until early in the new year. It leaves Slot with Hugo Ekitike, who has five goals in his past four games, and the little-used Federico Chiesa as his only senior forwards. Liverpool, whose Premier League title defence collapsed after a shocking run of results, have climbed to fifth in the table after extending their unbeaten league run to five games. Isak's injury raises the prospect of Liverpool moving to boost their attack in the January transfer window, with Bournemouth winger Antoine Semenyo linked with a move to Anfield. It may also change the conversation around Salah, who had been linked with a move to Saudi Arabia following his recent claim that he had been thrown under the bus by the club and no longer had a relationship with Slot. Salah's rant, which came after he was left on the bench for three successive matches, prompted Liverpool to leave him out of the squad for a Champions League match at Inter Milan. But he returned to action as a substitute against Brighton before leaving for international duty. Liverpool host bottom side Wolves on Saturday.

title: Bangladesh ethnosports team shines bright in Turkey
body: The Bangladesh Ethnosport team secured third place at the Togyzqumalaq and Mangala Asian Cup 2025, held in Ankara, Turkey, from December to 22, says a press release. The medal was won by Bangladeshi player Md Rezaul Karim Molla, marking a commendable achievement for Bangladesh on the Asian ethnosports stage. The tournament brought together elite ethnosport athletes from Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Russia, Mongolia, and host nation Türkiye, alongside Bangladesh. The wide participation and high level of competition underscored the tournament’s importance within the Asian ethnosports calendar. The championship opened in a dignified atmosphere, attended by senior officials, including Levent Kılıç, Governor of Ankara’s Sincan District, and Murat Era, Mayor of Sincan Municipality. Their presence underscored Türkiye’s commitment to promoting ethnosports and strengthening international cultural ties through ethnosports. The award ceremony was attended by several distinguished personalities from the global ethnosports community. Among them were Levent Kılıç, governor of the Ankara’s Sincan District; Alican KILIÇ, director of the Sincan District National Education of Ankara; Muhammad Shahanoor Alam, counsellor and deputy chief of mission, Bangladesh Embassy in Ankara, Turkey; Zeynep Safiye Baki NALCIOĞLU, vice president of the Turkish Traditional Sports Federation; Md. Al Mamun, vice president of the World Togyzqumalaq Federation and president of the International Ethnosport Bangladesh Association and others. The guests formally presented awards to the winning athletes. Bangladesh was represented by a three-member delegation, led by Md Al Mamun, president of the International Ethnosport Bangladesh Association. The delegation also included Salahuddin Chowdhury and medal winner Md Rezaul Karim Molla.

title: BPL is big preparation for T20 World Cup: Fahim
body: The Bangladesh Premier League will serve as good preparation for the national team players ahead of the forthcoming T20 World Cup, said the chairman of the cricket operations of the Bangladesh Cricket Board, Nazmul Abedeen Fahim, on Monday. The BPL will run between December 26 and January 23, while Bangladesh begin their T20 World Cup on February 7. Following the BPL, the Tigers will play two warm-up games before the main event in Bengaluru. Fahim said that the players from the teams failing to reach the top four of the BPL will begin training for the World Cup early. ‘BPL itself is a big preparation,’ Fahim told the reporters after the final of the Rangpur Riders-Bangladesh Sports Journalist Association Cricket Tournament at the Maulana Bhasani Hockey Stadium in Dhaka on Monday. ‘All the players will be in the BPL. And there will be little time in our hands. Most probably the players of the team failing to reach the top four will be freed by January 20. So the training will begin eventually as the coaches will come,’ he added. Fahim also informed that the wickets in the BPL will be batting friendly. ‘Wherever it is played, the wickets are batting friendly in the T20 World Cup. If there was no upcoming World Cup, we’d still want to make the wickets [in the BPL] batting friendly, where there’d be an opportunity to score 180-200 runs. ‘Whether they’ll be able to do that or not, that’s a different issue. But definitely we will try,’ he added. Fahim also hopes that the national team will do well in familiar conditions in India. ‘The condition won’t be too unfamiliar for us. We can predict the condition. That’s a positive for us,’ he said. ‘The first target will be to go into the next round. I am very much hopeful about that. And then the rest will depend on how we are able to adjust and what our mentality will be. ‘We have match winners now, and the number of skilful players has increased. If they are in form and carry the momentum, we can be hopeful enough,’ he said.

title: Chop and change in every hour to BPL plans
body: The Bangladesh Cricket Board is facing the challenge of frequent ‘chop and change’ to the plans of the forthcoming Bangladesh Premier League on an hourly basis, stated the member secretary of the governing council of the league, Iftekhar Rahman, on Monday. Just a couple of days after scrapping the opening ceremony altogether, the BCB announced the change in the schedule of the matches on the opening day ‘to accommodate pre-event inauguration ceremonies’. Iftekhar said that they’d arrange a small opening ceremony on December 26, the first day of the forthcoming edition, at the Sylhet International Stadium. ‘As we all know, the situation is a bit challenging,’ Iftekhar said after the final of the Rangpur Riders-Bangladesh Sports Journalist Association Cricket Tournament at the Maunala Bhasani Hockey Stadium in Dhaka on Monday. ‘We are forced to chop and change our plans every hour. As we are not able to hold the opening ceremony on December 24, we will hold it on the first day in a limited capacity. As the national team departs by the end of January [to play the T20 World Cup], the fixture cannot be changed,’ he said. The first match has been pushed by one hour, while the second match of the first day has been pushed by 45 minutes to accommodate the ceremony. ‘[The first part of the programme will begin at 2:15pm. The president and the sports secretary will shake hands with the players, and a one-minute silence will be observed for the recent event. And then a concert will be held in between the two matches,’ said Iftekhar. Iftekhar also reiterated the ‘zero tolerance’ policy for integrity while mentioning that the BCB were set to sign an MoU with the Criminal Investigation Department of the Bangladesh Police. He mentioned that the CID would monitor the situations. ‘We are doing this to prevent any incident. The thief will come, but he should be stopped before committing any crime. So that’s the process we are following, like the rest of the world,’ he said.
