title: Activities in Shilpakala to resume from Dec 21
body: Following the state mourning on the death of Sharif Osman Bin Hadi, all activities, including programmes and exhibitions, at the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy will resume from December 21. Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy confirmed it in a press release on Saturday. Chief adviser Muhammad Yunus announced the state mourning on December 20 in an address to the nation, it added. Considering the situation, all activities at the academy were suspended from December 19 until further notice. The academy clarified that claiming an indefinite closure of its all activities in some online and social media reports were unexpected and regrettable.

title: Playwright Mukid Chy gets CUKC Award
body: Playwright Mukid Chowdhury has been honoured with the Cumilla Kabi Parishad Literary Award 2025 for his special contribution to stage theatre. The award was announced by CUKC founder president R Mujib and president Abdul Latif on December 18. The literary award along with a monetary honorarium will be presented at a ceremony to be held in Dhaka on December 26. Mukid Chowdhury said, ‘Stage theatre attracts me deeply. Personally, I feel a strong affinity for the new-stream Bangla Movement Theatre art form. Essentially, this art form aims to easily involve those who have never performed on stage in theatrical presentation.’ Mukid Chowdhury is the youngest son of fiction writer Abdur Rauf Chowdhury and Shirin Chowdhury. He is a versatile personality — scientist, novelist, essayist, playwright, and poet — and has made significant contributions across almost every field of Bengali literature. His notable creative works include the following play-novels and plays: Ashtambasu- Dyu: Joddha; Atoi Falgun; Ashokananda; Karnapuran; Gomatir Upakhyan; Champabati; Phulbou; Joler Bhitor Joler Bisorjon; Aprakritik Prakriti; Ghalib Kiba Asad; Kolkatay Mirza Ghalib; Kobikothon; Apurnotar Paripurnota; Panchapuran; Panchabed; among others. His short story collections include Trishito Tithi; Tirer Brikkhoraji; Kosturi Gondho; Khut. His poetry collections include Anahuto Otithi; Bisher Bindu; Kabya Sangraha 1; Raja Gaur Gobinda; Gangariddhir Naribrindo. His research works include Italy: Adyanto Itihash; Germany: Otit Theke Bartoman; German Shahitto: Prarombho Theke Adhuna; England: Songkhipto Itihash; French Biplab (1789–1799); Napoleon Bonaparte; Shorup Onneshone; Prithibi; Nritya, among others.

title: ‘Nuremberg: Time of Truth’ screened at Russian House
body: The Russian House in Dhaka has recently organised a special screening of the documentary film titled Nuremberg: Time of Truth. Produced by RT Documentary, students, educators and all those interested in history attended the event, said a press release. The film is dedicated to the historic Nuremberg Trials of 1945-1946, where the leaders of Nazi Germany stood before an international court. The film details how the allies, and especially the Soviet Union, ensured a judicial proceeding based on documentary evidence to deliver justice, rather than mere revenge.

title: Bhumi Gallery at Uttara Centrepoint targets new audiences
body: The Bhumi Gallery inaugurated their Uttara Centrepoint branch with a group art exhibition aimed to connect new audiences. The group art exhibition titled ‘Resilient Becoming’ features more than a hundred contemporary artists’ artworks with master artists of Bangladesh including Zainul Abedin, SM Sultan, Qayyum Chowdhury, Abu Taher, Abdur Razzak and Qamrul Hasan. The exhibition, which was inaugurated on November 21, displayed more than 200 artworks in diverse media, including sculptures, prints, drawings and paintings by seasoned and young artists. Seasoned artists, including Monirul Islam, Shahabuddin Ahmed, Abdus Shakoor Shah, Biren Shome, Abdul Mannan, Farida Zaman and Mohammad Eunus, displayed their artworks with young artists, including Md Rasel Rana, Banani Simlai, Arif Bachchu, Shakirun Nahar Kanon and Nabaraj Roy. The gallery, set in a large space at Centrepoint adjacent to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Uttara, also comprises an extended lobby for visitors. Founder and chief executive officer of Bhumi Gallery, Saifur Rahman Lenin, said that the Centrepoint branch is not just the beginning of a new space, but the beginning of a renewed vision which will strengthen the cultural fabric of the society. The gallery attracts a large audience who visit the venue for shopping and cinemas. ‘The most of the gallery spaces are located in specialised areas where only related people visit the exhibition, but the Centrepoint is a shopping centre with a Cineplex that gathers a large number of new visitors for the gallery,’ said Saifur Rahman Lenin, adding that the place is costly for an art gallery but he hoped that with the support of artists, art lovers and art collectors, the gallery may survive. The exhibition will end on December 31.

title: Bangla Academy announces eight awards for 2025
body: Bangla Academy has announced the recipients of eight awards for 2025, recognising contributions to literature, research, science, theatre and translation. The awards will be formally presented at the 48th annual general meeting of the Bangla Academy, scheduled to be held on December 27, according to a press release. Professor Mansur Musa has been selected for the Mohammad Barkatullah Essay Literature Award 2025 for his evaluation-based contributions to language-focused research. The award carries a cash prize of Tk 1 lakh. The Meher Kabir Science Literature Award 2025 has been awarded to Khosru Chowdhury in recognition of his overall contribution to the study and practice of nature and science. The prize money is Tk 1 lakh. Poet Sanaul Haque Khan has received the Mazharul Islam Poetry Award 2025 for his overall contribution to Bangla poetry. The award includes a cash prize of Tk 1 lakh. Hafiz Rashid Khan has been honoured with the Sadat Ali Akhand Literature Award 2025 for his research on the life and literature of various national minority communities. The award carries Tk 1 lakh in prize money. Actor, theatre director and organiser Tariq Anam Khan has been awarded the Professor Momtazuddin Ahmed Theatre Award 2025 for his lifelong contribution to acting, theatre direction and organisational activities. The prize money is Tk 1 lakh. The Abu Rushd Literature Award 2025 has been conferred on Shibbrata Barman for his contribution to translation literature. The award includes a cash prize of Tk 1 lakh. Under the Halima-Sharafuddin Science Award 2025, Safiq Islam has been honoured for his book Ganiter Rajye Anandabhramon for presenting mathematics in an easy and enjoyable manner. The award carries a cash prize of Tk 50,000. The Rabeya Khatun Fiction Award 2025 has been given in two categories. Writer Subrata Barua has been honoured for his overall contribution to fiction and will receive Tk 2 lakh. In the under-49 category, Anisur Rahman has been awarded for his short story collection Sisyphus Srom, published in 2024, and will receive Tk 1 lakh.

title: Preservation of Ritwik Ghatak’s ancestral house demanded
body: Citizens of Rajshahi on Thursday formed a human chain demanding the preservation of the ancestral homestead of internationally acclaimed Bengali filmmaker Ritwik Kumar Ghatak, alleging that the historic site was unlawfully demolished and its remnants removed. The protesters also submitted memorandum to the chief adviser and the Rajshahi deputy commissioner, pressing for immediate intervention. The human chain was organised at Saheb Bazar Zero Point at about 11:00am, with participation from cultural activists, film society members, youth leaders and representatives of civil society. Addressing the programme, speakers strongly condemned the destruction of Ghatak’s ancestral residence at the Miyapara area of Rajshahi city and demanded exemplary punishment of those responsible following a proper investigation. Ahsan Kabir Liton, president of the Ritwik Ghatak Film Society, said that Ritwik Ghatak was among the most influential filmmakers in Bengali cinema, whose works are internationally recognised and taught as academic texts in universities across the world. He alleged that after the demolition of the filmmaker’s ancestral homestead following August 5, the district administration had assured cultural activists that the site would remain untouched. ‘However, on December 16, the authorities of Rajshahi Homoeopathic Medical College and Hospital attempted to erase the remaining traces of the homestead by removing historic bricks from the site,’ he alleged. Film society executive member Atikur Rahman alleged that the bricks removed from the site were dumped near Kharakhari bypass, adjacent to Shah Makhdum Nursing College, to fill a pond – an act he described as both heritage destruction and environmental damage. The participants urged the government to declare the remaining 0.1603 acres of land as protected property and allocate it for the establishment of a Ritwik Ghatak Film Centre. They also demanded a review and cancellation of the lease granted to the homoeopathic college during the Ershad regime, construction of a boundary wall around the site, and installation of a signboard declaring it the proposed site of a ‘Ritwik Complex’. The protesters further proposed the construction of a multi-storey Ritwik Complex centred on the filmmaker’s legacy, incorporating a film institute, archive, museum, studios, seminar halls, cineplex, exhibition galleries, laboratories, a library, and accommodation facilities for cultural workers and filmmakers. Ritwik Ghatak Film Society general secretary Mahmud Hossain, Jatiya Adivasi Parishad central committee organising secretary Subash Chandra Hembram, Bangladesh Chhatra Federation Rajshahi city unit general secretary Nadim Sina, Adivasi Juba Parishad president Upen Rabidas, cultural activist Ishita Yasmin, and student leader Tahmid Zakir spoke at the programme among others.

title: Dhaka Theatre premieres Rangmohal
body: Renowned theatre troupe Dhaka Theatre premiered their 54th production titled Rangmohal at the Bangladesh Mahila Samity on Thursday. The play written by Rubayet Ahmed and directed by Faruque Ahmed depicted the tragedy of a blind couple after receiving their eyesight. The play is set in a village of Mymensingh Division, where a blind couple Rajab and Khushbu lived happily by singing and begging. A mystical spiritual master who is famous for solving problems including physical diseases and difficulties fulfill their desires and give their eye-sight and one wish. As Rajab lived at Khushbu’s house and knew her as a beautiful woman, when he received eye-sight, he discovered that Khushbu wass not beautiful as he expected. He left her house and became a rich person by using the power of the mystical master. Rejected from her husband, Khushbu wished and became blindn again and lived in her house alone. Rajab fell in in love with a Jatra-artiste Mousumi who refused his marriage proposal. As he went back to Khushbu, she refused him. For that, Rajab inflicted blindness upon himself again. The stage of the production was designed by Shakil Siddhartha while Wasim Ahmed designed the light and Nasrin Nahar designed the costume for the play. Nasrin Nahar, Anik Islam, Farzana Chumki, Nayar Sultana, Mostofa Ratan, Irine Sultana and others performed in the play.

title: Azwad’s first solo exhibition opens at Gallery Chitrak
body: The first solo art exhibition by emerging artist Azwad Ahmed, titled ‘The Luminous Shade of Solitude,’ was inaugurated at Gallery Chitrak in Dhaka on Thursday. Curated by Professor Nisar Hossain, the exhibition presents a thoughtful selection of Ahmed’s recent works, exploring themes of silence, introspection, and emotional restraint. The opening ceremony was attended by a distinguished audience comprising artists, critics, academics, and art enthusiasts. Renowned artist Professor Emeritus Rafiqun Nabi graced the occasion as chief guest, while eminent artists Professor Mohammed Eunus and Javed Jalil were present as special guests. Professor Nisar Hossain was the curator of the exhibition. The event was presided over by noted art critic Professor Moinuddin Khaled, who reflected on the exhibition’s contemplative nature and its significance within contemporary visual discourse. Guests speaking at the inauguration highlighted Azwad Ahmed’s subtle yet evocative visual language, observing that his restrained expressions evoke deep emotional and intellectual resonance. The artworks invite quiet contemplation, drawing viewers into a reflective space where meaning emerges through attentive observation rather than overt narration. ‘The Luminous Shade of Solitude’ will remain open to the public up to December 24 daily from 11:00am to 8:00pm.

title: Photography exhibition sheds light on Manipuri community
body: A nine-day group photography exhibition titled Manipuri, which sheds light on the Manipuri community of Bangladesh, is under way at the Bishwo Shahitto Kendro Art Gallery of Banglamotor in the capital. Curated by KM Jahangir Alam, the exhibition was inaugurated on December 12 with the presence of cultural activist Shankar Shaojal, photographers Nafis Ahmed Nadvi and Hasan Saifuddin Chandan. Photographers Mohd Ashabul Haque Nannu, Mohammed Harun Ar Rashid and Md Kawsar Habib are alumni or former students of the Alor School Photography Course of Bishwo Shahitto Kendro, a year-long mentorship programme introduced by organiser Mesbah Uddin Ahmed Sumon. They began fieldwork on 22 October 2023 and the exhibition is part of a long-term documentary project mentored by KM Jahangir Alam. The exhibition displayed the nature, family relationships, contemporary cultural practices, religious beliefs, rituals, traditions, agriculture and the hand-loom system, the borders of the two countries, and life and death of the Manipuri community through 102 photographs. A photograph of Mohd Ashabul Haque Nannu shows a Manipuri mother carrying her son on her back while another photograph of Mohammed Harun Ar Rashid shows a baby boy prepared for Rakhal Raas, a traditional Manipuri folk performance depicting Lord Krishna’s playful childhood and Md Kawsar Habib portrayed the only Muslim national minority life in Bangladesh. The Manipuri community has lived in Bangladesh for more than two and a half centuries, adapting harmoniously to the region’s climate and landscape. The community consists of three groups: Maitai, Bishnupriya and Pangal. While their cultural foundations are similar, linguistic differences exist. The Bishnupriyas speak a language of the Indo-Aryan family, whereas the Maitai and Pangal communities use languages of the Tibeto-Burman branch. Mohammed Harun Ar Rashid said that they have planned to organise another exhibition at Moulvibazar in future. The exhibition will end on Saturday.

title: ‘Ghore Phera’ narrates horrific torture during War of Independence
body: Bangladeshi theatre troupe Mad Theatre’s fourth production, titled ‘Ghore Phera’, narrates horrific tortures, mostly against women, during the country’s War of Independence in 1971. The monodrama, performed by actress Sonia Hassan, is based on fiction writer Mojaffor Hossain’s story titled Paradhin Desher Shadhin Manushera. The play, written and directed by Asadul Islam, was staged on Tuesday at the ongoing Bijoy Boimela at the Bangla Academy in the capital. The play revolves around a woman’s struggle for survival during the War of Independence. Sonia Hassan portrays the character of a woman who lost her husband and child during the war. She also lost her tongue when she attempted to prevent rape in the torture cell. The torturers - the Pakistani occupation army and their collaborators - cut her tongue and belly. The play narrates her return journey from a camp to home, which was also burnt by the Pakistani marauding army. She also narrates what she witnessed on her return journey. The light was designed by Ashraful Islam and the background music of the play was also designed by the writer and director Asadul Islam. Ghore Phera premiered at the Parichay Utshab at Anulia Mahamaya Vidyamandir in the Indian state of West Bengal in March 2024.

title: Cultural organisations celebrate Victory Day
body: Different cultural organisations celebrated the 55th Victory Day through staging different programmes on Tuesday. Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy, Liberation War Museum, Chhayanaut along with BRAC University, Ganatantrik Sanskritik Oikya, Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi and others paid tribute to the freedom fighters and martyrs of the War of Independence organising cultural events at different venues. Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy hosts Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra’s songs at its 64 branches with a central concert at Suhrawardy Udyan in the capital. Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy Repertory Jatradal also staged their new production titled General Osmani at its experimental theatre hall directed by Tanvir Nahid Khan. Ganatantrik Sanskritik Oikya brought out a mass parade from the National Press Club to Shikha Chirantan at Suhrawardy Udyan protesting at the interim government’s decision to cancel the Victory Day parade to celebrate the day. Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi with Bangladesh Students Union and Bangladesh Juba Union organised a flag procession from the Institution of Engineers to the Central Shaheed Minar. Chhayanaut organised Bijoy Utsab on Abahani playground at Dhanmondi while the Liberation War Museum organised a cultural event for children at their venue. Chhayanaut along with BRAC University Cultural Club organised Bijoy Utsab on BRAC University campus. Dhaka University Photographic Society organised a photography exhibition depicting War of Independence and refugee camps of India in 1971.

title: Ekushey Book Fair 2026 begins Feb 20
body: The Bangla Academy on Wednesday announced that the Amar Ekushey Book Fair 2026 would begin on February 20 next year. According to a press release issued by the Bangla Academy, the decision was made at an emergency meeting held at its Shaheed Munier Choudhury Conference Room on the day. Cultural affairs secretary Md Mafidur Rahman, Dhaka University proctor Saifuddin Ahmed and Shahbagh police station inspector Md Asaduzzaman attended the meeting along with representatives of publishers and officials of the Bangla Academy. Bangla Academy director general Mohammad Azam chaired the meeting. The fair is scheduled to be inaugurated on February 20 morning and this edition of the fair will end on March 15. Earlier, on September 28, the Bangla Academy postponed the Amar Ekushey Book Fair 2026, which was scheduled to be held between December 17, 2025, and January 17, 2026, due to the national election scheduled for February 12, 2026. On September 21, the committee of the advisory council on law and order at a meeting decided to request the cultural affairs ministry to organise the book fair after the national election due to security concerns ahead of the polls. Consequently, the Bangla Academy postponed the fair. The month-long book fair usually begins on February 1 every year.

title: Rakter Dalil explores documents of 1971 War of Independence
body: A four-day programme titled ‘Rakter Dalil’, organised by the Dhaka University unit of the Bangladesh Students’ Union on the university campus to mark Victory Day and Martyred Intellectuals Day, explored the national and international documents of War of Independence 1971. The event that began on December 13 on the Teacher and Student Centre of the university campus ended on December 16. The organisers exhibited news and photographs published on international newspapers and a local newspaper, the Daily Sangram, during the war. They also screened films and held a discussion on genocide during the nine-month War of Independence. Bangladesh Students’ Union’s DU unit president Meghmallar Basu said that the event aimed to create an intellectual and social resistance against all attempts to reduce the importance of the War of Independence. The previous ruling parties made the War of Independence a political capital while the interim government neglected the history and elements of the nine-month struggle for the country’s independence, he alleged. He alleged that the interim government had released the identified war criminals and said that the Students’ Union’s event would clarify the false statements of Jamaat-e-Islami leaders against the history of the war.

title: Bangladeshi content creator RobinRafan joins Creators Guild of America
body: Bangladeshi content creator RobinRafan has officially been approved as a member of the Creators Guild of America (CGA), one of the world’s leading organisations dedicated to supporting and empowering digital creators, said a press release. The Creators Guild of America is a nonprofit organisation that represents and protects creators across digital platforms, from filmmakers and educators to influencers and designers. RobinRafan has become Bangladesh’s first representative within this influential organisation, the press release added. Speaking about the recognition, RobinRafan said, ‘Alhamdulillah. Being approved as a member of the Creators Guild of America is a huge honour for me as a content creator. I hope this recognition will inspire more creators from Bangladesh to dream bigger and reach the global platform.’ He shared that the membership, earned after a rigorous evaluation process, will strengthen his creative journey by providing global exposure, legal protection for his work, and new opportunities for international collaboration.

title: Cultural organisations observe Martyred Intellectuals Day
body: Various cultural organisations observed Martyred Intellectuals Day organising special programmes on Sunday. Bangla Academy, Liberation War Museum, Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi and others paid tribute to martyred intellectuals by organising diverse events. Bangla Academy placed wreaths at the memorials of martyred intellectuals at Rayerbazar, Mirpur and organised a seminar titled ‘Buddijibir jaban O jiban: itihaser aloke, akheri facibader jamanay’ at the academy’s Kabi Shamsur Rahman seminar room. The keynote was presented by writer-researcher Tahmidal Zami, while the Colgate University of the USA associate professor of political science Navine Murshid, cultural activist-singer Arup Rahi, and the Rastro Songskar Andolan president Hasnat Kaiyum spoke at the event chaired by the Academy director general Mohammad Azam. Tahmid Zami said that the government restricted intellectual pursuits and unofficially made killing poets and writers easily possible. Arup Rahi said that the colonial mind-set creates challenges to receive democracy, anti-colonialism and global capitalism, while decolonization is required from polity, society and state. Hasnat Kaiyum said that the political history of this land is always fighting against the colony and winning, but the wins always fade into oblivion. Mohammad Azam said that the Intellectuals took risks and expressed their thoughts systematically, and for that, in 1971 and afterwards they were targeted for killing. He also said that modern technology and social media created a new awareness among the people, which is a new experience for the intellectuals. Liberation War Museum organised special recital programme titled ‘Phire Dekhi Ekattor’ from Rashid Haider’s ‘Smrity: 71’ at the auditorium in the capital. Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy and Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi placed floral wreaths at the memorials of martyred intellectuals at Mirpur and Rayerbazar in the morning.

title: Manipuri Theatre stages Dhwajo Mestorir Moron at Natmandap
body: Moulvibazar-based theatre troupe Manipuri Theatre staged the fourth show of its production titled Dhwajo Mestorir Moron at the Natmandap of Ghoramara village of Kamalganj in Moulvibazar on Friday. The play has been directed and written by Subhasis Sinha. Dhwajo Mestorir Moron, based on a story by Smritikumar Singh, depicts the struggle of a carpenter who is famous for building traditional Manipuri houses but most of his works are replaced by modern architecture. Dhwajo came from a poor family and learned carpentry diligently and later he became famous for his talent for traditional Manipuri architecture. At the age of 80, Dhwajo was frustrated when his sons tore down his own house for an upgrade and planned to build modern architecture instead of following their tradition. Performed in a mix of Bengali and Bishnupriya Manipuri, the production aims to preserve the authenticity of the community’s language and traditions. Renowned actress Jyoti Sinha performed in the play as narrator in Bengali while the roles of young and old Dhwajo were played by Samarjit Singh and Bidhan Singh respectively. Swarnali, Shiuli, Subarna, Rajkanta, Diptangshu, Ruhit, Simanto, Anannya and Swarnali acted in the play while Sharmila Sinha, Anjana Sinha and Roni Singh played the music. The costume of the production was designed by Jyoti Sinha and the lighting was designed by Mohammd Asadurjaman Aslam Molla. ‘Manipuri Theatre revived the production which was first staged in 2005, and the current version features refined elements and a blend of senior performers and emerging actors,’ said the play director Subhasis Sinha. The two consecutive shows of Dhwajo Mestorir Moron will also be held today at the same venue.

title: Torch prosession demands  release of baul Abul Sarkar
body: Speakers, including baul artistes, on Friday demanded justice for the continuous attacks on shrines, artistes and bauls across the country and called for the release of baul singer Abul Sarkar. They made the demands at a cultural rally titled ‘Resistance March’ on the premises of the Shaheed Minar in the capital, jointly organised by several organisations including rights bodies, citizen platforms and student bodies. Speakers also called for ensuring security for all cultural and religious activities as well as freedom of speech. Presiding over the event, professor Anu Muhammad said, ‘From this rally, we call on the government to immediately release Abul Sarkar and take appropriate measures to bring those involved in mob violence incidents that occurred across the country to justice.’ He also urged the authorities to ensure security for all citizens. Other demands included the immediate resignation of the advisers for home affairs and cultural affairs ministries for their failure to ensure the safety of people of all identities and professions, an immediate end to ‘state-backed fascist activities’ carried out in the name of religion and visible government action to strictly curb nationwide attacks on people for their gender, profession, ethnicity, personal lifestyle, ideology or belief. The demands also included cancellation of all anti-national and environmentally destructive projects and agreements, including any secret deals, and reinstatement of the decision to recruit music and physical training teachers in government primary schools. Following a cultural programme performed by baul artistes, a torch procession starting at about 7:00pm marched through several city roads. Abul Sarkar was detained by Detective Branch officers in Madaripur on November 20 following a case filed by Mufti Md Abdullah. Later that day, a Manikganj court sent him to jail over allegations of making offensive remarks about Islam and hurting religious sentiments.

title: IUB stages Ibsen’s ‘Helen’
body: Independent University, Bangladesh staged Helen, a contemporary adaptation of Henrik Ibsen’s acclaimed play Hedda Gabler, at the IUB auditorium in Dhaka on Thursday. The production was performed by students of the department of English and modern languages, said a press release. The play was directed by Professor Ahmed Ahsanuzzaman, professor of English literature at the IUB and a noted Ibsen scholar. Set in the context of modern Bangladesh, Helen explores a woman’s psychological conflict, the pressures of social norms and the struggle for personal freedom. Themes of identity, power, desire and their collision with social realities form the core of the narrative. Hakon Harald Guldbrandsen, ambassador of Norway to Bangladesh, attended the event as special guest. Also present were Didar A Husain, chairman of the IUB board of trustees; Professor M Tamim, IUB vice-chancellor; and Professor Daniel W Lund, IUB pro-VC. The adaptation team included Ahmed Ahsanuzzaman, Kanija Chowdhury, Kazi Raidah Afia Nusaiba and Nurjahan Oishee. The cast featured Arnab Sarker, Farzana Faiza, M Rehneem Sajid Rohan, Nurjahan Oishee, Sadia Sultana, Srijon Shaikat, Syeda S Tahrin, and Yashna Zarine. Reefat Munmun served as dance director, with choreography by Mahbuba Jahan Ashra. Set and props were designed by Anika Jahan Ayshi, while stage management was led by Indira Barua, Md Shafwane Islam, Tahsin Ara Samanta and Tashriha Abdullah. Make-up was coordinated by Aiman Shahla, Jafna Binte Sakhawat and Tahsin Ara Samanta; costume design was by Sadia Sultana and Nusrat Islam Isha. Publication was handled by Kanija Chowdhury and Raidah Jahin. Lyrics and music were composed by Mehedi Hasan Akash and lighting and management were overseen by Sowharda Paul.

title: Concordia University invites Shamol Shishir
body: The Concordia University, one of Canada’s leading higher education institutions, has invited Bangladeshi researcher, writer and filmmaker Md Rabiul Islam, widely known as Shamol Shishir, as a research intern under the faculty of arts and science. The invitation comes from the university’s Centre for Oral History and Digital Storytelling. ‘In a recent letter signed by the Immigration Specialist of Concordia University, I am scheduled to take part in research activities under the IRCC’s special 120-day Researcher Exemption policy,’ Shamol Shishir said, This invitation from Concordia follows Shishir’s research and creative work on Bangladeshi wedding songs and women’s oral creativity. ‘My documentary project, “Wedding Songs: The Unseen Artistry of Women” is currently in progress, combining field research with filmmaking,’ he said. For many years, Shishir has documented the oral traditions, wedding rituals, songs and cultural memories of rural Bangladeshi women. ‘My collected oral histories, field recordings, and socio-cultural analysis have aligned closely with the research interests of Concordia University.’ Throughout my research stay, I will work under the supervision of a senior faculty member—an associate professor and lead co-director at COHDS. We will engage in collaborative research on folklore, oral history, women’s creativity, and methods of digital storytelling, Shishir added. Shishir’s work has brought new international attention to Bangladeshi folk culture—particularly the undocumented oral creativity of women. He said, ‘My research on wedding songs is not merely cultural documentation; it is also a valuable record of women’s stories, memories, emotions, and lived experiences.’ He said, ‘For centuries, Bangladeshi women have expressed their stories and emotions through wedding songs. My goal is to bring those voices to the world with dignity. The opportunity offered by Concordia University will help me take this work even further.’ He also shared his future plans. ‘During my stay in Montreal, I will study digital storytelling practices, archival preservation techniques, and global perspectives on oral traditions. Upon returning to Bangladesh, I will further develop both my documentary and research,’ he said.

title: Photographs depict citizens’ relation with Ramna Park
body: A three-day exhibition of photographs depicting the relationship between Dhaka people and the Ramna Park by photographer-activist Taslima Akhter began at the Shakuntala Chattar of the Ramna Park in the capital on Wednesday. The exhibition titled Valobasi Ramna: Pran O Prakirityr Golpo displayed 40 photographs of the park, mostly the activities of people and how they used the park as a citizen and green lover. The photographs taken in the past ten years portrayed the beauty of nature of the park in different seasons and the activities of members of Sakuntala Chattar, an organisation of the park visitors. The exhibition was inaugurated Bangladesh National Museum director general Tanzim Wahab while the Drik Gallery curator ASM Rezaur Rahman spoke as special guest at the event moderated by Khabeer Uddin Khan, an organiser of the Shakuntala Chattar. Tanzim Wahab said that the photographs of Taslima, also president Bangladesh Garment Sramik Samhati, are diverse in subject and approaches but deeply connected with the common people. The open-air exhibition will end on Friday.

title: Top superstar contestants go to AGB Colony
body: The Lux Superstar 2025 has taken a step closer to audiences across the country by engaging directly with people through a nationwide roadshow. As part of its ongoing promotional activities, the top five contestants of the popular reality show visited AGB Colony in Motijheel on Wednesday, drawing enthusiastic crowds of residents, traders, and consumers. The Motijheel event followed a series of roadshows earlier held in several divisional cities, including Mymensingh, aimed at creating interaction between contestants and viewers ahead of the grand finale. The top five finalists interacted with wholesale traders, retailers, and shoppers, sharing their competition experiences, seeking votes for the finale, and expressing gratitude for public support. A large numbers of fans gathered to see and meet the contestants. Speaking at the event, finalist Bidushi Bornita from Rajshahi highlighted that Lux Superstar provides a vital platform for young women in Bangladesh. ‘This show is a great opportunity for us. After a seven-year hiatus, we’ve gained valuable experiences, and being linked with Lux, a household name, helps us reach homes nationwide,’ she said. Nazah Naoar from Pabna, another finalist, initially underestimated the program's scale but recognised its impact after reaching the top five. ‘The support has been overwhelming during our visits across the country. I hope to apply what I’ve learned here in my future endeavours,’ she said. The organisers thanked the people of AGB Colony, Motijheel, along with the local administration, media partners, wholesale and retail traders, and spectators for their cooperation and enthusiastic participation.

title: Business automation will reduce BFDC syndicate: Mahfuj Alam
body: Bangladesh interim government information and broadcasting adviser Md Mahfuj Alam on Tuesday said that the Bangladesh Film Development Corporation’s business automation service will reduce syndicate and increase accountability. The remarks were made at an inauguration ceremony of the BFDC’s business automation service, with the opening of Jahir Raihan Archive, repairing of sound recording studio and fountain at BFDC in the capital. He also said that the film industry needs an eco-system from production to distribution, and filmmakers should think of diverse contents to attract audience in different platforms. The BFDC Managing Director Masuma Rahman Tani said that the BFDC have limited resources, but they try to improve its facilities for young filmmakers of the country aiming to promote Bangladeshi films in the worldwide film arena.

title: Begum Rokeya Day today
body: Begum Rokeya Day will be observed today to remember the contribution of Begum Rokeya, a pioneer of Bengali women’s education and a social reformer. The government and different organisations, including women rights organisations, will hold different events to mark the day. The women and children affairs ministry is going to give ‘Begum Rokeya Padak’ to four women for their contributions to empowering women in the country. For the award, Ruvana Rakib has been selected in the women’s education (research) category, Kalpona Akter in the women’s rights (labour rights) category, Nabila Idris in the human rights category and Ritu Porna Chakma in the women’s awakening (sports) category. Interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Monday issued a message, paying respect to the memory of Begum Rokeya for her contribution to the spread of education for women. In the message, Yunus said that Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain, widely known as Begum Rokeya, led women from darkness to light through her far-reaching movement for women’s liberation and human rights, state-run news agency Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha reports. ‘Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain brought the women’s community from darkness to light through a massive social movement for women’s liberation and human rights,’ he said in the message. The women and children affairs ministry’s different programmes include the vulnerable women benefit programme for the socio-economic development of underprivileged rural women, financial assistance for poor pregnant mothers in rural areas and low-income working mothers in urban areas and nationwide microcredit programmes aimed at promoting self-employment among women at the grassroots, he said. In addition, support is being provided to develop women entrepreneurs in marginalised communities, while working women’s hostels are being operated to ensure safe accommodation for employed women, he said. Under the project to strengthen integrated services for the prevention and redress of violence against women and children, a 24/7 toll-free hotline (109) has been launched to provide immediate assistance through the Quick Response Team, he added. The chief adviser also congratulated the women who are going to receive ‘Begum Rokeya Padak 2025’. Liberation War Museum is going to hold a special speech tilted ‘My Enconunter with Rokeya’ by Spanish artist and filmmaker Isabel Herguera, also Sultana’s Dream full-length animation film director, at its auditorium at 4:00pm today. At a debate competition held by Bangladesh Mahila Parishad at its office in the capital on Monday on the occasion of International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women and World Human Rights Day 2025, the association president, Fauzia Moslem, said that in the recent misogynistic attitudes, Begum Rokeya was not spared. For this reason, discussion on her works is very urgent as those are very vast, she added.

title: Naristhane Swagatam depicts Rokeya’s ‘Sultana’s Dream’
body: Visual and performance artist Efat Razowana Reya depicted Bengali feminist thinker, writer, educator, political activist and social reformer Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain’s story ‘Sultana’s Dream’ in her performance titled ‘Naristhane Swagatam’ at the Liberation War Museum in the capital Dhaka on Monday. The performance ‘Naristhane Swagatam’ invited audiences about their dreams and discussed Sultana’s dream and contemporary issues. With the performance, Reya proposed keeping peace by making a society free from gender violence. Liberation War Museum and Kala Kendra jointly organised a four-month group exhibition titled ‘Punorkalpanay Sultanar Swapna’ to mark the inscription of Rokeya’s ‘Sultana’s Dream’ in recognition of human innovation and imagination by UNESCO. The exhibition, curated by Sharmillie Rahman, features 20 artists’ artworks based on ‘Sultana’s Dream’. The exhibition was inaugurated on Saturday.

title: Training facilities for women filmmakers sought
body: Training facilities for women filmmakers are needed to boost their skills, speakers said at a seminar on Monday. They also said that the modern film industry was highly technology-based and future filmmakers needed technological skills for survival. The seminar titled ‘Women’s Empowerment and the Future of Cinema’ was held at the seminar room of Bangladesh Film Archive in the capital Dhaka. The Women’s Film Society Bangladesh president, Aktanin Khair Tanin, presented the keynote while information and broadcasting secretary Mahbuba Farjana was present as the chief guest at the event chaired by Bangladesh Film Archive director general M Javed Iqbal. In her keynote, Aktanin said that film played a vital role in women empowerment and the digital era expanded the film industry, which also created new hopes, including creative workplaces. She stressed proper training facilities for women filmmakers and other professions related to the industry, saying that the modern technologies, including artificial intelligence, virtual reality, augmented reality and online platforms, created new challenges for filmmakers. Filmmaker Nargis Akhter, joint secretary Nursia Komol and director of the Archive Farhana Rahman spoke on the topic and the seminar was moderated by the Women’s Film Society general secretary Syeda Farzana Zaman Rumpa. Nargis shared her early experience as a female director on the shooting floor and her relationship with casts and crew members. She also stressed the importance of technical skills for a director who wants to work in a domination-free environment as a director. Nursia urged to promote the new perspective of women representation in films and avoid stereotypical exhibition of women, which depicted women as objects for male pleasure. Aktanin also shared about the Women’s Film Society Bangladesh’s future plans, including organising workshops for women filmmakers in 64 districts and producing 1000 one-minute film productions to raise awareness on violence against women. Jointly organised by the Bangladesh Film Archive and the Women’s Film Society, the event also screened a film titled Char Sotiner Ghar directed by Bangladeshi filmmaker Nargis Akter.

title: Fawaz Rob’s prints address crises of Palestinians, Rohingyas
body: Visual artist Fawaz Rob addresses the crises of people in Palestine and Rohingya in his solo print exhibition at Zainul Gallery of Dhaka University in the capital. He also depicted Dhaka city’s night views and the city bird, a crow, in his solo exhibition, which ended on Sunday. The 11-day exhibition displayed 92 prints under nine series which began on November 27. The Palestine’s series displayed ten prints depicting Khan Yunis Mosque and The Church of Palestine images, before and after being destroyed by Israel. A print titled Gaza 1924 shows the beautiful landscape of Gaza city. His artwork titled Leaving Rafa shows people from Rafa carrying their bags to leave the city during the attack by the Israeli occupation. His series titled Activism also depicted the plight of the Rohingya people and others. His print titled Long Walk Home depicted Rohingyas fleeing genocide committed by the Burmese army, while another print titled Two Rohingya Girls showed the life of Rohingyas at the refugee camp located at the shore of the Bay of Bengal. A text based artwork titled Chiro Unnoto Momo Shir beautifully composed the national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam’s timeless poem Bidrohi. Fawaz Rob’s night series depicted Dhaka city’s night at different places including Street, a university, restaurants, bars and Ahsan Manzil. ‘If our art doesn’t speak up when it is necessary, if our art cannot stand up for the truth, if our art doesn’t speak the truth that everyone else is too scared to say, then what good is it?’ Fawaz Rob said, adding that activism through art is important and art can make a big difference. Fawaz Rob’s art has been exhibited in Paris, Istanbul, Zagreb, Budapest, Côte d’Azur, Amsterdam, Kathmandu and Dhaka. His exhibition ‘Dhaka, I love you’ was appreciated by French art critics and was featured in ‘Le Parisian’. His etching titled ‘Long Walk Home’ brought him international award. His work has been archived at the International Printmaking Museum in Guanlan, China.

title: Mystic poet Hason Raja’s death anniv observed
body: The 103rd anniversary of death of the celebrated mystic poet and philosopher Hason Raja was observed in Sunamganj on Saturday with tributes highlighting his lasting influence on Bangla literature and folk music. The occasion was marked with cultural programmes, including renditions of his songs and discussions on his life and legacy. Speakers noted that his works, deeply rooted in Sufi philosophy, continued to inspire generations for their spiritual depth and simplicity. Born at Lakshmanshree village on the banks of the Surma River on December 21, 1854, Hason Raja devoted his life to spiritual reflection and emerged as one of the most distinctive voices in Bangla mystical music. According to national professor Dewan Mohammad Azraf, Hason Raja owned about 5 lakh 27 thousand bighas of land, which included several notable parganas of Sylhet and Sunamganj. Despite his privileged background, he crossed social and religious boundaries through his songs, which expressed devotion, humanism and a yearning for the creator. Hason Raja is believed to have composed around 200 songs, although many remain orally preserved among the people of Sylhet and Sunamganj. His landmark collection ‘Hason Udas’, featuring 206 songs, was published in 1907, while other works appeared in various periodicals such as ‘Hason Rajar Tinpurush’ and ‘Al Islah’. Rabindranath Tagore praised his compositions on several occasions, including in Kolkata in 1925 and later during the Hibbert Lectures in London in 1933, recognising his role in blending philosophy with music after the tradition of Lalon Shah. Hason Raja passed away on December 6, 1922.

title: Dhaka Pen Show rediscovers tradition of fountain pens
body: At the heart of Dhaka city, inside the warm halls of the Bishwo Shahitto Kendro, something quietly magical is unfolding: the first-ever Dhaka Pen Show. For the first time in Bangladesh, collectors, writers and young enthusiasts have gathered to celebrate an unlikely article—the timeless beauty of ink on paper. What began as small conversations among hobbyists has now grown into a movement. The Dhaka Pen Club, founded in 2019, leads this revival with a simple dream: to bring back the golden age of fountain pens. Seven stalls glow like little museums, offering vintage pens, handmade inks, calligraphy tools and uniquely made notebooks. Some items at the show are so rare that visitors pause in disbelief, discovering antique articles for writing they never knew existed. Organisers even hope to revive the historic Karnaphuli Paper Mill one day, to produce high-quality GSM (grams per square meter) paper ideal for writing with fountain pens. Among the many storytellers present at the fair stands Nazmul Haque Montu, the passionate owner of ‘Bari’r Naam Doyat Kali’, a museum housing artefacts and antique articles for writing he has established at his home at Pallabi in Dhaka city. Inspired by his uncle’s ink factory, he began collecting inks in 1983, Nazmul recalls. Today, his museum boasts a collection of around 1,000 inkpots, some over a century old, crafted from silver, clay, crystal, copper and 20–25 varieties of ink, including iconic names such as Subarna, Agnibeena—which poet Kazi Nazrul Islam once used—Kajol Kali and Palash Kali. His stall displays everything from Mughal-era Bidri art to once famous and widely used Pelikan ink from 1890. Younger collectors are also shaping the rising culture. Fahim Mosaddeq, a 27-year-old designer, began his collection in 2024 with a Lamy Safari pen. He now owns 150 pens and over 150 pencils, priced from Tk 60 to Tk 92,000. Sohanur Rahman, a 26-year-old notebook maker, showcases his creations, each inspired by archaeological sites and old architectural designs, and suitable for writing with fountain pens. Honouring the legacy of handwriting, the exhibition also highlights the work of Md Khorshed Alam Bhuiyan, the legendary certificate writer of Dhaka University. Enthusiastic visitors were seen having their names written on special papers by him, while his calligraphy and other artistic works were also on display. For decades, he carved bamboo into pens and hand-wrote thousands of certificates, shaping a tradition with his elegant calligraphy. The fair also has workshops, seminars and open discussions for visitors to educate themselves in the art of writing and of the priceless traditions of ink, pens and paper. In an age ruled by screens, the Dhaka Pen Show stands as a gentle reminder: writing is still alive, steady, soulful and full of meaning.

title: Discussion warns against abuse of images
body: Speakers at a discussion on Saturday called for attention to the abuse of images, noting that media houses used photographs without permission on digital platforms. They condemned the publishing by law enforcement agencies of photographs of detained persons, which create a media trial without the allegations being proven. They also highlighted the need for policy education and specialised training for lawyers and media professionals to ensure proper recognition of photographers’ creative ownership. The panel discussion titled ‘Use and Abuse of the Photo in Public Discourse’ featured Lawyer and Human Rights activist Sara Hossain, chief photographer of The Business Standard, Syed Zakir Hossain, and activist-curator Shahidul Alam. The discussion was held at the DrikPath Bhaban at Panthapath in the capital. Shahidul Alam said that images are powerful, and for this reason, they become dangerous when they mislead, with powerful authorities abusing images most often. He also said that people need to be concerned about the use of females’ photographs and that without protest nothing will change. Syed Zakir Hossain said that photographers mostly suffer because of the lack of implementation of the copyright law and most online news sites have no photographer and use photographs which are copied from others. He also alleged that recently the Chief Advisor Office’s Facebook page used his photograph without any permission from him. Sara Hossain said that an integrated process should be established for applying copyright laws for photographers, suggesting that young photographers and lawyers could work together as a team. She also said that photographs of people who are under trial and accused are being used for media trials, which is unethical. The discussion also commemorated the 70th anniversary of World Press Photo while the Drik Picture Library hosted a 16-day exhibition titled ‘What Have We Done?’ As a part of the event, visual artist and educator Sumi Anjuman discussed her work ‘River Runs Violet’ and how it explores rising sexual and physical violence against women and children in Bangladesh and challenges patriarchal narratives at the venue. The exhibition will run until December 20.

title: Russian House in Dhaka celebrates Bangladesh Victory Day
body: The Russian House in Dhaka organised a concert, dedicating the 100th anniversary of Russian people’s diplomacy and Bangladesh Victory Day, at the open-air stage at Rabindra Sarobar in Dhaka on Friday. The programme featured the Shilpakala Academy artistes, the band Shonar Bangla Circus and the Akaash and Co, who performed traditional and contemporary Russian and Bangladeshi works, said a press release. The evening underscored the depth of bilateral ties, highlighting the decisive diplomatic and strategic assistance provided by the USSR in 1971, including the use of its UN veto power and its support for the international recognition of Bangladesh’s independence. Today, this friendship is strengthened by over 6,000 graduates of Soviet and Russian universities, who are leaders in Bangladesh’s economy, energy sector, science, and public administration. Russian compatriots living in the country act as mentors and guides for the younger generation, introducing them to the opportunities of Russian education and culture and opening pathways for professional growth in high-tech industries. Special tribute was paid to the courage of the young heroes of the 1971 Liberation War, whose sacrifice laid the foundation for the country’s sovereignty. The discussion also highlighted the vivid symbol of modern strategic partnership — the Rosatom State Corporation’s project to construct the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant. This facility, with a capacity of 2400MW, will enable the provision of stable energy for Bangladesh’s growing economy and includes extensive technology transfer and the training of national personnel, added the press release.

title: Seminar on Fakir Lalon Shah held at Bangla Academy
body: A seminar and demonstration organised by Nabapran Andalan and Bangla Academy on ‘Nadiar Bhabukatar Etihashe Fakir Lalon Shah’ was held at Abdul Karim Sahitya Bisharad Auditorium of the Academy in the capital on Saturday, said a press release. Poet and thinker Farhad Mazhar spoke as the keynote speaker while cultural affairs adviser Mostofa Sarwar Farooki was present as chief guest at the event chaired by Bangla Academy director general Mohammad Azam. Farhad Mazhar said that the post-colonial mindset ignored the Bengal schools of philosophy which created slavery of western philosophy and they misread Baul and also Lalon. Mostofa Sarwar Farooki said that a lack of philosophical concept and practice created many obstacles, and that people’s perception about Lalon needs research, even though his philosophy and works are popular among the common people of the country. Fisheries and livestock adviser Farida Akhtar, and Farhad Mazhar presented the theoretical discussion on the topic while artistes of Nabapran Andalan demonstrated musical works of Lalon at the event.

title: Award winning film ‘Nishi’ premiered at European Film Festival in Bangladesh
body: The 35th annual Environmental Media Association Award winning film Nishi’s premiere in Bangladesh was held at the European Film Festival at Goethe-Institut Bangladesh on Saturday. The film Nishi, based on a story and screenplay by Golam Rabbany, is jointly directed by Rabbany and Zahirul Islam. Produced by the International Academy of Film and Media, the film was also co-produced by the European Union Bangladesh, Green Film School Alliance and UNESCO Dhaka. An eight-minute duration environmental film, Nishi, was shot one day in a tea garden and surrounding areas in Sylhet, featuring the local people of the garden. The film revolves around a tea-worker’s daughter named Nishi, who collects water from a long distance, which hampers her schooling, and her father, however, plans to organise Nishi’s marriage to another tea-worker in exchange for a tube well. The film featured performances by Nishi, daughter of a tea estate worker, along with Biswajit, Ganesh and Bharati. The film’s cinematography was done by Natalia Pusnik, an alumnus of Poland’s renowned Łód Film School. A four-day ‘European Film Festival 2025’ which began Thursday evening at the Bangladesh Shishu Academy Auditorium showcases European and Bangladeshi films at Alliance Francaise Dhanmondi branch and Goethe-Institut in the capital. The closing and award giving ceremony will be held at BRAC University Auditorium today.

title: Kalpanar Tulite nurtures child visual artists
body: A group art exhibition by children, titled Kalpanar Tulite, displaying drawings and paintings by 42 child artists, was held at Gallery The Illusions at Lalmatia in the capital. The three-day exhibition organised by the Dhaka Adventist Pre-Seminary and School aims to nurture child visual artists and promote their works, was inaugurated on Thursday. The artists depicted landscapes, rivers, fishes, birds, boats, religious and cultural events, animals, villages and replicas of famous painters’ artworks at the exhibition. The exhibition displayed artworks of Nursery to Class Ten students, created with diverse mediums including watercolour, acrylic, pastel and charcoal on paper and canvas. Tahrim Rahman Priha , a Nursery student, drew a riverside village while Amatullah Noorain, a student of play group, portrayed colourful flowers and Fatiha Fairuz Ohee, a kindergarten student, depicted a hilly falls becoming a river in a plain land. ‘Our school is focusing on improving our children’s skills, we aim to nurture and recognise their talents and provide opportunities to grow and develop them,’ said principal of the school Thomas Hridoy Baroi. Curated by artist Bappy Linkon Roy, the exhibition will end today.

title: Drik hosts World Press Photo 70-year anniversary exhibition
body: The Drik Picture Library hosts the World Press Photo 70-year anniversary exhibition, titled ‘What Have We Done?’, which depicts a selection of seven decades of photo-journalism from the archive and is curated by artist and photographer Cristina de Middel. The exhibition was inaugurated on Friday at the DrikPath Bhaban at Panthapath in the capital with a short-discussion where the World Press Photo manager of programs Anna Kućma, Chaarcha.com editor Sohrab Hasan and Drik Managing Director Shahidul Alam participated. The discussion was moderated by the Curator and General Manager of Drik, ASM Rezaur Rahman. Shahidul Alam said that it is necessary to practice self-criticism and raise important questions about the mistakes, otherwise, progress is impossible. He also stressed on image studies at schools and colleges and said that with proper awareness and understanding of these images, we can start to ask critical questions about what a picture could represent or signify. Anna Kućma said that while photographers were devoted to public interest and the right to inform, often at personal risk, the Archive has simultaneously become a global history. ‘Today, we no longer see photography archives as simple records of the past, rather as active sites of interpretation where memory and meaning are constantly revisited, challenged, and reshaped,’ she said. Sohrab Hasan said that the photographs of the war of independence serve as the primary evidence captured by the Bangladeshi and foreign photographers. ‘Uprising come in decades, but daily struggle is also portrayed in photography while wars and killings go on worldwide, and you know who is pulling the strings behind them,’ Sohrab said. He also added that the critical process of selecting images mean deciding which ones to include or exclude and what message to convey through them. He then praised Bangladeshi photographers in photo-journalism and also congratulated photographers K M Asad and Suvra Kanti Das on their earning recognitions at the world press photo contest. The 16-day exhibition displayed 90 photographs around six recurring visual patterns from the archive, which are ‘Weeping Women and Men Rescuing’, ‘Emotional Soldiers and Debris’, ‘Being a Man and Being a Woman’, ‘Fire and Smoke’, ‘Black Skin and The Dark Continent’ and ‘Silhouettes and Shadows - The ‘Wow’ Moment’. In the event, a 3-day workshop was also organised on Photojournalism and Visual Narrative led by Gabrielle Fonseca Johnson, South Asia Editor for Reuters Pictures. A keynote presentation and panel discussion will be held today at 4:30 pm at the venue. The exhibition will run until December 20.

title: Disappearing species cast gloom on JU butterfly fair
body: Concerns for the fast disappearance of species of the vibrant winged creature from the leafy grounds of Jahangirnagar University were voiced amid the festivities with which the university held its annual Butterfly Fair on Friday. The 15th edition of the fair, centred on the theme ‘When butterflies fly, nature finds new rhythm’, drew hundreds of visitors from nearby areas to the university’s lush green campus, considered one of the country’s richest urban wildlife habitats. University vice-chancellor Mohammad Kamrul Ahsan inaugurated the fair in front of the Zahir Raihan auditorium in the morning following which he led a colourful procession to parade through the campus streets. The daylong fanfare featured children’s art competitions, puppet shows, quiz contests, documentary screenings and display of live butterflies, allowing visitors a close view of their flight behaviour. A key attraction this year was the launch of the third edition of the ‘Butterflies of Bangladesh’, a field guide documenting 360 species with photographs and gene-based identification notes. Organisers also honoured conservationist Ali Reza Khan with the Butterfly Award 2025, while zoology students Shahariar Rabbi Tanmoy and Nure Afsari jointly received the Butterfly Young Enthusiast Award. Children were seen chasing toy butterflies fashioned with paper and bamboo, while university students were seen guiding visitors through the shaded areas of the campus. Throughout the day, visitors strolled through the Butterfly Park, dotted with host plants and fluttering specimens, and also visited the stalls where students exhibited posters, photographs and hand-drawn field maps. A kite-flying corner and children’s painting sessions added to the crowds. Among the visitors was Shahnaz Parvin, who travelled from Dhaka’s Khilgaon area with her two young children as she saw the fair’s announcement online. ‘My kids grew up in city where butterflies feel like a storybook thing,’ she said as her daughter held up an origami swallowtail. ‘Seeing them up close and understanding why they’re disappearing this place feel like a reminder of what nature used to be.’ The organisers’ sharing their concern that the campus was experiencing a steep decline in the butterfly species rang a note of gloom in the fair’s festive mood. Once home to more than 100 species, the area now hosted only 72, said the worried butterfly enthusiasts of the university. ‘The decline in butterfly populations is not just the disappearance of something beautiful—it signals deeper ecological imbalance,’ said Professor Monwar Hossain, convener of the fair. ‘Butterflies are crucial pollinators, and losing the plants they depend on disrupts their entire lifecycle,’ he said. Attributing the loss of species variety to the climate change impacts, he observed, ‘This year’s excessive rainfall damaged the wings of many butterflies. They need sunlight for energy, and prolonged rain deprives them of it.’ The fair concluded with a prize-giving ceremony, while organisers stressed the message of urgency. ‘We host this festival to inspire joy,’ Professor Monwar Hossain said, ‘but also to remind people that if we lose the forests and the plants butterflies depend on, we lose far more than colourful wings.’

title: Shironamhin releases Ei Obelay 2
body: Founder and leader of the rock band Shironamhin Ziaur Rahman at an event in Dhaka on Thursday said that a band existed because of its creative soul. He made the remark while releasing the final track, Ei Obelay 2, of its eighth studio album titled Baatighor at the Aerial Hall of Hotel Sheraton under the sponsorship of The Premium Homes Limited, said a press release. Speaking about their artistic philosophy, Ziaur Rahman said, ‘We are musicians; our fulfilment lies in creation. A band exists because of its creative soul.’ The lyricist and composer mentioned, ‘We never make music just for profession or profit. Out of love for music and commitment to our listeners, creating new songs and new albums is our responsibility as artists.’ During the event, both the Bangla version, Ei Obelay 2, and its English counterpart titled Remember Me were screened on an LED display. Shortly after the premiere, both versions were released on Shironamhin’s oficial YouTube channel and simultaneously made available on all major global and local digital platforms, including Spotify, Apple Music, iTunes, Amazon and the Shadhin app. With this release, Shironamhin announced the completion of their Baatighor album. Ziaur Rahman also stated that, as always, the Batighor album will be published as a collector’s edition book with QR codes at the upcoming book fair—allowing listeners to enjoy the music while also exploring the lyrics and stories behind each song. Ei Obelay – 2 is written by Ziaur Rahman, composed and music-video directed by Kazy Ahmad Shafin and the English version, Remember Me, was translated by Sarika Resh Rahman. The music video features popular television anchor and actress Neel Hurerzahan, with actor Tausif Mahbub appearing in still photography sequences. Shironamhin has recently surpassed one million YouTube subscribers and earned the Golden Play Button, further proving their consistency in releasing new music. The ten-track Batighor album stands as a testament to this creative momentum. Mentioning that this is the busiest period in Shironamhin’s history, composer Kazy Ahmad Shafin said, ‘We have never had so many live performances and musical engagements at once. This success inspires us to create even more diverse work.’ Guitarist Sudipto Sinha shared that while Baatighor was an unplugged album, the band intends to return to their signature plugged-in experimental sound for future releases. Following their recent Canada tour, Shironamhin has been performing back-to-back live shows across Bangladesh. Beyond the Baatighor album, the band also recorded a rendition of Kandari Hushiar for the Nazrul Institute project and Ek Jhak Torun composed by Foad Nasser Babu with lyrics by Shahid Mahmud Jangi for the BTV original music project. After releasing Klanto Cofeeshop, the band members boarded a flight to Toronto for Shironamhin’s first-ever Canada tour. Despite a packed schedule, the band continues to maintain their commitment to releasing new music. Shironamhin has announced plans for a United States and Europe tour next year along with the commencement of their ninth studio album.

title: Sanad Biswas’s installation ‘resonance’ searches inner-self
body: Sculptor and multidisciplinary artist Sanad Biswas searched for his inner-self in his solo art exhibition titled Resonance which is under way at Daagi Art Garage at Hazaribagh in the capital. The exhibition displayed an interactive installation consisting of a dark red chamber with ankle-height water while the audience visited the place barefoot to find the source of light. The space is designed with red polythene as a tunnel, and the chamber also provides soundproofing, allowing visitors to hear the sound of their footsteps and water splash. ‘The project ideas came from the Mahabharata Chakravyuh, which was a multi-layered rotating spinning wheel and at the same time, we were drowning in a lot of social, political and international issues, and our art also incorporated multiple forms of craftsmanship,’ Sanad Biswas said, adding that the installation used only water and the plotline, while visitors made the space come alive. ‘The conflicts of time, events and issues mostly form the body of the artwork while this interactive installation offers experience as a tool of communication,’ he said. The eight-day exhibition was inaugurated on November 28, and will end today.

title: Bijoy Boimela to be held in Dec 10-22 at Bangla Academy
body: The Bijoy Boimela marking Victory Day will be held on the Bangla Academy premises in the capital Dhaka in December 10-22. The Bangladesh Publishers and Booksellers Association announced the schedule of the fair at a press conference held at the Al Mahmud Writers’ Corner at Bangla Academy on Thursday. The fair will feature more than 200 publications and cultural events for children with the liberation war corner, the association said. It also said that the market for creative books in the country had decreased and there were no regular activities about books except the Ekushey Book Fair in February. BUPUS director Abul Bashar Firoz, Granthik publisher Abdur Razzak Rubel and Renaissance publisher Sabah Khaled, among others, were present at the press conference. Abul Bashar Firoz said that they planned to hold the Bijoy Boimela every year at the venue. ‘We plan to organise the book fair at 64 districts in two or three phases across the country in the future,’ he said, adding that they also planned to organise an international children’s book fair in May. To increase the reading habit of youth and children, the BAPUS will organise educational institutions-based book fair, he said. The Bijoy Boimela will also introduce some awards for different categories of books.

title: Bijoy Sarkar’s death anniv today
body: Today is the 40th anniversary of death of poet and musician Bijoy Sarkar. Born at Dumdi village in Narail on February 20, 1903, the folk bard penned and composed at about 1,800 songs in different folk genres, including Jari, Sari, Kirtan, Bhajan, Bhatiali, which endeared him to thousands. He used to practice various folk music and acted in a jatra troupe. In 1925, Bijoy Sarkar took lessons on Kabi Gaan for two years from Manohar Sarkar and for one year from Rajendra Sarkar. He joined a troupe of Kabi Gaan in 1929 and established himself as a Kabial within short time. He was posthumously awarded Ekushey Padak in 2013. Bijoy Sarkar passed away at Keutia in Kolkata, India on December 4, 1985.

title: Israfil participate in Asia-Pacific Theatre Festival in Shanghai
body: Dhaka University’s theatre and performance studies department teacher, professor Israfil Shaheen, has participated in the 18th Asia-Pacific Bond of Theatre Schools Festival and Directors’ Conference 2025 in Shanghai of China, said a press release. The five-day festival hosted by Shanghai Theatre Academy ended on Wednesday. It comprised of eight theatre performance and five theatre workshops with conferences and symposiums at Huashan campus of the Shanghai Theatre Academy. The festival was participated by 15 theatre schools from Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines, South Korea, India, Bangladesh, Australia, and New Zealand, as well as from Shanghai, Beijing, Yunnan, Guangxi, and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of China. Israfil Shaheen represented Bangladesh at the directors’ conference and the academic symposium on ‘Theatre · Future · AI’, conducted in-depth discussions on the impacts and transformations of future technologies on November 29. He also conducted a three-day workshop on ‘Performing Healing - A New Multimedia Workshop on Theatre and Rehabilitation through Ethnographic Research’ at the Multifuncational Conference Room of the Shanghai Theatre Academy. Israfil Shaheen, who graduated from India’s National School of Drama, chaired his department at DU from 2006 to 2009.

title: Sur Sudha Sangeetayon hosts contest for visually impaired
body: Sur Sudha Sangeetayon marked the 27th National and 34th International Day of Persons with Disabilities 2025 by hosting a discussion session, cultural programme, and the closing ceremony of a special nationwide music and recitation competition for visually impaired participants. The event was held at the organisation’s Mohammadpur centre in Dhaka on Sunday, said a press release on Wednesday. The programme was presided over by Sur Sudha Sangeetayon founder and general secretary Shahabuddin Dolon, who described visually impaired people as a ‘national asset’ whose creativity enriches society. Among the distinguished guests were Nari Unnayan Shakti executive director Afroja Parvin, social worker and singer Mashrura Shafik Swapna, paediatric surgeon Bijoy Krishna Das, freedom fighter Nizamuddin Ahmed Alam, and Inner Wheel Club representatives Rahenuma Khanam and Afroza Kabir. Speakers stressed the importance of dignity, participation and skill development for persons with disabilities. Awards were later handed to competition winners.

title: ULAB inaugurates photo exhibition on archaeological objects
body: The University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh inaugurated a seven-day photography exhibition on archaeological objects titled A History of Bangladesh in 25 Objects from the Collections of the Varendra Research Museum at their campus in the capital on Tuesday. The exhibition was organised by the Department of General Education and the Center for Archaeological Studies of ULAB as part of Varendra Research Museum’s Heritage Festival. The exhibition displayed the photographs from the collections of the Varendra Research Museum, including desk of Saratkumar Ray, a punch-marked silver coin of the 2nd century BC, fossilised wood, a Kushan gold coin of 2nd century CE, a copper plate grant, a standing Buddha sandstone statue of the 5th century CE, a Jaub sculpture and intangible heritage including clay sculpture making. Co-curated by the Varendra Research Museum, Durham University’s UNESCO Chair on Archaeological Ethics and Practice in Cultural Heritage, and ULAB, the exhibition is supported by the British Council’s Cultural Protection Fund, in partnership with the UK Government’s Department for Culture, Media and Sport. ULAB’s acting vice chancellor professor Milan Kumar Bhattacharjee delivered the welcome address at the inaugural ceremony, the deputy director of British Council Dhaka Maarya Rehman and director of the Varendra Research Museum Professor Kazi Md Mostafizur Rahman also spoke and head of the Department of General Education and director of the Center for Archaeological Studies, ULAB, professor Shahnaj Husne Jahan delivered the vote of thanks. The UNESCO Chair Professor Robin Coningham, delivered a presentation entitled ‘Breaking the Myth: Engaging Museum Professionals and Community’ at the event which depicts how a museum can engage with communities and become popular. He also shared the two-phase workshop with the Varendra Research Museum, which was set up in Rajshahi in 1910, the first private museum in British Bengal. Distinguished guests included ULAB’s former vice chancellor professor Imran Rahman, Durham University, UK professors Emily Williams, Mark Manuel, and Christopher Davis, Advisor of ICOMOS, Nepal, Kai Weise, Varendra Research Museum deputy librarian Aslam Reza, museum professionals, archaeologists, historians, heritage practitioners of Bangladesh and ULAB’s deans, heads, directors, faculties and students. The exhibition will run until December 6.

title: ‘Glimpses’ features artists of Bangladesh in Thailand
body: The Embassy of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh in Thailand and Uttara-based Galleri Kaya organized a group art exhibition titled Glimpses featuring 12 contemporary and modern artists of Bangladesh in Thailand. A 13-day exhibition commemorated the 54th anniversary of the Victory Day of Bangladesh which was inaugurated by the deputy permanent secretary for Culture of the Kingdom of Thailand, Yuthika Isarangkura, on Tuesday at Bangkok Art and Culture Centre, according to a press release. Bangladesh ambassador to the Kingdom of Thailand Faiyaz Murshid Kazi, honorary consul of Bangladesh in Central Thailand, Galleri Kaya director artist Goutam Chakraborty, artists Ashraful Hasan and Kanak Chanpa Chakma were present at the ceremony as guests. The exhibition, which displayed 37 artworks of artists Abdus Shakoor Shah, Ashraful Hasan, Chandra Shekhar Dey, Hamiduzzaman Khan, Ivy Zaman, Jamal Ahmed, Kanak Chanpa Chakma, Maksuda Iqbal Nipa, Mohammad Iqbal, Ranjit Das, Shambhu Acharya and Sheikh Afzal Hossain, depicted diverse culture, riverine aesthetics, textile traditions, ritual life and urban experience of Bangladesh. The exhibition will end on December 14.

title: Month-long Jatra Utsab begins at BSA
body: Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy inaugurated a month-long Jatra Utsab to celebrate the Victory Day in December at its experimental theatre hall on Monday. The festival features 31 Jatra troupes’ performances across the country as part of implementation of Jatrashilpa Development Policy 2012, which distributes registration based on performance. According to the policy, after receiving a certificate from BSA, a jatra troupe can perform anywhere in Bangladesh. A notification on November 30 stated that the ministry of cultural affairs formed a 15-member Jatrashilpi Unnayan Committee including five members from different ministries led by the director general of the academy. The festival was inaugurated by cultural affairs secretary Md Mafidur Rahman while the drama and film department director Deepak Kumar Goswami delivered the welcome speech at the inauguration ceremony presided by director general of the academy Rezauddin Stalin. Deepak Kumar Goswami said that from the registered 205 troupes across the country only 55 are active while rest of the troupe stoppped their activities for many reasons. ‘Many troupes or their members are allegedly involved with obscenity and gambling during the pala and we need to set a guideline about these issues from the centre that the troupes are not to be involved with these activities,’ said Deepak. Md Mafidur Rahman said that jatra-pala is mostly watched by common people of the country which need more patrons. ‘We need to organise events round the year for common people to build an inclusive nation and society,’ Mafidur said, adding that the ministry is also focused on cultural events across the country. Mafidur also stressed on the publicities of the event so that common people would attend the jatra festival. The income generated from the ticket sold at the festival would be donated to the jatra troupes, as the ticket price was fixed at BDT 100 at the opening show which was watched by enthusiastic audiences. On the opening day, Khulna- based Jatra troupe Suryatarun Natya Sangstha staged Mrityuur Cokhe Jal which was written by Pranab Mondal and directed by Debendranath. Today, Narsingdi-based jatra troupe, New Jahura Opera, will stage Kashem Malar Prem, written by Shamsul Haque and directed by Mostafijur Rahman at the same venue.

title: Firoz Mahmud’s Multi-Layered Legacies concludes at Japan embassy
body: The six-day solo art exhibition of New york-based Bangladeshi artist Firoz Mahmud titled Multi-Layered Legacies concluded at the gallery of Japan embassy at Baridhara in Dhaka on Monday. The exhibition was inaugurated in the presence of Japan ambassador to Bangladesh Saida Shinichi, who attended as chief guest and praised Mahmud’s ability to connect global narratives through a rich visual language, said a press release. Presented in collaboration with Paper Rhyme Advertising Limited, this exhibition also commemorates the agency’s 20th anniversary, celebrating its partnership with the artist and its support of his global artistic journey. Visitors to the exhibition experienced an immersive presentation of Mahmud’s multi-layered approach to history, identity and contemporary culture, reflecting through his distinctive multidisciplinary practice. Firoz Mahmud is known for his engagement in major international exhibitions, including the Bangkok Art Biennale, Congo Biennale, Lahore Biennial, Dhaka Art Summit, Setouchi Triennale, Aichi Triennial, Sharjah Biennale, Cairo Biennale, Echigo-Tsumari Triennial and the Asian Biennale. Over the course of his career, he has received numerous honours, including the Asian Art Council in New York; the COAL Prize, Paris, nomination; Queens Council on the Arts in New York; Hiroshima City Museum of Contemporary Art, OT Prize; and the Sovereign Asian Art Prize in Hong Kong. He has been awarded both the Dilnasheen Khanom Gold Medal and the Shilpacharya Zainul Gold Medal from the Institute of Fine Art, University of Dhaka, and is a recipient of the Elizabeth Greenshields Foundation Grants in Canada. Mahmud’s academic journey spans the Institute of Fine Arts at the University of Dhaka, Tama Art University, and Tokyo University of the Arts, where he completed his PhD. He also served as a postgraduate scholar at the Rijksakademie van Beeldende Kunsten in Amsterdam and has collaborated closely with the globally celebrated Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama. He is represented internationally by Ota Fine Arts in Tokyo, Shanghai, and Singapore.

title: Heritage festival, special exhibition held at Varendra Research Museum
body: Rajshahi University’s Varendra Research Museum on Friday hosted a daylong heritage festival and special exhibition celebrating Bangladesh’s rich cultural traditions, archaeological heritage and diverse communal practices.
